    d^a>2^{-sn/2}2^{-8\varepsilon n}.
\]
The corresponding families are denoted by

and

body:
PRIVATE NUMERICAL EVIDENCE, not a proof. Lyons (ICM 2014, Question 2.8) asks whether for H = H_1 (+) H_2 orthogonal in l^2(E) there is a coupling of the determinantal projection measures P_{H_1}, P_{H_2} whose union has law P_H. Since the cardinalities are dim H_1, dim H_2 and dim H almost surely, the union must be disjoint, and the question is the nonemptiness of the transportation polytope with the three marginals. Exact LP (HiGHS, minimum total violation) on 1360 random pairs of orthogonal subspaces with |E| in {3,...,6} over all dimension splits, on generic instances with |E| = 7 and 8, on Fourier-mode subspaces of cycles of length 5..8, and on star-space splits in the edge space of K_4 found a feasible coupling with zero violation every time (intake raw/C_lyons_q28_lp_check.json and _structured.json). A structural observation: the naive rule 'sample X_1 from P_{H_1} conditioned on X_1 subset C, set X_2 = C minus X_1' does NOT reproduce the P_{H_2} marginal in general (checked on |E| = 4), so the coupling, when it exists, is not the conditional splitting. Open: a general construction.
Finite E, orthogonal subspaces H_1, H_2
Evidence is computational on |E| <= 8 only
title: Lyons's union-marginal coupling question: transportation polytope feasible in every tested instance, naive conditional splitting fails

[Dfn 11 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] For any finite positive semidefinite matrix $Q$, its \textbf{log-determinant entropy} is
\[\rmH(Q) := \log \det Q,\]
with the usual convention that $\log 0 = -\infty$.

If $S$ is any set (not necessarily finite), $Q$ is a positive semidefinite $S$-by-$S$ matrix, and $F$ is a finite subset of $S$, then we define
\[\rmH_Q(F) := \rmH(Q[F]),\]
where $Q[F]$ is the $F$-by-$F$ submatrix of $Q$. (Recall our notation for submatrices from Section~\ref{sec:lin-alg}.)
title: Definition 11 of arXiv:2507.08909

$$ \item 
 When $A_n$ is real valued, we further prove that for any $\epsilon>0$,
 $$

 $$
\mathbb{P}(\det A_n\neq 0)=1.

Let $\mu$ be a finite positive measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with Stieltjes transform $m(z) = \int \frac{d\mu(t)}{t - z}$, defined and analytic for $\operatorname{Im} z > 0$, with $\operatorname{Im} m(z) > 0$ there. Then for every $a < b$ that are continuity points of $\mu$, $\mu((a, b]) = \lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} \frac{1}{\pi}\int_a^b \operatorname{Im} m(x + i\eta)\,dx$, and if $\mu$ has a continuous density $f$ at $x$ then $f(x) = \frac{1}{\pi}\lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} \operatorname{Im} m(x + i\eta)$. The real part has the companion limit $\operatorname{Re} m(x + i\eta) \to \pi H_f(x) := \mathrm{PV}\int \frac{f(t)}{t - x}\,dt$ wherever $f$ is Hölder continuous, so the boundary value $\breve m(x) = \lim_{\eta\downarrow0} m(x + i\eta) = \pi H_f(x) + i\pi f(x)$ (Sokhotski-Plemelj). In particular two measures with the same Stieltjes transform on $\mathbb{C}^+$ coincide, and a sequence of probability measures converges weakly if and only if the Stieltjes transforms converge pointwise on $\mathbb{C}^+$ (to the transform of a probability measure).
mu a finite positive Borel measure on the real line
for the density statement: mu absolutely continuous with a density continuous at x; for the real-part statement: the density Hölder continuous near x

[Theorem thm : big 4 of arXiv:2609.00105, 'Weighted composition operators and classification of weighted Hardy spaces'] Let $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2$ be weighted Hardy spaces in $d$ variables.
    Assume that $G_1(t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nt^n$ is the generating function of $\mathcal{H}_1$  and $G_2(t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_nt^n$ is the generating function of $\mathcal{H}_2$.
    The following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There exists a unitary $W_{\lambda,\varphi}:\mathcal{H}_2\to\mathcal{H}_1$.
        \item There exists a coisometry $W_{\lambda,\varphi}:\mathcal{H}_2\to\mathcal{H}_1$.
        \item There exists $\gamma\in(0,\infty)$ such that $a_n=b_n\gamma^n$ for all $n$.
    \end{enumerate}

(prop:four-dimensional-global-minimizer of the paper), set $s_0:=v(0)$, and define
\begin{equation}
\kappa_*
:=
q_5'\bigl(q_5^{-1}(s_0)\bigr)
=
\frac{\sqrt{2W(s_0)}}{F_5(e_5)}.
\end{equation}
For every $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_*)$, there exists a global minimizer
\[
U\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^5),
\qquad
-1<U<1,
\]
such that
\begin{equation}
-\operatorname{div} a_5(DU)+W'(U)=0,
\qquad
\partial_5U>0
\qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^5,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
U(0)=s_0,
\qquad
\partial_5U(0)=\kappa.
\end{equation}
The solution is even in the first four variables and is not
one-dimensional.

body:
Fix 0<gamma<2. For the zero-boundary GFF on the unit disk, with covariance singularity log(1/|x-y|), let mu_gamma be the GMC of Lebesgue measure defined by the weak limit of 2^(-n*gamma^2/2) exp(gamma*h_{2^(-n)}(y))dy. Almost surely, for mu_gamma-almost every interior x, the centered logarithmic disk potential T_x(r) has log exponent 2-gamma^2/2. A strictly positive continuous local weight multiplying mu_gamma preserves this conclusion. This is a derived Euclidean-potential corollary, not an exact metric dimension formula.

[Cor 3 of arXiv:2609.01101, '2609.01101'] Let $K$ be a fixed number field, let $L$ be its Galois closure, and set
$$
G=\Gal(L/\Q),\qquad H=\Gal(L/K),\qquad
\rho_K=|H\backslash G/H|.
$$
Assume GRH for $\zeta_L$.  Then, for every fixed real $k>0$ and all
sufficiently large $T$,
\begin{equation}
\int_T^{2T}
\left|\zeta_K\left(\tfrac12+it\right)\right|^{2k}\,dt
\gg_{K,k}
T(\log T)^{\rho_Kk^2}.
\end{equation}
If $K$ is a non-Galois cubic field whose Galois closure has group $S_3$,
then $\rho_K=2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 3 of arXiv:2609.01101

[Lemma 6 (Cohomological lifting) of arXiv:2609.03282, 'Characteristic-free characterizations of projective space for smooth toric varieties'] Suppose that
\[
0\longrightarrow\cK_m\longrightarrow\cK_{m-1}
\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\cK_0
\longrightarrow\cF\longrightarrow0
\]
is an exact complex of vector bundles on a projective variety $X$. 
If 
$H^q(X,\cK_q)=0$ for 
every $1\leq q\leq m$, 
then the natural map 
$H^0(X,\cK_0)\to H^0(X,\cF)$ 
is surjective.

[Definition 89 (Strings of commutation vectorfields and vectorfield seminorms) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Recall that 
	$\Fullset = \{\Lunit, \muX, \Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$, 
	$\Tanset = \{\Lunit,\Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$,
	and 
	$\Angularset = \{\Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$ are the sets of commutation vectorfields 
	defined in \eqref{E:COMMUTATIONVECTORFIELDS}.
	We adopt the following definitions for differential operators constructed out of strings of commutation vectorfields.
	In this section, $f$ denotes a scalar function.
	
	\begin{itemize}
		\item $\comder^{N;M} f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\comder$ applied to $f$, where the string contains \emph{precisely} $M$ factors of $\muX$. We set $\comder^{0,0}f = f$. We often write
		$\comder f$ instead of $\comder^{1;1} f$ and $\comder^{N;M} f$ when the string contains \emph{precisely} factors of $\muX$.
		\item $\tander^N f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\tander$ applied to $f$. We set $\tander^0 f = f$. We often write $\tander f$ instead of $\tander^1 f$.
		\item $\tanderY^N f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\mathscr{Y}$ applied to $f$. We set $\tanderY^0 f = f$.
		\item $\comdersmall^{N;M} f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\comder$ applied to $f$, where the string contains \emph{at least} one factor of $\tander$ and \emph{precisely} $M$ factors of $\muX$.
		\item $\tandersmall^N$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\tander$ applied to $f$, where the string contains \emph{at least two factors} of $\Lunit$ or \emph{at least one factor of $\Yvf{2}, \Yvf{3}$}.
		\item $\comderdoublesmall^{N;M} f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\comder$ applied to $f$, 
		where the string contains at least two factors of $\Lunit$ or at least one factor of $\Yvf{A}$ and \emph{precisely} $M$ factors of $\muX$.
		\item $\mathfrak{P}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of all differential operators of the form $\tander^N$.
		\item $\mathfrak{Y}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of all differential operators of the form $\tanderY^N$.
		\item $\mathfrak{Z}_*^{(N;1)}$ and $\mathfrak{Z}_*^{(N;\le 1)}$ denote the set of all differential operators of the form $\comdersmall^{N;1}$ and $\comdersmall^{N;\le 1}$.
		\item  We define order $N$ strings of $\ell_{t,u}$-projected Lie derivatives
	such as $\angLie_{\tander}^N$ and $\angLie_{\comder}^{N;M}$ in an analogous fashion.  
	Such operators act on $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfields $\upxi$, e.g., $\angLie_{\tander}^N \upxi$.
		\item $\angLie_{\mathfrak{P}}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of all differential operators of the form $\angLie_{\tander}^N$.
		\item $\angLie_{\mathfrak{Y}}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of all differential operators of the form $\angLie_{\tanderY}^N$.
		\item  $\comder^{\leq N;M} f$ denotes the array of all terms of the form
		$\comder^{N';M} f$, where $0 \leq N' \leq N$. 
		\item If $N_1 < N_2$, then
		$\comder^{[N_1,N_2];M} f$ denotes the array of all terms of the form
		$\comder^{N';M} f$, where $N_1 \leq N' \leq N_2$.
		\item We define arrays such as $\tanderY^{\leq 2} f$ in an analogous fashion.
	\end{itemize}
	We also define pointwise seminorms:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item $|\comder^{N;M} f|$ denotes the magnitude of $\comder^{N;M}f$ as defined above (there is no summation).
		\item $|\comder^{\leq N;M} f|$ denotes the sum over all terms of the form $|\comder^{N';M} f|$ with $N' \leq N$. 
		\item $| \comder^{[N_1,N_2];M}f |$ is the sum over all terms of the form $|\comder^{N';M} f|$ with $N_1 \leq N' \leq N_2$. 
		\item Terms such as 
		$|\tandersmall^{[N_1,N_2]}f|$, 
		$|\angLie_{\comder}^{\leq N;M} \upxi|_{\gtorus}$, 
		$|\tanderY^{\leq N} f|$,
		etc., are defined analogously,

		with $N' \leq N$.

Two filtered processes $\mathbb{X}, \mathbb{Y} \in \mathcal{FP}_p$ are called equivalent, denoted $\mathbb{X} \sim_{\mathrm{FP}} \mathbb{Y}$, if $\mathcal{AW}_p(\mathbb{X}, \mathbb{Y}) = 0$. The space of equivalence classes is denoted by $\mathbb{FP}_p := \mathcal{FP}_p / \sim_{\mathrm{FP}}$. The pair $(\mathbb{FP}_p, \mathcal{AW}_p)$ forms a complete and separable metric space.
p \in [1, \infty)
\mathcal{AW}_p is the adapted Wasserstein distance
title: Equivalence of Filtered Processes and the Metric Space FP_p

[Theorem th:main of arXiv:2510.00214, 'On the local well-posedness of randomly forced reaction-diffusion equations with $\bm{L^2}'] Suppose that $u_0\in L^2[0\,,1]$,
	and that Assumption (cond-dif of the paper) holds. Then, there exists 
	a nonrandom number $t_0>0$ such that 
	(equation SHE:1 of the paper) has a random-field solution $u=u(t\,,x)$ 
	for all $(t\,,x)\in(0\,,t_0]\times[0\,,1]$ that
	satisfies the following:
	\begin{compactenum}[\indent\indent\rm (1)]
	\item $(t\,,x)\mapsto u(t\,,x)$ is a.s.\ continuous on $(0\,,t_0]\times[0\,,1]$;
	\item $\lim_{t\to0+} t^\alpha \|u(t)\|_{C[0,1]}=0$ a.s.\ 
		for every $\alpha>\frac14$, in fact there exists $\gamma=\gamma(b\,,\sigma,\alpha) >0$ such that
		\[
			\E\exp\left\{\gamma\sup_{t\in(0,t_0]}(t^\alpha\|u(t)\|_{C[0,1]})^{2/3}
			\right\}<\infty;
		\]
	\item As $t\to0+$, $\| u(t)-u_0\|_{L^2[0,1]}\to 0$ in probability.
	\end{compactenum}
	Finally, if $v$ is any other continuous random-field solution to (equation SHE:1 of the paper) on 
	the time interval $(0\,,t_0]$ such that 
	$\sup_{s\in(0,t_0]}(s^\alpha\|v(s)\|_{C[0,1]})<\infty$ a.s.~for 
	some $\alpha>\frac14$, then $\mathrm{P}\{u(t)=v(t)\ \forall t\in(0\,,t_0]\}=1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th:main of arXiv:2510.00214

body: In statistics, sufficiency is a property of a statistic computed on a sample dataset in relation to a parametric model of the dataset. A sufficient statistic for a model parameter contains all of the information that the dataset provides about that parameter. It is closely related to the concepts of an ancillary statistic which contains no information about the model parameters, and of a complete statistic which only contains information about the parameters and no ancillary information.
title: Sufficient statistic

[Definition 20 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(\iota \colon X \to S\) be a morphism of $\F_p$-stacks.
We say that $X$ is \emph{Hodge--Tate split} (\emph{HT-split}, for short) over $S$ if the homomorphism
\[
\nu_{X/S}^{\sharp} \colon \cO_{X^{(1)}} \to R\nu_{X/S,*}\cO_{(X/S)^{\dR}} \eqdef \OdR{X/S}
\]
is ind-split in $\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X^{(1)})$, where \(X^{(1)}\) is the Frobenius twist of \(X\) over \(S\).

We say that an \(\setF_p\)-stack \(X\) is \emph{HT-split} if $X$ is HT-split over $\Spec(\F_p)$.
title: Definition 20 of arXiv:2609.00567

[Lemma lem: technical lemma bound on S prime of arXiv:2605.28770, 'Cutoff profiles for conjugacy invariant random walks on symmetric groups'] Let $r\geq 1$.
    Let $n\geq 3r$. Let $\lambda \vdash n$ such that $r(\lambda) = r$. Let $\sigma \in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{S}}} _n$ such that $f:= f_1(\sigma) \geq 2r$, and denote its cycle structure written in weakly increasing order by $\alpha$. Let $K\in \left\{  0, 2,3,4, \ldots\right\} $. Let $S'(\lambda, \alpha, K)$ be the set of all ribbon tableaux of $\lambda$ with weight $\alpha$ such that all but $K$ boxes in $\lambda^*$ are filled with 1-ribbons. Then
\begin{equation}
    |S'(\lambda, \alpha, K)| \lesssim_r
    f^{r-K} G(\sigma)^K \leq M(\sigma)^r.
\end{equation}
Moreover, $S'(\lambda, \alpha, 0)$ consists of $d_{(\lambda_1-k, \lambda_2, \lambda_3, \ldots)}$ ribbon tableaux of height 0.
title: Lemma lem: technical lemma bound on S prime of arXiv:2605.28770

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2506.16260, 'Fractional Compound Poisson Random Fields on Plane'] (\textbf{Two parameter L\'evy process})
A real valued two parameter random process $\{X(t_1,t_2),\ (t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2_+\}$ is called L\'evy process if \\
\noindent (i) $X(0,t_2)=X(t_1,0)=0$ almost surely,\\
\noindent (ii) for fix $(h,k)\in\mathbb{R}^2_+$,  the distribution of $\Delta_{t_1,t_2}X(t_1+h,t_2+k)$ is independent of the choice of $(t_1,t_2)$. This is known as the stationary increment property,\\
\noindent (iii) for disjoint rectangles $R_1,R_2,\dots,R_m$ in $\mathbb{R}^2_+$ of type $(s_1,t_1]\times (s_2,t_2]$, the random variables $X(R_1),X(R_2)$, $\dots,X(R_m)$ are independent of each other. This property is known as the independent increments property.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2506.16260

Let T > 0 and let H: R^n × R^n → R be continuous and satisfy, for some constant C and all x,y,p,q ∈ R^n: (H1) |H(x,p) - H(x,q)| ≤ C|p-q| (H is Lipschitz in p, uniformly in x); (H2) |H(x,p) - H(y,p)| ≤ C|x-y|(1+|p|). Let u and v be bounded and uniformly continuous on R^n × [0,T], with u a viscosity subsolution and v a viscosity supersolution of w_t + H(x,Dw) = 0 in R^n × (0,T). If u(x,0) ≤ v(x,0) for all x ∈ R^n, then u ≤ v on R^n × [0,T]. Consequently the Cauchy problem u_t + H(x,Du) = 0 in R^n × (0,T), u(·,0) = g, has at most one viscosity solution that is bounded and uniformly continuous on R^n × [0,T].

Let Phi be a stationary simple locally finite planar point process with finite positive intensity, bounded Voronoi cells, finite nonempty edge-neighbor sets, no four cocircular points, no three collinear points, and almost surely unique nearest nuclei p_x at deterministic observation points. Define F6(x) as the mean of ((q-p_x)/|q-p_x|)^6 over its Delaunay edge-neighbors. Put C6(x,y)=E[F6(x)conjugate(F6(y))]-E[F6(x)]E[conjugate(F6(y))], V(t)=P(Phi intersect B(0,t) is empty), and alpha(A,B)=sup |P(E intersect H)-P(E)P(H)| over events of the restrictions to A and B. Suppose for D=|x-y|>6r and r>=r0, uniformly in x,y,r, alpha(B(x,3r),B(y,3r))<=Am(1+r)^kappa(1+D-6r)^(-p), and V(t)<=Av exp(-a t^nu) for t>=t0, with p,a,nu>0, kappa>=0, and finite Am,Av. Then |C6(x,y)|=O(D^(-p)(log D)^(kappa/nu)). Thus an eventual lower bound cD^(-eta), c,eta>0, is impossible when p>eta. This is a conditional correlation-transfer result and does not construct a Riesz Gibbs phase.

Let $W \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded measurable set, and let $f$ be a real-valued measurable functional defined on finite simplicial complexes with vertices in $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{A}$. For $(x, a, t, u) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{A} \times [0, 1] \times \mathbb{M}$, let $\Delta_W^{(x, a, t, u)}$ denote the simplicial complex restricted to $W$ obtained from the augmented Poisson process $\Psi + \delta_{(x, a, t, u)}$. The difference operator $\Lambda_{(x, a, t, u)} f(\Delta_W)$ is defined by $\Lambda_{(x, a, t, u)} f(\Delta_W) := f(\Delta_W^{(x, a, t, u)}) - f(\Delta_{W \setminus \{x\}}^{(x, a, t, u)})$, which measures the exact change in $f$ caused by the addition of the vertex $(x, a)$ with auxiliary randomization marks $(t, u)$.

[Proposition prop:poly-growth of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be an infinite, locally finite, connected graph with degree bounded by~$d$.  Assume:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)}]
			\item \textup{(Volume growth)}\; $|B(o,r)|\leq C_{\mathrm{vol}} r^{d_f}$ for some $o\in V$, $d_f>0$, and all $r\geq 1$.
			\item \textup{(Spectral dimension)}\; $\sup_{x\in V}\mathbb{P}_x(X_n=x)\leq A n^{-d_s/2}$ for all $n\geq 1$, for some $d_s\in(0,2)$ and $A<\infty$.
			\item \textup{(Walk dimension)}\; For all $x\in V$, all $n\geq 1$, and all $r\geq 1$,
			\[
			\mathbb{P}_x\bigl(\tau_{B(x,r)}\leq n\bigr)\leq C_{\mathrm{disp}}\exp\biggl(-c_{\mathrm{disp}}\Bigl(\frac{r^{d_w}}{n}\Bigr)^{\!1/(d_w-1)}\biggr)\,,
			\]
			for some $d_w\geq 2$ and constants $C_{\mathrm{disp}},c_{\mathrm{disp}}>0$.
		\end{enumerate}
		Let $(\xi(v))_{v\in V}$ be i.i.d.\ and independent of the walk with $\mathbb{E}[\xi]\in[-\infty,0)$ and $\mathbb{E}[(\xi^+)^p]<\infty$ for some $p>\max(2d_f/(d_w\,d_s),\,1)$.  Then $\sup_\tau\mathbb{E}_o[S_\tau\mid\xi]<\infty$ almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:poly-growth of arXiv:2604.13968

[Lemma 6 (Convex ordering for i.i.d.\ copies) of arXiv:2605.28766, 'Convex order and faster transmission in first contact percolation'] Let $\X\gg\X'$ and consider i.i.d.\ copies $\X_1,\X_2,\dots$ of $\X$ and  i.i.d.\ copies $\X'_1,\X'_2,\dots$ of $\X'$. Then, for every finite collection of Borel sets $B_1,\dots,B_k\in\mathcal{B}(\R^d)$ and every increasing concave function $\varphi\colon\R^{k\times k}\to\R$, we have
        $$\bbE[\varphi((\X_i(B_j))_{i,j\leq k})] \geq \bbE[\varphi((\X'_i(B_j))_{i,j\leq k})] \,.$$

body:
[Theorem thm:colorTASEPconv of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] For $\epsilon>0$, define the rescaling $(x, s)_\epsilon = (\lfloor 2\epsilon^{-1}x \rfloor, 2\epsilon^{-3/2}s)$ and define $H_\epsilon:\mathbb H^2_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R}$ by
		\[
		H_\epsilon(x, s; y, t) = -\epsilon^{1/2}H((x, s)_\epsilon; (y, t)_\epsilon) + \epsilon^{-1}(t-s).
		\]
		Take either (i) fixed $\alpha > \frac{1}{2}$ and $\rho=-\infty$, or (ii) $\alpha = \frac{1}{2}-\rho\epsilon^{1/2}/2$ for some $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$.
		Then as $\epsilon\to 0$, $H_\epsilon$ converges in distribution to $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ in the uniform-on-compact topology. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:sc-dual-diamonds of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] The dual linear system
(equation eq:sc-dual-linear-1 of the paper)--(equation eq:sc-dual-linear-j of the paper)
is compatible if and only if two families of conditions hold.
First, for each $j \geq 2$ and $u \in \mathcal{V}$, the
following dual diamond equations hold:
\begin{align}
\partial_1 C_j(Tu) + C_1(Tu)C_j(Tu)
  &= C_j(Tu)C_1(S_j u),
   \\
\Lambda_1(u)\Lambda_j(Tu)
  &= \Lambda_j(u)\Lambda_1(S_j u),
   \\
\partial_1\Lambda_j(Tu)
  + C_1(u)\Lambda_j(Tu)
  &+ \Lambda_1(Tu)C_j(Tu)
  - C_j(u)\Lambda_1(S_j u) \notag \\
  &\quad - \Lambda_j(Tu)C_1(S_j u) = 0.
  
\end{align}
Second, for each pair $i, j \geq 2$ and
$u \in \mathcal{V}$, the fully discrete diamond equations
(equation eq:diamond-C-ij of the paper)--(equation eq:diamond-mixed-ij of the paper) of
Proposition~(prop:CL-gen-system of the paper) hold.

Suppose that: (1) \sum_{k=1}^{k_n} \mathbb{E}[X_{n, k}^2 \mid \mathcal{F}_{n, k-1}] \xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}} \sigma^2 for some constant \sigma^2 > 0; and (2) for every \epsilon > 0, \sum_{k=1}^{k_n} \mathbb{E}[X_{n, k}^2 \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_{n, k}| > \epsilon\}} \mid \mathcal{F}_{n, k-1}] \xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}} 0. Then S_n = \sum_{k=1}^{k_n} X_{n, k} \xrightarrow{d} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2) as n \to \infty.

G is real-valued on P_2(R^d), admits a first variation V[mu] in C^1(R^d), and for one L>0, |grad V[mu](x)-grad V[nu](y)| <= L(|x-y|+W_2(mu,nu)) for all mu,nu,x,y. G is convex under linear mixing of measures. For the temperature tau>0, F_tau(mu)=G(mu)+tau H(mu), where H(mu)=integral log(dmu/dx) dmu, admits a minimizer mu_tau^*. For every mu in P_2(R^d), Z_mu=integral exp(-V[mu]/tau) dx is finite and positive and nu_mu=Z_mu^(-1) exp(-V[mu]/tau) dx satisfies the uniform logarithmic Sobolev inequality KL(eta||nu_mu) <= I(eta||nu_mu)/(2 rho_tau), with rho_tau>0 independent of mu. Here I(eta||nu)=integral |grad log(deta/dnu)|^2 deta. Let mu_t solve partial_t mu_t=div(mu_t grad V[mu_t])+tau Delta mu_t, with mu_0 in P_2(R^d) and F_tau(mu_0)<infinity. Then for every t>=0, F_tau(mu_t)-F_tau(mu_tau^*) <= exp(-2 tau rho_tau t) [F_tau(mu_0)-F_tau(mu_tau^*)]. This bounds the regularized objective at fixed temperature; it does not give a temperature-uniform rate for G alone.

[Lemma timedecor of arXiv:2601.05361, 'Noise sensitivity in last-passage percolation'] For $i \in {\mathbb{N}}$, we denote by $\mathrm{pr}_i:\{0, 1\}^{{\mathbb{N}}}\to{\mathbb{R}}$ the map $x \mapsto x_i$. For all $t \geq 0$ and $f \in L^2$,
\begin{equation}
P_t \nabla_i f = e^{-t} (p-\mathrm{pr}_i) P_t \Big( \frac{\nabla_i f}{p - \mathrm{pr}_i} \Big)  .
\end{equation}
It follows that $\I_i(P_t f) = {\mathbb{E}} \big[|\nabla_i P_t f| \big]$ decays exponentially in $t$, in that
\[
\I_i(P_t f) \leq 2 e^{-t} \max(p, 1-p) \I_i(f)  .
\]

[Definition def:heavy-neighbor-light-root of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] For a $G=(I,J,M)$ with maximum right degree $d$. 
For $i\in I$, write
\[
D_i:=|N_G(i)|.
\]
Let
\(
N^\dagger_G(i)\subseteq N_G(i)
\)
be any set of cardinality $\lceil \tfrac{1}{32d} D_i\rceil$, 
such that
\[
|M_{ij}|\ge |M_{ij'}|
\qquad
\forall j\in N^\dagger_G(i),\ 
\forall j'\in N_G(i)\setminus N^\dagger_G(i).
\]
A right vertex $j_\star\in J$ is \hyperref[def:heavy-neighbor-light-root]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{light}}}{} if
\[
j_\star\notin N^\dagger_G(i)
\qquad
\forall i\in N_G(j_\star).
\]
title: Heavy-neighbor sets and light roots

[Definition def:rgen of arXiv:2608.24963, 'Why and When Neural Networks Improve Local Approximation in Optimization'] Fix a floor $\epsilon_{g,0}\ge0$ and a rate $\kappa_g>0$, and set
$\bar e_g(\delta):=\epsilon_{g,0}+\kappa_g\delta$, with $\bar e_f$ defined analogously from
$\epsilon_{f,0}$ and $\kappa_f\delta^2$. The \emph{effective generalization radius} around
$x$ is
\begin{equation}
r_{\mathrm{gen}}(x) := \sup\bigl\{\Delta>0:\ e_f(x,\delta)\le \bar e_f(\delta)\ \text{and}\ e_g(x,\delta)\le \bar e_g(\delta)\ \text{ for every } 0<\delta\le\Delta \bigr\}.
\end{equation}
title: Effective local generalization radius

[Defn Horizontal Cluster of arXiv:2609.01499, 'On the rigidity of sloped height functions in $d\ge 3$ \\ and non-crossing surfaces'] In any measure $\mu$ satisfying densely dominant heights, almost every extremal component of $\mu$ has a dominant height. Given an extremal component that has dominant heights, we say that an \emph{excitation} is any vertex $v$ such that $\phi_v $ is not equal to the dominant height at that layer. 

In a configuration $\phi$, a horizontal cluster is a connected set of excited vertices within a layer. 
 Abusing notation, a  horizontal cluster 
is a connected set of vertices that lie within a single layer, not necessarily associated with a  configuration or measure. The interior of a horizontal cluster $HC$ in layer $\mathcal L_{\vec{k}} = \mathbb Z^2\times \vec{k}$ is the union of vertices in the horizontal cluster or in a finite connected component of $\mathcal L \setminus HC$.
title: Horizontal Cluster

[Definition def:OPRE-alternative-embedding of arXiv:2507.00329, 'Oriented bond-site percolation in random environment and contact processes with periodic r'] Let $B\in\{0,1\}$ be a Bernoulli random variable with parameter $1/2$ independent of everything else. Given (a realisation of) $B$ and $X$, consider the graph $G=(V,E)$ with vertex set
    \[
    	V=\big\{(t,X_i)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}^2 \colon t\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}, t+i+B \text{ even}\big\}
    \]
and edge set
    \[
    	E=\big\{(t,X_i)\to(t+1,X_{i\pm 1}) \colon  (t,X_i)\in V\big\}.
    \]
Consider $\kappa_\lambda\colon[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ as in Definition~(def:OPRE-model of the paper).
We consider the independent bond-site percolation model on $G$, where for either $(t,X_{i})\in V$ or $(t,X_{i+1})\in V$, the edges \((t,X_{i})\to(t+1,X_{i+1})\) and \((t,X_{i+1})\to(t+1,X_{i})\), respectively, are open with probability \(\kappa_\lambda(\nu_{i,i+1})\).
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    Similarly, vertices $(t,X_i)\in V$ are open independently with probability \(\kappa_\lambda(\xi_i)\).
    
    
    
    We denote by $\mathbb{P}_\lambda^X(A):=\mathbb{P}_\lambda(A|X)$ the probability measure, conditionally given $X$ (as defined in~(equation eq:OPRE-stationarised-renewal-X of the paper)).
title: Alternative stationary spatial embedding

body:
[Ppn 140 (\hyperlink{proof:p.Ising-IAMP-analysis}{proved in \S\ref{ss:proof.iamp.diffus.limit}}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-main}, and recalling the notation \eqref{e:state.evol.piecewise}, there exist standard Brownian motions $B$ and $W$ such that the behavior of the state evolution limit \eqref{e:state.evol.x.y.increments} can be described as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item 
  
The random variables $V^k,Y^k,\prxY^k$ can be written as
  \begin{align*}
  V^k
  &=
        V^0
        +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  s_\delta(t_\delta)
  \,\de B(t),
  \\
  Y^k
  = \breve{Y}(q_0+k\delta)
  &=
        \breve{Y}(q_0)
        +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  \frac{w_{t_\delta}(\prxY(t))}
  {
  \bbE[w_{t_\delta}(\prxY(t))^2]^{1/2}
  }
  \,\de W(t),
  \\
  \prxY^k
  = \prxY(q_0+k\delta)
  &=\prxY^0+
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  w_{t_\delta}(\prxY(t))
  \,\de W(t)
  .
  \end{align*}

\item

The random variables $M^k$, $X^k$, $\prxX^k$ can be written as
  \begin{align*}
  M^k
  &=
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta} \frac{s_\delta(t_\delta)}{p(t_{\delta})}
  \Big(\sigma_{t_{\delta}}(\prxX(t))-1\Big)
  \,\de B(t);
  \\
  X^k = \breve{X}(q_0+k\delta)
  &=
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  s_\delta(t_\delta)
  \sigma_{t_{\delta}}(
  \prxX(t))
  \,\de B(t)
  +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  p'(t_{\delta})^{1/2}
  b_{t_{\delta}}(\prxX(t))
  \,\de t
  \\
  \prxX^k
  =\prxX(q_0+k\delta)
  &=
  \prxX^0
  +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  s_\delta(t_\delta)
  \sigma_{t_{\delta}}
  (\prxX(t))
  \,\de B(t)
  +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  p'(t_{\delta})^{1/2}
  b_{t_{\delta}}
  (\prxX(t))\,\de t
  .\end{align*}
(Recall from Definition~\ref{d:iamp.v1} that $\breve{X}(q_0)=0$.)
\end{enumerate}
Recall $\prxX^0$ and $\prxY^0$
are equidistributed respectively as $X(q_0)$ and $Y(q_0)$ from the SDEs
\eqref{e:IAMP.X.SDE} and \eqref{e:IAMP.Y.SDE}. Moreover $\prxY^0$ is independent of $W$, and $\prxX^0$ is independent of $B$.\footnote{We recall from the discussion after Corollary~\ref{cor:psi-state-evolution} that $N$-dimensional and $M$-dimensional state evolution variables such as $W$ and $B$ are defined on different probability spaces, and can thus be  thought of as independent.} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For N unit-speed servers with Poisson input N*lambda, independent uniformly chosen destinations, and independent nonnegative job sizes S with rho=lambda*E S<1 and E S^2 finite, the product stationary workload law consists of N independent M/G/1 workloads. The stationary mean workload per server is exactly lambda*E S^2/(2*(1-rho)) for every N. Its first-order 1/N bias and remainder are zero, and off-diagonal covariances are zero. This is the d=1 random-routing case; no zero-bias claim is made for workload-dependent least-of-d routing.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:29913fc85e305f983882cf66a8c6e64f9488845b92275853a10fcb201d718b2f","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/29/29913fc85e305f983882cf66a8c6e64f9488845b92275853a10fcb201d718b2f.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:99d64882c5c75414d2299d44273aa7edeab6ec6f4e682881d811b14888f8baf5","bundle_entry_key":"random-routing-workload-exact-zero-finite-population-bias","bundle_id":"population.w336-p0294-checked-attempt-20261010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"w336/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.queueing:random-routing-workload-exact-zero-finite-population-bias","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0294: a genuine workload benchmark with zero finite-N bias

Status: proof written; w346 KEEP pending. This is the d=1 random-routing special case, not a result for interacting least-of-d routing with d>=2.

Consider N rate-one workload servers, a Poisson input of rate N*lambda, independent uniformly chosen routing destinations, and i.i.d. nonnegative job sizes S independent of routing. Assume rho=lambda*E[S]<1 and E[S^2]<infinity. The N workload processes are independent M/G/1 workload processes when started in their product stationary law. For every N, the stationary mean of one server (and of the empirical mean workload) is

    lambda*E[S^2]/(2*(1-rho)).

Consequently its expansion in 1/N has exactly zero bias coefficient and zero remainder for this observable; stationary off-diagonal covariances are zero.

Proof: marked Poisson thinning produces N independent rate-lambda input processes with independent job marks. Each queue drains at rate one while positive and has upward jumps S. Its stability and stationary construction follow from the negative-drift reflected compound-Poisson input. The stationary idle mass is 1-rho by workload balance. For beta(s)=E[e^(-sS)] and L(s)=E[e^(-sW)], the bounded stationary generator test e^(-sW) gives

    0=s*(L(s)-(1-rho))+lambda*(beta(s)-1)*L(s),
    L(s)=(1-rho)*s/(s-lambda+lambda*beta(s)), s>0.

The second-moment assumption gives beta(s)=1-E[S]*s+E[S^2]*s^2/2+o(s^2). Expansion at zero gives L(s)=1-[lambda*E[S^2]/(2*(1-rho))]*s+o(s); the right derivative of a nonnegative variable's Laplace transform identifies its finite mean. Product stationarity proves all finite-N claims. This handles the actual empty-workload boundary, unlike a Gaussian OU control model.

For exponential service sizes of rate mu>lambda, P(W=0)=1-lambda/mu and P(W>x)=(lambda/mu)*exp(-(mu-lambda)*x) for x>=0, so the mean is lambda/(mu*(mu-lambda)). These formulas are a control for implementations of any proposed first-order correction. They do not justify setting the correction to zero under workload-dependent routing.

Checks: Laplace-transform generator identities, mean calculations for several service parameters, and exact Poisson-thinning algebra. Then there exists at least one point $c \in (a, b)$ such that
\begin{equation*}
    \int_{a}^{b} f(x)g(x) \, dx = f(c) \int_{a}^{b} g(x) \,dx.

body: [Definition 4 (Covering number and $\epsilon$-net) of arXiv:2608.22636, 'Q-Learning with Stable Infinite-Dimensional \\Linear Function Approximation'] An $\epsilon$-net of $(\mbb L,\rho)$ is a subset $\mfk N\subseteq\mbb L$ such that, for every $\ell\in\mbb L$, there exists $\ell'\in\mfk N$ with $\rho(\ell,\ell')\leq\epsilon$. For $\epsilon>0$, let $\cN_\rho(\epsilon)$ denote the covering number of $\mbb L$ by $\rho$-balls of radius $\epsilon$; that is, $\cN_\rho(\epsilon)$ is the smallest cardinality of any $\epsilon$-net. Moreover, let $\mfk N_\rho(\epsilon)$ denote an $\epsilon$-net satisfying $|\mfk N_\rho(\epsilon)|=\cN_\rho(\epsilon)$.
title: Covering number and $\epsilon$-net

body:
[Definition boundarydef of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let $(T, d, \rho)$ be a rooted complete $\mathbb{R}$-tree. 
 
 \smallskip
 
\begin{compactenum}
\item[$(a)$] A \emph{ray with endpoint $\rho$} is a subset $\mathbf r\! \subseteq\! T$ such that $\mathbf r\! = \!  c(\mathbb{R}_+)$ where 
$c\colon\mathbb{R}_+ \! \to \! T$ is a geodesic arc of infinite length necessarily, such that $c(0)\! = \!  \rho$. 

 \smallskip
 

\item[$(b)$] The \emph{boundary} of $(T,d , \rho)$ is the set  
$\partial T\! = \!  \big\{ \mathbf r \, ; \textrm{$\mathbf r$ is a ray whose endpoint is $\rho$} \big\}$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(c)$] $(T, d, \rho)$ is said to be \emph{boundaryless} if $\partial T\! = \!  \emptyset$. 

\smallskip

\end{compactenum}
{\noindent}
Let $\sigma \! \in \!  T$ and let $\mathbf r_1, \mathbf r_2\! \in \!  \partial T$. Let 
$c\colon [0, d(\rho, \sigma) ] \! \to \! T$, $c_i\colon \mathbb{R}_+ \!\! \to \! T$, $i\! \in \!  \{ 1, 2\}$, be geodesics such that $ c(0)\! = \!  \rho$, 
$c([0, d(\rho, \sigma)])\! = \!  [\![ \rho, \sigma ]\!]$ and $c_i(\mathbb{R}_+)\! = \!  \mathbf r_i$, $i\! \in \!  \{ 1,2\}$. We next introduce the following. 
 
\medskip
 
\begin{compactenum}
\item[$(d)$] For all $i\! \in \!  \{ 1, 2\}$, we set $d(\rho, \mathbf r_i)\! :=\!  \infty$ and $\underline{\mathbf r}_i(s)\! :=\!  c_i(s)$, for all $s\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(e)$] For all $s\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+$ we set $\underline{\sigma} (s) \! :=\! c(s\wedge d(\rho, \sigma))$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(f)$] We set $\mathbf r_1\! \wedge \mathbf r_2\! :=\!  c_1(s_0)$ where $s_0\! = \!  \max \{ s\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+ \! : \! c_1(s)\! = \!  c_2(s) \}$ if $\mathbf r_1\!\neq \! \mathbf r_2$, otherwise we set  $\mathbf r_1\! \wedge \mathbf r_2 \! :=\! \mathbf r_1$.  

\smallskip

\item[$(g)$] We set  $\sigma \! \wedge \mathbf r_1\! :=\!  c(s_0)$ where $s_0\! = \!  \max \{ s\! \in \!  [0, d(\rho, \sigma)] : c(s)\! = \!  c_1(s) \}$. $\hfill \square$ 

\end{compactenum}
title: Definition boundarydef of arXiv:2608.09856

			\\

			\EllipticHyperbolicCurrentIntegralIdentityTotalSpacetimeErrorTerm[ \tander^{\Ntop} \GradEnt, \pmb{\partial} \tander^{\Ntop} \GradEnt] \weight^{ \blowupratetoporderacoustic}\ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction 
		\, \voldiamond
		\right|
		& \lesssim

			\frac{1}{|\ubar'|^{0.5}}

[Proposition prop:min-vs-max:formal of arXiv:2609.02304, 'Bayes-Optimal BER and AUC: \\Estimation and Evaluation of Estimators'] Assume that the random variable $\eta(x)$ 
  is not a.s.\ constant.
  Then, we have
  $\Delta_{\mathrm{BER}} \geq 0$ and $\Delta_{\mathrm{AUC}} \geq 0$
  if one of the following conditions holds:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item 
      
      The two classes are balanced, i.e., $\theta = \frac{1}{2}$.
    \item 
      
      The law of $\eta(x)$ is symmetric around its mean $\theta$
      (which may or may not be equal to $\frac{1}{2}$).
    \item 
      
      The Bayes error satisfies $\mathrm{Err}^* \leq \delta_{\theta}$,
      where $\delta_{\theta} > 0$ is a certain constant 
      depending only on $\theta$.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 51 of arXiv:2607.08536, 'Soft edge limit of the Laguerre beta-ensemble at the lower edge'] Define 
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{A}_{n,1}^G &= \{|g_k|\le \log n,\quad 1\le k\le n\},\\
    \mathcal{A}_{n,2}^G &= \{ |Y_k-\sqrt{n-k}|\le  2 \beta^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log(\beta(n-k))},\quad 1\le k\le n-\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor\},\\
    \mathcal{A}_{n,3}^G &= \{\sqrt{\tfrac{{n-k}}{\log n}}\le Y_k\le \sqrt{(n-k)\log n},\quad n-\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor\le k<n\}.
\end{align*}
    Let $\mathcal{A}_n^G=\mathcal{A}_{n,1}^G\cap \mathcal{A}_{n,2}^G\cap \mathcal{A}_{n,3}^G$, then  $\pr(\mathcal{A}_n^G)\ge 1- c_\beta(\log n)^{-\beta/2}$, where $c_\beta>0$ is independent of $n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 15 (Boolean-polynomial description) of arXiv:2608.31157, 'Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations'] Let $d,r,s,d_{\mathrm{pol}}\in\N^+$, let $X\subseteq\R^{d}$, and let
\[
 \calF:=\{g_{\bmmu}:X\to\R:\bmmu\in\R^r\}.
\]
Its joint truth set is
\begin{equation}
 \calS
 :=\left\{(\bmx,t,\bmmu)\in X\times\R\times\R^r:
 g_{\bmmu}(\bmx)>t\right\}.
\end{equation}

Choose a number of leaf occurrences $s_0$ with $1\le s_0\le s$.
For each occurrence $j=1,\ldots,s_0$, choose a polynomial
\[
 p_j\in\R[x_1,\ldots,x_{d},t,\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r]
\].
We use the standard convention that the zero polynomial has degree
$-\infty$; thus identically zero atoms are covered by every nonnegative
degree bound below.
The $j$th atom produces the bit
\begin{equation}
 A_j(\bmx,t,\bmmu)
 :=\one_{\{p_j(\bmx,t,\bmmu)>0\}}.
\end{equation}
Finally, choose one Boolean formula tree
$\mathfrak{B}(Z_1,\ldots,Z_{s_0})$ as described above, and let
$\mathsf{B}:\{0,1\}^{s_0}\to\{0,1\}$ be the map obtained from its recursive
evaluation.  We say that $\calS$
has an $(s,d_{\mathrm{pol}})$ Boolean-polynomial description in the parameter
$\bmmu$ when, for every $(\bmx,t,\bmmu)$,
\begin{equation}
 \one_{\calS}(\bmx,t,\bmmu)
 =\mathsf{B}\bigl(
 A_1(\bmx,t,\bmmu),\ldots,
 A_{s_0}(\bmx,t,\bmmu)\bigr),
\end{equation}
and, for each fixed $(\bmx,t)$,
\begin{equation*}
 \deg_{\bmmu}p_j(\bmx,t,\cdot)\le d_{\mathrm{pol}},
 \qquad j=1,\ldots,s_0.
\end{equation*}
The integer $s$ is only an upper bound; $s_0$ is the number of leaf
occurrences actually used after all comparisons have been written in the
strict-positivity form of \eqref{eq:atom-truth-value}.
title: Boolean-polynomial description

body: [Setting/notation of arXiv:2609.03750, section 'Stochastic setting and assumptions'] $\bullet~\textbf{Notation.}$ Let $X$ be a metric space and $E$ a locally compact Polish space. Denote by $\mathcal B(X)$ the Borel $\sigma$-field on $X$, and by $C_c(X)$ the space of continuous compactly supported functions. We equip $C([a,b];X)$ with the uniform topology and $\mathcal D([a,b];X)$ with the Skorokhod topology; the latter is Polish under the usual Skorokhod metric, see \cite[Chapter 2]{Mtivier-1988}. We use $L^2(a,b;X)$ for the space of square-integrable $X$-valued functions. Let $\mathcal M_{FC}(E)$ denote the space of Borel measures $\vartheta$ on $E$ that are finite on compact sets. We equip $\mathcal M_{FC}(E)$ with the weakest topology for which $$ \vartheta\longmapsto\int_E f(v)\,d\vartheta(v) $$ is continuous for every $f\in C_c(E)$. body:
[Lemma lem:lower of arXiv:2609.03448, 'Prime-power Diophantine tuples'] Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ be a positive reduced $D(\varepsilon N)$-tuple.
If $\varepsilon=1$, then $a_3>N^{1/4}$, so at most two elements fail the lower
bound $a>N^{1/4}$. If $\varepsilon=-1$, then $a_2>N^{1/2}$, so at most one
element fails the stronger lower bound $a>N^{1/2}$.

[Lem Nondegeneracy_metric_entropy of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $(X,\rho,\mathfrak{m})$ be a compact metric measure space.
Assume that $(X,\rho,\mathfrak{m})$ is $0<d$-Ahlfors regular, and write
$
    \mathcal{F}_1
\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}
    \operatorname{Lip}((X,\rho),[-1,1];1)
$.  
Then, there are constants
$
    0<c\le C<\infty
$
and
$
    0<\varepsilon_0<1
$
(depending only on on $(X,\rho,\mathfrak{m})$) such that, for every
$
    0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0
$,
\begin{equation}

    c\,\varepsilon^{-d}
    \le
    \log_2
    \mathcal N
    \bigl(
        \mathcal{F}_1,
        \|\cdot\|_{\infty},
        \varepsilon
    \bigr)
    \le
    C\,\varepsilon^{-d}.
\end{equation}

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Fix any $\delta\in (0,1)$, and set
$
\tilde{\varepsilon}=\frac{\delta}{20\tau},
\bar\varepsilon=\frac{\tilde{\varepsilon}}{4.4\tau}
$.
Let $G=G(n,\tau)$ be a power-law random graph on $n$ vertices with exponent $\tau>2$, and let
$
\bm d=(d_1,\dots,d_n)
$
denote its degree sequence. Suppose that $v_1,v_2,\dots,v_{\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil}$ are vertices with degrees greater than $n^{2\tilde{\varepsilon}}$. Let $A$ denote the event that, for each $j=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil$, the vertex $v_j$ has at least $\lceil n^{\tilde{\varepsilon}}\rceil$ distinct neighbors
$
u_1^{(j)},\dots,u_{\lceil n^{\tilde{\varepsilon}}\rceil}^{(j)}
$
such that all vertices in the collection
$
\{
u_i^{(j)}:
1\le j\le \lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil,\,
1\le i\le \lceil n^{\tilde{\varepsilon}}\rceil
\}$
are distinct and have degrees between $n^{\bar\varepsilon}$ and $n^{3\bar\varepsilon}$. Then, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}(A\mid \bm d)\ge 1-\exp(-n^{\bar\varepsilon (\tau-2)/2}), \qquad \text{on the event $D_{\bar\varepsilon}$ defined in \eqref{eq_D}. }
\end{equation}

body:
[Defi 55 (The saturation of $(E,\mathcal{U})$ w.r.t. $\mathcal{U}_\beta$) of arXiv:2603.05174, 'Regularization of the superposition principle: Potential theory meets Fokker-Planck equati'] Let $\beta >0$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item The {\it energy functional} associated with $\mathcal{U}_\beta$ is $L^{\beta}: Exc(\mathcal{U}_\beta)\times \mathcal{E}(\mathcal{U}_\beta) \rightarrow \overline{\mathbb{R}}_+$ given by
\begin{align*}
L^{\beta}(\xi,v):&=\sup\{\mu(v) \; : \; \mu \mbox{ is a } \sigma\mbox{- finite measure, } \mu \circ U_\beta \leq \xi\}\\
&=\sup\{\xi(f) \; : \; f\geq 0 \mbox{ is a } \mathcal{B}\mbox{-measurable function such that } U_\beta f \leq v\}.
\end{align*}
\item The {\it saturation} of $E$ (with respect to $\mathcal{U}_\beta$) is the set $E_1$ of all extreme points of the set $\{\xi \in Exc(\mathcal{U}_\beta)\; : \; L^{\beta}(\xi,1)=1\}$.
\item The map $E\ni x \mapsto \delta_x \circ U_\beta \in Exc(\mathcal{U}_\beta)$ is a measurable embedding of $E$ into $E_1$ and 
every $\mathcal{U}_\beta$-excessive function $v$ has an extension $v_1$ to $E_1$, defined as $v_1(\xi):=L^{\beta}(\xi,v)$.
The set $E_1$ is endowed with the $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{B}_1$ generated by the family $\{v_1: \; v\in \mathcal{E}(\mathcal{U}_\beta)\}$.
In addition, as in \cite[Sections 1.1 and 1.2]{BeBoRo06}, there exists a unique resolvent of kernels $\mathcal{U}^{1}=(U^{1}_\alpha)_{\alpha>0}$ on $(E_1, \mathcal{B}_1)$ 
which is an {\it extension} of $\mathcal{U}$ in the sense that
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(iii.1)] $U^1{1_{E_1\setminus E}}=0$ on $E_1$,
    \item[(iii.2)] $(U^1f)|_E=U(f|_E)$ for all $f \in b\mathcal{B}_1$.
\end{enumerate}
More precisely, it is given by
\begin{align} 
U^{1}_\alpha f(\xi)&=L^{\beta}(\xi, U_\alpha (f|_E))\nonumber\\
&=L^{\beta}(\xi,U_\beta(f|_E+(\beta-\alpha)U_\alpha))\\
&=\xi(f+(\beta-\alpha)U_\alpha f) 
\mbox{ for all } f \in bp\mathcal{B}_1, \xi\in E_1, \alpha >0.
\end{align}
\end{enumerate}
title: The saturation of $(E,\mathcal{U})$ w.r.t. $\mathcal{U}_\beta$

body:
[Theorem Thm:PW_Robin of arXiv:2609.02325, 'A Payne-Weinberger inequality\\for quantum dot Dirac operators'] Let $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded simply connected domain with $C^2$~boundary and let~$\delta_\Omega$ denote its isoperimetric deficit, as in (equation Eq:IsopDeficit of the paper).
    Then, for all $a>0$ there holds
    \begin{equation} 
        |\Omega| \, \mu_\Omega^\mathrm{Rob} \bigg(\frac{a}{\sqrt{|\Omega|}}  \bigg)
         - \pi \, \mu_\mathbb{D}^\mathrm{Rob}\bigg(\frac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}  \bigg) 
        \leqslant 
        F \left(\sqrt{\mu_\mathbb{D}^\mathrm{Rob}\big(\tfrac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}\big)} \right) \delta_\Omega( \delta_\Omega+2) +  G \left(\sqrt{\mu_\mathbb{D}^\mathrm{Rob}\big(\tfrac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}\big)} \right) \delta_\Omega,
    \end{equation}
    where $F$ and $G$ are as in (equation Eq:def_FG of the paper). In particular, 
    \begin{equation} 
        |\Omega| \, \mu_\Omega^\mathrm{Rob} \bigg(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{|\Omega|}}  \bigg)
        - \pi \, \mu_\mathbb{D}^\mathrm{Rob}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}  \bigg) 
        \leqslant  
        C_{\mathrm{PW}} \, \delta_\Omega( \delta_\Omega+2) + \pi j_{0,1} \, \delta_\Omega
    \end{equation}

[Lem 112087 of arXiv:2606.29143, 'Comonotonic and moment matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables'] Let $X$ be a random variable, not necessarily continuous, $\omega(x)$ a nonnegative weight function such that $0 < E[\omega(X)] < \infty$ and ${X_\omega}$ the weighted version of $X$ associated with $\omega$. Then we have that 
\begin{itemize} 
\item $F_{X_\omega}(x)  = G_{X, \omega}(F_X(x)) \,\, \text{for any} \,\, x \in \mathbb{R}$, 
\item $F_{X_\omega}^{-1}(p) = F_X^{-1}(G^{-1}_{X, \omega}(p))$ for any $p \in (0, 1)$, 
 \item $F_{X_\omega}^{-1+}(p) = F_X^{-1+}(G^{-1+}_{X, \omega}(p))$ for any $p \in (0, 1)$, 
\end{itemize}
where $G_{X, \omega}(t)$ is the continuous distortion function as given in Lemma (112074 of the paper).

Let A_1, ..., A_m be events, X_i = 1_{A_i}, U their union, V = span{X_1, ..., X_m} in L2(P), alpha_i = P(A_i) and Sigma_ij = P(A_i and A_j). Then G = alpha^T Sigma^+ alpha (Sigma^+ the Moore-Penrose inverse) equals ||P_V 1_U||^2, the squared norm of the orthogonal projection of 1_U onto V, so P(U) - G = ||1_U - P_V 1_U||^2 >= 0 (Gallot 1966, Kounias 1968). The bound is exact, G = P(U), if and only if 1_U is a linear combination of the X_i almost surely. G = max over c with c^T alpha > 0 of (c^T alpha)^2/(c^T Sigma c), so it is at least the Chung-Erdős value (sum_i alpha_i)^2 / sum_{i,j} Sigma_ij obtained at c = (1, ..., 1).

[Proposition propRepresentation of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] The raw symbol-valued augmented data and the ordinary prime data generate the same sigma-field.
Fix a training sample, give each derived coordinate the missing mask of its base coordinate, and fill every numeric column with its training-sample mean.
Within an affine linear model, the imputed panel $X_1+H_2$ has the same column span as the imputed ordinary prime panel together with the selected squares $x_p^2$.
The corresponding statement holds for $X_1+H_3$ and the selected cubes $x_p^3$.
Subsequent columnwise standardization preserves these affine spans for nonconstant columns.

[Definition 37 of arXiv:2609.03976, '2609.03976'] Suppose $f_{1},...,f_{r} \in \mathbb{C}[x_{1},...,x_{n}]$ are polynomials of degree $d$. We say these polynomials have the polynomial PDE property if they satisfy the condition in Theorem \ref{PDE_theorem}, that is, there exist polynomials $P_{\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{r}}$ indexed by $\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{r} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ satisfying the following conditions.
	
	$(1)$ $P_{\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{r}}$ is homogeneous of degree $d \cdot (\alpha_{1}+...+\alpha_{r})$,
	
	$(2)$ $P_{0,...,0} \neq 0$,
	
	$(3)$ $x_{i}P_{\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{r}}(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{r}\partial_{i}f_{k}(\partial) \cdot P_{\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{k}+1,...,\alpha_{r}}(x)$.

[Proposition 2 (Basic properties of normal random variables) of arXiv:2605.14630, '2605.14630'] \begin{enumerate}
\item   One has $X\sim\cN(m,\sigma^2)$ if, and only if, $X = m + \sigma Y$ 
with $Y \sim \cN(0,1)$. 

\item   Assume $X\sim\cN(m_1,\sigma_1^2)$ and $Y\sim\cN(m_2,\sigma_2^2)$ 
are defined on a common probability space, and let $Z = X + Y$. Then 
$Z$ is Gaussian, with parameters 
\begin{equation}
 Z \sim \cN \bigpar{m_1+m_2, \sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2 + 2\cov(X,Y)}\;.
\end{equation} 

\item   Two Gaussian variables $X$ and $Y$ are independent if, and only if, 
they are uncorrelated, that is, $\cov(X,Y) = \expec{XY} - \expec{X}\expec{Y} = 0$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Basic properties of normal random variables

[Theorem 10 (Survival bound and extinction criterion) of arXiv:2609.02156, 'The higher-dimensional Shepp problem: an exact criterion for random ball coverings of tori'] If \(m_j>0\) for \(0\le j\le N\), then
\begin{equation}
 \Pp(\Xi_N\ne0)
 \le
 \left[
 \frac{2}{3m_N}
 +\frac16\sum_{j<N}\frac{\delta_j}{m_j}
 \right]^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \left[
 m_j>0\ (j\ge0),\qquad
 \sum_{j\ge0}\frac{\delta_j}{m_j}=\infty
 \right]
 \Longrightarrow
 \Pp(\Xi_N\ne0)\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
If, in addition, $(\mathfrak R_j)_{j\ge0}$ is a sequence of random sets such
that, for every $j\ge0$,
\[
 \mathfrak R_{j+1}\subseteq\mathfrak R_j\quad\text{a.s.},\qquad
 \{\Xi_j\ne0\}=\{\mathfrak R_j\ne\varnothing\},
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \Pp(\exists N:\mathfrak R_N=\varnothing)=1.
\end{equation}

[Thm 8 of arXiv:2608.25829, 'Topology of low-dimensional generalized Ricci solitons and string backgrounds'] If $(M, g, H, f)$ is a compact generalized Ricci soliton, then $M$ is finitely covered by $N \times T^k$, where:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\pi_1(N) = 0$,
    \item $g = g_N + g_F$ where $g_F$ is a flat metric on $T^k$,
    \item $H = \pi_N^* H_N$ for a closed three-form on $H_N$,
    \item $f = \pi_N^* f_N$ for $f \in C^{\infty}(N)$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence, $(g_N, H_N, f_N)$ is a generalized Ricci soliton.
\begin{proof} Since a generalized Ricci soliton has nonnegative Bakry-\'Emery Ricci curvature, all of the claims except item (3) follow immediately from \cite[Theorem 6.6]{wei2009comparison}.  Given this structure, inspecting the generalized Ricci soliton equation it follows that for any Killing field $X$ tangent to the torus we have $i_X H = 0$.  Using \cite[Proposition 2.8]{kopfer2023bochner} it follows that $H$ is Levi-Civita parallel with respect to $X$, and hence item (3) follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited), independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2 and 1<=r<K be integers. There are N contexts, K candidates each, d pairs with one arbitrary A and one systematic S context, and N-2d known S contexts. S has all candidates true; A has an independent uniform random r-subset of truths. The factual law p is uniform over contexts, then uniform over true candidates within context. Training supplies n iid uniform context indices and A/S tags, without candidate identities; the partition class has VC dimension d. After training a perfect verifier independently draws a uniform ell-subset of truths in EVERY variable context, including paired S contexts, with 0<=ell<=r; it certifies these identities but gives no orientation tags. It verifies fraction gamma=ell/r of arbitrary truths. The two orientations have the same verifier-output likelihood, so U pairs untouched by training retain both orientations. For arbitrary generators g, require TV(p_Pi,g)<=c in every compatible world, where Pi is the exact partition into nonempty g-probability level sets and p_Pi(y)=p(B)/|B| in each bin B. Define beta=r/K,kappa=1-beta,q=ell/K,alpha=(K-r)/(K-ell),m=U/N,w=(d-U)/N,A0=w*(1-gamma),M0=m*(2-gamma-q). For every c in [0,1], the exact conditional worst-world hallucination frontier is V=alpha*((A0-c)_+ +(A0+M0-c)_+)/2. The oracle given orientations but the same certified identities has value alpha*((d/N)*(1-gamma)-c)_+. The conditional posterior-average game under uniform compatible orientations/supports has the same value. An ERM-version-space generator attains V in every compatible world in expected polynomial bit complexity for rational c. The exact minimax expected value is E[V], where E[z^U]=sum_{j=0}^d binom(d,j)*(z-1)^j*(1-2j/N)^n. At c=(d/N)*(1-gamma), the oracle is zero and V=kappa*U/(2N), with exact expected value kappa*d/(2N)*(1-2/N)^n, half kappa times the minimax expected partition-classification error. For n,d>=1,N=4max(n,d), it lies between (kappa/16)*min(1,d/n) and (kappa/8)*min(1,d/n). At ell=0 it recovers the no-verifier frontier. At ell=r the exact frontier is (kappa*U/N-c)_+/2, so complete arbitrary truth certification without orientation disclosure can still force hallucination at zero calibration error. The unrestricted lower bound also holds for coarser source bins, but its matching upper bound is asserted only for exact-level Mis_infinity. Ordinary factual training, unequal coverage and noisy/adaptive verifiers are not covered.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a254903c9f76a4edf6c7529869019c109a0589cc9d8bbfaf7768c7cda602fef6","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a2/a254903c9f76a4edf6c7529869019c109a0589cc9d8bbfaf7768c7cda602fef6.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:4046749ef851f0b6bc64f25b25012eb3cf5630630ce341100c131924ae8d22b2","bundle_entry_key":"partial-support-verifier-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-partial-support-verifier-no-orientations-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; minimax decision theory","draft":"w709/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:paired-vc-partial-truth-verifier-without-orientations","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Certified partial supports without orientation disclosure

Candidate T379-C008 v2; Own-work draft, proof (unaudited).
Target 2 and its interaction with target 1. Independent checking and
priority review pending. Exact finite verification passed; it supplements
the general proof rather than replacing it.
The hardest remaining generalization is ordinary unannotated factual
training, or a verifier revealing unequal numbers of truths per context:
the posterior density ordering used below can then fail.

## Model

Use the paired VC model: integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2 and
1<=r<K; d pairs each have one A and one S context, the rest known S.
All K candidates are true in S; an independent uniform random r-subset
is true in A. The factual law p chooses contexts uniformly, then a true
candidate uniformly. Training is n iid uniform context indices and
their partition tags, with no candidate identities. The class has VC
dimension d. There are U pairs untouched by training. Let a=d/N,
m=U/N and w=a-m. A known partition is not given for untouched pairs.

Fix an integer 0<=ell<=r. A perfect post-training truth-sampling verifier
supplies a uniformly chosen ell-subset of true candidates in EACH of the
2d variable contexts, without disclosing any orientations or other truth
information. In known S contexts it also samples among true candidates,
namely all K. Thus it verifies the fraction gamma=ell/r of arbitrary
truths in every A context, and additionally supplies ell truths per paired
S context. This additional systematic information is explicitly part of
the experiment. The fixed S reservoir needs no queries. Sampling is
without replacement and independent across contexts given the world.

Put beta=r/K, kappa=1-beta, q=ell/K=beta*gamma,
alpha=(K-r)/(K-ell)=kappa/(1-q). Define posterior group masses

 A0=w*(1-gamma),       M0=m*(2-gamma-q).

The proposed exact conditional robust Mis_infinity frontier over ALL
generators is

 V_ell(c,U)=alpha/2 * [(A0-c)_+ +(A0+M0-c)_+],  c in [0,1].       (1)

The oracle with orientations known but the SAME certified truths has
value alpha*[a*(1-gamma)-c]_+. The expected minimax value is E[V_ell],
where U has the original d-pair occupancy law of C004; the verifier does
not reveal orientations. A matching lower bound also holds for coarser
output bins, but only exact levels are asserted for the attaining upper
bound. The specified uniform-posterior average game has the same
conditional value. All claims below remain unaudited derivations.

## Why the verifier does not label the unknown partition

Under a uniform random r-subset R, sample T uniformly among ell-subsets
of R. Every ell-subset of [K] has probability 1/binom(K,ell), since
binom(K-ell,r-ell)/(binom(K,r)*binom(r,ell))=1/binom(K,ell).
This is the same law as a uniform ell-subset from an S context. Hence
the verifier output has identical likelihood under either orientation.
Conditional on it, the untouched pair orientations remain independent
fair bits under the uniform world prior. Each A support is uniform over
r-subsets containing its certified T. Known tags are unchanged.

Let mu=E[p|tags,T] and s(y)=P(y false|tags,T). For uncertified atoms,

 known A:     mu_A=(r-ell)/(N*r*(K-ell)), s=alpha;
 unknown pair:mu_M=(mu_A+1/(N*K))/2,     s=alpha/2;
 known S:     mu=1/(N*K),               s=0.

Certified atoms have risk zero, and their mu is respectively 1/(Nr),
(1/(Nr)+1/(NK))/2, or 1/(NK). Therefore mu is nonincreasing with
positive false-risk level: mu_A<=mu_M<=1/(NK), while certified-safe
atoms have density at least 1/(NK). Let A be all uncertified atoms of
known A contexts; let M be all uncertified atoms of unknown pairs.
Their mu masses are exactly A0 and M0. All other atoms are safe.

## Unrestricted mixed-bin lower bound

For E=A and E=A union M, each atom inside E has mu-density at most
every atom outside E. For any uniform coarsening Pi, this implies
mu_Pi(E)>=mu(E): in a cell with l inside and h outside atoms, writing
their mu sums L,H, the ordering gives L/l<=H/h if both are nonempty,
so l(L+H)/(l+h)>=L. Empty intersections give equality. Sum cells.

For every generator g its output bins Pi(g) are fixed when worlds are
averaged. By linearity and the coordinatewise triangle inequality,
TV(mu_Pi,g)<=E[TV(p_Pi,g)]. A robust or stated posterior-average
calibration budget therefore implies

 g(A)>=(A0-c)_+,     g(A union M)>=(A0+M0-c)_+.

Expected hallucination is alpha*g(A)+(alpha/2)*g(M), exactly alpha/2
times the sum of these two events. This proves (1)'s lower bound for
every g, even bins that mix verified supports, contexts and risk levels.
Worst-world hallucination dominates the posterior average. No restriction
on the competing generator has been inserted into this argument.

## Worldwise attaining generator

Start from mu. Remove tA=min(c,A0) uniformly from A and
tM=min((c-A0)_+,M0) uniformly from M, taking zero from empty groups.
Add tA+tM uniformly to the N-2d fixed S contexts. Leave certified atoms
and all other contexts unchanged. This is nonnegative, normalized and
has TV(mu,g)=tA+tM<=c.

For a known A context, g is constant across its certified atoms and
across its uncertified atoms separately. Each of those groups has the
same p mass as mu in every compatible support. For each unknown pair,
g is constant on all certified atoms of BOTH siblings, and separately
on all uncertified atoms of both siblings. Their pairwise p masses are
respectively ell*(1/K+1/r)/N and (2-ell/K-ell/r)/N, independent of the
orientation and compatible supports. Known S context fibres are constant.
Consequently every exact g-score cell is a union of these invariant-mass
groups (including any merging levels and zero scores). It follows that
p_Pi=mu_Pi in every compatible world. With g_Pi=g,

 Mis_infinity(g,p)=TV(mu_Pi,g_Pi)<=TV(mu,g)<=c.

In known A uncertified groups a fraction alpha of candidates is false;
in unknown-pair uncertified groups a fraction alpha/2 is false. They
are uniform under g, so in EVERY compatible world

 H=alpha*(A0-tA)+(alpha/2)*(M0-tM)=V_ell(c,U).

There are no false certified atoms. The three budget ranges c<=A0,
A0<=c<=A0+M0, and c>=A0+M0 give (1). Empty groups, ell=r, ell=0,
U=0 and zero output bins are included by the stated conventions.

With orientations known, all uncertified A mass is a*(1-gamma), with
constant false-risk alpha. The same tail lower bound and removal
construction give the oracle claimed above. It is not given any
uncertified arbitrary identities beyond those disclosed by the verifier.

## Minimax expectation and informative budgets

Conditional posterior lower bounds integrate under the uniform prior on
orientations and supports, and the maximum over fixed worlds dominates
this average. The construction has the same H=V_ell(U) for every world
and every compatible verifier output. U's distribution is independent of
worlds and outputs because tags reveal a pair iff a training context
touches it, and the verifier conveys no orientation likelihood. These
facts give matching global expected minimax value E[V_ell(U)] under
conditional robust feasibility, without an unjustified sup/expectation
interchange. Its law is

 E[z^U]=sum_{j=0}^d binom(d,j)*(z-1)^j*(1-2j/N)^n,
 E U=d*(1-2/N)^n.

Put T=a*(1-gamma)-c. The exact excess over the known-partition oracle is

 alpha/2 * [(T-m*(1-gamma))_+
           +(T+m*(1-q))_+ -2*T_+].                    (2)

This is nonnegative: split T at -m*(1-q), 0, and m*(1-gamma), using
q<=gamma in the positive middle range. At c=0 it equals
alpha*kappa*gamma*m/2. At the oracle's zero-hallucination threshold
c=a*(1-gamma), the actual value is

 V_ell = alpha*m*(1-q)/2 = kappa*U/(2N).              (3)

Thus its exact expected value is kappa*d/(2N)*(1-2/N)^n, or kappa/2
times the minimax expected classification error R=d/N*(1-2/N)^n of
fair consistent ERM. The verifier does not change R because its law
does not distinguish orientations. It shifts the critical calibration
budget but the generation learning penalty there stays the same.

At ell=0, (1) reduces to C004. At ell=r, every A truth is certified,
but the verifier does not identify which contexts are A. Formula (1)
then becomes (kappa*U/N-c)_+/2. In particular zero calibration error
still costs kappa*U/(2N) unless the tags determine all orientations.
This contrasts with C006's orientation-disclosing full verifier, which
can yield zero hallucination and calibration error when all pairs are
verified. The source of side information, not merely its fact fraction,
must therefore be stated in a frontier claim.

For n,d>=1 choose N=4*max(n,d). Bernoulli's inequality gives
1/2<= (1-2/N)^n <=1. Thus the exact expected value at the threshold
in (3) lies between (kappa/16)*min(1,d/n) and
(kappa/8)*min(1,d/n). These are matching sample-complexity bounds for
this entire annotated VC family, for every allowed verifier fraction;
they do not extend automatically to an arbitrary VC class.

The version space, verifier sets and group counts admit the same efficient
representation as C004/C006. For rational c, group sampling has expected
polynomial bit complexity, with O(n+d+d*ell) explicit data processing.
The probability bound P(U>0)<=d*(1-2/N)^n also applies; U=0 gives the
oracle frontier simultaneously at every c. No independence between
missing-pair indicators is presumed.

This derivation uses the source exact-level Mis_infinity (Kalai--Vempala
2311.14648v3, Definitions 1--2, pp.8--9) and standard finite TV/event
inequalities. No novelty is asserted for those inequalities, occupancy,
or uniform-subset counting. The proposed new result is the stated
explicit partial-truth-verifier frontier. Exact Fraction checks passed:
886 unrestricted-generator/bin checks, 1982 attaining-world checks,
23 posterior experiments, 288 VC-rate scaling checks, and an unequal-
coverage negative control. Source/priority comparison and independent

and let $A\subseteq[0,\infty)^n$ be Borel. If $q\in[0,1]$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\left( \bigotimes_{i=1}^nQ_{\theta_i} \right)(A) \geq q
\end{equation}
for $(\eta_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\eta_n)$-almost every $(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)$, then
$$
\left( \bigotimes_{i=1}^n\nu_i \right)(A) \geq q.
$$

body:
[Thm matrix-sharpness of arXiv:2608.29018, 'Sharp Restricted Isometry Thresholds for\\ Global Minima of Rank-Restricted Matrix LASSO'] Fix integers $r_{\star}\ge1$ and $k\ge2$.
Set $t\coloneqq k/r_{\star}$ and
\begin{equation}
\mathsf{C}(t)\coloneqq1+\frac{(3t-4)_{+}}{2-t+\sqrt{t(t-1)_{+}}}.
\end{equation}
If $\delta\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sharp}}(t)+1/r_{\star}$, then:
\begin{itemize}
\item (Matrix) There exist adversarial data $(X_{\star},\mathcal{A},b)$ satisfying
\[
\operatorname{rank}(X_{\star})=r_{\star},\quad\mathcal{A}\in\operatorname{RIP}(\delta,k),\quad b=\mathcal{A}(X_{\star}),
\]
such that every global minimizer $X_{\lambda,r}$ in ((eq:matrix-lasso of the paper))
satisfies 
\begin{equation}
\lambda>0,\;r\ge\mathsf{C}(t)r_{\star}\implies\normF{X_{\lambda,r}-X_{\star}}\ge\normF{X_{\star}}.
\end{equation}
\item (Vector) There exist adversarial data $(x_{\star},A,b)$ satisfying
\[
\normzero{x_{\star}}=r_{\star},\quad A\in\operatorname{rip}(\delta,k),\quad b=Ax_{\star},
\]
such that every global minimizer $x_{\lambda,r}$ in ((eq:vector-lasso of the paper))
satisfies 
\begin{equation}
\lambda>0,\;r\ge\mathsf{C}(t)r_{\star}\implies\normtwo{x_{\lambda,r}-x_{\star}}\ge\normtwo{x_{\star}}.
\end{equation}
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm matrix-sharpness of arXiv:2608.29018

[Proposition 95 (Exterior degree is not primitive ancestry) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $V$ be a complex vector space with $\dim V\ge j$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Hom}_{GL(V)}(\Lambda^jV,L_j(V))=0,
 \qquad j\ge3.
 
\end{equation}
Equivalently, in stable dimension there is no nonzero homogeneous linear
natural transformation from the degree-$j$ fermionic sector to the
degree-$j$ free-Lie sector.  The coincidence $L_2(V)=\Lambda^2V$ is therefore
exceptional: exterior particle number is a covariance-reader degree, not a
second model of the Rees ancestry filtration.

body: [Definition of arXiv:2608.30346, '\textbf{Classification complexity of homeomorphism group actions}'] Let \(G\) be a Polish group acting continuously on a Polish space \(X\). For \(x \in X\), \(U \subset X\) open with \(x \in U\) and \(V \subset G\) open with \(1_G \in V\), the \textit{local \(U \text{-} V\)-orbit of} \(x\), denoted \(\mathcal{O}(x,U,V)\), is the set of \(y \in U\) for which there exist \(l \in \mathbb{N}\), \(x = x_1\in U, x_2\in U, \dots x_l = y \in U\) and \(g_1, \dots ,g_{l-1} \in V\) such that \(x_{i+1} = g_i \cdot x_i\) for \(i < l\).

[Theorem 10 (Explicit solution with $q$-drift and source term) of arXiv:2604.02998, 'Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Differential Games for Controlled Convection-Diffusion SPDEs'] The BSPDE defined in \eqref{BSPDE-main-f} admits a unique adapted classical solution satisfies
\begin{equation}
u(t,x)
=
\mathbb E^{\mathbb Q}
\Bigg[
e^{c(T-t)} g(X_T^{t,x})
+
\int_t^T
e^{c(s-t)} f(s,X_s^{t,x})
\, ds
\;\Bigg|\; \mathcal F_t
\Bigg],
\end{equation}
where under $\mathbb Q$ the forward diffusion SDE  solves
\[
dX_s
=
-(b_0+\sigma\gamma)\,ds
+
\sigma\, dW_s^{\mathbb Q},
\qquad X_t=x,
\]
with $dW_s^{\mathbb Q}=dW_s+\gamma ds.$
In particular, the solution of the forward can be written explicitly as
\[
X_T=x-(b_0+\sigma\gamma)(T-t)+
\sigma\big(W_T^{\mathbb Q}-W_t^{\mathbb Q}\big).
\]

Moreover, the associated martingale term satisfies
\begin{equation}
q(t,x)=\sigma\,u_x(t,x).    
\end{equation}

[Lemma 38 of arXiv:2605.16868, '\ttl'] \begin{itemize} 
    \item []
\item  [(i)]
If $x \in \mathcal{D}_T^\uparrow(L_1)$, then $\pi(x) \in \mathcal{D}_T^\uparrow(L_1)$.

\item [(ii)]
 If $x \le y$ in $\mathcal{D}_T^\uparrow(L_1)$, then $\pi(x) \le \pi(y)$ in $\mathcal{D}_T^\uparrow(L_1)$.
    
\item [(iii)]
If $x^n \uparrow x$ in $\mathcal{D}_T^\uparrow(L_1)$, then $\pi(x^n) \uparrow \pi(x)$ in $\mathcal{D}_T^\uparrow(L_1)$. 
\end{itemize}

[Definition def:random_length_worms_model of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Let us consider a probability mass function $\eta: \mathbb{N}_{>0} \to [0,1] $ and an $\mathbb{N}_{>0}$-valued random variable $\mathcal{L}$ satisfying $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{L}=\ell)=\eta(\ell), \, \ell \in \mathbb{N}_{>0}$. 
	We call the distribution of $\mathcal{L}$ the length distribution of the worms. Let us also consider a nearest neighbour simple random walk $(X(t))_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ on the vertices of $G$ starting from $X(0)=o$, independent of $\mathcal{L}$.
	Let us define the probability measure $\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}$ on $\mathcal{H}_{o}$ by 
	\begin{equation}
		
		\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}(H) := P_{o}( \{ X(0), X(1), \ldots, X(\mathcal{L} - 1) \} = H )
	\end{equation}
	for each $H \in \mathcal{H}_{o}$.
	Given any $\lambda >0$, the Poisson zoo $\mathcal{N}_{\eta}^{\lambda} := \mathcal{N}_{\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}}^{\lambda}$ built upon this measure via Definition (def:poisson_zoo of the paper) is called the random length worms model at level $\lambda$, and the corresponding random set $\mathcal{S}_{\eta}^\lambda := \mathcal{S}_{\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}}^\lambda$ is the random length worms set at level $\lambda$.
title: Definition def:random_length_worms_model of arXiv:2505.07145

[Prop 11 ($p$-Powers of Derivations on Curves) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $K$ be a generic point of a curve with a coordinate $x$. 
    Let $f\in K$. We define a derivation on $K$ by
    \[
    D=f\frac{\partial}{\partial x}
    \]
    Then, its $p$-power is given by 
    \[
    D^{\circ p}=-b_{p-1} D
    \]
    where $b_{p-1}\in K^p$ is the unique coefficient in the expansion in the $p$-basis $\frac{x^{j}}{(j)!}$ for $0\le j<p$
    \[
    f^{p-1}=b_0+b_1\frac{x}{1!}+\ldots +b_{p-1}\frac{x^{p-1}}{(p-1)!},
    \]
    where $b_i\in K^p$.
title: $p$-Powers of Derivations on Curves

[Thm 25 of arXiv:2608.30380, 'Morita Induction and Geometric Ideals in $\ell^p$ Roe-Type Algebras'] Let $X$ be a metric space with bounded geometry and $1\leq p<\infty$.  The Morita equivalence of \cite{Chung2025} induces an order isomorphism
\[
 \mathcal G\bigl(B_u^p(X);\C_u[X]\bigr)
 \xrightarrow{\cong}
 \mathcal G\bigl(UB^p(X);U\C^p[X]\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, a closed ideal $I\triangleleft B_u^p(X)$ is geometric if and only if the induced ideal $\Ind_{B_u^p(X)}^{UB^p(X)}(I)$ is geometric.

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] With the notation above, the normalized energy is nonincreasing and satisfies
\begin{equation}
  e^{-2t}E_{u_0}(X_t)
  \searrow
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  \qquad
  \text{as }t\to\infty.
  
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{t\to\infty}
  \frac{E_{u_0}(X_t)}{e^{2t}}
  =
  \mathscr V_q(Y),
  \qquad
  E_{u_0}(X_t)
  =
  \mathscr V_q(Y)e^{2t}
  +
  o(e^{2t}).
  
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\(
  0<\mathscr V_q(Y)<\infty.
\)

If \(q\) is Jenkins--Strebel and its vertical foliation is the contracting
foliation of the ray, let
\(
  C_1,\ldots,C_r
\)
be its maximal flat cylinders. Write
\(
  C_i
  \cong
  (0,h_i)\times
  \bigl(\mathbb R/c_i\mathbb Z\bigr),
\)
where the closed vertical trajectories have \(q\)-length \(c_i\), the
transverse height is \(h_i\), and \(\delta_i\) is the core curve of \(C_i\).
Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \operatorname{Mod}(C_i)\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \frac{h_i}{c_i}\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2.
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{t\to\infty}
  \frac{E_{u_0}(X_t)}{e^{2t}}
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \operatorname{Mod}(C_i)\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2.
  
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.30752

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); T232-w704-C014 v1. No independent PASS or established novelty/priority. Let m>=2,w>=2 be finite, M a real m-by-2 matrix of rank two, and Sigma a real symmetric positive definite 2-by-2 matrix. Suppose M Sigma has distinct singular values s1>s2>0. For gradient flow B'=-(BA-M)Sigma A^T, A'=-B^T(BA-M)Sigma, form U=(B;A^T) and D=[[0,M Sigma],[Sigma M^T,0]]. Let v1,v2 be positive unit eigenvectors of D. Fix a finite seed U0 with c1=||v1^T U0||>0 and one hidden orthogonal rotation R with v1^T U0 R=(c1,0,...,0). Split U0 R=[z0,X0] and assume c2=v2^T X0 is nonzero. Start at alpha U0 R, let tau=log(1/alpha)/s1, epsilon=alpha^(1-s2/s1), and write U_alpha(t+tau)=[z_alpha(t),X_alpha(t)]. On every fixed shifted compact, z_alpha converges to zbar and X_alpha/epsilon converges to chi c2. With H(P)=[[0,P Sigma],[Sigma P^T,0]], these are the unique weighted-bounded canonical Volterra solutions zbar=c1 exp(s1 t)v1-integral_-infinity^t exp(D(t-u))H(bbar abar^T)zbar du and chi=exp(s2 t)v2-integral_-infinity^t exp(D(t-u))H(bbar abar^T)chi du, where zbar=(bbar;abar). Their backward remainders are O(exp(3s1 t)) and O(exp((2s1+s2)t)), respectively; they extend to every finite time. If Pi projects onto col(M)^perp, then ||Pi B_alpha(physical time)||_F<=alpha||Pi B0||_F for all forward times, and ||Pi (X_alpha)_b/epsilon||_F<=alpha^(s2/s1)||Pi B0||_F. Thus bbar and chi_b belong to col(M), and their ideal equations reduce isometrically to the square target Q^T M for any orthonormal basis Q of col(M). The nondegeneracy assumptions hold almost surely for one fixed iid standard Gaussian seed, then scaled by alpha. This is fixed-compact origin matching, not a full Gaussian saddle passage or an entire normalized-error rate.

Sigma symmetric positive definite
rank M=2
s1>s2>0 singular values of M Sigma
fixed finite seed, nonzero top row and nonzero orthogonal second row
