body:
[Lemma 6 (The reduced-Palm product) of arXiv:2608.20101, '\bfseries Largest bulk gap of the complex Ginibre ensemble'] For the infinite Ginibre process of intensity \(1/\pi\),
\[
 \Pp\{\xi_\infty^{0,!}(D_r)=0\}
 =\det(I-\one_{D_r}K_\infty^0\one_{D_r})
 =\prod_{k=2}^{\infty}Q(k,r^2)=q(r).
\]
The product converges locally uniformly, and \(q\) is continuous and
strictly decreasing from \(1\) to \(0\).
If \(H(r)=\Pp\{\xi_\infty(D_r)=0\}\), then
\begin{equation}
 q(r)=e^{r^2}H(r).
\end{equation}
This identity is also recorded in
\cite[Remark~3.1(1)]{ByunForrester}.

[Lem 161 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $1 \leq \ell\leq \ubl$ we have:
  \begin{align}
  
  \bbE[\hat U^{\ell}-\hat U^{\ell-1}
  \,|\,
  \cF^{\hat U,\tilde U}(\ell-1)]
  &=0\,,
  \\
  
  \bbE[\hat Y^{\ell}-\hat Y^{\ell-1}
  ~|~
  \cF^{\hat Y,\tilde Y,\hat{\prxY},\tilde{\prxY}}(\ell-1)]
  =
  \bbE[\hat Y^{\ell}-\hat Y^{\ell-1}
  ~|~
  \cF^{\hat U,\tilde U}(\ell-1)]
  &=
  0\,,
  \\
  
  \bbE[\hat V^{\ell}-\hat V^{\ell-1}
  ~|~
  \cF^{\hat V,\tilde V}(\ell-1)]
  &=0\,,
  \\
  
  \bbE[\hat M^{\ell}-\hat M^{\ell-1}
  ~|~
  \cF^{\hat M,\tilde M}(\ell-1)]
  =
  \bbE[\hat M^{\ell}-\hat M^{\ell-1}
  ~|~
  \cF^{\hat V,\tilde V}(\ell-1)]
  &=
  0
  \,.
  \end{align}

\begin{proof}
  We will show inductively that
  \eqref{eq:pair-u-increments-orthogonal} implies
  \eqref{eq:pair-y-increments-orthogonal}, which implies
  \eqref{eq:pair-v-increments-orthogonal}, which implies
  \eqref{eq:pair-m-increments-orthogonal}, which implies
  \eqref{eq:pair-u-increments-orthogonal} with $\ell+1$ in place of $\ell$.
We therefore proceed with the inductive argument: 

\begin{itemize}
\item \eqref{eq:pair-u-increments-orthogonal} $\Rightarrow$
  \eqref{eq:pair-y-increments-orthogonal}: 
for this we use
the recursion \eqref{e:state.evol.x.y.increments.CHAOTIC}. Note that $w^{\ell-1}(\hat{\prxY}^{\ell-1})$ is measurable with respect to the $\sigma$-field $\cF^{\hat Y,\tilde Y,\hat{\prxY},\tilde{\prxY}}(\ell-1)$, which in turn is contained in the $\sigma$-field 
$\cF^{\hat U,\tilde U}(\ell-1)$. Therefore
  \[
  \bbE[\hat Y^{\ell}-\hat Y^{\ell-1}
    ~|~
    \cF^{\hat U,\tilde U}(\ell-1)]
  = \frac{w^{\ell-1}(\hat{R}^\eta\hat{\prxY}^{\ell-1}) }
    {\hat{\gamma}(\ell,\delta,\eta)}
  \E[\hat{U}^\ell-\hat{U}^{\ell-1}
  ~|~ \cF^{\hat U,\tilde U}(\ell-1)
  ]=0\,,
  \]
where the last step is by the inductive hypothesis \eqref{eq:pair-u-increments-orthogonal}. This implies
\eqref{eq:pair-y-increments-orthogonal}.

\item \eqref{eq:pair-y-increments-orthogonal} $\Rightarrow$ \eqref{eq:pair-v-increments-orthogonal}:
it follows from the state evolution definition that the random variables $\hat{V}^{\ell,k}$ and $\tilde{V}^{\ell,k}$ are jointly gaussian. Using the covariance formula \eqref{eq:state-evolution-setup}, for $0\le k\le s \le \ell-1$ we have
  \begin{align*}
  \E[(\hat{V}^{\ell,k}-\hat{V}^{\ell-1,k})
  \tilde{V}^{s,k}]
  &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:state-evolution-setup}}{=} \E\bigg[
   \Big(h_{\chaos,\ell,k}(\hat{U}[[\ell]])-
  h_{\chaos,\ell-1,k}
  (\hat{U}[[\ell-1]])
  \Big)
    h_{\chaos,s,k}
    (\tilde{U}[[s]])
    \bigg]\\
  &\stackrel{
  \eqref{e:f.h.l.k.explicit.CHAOTIC}
  }{=} (a_k)^2
  \E[(\hat{Y}^\ell-\hat{Y}^{\ell-1})
    \tilde{Y}^s]
  = 0\,,
  \end{align*}
where the last step is by the inductive hypothesis \eqref{eq:pair-y-increments-orthogonal}. A similar calculation gives the same identity but with $\hat{V}^{s,k}$ in place of $\tilde{V}^{s,k}$. Since the $V$ are jointly gaussian, this implies \eqref{eq:pair-v-increments-orthogonal}.

\item \eqref{eq:pair-v-increments-orthogonal} $\Rightarrow$ \eqref{eq:pair-m-increments-orthogonal}: this follows from the recursion \eqref{e:state.evol.x.y.increments.CHAOTIC}, by the same reasoning as for \eqref{eq:pair-u-increments-orthogonal} $\Rightarrow$ \eqref{eq:pair-y-increments-orthogonal} above.

\item
\eqref{eq:pair-m-increments-orthogonal}
$\Rightarrow$
\eqref{eq:pair-u-increments-orthogonal}:
this follows by similar reasoning as for
\eqref{eq:pair-y-increments-orthogonal}
$\Rightarrow$
\eqref{eq:pair-v-increments-orthogonal} above.
\end{itemize}
The above steps give one complete round of the induction, and the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

They have since become fundamental concepts in many branches of mathematics and physics, such as string theory, Chern–Simons theory, knot theory, and Gromov–Witten invariants. [Corollary 15 (A sufficient deletion-chord curvature bound) of arXiv:2608.30261, 'Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample'] \label[corollary]{cor:cpp-bound}
Fix $\kappa\in[0,\infty)$.
For every $i\in[n]$, $0\leq\alpha_0\leq(n-1)^{-1}$, and
$P=P_n+\alpha_0 h_i\in\mathfrak P_S$ with $h_i\ne0$, define the
sample-dependent realized normalized deletion direction
$\widetilde h_i:=h_i/\|h_i\|_{\TV}\in\mathcal M_0$.  For every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and
$t\in[0,T]$, suppose there is an interval containing zero on which the flows
trained under $P+\alpha\widetilde h_i$ exist, the map
$\alpha\mapsto\theta_t^{P+\alpha\widetilde h_i,\lambda}$ is twice
continuously differentiable, and the first and second $\alpha$-derivatives of
$\theta_t^{P+\alpha\widetilde h_i,\lambda}$ commute with the time derivative
and may be passed through the training and population-risk integrals.  Suppose
there are
$G_h,H_h,J_3,G_0,H_0\in[0,\infty)$, possibly depending on the realized sample
$S$, such that, uniformly over
$i\in[n]$ with $h_i\ne0$, $\alpha_0\in[0,(n-1)^{-1}]$, $\lambda\in\Lambda$, and
$t\in[0,T]$,
\[
\begin{gathered}
 \left\|\int\nabla\ell^{\rm tr}_{\lambda,z}(\theta_t^{P,\lambda})
          \,\dd\widetilde h_i(z)\right\|\leq G_h,\quad
 \left\|\int\nabla^2\ell^{\rm tr}_{\lambda,z}(\theta_t^{P,\lambda})
          \,\dd\widetilde h_i(z)\right\|_{\op}\leq H_h,\\
 \|\nabla_\theta^3F_{P,\lambda}(\theta_t^{P,\lambda})\|_{\op}\leq J_3,
 \quad \nabla^2F_{P,\lambda}(\theta_t^{P,\lambda})\succeq-\kappa I,\\
 \|P_0\nabla\ell^{\rm ev}_{\lambda,Z}(\theta_t^{P,\lambda})\|
 \leq G_0,\quad
 \|P_0\nabla^2\ell^{\rm ev}_{\lambda,Z}(\theta_t^{P,\lambda})\|_{\op}
 \leq H_0.
\end{gathered}
\]
The averaged first-order cancellation condition
\eqref{eq:average-first-order-cancellation} holds, and the curvature condition
\eqref{eq:measure-curvature-bound} holds with
\begin{equation}
 C_{PP}=H_0G_h^2\phi_\kappa(T)^2
 +G_0\{2H_hG_h\chi_\kappa(T)+J_3G_h^2\mathcal J_\kappa(T)\}.
\end{equation}
If $h_i=0$, then $P_n+\alpha_0 h_i=P_n$ for every
$0\leq\alpha_0\leq(n-1)^{-1}$.  Consequently, the scalar chord map
$\alpha_0\mapsto\psi_{i,t,\lambda}(\alpha_0)$ in
\eqref{eq:deletion-chord-functional} is constant, so
$\psi_{i,t,\lambda}''(\alpha_0)=0$.

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2512.01483, 'Scaling Limits of Line Models in Degenerate Environment'] Let $(\xi(t))_{t \geq 0}$ be a one-dimensional, simple random walk with generator given by
    \begin{equation}
 
\mathcal{L} f(x) = f(x+1) - 2 f(x) + f(x-1), \qquad x \in \mathbb{Z}, 
\end{equation}
for all $f: \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$. Let, for all $T>0$,
    \[\ell^{\xi,T}_t(x) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}} \int_0^{Tt} \mathbf{1}_{\{\xi(s) = \lfloor \sqrt{T} x \rfloor \}} \, ds, \qquad  t \geq 0, \quad x \in \mathbb{R},\]
    and let $(\tilde{\ell}^{T}_t(x))_{x \in \mathbb{R}, t \geq 0}$ be the continuous version, obtained by a linear interpolation in space
    \[\tilde{\ell}^{\xi, T}_t(x) = \left(\lceil \sqrt{T} x \rceil - \sqrt{T} x\right)\ell^{\xi,T}_t(x) + \left(\sqrt{T} x - \lfloor \sqrt{T} x \rfloor \right) \ell^{\xi, T}_t(x+1),  \qquad t \geq 0,
    \quad x \in \mathbb{R},\]
    where $\lfloor x \rfloor$ designates the integer part of $x$, and $\lceil x \rceil := \lfloor x \rfloor + 1$.
    Then, we have the joint convergences in law 
    \[ \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}} \xi(Tt) \right)_{t \geq 0} \Longrightarrow (B_t)_{t \geq 0} \qquad \hbox{in} \quad D  \]
     for the Skorohod topology and 
    \[(\tilde{\ell}^{\xi,T}_t(x))_{x \in \mathbb{R}, t \geq 0} \Longrightarrow  (L^B(t,x))_{x \in \mathbb{R}, t \geq 0} \qquad \hbox{in} \quad C([0,\infty) \times \mathbb{R}) \]
    for the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. Here $(B_t)_{t \geq 0}$ is a Brownian motion started from $0$ with diffusion coefficient $\sqrt{2}$ and $(L^B(t,x))_{x \in \mathbb{R}, t \geq 0}$ is its family of local times.

[Proposition 38 (A confluence-safe residue determinant in one variable) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let
\[
 g(x)=a_\mu x^\mu+a_{\mu-1}x^{\mu-1}+\cdots+a_0,
 \qquad a_\mu\neq0,
\]
and define the global residue functional on \(\C[x]/(g)\) by
\[
 \operatorname{Res}_g(f)
 =
 -\operatorname{Res}_{x=\infty}\frac{f(x)\,\mathrm d x}{g(x)}.
\]
In the basis \(1,x,\ldots,x^{\mu-1}\), the residue Gram matrix
\[
 R_g=
 \bigl(\operatorname{Res}_g(x^{i+j})\bigr)_{0\leq i,j<\mu}
\]
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \det R_g
 =
 (-1)^{\mu(\mu-1)/2}a_\mu^{-\mu}.
 
\end{equation}
Thus this residue pairing remains nondegenerate when critical points
coalesce; it can lose rank only when the leading coefficient vanishes.

For \(P=H_3\), take
\[
 g_t(x)=x-itH_3'(x)
 =-3itx^2+x+3it.
\]
In the basis \(1,x\),
\begin{equation}
 R_{g_t}
 =
 \begin{pmatrix}
  0&i/(3t)\\
  i/(3t)&1/(9t^2)
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \det R_{g_t}=\frac1{9t^2}.
 
\end{equation}
In particular the residue pairing stays nondegenerate at the finite
confluence points \(1-36t^2=0\); its only rank boundary in this family is
\(t=0\).

There is an $L_2$ such that for all $L \ge L_2$,
if $b(m) \le 4$ and $mL \le 1$ then
\begin{equation}

\square ^{(m)}_p \lesssim L^{-d+1} \le \frac 1 {100},
\end{equation}
and, for any $a \in [ 0, \frac{ d-4} 2 )$ there is a constant $K_a$ independent of $L$ such that
\begin{align} 
\sum_{x\in \mathbb{Z}^d} \abs x^a  \abs{\Pi_p ^{(m)}(x)}   \le K_a .
\end{align}
Moreover, if $b(m)\le 4$
uniformly in
$m<m(p)$

where $M > 0$ is a constant independent of $k$, $\eta$, $B$, and $\rho$.

[Lemma 17 (Poisson kernels away from their angular cell) of arXiv:2609.01116, 'Vector-Carleson, Calder\'on, and Poisson--Atomic Criteria for\\ Generalized Hilbert Operat'] Partition $\T$ into $N\ge2$ half-open arcs $I_0,\ldots,I_{N-1}$ of
equal normalized length $1/N$.  For each $a\in\D\setminus\{0\}$ mark
the cell containing $a/|a|$ and its two circular neighbors.  If $I$ is
unmarked for each of $a_1,\ldots,a_K$, then, for nonnegative $c_\nu$,
\[
 \sup_I\sum_{\nu=1}^Kc_\nu P_{a_\nu}
 \le C\inf_I\sum_{\nu=1}^Kc_\nu P_{a_\nu},
 \tag{6.1}
\]
where $C$ is absolute.  Kernels with $a_\nu=0$ may be included without
marking any cell. Consequently, if $0<\beta\le1$ and
$Q=\sum_\nu c_\nu P_{a_\nu}$, then
\[
 \sup_I Q^\beta\le C N\int_IQ^\beta\,dm.
 \tag{6.2}
\]

    A_{n,k}:\Delta^{=}_{n,k}\times\Omega_n
\to
    \mathcal S_{n,k}
\]
such that
\[
    A_{n,k}(x,\cdot)\sim\mu_x
\qquad
    \text{for every }x\in\Delta^{=}_{n,k},
\]
and
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb E_\omega\left[\left|A_{n,k}(x,\omega)\triangle A_{n,k}(y,\omega)\right|\right]
\le
    16\|x-y\|_1
\qquad
    \text{for every }x,y\in\Delta^{=}_{n,k}.

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:RGP-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le m}
  \sum_{r \le a_i} \sum_{r' \le a_j}
   \psi_{t, r, n_i}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').
\]
This identifies $K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ with the
kernel~(equation eq:K-def of the paper) on the product graph
$\mathcal{G}^m$, with $\psi, \phi$ as the seed data and
$B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ as the propagator.

    \(\exists C_1\geq 0\), \(\forall \alpha\), \(\forall \xi_0\in \Compact\), \(\forall \xi\in \BV{\xi_0}{\delta_0}\),

[Proposition 28 (Sectorial stability at the irregular boundary) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Assume the hypotheses of
\cref{thm:ramified-Brieskorn-lattice}, with \(G\) Morse and with distinct
critical values.  Let \(K\) be a closed angular subsector whose directions
remain a positive distance from the finitely many principal rays
\[
 \Im\!\left(
  \frac{G(c_\alpha)-G(c_\beta)}{s^2}
 \right)=0,
 \qquad \alpha\neq\beta,
\]
viewed as equations for \(\arg s\).  For \(|s|\) sufficiently small, the
cycle-coordinate matrix of every sectorially continued contour is constant
on \(K\).  Its two lateral values across an actual Stokes wall satisfy
\[
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^+
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^-S_{\mathrm{top}}^{-1}.
\]
For a real polynomial, in a sector anchored at \(s>0\) by the oriented
Gaussian contour \(\R^d\), let
\(c_0(s)=O(s^{m-1})\) be the critical branch issuing from the
point \(u=0\) of \(G\).  Its local Morse group occurs with
intersection multiplicity of absolute value one.  After orienting the dual
ascending thimble by the normalisation
\eqref{eq:dual-thimble-normalisation}, this coefficient is \(+1\).  Thus
the ordinary Gaussian contribution is the origin branch; all
other coordinates are sectorial Stokes data.

[Defn of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] A measure $\mu$ on a measure space $(X,{\mathcal F})$ is said to be \textbf{invariant} for a group action $G$ on $X$, if for all $A\in {\mathcal F}$ and all $g\in G, \,\mu(A) = \mu(gA)$.

The measure $\mu$ is said to be \textbf{quasi-invariant}, if $\mu$ and $g_{\ast}\mu$ are in the same measure class for all $g\in G$, i.e. if they are mutually absolutely continuous.

A quasi-invariant measure is called \textbf{ergodic} with respect to the action of $G$, if for all invariant sets $A\in {\mathcal F}$, i.e.\ sets $A$ with $$\mu(A \backslash gA) + \mu(gA \backslash A) =0 \,\,\  \forall \, g\in G,$$  either $\mu(A)=0$ or $\mu(A^c)=0$.
title: Unnumbered defn of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'

body:
[Theorem thm:regularity-SRBM of arXiv:2607.03639, '\vspace{-0.6in}An AI-Assisted Solution to the Signed BAR Conjecture: Uniqueness in the Har'] Under the standing assumptions (equation eq:Mmatrix of the paper)--(equation eq:stability of the paper), the
following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For each $x\in E$ and each prescribed Brownian motion there is a pathwise
unique SRBM $Z^x$, and $Z^x$ is strong Markov.

\item The semigroup $(P_t)$ maps $C_0(E)$ into itself and is strongly continuous
there.

\item There is a constant $K_\Gamma<\infty$, depending only on the normalized
reflection data, such that synchronous solutions satisfy, for all $x,y\in E$ and
$t\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
        \sup_{0\le s\le t}\left\lvert Z_s^x-Z_s^y\right\rvert
        \le K_\Gamma\left\lvert x-y\right\rvert
        \qquad\text{almost surely.}
\end{equation}

\item For every $x\in E$ there is an adapted RCLL derivative process
$\mathsf J_t^x\in\operatorname{Lin}(H_x,\mathbb R^d)$, $t\ge0$.  For each fixed
$w\in G_x$, on an event of probability one the derivative
\[
        \partial_w Z_t^x
        :=
        \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
        \frac{Z_t^{x+\varepsilon w}-Z_t^x}{\varepsilon}
\]
exists for every $t\ge0$.  Moreover, for every fixed $t>0$,
\begin{equation}
        \partial_w Z_t^x
        =
        \mathsf J_t^x[\mathsf L_xw]
        \qquad\text{almost surely.}
\end{equation}

\item For every $x\in E$ and every fixed $u\in H_x$,
\[
        \left\lvert \mathsf J_t^x[u]\right\rvert
        \le
        K_\Gamma\left\lvert u\right\rvert
        \qquad
        \text{for }dt\otimes\mathbb P\text{-almost every }(t,\omega).
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Regularity of SRBM

body:
[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2607.28215, 'Almost stochastic dominance via optimal transport'] If the Borel measurable cost function $c:E\times E \to [0,\infty)$ satisfies the triangle inequality 
\begin{align}
c(x,z) \le c(x,y) + c(y,z)\quad \mbox{ for all } x,y,z \in E,
\end{align}
then we also have the corresponding triangle inequality for $\mathrm{OT}_c$ for arbitrary $E$-valued random variables $X,Y,Z$:
$$
\mathrm{OT}_c(X,Z) \le \mathrm{OT}_c(X,Y) + \mathrm{OT}_c(Y,Z).
$$

body:
[Lemma 51 (Function-indexed martingales of a class-$(\Sigma)$
process~\cite{Nikeghbali2006essay}) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Let $X=N+A$ be of class $(\Sigma)$ and let $f\colon\R_+\to\R$ be Borel and locally bounded.  Then
\begin{equation}
  \int_0^{A_t} f(z)\,\dd z-f(A_t)\,X_t
  \;=\;-\int_0^t f(A_u)\,\dd N_u
\end{equation}
so the left-hand side is a local martingale null at $0$.
Conversely, let $X$ be a nonnegative local submartingale with $X_0=0$ and let $C$ be a continuous adapted nondecreasing process with $C_0=0$ such that $\int_0^{C_t}f(z)\,\dd z-f(C_t)X_t$ is a local martingale for every locally bounded Borel $f$.
Then $X$ is of class $(\Sigma)$ and $C=A$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title:
Function-indexed martingales of a class-$(\Sigma)$
process~\cite{Nikeghbali2006essay}

body:
[Cor of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The $\infty$-category ${\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G$ is stable.
    \begin{proof}
        As the underlying $\infty$-category of a model category, ${\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G$ is complete and cocomplete, with the localization preserving initial and final objects. Thus, ${\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G$ is pointed. Observe now that the $\infty$-categorical suspension functor on ${\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G$ is induced by the suspension functor on the pointset level (e.g.~since the left Quillen bifunctor $\textbf{\textup{Top}}_*\times\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}\to\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ describing the tensoring descends to a functor $\Spc_*\times{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G\to{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G$ preserving colimits in each variable and restricting to the identity on $\{S^0\}\times{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G$, and there is only one such functor). Thus, the claim follows by specializing the previous proposition to the 1-dimensional trivial $G$-representation.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem t:clt_linear_marks of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Consider the family  
$(\tilde\mathcal{P}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}:=  \bigl(\{(x_i,\xi_{i,n})\}_{x_i \in \mathcal{P}_n}\bigr)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$,
$\xi_{i,n}\in\mathbb{R}$,  of real-valued marked point processes sharing the same ground point process $\mathcal{P}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, all satisfying Assumption~(Ass1 of the paper).
Assume that $(\tilde{\mathcal{P}}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ has fast $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing   correlations as in Definition (d.omegahmixing of the paper)(i.family-mixing of the paper) with scores $\xi_{i,n}$ 
satisfying  the $p$-moment condition 
    (equation e:xinpmom of the paper) for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$. 
    Furthermore,  if  
   $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$ satisfies ${\rm Var} \,\mu_{n}^{\xi}(f) =
 \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$,  then as $n \to \infty$, 

 \begin{equation}
({\rm Var} \,\mu_{n}^{\xi}(f) )^{-1/2}\Big( \mu_{n}^{\xi}(f) - \mathbb {E}  \mu_{n}^{\xi}(f) \Big) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z,
\end{equation}
where $Z$ is the standard normal random variable and $\stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow}$ denotes convergence in distribution. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition def:under-backoff of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1/3)$ and
a \emph{send sequence}  
$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$.
The \emph{under-backoff process} $U$
with birth rate~$3\lambda$ and send sequence~$\overline{p}$  
is a 3-tuple $U=(U^A,U^B,U^C)$ of generalised backoff processes with 
send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$0$, 
birth distribution
 $\mathcal{D} =  \mathsf{Po}(\lambda)$
where for each stream $D\in \{A,B,C\}$ 
each bin $k\geq 1$,
and each time $t\geq 0$,
$\overline{\mathbf{arr}}_k^{U^D}(t) = \emptyset$. 
The streams
evolve independently  
except 
that $\mathbf{e}_j^{U^A}(t)$, $\mathbf{e}_j^{U^B}(t)$, and
$\mathbf{e}_j^{U^C}(t)$ are defined as follows for $t>0$ and $j\geq 1$. 
 
\begin{itemize}

\item For $D\in \{A,B\}$, if $s_j^{U^D}(t) = s^{U^A}(t)+ s^{U^B}(t)=1$ then $\mathbf{e}_j^{U^D}(t) = \mathbf{s}_j^{U^D}(t)$. 
Otherwise $\mathbf{e}_j^{U^D}(t) = \emptyset$.

\item If $s_j^{U^C}(t) = s^{U^A}(t)+ s^{U^B}(t) + s^{U^C}(t)=1$ then $\mathbf{e}_j^{U^C}(t) = \mathbf{s}_j^{U^C}(t)$. Otherwise $\mathbf{e}_j^{U^C}(t) = \emptyset$.

 
  
\end{itemize}
title: Definition def:under-backoff of arXiv:2602.21315

Own-work draft; C19 v1 status SKETCH, independent audit pending, no novelty claim; not a certified theorem. Let hidden instance Theta have prior pi independent of all sampler randomness U, including continuous query and output randomness. For each instance, let P_theta be the desired smoothed endpoint, s_theta its subsequent OU scores, and b_theta a fixed jointly measurable estimated field with E_{OU_t(P_theta)}||b_theta-s_theta||^2<=epsilon^2 for every t>=0. Assume b_theta equals one public deterministic reference field c exactly outside a measurable informative set A_theta of time-point pairs. Run a sampler with a uniform query cap Q on c; its adaptive reference queries Z_j^0(U), padded by no-query symbols, are independent of Theta. Write H=Pr{some Z_j^0 in A_Theta} and H_j=Pr{Z_j^0 in A_Theta}. Coupling actual and reference samplers on the same U gives E_Theta TV(R_Theta,R_0)<=H<=sum_j H_j. No product of marginal miss probabilities or conditional independence of actual hits is asserted. If each H_j<=h and the endpoint Bayes radius inf_R E_Theta TV(R,P_Theta)>=beta, average sampling error is at least beta-Qh. Error alpha<beta on every instance therefore requires Q>=(beta-alpha)/h when h>0. For B queries per parallel round this gives only L>=(beta-alpha)/(B h); an independent polynomial-batch-safe round bound needs additional structure. One sufficient L2-only oracle construction uses the exact score on A_theta and c outside, requiring the outside-set score-error energy to be <=epsilon^2 at every OU time. Any gradient, smoothness, or prescribed Lipschitz condition must be checked separately. Exact equality of oracle replies outside A matters: arbitrarily close distinct deterministic real replies still have transcript TV one. The actual well-conditioned family, energy budget, endpoint Bayes radius and small continuous-query hit bound are not supplied. Hence Target 2 and the super-square-root exponent remain open. Finite probability checks illustrate the conditioning pitfall but do not certify this full method.
Measurable fixed instance-specific estimated fields and informative sets
Hidden prior independent of all sampler randomness, including continuous variables
Exact agreement with public reference outside each informative set
Uniform finite query cap applies even on reference reply histories
Uniform absolute-OU error, hit bounds and Bayes radius refer to the same smoothed endpoint
Additional oracle regularity and any parallel batch bound remain separate obligations

[Theorem thm.BRW of arXiv:2411.19145, 'On the intersection of critical percolation clusters and other tree-like random graphs'] Let $(\mathcal R_c^i)_{i\ge 1}$ and $(\mathcal R_\infty^i)_{i\ge 1}$, be independent copies of $\mathcal R_c$ and $\mathcal R_\infty$ respectively, on $\mathbb Z^d$, with $d\ge 5$.

[Lemma generic decoupling of arXiv:2412.07936, 'Simple Norm Bounds for Polynomial Random Matrices via Decoupling'] For natural numbers $n \geq m$, let ${\bf x} = \{x_i\}^n_{i=1}$ be a sequence of $n$ independent random variables in a measurable space $(S, \mathcal S)$, and let $\{x_i^{(k)}\}^n_{i=1}$, $k = 1, \dots, m$, be $m$ independent copies of this sequence. Let $B$ be a separable Banach space, and let $h_{{\bf i}}: S^m \rightarrow B$ be a measurable function such that ${\mathbb E} (\norm{h_{{\bf i}} (x_{i_1}, \dots, x_{i_m})}) \leq \infty $ for each ${\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^m_n$. Let $\Phi: [0, \infty) \rightarrow [0,\infty)$ be a convex nondecreasing function such that ${\mathbb E} \Phi (\norm{h_{{\bf i}} (x_{i_1}, \dots, x_{i_m})}) \leq \infty $ for all ${\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^m_n$. Then, 
$$
{\mathbb E} \Phi \left( \norm{\sum_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^m_n} h_{{\bf i}} (x_{i_1}, \dots, x_{i_m})} \right) \leq {\mathbb E} \Phi \left( C_m\norm{\sum_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^m_n} h_{{\bf i}} (x_{i_1}^{(1)}, \dots, x_{i_m}^{(m)})} \right),
$$
where $C_m = 2^m \cdot (m^m-1) \cdot ((m-1)^{(m-1)} - 1) \cdot \ldots \cdot 3.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Decoupling Inequality, see \cite{PG:book} Theorem 3.1.1

[Theorem thm.fIForParablic of arXiv:2411.05534, 'Inverse problems for stochastic partial differential equations'] Let
\begin{align} 
    b^{j k}=b^{k j} \in L_{\mathbb{F}}^2\left(\Omega ; C^1\left([0, T] ; W^{2, \infty}(G)\right)\right), \quad j, k=1,2, \cdots, n,
\end{align}
$\ell \in C^{1,3}((0,T)\times G)$ and $\Psi \in C^{1,2}((0,T)\times G)$.
Let $ u $ be an $H^2(G)$-valued continuous Itô process.
Set  $\theta=e^{\ell}$ and $w=\theta u$. Then, for any $t \in[0, T]$ and a.e. $(x, \omega) \in G \times \Omega$,
\begin{align}\notag
    & 2 \theta \Big [\!-\!\sum_{j, k=1}^n \big(b^{j k} w_{x_j}\big)_{x_k}+\mathcal{A} w \Big ]\Big[d u\!-\!\sum_{j, k=1}^n\big(b^{j k} u_{x_j}\big)_{x_k} d t\Big]
    \!+\! 2 \sum_{j, k=1}^n\big(b^{j k} w_{x_j} d w\big)_{x_k}
    \\\notag
    &
     \quad+2 \sum_{j, k=1}^n\Big[\sum_{j^{\prime}, k^{\prime}=1}^n\big(2 b^{j k} b^{j^{\prime} k^{\prime}} \ell_{x_{j^{\prime}}} w_{x_j} w_{x_{k^{\prime}}}-b^{j k} b^{j^{\prime} k^{\prime}} \ell_{x_j} w_{x_{j^{\prime}}} w_{x_{k^{\prime}}}\big)
    \\
    &
     \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad  ~ +\Psi b^{j k} w_{x_j} w-b^{j k}\Big(\mathcal{A} \ell_{x_j}+\frac{\Psi_{x_j}}{2}\Big) w^2\Big]_{x_k} d t
    \\\notag
    &
     =2 \sum_{j, k=1}^n c^{j k} w_{x_j} w_{x_k} d t+\mathcal{B} w^2 d t+d\Big(\sum_{j, k=1}^n b^{j k} w_{x_j} w_{x_k}+\mathcal{A} w^2\Big)
     -\theta^2 \mathcal{A}(d u)^2,
    \\ \notag
    &
     +2\Big[-\sum_{j, k=1}^n\big(b^{j k} w_{x_j}\big)_{x_k}+\mathcal{A} w\Big]^2 d t
      -\theta^2 \sum_{j, k=1}^n b^{j k}\big(d u_{x_j}+\ell_{x_j} d u\big)\big(d u_{x_k}+\ell_{x_k} d u\big)
\end{align}
where
\begin{align}
    
    \left\{\begin{aligned}
        & \mathcal{A} \triangleq-\sum_{j, k=1}^n\big(b^{j k} \ell_{x_j} \ell_{x_k}-b_{x_k}^{j k} \ell_{x_j}-b^{j k} \ell_{x_j x_k}\big)-\Psi-\ell_t, \\

[Lemma EI of arXiv:2607.05418, 'On the Group Randomness of 0-1 Real Sequences from Binary Linear Codes'] Let $A,B$ be $p \times n$ real matrices with $\mathrm{rk}(B)=1$ and $p \leq n$. Let $G=AA^T$ and $G'=(A+B)(A+B)^T$ be the Gram matrices of $A$ and $A+B$ respectively. If $\lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_p$ and $\lambda_1' \geq \lambda_2' \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_p'$ are the eigenvalues of $G$ and $G'$ respectively, then for $1 \leq i \leq p$,
    $$\lambda_{i+1} \leq \lambda_i' \leq \lambda_{i-1}$$
    where by convention $\lambda_{p+1}=0$ and $\lambda_0=+\infty$.

[Lemma funCRP of arXiv:2411.06089, '{\Large \bf Averaging principle for semilinear slow-fast rough partial differential equati'] Let $G\in C_{\alpha,0}^2(\mathcal{H};\mathcal{H}^d)$,
and let $(Y,Y^{\prime})\in \mathscr{D}_{S,\mathbf X}^{2\gamma}([0,T];\mathcal{H}_\alpha)$ for each $T>0$ and $\mathbf X=(X,X^2)\in \mathscr{C}^{\gamma}([0,T];\mathbb R^d)$ with $\gamma \in (1/3,1/2]$.
In addition, we also assume that $Y\in \hat{C}^\eta([0,T];\mathcal{H}_{\alpha+2\gamma})$ with $\eta \in [0,1]$
and $Y^\prime \in  \mathcal L^\infty([0,T];\mathcal{H}_{\alpha+2\gamma}^d)$.
Define $(Z_{t},Z_{t}^{\prime})=(G(Y_t),DG(Y_t)\circ Y_t^{\prime})$,
then one has $(Z,Z^\prime)\in \mathscr{D}_{S,\mathbf X}^{2\gamma}([0,T];\mathcal{H}_\alpha^d)$ and the estimation
$$\|Z,Z'\|_{X,2\gamma,\alpha}\leq C(1+|X|_\gamma)^2(1+\|Y_0\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\alpha+2\gamma}}+\|Y\|_{\eta,\alpha+2\gamma}+\|Y^\prime\|_{\infty,\alpha+2\gamma}+\|Y,Y^\prime\|_{X,2\gamma,\alpha})^2,$$
where the constant $C$ depends on the bounds on $G$ and its derivatives, as well as on time $T$, but is uniform over $T\in(0,1]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a finite measure space and let F be a subset of L^1(mu). Then F is relatively weakly compact in L^1(mu) if and only if F is bounded and uniformly integrable. By the Eberlein-Smulian theorem the same condition characterises relative weak SEQUENTIAL compactness, so every bounded uniformly integrable sequence has a subsequence converging weakly in L^1 to some limit in L^1.
mu finite (or sigma-finite with the tightness condition added).
Uniform integrability is the crucial half: boundedness in L^1 alone does NOT give weak compactness - the standard counterexample is an approximate identity, bounded in L^1, with no weakly convergent subsequence because its limit is a Dirac mass and not a function.

[Proposition 1 (Size biasing across the family) of arXiv:2608.13631, 'The classical discrete laws near the mode:\\ complete local expansions for the negative bi'] Let $P_\theta(k)$ denote one of the four laws in this paper, with mean $\mu(\theta)$.  Then
	\begin{equation}
		k\,P_\theta(k)=\mu(\theta)\,P_{\theta^\downarrow}(k-1),
	\end{equation}
	where the size-biased parameter $\theta^\downarrow$ is given by
	\[
	\begin{array}{c|c|c}
		\text{law} & \mu(\theta) & \theta^\downarrow\\ \hline
		\Bin(N,p) & Np & (N-1,p)\\[2pt]
		\Poi(\lambda) & \lambda & \lambda\\[2pt]
		\NB(r,p) & rq/p & (r+1,p)\\[2pt]
		\Hyp(N,K,n) & nK/N & (N-1,K-1,n-1).
	\end{array}
	\]
	The negative binomial is in the failures parametrisation,
	\[
		P(k;r,p)=\binom{k+r-1}{k}p^rq^k .
	\]

$\Omega G_{p,\omega}([a,b],V)$ consists of all maps
\(
\mathbf{X}\in C^{0,p}_\omega\!\left(\Delta_{[a,b]},G^{\lfloor p\rfloor}(V)\right)
\)
that are multiplicative, i.e.
\[
\mathbf{X}_{s,s}=\mathbf{1}

\mathbf{X}_{s,u}=\mathbf{X}_{s,t}\otimes \mathbf{X}_{t,u},
\qquad \text{for all } a\le s\le t\le u\le b.
\]

body:
[Lemma lem:raw-arrays-controlled-compensators-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Assume \(\mathcal G_n^{\mathrm{pre}}\) holds. For 
\(d\in\mathfrak D_{\xi,n}^{\mathrm{osc}},\)
define
\[
D^{\mathrm{pre}}_{\xi,d,n}
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{m_{\xi,d}-1}
\sum_{I\in\mathcal D_\ell^\circ}
\sum_{\substack{J\in\mathcal D_{\ell+1}^\circ\\J\subset I}}
D_{J,n},
\]
and
\[
D^{\mathrm{post}}_{\xi,d,n,L}
=
\sum_{\ell=m_{\xi,d}}^{L-1}
\sum_{I\in\mathcal D_\ell^\circ}
\sum_{\substack{J\in\mathcal D_{\ell+1}^\circ\\J\subset I}}
D_{J,n}.
\]
Then
\[
F^{\mathrm{pre}}_{\xi,d}
=
F^{\mathrm{pre,cap}}_{\xi,d,n}
+
D^{\mathrm{pre}}_{\xi,d,n},
\]
and, for every \(L>m_{\xi,d}\),
\[
F^{\mathrm{post}}_{\xi,d,L}
=
F^{\mathrm{post,cap}}_{\xi,d,n,L}
+
D^{\mathrm{post}}_{\xi,d,n,L}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\lvert D^{\mathrm{pre}}_{\xi,d,n}\rvert
\le
\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{pre}}_{\xi,d,n},
\qquad
\lvert D^{\mathrm{post}}_{\xi,d,n,L}\rvert
\le
\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{post}}_{\xi,d,n,L}.
\]
If the absolute post-bin compensator is finite, then the signed post-bin compensator converges as 
\(L\to\infty,\) 
and the same identity holds for the limiting post-bin arrays.

[Theorem 28 (Derivative estimates through surgery) of arXiv:2608.25971, 'Positive \texorpdfstring{$\tau$}{tau}-bi-Ricci curvature and Mean curvature flow with surg'] Fix an integer $m_0\geq2$ and choose the standard replacement so that
  Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-replacement} holds with parameter $\vartheta_n/2$
  and derivative order $m_0$.  Assume that the first surgery time is not
  earlier than $\tau_nR^2$.  Then there exists $C=C(n,\tau,\alpha,m_0)<\infty$  
  such that every surgically modified flow satisfying the hypotheses of
  Theorem~\ref{thm:surgical-cylindrical-estimates} obeys
  \begin{align}
    |\nabla A|^2
    &\leq
    C(H^4+R^{-4}),
    \\
    |\nabla^2A|^2
    &\leq
    C(H^6+R^{-6})
    
  \end{align}
  for every $t\geq\tau_nR^2$.

  More generally, for every pair of nonnegative integers $a,b$ with
  $2a+b\leq m_0$,
  \begin{equation}
    |\nabla_t^a\nabla^bA|^2
    \leq
    C_{a,b}
    \left(
    H^{4a+2b+2}+R^{-4a-2b-2}
    \right),
  \end{equation}
  where $ C_{a,b}
  =  C_{a,b}(n,\tau,\alpha,m_0,a,b)$.  
  At a surgery time the derivatives are understood one-sidedly.

AUTHOR PROOF; independent audit pending. Let G be any finite undirected forest, o,b any vertices, and A any nonempty vertex set. For independent Bernoulli edge states with arbitrary edge probabilities in [0,1], P(o connects to b)>=P(o connects to A)min_{a in A}P(a connects to b). There is also a deterministic a_star in A such that {o connects to A,a_star connects to b} is contained in {o connects to b,o connects to A} in every configuration. Consequently P(o connects to b,o connects to A)>=min_{a in A}P(o connects to A,a connects to b) holds for any edge-state law. The product inequality's coefficient 1 is sharp. Connection means an open path; overlap of terminals and relays, disconnected forests, and o=b are allowed.

\begin{align*}
&\pi_1 \otimes \pi_2 \Big(\bigcap_{i:a_i=1} \{ HC_i  \text{ is a horizontal cluster for } \phi_1\} \cap \bigcap_{i: a_i =2} \{ HC_i \text{ is a horizontal cluster for } \phi_2 \}\Big) \\ \nonumber &
\qquad \le \exp\Big(- \frac{c \beta_0}{4} \sum_{i=1}^m |\partial_o(HC_i)| \Big),
\end{align*}
where $\partial_o(HC_i)$ is the outer boundary of the horizontal cluster, i.e., the number of dual edges in the horizontal contour that forms its outer boundary, and 
where $c \beta_0$ is as in~(equation eq:exp-suppressed-gradients-condition of the paper).

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), no novelty established. For the equal-weight teacher q_a=(1/3)sum_j N(a E diag(1,3)u_j,I_d), d>=2, and canonical equal-weight identity-covariance mixture-score population DDPM risk R_a(nu) with noisy student means M=a nu, the C06 strict bad branch nu_b(a) has a dimension-uniform local slow-noise tracking property. There exist fixed positive a_cut,r,eta,c such that for any nondecreasing schedule 0<a_k<=a_{k+1}<=a_cut with a_{k+1}-a_k<=eta a_k^7, unit-step GD nu_{k+1}=nu_k-grad_nu R_{a_k}(nu_k), initialized within r a_i^2 of nu_b(a_i), stays within r a_k^2 of nu_b(a_k). If noise is held at a_f<=a_cut eventually, it converges to the strict non-global minimum nu_b(a_f). The capped schedule a_{k+1}=min(a_f,a_k+eta a_k^7) takes at most 1+(a_f-a_i)/(eta a_i^7) changing-noise steps. This is a local high-noise continuation application, not a general tracking novelty, full annealed random-start failure theorem, empirical guarantee or resolution of well-separated K=3 learning. The distinction between noisy-mean and underlying-location GD is explicit: unit noisy-mean GD corresponds to underlying-location step size a^(-2), while this statement uses unit underlying-location steps.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a0c99588640e91190f9fda873e3c781fe1d44cec3a6431156037dab7192f5142","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a0/a0c99588640e91190f9fda873e3c781fe1d44cec3a6431156037dab7192f5142.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:de1724eba3c38a828716f6d349e408c59c49bdd88bc1e6627745242f9ea4a390","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c20","bundle_id":"population.t309-anisotropic-slow-noise-tracking-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and diffusion objectives","draft":"w721/bundle_013.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:gaussian-mixture-ddpm-anisotropic-slow-noise-bad-branch-tracking","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own work draft; T309-w721-C20 v1; proof (unaudited); Target 2 route 12 auxiliary continuation lemma.

# Slow noise changes can track the anisotropic bad branch at sufficiently high noise

This is a local continuation application of C06's bad minimum, not a new general tracking theorem. It fixes the parameterization before changing noise. It does not cover a jump to moderate or low noise, a complete annealing schedule, or general well-separated K=3 learning. No novelty finding is asserted; all analytic inputs remain unaudited.

## Statement

Use the teacher q_a=(1/3)sum_j N(a E diag(1,3)u_j,I_d), d>=2, E^T E=I_2. Parameterize the student's three noisy means as M=a nu, where nu is a d-by-3 matrix of underlying unit-scale locations. Write R_a(nu) for the canonical mixture-score population single-time DDPM excess risk. In particular changing a while holding nu fixed changes the noisy means.

C06 supplies a smooth bad critical branch nu_b(a)=-E diag(1,3)U+O(a^2), up to a fixed label permutation. There are dimension-independent positive a_cut,r,eta,c,C such that the following holds. For any nondecreasing schedule

    0<a_k<=a_{k+1}<=a_cut,
    a_{k+1}-a_k<=eta a_k^7,                     (1)

apply unit-step GD to the underlying locations at the current noise:

    nu_{k+1}=nu_k-grad_nu R_{a_k}(nu_k).         (2)

If ||nu_0-nu_b(a_i)||<=r (a_i)^2, where a_i is the schedule's first value, then

    ||nu_k-nu_b(a_k)||<=r a_k^2                  (3)

at every step. If the schedule eventually holds at a_f<=a_cut, the iterates converge to the strict bad minimum nu_b(a_f). The cutoff a_cut denotes a small fixed high-noise amplitude, not the original unsmoothed noise endpoint.

One explicit admissible schedule is a_{k+1}=min(a_f,a_k+eta a_k^7), followed by holding at a_f. For fixed a_f, its changing-noise phase has at most 1+(a_f-a_i)/(eta a_i^7) steps from initial a_i>0. Thus inverse-polynomial initial amplitudes permit a polynomial-length slow continuation phase. This is conditional on the local initialization in (3), not a complete random-initialization runtime statement.

## 1. Uniform spectral and derivative estimates

Near C06's branch, its bounded-location expansion in orthogonal centroid/shape coordinates is

    R_a=a^2||b||^2
       +a^4[||ZZ^T-D||^2/4-b^T ZZ^T b]+a^6 H_a(b,Z),
    D=E diag(1,9)E^T.

The coordinates (b,Z) are a fixed linear transformation of nu with singular values bounded above and below independently of d. All fixed finite orders of derivatives of H_a are bounded on this fixed neighborhood by C06's finite-span Gaussian argument. The leading order-a^2 term is quadratic, so

    ||D_nu^3 R_a||<=C a^4.                     (4)

The upper Hessian bound is ||D_nu^2 R_a||<=C a^2 there.

At the bad critical point, C06's eliminated-centroid block has order a^2 positive curvature. After eliminating it, the covariance and perpendicular blocks have order a^4 positive curvature, and the angular Schur complement has order a^6 positive curvature, with leading coefficient inherited from H''(pi/3)=603/4. The covariance-angular mixed block is O(a^6); its inverse-normal Schur correction is O(a^8). The centroid mixed block is O(a^6), whose Schur correction is O(a^10). The eliminating triangular coordinate maps and the critical-point chart Jacobian have uniformly bounded norms and inverses. Consequently there exist c_0,C_0>0 such that

    c_0 a^6 I <= D_nu^2 R_a(nu_b(a)) <= C_0 a^2 I. (5)

Here the lower bound includes every free-centroid and perpendicular direction, not just the angular restriction. C06 supplies those normal positivities; no invariant covariance section is assumed.

Choose a sufficiently small fixed r. By (4), Hessian displacement on the Euclidean ball B_a={||nu-nu_b(a)||<=r a^2} is at most C r a^6. Choosing C r<=c_0/2 gives

    c a^6 I <= D_nu^2 R_a(nu) <= C' a^2 I     (6)

throughout B_a. Shrink a_cut so C' a_cut^2<=1. This justifies a shrinking Euclidean convexity ball; an arbitrary fixed-radius ball would not follow from the different curvature scales.

C06's smooth implicit reductions extend to a=0 after division by the specified powers of a. Parity and uniqueness make the branch even in a, and its second derivative is bounded near zero. Therefore

    ||nu_b'(a)||<=C_b a.                       (7)

In particular the O(a^2) branch displacement is not used alone to infer a derivative bound; smoothness, parity and the differentiated implicit equations supply it. All constants above can be chosen independently of d by the same bounded finite-span directional estimates as C06.

## 2. A contraction at fixed noise

Let T_a(nu)=nu-grad R_a(nu). The straight segment from nu_b(a) to any point of B_a stays inside B_a. The fundamental theorem of calculus writes

    T_a(nu)-nu_b(a)=(I-H_avg)(nu-nu_b(a)),

where H_avg is the segment-average Hessian. By (6), it is symmetric with eigenvalues in [c a^6,1]. Hence

    ||T_a(nu)-nu_b(a)||<=(1-c a^6)||nu-nu_b(a)||. (8)

This uses the fixed Euclidean metric in the underlying locations. It is not a flow approximation or a bound obtained by multiplying conditional event probabilities.

## 3. The moving branch

Let h=a_{k+1}-a_k>=0. Shrink eta or a_cut so eta a_cut^6<=1, hence a_{k+1}<=2a_k. By (7),

    ||nu_b(a_{k+1})-nu_b(a_k)||<=2 C_b a_k h.

With e_k=||nu_k-nu_b(a_k)||, (8) yields

    e_{k+1}<=(1-c a_k^6)e_k+2 C_b a_k h.       (9)

Choose eta<=c r/(4 C_b), interpreting the condition as unnecessary if C_b=0. On the boundary e_k<=r a_k^2, equations (1),(9) give

    e_{k+1}<=r a_k^2-c r a_k^8+2 C_b eta a_k^8
             <=r a_k^2-(c r/2)a_k^8
             <=r a_{k+1}^2.

Induction proves (3); it also keeps every update segment in the relevant convexity ball. Once a_k=a_f forever, (8) gives geometric convergence to nu_b(a_f). For the explicit capped schedule, every nonfinal increment is at least eta a_i^7, proving the displayed bound on the number of changing-noise steps.

## 4. Parameter conversion and scope

At fixed a, M=a nu implies grad_nu R_a=a grad_M F_a. Thus physical noisy-mean unit GD is equivalent to

    nu_+=nu-a^(-2)grad_nu R_a,

whereas (2) is equivalent to physical noisy-mean GD with step size a^2 before changing a. Across noise levels this statement uses one persistent nu; it does not hold M fixed and silently relabel it. For original mixture means R E A u_j with fixed R, write original student locations Theta=R nu and use OU factor exp(-t)=a/R. Unit GD on nu is GD on Theta with step size R^2; any different learning rate must be converted explicitly.

C19's fixed-noise physical-GD trajectory converges on its bad event and therefore eventually enters the local ball needed here. However no polynomial bound for that preliminary waiting time is supplied by C19, and the change of learning rate must be specified before composing those algorithms. Accordingly this lemma does not claim a polynomial-time random-start failure theorem for a full schedule.

The substantive conclusion is limited: sufficiently slow noise reduction does not force escape while a stays inside this small-amplitude range. What happens when a approaches order one remains unpaid. The next step is an explicit stability or bifurcation certificate for the bad branch outside the local a->0 regime, or a scheduled escape proof that uses that change.

## Checks

Exact checks cover the learning-rate chain rule, the a^8 contraction/branch-drift balance, and the rational constants in the induction. They do not certify the analytic Schur bounds, third-derivative domination, branch regularity or independent validity of C06. Rung: proof (unaudited). [Lemma lem:many-degree-one-right-vertices of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Work under the assumptions and notation of Proposition~(prop:average-degree-bridge-alternatives of the paper). Let $\Omega_k\subseteq J^{(k)}$ be uniform of size $r(k)$, and let $\delta_k\downarrow0$ satisfy
\[
\delta_k \frac{n_k}{k}\to\infty,
\qquad
\delta_k^2k\to\infty.
\]
If $|B_1^{(k)}|\ge\delta_k n_k$, then with probability $1-o(1)$, the graph $G^{(k)}[\Omega_k]$ contains distinct degree-one right vertices $j,j'$ with the same unique left neighbor.

[Lemma Regularity of the area functional of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] For $\theta_0\in [0,2\pi)$, let us denote by $\square(c,\theta_0)$ the eventually broken flow rectangle 
\[ \{ x\in \mathcal{S}: \theta(x)\in [0,\theta_0], f(x)\leqslant c    \} .\]
Then for all interval $I_i$, the map
\begin{align*}
\theta\in I_i\mapsto \int_{\square(r,\theta)  } \sigma    
\end{align*}
belongs to $W^{1,p}(I_i)$ for all $p\in \mathbb{N}$ and is $C^\infty$ in the interior of $I_i$. 
\EN{Is $r$ here fixed or what ? I feel we need a similar result in $(r,\theta)$ to be able to bound the integral
\[\int_{[\min(f),\max(f)]^2\times I^2} \frac{ \left(\int_{\square(r_1,r_2,\theta_1,\theta_2)} \sigma(r,\theta)\mathrm{d} rd\theta \right) ^p }{ \vert r_1-r_2 \vert^{1+2\alpha p}\vert \theta_1-\theta_2 \vert^{1+2\alpha p}  }  \mathrm{d} r_1\mathrm{d} r_2\mathrm{d}\theta_1\mathrm{d}\theta_2\]
in the next section.}\\
\EN{I think what we need is the following. 
Let
\[F:(r,\theta)\in [\min(f),\max(f)]\times I_i\mapsto F(r,\theta)=\int_{\square(r,\theta)  } \sigma \in  \mathbb{R}  \],
then $F$ is in $\mathcal{W}^{\alpha;p}_r\mathcal{W}^{\alpha;p}_\theta([\min(f),\max(f)]\times I_i,\mathfrak{g})$}
Moreover, the map
\begin{align*}
(r,\theta)\in [\min(f),\max(f)]\times I_i \longmapsto  \partial_\theta \left(\int_{\square(r,\theta)  } \sigma \right),   
\end{align*}
is partially $C^\infty$ of the $r$ variable on 
\[[\min(f),\max(f)]\times I_i \setminus \{(f,\theta)(\mathrm{Crit}(f)_1)\}\] and given 
\[r\in [\min(f),\max(f)]\setminus \mathrm{Critical}\,\ \mathrm{values}(f),\]
it is $C^\infty$ in $\theta\in \mathrm{int}(I_i)$ with at worst $\log$ blow--up at the endpoints of $I_i$.

OWNER RESULT DRAFT: proof (unaudited), T336-w727-C017 v2. Under ALL C016 raw-input Gaussian-kernel GP task-law, bounded attention-plus-residual-MLP class and comparator hypotheses (iid fresh-GP tasks, exogenous joint input design and length, independent N(0,s) observation noises, d>=1,n>=0,ell,s,epsilon>0, raw cube inputs, original unclipped target posterior, context labels clipped only in predictor encoding), fix class P,W_max,Lambda,U,0<v0<=v1,V and all approximation constants before sampling. Let alpha in (0,1), eta>0 and xi>=0. Put C=0.5log(v1/v0)+U^2/v0, K=4(C+V/v0), Q=1/(2v0)+(U+sqrt(V))/v0+(U^2+V)/v0^2, gamma=eta/[4Q(1+2/alpha)], q=max(1,ceil(2W_max Lambda/gamma)), u=log(4/alpha)+Plog(q+1), m0=max(1,ceil(2048K^2u/eta^2),ceil(16Ku/eta)). For every integer m>=m0, any measurable xi-approximate global empirical minimizer has fresh original-task expected forward KL <=epsilon+eta+xi, with probability >=1-alpha. Markov on the nonnegative sample-average output-loss sensitivity gives population/empirical cover transfer <=gamma Q(1+2/alpha)=eta/4, with failure probability <=alpha/2. The fixed-cover Chernoff bound, which separately requires iid tasks and a finite exponential loss moment, costs the other alpha/2; the explicit sample requirement makes beta_m<=eta/4. Thus uniform risk deviation <=eta/2, and ERM excess <=eta+xi. This is a standard composition with an explicit m-independent cover tolerance, not a novelty or efficient-training claim. Saved C007 and C013-C016 dependencies remain unaudited. The 54 exact rational budget checks are finite algebra checks, not a universal or probabilistic certificate. Lean scalar allocation is written but UNVERIFIED. Version 2 corrects only the v1 prose case count 162 to actual 54; formulas unchanged.

IID tasks; marginal Gaussian query envelope with V; bounded mean and strictly positive bounded variance outputs; fixed data-independent cover

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:520096c5120c6c5ee7fdae3af54826d2608cd90886c9d0f47263b6cb5e4efed6","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/52/520096c5120c6c5ee7fdae3af54826d2608cd90886c9d0f47263b6cb5e4efed6.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a3424003c82069c1c37d3935e800bf94f2dfdca16e0ead63d31d7073bea8aa8d","bundle_entry_key":"t336-w727-c017-v2","bundle_id":"population.w727-t336-explicit-erm-sample-requirement-012","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Transformer generalization; Gaussian log-loss covering bounds","draft":"w727/bundle_012.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.transformers:draft-explicit-erm-sample-requirement-average-loss-sensitivity","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C017 v2: an explicit sample requirement for the C016 ERM guarantee
Kind: bound. Target: none. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim.

The sample requirement can be stated without m inside the covering tolerance. The change is to bound average loss sensitivity rather than the largest observed query. All approximation and task-law assumptions of C016 remain in force.

## 1. Statement
Fix C016's approximation parameters, bounded class, P, W_max, Lambda, U, v0,v1 and V before sampling. In particular v0=s>0, V=s+1 and 0<v0<=v1. Let alpha in (0,1) and let eta>0 be the desired ESTIMATION excess-risk allowance, distinct from the approximation allowance epsilon. Put

    C=0.5 log(v1/v0)+U^2/v0,
    K=4(C+V/v0),
    Q=1/(2v0)+(U+sqrt(V))/v0+(U^2+V)/v0^2,
    gamma=eta/[4 Q(1+2/alpha)],
    q=max(1,ceil(2 W_max Lambda/gamma)),
    u=log(4/alpha)+P log(q+1),
    m0=max(1,ceil(2048 K^2 u/eta^2),ceil(16 K u/eta)).     (1)

For every integer m>=m0, with probability at least 1-alpha over iid training tasks, every measurable xi-approximate global empirical minimizer satisfies

    E_fresh W KL(P_W || h_theta_hat(c_B(W)))
                     <= epsilon+eta+xi.                 (2)

The target posterior and task law are the ORIGINAL, unclipped ones of C016. The predictor input alone clips context labels at C016's fixed B. The class is exactly C016's counted raw-input normalized ReLU attention plus residual MLP class, with its explicit parameter radius and fixed output clips. No new optimization algorithm or independent audit is asserted. Dependencies C007 and C013-C016 remain unaudited.

Unlike C016's maximum-query formulation, every quantity in (1) is fixed before selecting m. There is no claim of an optimal sample requirement or efficient architecture size.

## 2. Hypotheses and named inequalities
The C016/C007 loss-envelope argument supplies, for every fixed predictor, a nonnegative normalized Gaussian log loss with a finite exponential moment and

    log E exp(z(loss-E loss)) <= 8 K^2 z^2/(1-2K|z|),
                  |z|<1/(2K).

IID tasks and this mgf, not just finite variance, are the hypotheses for the Chernoff bound. The bound is exponential: for a fixed predictor the probability that its empirical risk differs from its risk by more than

    beta_m=4sqrt(2) K sqrt(u/m)+2K u/m

is at most 2exp(-u). The fixed C014 cover has J_cover=(q+1)^P members and output radius gamma. Union over that cover therefore costs at most 2J_cover exp(-u)=alpha/2.

The other event uses Markov's inequality. Its hypothesis is a nonnegative integrable random variable. Its conclusion is an upper bound P(Z>b)<=E Z/b, which is a reciprocal, not exponential, threshold bound. Independence is NOT needed for this event.

## 3. Average sensitivity event
On the fixed output rectangle the loss is Lipschitz in the two output coordinates, in their maximum norm, with random constant

    L(Y)=1/(2v0)+(|Y|+U)/v0+(|Y|+U)^2/(2v0^2).

As established in C007 and used in C016, the Gaussian query marginal has E|Y|<=sqrt(V), EY^2<=V. The ordinary scalar inequality (|Y|+U)^2<=2Y^2+2U^2 gives E L(Y)<=Q. These are marginal statements: no independence of Y from the context or predictor is assumed.

Let Lbar_m=(1/m)sum_i L(Y_i). It is nonnegative and E Lbar_m<=Q. Markov's inequality gives

    P(Lbar_m>2Q/alpha)<=alpha/2.                        (3)

On the intersection of this event's complement and the fixed-cover concentration event, choose a covering predictor g for any theta. This choice can depend on theta but the finite cover itself was fixed before sampling. The population loss difference is <=gamma E L(Y)<=gamma Q, and the empirical loss difference is <=gamma Lbar_m<=2gamma Q/alpha. Hence uniformly in theta,

    |R(theta)-Rhat(theta)|
       <= beta_m+gamma Q(1+2/alpha)
       = beta_m+eta/4.                                 (4)

The two events jointly have probability at least 1-alpha by a union bound; independence between them is not asserted. No maximum-query cutoff or union over query extremes is needed in this transfer.

## 4. Explicit sample budget and excess risk
All constants in (1) are positive: v0,V,eta>0, Q>=1/(2v0)>0, K>0, W_max>=1, Lambda>0, alpha in (0,1) and u>0. Thus every division and square root below is valid. For m>=m0,

    m eta^2 >= 2048 K^2 u,
    m eta >= 16 K u.

Since all terms are nonnegative, the first inequality implies

    (4sqrt(2)K sqrt(u/m))^2
       =32 K^2 u/m <= eta^2/64,

and therefore 4sqrt(2)K sqrt(u/m)<=eta/8. The second gives 2K u/m<=eta/8. No sign reversals occur: all reciprocals divide strictly positive quantities. Thus beta_m<=eta/4 and (4) is at most eta/2.

An xi-approximate empirical minimizer then satisfies

    R(theta_hat)
       <= Rhat(theta_hat)+eta/2
       <= inf_theta Rhat(theta)+xi+eta/2
       <= inf_theta R(theta)+xi+eta.

Subtract the same expected conditional Gaussian entropy as in C016 and use its comparator KL<=epsilon. This proves (2). Fresh-task expectations are conditional on the trained predictor; the event is uniform over the whole parameter class.

## 5. Checks and limitations
The rerunnable scripts/check_C017_budget.py checks 54 exact rational parameter combinations, including small/large eta and small confidence, the ceiling sample requirement, the squared square-root allocation, the linear allocation and the transfer allocation. The log is logs/C017_budget.json. These are finite algebraic checks, not a certificate for all parameters or for probability statements. The universal inequalities are the analytic argument in Sections 2-4.

Boundary checks: m0>=1; eta is strictly positive and may be arbitrarily large or small; alpha cannot be zero or one under the stated confidence convention; n=0 is already allowed by C016 and leaves all statistical constants finite since s>0. Query dependence within a task is permitted and unused; dropping it changes nothing. Independence BETWEEN tasks is used in the loss-mgf product. Without it, repeated copies of one nonconstant random loss need not concentrate as m grows. The finite exponential moment is used for the Chernoff rate; an arbitrary finite-variance heavy-tailed loss cannot be substituted there. The finite first moment of L alone is sufficient for (3). Positive variance floor and bounded mean outputs are used by the derivative envelope. Fixed cover and data-independent class are used by the finite union bound. These checks concern the precise statement, not a claim that every assumption is necessary for every possible theorem.

A Lean budget statement is written in proofs/C017_budget.lean. It certifies nothing yet: it is UNVERIFIED, and no compiler or dependency audit is asserted. Mathlib checking was previously measured above this worker's 1 GB allowance; no repeat heavy check is launched. Its intended mathematical content is only the final scalar allocation, not the Gaussian mgf, Markov argument, covering theorem, or task-law composition. The analytic rung is proof (unaudited), not Lean-checked or independently checked proof.

Sources: C007 Section 3 and C016 Sections 3-5 supply the saved Gaussian loss mgf, sensitivity envelope and entropy conversion; C014 supplies the counted attention-MLP cover. C016 supplies the approximation comparator and original task-law assumptions. No accepted result is re-audited. [Coro 21 of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Assume that $0<\alpha<1$, $m\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, $|\Omega^0|>0$, and
\[
\int_\Omega m(x)\varphi_{1,\Omega}^{\alpha+1}\,dx<0.
\]
Suppose that there exist $\rho_0>0$ and $m_{\rho_0}^->0$ such that
\[
\mathcal C_{\rho_0}
:=
\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)<\rho_0\}
\subset\{m<0\},
\qquad
-m(x)\geq m_{\rho_0}^-
\quad\text{a.e. in }\mathcal C_{\rho_0}.
\]
Assume, in addition, that for some
$\lambda_c\in(\lambda_{1,\Omega},\lambda_{1,\Omega^0})$,
equation \eqref{Eq1} has a non-negative weak solution $u_{\lambda_c}^-$
satisfying $E_{\lambda_c}''(u_{\lambda_c}^-)<0$ and, for some
$q_0\in(0,m_\rho^-)$,
\[
\psi_{1/N,q_0}
\bigl(\|u_{\lambda_c}^-\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\bigr)
<
\frac{\rho_0}{4},
\qquad
\|u_{\lambda_c}^-\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}
<
\delta_{\lambda_c,q_0}.
\]
Then $u_{\lambda_c}^-$ has compact support in $\Omega$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2604.08623, 'Central limit theorem for the Allen-Cahn equation with supercritical random initial condit'] For all $t>0,\:x\in \mathbb{R}^d,$  the map $J_{t,x} : X_a \to \mathbb{R}$ that sends $u_0$ to $u(t,x)$
is Fréchet differentiable. Furthermore, the Fréchet derivative at $u_0$ of the maps $(J_{t,x})_{t,x}$, defines for each $h \in X_a$
a function $v : t,x\mapsto v(t,x) := J'_{t,x} (u_0)[h] $ that is the unique classical solution of the equation
\[\partial_t v(t,x) = \Delta v(t,x) - 3 \lambda u(t,x) ^2v(t,x),\quad t>0,\:x\in \mathbb{R}^d,\]
with initial data $h$.

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2607.26894, 'Stability in stochastic hypergraph matching II: weights, batch arrivals, and continuous ti'] If $(G, \mu)$ is stabilisable if and only if it is stabilisable using a set $M'$ of finitely many matching types. When this is the case, one may need exactly $|E|$ stabilising generalised matching types and this is optimal.
	
	In view of Theorem \ref{theorem: necessity and sufficiency of inccond}, this is equivalent to the existence of a matrix $N \in \N^{E \times E}$ such that the map $G_N = G\circ N$ is surjective and the equation $G_N \lambda = \mu$ admits a positive solution $\lambda \in \R_{> 0}^E$.
	
	With respect to $(G_{M'}, \mu)$, both $L_+$-MaxWeight and the family of Markovian, size-based, online assignment polices constructed in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma: necessity of onlcond} admit maximum stability region. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 14 of arXiv:2607.28578, 'On two differing geometric descriptions of the passage from microscopy to macroscopy in Ma'] Let $E\subseteq H^{\Wass}_{\rho}$ be closed and suppose the gradients of regular covectors which belong to $E$ are dense in $E$. The Otto and Stein law gradients agree for every such covector if and only if
	\[
		\Mop_{\rho}|_E=\id_E.
	\]
	This condition makes their cotangent forms and tangent metrics agree on the law directions generated by $E$. The included particle fields agree for every such covector if and only if
	\[
		\mathsf{S}_{\rho}|_E=\id_E.
	\]
	Taking $E=H^{\Wass}_{\rho}$ characterises agreement of the complete fibrewise law geometries; agreement of the complete particle response remains the stronger condition.

Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space, f measurable, and d_f(t) = mu({|f| > t}). (a) Chebyshev / Markov: for 0 < p < infinity and t > 0, d_f(t) <= t^{-p} int_X |f|^p dmu. (b) Layer cake: for 0 < p < infinity, int_X |f|^p dmu = p int_0^infinity t^{p-1} d_f(t) dt, both sides possibly infinite. More generally, if phi: [0, infinity) -> [0, infinity) is nondecreasing, absolutely continuous on compacts with phi(0) = 0, then int_X phi(|f|) dmu = int_0^infinity phi'(t) d_f(t) dt. (c) Consequently ||f||_{L^{p,infinity}} <= ||f||_{L^p}, and an L^p bound can always be recovered from a bound on the distribution function.
(X, Sigma, mu) is a measure space
f is Sigma-measurable

body:
[Lemma lem:blocks of arXiv:2606.08325, 'Digit Mixing under Polynomial Maps'] Fix integers \(d\ge2 , r\), and a positive real number $\beta>0$. 
			We define the functions
			$s :=\lfloor \beta n\rfloor+r$.
			and  $L:=\lfloor(\log n)^2\rfloor$.
			Given an integer $R$, we define the scale function
			$$H:= H(R) =\left\lfloor \frac{s}{L^R}\right\rfloor.$$
			Provided \(R=R(d)\) is chosen large enough, for
			all sufficiently large \(n\), there exist pairwise disjoint integer intervals
			\[ I_{j,k}\subset\mathbb N, \qquad 1\le j\le d,\quad 1\le k\le L,
			\]
			and an absolute constant $c_d$ (only depending on $d$)  with the following properties. \\	
			First, every \(i\in I_{j,k}\) satisfies
			\begin{equation}
				i\asymp_{\beta,d} n.
			\end{equation}
			Second, for each \(k\),
			\begin{equation}
				|\left\{(i_1,\ldots,i_d)\in I_{1,k}\times\cdots\times I_{d,k}:
				i_1+\cdots+i_d=s\right\}|
				\asymp_d H^{d-1}.
			\end{equation}
			Third, suppose that for every \(1\le k\le L\) one chooses a tuple
			$(i_{1,k},\ldots,i_{d,k}) \in I_{1,k}\times\cdots\times I_{d,k}$
			such that
			\begin{equation}
			i_{1,k}+\cdots+i_{d,k}=s.
			\end{equation}
			Then, whenever $(k_1,\ldots,k_{d-1})\succ(k_d,\ldots,k_d)$,
			one has
			\begin{equation}
			i_{1,k_1}+\cdots+i_{d,k_d}\ge s+c_d H.
			\end{equation}

body: For a subset A of a topological space X: the interior int(A) is the union of all open sets contained in A (the largest open set inside A); the closure cl(A) is the intersection of all closed sets containing A - which is closed, being an arbitrary intersection of closed sets, contains A, and lies inside every closed superset of A, hence is the smallest closed set containing A; the boundary is cl(A) minus int(A), equivalently cl(A) intersect cl(X\A). Then A is open iff A = int(A) and closed iff A = cl(A). Point characterization: x is in cl(A) iff every open neighborhood of x meets A (if not, X\cl(A) is an open neighborhood of x missing A; conversely a neighborhood U of x missing A makes X\U a closed superset of A avoiding x). The closure operator satisfies the Kuratowski axioms - cl(empty)=empty, A subset of cl(A), cl(cl(A))=cl(A), cl(A union B)=cl(A) union cl(B) - and these four axioms on a set determine a unique topology whose closed sets are exactly the closure-fixed subsets.
title: Closure, Interior, and Boundary

body: [Definition def:MRF of arXiv:2412.07710, 'An H-theorem for a conditional McKean-Vlasov process related to interacting diffusions on '] Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite graph. Let $(Y_v)_{v \in V}$ be a random element of $(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^d)^V$ with distribution $P \in \mathcal{P}((\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^d)^V)$. Then  $Y = (Y_v)_{v \in V}$, or equivalently its distribution $P$, is said to be a \emph{first-order Markov random field} (abbreviated as 1-MRF) on $(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^d)^V$ if $Y_A$ is conditionally independent of $Y_{(\bar{A})^c}$ given $Y_{\partial A}$, for every finite set $A \subset V$. Similarly,  $Y = (Y_v)_{v \in V},$ or equivalently its distribution $P$, is said to be a \emph{second-order Markov random field} (abbreviated as 2-MRF) on $(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^d)^V$ if $Y_A$ is conditionally independent of $Y_{(A \cup \partial^2 A)^c}$ given $Y_{\partial^2 A}$.
title: Markov random field

[Proposition 7 (Theorem 32 in \cite{ZhaoZhu2008}) of arXiv:2609.03243, 'Weighted Ces\`aro type operators on the weighted Bergman spaces in the unit ball'] Let $\alpha>-1$, $0<p<\infty$, and choose
\[
    M>n\max\left\{1,\frac{1}p\right\}+\frac{\alpha+1}{p}.
\]
There is a Bergman-metric separated lattice
$\{w_j\}\subset\mathbb B_n$ such that every $f\in A_\alpha^p(\mathbb B_n)$
has a representation
\begin{equation}
    f(z)=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}c_j a_{w_j,M}^{(p)}(z),
    \qquad
    a_{w,M}^{(p)}(z)=
    \frac{(1-|w|^2)^{M-(n+1+\alpha)/p}}{(1-\langle z,w\rangle)^M},
    \end{equation}
where $\{c_j\}\in\ell^p$.  The series converges in $A_\alpha^p$ and
locally uniformly, and
\[
    \|f\|_{p,\alpha}\simeq
    \inf\left\{\|\{c_j\}\|_{\ell^p}:
    f=\sum_jc_ja_{w_j,M}^{(p)}\right\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 32 in \cite{ZhaoZhu2008}

body: [Definition 2 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] Given $0< t \le T$, we say that the process $X^\varepsilon$ does not jump from $0$ to $1$ during the time interval $(0,t)$ if and only if for any $r \in (0,t)$, we have $0 \le X_r^\varepsilon \le y_*^\varepsilon$, i.e. $e_1^\varepsilon \ge t$. This is equivalent to saying that for all $i\ge 1$ such that $\tau_i^\varepsilon \in (0,t)$, the condition $0<\tau^{\varepsilon}_{i+1} -\tau_i^\varepsilon<T_*^\varepsilon$ holds.

[Theorem TheoGW1 of arXiv:2604.06012, 'Large fringe trees for random trees with given vertex degrees'] {Cai2017}}] 
Let $\mathbf{p} := (p_{i})_{i \geq 0}$ be a probability distribution on
$\mathbb{N}_0$ such that $p_{0} >0$ and $p_{i} >0$ for at least one $i \geq 2$. Let
$\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{p},n}$ be a Galton--Watson tree 
with offspring distribution $\mathbf{p}$ conditioned to have
size $n \in \mathbb{N}$
(we only consider $n$ along values for which the conditioning is well
defined). 
Furthermore, suppose that the mean 
$\sum_{i \geq 0} i p_{i} = 1$ and that
$\mathbf{p}$ satisfies one of the following conditions: 
\begin{enumerate}[label=\upshape(\alph*)]
\par
 \refstepcounter{thmenumerate}\textup{(\roman{thmenumerate})\enspace}  
$\sigma^{2}_{\mathbf{p}} 
:= \sum_{i \geq 0}(i-1)^{2}p_{i} \in  (0,\infty)$. 
(I.e., the distribution $\mathbf{p}$ has finite variance $\sigma^2$.) 
\par
 \refstepcounter{thmenumerate}\textup{(\roman{thmenumerate})\enspace} $\sigma^{2}_{\mathbf{p}} = \infty$ and
  $\mathbf{p}$ belongs to the domain of attraction of a stable law
  of index $\alpha \in (1,2]$. 
(The last condition is equivalent to that
there exists a slowly varying function
  $L:\mathbb{R}_{+} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{+}$ such that $\sum_{i = 0}^{k}
  i^{2} p_{i} = k^{2-\alpha} L(k)$,
  as $k \rightarrow \infty$
[FellerII].) 
\end{enumerate}
\noindent Let $T_{n} \in \mathbb{T}$ be such that $m_{n} := |T_{n}| \rightarrow \infty$. As $n \rightarrow \infty$, 
\begin{enumerate}[label=\upshape(\roman*)]
\par
 \refstepcounter{thmenumerate}\textup{(\roman{thmenumerate})\enspace}  
If\/ $n \pi_{\mathbf{p}}(T_{n}) \rightarrow \lambda$, 
for some $\lambda \in [0,\infty)$, then 
\begin{align}  
N_{T_n}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{p},n}) \overset{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{Po}\bigl(\lambda\bigr)
\end{align} 
\noindent with convergence of all moments.
\par
 \refstepcounter{thmenumerate}\textup{(\roman{thmenumerate})\enspace}  If\/ $n \pi_{\mathbf{p}}(T_{n}) \rightarrow \infty$, then 
\begin{align} 
\frac{N_{T_{n}}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{p},n}) - n \pi_{\mathbf{p}}(T_{n})}{\sqrt{n \pi_{\mathbf{p}}(T_{n})}} \overset{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow}\mathrm{N}\bigl(0,1\bigr).
\end{align}

\end{enumerate}

body: In set theory, the constructible universe (or Gödel's constructible universe), denoted by $L,$ is a particular class of sets that can be described entirely in terms of simpler sets. $L$ is the union of the constructible hierarchy $L_{\alpha }$. It was introduced by Kurt Gödel in 1938, who proved that the constructible universe is an inner model of ZF set theory, and also that the axiom of choice and the generalized continuum hypothesis are true in the constructible universe. This shows that both propositions are consistent with the basic axioms of set theory, if ZF itself is consistent. Since many other theorems only hold in systems in which one or both of the propositions is true, their consistency is an important result.

body: Let $M$ predictors produce, on $n$ calibration cases with vector-valued targets $y_i \in \mathbb{R}^D$, the per-case error vectors $e_{im} \in \mathbb{R}^D$ (member $m$'s prediction minus $y_i$). For one output coordinate $d$ write $e_i^{(d)} \in \mathbb{R}^M$ for the vector of the $M$ members' errors on that coordinate. The ordinary error covariance is $\Sigma_E^{(d)} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i (e_i^{(d)} - \bar e^{(d)})(e_i^{(d)} - \bar e^{(d)})^T$. The error covariance in the per-sample relative metric is the same average with each case weighted by the inverse squared norm of its target, $$\Sigma_E^{\mathrm{rel},(d)} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i \frac{(e_i^{(d)} - \bar e^{(d)}_{w})(e_i^{(d)} - \bar e^{(d)}_{w})^T}{\|y_i\|^2}, \qquad \bar e^{(d)}_w = \frac{\sum_i e_i^{(d)}/\|y_i\|^2}{\sum_i 1/\|y_i\|^2}.$$ It is the covariance whose minimum-variance portfolio $w = \Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}/(\mathbf{1}^T\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1})$ minimises the calibration value of the objective $\frac{1}{n}\sum_i \|\hat y_i - y_i\|^2/\|y_i\|^2$ restricted to that coordinate, i.e. the squared version of the mean per-sample relative $L^2$ error that emulator benchmarks report, rather than the unweighted squared error that ordinary least squares minimises. Its spectrum is typically far more heavy-tailed than the ordinary one, because the cases with the smallest $\|y_i\|$ carry weights orders of magnitude larger than the rest.

	Let $q \colon [0,T] \to (0,\infty)$ be a Lipschitz continuous function. Then, for any $n \geq 0$, $c_n$ is continuous on $[0,T]$.
	
	If moreover $q$ is differentiable at some $t \in (0,T]$, then $c_n$ is differentiable at $t$ and, writing $c(t)=(c_0(t),c_1(t),\ldots)$, we have $\partial_t c(t)= (-D(t) + A(t))c(t)$, where we set
	\[
	\begin{cases}
	D(t) = \varrho q(t)^{2/(2+\alpha)} D, \\
	D = \mathrm{Diag}((\lambda_i - \lambda_0)_{i\geq 0}),
	\end{cases}
	\quad \quad 
	\begin{cases}
	A(t) = \frac{q'(t)}{q(t)}A, \\
	A = \frac{1}{2(2+\alpha)} (\langle \varphi_{j}, x\varphi_{i}'\rangle - \langle x\varphi_j', \varphi_i \rangle)_{i,j \geq 0}.
	\end{cases}
	\]

Own work draft, proof (unaudited), classical counting application with novelty unverified. Fix unit probe q, theta in (0,pi/2], ell=d-1>=2 and N independent isotropic Gaussian covariates. A teacher is w=cos(theta)q+sin(theta)u with u uniform on the unit sphere in q-perp, and labels are noiseless signs. Any learner outputting a unit linear-classifier normal from the full labeled pool, q, theta and independent randomness has prior-average expected Gaussian test error at least sin(theta)*(2*(e*max(1,N/ell))^ell)^(-1/(ell-1))/(2*pi). An affine arrangement has at most sum_{j=0}^ell binomial(N,j)<=(e*max(1,N/ell))^ell label patterns, and each output captures latitude prior mass at most (delta/sin(theta))^(ell-1) for angular tolerance delta<=sin(theta)/2. The union bound proves the claim. For a rotation-equivariant learner the expected bound holds for each fixed teacher-probe pair. Hence if N/(d-1)->beta>0, liminf expected error is at least sin(theta)/(2*pi*e*max(1,beta)). Threshold max-margin is rotation equivariant, so an exponential ORIGINAL-pool envelope is impossible at fixed nonzero theta. The bound does not rule out an exponential retained-data regime or determine its crossover. No independent audit or novelty claim.

[Theorem theo:(dis)continuity of arXiv:2512.12124, 'A discontinuous percolation phase transition on the hierarchical lattice'] Let $\mathcal{J} : \left[0,\infty\right) \times E \to \left[0,\infty \right)$ be a proper family of kernels on the hierarchical lattice $\mathbb{H}^d_L$.
     \begin{enumerate}
     \item \emph{(Slow decay $\Rightarrow$ Continuity.)} If $\mathcal{J} \gg n^{-2d}\log\log n$ and $\lambda_c<\infty$ then the phase transition is \emph{continuous} in the sense that  $\mathbb{P}_{\lambda_c} ( |K_0| = \infty ) = 0$.
        \item  \emph{(Fast decay $\Rightarrow$ Triviality.)} If $\mathcal{J} \ll n^{-2d}\log\log n$ then there is \emph{no phase transition} in the sense that $\lambda_c=\infty$.
  \item \emph{(Critical decay $\Rightarrow$ Discontinuity.)} If $\mathcal{J}\approx n^{-2d}\log\log n$ and $\lambda_c<\infty$ then the phase transition is \emph{discontinuous} in the sense that $\mathbb{P}_{\lambda_c} ( |K_0| = \infty ) > 0$.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem theo:(dis)continuity of arXiv:2512.12124

Let g: {-1, 1}^n -> {-1, 1}. Then Var(g) = I(g) if and only if g is constant or g = +-x_i for some i. Equivalently, for f: {0, 1}^n -> {0, 1} with flip influence I_flip(f) = sum_i P(f(X) != f(X with bit i flipped)) under the uniform measure, I_flip(f) = 4 Var(f) if and only if f is constant or f is the indicator of a half-cube {x_i = 0} or {x_i = 1}. A direct recursive certificate: with D(f) = I_flip(f) - 4 Var(f), restricting coordinate i to 0 and 1 gives D(f) = (D(f_0) + D(f_1))/2 + Var(f_1 - f_0) with every term nonnegative, so D(f) = 0 iff D(f_0) = D(f_1) = 0 and f_1 - f_0 is constant.
uniform measure
g Boolean (+-1) or f Boolean (0/1)

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.11434, 'Maxima of stationary systems of randomly time-changed L\'evy particles'] Let $(X_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be a  Markov process,
  $(\RR,\mathcal{B}(\RR),\mu)$ a $\sigma$-finite measure space with $\mu(\RR)=\infty$,
  and $g$ a measurable function from $(\mathbb{D}([0,\infty)), \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{D}([0,\infty)))$ to a measurable space $(E,\mathcal{E})$.
  Then the following holds:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item
    The particle system $\mathfrak{P}_g((X_t)_{t\ge 0},\mu)$ defines a PPP on $(E,\mathcal{E})$ with intensity measure
    \begin{align*}
      \mu_g(A)
      \ = \
      \int_{\RR}
      \PP
      \left[
      g
      \left(
      (X_{t}(x))_{t\ge 0}
      \right)
      \in A
      \right]
      \,
      \mu(\mathrm{d}x)
      \qquad\text{for}\ A\in \mathcal{E}
      \,.
    \end{align*}
        \item
    The particle system $\mathfrak{P}((X_t)_{t\ge 0},\mu)$ is stationary if and only if
    the process--measure pair $((X_t)_{t\ge 0},\mu)$ is invariant.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.11434

[Theorem verif of arXiv:2411.04802, 'Dynkin ghost games with asymmetry and consolation'] Let two continuous functions $u_1,u_2:\mathcal I\times[0,1]^2\to[0,\infty)$ and a pair $(\Gamma^1,\Gamma^2)\in\mathcal A^2$ be given. 
Assume that $u_i\leq V^{g_i}$, and that $\Gamma^i_{\tau_{g_i}}=1$, $i=1,2$. Define on $[0,\infty)$ two processes
		\[M^1_t:=
			e^{-rt}(1-p_{1}\Gamma^{2}_{t})u_1(X_{t},\Pi^{1}_{t}, \Pi^2_{t}) + p_{1}\int_{[0,t]} e^{-rs}V^{h_1}(X_s)\,d\Gamma^{2}_s\]
   and 
   	\[M^2_t:=
			e^{-rt}(1-p_{2}\Gamma^{1}_{t-})u_2(X_{t},\Pi^{1}_{t-}, \Pi^2_{t-}) + p_{2}\int_{[0,t)} e^{-rs}V^{h_2}(X_s)\,d\Gamma^{1}_s,\]
and assume that 
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]
$M^i$ is a supermartingale, and it is a martingale 
on $[0,\gamma_i(u)]$ for any $u<1$, $i=1,2$;
\item[(i')] 
$M^2$ is continuous on $[0,\tau_{g_2}]$ and on $(\tau_{g_2},\infty)$, with 
$M^2_{\tau_{g_2}+}-M^2_{\tau_{g_2}}\leq 0$;
\item[(ii)]
$u_1(X_t,\Pi^1_{t},\Pi^2_{t})\geq g_1(X_t)$ and $u_2(X_t,\Pi^1_{t-},\Pi^2_{t-})\geq g_2(X_t)$ for all $t\geq 0$ $\mathbb P_x$-a.s.;
\item[(iii)]
$\Gamma^1_t=\int_{[0,t]} 1_{\{u_1(X_s,\Pi^1_{s},\Pi^2_{s})=g_1(X_s)\}}\,d\Gamma^1_s$ and $\Gamma^2_t=\int_{[0,t]} 1_{\{u_2(X_s,\Pi^1_{s-},\Pi^2_{s-})=g_2(X_s)\}}\,d\Gamma^2_s$.
\end{itemize}
Then $(\Gamma^1,\Gamma^2)$ is a Nash equilibrium, 
and the equilibrium values are given by 
\[M^1_0=(1-p_1\Gamma_0^2)u_1(x,\Pi^1_0,\Pi_0^2) + p_1\Gamma^2_0 V^{h_1}(x)\]
and $M^2_0=u_2(x,p_1,p_2)$, respectively.
title: Theorem verif of arXiv:2411.04802

body: The characteristic polynomial of an n x n matrix A is p(lambda) = det(A - lambda I), a degree-n polynomial whose roots are the eigenvalues of A. Its coefficients are basis-independent (similar matrices share it): the coefficient of lambda^{n-1} is -trace(A) and the constant term is det(A), so the sum of eigenvalues is the trace and their product is the determinant.
title: Characteristic Polynomial

[Lem r-j_infty of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] For each $w>0$, the following statements hold$:$
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $($From reachability to join$)$.
    If $\Delta\rightsquigarrow_w\infty$, then
    \[
    S_\Delta\approx_w\infty.
    \]
    \item $($From join to reachability$)$.
    Let $S$ be a discrete $(k-1)$-sphere.
    If $S\approx_w\infty$, then there exists $\Delta\in V_{2w+4}$ with $S_\Delta=S$ such that
    \[
    \Delta\rightsquigarrow_{2w+4}\infty.
    \]
  \end{itemize}

[Theorem 32 (one-shot) of arXiv:2606.22611, 'Upper and Lower Bounds on Expected Soft Maxima\\of Gaussian Processes'] Let $X = (X_t)_{t\in T}$ be a centered subgaussian process
with a finite index set $T$. Let $\tau$ be a random element of $T$ jointly distributed with $X$, such that $P_\tau=\nu$.
Then 
\begin{align*}
\Ex{X_\tau} \lesssim \Delta + \int_0^\Delta 
\Big(\sM_{\nu}^*(\epsilon) \wedge \sqrt{I(X ; \tau) }\Big) \dif \epsilon,
\end{align*}
where, as before, $\Delta$ denotes the diameter of $(T,d)$. If $X$ is a Gaussian process, 
then there exists a probability measure $\mu\in \eP(T)$, such that 
\begin{align*}
\eF_\beta(X;\mu_\beta^*) + \Delta
&\gtrsim \sup_{t\in T}\int_0^\Delta 
 \Big(\sM_{\delta_t}(\mu,\epsilon)\wedge \beta \epsilon\Big) \dif \epsilon
\end{align*}
In particular,
\begin{align*}
\Ex X_{\uptau_\beta^*}+ \Delta \gtrsim 
\sup_{\nu\in\eP(T)}\int_0^\Delta 
\Big(\sM_\nu^*(\epsilon)\wedge
\sqrt{I(X ; \uptau_\beta^*) }\Big) \dif \epsilon.
\end{align*}
title: one-shot

[Lemma stablifting of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be a simple, stationary point process on \(\mathbb{R}^{d}\) with bounded
(reduced) Palm intensity function, as in~(equation bdedreduced of the paper).
Let \(\Psi=\Psi(\cdot)\) be a stabilizing interaction graph on finite windows with
respect to~\(\mathcal{P}\), in the sense of Definition~(d:stabilizing-graph of the paper).
Assume that the Gibbs specification~(equation eqn:gibbs of the paper) satisfies averaged weak
spatial mixing on~\(\Psi\) with respect to~\(\mathcal{P}\), as in
Definition~(d:ssm-pp of the paper).
Then for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$ there are fast decreasing functions  $\varphi_p$ and constants such that 

\begin{align} 
\sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_p \in W_n} d_{\textnormal{BL}, \bk x1p}(V_{\bk x1p}(\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n)), V_{\bk x1p}(\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n \cap B_r(\bk x1p))))  \leq 2\varphi_p(r), \ r > 0
\end{align}
and for all $l \in \{1,\ldots,p-1\}$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_p\in\mathbb{R}^d$ such that  $0< r < d(\bk{x}{1}{l},\bk{x}{l+1}{p})$, we have 

\begin{align}

& 
d_{\textnormal{BL},\bk{x}{1}{p}}
\left(V_{\bk x1p}(\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n \cap B_r(\bk x1p))),
\left(V_{\bk x1l}(\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n \cap B_r(\bk x1l))), V_{\bk x{l+1}p}(\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n \cap B_r(\bk x{l +1}p)))
\right)\right)
\;\le\; 2\varphi_p(r),
\end{align}

where $V_{\bk x1l}(\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n \cap B_r(\bk x1l))), V_{\bk x{l+1}p}(\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n \cap B_r(\bk x{l+1}p)))$ are conditionally independent (given $\mathcal{P}_n$) spin vectors with laws $\pi_{\bk x1l}$ and $\pi_{\bk x{l+1}p}$ induced respectively by graphs $\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n \cap B_r(\bk x1l))$ and $\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n \cap B_r(\bk x{l+1}p))$.

The above   bound also holds under the stronger total variation distance.
title: Fast  \BL~cluster-localization of spins  on stabilizing graphs
