body:
[Definition 5 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] Let $\fh = \fh_1 + \fh_2$ be a graded Heisenberg algebra.  Let $U(\fh) = \oplus_{k \geq 0} U_k(\fh)$ be its  universal enveloping algebra with the grading induced by the grading of $\fh$ and let $U(\fh)^* = \oplus_{k \geq 0} U_k(\fh)^*$ be its graded dual.
We can identify $U(\fh)^*$ with the space of polynomial functions on the Heisenberg group $\sH$ of $\fh$ by regarding $U(\fh)$ as the space of left-invariant differential operators on $\sH$ (see Remark \ref{r.jet}). Let $\iota:\fh_2\hookrightarrow U_2(\fh)$ be the natural inclusion and let $\rho_2:=\iota^*:U_2(\fh)^*\to\fh_2^*$ be the restriction map.  
 A finite-dimensional graded subspace $$S = \oplus_{k \geq 0} S^k \subset U(\fh)^*, S^k \subset U_k(\fh)^*,$$ is called a {\em contact symbol system} on $\fh$,
if $S^0 = \C, S^1 = \fh_1^*$, $\rho_2(S^2)=\fh_2^*$, and $S$ is preserved under the operation of right-invariant vector fields on $\sH$.  The {\em rank} of a contact symbol system $S$ is ${\rm rk}(S):=\max\{k\mid S^k\ne0\}.$
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2609.02105

[Theorem 27 of arXiv:2609.01128, 'Nonabelian Chabauty for the Thrice-punctured Line over Cyclotomic Fields'] Let $K=\bQ(\zeta_8)$ and $S=\left\{(1-\zeta_8)\right\}$. If $c_{\chi_i},c_{\kappa_i},c_{\mu_i}\ne 0$ for $i=1,2$ and $c_{\tau_\alpha\tau_\beta}\ne 0$, the depth-4 polylogarithmic Chabauty--Kim locus $X(\cO_K\otimes \bZ_p)_{S,\PL,4}$ is the solution set of the following equations in addition to \eqref{eq:keyeq} and \eqref{eq:depth3} (with the coordinates $(X_i,Y_i,Z_i,W_i,V_i)=(\log(z_i),L_1(z_i),L_2(z_i),L_3(z_i),L_4(z_i))$ for $i=1,2,3,4$):
\begin{equation}

\left\{
\begin{aligned}
& V_{1}+V_{2}+V_{3}+V_{4} = c_{4,1} (X_{1}+X_{3})(W_{1}+W_{2}+W_{3}+W_{4})  \\
& \quad + c_{4,2} (X_{1}-X_{3})(W_{1}+W_{2}-W_{3}-W_{4}) + c_{4,3} (X_{1}-X_{3})(X_{1}+X_{3})(Z_{1}+Z_{2})  \\[4pt]
& V_{1}+V_{2}-V_{3}-V_{4} = c_{4,4} (X_{1}-X_{3})(W_{1}+W_{2}+W_{3}+W_{4})  \\
& \quad + c_{4,5} (X_{1}+X_{3})(W_{1}+W_{2}-W_{3}-W_{4}) \\ &\quad+ c_{4,6} (X_{1}-X_{3})^{2}(Z_{1}+Z_{2}) + c_{4,7} (X_{1}+X_{3})^{2}(Z_{1}+Z_{2}) 
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}
where
\begin{gather}
c_{4,1} = \frac{c_{\tau_\alpha \kappa_1}}{2c_{\tau_\alpha} c_{\kappa_1} }, \quad
c_{4,2} = \frac{c_{\tau_\beta \kappa_2}}{2c_{\tau_\beta}c_{\kappa_2}}, \quad
c_{4,3} = \frac{c_{\tau_\beta\tau_\alpha\tau_\alpha\tau_\beta}}{2 c_{\tau_\alpha\tau_\beta} c_{\tau_\alpha} c_{\tau_\beta}}, \\
c_{4,4} = \frac{c_{\tau_\beta \kappa_1}}{2 c_{\tau_\beta} c_{\kappa_1}}, \quad
c_{4,5} = \frac{c_{\tau_\alpha \kappa_2}}{2 c_{\tau_\alpha} c_{\kappa_2}}, \quad
c_{4,6} = \frac{c_{\tau_\beta\tau_\beta\tau_\alpha\tau_\beta}}{2 c_{\tau_\alpha\tau_\beta} c_{\tau_\beta}^2},\quad 
c_{4,7} = \frac{c_{\tau_\alpha\tau_\alpha\tau_\alpha\tau_\beta}}{2 c_{\tau_\alpha\tau_\beta} c_{\tau_\alpha}^2}.
\end{gather} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:delgd of arXiv:2606.02472, 'Correlated uniform attachment trees'] For $K\in \N$, $\delta\in (0,1)$, and $c_1\geq 1$,  we say a tree $T$ on vertices $\{0,\ldots, n\}$  is $(K,\delta, c_1)$-good if
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
      \item $\sum_{ \delta K/2-1< k \leq n} \mathbbm{1}_{\left\{ F_{T}(k) \geq 0.4 n \right\} } = 0$,
        \item $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{\left\{F_{T}(k) \geq n/(c_1 K) \right\} } \leq \ceil{(c_1+\delta)K} - \delta K/2$, and
        \item $\sum_{k=0}^{K-1} \mathbbm{1}_{\left\{ F_{T}(k) \geq n/(c_1 K) \right\} } \geq  ( c_1 (1-e^{-1/c_1})- \delta/2)K$.
        \end{enumerate}

Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open and F: Ω × R × R^n → R continuous. (i) If u ∈ C^1(Ω) satisfies F(x,u(x),Du(x)) = 0 for every x ∈ Ω, then u is a viscosity solution. (ii) Conversely, if u ∈ C(Ω) is a viscosity solution and u is differentiable at a point x0 ∈ Ω, then F(x0,u(x0),Du(x0)) = 0; if u is only a viscosity subsolution then F(x0,u(x0),Du(x0)) ≤ 0, and if only a supersolution then ≥ 0. (iii) Consequently a locally Lipschitz viscosity solution satisfies the equation pointwise at almost every point of Ω. The converse of (iii) is false: an almost-everywhere solution need not be a viscosity solution.

F continuous
in (i): u ∈ C^1(Ω) and the equation holds at every point
in (ii): u continuous and differentiable at the single point x0
in (iii): u locally Lipschitz (to invoke Rademacher)

body:
[Lem 36 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The following functions are $C_6$-Lipschitz, with $C_6 = 2/\iota$:
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item  $z \mapsto m^{-1}(1/z)$, on $(0,+\infty)$.
        \item  $\gamma \mapsto g(\gamma^2)$, on $[0,+\infty)$.
        \item  $\gamma \mapsto \beta_\star(\gamma^2)$, on $[0,+\infty)$.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
    A routine calculation and application of Lemma~\ref{l:fp-m-fns-conversion} implies
    \[
        \frac{d}{dz} m^{-1}(1/z) = \frac{1/z^2}{m_2(m^{-1}(1/z))}
        \le \frac{1/z^2}{\iota / z^2} = \frac{1}{\iota}\,.
    \]
    This proves part~\eqref{i:fp-m-inv-lipschitz}.
    Since $m$ is strictly decreasing, and $\beta_\star \ge \beta_{
    \min}$, we also have, for $\gamma > 0$,
    \[
        \frac{d}{d\gamma} g(\gamma^2) 
        = 2\gamma m(\beta_\star(\gamma^2))
        \le 2\gamma m(\beta_{\min}(\gamma^2))
        = 2\gamma m(s_2(1/\gamma^2))
        \le \frac{2}{\iota^{1/2}}\,,
    \]
where the final inequality is by Lemma~\ref{l:fp-m-fns-conversion}.
This shows that $\gamma \mapsto g(\gamma^2)$ is $2/\iota^{1/2}$-Lipschitz on $(0,+\infty)$, and the estimate extends to $[0,+\infty)$ since $g$ was defined to be continuous on $[0,\infty)$ (see the comments below \eqref{e:freeprob.g.of.gamma}). 
    This proves part~\eqref{i:fp-g-sq-lipschitz}. For part~\eqref{i:fp-betast-sq-lipschitz}, it suffices to prove that the function
    \[
        \gamma \mapsto \beta_{\min}(\gamma^2)
        = s_2\bigg(\frac1{\gamma^2}\bigg)
    \]
    is $O(1)$-Lipschitz on $[0,+\infty)$. Similarly as above, a routine calculation and application of Lemma~\ref{l:fp-m-fns-conversion} shows that at any $\gamma > 0$, 
    \[
        \frac{d}{d\gamma} 
        s_2\bigg(\frac1{\gamma^2}\bigg)
        = \frac{1/\gamma^3}
            {m_3(s_2(1/\gamma^2))}
        \le \frac{1/\gamma^3}{\iota / \gamma^3}
        = \frac{1}{\iota}\,.
    \]
This shows that $\gamma \mapsto \beta_{\min}(\gamma^2)$ is $1/\iota$-Lipschitz on $(0,+\infty)$, and the estimate extends to $[0,+\infty)$ since the function $\beta_{\min}$ was defined to be continuous on $[0,\infty)$ (again we refer to the comments below \eqref{e:freeprob.g.of.gamma}). 
This proves part~\eqref{i:fp-betast-sq-lipschitz}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 36 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2609.04153, '\vspace*{-3cm}Smooth autonomous fast dynamo action on the three-torus'] Let $E_u(a):\CC^3 \to \CC^3$ be the linear map defined by 
$$
E_u(a)(h,c)=\begin{pmatrix}
D\kappa_u(a) h\\
0
\end{pmatrix}+c u(\kappa_u(a),0), \quad (h,c) \in \CC^2 \times \CC.
$$
Then, $E_u(a):\CC^3 \to \CC^3$ is invertible, and there holds the identity
\begin{equation}

E^{-1}_u(P^m_u(a))D\Phi_u^{\tau^m_u(a)}(\kappa_u(a),0)E_u(a)=\begin{pmatrix}
DP^m_u(a) & 0\\
-D \tau^m_u(a) & 1

body:
Let Omega in R^n be open, L = -div(A grad u) + b.grad u + c u uniformly elliptic with A measurable and b, c in L^infinity(Omega), and f in L^2_loc(Omega). Put B[u,phi] = integral_Omega ( sum_{i,j} a^{ij} D_j u D_i phi + (b.grad u) phi + c u phi ) dx. A function u in H^1_loc(Omega) = W^{1,2}_loc(Omega) is a weak solution of Lu = f in Omega if B[u,phi] = integral_Omega f phi dx for every phi in C_c^infinity(Omega); a weak subsolution (Lu <= f) if B[u,phi] <= integral f phi for every phi in C_c^infinity(Omega) with phi >= 0; a weak supersolution (Lu >= f) if B[u,phi] >= integral f phi for every such phi >= 0. By density the test class extends to phi in H^1(Omega) with compact support in Omega (phi >= 0 for the one-sided notions), and, when u in H^1(Omega) and f in L^2(Omega), to all phi in H^1_0(Omega) (nonnegative ones for the one-sided notions). A right-hand side in H^{-1}(Omega), e.g. f = f_0 + sum_i D_i f_i with f_0, f_i in L^2, is paired as <f,phi> = integral (f_0 phi - sum_i f_i D_i phi). If a^{ij} in C^1 and u in C^2, u is a weak solution iff it is a classical solution (integrate by parts). The energy class u in H^1_loc is part of the definition; distributional solutions with less integrable gradients need not enjoy any of the regularity theory.
Omega open in R^n
A measurable and uniformly elliptic; b, c in L^infinity(Omega)
u in H^1_loc(Omega)
f in L^2_loc(Omega), or more generally in H^{-1}
title: Weak Solution, Subsolution and Supersolution of a Divergence-Form Elliptic Equation

[Lem 20 of arXiv:2604.13134, '\bf From Gaussian to Gumbel: extreme eigenvalues of complex Ginibre products with exact ra'] Let \(1\leq j\leq r_n.\) Set  
\[
c_1=\frac{\sqrt{\log(\alpha+1)}}{w(\alpha+1)}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{\log(\alpha+e)}w(\alpha+e^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}})}-\frac{\log(\sqrt{2\pi}\log(\alpha+e^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}}))}{w(\alpha+e)\sqrt{\log(\alpha+e)}}
\]  
and  
\[
c_2=\frac{1}{2(\alpha+e)(\log(\alpha+e))^{3/2}},
\]  
where \(w(t)=2t\log t.\) Then, uniformly on \(-\ell_{1,\alpha}(n)\leq x\leq \ell_{2,\alpha}(n)\),
\[
M^{(n)}_{j, j}(x)=\Psi(v_\alpha(j, x))-\phi(v_\alpha(j, x))\Bigl(\frac{1}{n}q_{1}(j, x)+(\alpha_n-\alpha)q_2(j, x)\Bigr)+O(s_n^{-3/2}),

where  
\[
q_{1}(j, x)=\frac{2\alpha(v^{2}_\alpha(j, x)-1)-3\sqrt{\alpha}(2j-1)v_{\alpha}(j, x)+6j(j-1)}{12\sqrt{\alpha}}
\]  
and  
\[
q_{2}(j, x)= c_1-c_2x-\frac{j-1}{2\alpha^{3/2}}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thmIntroProfile of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] There is a single continuous function $G:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ with the following property.
For every fixed integer $k\geq1$, let $X$, $Y$, and the prime $P$ tend to infinity while $P^k/X$ remains in a fixed compact subset of $(0,\infty)$.
For $k\geq2$, assume the short-window and growth conditions of Theorem~(thm:scaled-murmuration of the paper); for $k=1$, assume the conditions of Zubrilina~[Zubrilina2025].
Then, for normalized weight $2$ newforms of squarefree level in $[X,X+Y]$ with trivial nebentypus,
\begin{equation*}
\sqrt X\,
\mathbb E_{X,Y}
\bigl[\varepsilon(f)\lambda_{\operatorname{sym}^k f}(P)\bigr]
=
G\left(\frac{P^k}{X}\right)+o_k(1),
\end{equation*}
locally uniformly in $P^k/X$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The common profile in the weight $2$ level aspect

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2606.17381, 'Large deviation principle for friendship-biases\\ in Galton--Watson trees'] {\bf[Smoothness and steepness of $\Lambda$]}

The cumulant generating function $\Lambda$ satisfies the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm (a)}] $\Lambda$ is differentiable on $\cD_{\Lambda}$. 
\item[{\rm (b)}] $\Lambda$ is lower semi-continuous on $\R^3$. 
\item[{\rm (c)}] $\Lambda$ is steep at $\partial\cD_{\Lambda}$, i.e.,
\[
\lim_{t \to \partial\cD_{\Lambda}\colon\, t\in \cD_{\Lambda}}\|\nabla \Lambda(t)\|_2 = \infty,
\]
where $\nabla$ denotes the gradient operator and $\|\cdot\|_2$ denotes the Euclidean norm.
\end{itemize}

body:
[Theorem kpartW2 of arXiv:2607.00149, '\bf Uniform-in-time Propagation-of-Chaos for\\ Stein Variational Gradient Descent'] Let Assumption~(ass:Wass of the paper) hold and suppose the joint
initial law of the particles is exchangeable. For fixed \(k\ge1\), define
the random \(k\)-fold empirical occupation measure
\[
        \widehat\mu_T^{N,k}
        :=
        \frac1T\int_0^T (\mu_t^N)^{\odot k}\,dt,
        \qquad
        \overline{\mu^{\otimes k}}_T
        :=
        \frac1T\int_0^T \mu_t^{\otimes k}\,dt,
\]
where
\[
(\mu_t^N)^{\odot k}
:=
\frac{1}{(N)_k}
\sum_{\substack{1\le i_1,\ldots,i_k\le N\\
i_1,\ldots,i_k\ {\rm distinct}}}
\delta_{\bigl(x_{i_1}^N(t),\ldots,x_{i_k}^N(t)\bigr)},
\qquad
(N)_k:=N(N-1)\cdots(N-k+1).
\]
Let \(W_2^{(k)}\) be the Wasserstein distance on \((\mathbb R^d)^k\)
associated with the quadratic product cost
\(
        d_k(x,y)^2:=\sum_{\ell=1}^k \|x_\ell-y_\ell\|^2 .
\)
Then, with $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak r(d,\nu)$ as in~(equation eq:rdef of the paper), there is \(C_k<\infty\)
such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
\sup_{T>0}
\mathbb P\left(
W_2^{(k)}
\left(
\widehat\mu_T^{N,k},
\overline{\mu^{\otimes k}}_T
\right)
>
(\log N)^{-r/4}
\right)
\le
C_k(\log N)^{-\min\{r/4,\beta_{\rm init}\}} .
\]
title: Time-averaged \(k\)-particle chaos in \(W_2\)

[Lemma lem:reservoirs-produce-tree of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Fix integers $d\ge1$ and $m\ge1$, and set
\[
\beta_d:=1+(d-1)^2.
\]
Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be $C_4$-free and suppose every right vertex has degree at most $d$. Fix $j_\star\in J$, set $I_\star=N_G(j_\star)$, and assume that for every $i\in I_\star$ there is a \hyperref[def:c4-witness-block]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{reservoir}}}{}
\[
\mathcal R_i\subseteq N_G(i)\setminus\{j_\star\}

with

|\mathcal R_i|\ge m\beta_d.
\]
Then $G$ contains an \hyperref[def:rooted-matching-tree]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{$m$-matching rooted tree}}} at $j_\star$ with $\mathcal K_i\subseteq\mathcal R_i$ for every $i\in I_\star$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For fixed finite t in sparse critical Z4 parking, full-space SRW Green weighted sums over Euclidean radius R have variance (16p/pi^2)log R+O_{t,p}(1) for the signed field S_t=A_t-H_t, equal to the initial iid coefficient. For exploration mean K_t=A_t-q V_t, q=p/(1-p), the coefficient is (8/pi^2)[2p-(1-q)h_t]. The exact finite-R variance difference equals (1-q)h_t sum G_R^2. Initial scenery at R=sqrt(T) has variance (8p/pi^2)log T+O_p(1). Assumptions: Z4; fixed finite t; 0<p<1/2 sparse critical iid law; Euclidean spatial cutoff, full-space discrete-time nearest-neighbor G; C19 signed susceptibility; C23 exploration posterior; R->infinity with t fixed for evolved fields. Limitation: No uniform t-dependent error or simultaneous t,R asymptotic for evolved fields; no nearest-distance conclusion. Novelty: KNOWN stationary convolution/covariance methods; UNCHECKED exact parking coefficients. Status: independently checked proof. The model is discrete-time uniform nearest-neighbor synchronous parking on Z^d with stationary capacity-one holes; A_t(x) is the active-particle count and H_t(x) the unfilled-hole indicator. In the sparse law eta(x) is initially +1 and -1 each with probability p, and zero otherwise, independently across sites. Here h_t=E H_t(0), V_t(x) is the indicator of no initial active particle and no arrival through t, and W_R(X)=sum_{|y|_2<=R}G(y)X(y), with G=sum_{n>=0}p_n.
Z4; fixed finite t; 0<p<1/2 sparse critical iid law
Euclidean spatial cutoff, full-space discrete-time nearest-neighbor G
C19 signed susceptibility; C23 exploration posterior
R->infinity with t fixed for evolved fields

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:22c242a8d1088ed7c20731b241cb7fbc3793f444064ea53738f696b79307db12","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/22/22c242a8d1088ed7c20731b241cb7fbc3793f444064ea53738f696b79307db12.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:003ee7cd411bd14e46e167b8c6d8c2748dacb1466880217907ba41819bb91206","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c24","bundle_id":"population.i0005-final-exploration-energy-and-charge-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"parking and interacting particle systems","draft":"w661/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:four-dimensional-parking-fixed-time-green-charge-variance-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C24 v1: exact logarithmic Green variance from conserved charge

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN stationary convolution/total
covariance methods; UNCHECKED these exact parking/exploration coefficients.

Fix a finite time t in the sparse critical parking process on Z^4,
0<p<1/2. Put S_t=A_t-H_t, q=p/(1-p), V_t as in C23,
K_t=A_t-q V_t=E[S_t|E_t], and h_t=E H_t(0). Let G be the full-space
discrete-time uniform nearest-neighbor SRW Green kernel, and

    W_R(X)=sum_{|y|_2<=R}G(y) X(y).

The three fields X=eta,S_t,K_t have mean zero. As R tends to infinity,

    Var W_R(eta)=(16p/pi^2)log R+O_p(1),
    Var W_R(S_t)=(16p/pi^2)log R+O_{t,p}(1),
    Var W_R(K_t)=(8/pi^2)[2p-(1-q)h_t]log R+O_{t,p}(1).

Moreover at every finite R,

    Var W_R(S_t)=Var W_R(K_t)+(1-q)h_t sum_{|y|<=R}G(y)^2.

This is a fixed-t, growing-R assertion. Its t-dependent error is not
controlled for a simultaneous choice such as R=sqrt(t). For the initial
iid eta only, the first error is t-independent, so R=sqrt(T) directly
gives initial variance (8p/pi^2)log T+O_p(1). The raw individual fields
do not have finite full-space Green-potential variance in d4.

## 1. Susceptibilities and posterior covariance

Finite propagation makes the covariances of S_t and K_t finitely
supported; all relevant counts have finite second moments at fixed t.
C19 gives sum_z Cov(S_t(0),S_t(z))=2p. C23 gives conditional mean K_t
and conditional covariance

    Cov(S_t(0),S_t(z)|E_t)=q(1-q)V_t(0)1{z=0}.

On averaging, q E V_t(0)=h_t, so total covariance yields

    Cov(S_t(0),S_t(z))=Cov(K_t(0),K_t(z))+(1-q)h_t 1{z=0}.

Thus K_t susceptibility is 2p-(1-q)h_t. The initial eta susceptibility
is Var eta(0)=2p. Weighting the same covariance identity immediately
proves the exact finite-R variance decomposition.

## 2. The full-space Green-square coefficient

Lawler--Limic Theorem 4.3.1, including its SRW bipartite convention, gives

    G(y)=(2/pi^2)|y|_2^(-2)+O(|y|_2^(-4)).

Squaring and summing, the error is summable, while
sum_{1<=|y|<=R}|y|^(-4)=2pi^2 log R+O(1), by unit-cube comparison
with the radial integral. Consequently for G_R=G 1_{B_R^Euclidean},

    ||G_R||_2^2=(8/pi^2)log R+O(1).

For each fixed displacement z,

    sum_y G_R(y)G_R(y+z)=||G_R||_2^2
                                  -(1/2)||G_R-shift_z G_R||_2^2
                         =(8/pi^2)log R+O_z(1).

To justify the uniform-in-R shift bound, on the common cutoff region at
large |y| the Green asymptotic gives a difference at most
C_z |y|^(-3)+C|y|^(-4), whose square is summable in dimension four.
The cutoff mismatch is in a shell of width O_z(1), with O_z(R^3) sites
and squared kernel O(R^(-4)), so it contributes O_z(1/R). The finitely
many sites near the origin cause only a finite additional constant.

## 3. Finite-range covariance summation

For a mean-zero stationary field X with finitely supported covariance
c_X(z), expansion of the finite weighted sum gives

    Var W_R(X)=sum_z c_X(z) sum_y G_R(y)G_R(y+z)
      =(8/pi^2)[sum_z c_X(z)]log R+O_X(1).

There are only finitely many displacements here, so Step 2's individual
error bounds can be summed. Substitute the three susceptibilities from
Step 1 to obtain all displayed coefficients.

## Scope and source

This identifies a real logarithmic variance in conserved source charges,
not just a Gaussian comparison. It does not show a parking pair bound
fails at mean spacing, because the evolved-field errors have no uniform
t estimate. It also does not prevent the charge difference eta-S_t from
having a well-defined potential; its cross-covariances must be retained.

Sources: C19 for signed susceptibility, C23 for the exact exploration
posterior, Lawler--Limic Theorem 4.3.1 for the normalized Green asymptotic,
and source finite propagation. All covariance and cutoff steps are given
explicitly above.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:910b07332d3c65bdc4ce5cdeda4b2465d185fe70eef164a8962607b3724a5daf","revision_digest":"sha256:9ec7441593a959d5ce2da020dde07bc2bb522980d5661f7063a980a2219b64b8","source_id":"own-work:w661:I0005-C24:v1","source_revision":"v1; packaged 2026-10-14T07:46:54.3984460+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2609.00483, 'On Embedding Hamming Spheres with Applications to Positive Curvature'] For a $p$-ary code $\mathcal C$ of dimension $k$ and length $m$, the \emph{\bf minimum distance} of $\mathcal C$ is
$$
d_{\mathcal C}=\min\{|x-y|:x,y\in\mathcal C,\ x\neq y\}.
$$
If $d_{\mathcal C}\ge d$, then $\mathcal C$ is called an $[m,k,d]_p$-code.

body: [Lemma 4.1 of arXiv:2608.14638, 'Randomly initialized autoencoders: fixed points and edge-of-chaos'] Let $g,h\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ be independent Gaussian vectors with i.i.d. entries $N(0,1)$, $\rho\geq 0$, $\mu\geq 0$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$. [Theorem 72 (Optimal strong stationary times for the reversed chain) of arXiv:2604.09933, 'Explicit cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles'] For the reversed chain, if \(p\ge2\), then \(\tau_{\mathrm{cov}}:=\min\{k:T_k=[n]\}\) is an optimal strong stationary time and, for every \(k\ge0\),
\[
\Prob(\tau_{\mathrm{cov}}>k)
=
1-P_k^{(m)}(0)
=
\sep\bigl((Q^{(m)})^{*k},U\bigr).
\]
If \(p=1\), then \(\tau_{n-1}:=\min\{k:|T_k|\ge n-1\}\) is an optimal strong stationary time and, for every \(k\ge0\),
\[
\Prob(\tau_{n-1}>k)
=
1-P_k^{(m)}(0)-P_k^{(m)}(1)
=
\sep\bigl((Q^{(m)})^{*k},U\bigr).
\]

body: In graph theory, the handshaking lemma is the statement that, in every finite undirected graph, the number of vertices that touch an odd number of edges is even. For example, if there is a party of people who shake hands, the number of people who shake an odd number of other people's hands is even. The handshaking lemma is a consequence of the degree sum formula, also sometimes called the handshaking lemma, according to which the sum of the degrees equals twice the number of edges in the graph. Both results were proven by Leonhard Euler in his famous paper on the Seven Bridges of Königsberg that began the study of graph theory.
title: Handshaking lemma

[Thm 16 (\cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $A$ and $C$ be real matrices of dimensions $m\times n$ and $q\times n$ respectively. Let $b$ and $d$ denote vectors in $\R^m$ and $\R^q$ respectively. Define
	\begin{align*}
	S_{A,C}(b,d)
	&\equiv \Big\{x\in\R^n: Ax\le b, Cx=d\Big\}\,,\\
	F(A,C)
	&\equiv\Big\{(b,d) \in\R^{m+q}:
	S_{A,C}(b,d) \ne\emptyset\Big\}\,.\end{align*}
Let $(b,d)\in F(A,C)$, so that 
$S_{A,C}(b,d)$ is nonempty. If $\hat{x}$ is any point in $\R^n$, then there is a point $\bar{x}\in S_{A,C}(b,d)$ with
	\[
	\|\bar{x}-\hat{x}\|_2
	\le \sigma(A,C)\left\|
	\begin{pmatrix}
	(A\hat{x}-b)_+\\ C\hat{x}-d
	\end{pmatrix}\right\|\,,
	\]
where $\sigma(A,C)$ is a finite number depending only on $A,C$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}

Klainerman's bounded $L^2$ curvature conjecture posits that the Cauchy problem for the vacuum Einstein equations admits a unique local solution for initial data whose Riemannian curvature tensor satisfies $Rm(g) \in L^2_{loc}(\Sigma)$ and second fundamental form satisfies $h \in H^1_{loc}(\Sigma)$ (corresponding to the critical Sobolev threshold $s = 2$). The conjecture was resolved affirmatively by Klainerman, Rodnianski, and Szeftel in spacetimes admitting a maximal foliation.
Initial slice has Rm \in L^2 and h \in H^1
Critical regularity threshold for 3+1 Einstein equations

[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2605.27713, 'Lower path regularity in all dimensions'] Suppose that $X=(X_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ satisfies Assumption \ref{a1} (i). Let $0\leq \alpha < d$ and $0\leq \beta \leq 1$ be such that 
		\eqref{eq:key-restriction} holds. The random field $(x,t)\mapsto L^{\alpha,X}(x,[0,t])$ (has a modification which) is $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. jointly H\"older continuous in $(x,t)\in \mathbb{R}^d\times [0,T]$. 
		
		More precisely, for any cube $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, any $0<\gamma_1<\beta$ and any $0<\gamma_2<1-H(d-\alpha)$  there exists a random variable $A$ such that $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. we have 
		\[|L^{\alpha,X}(x+h,[u,v])-L^{\alpha,X}(x,[u,v])|\leq A\|h\|^{\gamma_1}(v-u)^{\gamma_2}\]
		for all $x,x+h\in Q$ and all $0\leq u<v\leq T$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 14 of arXiv:2605.27713

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Any Hilbert space $H$ has an orthonormal basis $\{e_i\}_{i\in I}$, which is by definition a set of vectors whose span is dense in $H$, and which satisfy
$$<e_i,e_j>=\delta_{ij}$$
with $\delta$ being a Kronecker symbol. The cardinality $|I|$ of the index set, which can be finite, countable, or uncountable, depends only on $H$, and is called dimension of $H$. We have
$$H\simeq l^2(I)$$
in the obvious way, mapping $\sum\lambda_ie_i\to(\lambda_i)$. The Hilbert spaces with $\dim H=|I|$ being countable, such as $l^2(\mathbb N)$, are all isomorphic, and are called separable.

The survey records why: 'This specific distribution was needed to take advantage of Talagrand's influence inequality on the hypercube.' Any statement of the form 'BKS proved sublinear variance for FPP' without the two-point qualifier is a misquotation of the 2003 paper; the general-distribution version is Damron-Hanson-Sosoe, a decade later.

VERSION TRAP: the arXiv comment on v5 reads 'Replaced theorem 2 (which was incorrect) by a new theorem'. Cite v5 or the journal version; a citation resolved to an earlier version can carry a withdrawn Theorem 2.

[Thm lower final of arXiv:2411.15724, 'Wasserstein Convergence Rates for Empirical Measures of Random Subsequence of $\{nα\}$'] Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be integer-valued i.i.d. random variables with characteristic function $\varphi$, and let $S_j = \sum_{i = 1}^{j} X_i$. Let $\alpha$ be an irrational number such that
$$\| q \alpha \| \leq C q^{-\gamma}$$
holds for infinitely many $q \in \mathbb N$ with some constants $\gamma \ge 1$ and $C > 0$. Suppose that
$$|1 - \varphi(x)| \leq c |x|^\beta $$
holds for any $x \in \mathbb R$ with constants $c > 0$ and $0 < \beta \leq 2$. Set $\mu_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{j = 1}^{n} \delta_{\{ S_j \alpha \}}$, $n \geq 1$. Then there exists $C' > 0$ such that
$$
\mathbb E \big[ \mathbb W_1(\mu_n, \mu) \big] \geq \frac{C'}{n^{1/(\beta \gamma)}}
$$
holds for infinitely many $n \in \mathbb N$. In other words,
$$
\limsup_{n \rightarrow \infty} n^{1/(\beta \gamma)} \mathbb E \big[ \mathbb W_1(\mu_n, \mu) \big] > 0.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm lower final of arXiv:2411.15724

[Lemma couplings for APCRW of arXiv:2605.26869, 'Law of Large Numbers for a random walk on dynamic environments with drift'] Let $K> 1$ such that $J \subseteq (K^{-1}, K)$, $\rho \in (K^{-1}, K)$, $\varepsilon \in (0, (K-\rho) \wedge \rho\wedge 1$, and $H, \ell, t \in \mathbb{N}$ be such that $\Cr{lower bound for t in sltc}\ell^2 < t < H/2$ and $(\rho + 3 \varepsilon/2)(t^{-1}\log t)^{1/2}\ell < \Cr{upper bound on t with epsilon in sltc}\varepsilon/4$.
Let $\eta_0, \eta'_0 \in \Sigma$ be such that for every interval $I \subseteq [0,H]$ of length $\ell$, we have that $\eta_0(I) \geq (\rho + 3\varepsilon/4)\ell$ and $\eta'_0(I) \leq (\rho + \varepsilon/4)\ell$. 
We then have a coupling $\mathbb{Q}$ of $\eta$ and $\eta'$ such that
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{Q} \left( \eta'_t|_{[t, H-t]} \preccurlyeq \eta_t|_{[t, H-t]} \right)
    \geq 1 - 4H \exp \left( -\Cr{prob bound for G in sltc} (\rho + \varepsilon)^{-1} \varepsilon^2 \sqrt{t}/4 \right).
\end{equation}

We then also have that condition (pe:couplings of the paper) holds for the APCRW when $\nu = 1$. 
Additionally, $\mathbb{Q}$ is local, meaning that $(\eta_t, \eta'_t)|_{[t, H-t]}$ depends only on the initial conditions $(\eta_t, \eta'_t)|_{[0, H]}$.

[Proposition 29 ({\cite{BB23}}) of arXiv:2510.27589, 'Geodesic switches and exceptional times in dynamical Brownian last passage percolation'] Fix $\mu\in (0,1)$. There exist positive constants $c,C,K,\delta_0,\beta$ such that for any $p=(x,s) \in [\![-(1+\gamma/2)n,-(1-\gamma/2)n]\!]_\RR, q\in [\![(1-\gamma/2)n,(1+\gamma/2)n]\!]_\RR$ additionally satisfying $\slope(p,q)\in (\mu,\mu^{-1})$, and for all $\varepsilon, n$ satisfying $\varepsilon^{1/\delta_0} n\geq K$, we have
  \begin{align}
    
    &\PP(|\underline{V}_n(p,q)\cap B_{\beta\varepsilon^{5/11}n^{2/3}}(\Gamma_{p}^{q})|_{\hor}\leq \varepsilon n^{5/3})\leq Ce^{-c\varepsilon^{-3/11}},\nonumber\\
    &\PP(|\overline{V}_n(p,q)\cap B_{\beta\varepsilon^{5/11}n^{2/3}}(\Gamma_{p}^{q})|_{\hor}\leq \varepsilon n^{5/3})\leq Ce^{-c\varepsilon^{-3/11}}.
  \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: {\cite{BB23}}

body:
[Cor of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let $(\ell, m)$ be a pair of natural numbers
	with 
	 $\ell \equiv 1 \bmod 4$  and $\ell \geq 9$.  If 
	$m \geq  \frac{7}{3}\ell +8$, there are infinitely many 
	distinct  smooth structures on $\ell \mathbb{CP}_{2}\# m \overline{\mathbb{CP}}_{2}$
	 for which no  compatible Einstein metric exists. Nonetheless,
there are also infinitely many choices of   	$(\ell , m)$  satisfying these conditions 
for which  $\ell \mathbb{CP}_{2}\# m \overline{\mathbb{CP}}_{2}$  also admits 
a different smooth structure for which Einstein metrics do actually  exist.

body:
[Defn def-le of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] Let $a,b\in\mathbbm Z$ with $a < b$ and let $Z : [a,b] \cap \mathbbm Z \to \mathcal V\mathcal G$ be a finite path in $\mathcal G$. 
The \textbf{loop erasure} of $Z$ is the path $\operatorname{LE}  : \mathbbm N_0 \to \mathcal V\mathcal G$ defined inductively as follows. 
Let $\operatorname{LE}(0) = Z_a$. Inductively, suppose $k\geq 1$ and $\operatorname{LE} (k-1)$ has been defined.  
If $\operatorname{LE} (k-1) = Z_b$, we set $\operatorname{LE} (k) = Z_b$. 
Otherwise, let $j_k$ be the last time at which $Z$ visits $\operatorname{LE}(k-1)$ and let $\operatorname{LE}(k) := Z_{j_k + 1}$.
title: Defn def-le of arXiv:2506.18827

body:
[Corollary cor:conditional-revealability of arXiv:2608.23860, 'Revelation Control'] Let $M_h=|m_h|$ and write
\begin{equation}
r(m,s)=s\,\psi(m/s),
\end{equation}
with the same zero-scale convention as in Theorem~(thm:two-coordinate-revelation of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \emph{Scalar-redundant regime.} If $\sigma_h=g(M_h)$ almost surely on a decision-relevant event $E$ for some measurable $g$, then
\begin{equation}
\mathcal R_{h\to h'}=\widetilde r(M_h)
\qquad\text{on }E,
\end{equation}
for the scalar function $\widetilde r(m)=r(m,g(m))$. Hence current margin is sufficient for the one-step oracle continuation value on $E$. A single monotone margin threshold requires the additional condition that $\widetilde r$ be monotone relative to the fixed compute price.
\item \emph{Nonredundant regime.} If the conditional law of $\sigma_h$ given $M_h$ is nondegenerate on a set of positive probability and, on the corresponding conditional support, $s\mapsto r(M_h,s)$ is strictly increasing, then the conditional law of $\mathcal R_{h\to h'}$ given $M_h$ is also nondegenerate on a set of positive probability. Consequently no measurable function of current margin alone can reproduce the oracle continuation value there.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Conditional value nonredundancy and scalar reduction
Tree pruning

body: The rank–nullity theorem is a theorem in linear algebra, which asserts:the number of columns of a matrix M is the sum of the rank of M and the nullity of M; and the dimension of the domain of a linear transformation f is the sum of the rank of f and the nullity of f.

[Theorem thmKP of arXiv:2411.07809, 'Pirogov--Sinai Theory Beyond Lattices'] Let $\alpha_1 \colon \mathcal P \to [0,\infty)$
  and $\alpha_2\colon \mathcal P \to [0,\infty)$ be two given functions and
  suppose that for all $\gamma \in \mathcal P$,
  \begin{align}
    
    \sum_{\gamma' \nsim \gamma}  |w_{\gamma'} |e^{\alpha_1(\gamma') + a_2(\gamma')}  &\le \alpha_1 (\gamma) \,.
  \end{align}
  Then the cluster expansion for the polymer model defined by
    any finite subset of polymers converges absolutely. Moreover, for
  all $\gamma \in \mathcal P$ we have
  \begin{equation}
    
    \sum_{\substack{X \in \mathcal X :\\ \exists \gamma' \in X, \gamma' \nsim
        \gamma }}   |w(X) | \prod_{\gamma' \in X} e^{\alpha_2(\gamma')} \le
    \alpha_1(\gamma) \,. 
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{kotecky1986cluster}

[Prop PL_implies_Hessian_control of arXiv:2411.11415, 'The ballistic limit of the log-Sobolev constant equals the Polyak--\L{}ojasiewicz constant'] Suppose $h \colon \R^d \to \R$ is such that $C_{\msf{PL}}(h) < \infty$,
and that $h$ has a unique minimizer $x_\star$, around which it is
$C^2$. Then the quadratic growth inequality~(equation eqn:qg of the paper)
implies that
\begin{equation}
\nabla^2 h (x_\star ) \succeq \frac{1}{C_{\msf{PL}}(h)}\,I\,.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Hessian of PL functions at the minimizer

body: Record of outside readings, 14 October 2026, of Y. Shmalo, The storage capacity of the Ising perceptron: verification of the outstanding numerical conditions (arXiv:2607.11010; repository yspennstate/ising-perceptron-capacity, tag v1.0). The first reader (a Claude model, fresh clone) found it correct with fixable gaps. F1: the third clause of Ding and Sun's Condition 1.2, that S_*'(lambda) has a positive limit as lambda -> 1, is asserted in Ding-Sun (journal p. 704) but not proved there, and the paper credits it to their endpoint calculation. F2: A = inf_s B is used as a C^2 function at 0 without the implicit-function step. F4: phi_v(0) = phi_v'(0) = 0 in Lemma 4.4 is asserted without computation. F5: two reductions in the Huang sweep are argued in prose only. The reader's own floating-point recomputation gives alpha_* = 0.833078599740, inside the stated interval, and every Ding-Sun sign matches. A follow-up proof closes F1, F2 and F4: S_*'(lambda) = -K_0/(2 c_lambda) + O(1 + log(1/(1-lambda))) with c_lambda = sqrt((1-lambda)/(1+lambda)) and K_0 < 0, so S_*'(lambda) -> +infinity as lambda -> 1, uniformly along the fixed-point curve in a box containing Ding-Sun's; A''(0) = -alpha E[E(xi)^2 (1 - E'(xi))] < 0 by the implicit function theorem; and phi_v(0) = phi_v'(0) = 0 is computed in every ray direction. That fix has had one review and is not yet in the posted repository; F5 remains open. The second reader (a Codex model), still auditing the Huang code and certificates on 14 October, found M. Stojnic, Binary perceptrons capacity via fully lifted random duality theory (arXiv:2312.00073, November 2023), which obtains the same value 0.8330786 at zero threshold from the fully lifted random duality theory at its second (stationarized) lifting level, in agreement with the replica-symmetry-breaking prediction; the reader judged that derivation to rest on assumptions not verified there. The repository's paper does not cite it. Not refereed.
title: Outside readings of the Ising perceptron capacity proof (arXiv:2607.11010), 14 October 2026: correct with fixable gaps, three of them since closed; earlier derivation by Stojnic

[Definition of arXiv:2609.03731, 'Weightings and Lie groupoids'] A \emph{weighting} of $M$ is a sequence of ideal sheaves
\[ C^\infty_M=\ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_0\supset \ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_1\supset \ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_2\supset\cdots \]
such that for every $p \in M$, there exists a coordinate chart $(U,\phi=(x^1,...,x^n))$ around $p$ and a weight sequence $w=(w_1,...,w_n)$, such that in $\phi$-coordinates, $\{\ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_k(U)\}$ is of the form (equation e:wt-loc-form of the paper). We refer to such a coordinate chart as a \emph{weighted coordinate chart}. The maximal weight $r$ across all weighted coordinate charts is assumed to be finite and is called the \emph{order} of the weighting. The pair consisting of the manifold $M$, together with a weighting of $M$, is called a \emph{weighted manifold}. A morphism of weighted manifolds from $(M,\ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_\bullet)$ to $(M',\ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}'_\bullet)$ is a smooth map $f\colon M\rightarrow M'$ such that $f^*\ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_k'\subset \ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_k$ for all $k$.

[Theorem thm:localization-modulus of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Under (equation eq:oracle-base-feasibility of the paper), every nonempty
\(\mathfrak X\subset
\mathfrak X_{s,\kappa}(\gamma,\overline\mu)\) satisfies
\begin{equation}

    \mathfrak R_{\mathfrak X}(\eta)
    \leq
    \frac{2}{\sqrt3c_\eta}\frac{\eta}{\kappa},
    \qquad 0\leq\eta<\eta_\star,
\end{equation}
where  $$  c_\eta
    :=\frac23-\overline C_2-\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right)\eta.$$

Suppose, in addition, that there exist
\(X_0=\{{\bm x}_1,\ldots,{\bm x}_s\}\in\mathfrak X\), a unit vector
\({\bm v}\in\mathbb R^3\), and \(t_0>0\) such that
\begin{equation}

    X_t:=\{{\bm x}_1+t{\bm v},{\bm x}_2,\ldots,{\bm x}_s\}\in\mathfrak X,
    \qquad 0\leq t\leq t_0,
    \qquad t_0\leq\frac{\delta_{X_0}}4.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}

    \frac{\sqrt{3(1-\bar\mu)}}2\frac{\eta}{\kappa}
    \leq
    \mathfrak R_{\mathfrak X}(\eta)
    \leq
    \frac{2}{\sqrt3c_\eta}\frac{\eta}{\kappa}
\end{equation}
whenever
\begin{equation}

    0<\eta<\eta_\star,
    \qquad
    \eta\leq\frac{\kappa t_0}{\sqrt{3(1-\overline\mu)}}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, on every uniform class containing such an interior
one-point displacement path,
\[
    \mathfrak R_{\mathfrak X}(\eta)
    \asymp_{\bar\mu, s}\frac{\eta}{\kappa}
    \qquad(\eta\downarrow0).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:properties of arXiv:2601.09976, 'Stochastic Calculus as Operator Factorization:\\ An Operator--Covariant Derivative and Uni'] The operator--covariant derivative $D_X \colon L^2(\Omega) \to \mathcal{H}_X$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \textup{Linearity:} $D_X(\alpha F + \beta G) = \alpha\, D_X F + \beta\, D_X G$ for $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$.
\item \textup{Boundedness:} $\|D_X F\|_{\mathcal{H}_X} \le C\,\|F\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ where $C = \|\delta_X\|_{\mathrm{op}}$.
\item \textup{Adjointness:} $D_X = \delta_X^*$, i.e., $D_X$ is the Hilbert space adjoint of~$\delta_X$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:hms_coupling_criterion of arXiv:2609.01697, 'Unique ergodicity of projective cocycles over the 2D stochastic Navier--Stokes equations'] Let $P$ be a Markov operator on a Polish space $\mathcal{X}$ admitting two ergodic invariant measures $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$, and let $m_i = P^{[\infty]}\mu_i$ for $i = 1,2$ be the associated path-space measures on $\mathcal{X}^\infty$. Then $\mu_1 = \mu_2$ whenever there exists a measure $\Gamma$ on the product path space $\mathcal{X}^\infty \times \mathcal{X}^\infty$ such that:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item The two marginals of $\Gamma$ are absolutely continuous with respect
      to $m_1$ and $m_2$, respectively.
    \item $\Gamma$ assigns positive measure to the diagonal
      \begin{equation}
        D = \Big\{ (z, z') \in \mathcal{X}^\infty \times
        \mathcal{X}^\infty : \lim_{n\to\infty} d\big(z_n, z_n' \big) = 0 \Big\} ,
        \qquad \Gamma(D) > 0 .
      \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.05514, 'It\^{o}'s formula for L\'evy-It\^{o} processes taking values in the dual of nuclear space'] Let $L$ be an $\Phi'$-valued c\`adl\`ag L\'{e}vy process with L\'{e}vy-It\^{o} decomposition \eqref{eqLevyItoDecomposition} and assume $\Gamma$ is a separable complete bornological nuclear space. 
Let $X$ be a L\'{e}vy-It\^{o} process of the form \eqref{eqDefiLevyItoProcess} for $U=B_{\rho'}(1)$. Let $F:[0, \infty) \times \Psi' \rightarrow \Gamma$ be a function of class $C^{1,2}$. We assume $F_{t}$ and $F_{xx}$ is uniformly continuous on bounded subsets of $[0,\infty)\times \Psi'$. Then  almost surely we have for every $t\geq 0$
\begin{flalign*}

[Theorem 29 (Canonical Decomposition) of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional representation of a compact Lie group $G$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a $G$-intertwining isomorphism
\[
\iota_\pi :
\mathrm{Hom}_G(E_\pi, V)\otimes E_\pi
\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;
V[\pi]
\]
induced by mapping $T \otimes v \mapsto T(v)$ for $T \in \mathrm{Hom}_G(E_\pi, V)$ and $v \in V$.
In particular, the multiplicity of $\pi$ is
\[
m_\pi = \dim \mathrm{Hom}_G(E_\pi, V).
\]

\item There is a $G$-intertwining isomorphism
\[
\bigoplus_{[\pi]\in \widehat{G}} \mathrm{Hom}_G(E_\pi, V)\otimes E_\pi
\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;
V
=
\bigoplus_{[\pi]\in \widehat{G}} V[\pi].
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Canonical Decomposition

[Proposition prop:SDPI:asynchronous of arXiv:2605.16904, 'Positive-rate PCA and IPS with stationary Bernoulli measures are rapidly forgetful \footno'] Let $\Sigma$ be a finite set.
	Let $\theta\colon\Sigma\times\Sigma\to(0,1)$ be a strictly positive stochastic matrix with stationary distribution~$q\colon\Sigma\to(0,1)$.  Let $\kappa>0$ be such that $\theta(a,b)\geq\kappa q(b)$ for each $a,b\in\Sigma$.
	Let $n$ be a positive integer.
	Then,
	\begin{equation}
		D\big(\underline{p}\widehat{\theta}_n \relto[\big] \otimes_{i=1}^n q\big) \leq (1-\sfrac{\kappa}{n}) D\big(\underline{p} \relto[\big] \otimes_{i=1}^n q\big)
	\end{equation}
	for every probability distribution $\underline{p}\colon\Sigma^n\to[0,1]$.
title: Strong data processing inequality for asynchronous updating

[Lemma lem.aux3 of arXiv:2607.10105, 'The four-dimensional Anderson model: a case study for critical SPDEs'] Let $A$ and $B$ be two finite subsets of $\mathbb{Z}^4$, and $M,N\in 2^\mathbb N$, such that the distance between any two points in $A$ is $\gtrsim M$, and the distance between any two points in $B$ is $\gtrsim N$. Then uniformly in $u\in\mathbb{Z}^4$ and in all parameters, we have
\begin{equation}\sum_{x\in A, y\in B}\mathbf{1}_{|u-x|\gtrsim M}\cdot\mathbf{1}_{|x-y|\gtrsim\max(M,N)}\cdot\frac{1}{|u-x|^2|x-y|^2}\lesssim |A|^{1/2}M^{-2}\cdot |B|^{1/2}N^{-2}\cdot\min(1,(Q/P)^{1/4}),
\end{equation} where
\begin{equation} P:=|A|\cdot M^4,\quad Q:=|B|\cdot N^4.
\end{equation}
title: Lemma lem.aux3 of arXiv:2607.10105

body:
[Definition def:two-stream of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$,
a \emph{send sequence}  
$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$, and a non-negative integer~$\tau$.
A \emph{two-stream process} 
with birth rate~$\lambda$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and start time~$\tau$ 
is a pair $Z=(Z^A,Z^B)$ of generalised backoff processes with 
send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$\tau$, 
birth distribution
 $\mathcal{D} =  \mathsf{Po}(\lambda/2)$
and some initial populations $\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^{Z^A}(\tau)$ and $\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^{Z^B}(\tau)$. 
We refer to $Z^A$ and $Z^B$ as the \emph{streams} of~$Z$. 
The streams
evolve independently  
except 
that $\mathbf{e}_j^{Z^A}(t)$ and $\mathbf{e}_j^{Z^B}(t)$ are defined as follows for $t> \tau$. 
\begin{itemize}
    \item  
If there are distinct $C$ and $D$ in $\{A,B\}$ such that
$s^{Z^C}(t) = 0$ and $s^{Z^{D}}(t)>0$ then for all $j$, $\mathbf{e}_j^{Z^C}(t)=\emptyset$. In this case, a bin~$J^D$ is chosen with probability proportional to $s^{Z^{D}}_{J^D}(t)/s^{Z^{D}}(t)$ and $\mathbf{e}_{J^D}^{Z^D}(t)$
contains a single uniformly-chosen ball from 
$\mathbf{s}^{Z^D}_{J^D}$.
Also, 
for all $j\neq J^D$, $\mathbf{e}_j^{Z^D}(t)=\emptyset$. 
\item Otherwise, for   all $j$, $\mathbf{e}_j^{Z^A}(t)= \mathbf{e}_j^{Z^B}(t)=\emptyset$.
\end{itemize}
There are no end-of-step arrivals after step~$\tau$. That is, for all $D\in \{A,B\}$, all $t> \tau$, and all positive integers~$j$, $\mathbf{arr}_j^{Z^D} = \emptyset$.
title: Definition def:two-stream of arXiv:2602.21315

[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2605.17296, 'Zero correlations and averaged fields of orthonormal Gaussian Functions'] Fix $m\ge 1$, $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_m \in \C$, and $a_1,\dots,a_m \in \R$. Then

\sum_{j=1}^m a_j \cG_N(\xi_j)
\inlawto N(0,\sigma^2),
\]
where
\[
\sigma^2
=
\sum_{j,k=1}^m a_j a_k \kappa(|\xi_j-\xi_k|).
\]
Consequently, the finite-dimensional distributions of $\cG_N$ converge to those of
the centered real Gaussian field with covariance $\kappa(|\xi-\eta|)$.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2605.02771, 'Universality in Deep Neural Networks:\\ An approach via the Lindeberg exchange principle'] Let \(L,n_0,n_{L+1},r\in\N\) be fixed, and assume that \(\sigma\) is  polynomially bounded
    to order \(r\) in the sense of \cite[Definition \(2.1\)]{MR4898096}. Under \textbf{Assumptions \ref{assum:weights}} and \textbf{\ref{assum:biases}}, the process
    \[
        x\mapsto z^{(L+1)}(x)
    \]
    converges weakly in \(C^{r-1}(\R^{n_0},\R^{n_{L+1}})\) to a Gaussian process
    \[
        x\mapsto \Zcal^{(L+1)}(x),
    \]
    whose \(n_{L+1}\) components are i.i.d.\ and whose covariance structure is defined recursively by
    \[
        K^{(\ell+1)}(x,y)=
        \begin{cases}
            c_b+C_W \E[\sigma(\Zcal^{(\ell)}(x))\sigma(\Zcal^{(\ell)}(y))], & \ell\geq 1,\\[0.3em]
            c_b+\dfrac{C_W}{n_0}x\cdot y, & \ell=0.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    The same convergence is true when the DNN \(z^{(L+1)}\) has zero biases and weights satisfying \textbf{Assumption \ref{assum:weights}}. The limiting Gaussian process is defined recursively as above, with \(c_b=0\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 17 of arXiv:2605.15501, 'Well-posedness of the obstacle problem for generalized Dean--Kawasaki equation\thanks{ The'] (Existence of solutions to the approximated penalized equation)
Let Assumption \ref{assu:assu for existence} and Assumption \ref{assu:assum for F} hold.
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\alpha,\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exists a solution $u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}$ of \eqref{eq:appro penalized eq}, defined on the original probability space $\Omega$, in the sense of Definition \ref{def:Weak solution approximating penalized}.
Furthermore, let $\chi_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}(x,\xi,t):=\mathbf{1}_{\{0<\xi<u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}(x,t)\}}$ be the kinetic function of $u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}$.
Then, $u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}$ satisfies that, almost surely for every $\phi\in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^{d}\times(0,\infty)\times[0,T))$,
\begin{align}
& -\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\chi_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}(x,\xi,s)\partial_s\phi(x,\xi,s)\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}\xi\mathrm{d}s\\
 & =\int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{\mathbb{T}^{d}}\bar{\chi}(u_{\mathrm{init}},\xi)\phi(x,\xi,0)\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}\xi-\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\mathbb{T}^{d}}\Phi^{\prime}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})\nabla_x u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\cdot(\nabla_x\phi)(x,u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon},s)\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}s\nonumber \\
  & \quad-\alpha\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\nabla_{x}u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\cdot(\nabla_{x}\phi)(x,u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon},s)\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}s\nonumber\\
 & \quad-\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\mathbb{T}^{d}}\big(F_{1}(x)[\sigma_n^{\prime}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})]^{2}\nabla_x u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}+\sigma_n(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})\sigma_n^{\prime}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})F_{2}(x)\big)\cdot(\nabla_x\phi)(x,u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon},s)\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}s\nonumber\\
 & \quad-\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{\mathbb{T}^{d}}\partial_{\xi}\phi(x,\xi,s)\mathrm{d}m_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}(x,\xi,s)-\int_0^{T}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\phi(x,u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon},s)\nabla_x\cdot g(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}s\nonumber \\
 & \quad+\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\mathbb{T}^{d}}\Big(\sigma_n(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})\sigma_n^{\prime}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})\nabla_x u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\cdot F_{2}(x)+\sigma_n^{2}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})F_{3}(x)\Big)(\partial_{\xi}\phi)(x,u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon},s)\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}s\nonumber \\
 & \quad-\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\mathbb{T}^{d}}\phi(x,u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon},s)\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}-\psi)^+\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}s-\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\mathbb{T}^{d}}\phi(x,u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon},s)\nabla_x\cdot(\sigma_n(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})f_{k})\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}B_{s}^{k},\nonumber
\end{align}
where the kinetic measure $m_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}$ is
\begin{align}\notag
m_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}&:=\delta_{0}(\xi-u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})\Big(\Phi^{\prime}(\xi)|\nabla u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^{2}+\alpha|\nabla u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^{2}\Big).
\end{align}
It follows from  (\ref{eq:priori}) that the $\{m_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\}_{(\alpha,n)\in(0,1)\times\mathbb{N}}$ are finite kinetic measures.

[Lem reach-join of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] For each $w>0$, the following statements hold$:$
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $($From reachability to join$)$.
    If $\Delta\rightsquigarrow_w\Delta'$, then

    S_\Delta\approx_wS_{\Delta'}.
    \]
    \item $($From join to reachability$)$.
    Let $S,S'$ be discrete $(k-1)$-spheres.

    \Delta\rightsquigarrow_{2w+4}\Delta'.
    \]
  \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 38 of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{thm:main}
Let \(w,w'>0\) and \(u,u'\geq 0\), and assume
\[
\frac{u}{w^2}=\frac{u'}{(w')^2}.
\]
Set
\[
a^2=w^2+u^2,\qquad b^2=(w')^2+(u')^2,
\qquad \delta=u+u'.
\]
Suppose 
\(c_{**}\) is the positive solution of
\[
\delta^2
=
\frac{
2c_{**}^4(c_{**}^2-a^2-b^2)
}{
(c_{**}^2-a^2+b^2)(c_{**}^2+a^2-b^2)
}.
\]

Let \(h_n\) be the hive obtained from the two deformed GUE minor processes by
applying the octahedron recurrence, and write
\[
q_n:=\operatorname{Density}(h_n).
\]
Then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(
q_n\,
\middle\|\,
\operatorname{Density}\bigl(\mathcal H_n(a\sqrt n,b\sqrt n,c_{**}\sqrt n)\bigr)
\right)
=
O(n\log n).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 38 of arXiv:2607.04138

[Proposition adj2 of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces and let $1\leq p<\infty$. \\
{\rm (1)} If the pair $(X^*,Y^*)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_p$, then it has the $\mathrm{SMP}_p$ for adjoint operators. \\
{\rm (2)} If the pair $(X^*,Y^*)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_p$ for adjoint operators, then it has the $\mathrm{SMP}_q$ for adjoint operators for every $q>p$.\\
{\rm (3)} If the pair $(X^*,Y^*)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_p$ for adjoint operators, then it has the weak$^*$-to-weak$^*$ maximizing property.

[Lemma 21 (Pseudo-dimension after affine parameter tying) of arXiv:2608.31157, 'Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations'] Let $\Phi$ be a fully connected $d$-input ReLU architecture with at least
one hidden unit, let $P_\Phi$ be its number of scalar weight and bias entries,
and let
$\calA\in\aff(M,P_\Phi)$.  If $U_\Phi$ is the total number of hidden
ReLU units, then
\begin{equation}
 \VCdim(\calF_{\Phi,\calA})
 \le\Pdim(\calF_{\Phi,\calA})
 \le8r_{\calA}(U_\Phi+1)
 \le8r_{\calA}P_\Phi.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $P_\Phi\le P$, then
\begin{equation}
 \Pdim(\calF_{\Phi,\calA})
 \le8P\min\{M,P\}.
\end{equation}

body: [Definition 3.3 (Hypergraph) of arXiv:2505.15746, 'Higher-order Structure Boosts Link Prediction on Temporal Graphs'] A hypergraph can be represented by a tuple (V, H). V = {n1, n2, ...} is the set of nodes. And the set of hyperedges is H = {Ei |Ei ⊆V; 1 ≤ i ≤m}, where Ei is hyperedge and m is the number of hyperedges. Furthermore, in homogeneous graphs, the construction of hyperedges usually relies on the enumeration of maximal cliques (Wang & Kleinberg, 2024).

Use the likelihood-tempered q_lambda and total-data objective J(rho)=-E_rho log p(D|theta) defined above. Let k_s(theta)=p(y|x,theta), m_lambda(s)=E_q_lambda k_s>0 for nu-almost every s, and define the one-sample update qtilde_lambda,s(dtheta)=k_s(theta)q_lambda(dtheta)/m_lambda(s), then qbar_lambda=E_s~nu qtilde_lambda,s. The new likelihood factor is untempered, and each updated posterior is normalized before averaging. Assume the covariance differentiation identity applies to each k_s, B(q_lambda)=E_nu[-log m_lambda] is finite, differentiation through nu is justified by a nu-integrable local envelope for |d log m_lambda/dlambda|, and E_nu E_qtilde_lambda,s |L|<infinity. Then Bprime(lambda)=J(qbar_lambda)-J(q_lambda)=n[Ghat(qbar_lambda,D)-Ghat(q_lambda,D)]. At lambda=1, Bprime(1)=0 iff the two empirical Gibbs losses agree; this is a stationarity criterion, not a minimization theorem. Under the covariance regularity also for f=-L, local CPE Bprime(1)<0 implies that, for every sufficiently small h>0, q_(1+h) has strictly smaller Bayes loss and empirical Gibbs loss than q_1, so q_1 underfits in the authors simultaneous-loss sense. If the finite minimum a=min_theta[-L(theta)] exists, local CPE also forces J(q_1)>a, or Ghat(q_1,D)>a/n.

body:
[Lemma lem:chain_of_pockets of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] For any $p,\delta \in (0,1)$ there exists $a > 0, \epsilon_0 \in (0,1)$ (depending only on $\kappa, \delta$ and $p$) such that for every $\epsilon \in (0, \epsilon_0)$ the following events hold with probability at least $1 - p$. 
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item There exist $x_1,\dots,x_n \in a \mathbf{Z}^2 \cap A_0^a$ and $y_1,\dots,y_m \in a \mathbf{Z}^2 \cap A_2^a$ such that $A_0 \subseteq \cup_{j=1}^n F_j \subseteq A_0^a$ where $F_j$ is the pocket with opening point $x_j$ for every $1 \leq j \leq n$, and $A_2 \subseteq \cup_{i=1}^m L_i \subseteq A_2^a$,  where $L_i$ is the pocket with opening point $y_i$ for every $1 \leq i \leq m$, and where all such pockets exist. 
        \item For each $z \in (a\mathbf{Z}^2 \cap A_0^a) \cup (a\mathbf{Z}^2 \cap A_2^a)$, the flow lines $\eta_z^0$ and $\eta_z^{-\epsilon}$ are $\delta$-close until $\eta_z^0$ exits $A_4^a$, and the flow lines $\eta_z^{-\pi}$ and $\eta_z^{-\pi-\epsilon}$ are $\delta$-close until $\eta_z^{-\pi}$ exits $A_4^a$.
    \end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:chain_of_pockets of arXiv:2411.13133

body:
[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2608.05679, 'Small ball probabilities and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for Gaussian Volterra p'] \cite[Lemma 4]{MS22a}
    Let $\beta\in \mathbb R$ and $\gamma>-1$.  Then, for every fixed $t>0$, the following asymptotic relations hold as $s\to0^+$.
		\begin{itemize}
			\item[(i)] When $\beta+\gamma<-1$,
			\[
			\int_s^t u^{\beta}(u-s)^{\gamma}du\sim s^{\beta+\gamma+1} \mathbf B(\gamma+1, -\beta-\gamma-1).
			\]
			\item[(ii)] When $\beta+\gamma=-1$,
			\[
			\int_s^t u^{\beta}(u-s)^{\gamma}du\sim \log \left(\frac{t}{s}\right).
			\]
			\item[(iii)] When $\beta+\gamma>-1$,
			\[
			\int_s^t u^{\beta}(u-s)^{\gamma}du\rightarrow \frac{t^{\beta+\gamma+1}}{\beta+\gamma+1}.
			\]
		\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 23 of arXiv:2608.05679

body:
[Defn def: DP of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] Let $n, m\geq 1$ and 
    let $M$ be an $m \times n$ matrix with non-negative entries. 
    Given $S\subset [m], T \subset [n]$, define the edge count as  
    \[
    e_{M}(S,T):=\sum_{i \in S}\sum_{j \in T} M_{ij}.
    \]
    Furthermore, we say that the matrix $M$ has the discrepancy property $DP(\delta,\kappa_1, \kappa_2)$ with parameters 
    $\delta \in (0,1)$, $\kappa_1>0$, $\kappa_2 \geq 0$ 
    if for all nonempty $S \subset [m]$ and $T \subset [n]$  either 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[(1)] $\frac{e_{M}(S,T)}{\delta|S||T|} \leq \kappa_1$, or 
        \item[(2)] $e_{M}(S,T) \log \frac{e_{M}(S,T)}{\delta|S||T|} \leq \kappa_2 (|S| \vee |T|) \log \frac{en}{|S| \vee |T|}$.
    \end{itemize}
title: Defn def: DP of arXiv:2604.10446

body:
[Theorem thm:Main of arXiv:2606.19313, 'Stability of Khintchine-type inequalities via log-monotonicity'] Let $X$ be a symmetric random variable, $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ iid copies of $X$ and $r_k=r_k(X)$. Let $(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $p\geq 2$ be an even integer. Then the following bounds hold for the sum $S=\sum_ka_kX_k$. Moreover, the constants are optimal.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $(r_k)$ is log-concave, then $\big( \frac{\| X \|_p}{\| X \|_2}\big) \| S \|_2\leq \| S \|_p\leq \gamma_p\| S \|_2$;\\

\item If $(r_k)$ is log-convex, then $\gamma_p\| S \|_2\leq \| S \|_p\leq \big( \frac{\| X \|_p}{\| X \|_2}\big) \| S \|_2$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:Main of arXiv:2606.19313

body:
[Thm 2 of arXiv:2605.07050, 'Universality of the fluctuations of the free energy in generalized Sherrington--Kirkpatric'] Suppose that Assumption \ref{assump:decay} holds for $W$. Suppose that $\sqrt{N} x_k$  $(1 \leq k \leq N)$ are i.i.d., symmetric, and strictly sub-Gaussian random variables with variance $1$, independent of $W$. Define the likelihood ratios by
\beq
	 \caL(\SNR) := \E_\caX \left[ \prod_{i<j} \frac{p(\sqrt{N} W_{ij} - \sqrt{\SNR N} x_i x_j /\| \bsx \|^2)}{p(\sqrt{N} W_{ij})} \prod_k \frac{p_d(\sqrt{N} W_{kk} - \sqrt{\SNR N} x_k^2  /\| \bsx \|^2)}{p_d(\sqrt{N} W_{kk})} \right]
\eeq
and
\beq
	\ol \caL (\SNR) := \E_\caX \left[ \prod_{i<j} \frac{p(\sqrt{N} W_{ij} - \sqrt{\SNR N} x_i x_j)}{p(\sqrt{N} W_{ij})} \prod_k \frac{p_d(\sqrt{N} W_{kk} - \sqrt{\SNR N} x_k^2)}{p_d(\sqrt{N} W_{kk})} \right].
\eeq
Define
\[
	F_p:= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{(p'(x))^2}{p(x)} \dd x, \quad F_d:= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{(p_d'(x))^2}{p_d(x)} \dd x, \quad G_p:= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{(p''(x))^2}{p(x)} \dd x.
\]
Then, for any $\SNR \in (0, 1/F_p)$,
\[
	\log \caL(\SNR) \Rightarrow \caN(-\rho_L, 2\rho_L), \quad \log \ol \caL(\SNR) \Rightarrow \caN(-\rho_L, 2\rho_L),
\]
as $N \to \infty$, i.e., $\log \caL(\SNR)$ and $\log \ol\caL(\SNR)$ converge in distribution to the Gaussian with mean $-\rho_L$ and the variance $2\rho_L$ as $N \to \infty$, where
\[
	\rho_L:= -\frac{1}{4} \left( \log (1-\SNR F_p) + \SNR(F_p- 2F_d) + \frac{\SNR^2}{4} (2F_p^2 - G_p) \right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 2 of arXiv:2605.07050

body: [Theorem 12 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] Let $\mu$ be a non-atomic measure on $[0,t]\times[\delta,1]$, finite on bounded sets. Suppose that the simple point process $\mathcal{N}$ is such that for any set $\Delta$ which is a finite union of rectangles (32) $P(\mathcal{N}(\Delta)=0)=\exp\{-\mu(\Delta)\}.$ Then $\mathcal{N}$ is a Poisson process with intensity measure $\mu$.

[Prop link-with-compositions of arXiv:2411.03065, 'Growing conditioned BGW trees with\\ log-concave offspring distributions'] Let ${\mathbf{w}}=(w_0,w_1,\dots)$ be a non-negative sequence which has no internal zeros and such that $w_0w_1>0$.
	Set ${\mathbf{b}}=(\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{n})_{n\geq 1}$.
	Then $({\mathbf{w}},{\mathbf{b}})$ is a non-degenerate weight pair.
	For $n\geq 1$ we have $\PFtrees{\mathbf{w}} n=\PFComp{{\mathbf{w}},{\mathbf{b}}}{n-1}$, and for $T\in\trees_n$ if we write $c(T)=\underline{n}_1 \cdots  \underline{n}_i$ and $\varphi(T)=(T^{[1]},\dots,T^{[i]})$, then
	\begin{align}
	\SimpGen{{\mathbf{w}}}{n}(T)=\PComp{{\mathbf{w}},{\mathbf{b}}}{n-1}\bigl(c(T)\bigr)\cdot\left(\SimpGen{{\mathbf{w}}}{n_1}\bigl(T^{[1]}\bigr)\cdots \SimpGen{{\mathbf{w}}}{n_i}\bigl(T^{[i]}\bigr)\right).
	\end{align}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a Hilbert space $H$, consider the linear operators $T:H\to H$, and for each such operator define its norm by the following formula:
$$||T||=\sup_{||x||=1}||Tx||$$
The operators which are bounded, $||T||<\infty$, form then a complex algebra $B(H)$, which is complete with respect to $||.||$. When $H$ comes with a basis $\{e_i\}_{i\in I}$, we have
$$B(H)\subset M_I(\mathbb C)$$
with the correspondence $T\to M$ coming via the usual linear algebra formulae, namely:
$$T(x)=Mx\quad,\quad M_{ij}=<Te_j,e_i>$$
In infinite dimensions, the inclusion $B(H)\subset M_I(\mathbb C)$ is not an equality.

body: Publication record. P. Thévenin (Electron. J. Probab. 25, 2020, Section 6.2) proved a central limit theorem for the numbers of vertices of fixed outdegree in a subcritical Galton-Watson tree conditioned to have n vertices when the offspring law has a power-law tail, and conjectured that it extends to every subcritical law without exponential moment and every critical law with infinite variance. Y. Shmalo, Non-Gaussian fluctuations of degree counts in conditioned Galton-Watson trees (2026) gives two offspring laws for which the extension fails, an explicit subcritical law with finite third moment and no exponential moment and a critical law with infinite variance: along a sequence of sizes the centred and normalised number of vertices of outdegree one has a non-Gaussian limit, a mixture of two Gaussian laws. The second version (13 October 2026) adds, for Problems 21.2-21.4 of S. Janson, Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation (Probab. Surveys 9, 2012), a joint central limit theorem for the box counts of balls-in-boxes models below the critical density, and at the critical density under a second moment condition when the number of balls exceeds its critical value by at most O(sqrt(n)), and the two-Gaussian mixture for every fringe count with 0 < pi_A < 1, the leaves included. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/non-gaussian-degree-counts (commit 16f5fcef7b00); ResearchGate record 414333267. Not refereed; an outside audit is owed.

[Lem 174 (eighth moment bounds for $X^{\Ising}$, $X^{\trunc,\Ising}$, and $X^{\frozen,\Ising}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The bound of Lemma~\ref{l:subgaus.X.II}
also holds with $X^{\Ising}$ in place of $X^{\RomII}$: for $N$ large enough, we have
	\[
	\E\bigg[\bigg(
	\sum_{\ell=a}^{b-1} 
	\Delta X^{\Ising}(q_d,
	{i(q_{d+1})})
	\bigg)^8\bigg]
	\le L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a)^4
	\]
for all $0\le a\le b\le \dmax$. The same bound holds with 
$X^{\trunc,\Ising}$ or $X^{\Isplus}$ in place of $X^\Ising$. 

\begin{proof}
Recall from \eqref{e:Delta.X.Ising} that
	\[
	\Delta X^{\Ising}(q_d,i(q_{d+1}))
	= \sqrt{\delta_d}
	({\boldsymbol e}_i,\by(q_{d+1}))
	\]
where ${\boldsymbol e}_i$ is the $i$-th standard basis vector in $\R^N$.
The claim then follows essentially by the argument of Lemma~\ref{l:subgaus.X.II}, replacing $\bar{\bg}(q_d)/N^{1/2}$ with
${\boldsymbol e}_i$. (Moreover, since clearly $\|{\boldsymbol e}_i\|=1$, we can skip the step of restricting to the event that
$\|\bar{\bg}(q_d)\|$ is not atypically large.) It is straightforward to verify that the same argument applies with $X^{\trunc,\Ising}$ or $X^{\Isplus}$ in place of $X^\Ising$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: eighth moment bounds for $X^{\Ising}$, $X^{\trunc,\Ising}$, and $X^{\frozen,\Ising}$

Let N be a positive integer, R a commutative ring, f: D(N) -> R and F(n) = sum_{d | n} f(d) for n | N. Then f(n) = sum_{d | n} mu(n/d) F(d) for every n | N, where mu is the arithmetic Moebius function: mu(1) = 1, mu(m) = 0 if p^2 divides m for some prime p, and mu(m) = (-1)^omega(m) for squarefree m, omega(m) the number of distinct prime divisors. Equivalently, with P(n) the set of prime divisors of n, f(n) = sum over S subset of P(n) of (-1)^{|S|} F(n / prod_{p in S} p) (empty product 1).

On the uniform cube {-1, 1}^n let f be real, f^(S) = E[f chi_S] its Walsh coefficients and W_k = sum over |S| = k of f^(S)^2. For rho in [-1, 1], T_rho is the noise operator: T_rho f(x) = E[f(Y)] where the Y_i are independent with P(Y_i = x_i) = (1 + rho)/2, so T_rho chi_S = rho^|S| chi_S. For convex Phi on an interval containing the values of f, Phi(T_rho f(x)) <= T_rho(Phi o f)(x) for every x, and hence E[Phi(T_rho f(X))] <= E[Phi(f(X))] for uniform X. In particular ||T_rho f||_p <= ||f||_p for 1 <= p <= infinity. If -1 < rho < 1 and f is not constant, then min f < T_rho f(x) < max f at every x; for all rho in [-1, 1], min f <= T_rho f(x) <= max f.

[Proposition 4 (Positive and unitary zeros) of arXiv:2511.01456, 'Zero distribution of multiplicative Hermite and Laguerre polynomials'] Let $n\in \N$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)]
The positive case: For $s\geq 0$, all zeros of $H_n^*(\cdot; s)$ are real and positive.
\item[(b)]
The unitary case: For $s\leq 0$, all zeros of $H_n^*(\cdot; s)$ are located on the unit circle $\{z\in \mathbb C: |z| =1\}$.  \item[(c)] For all $s\in \C$, the multiset of zeros of $H_n^*(\cdot; s)$ is invariant w.r.t.\ the map $z\mapsto 1/z$.
\end{itemize}

[Corollary 29 of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] For every $1 \le i \le m \le 2^N - 1$, let $\mathrm{Poly}_{\emptyset}$ denote the number of operations required to compute
\[
\sum_{|\omega| = 1}^{\kappa} \sum_{m=i+1}^{j+1} K^{(\omega)}(i,m) \, \mathbf{X}^{(\omega)}_{m-1, m}.
\]

Then, for $d > 1$, there exists $\alpha^* \in [0,1/2]$ that maximizes the expression on the left, such that
\[
c\left(d^{1 - \alpha^*} \frac{2^{H(\alpha^*)}}{\sqrt{\kappa + \zeta}}\right)^{\kappa + \zeta}
\;\leq\; \mathrm{Poly}_{\emptyset} \;\leq\; C(d+1)^{\kappa+\zeta},
\]
where $H(\alpha) = -\alpha \log_2 \alpha - (1-\alpha) \log_2 (1-\alpha)$ is the binary entropy function and some constants $C,c \geq 0$ independent from $\kappa, \zeta$ and $d$.

In the special case $d=1$, we have
\[
\frac{2^{\kappa + \zeta}}{\kappa + \zeta + 1}  \leq \mathrm{Poly}_{\emptyset} \leq C\left(2^{\kappa + \zeta}\right).
\]

[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.00254, 'On the geometry and cohomology of almost abelian solvmanifolds'] Choose a basis $u_1,\dots,u_{2n}$ of $\mathfrak L$ and let $\bar u^1,\dots,\bar u^{2n}$ be the basis
of $\overline{\mathfrak L}$ determined by
\begin{equation}
2\left\langle u_a,\bar u^{b}\right\rangle=\delta_a^{b}.
\end{equation}
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item  The following decomposition holds
\begin{equation}
\textstyle\bigwedge^{\bullet}\mathfrak g^{*}\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C
=\bigoplus_{r=0}^{2n}\bigwedge^{r}\overline{\mathfrak L}\cdot\rho ,
\end{equation}
where each summand has dimension $\binom{2n}{r}$ and basis
$\left\{\bar u^{a_1}\!\cdots \bar u^{a_r}\cdot\rho\right\}_{a_1<\dots<a_r}$.

\item Let $N$ be the operator acting as multiplication by $r$ on
$\bigwedge^{r}\overline{\mathfrak L}\cdot\rho$. Then the spin action $\widehat{\mathcal J}$ of
$\mathcal J\in\mathfrak{so}\left(\mathfrak g\oplus\mathfrak g^*\right)$ is
$\widehat{\mathcal J}=\mathbf i\,(n-N)$. Consequently, setting
$\mathfrak U^{j}:=\ker\left(\widehat{\mathcal J}-\mathbf ij\right)$, we have
\[
 \mathfrak U^{\,n-r}=\textstyle\bigwedge^{r}\overline{\mathfrak L}\cdot\rho,
 \qquad \dim_{\mathbb C}\mathfrak U^{j}=\binom{2n}{n-j},
 \qquad \bigwedge^{\bullet}\mathfrak g^{*}\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C
 =\bigoplus_{j=-n}^{n}\mathfrak U^{j}.
\]

\item The Clifford action shifts the grading by one:
$\mathfrak L\cdot\mathfrak U^{j}\subseteq\mathfrak U^{j+1}$ and
$\overline{\mathfrak L}\cdot\mathfrak U^{j}\subseteq\mathfrak U^{j-1}$.

\item Conjugation reverses the grading, $\overline{\mathfrak U^{j}}=\mathfrak U^{-j}$, and every
element of $\mathfrak U^{j}$ has form-parity congruent to $n-j$ modulo $2$.

\item The grading is orthogonal for the Mukai pairing:
$\left(\mathfrak U^{j},\mathfrak U^{j'}\right)_{\mathrm{Mk}}=0$ unless $j+j'=0$, and the induced
pairing $\mathfrak U^{j}\times\mathfrak U^{-j}\to\mathbb C$ is perfect.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 8 (Canonical sausages) of arXiv:2608.26259, 'Cutoff with an $O(1)$ window for Potts Glauber Dynamics\\on lattice at High Temperature'] Let
\[
\Xi_i:=\{x\in\Xi:\ b(x)=i\},
\qquad
\Xi_{\ge3}:=\{x\in\Xi:\ b(x)\ge3\}.
\]
Then:

\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(x\in\Xi_0\), then \(y(x)=0\) and \(p(x)=1\).

\item If \(x\in\Xi_1\), then \(p(x)=p_1\), where 
\[
p_1=\frac1{2d}+O_{d,q}(\beta)
=\frac1{2d}+O_{d,q}(\alpha).
\]
Thus, after decreasing \(\beta_0(d,q)\), we have \(1/(4d)<p_1<1\).

\item If \(x\in\Xi_2\), then
$p(x)\in\{p_1,\ p_1^2\}$,
and in particular
\begin{equation}
0\le p(x)\le p_1.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.13732, '\textbf{On the First Hitting Time Problems \\ for Diffusion Processes: \\ Local Time-Space'] The cumulative distribution function $G(t,x)$ of the first-hitting time of the
upper boundary $b(t)$ is given by
\begin{align}
G(t,x)
=
\mathbb{P}_{T-t,x}\!\left(Y_T\ge b(0)\right)
+
\frac{1}{2}
\int_0^t
f(u)\,
q(T-u,b(u);T-t,x)
\,du
\end{align}
for $t\in[0,T]$, where $f(t)=G_x(t,b(t)-)\sigma^2(t,b(t))$
is the solution to the linear Volterra equation of the first kind
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}_{T-t,b(t)}\!\left(Y_T<b(0)\right)
=
\frac{1}{2}
\int_0^t
f(u)\,
q(T-u,b(u);T-t,b(t))
\,du
\end{align}
for $t\in[0,T]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given an ellipse, parametrized as usual as
$$\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)^2+\left(\frac{y}{b}\right)^2=1$$
with $a,b>0$, its area is $A=\pi ab$. As for the length, this is given by the formula
$$L=4\int_0^{\pi/2}\sqrt{a^2\sin^2t+b^2\cos^2t}\,dt$$
and with this integral being generically not computable.

Attributed primary-source theorem, not independently audited here. Let pi_t be the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck evolution of a law pi_0 on R^d with E_pi_0||X||^2<=M_2^2<infinity. Let e be in (0,1], and suppose supplied score estimates s_t have E_pi_t||s_t-grad log pi_t||^2<=e^2 at all relevant times up to T. Require global spatial Lipschitz control of the relative estimated score tilde_s_t(x)=s_t(x)+x: ||tilde_s_t(x)-tilde_s_t(y)||<=beta_tilde_0||x-y||/(1-exp(-2t)) for positive times. With T asymptotic to max{1,log((d+M_2^2)/e^2)}, the analysed denoising diffusion randomized midpoint method with its decaying schedule has output hat_pi and an intermediate pi_approx satisfying KL(pi_approx||hat_pi)<=O_tilde((1+log^2((1 vee beta_tilde_0)(d+M_2^2)))e^2) and W2^2(pi_approx,pi_0)<=O(e^2), using N=Theta_tilde(beta_tilde_0 sqrt(d+M_2^2)/e) steps. The theoretical variant samples each midpoint time tau_k on [0,rho_k h_k] with density proportional to exp(tau_k-h_k), with source-prescribed rho_k<1 sufficiently near 1. The bounds retain the source universal constants and logarithmic factors. The guarantee is hybrid KL/Wasserstein and assumes smooth supplied relative-score estimators; it is not a generic L2-oracle TV bound to unsmoothed data.
Source Assumptions 1–3, including Lipschitz control of the relative estimator s_t+x
Uniform absolute L2 score error e in (0,1] over the required source horizon
Finite second moment M_2^2
Relative estimated-score Lipschitz constant beta_tilde_0/(1-exp(-2t)) for all spatial pairs at positive times
Source-prescribed decaying step schedule, horizon and analysed truncated midpoint-time variant

    \[
    R_i \in \Gamma(G_i, \Hom((p^i_i)^*E^\bullet, (p^0_i))^*E^{\bullet+1-i}))
    \]
    such that the associated derivation on
    \[
    C^\bullet(G, E) := \Gamma(G_\bullet, (p^0_\bullet)^*E)
    \]
    defines a differential. The term $R_0$ can equivalently be expressed as a differential on $E$.

Let X be a metrizable topological space. A sequence of Borel probability measures (mu_n)_{n in N} in M_1(X) is asymptotically tight (or uniformly tight in Pollard's terminology) if for every epsilon > 0 there exists a compact subset K_epsilon subset X such that for every open set G subset X containing K_epsilon, liminf_{n -> infinity} mu_n(G) >= 1 - epsilon.
X is a metrizable topological space
(mu_n)_{n in N} in M_1(X)
title: Asymptotic Tightness (Uniform Tightness) on Metrizable Spaces

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2604.20617, 'Structured random perturbations of \\ tridiagonal twisted Toeplitz matrices'] Let $R_k^{(j)}$ be the $j$-th principal block of $R_n(a)$. Then, for a.e. $z \in \C$ and any $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\prob \left( \bigl| \log |\det(R_k^{(j)} - zI)| - k \gamma(jk/n,z) \bigr|  \geq k \varepsilon \right) = o(1).
\]
\begin{proof}
Let us fix $z \in K$ and $j \in \N$, with $1 \leq j \leq n/k$. Denote by $\alpha_r^{(n)}$, $\beta_r^{(n)}$, and $\zeta_r^{(n)}$ the entries of $X_n$ on the lower, main, and upper diagonals, respectively. In light of Theorem \ref{thm:approx}, it is enough to prove that
\begin{multline*}
\varepsilon_k=\max_{1\le r \le k} \bigg(
\left| d\left( \frac{(j-1)k+r}{n} \right) + \sigma_n \alpha_r^{(n)} - d\left( \frac{jk}{n} \right) \right|
+\left| b\left( \frac{(j-1)k+r}{n} \right) + \sigma_n \beta_r^{(n)} - b\left( \frac{jk}{n} \right) \right| \\
+\left| c\left( \frac{(j-1)k+r}{n} \right) + \sigma_n \zeta_r^{(n)} - c\left( \frac{jk}{n} \right) \right|
\bigg) \longrightarrow 0
\end{multline*}
in probability.

By the triangle inequality,
\[
\left| b\left( \frac{(j-1)k+r}{n} \right) + \sigma_n \beta_r^{(n)} - b\left( \frac{jk}{n} \right) \right|
\le
\left| b\left( \frac{(j-1)k+r}{n} \right) - b\left( \frac{jk}{n} \right) \right|
+ \sigma_n |\beta_r^{(n)}|.
\]
Since $b$ is uniformly continuous on $[0,1]$, its modulus of continuity
\[
\omega_b(\delta):=\sup_{|x-y|\le\delta}|b(x)-b(y)|
\]
satisfies $\omega_b(\delta)\to0$ as $\delta\to0$. Hence, uniformly in $j$ and $1\le r\le k$,
\[
\left| b\left( \frac{(j-1)k+r}{n} \right) - b\left( \frac{jk}{n} \right) \right|
\le \omega_b\!\left(\frac{k}{n}\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.
\]

For the random term, Chebyshev's inequality gives, for every $\epsilon>0$,
\[
\prob\!\left(\sigma_n |\beta_r^{(n)}|\ge \epsilon\right)
\le \frac{\sigma_n^2 \operatorname{Var}(\beta_r^{(n)})}{\epsilon^2}
\le \frac{C\sigma_n^2}{\epsilon^2},
\]
where $C>0$ is independent of $r$ and $n$. Therefore, by the union bound,
\[
\prob\!\left(\max_{1\le r\le k}\sigma_n |\beta_r^{(n)}|\ge \epsilon\right)
\le \sum_{r=1}^k \prob\!\left(\sigma_n |\beta_r^{(n)}|\ge \epsilon\right)
\le \frac{Ck\sigma_n^2}{\epsilon^2}.
\]
Since $k\sigma_n^2\to0$, it follows that
\[
\max_{1\le r\le k}\sigma_n |\beta_r^{(n)}| \longrightarrow 0
\qquad\text{in probability.}
\]

Applying the same argument to the lower and upper diagonals, we conclude that $\varepsilon_k\to0$ in probability. The claim now follows from Theorem \ref{thm:approx}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 19 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The following three estimates will be used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:mainwholeline}.

\textup{(i)} Assume $\lambda<\Lp(\R)$. Suppose that there exist $W\in C^1(\R)$, $W\ge1$, $W(x)\to+\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$, a compact interval $K$, and $\delta>0$ such that
\[
\cA_\R W+\lambda W\le-\delta W\;\hbox{in }\R\setminus K.
\]
Then $\cA_\R+\lambda$ satisfies the bounded maximum principle.

\textup{(ii)} Let $\lambda<\Lp(\R)$ and assume $\limsup_{|x|\to\infty}(a(x)+\lambda)<0$.
Then $\cA_\R+\lambda$ satisfies the bounded maximum principle. In particular, if $\Lp(\R)>0$ and $\limsup_{|x|\to\infty}a(x)<0$, then $\cA_\R$ satisfies the bounded maximum principle.

\textup{(iii)} For every $\mu\in\R$,
\[
\Lp(\cA_\R+\mu)\ge \mathfrak G(\mu).
\]
In particular, $\Lp(\cA_\R+\mu)\ge H_d(q_0)-\sup_\R(a+\mu)$.

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] A variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ follows the exponential law of parameter $\lambda>0$ precisely when the following happens, for any measurable function $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$:
$$E(\phi(f))=\lambda\int_0^\infty\phi(x)e^{-\lambda x}dx$$
Equivalently, we must have $f:X\to[0,\infty)$, up to a set of null measure, and given a measurable set $Y\subset[0,\infty)$, the following must happen:
$$P(f\in Y)=\lambda\int_Ye^{-\lambda x}dx$$
Also, in this latter statement, we can restrict the attention to the intervals $Y\subset[0,\infty)$.

[Thm 51 (Sawashita) of arXiv:2608.26698, 'Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion '] Given a space $X$, let $\mathcal{I}^h(X)$ be the group of homotopy classes of homotopy equivalences of $X$ that act trivially on $H_*(X)$.
      	\begin{itemize}
      		\item[(1)] There is an isomorphism \[\pi_3(S^2) \xrightarrow{\cong} \mathcal{I}^h(S^2 \vee S^3)\] mapping a homotopy class $a[\eta]$ to the homotopy class of the homotopy equivalence \[S^2 \vee S^3 \rightarrow S^2 \vee S^3 \vee S^3 \xrightarrow{i_1 \vee a\eta \vee j_1} S^2 \vee S^3,\] where $S^2 \vee S^3 \rightarrow S^2 \vee S^3 \vee S^3$ is the quotient map collapsing the equator of $S^3$ to a point, $i_1 : S^2 \hookrightarrow S^2 \vee S^3$ and $j_1 : S^3 \hookrightarrow S^2 \vee S^3$ are the inclusion maps, and $a\eta$ denotes a map representing the homotopy class $a[\eta]$.
      		
      		\item[(2)] Identify $S^2 \vee S^3$ with the 4-skeleton of $S^2 \times S^3$. Then there is a splitting short exact sequence \[0 \rightarrow \pi_5(S^2 \times S^3) \rightarrow \mathcal{I}^h(S^2 \times S^3) \rightarrow \mathcal{I}^h(S^2 \vee S^3) \rightarrow 0\] where $\mathcal{I}^h(S^2 \times S^3) \rightarrow \mathcal{I}^h(S^2 \vee S^3)$ is induced by restriction on the 4-skeleton, and $\pi_5(S^2 \times S^3) \rightarrow \mathcal{I}^h(S^2 \times S^3)$ is the homomorphism defined in Remark \ref{rmk:homotopyconstruction}. The action of $\mathcal{I}^h(S^2 \vee S^3)$ on $\mathcal{I}^h(S^2 \times S^3)$ is as follows: identify $\mathcal{I}^h(S^2 \vee S^3)$ with $\pi_3(S^2)$ via the isomorphism in (1), let $a[\eta] \in \pi_3(S^2)$ and $([x], [y]) \in \pi_5(S^2) \oplus \pi_5(S^3) = \pi_5(S^2 \times S^3)$ be homotopy classes, then \[a[\eta] \cdot ([x], [y]) = ([x] + [(a\eta) \circ y], [y]).\]
      	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 33 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] For later perturbation arguments we also record the adjoint critical limit and the resulting first-variation limit.

\textup{(i)} Let $\phi_\sigma^*>0$ be the positive adjoint eigenfunction of $\cA_{\sigma,2,L}$. Normalize it by $\|\phi_\sigma^*\|_{L^2(-L,L)}=1$. Then
\[
\phi_\sigma^*\longrightarrow\phi_0^*\quad \hbox{strongly in }L^2(-L,L),
\]
where $\phi_0^*>0$ is the normalized Dirichlet principal eigenfunction of
\[
d_Jv''-(qv)'+av+\lambda_0v=0\quad \hbox{in }(-L,L),\qquad v(-L)=v(L)=0.
\]
The zero-extension energies satisfy
\[
E_\sigma(\phi_\sigma^*)\longrightarrow d_J\int_{-L}^{L}|(\phi_0^*)'|^2\,dx,
\]
and $\phi_\sigma^*(L)\to0$.

\textup{(ii)} Let $h\in C([-L,L])$ and, for $|\tau|$ small, replace $a$ by $a+\tau h$. Denote the corresponding principal eigenvalue by $\lambda_\sigma(\tau)$. Then
\[
\partial_\tau\lambda_\sigma(0)=-\frac{\int_{-L}^{L}h(x)\phi_\sigma(x)\phi_\sigma^*(x)\,dx}{\int_{-L}^{L}\phi_\sigma(x)\phi_\sigma^*(x)\,dx}.
\]
After normalizing the direct and adjoint eigenfunctions in $L^2$,
\[
\partial_\tau\lambda_\sigma(0)\longrightarrow-\frac{\int_{-L}^{L}h(x)\phi_0(x)\phi_0^*(x)\,dx}{\int_{-L}^{L}\phi_0(x)\phi_0^*(x)\,dx}.
\]
The right-hand side is the first variation of the local Dirichlet principal eigenvalue.
