[Lemma l:je-rs of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] Suppose that $f_t$, $\widehat f_t$ are Lipschitz in $x\in \mathbb R^n$ uniformly over $t\in [0,T]$, 
    \begin{align}
        & dx_t = f_t(x_t) dt + dB_t,&& x_0\sim  p_0\\
        
        &
        d\widehat{x}_t = \widehat{f}_t(\widehat{x}_t) dt+ dB_t 
        
        
        
        && 
        \widehat{x}_0\sim  p_0 
    \end{align}
    and define $\widehat{w}_t((\widehat{x}_s)_{s\in [0,T]})$ for $t\in [0,T]$ by 
    \begin{align}
    
        &d\widehat{w}_t = \omega_t(\widehat{x}_t)dt, && \widehat{w}_0=0
    \end{align}
    where (equation e:je-generic of the paper) and (equation e:je-generic-2 of the paper)
    is a SDE-ODE system arising from Jarzynski's equality applied to $\rho_t$, where $\rho_0= p_0$.  
    Let $ p_t$, $\widehat{p}_t$ be the distribution of $x_t$, $\widehat{x}_t$, respectively. 
    Below, $\widehat{w}_t=\widehat{w}_t((\widehat{x}_s)_{s\in [0,T]})$ unless specified otherwise.
    Let $Z_t = \mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}[e^{\widehat{w}_t}]$.
    Suppose
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item (Drift error)
        $\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\ba{\ve{\widehat{f}_t(x_t)-f_t(x_t)}^2}\leqslant \varepsilon(t)^2$.
        \item (Exponential upper tail for log-weights)
        $\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\ba{e^{\widehat{w}_T}\mathds{1}_{e^{\widehat{w}_T}/Z_T\geqslant C_1}}\leqslant \varepsilon_1 Z_T$, for $\varepsilon_1 = \fc{c_3\varepsilon}{6 \exp\pa{\fc{3}{\varepsilon}\left( {\fc 12 \int_0^T \varepsilon(t)^2dt+1} \right)}}$.
        \item (Lower tail for log-weights)
        $\mathop{{}\mathbb{P}}\ba{\fc{e^{\widehat{w}_T}}{Z_T}\leqslant c_3}\leqslant \varepsilon_3$, for $\varepsilon_3 = \fc{\varepsilon}{6 \exp\pa{\fc{3}{\varepsilon}\left( {\fc 12 \int_0^T \varepsilon(t)^2dt+1} \right)}}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then for $L=\exp\pa{\fc{3}{\varepsilon}\left( {\fc 12 \int_0^T \varepsilon(t)^2dt+1} \right)}$, $\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\ba{
            \fc{e^{\widehat{w}_T}}{Z_T} \dd{ p_T}{\rho_T}(\widehat{x}_T)\wedge \fc{2C_1L}{c_3}}\geqslant 1-\varepsilon$, and given query access to $\dd{ p_T}{\rho_T}$, we can sample from $ p_T$ with TV error $2\varepsilon$ by $O\pf{C_1^2L^2\log\prc\varepsilon}{c_3^2}$ simulations of (equation e:je-generic of the paper), by choosing the parameters  $C_1'=C_2'=\fc{2C_1L}{c_3}$ and using the estimate 
            $e^{\widehat{w}_T} \dd{ p_T}{\rho_T}(\widehat{x}_T)$
            in \pref{a:ars}. 

Suppose moreover that $(\widetilde{x}_t)_{t\in [0,T]}$ is a process and $\widetilde{w}_T((x_t)_{t\in [0,T]})$ are weights such that 
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
    \item (Path error) 
    $\operatorname{TV}((\widehat{x}_t)_{t\in [0,T]}, (\widetilde{x}_t)_{t\in [0,T]}) \leqslant \varepsilon_4$, where $\varepsilon_4 = \fc{\varepsilon}{384C_1^{\prime2}}$.
    \item (Weight error) 
    $\mathop{{}\mathbb{P}}\pa{|\widetilde{w}_T((\widetilde{x}_t)_{t\in [0,T]}) - \widehat{w}_T((\widetilde{x}_t)_{t\in [0,T]})|>\fc{\varepsilon_4}2}\leqslant \fc{\varepsilon_4}2$. 
    \item (Ratio error) 
    $\widetilde R_2(x)$ is a (randomized) estimate such that there is $R_2(x)$ with $\dd{ p_T}{\rho_T} \propto R_2$ with
\begin{align*}
(a) &&\forall x,\quad  \mathop{{}\mathbb{P}}\pa{\fc{\widetilde R_2(x_T)}{R_2(x_T)}\nin [0, e^{\varepsilon_4/2}] \Big| x_T=x} &\leqslant \fc{\varepsilon_4}2\\
(b)&&    \mathop{{}\mathbb{P}}\pa{\fc{\widetilde R_2(x_T)}{R_2(x_T)}\nin [e^{-\varepsilon_4/2}, e^{\varepsilon_4/2}]}&\leqslant \varepsilon
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate}
Then we can sample from $ p_T$ with TV error $6\varepsilon$ by $O\pf{C_1^2L^2\log\prc\varepsilon}{c_3^2}$ simulations of (equation e:je-generic of the paper) using the estimate $e^{\widetilde{w}_T((\widetilde x_t)_{t\in [0,T]})} \widetilde R_2(\widetilde{x}_T)$
            in \pref{a:ars}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2604.25336, 'Central limit theorem for slow-fast system under mixed fractional Brownian motion'] Under assumptions \textbf{H1}-\textbf{H3}. Define \(\hat g(x,y):=g(x,y)-\bar g(x)\) and 
\begin{equation}
\Psi(x,y) =\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathcal{P}_t^x \hat g(x, Y_t^x) \dd t.
\end{equation} 
The \(\Psi(x,y)\) is the solution to the Poisson equation \eqref{Poisson_eq} where \(h\) is replaced by \(\hat g\).
Moreover, \(\Psi(x,y)\in C^2\). For all \((x,y)\in \mathbb{R}^n\times \mathbb{R}^m\), \(D_x\Psi(x,y)\) and \(D^2_{xx}\Psi(x,y)\) are linear growth. Specially,
\(D_y\Psi(x,y), D^2_{xy}\Psi(x,y), D^2_{yy}\Psi(x,y)\) are globally bounded. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 7 (Nondecreasing search-cost functionals) of arXiv:2605.26107, 'Radial Extremality for LRU Caching and the Fill--Holst Conjecture'] Under the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{cor:stack-depth}, for every
nondecreasing function $g:\{1,\ldots,N\}\to\R$,
\[
        \E_{p(\theta_2)}g(D)\le \E_{p(\theta_1)}g(D).
\]
The inequality is strict whenever $g$ is not constant.  In particular, the
LRU miss probability
\[
        M_C(p):=1-H_C(p)=\Pp_p(D>C)
\]
is strictly decreasing along every nonconstant ray away from uniform for
each $1\le C<N$, and the expected move-to-front search cost
\[
        \E_p D=1+\sum_{c=1}^{N-1}M_c(p)
\]
is strictly decreasing along every such ray.
title: Nondecreasing search-cost functionals

[Prop 3 (Rank-one Markov description of complex Gaussian growth) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\geq1}$ be independent centered circular complex Gaussian variables satisfying $\E\abs{\xi_{ij}}^2=1$. Let $((m_t,n_t))_{t\geq0}$ be a deterministic sequence of positive integer pairs such that exactly one coordinate increases by one at each step. Put
\[
 A_t=(\xi_{ij})_{\substack{1\leq i\leq m_t\\1\leq j\leq n_t}},
\]
let $\Lambda_t$ be the decreasing list of positive squared singular values of $A_t$, and let $\mathcal E_t$ be the sigma-algebra generated by the entries of $A_t$.

For $d\geq1$ and a decreasing positive list
\[
 \ell=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_l),\qquad l\leq d,
\]
define $R_d(\ell)$ as the law of the decreasing list of positive eigenvalues of
\[
 \diag(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_l,0,\ldots,0)+gg^*,
\]
where $g$ is a standard complex Gaussian vector in $\C^d$. Then $(\Lambda_t)_{t\geq0}$ is a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain relative to $(\mathcal E_t)_{t\geq0}$. Conditionally on $\mathcal E_t$, a column addition applies $R_{m_t}$ and a row addition applies $R_{n_t}$.

If $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ are the diagonal entries $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_l,0,\ldots,0$ and $q\notin\{b_1,\ldots,b_d\}$, then
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\det(qI_d-\diag(b_1,\ldots,b_d)-gg^*)\\
 &\qquad=\det(qI_d-\diag(b_1,\ldots,b_d))
 \left(1-\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{W_i}{q-b_i}\right),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where $W_i=\abs{g_i}^2$ are independent exponential random variables with density $\ee^{-w}$ on $w>0$. The eigenvalues of
\[
 \diag(b_1,\ldots,b_d)+gg^*
\]
interlace those of $\diag(b_1,\ldots,b_d)$.

Consequently, let $(M_N)_{N\geq1}$ be nondecreasing and define
\[
 X^{(N)}=(\xi_{ij})_{\substack{1\leq i\leq M_N\\1\leq j\leq N}},
 \qquad
 r_N=M_{N+1}-M_N.
\]
Conditionally on $X^{(N)}$, the law of $\Lambda_{N+1}$ is obtained from $\Lambda_N$ by applying $R_{M_N}$ once and then $R_{N+1}$ exactly $r_N$ times. If $r_N\leq K$ for all $N$, at most $K+1$ rank-one kernels occur in each transition.

[Theorem 27 of arXiv:2506.09637, 'Nonlinear Stochastic Filtering with Volterra Gaussian Noises'] Assume that Conditions \ref{cameron_martin_condition} and the hypotheses of Theorem
\ref{thm:lifted_rough_mz_wellposedness} hold. Let
\(
    \tilde{\varrho}(t,x)
\)
be the rough viscosity solution of equation \eqref{rough_mortensen_zakai}. Assume that
\[
    \tilde\pi_0(dx)=\tilde{\varrho}_0(x)\,dx.
\]
Then
\[
    \tilde\pi_t(dx)=\tilde{\varrho}(t,x)\,dx,
    \qquad t\in[0,T].
\]
In particular, the unnormalised filter admits a continuous density $\tilde{\varrho} = u$.

[Lemma 28 of arXiv:2506.09609, 'Schramm-Loewner evolution contains a topological Sierpi\'nski carpet when $\kappa$ is clos'] There exists a constant $C_1 = C_1(\varrho) \geq 100$ such that the following holds for all $N \geq C_1$ and any vertex sets $\{\mathcal{A}_m\}$ satisfying Conditions~\ref{condition:fractal-1} and~\ref{condition:fractal-2}, and $k \geq 0$.
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Any self-avoiding connected path at level $k$ whose $|\cdot|_\infty$-diameter is at least $N^k$ has length at least $N^{k/2}$. 

        \item For all $L \geq N^{k/2}$, the number of self-avoiding connected paths at level $k$ with length $L$ and starting from a fixed box is at most $(C_1)^L$. Moreover, any such path consists of at least $1/2$ fraction of boxes from $\mathcal{S}_0$. 
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm convergence of sizes and surpluses of ER of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{[Aldous_97_Brownian]}]  
  As $n \to \infty$, it holds that
  \begin{equation}
    (n^{-2/3} \bm{Z}^{n}, \bm{S}^{n}) \to (\bm{Z}, \bm{S})
  \end{equation}
  in distribution, where the convergence of the first coordinate
  takes place in $l^{2}_{\searrow}$,
  the set of infinite sequences $(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots)$
  with $x_{1} \geq x_{2} \geq \cdots \geq 0$ and $\sum_{i} x_{i}^{2} < \infty$,
  equipped with the usual $l^{2}$-norm. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop FKsummable of arXiv:2509.10990, 'On the Continuity of Enhancement Percolation'] Consider independent Bernoulli bond percolation on the sequence of tori $\set{\mathbb{T}_{2^{k}}}_{k \in \mathbb{N}}.$ For each $k \in \mathbb{N},$ let $A_k$ be a symmetric increasing event on $\mathbb{T}_{2^{k}},$ and let 
    \[r_c \coloneqq \sup\set{p : \limsup \mathbb{P}_p\left( A_k \right) = 0}\,.\]
    Then if $p < r_c,$
    \[\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \mathbb{P}_p\left( A_k \right) < \infty\,,\]
    and if $p > r_c,$
    \[\limsup_{k \to \infty} \mathbb{P}_p\left( A_k \right) = 1\,.\]

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: The all-one-ended event is not automatically a tail event Result: Take two disjoint one-ended infinite trees and add one edge joining them. Before the addition every component has one end; afterwards the connected tree has two ends, since deleting the joining edge separates two infinite pieces. Check: The added edge creates no cycle and the change is finite. Thus the property can change within the class of spanning forests under a finite edge modification. Obstruction: Uniform-forest tail triviality cannot be invoked until a separate tail representation of the event is proved. The example is a logical obstruction, not a uniform-forest counterexample.

[Lemma 14 (Asymptotic stability of the spherical transported flux) of arXiv:2609.00571, '\textbf{Shape Optimization and Bernoulli Free Boundary Problems\\ for the Riemannian $p$-L'] Let $L_\varepsilon'\to L$ and let $f_\varepsilon$ be the
$p$-harmonicity-preserving radial contractions defined by
\eqref{eq:spherical-conformal-radial-map}. Then
\[
A_\varepsilon
=
\frac{G_{\mathcal R}(L_\varepsilon')}
     {G_{\mathcal R}(L)}
\longrightarrow1
\]
and, by \eqref{eq:spherical-f-derivative},
\[
f_\varepsilon'(L)
\longrightarrow1.
\]
Consequently, if
\[
q_{\mathcal R}(L)
=
-\partial_{\nu_g}u(L)
=
-u'(L),
\]
then the transported geometric flux satisfies
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
Q_\varepsilon
\longrightarrow
q_{\mathcal R}(L).
}

\end{equation}
More precisely,
\begin{equation}
\left|Q_\varepsilon-q_{\mathcal R}(L)\right|
\leq
q_{\mathcal R}(L)
\left|
\frac{1}{f_\varepsilon'(L)}-1
\right|.

\end{equation}

[Theorem thmWood of arXiv:2607.06952, 'Universality for cokernels of partially random integral matrices'] {[Wood15]}
    Let $p$ be a prime, $u \geq 0$ an integer, $\varepsilon > 0$ a real number, and $B$ a finite abelian $p$-group. For each positive integer $n$, let $M(n)$ be a random matrix valued in $\M_{n \times (n+u)}(\mathbb{Z}_p)$ with independent entries $M(n)_{ij}$ which are all $\varepsilon$-balanced. Then \[\lim_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P}(\cok(M(n)) \simeq B) = \frac{\prod_{k=1}^\infty (1-p^{-k-u})}{|B|^{u}|{\mathrm{Aut}}(B)|}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition Continuous function spaces of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] For $A\subset\mathbb{R}$, let $C(A)$ denote the space of real-valued continuous
functions on $A$. We define
\[
    C_{\rm tem}(A)
    :=
    \left\{
        u\in C(A):
        \sup_{x\in A}|u(x)|e^{-a|x|}<\infty
        \text{ for every }a>0
    \right\}.
\]
For $\delta\in(0,1)$, define
\[
C^\delta(A)
:=
\left\{
u\in C(A):
\|u\|_{C^\delta(A)}
:=
\sup_{x\in A}|u(x)|
+
\sup_{\substack{x,y\in A\\x\ne y}}
\frac{|u(x)-u(y)|}{|x-y|^\delta}
<\infty
\right\}.
\] 
For any subsets $A$ and $B$ of Banach spaces, we denote by $C(A;B)$  the space of continuous functions from $A$ to $B$. We omit $A$ (or $B$) if $A$ (or $B$) is $\mathbb{R}$. We define $C_{c}^{\infty}$ as the space of infinitely differentiable function with compact support.

[Corollary cor:largest-nonprincipal-value of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] For every $h\geq2$ and $k\geq4$,
\[
 r_{h,k}(M_{h,k}-2)=2.
\]
Thus $M_{h,k}-2$ is the largest attainable cardinality outside the universal
principal skeleton.  It has a primitive complete-intersection witness, its
realization quasipolynomial has degree $k-2$, and its largest normalized
Hilbert-value stratum has dimension $k-4$.

[Lemma 58 of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] Let $g (t)$, $t \in [ 0, T )$, be a K\"ahler-Ricci flow under the circle-bundle ansatz \eqref{eq:ansatz} on compact two-nut closing, with $s$ the distance to $Q_0$. Then:

\noindent (i) We must have $q_1 = + 1$ and $q_2 = - 1$

\noindent (ii) About the two collapsing components $f_1$ and $f_2$:

\[
f_1^2 ( s ) \;=\; \int_0^s h\, d\sigma \,, \qquad f_2^2 ( s ) \;=\; \int_s^\ell h\, d\sigma \,,
\]
so that, on all of $\widehat{M}$, we have
\begin{equation}
f_1^2 \;+\; f_2^2 \;=\; L (t) \;:=\; \int_0^\ell h\, d\sigma \,.
\end{equation}
Furthermore, $f_1$ is related to $f_{k \geq 3}$ by the relations $f_k^2 = f_k^2 \big|_{Q_0} + q_k\, f_1^2$ for $k \geq 3$.

\noindent (iii) At the closings $Q_0$ and $Q_\ell$, the components $f_i$'s are given by:
\begin{align*}
f_i^2 \big|_{Q_0} (t) & \;=\; f_i^2 \big|_{Q_0} (0) \;+\; 2 \big( ( m_0 + 1 )\, q_i - p_i \big)\, t \,,\\
 f_i^2 \big|_{Q_\ell} (t) & \;=\; f_i^2 \big|_{Q_\ell} (0) \;-\; 2 \big( ( m_\ell + 1 )\, q_i + p_i \big)\, t \,.
\end{align*}
In particular, for $i = 2$ at $Q_0$ --- equivalently, by \eqref{eq:twonut_L}, for $i = 1$ at $Q_\ell$ --- they give the ``height'' of the $\mathbb{CP}^{m_0 + m_\ell +1}$-fibers:
\begin{equation}
L (t) \;=\; L (0) \;-\; 2 \big( m_0 + m_\ell + 2 \big)\, t \,,
\end{equation}
matching $\big\langle c_1 ( \widehat{M} ), [ \Lambda ] \big\rangle = ( m_0 + 1 ) + ( m_\ell + 1 )$ for a projective line $\Lambda$ in a fiber (\S\ref{subsec:periods-chern}).

\noindent (iv) There is $c > 0$ with

\[
f_k^2 \;\geq\; c\, ( T - t ) \quad ( k \geq 3 ) \qquad \text{and} \qquad L (t) \;\geq\; c\, ( T - t ) \qquad \text{on } \widehat{M} \times [ 0, T ) \,,
\]
each being a positive affine function of $t$, exactly as in Proposition \ref{prop:affine-laws}(iii). Note that no such bound holds for $f_1^2$ or $f_2^2$, as each of which vanishes on $Q_0$ and $Q_\ell$ respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 58 of arXiv:2609.03332

[Lemma lem:universal-root of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $X,Z\in\operatorname{End}(W)$ be arbitrary, let $a_1,\ldots,a_N$ be the Kac
orthonormal basis of $W=\mathfrak{so}(n)$, and put $A_i=\operatorname{ad}_{a_i}$.
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal R_i(X,Z)&=\{X,[A_i,Z]\}a_i,&
 U_i(X,Z)&=\{X,Z\}a_i,\\
 E_i(X,Z)&=\{[A_i,X],Z\}a_i,&
 \bar E(X,Z)&=\frac1N\sum_iE_i(X,Z).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.2.10a}
\]
Put $\Psi(T)=\sum_jA_jTa_j$.  Then, with no projection onto curvature
summands,
\[
 \mathcal R_i=A_iU_i-(E_i-\bar E)-\bar E,
 \qquad
 \bar E=\frac1N\sum_jA_jV_j+H(X,Z),\qquad V_j=XZa_j,
\tag{3.2.10b}
\]
where
\[
 H(X,Z)=\frac1N\{-X\Psi(Z)+Z\Psi(X)\}.
\tag{3.2.10b$'$}
\]
Moreover, writing $\|\cdot\|_2$ for Hilbert--Schmidt norm,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac1N\sum_i\|U_i\|^2
 &\le\frac4N\|X\|_2^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2,\\
 \frac1N\sum_j\|V_j\|^2
 &\le\frac1N\|X\|_2^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2,\\
 \frac1N\sum_i\|E_i-\bar E\|^2
 &\le\frac{16(n-2)}N\|X\|_2^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.2.10c}
\]
The residue satisfies
\[
 \|H(X,Z)\|
 \le\frac{\sqrt{n-2}}N
 \bigl(\|X\|_\mathrm{op}\|Z\|_2+\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}\|X\|_2\bigr).
\tag{3.2.10e}
\]
If $X$ and $Z$ are symmetric, then $\Psi(X)=\Psi(Z)=0$, so $H=0$.
The identities and estimates remain valid when all maps are tensored by
an ancillary identity and the Hilbert--Schmidt norm is taken on the
amplified space.

body:
[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] Let \( \Gamma \) be a functional satisfying Assumption~\ref{B1}, and let
  \(E_1,\dots,E_k\in\mathcal K\), \(k\geq2\), be compact sets. For
  \(\bm f\in C(\cup_{i=1}^kE_i,\R^d)\) and \(L\in\mathcal L\), put
  \[
    A_i=\{\Gamma_{E_i}(\bm f)>L\},\qquad
    C_i=\left\{\sup_{t\in E_i}\min_{j=1,\dots,d}f_j(t)>0\right\}.
  \]
  Then
  \[
    \bigcup_{i=1}^k A_i
    \subset
    \left\{\Gamma_{\cup_{i=1}^kE_i}(\bm f)>L\right\}
    \subset
    \bigcup_{i=1}^k A_i \cup
    \bigcup_{1\leq i<j\leq k}(C_i\cap C_j).
  \]
  Consequently, if \(\bm f\) is random, then
  \begin{align*}
    \pk{\Gamma_{\cup_{i=1}^k E_i}(\bm f)>L}
    &\leq
    \sum_{i=1}^k\pk{\Gamma_{E_i}(\bm f)>L}
    +\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq k}\pk{C_i\cap C_j},
    \\
    \pk{\Gamma_{\cup_{i=1}^k E_i}(\bm f)>L}
    &\geq
    \sum_{i=1}^k\pk{\Gamma_{E_i}(\bm f)>L}
    -\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq k}\pk{C_i\cap C_j}.
  \end{align*}

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] For every integer $n\geqslant 1$ and every $\kappa>0$, there are $
 \varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,\kappa)>0$ and $
 C=C(n,\kappa)>0$
with the following property. Let $(X,\ensuremath{\mathrm d},\mathcal H^n,x)$ be a pointed
$\operatorname{RCD}(-\eta,n)$ space, where $0\leqslant\eta\leqslant1$, and let
\[
 u=(u^1,\ldots,u^n):B_2(x)\to \mathbb R^n
\]
have harmonic components. Denote by $I$ the $n\times n$ identity matrix and put
\begin{equation}
 G_u:=\left(\langle\nabla u^i,\nabla u^j\rangle\right)_{i,j=1}^n,
 \qquad
 D:=\fint_{B_1(x)}|G_u-I|\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal H^n.
\end{equation}
If $D+\eta\leqslant \varepsilon$, then
\begin{equation}
 \fint_{B_r(x)}|G_u-I|\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal H^n
 \leqslant Cr^{-\kappa}(D+\eta)
 \qquad\forall 0<r<\frac14.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:interior-dirichlet-gmc-comparison of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Let $M_{h_D}^{\rm can}$ and $M_{h_U}^{\rm can}$ be the canonical GMC measures
obtained from the construction of Lemma~(lem:canonical-borel-gmc of the paper) on $D$
and $U$, respectively.  Under the coupling above, for every fixed $V\Subset U$,
almost surely,
\begin{equation}
 M_{h_D}^{\rm can}|_V
 =w_{D,U}\,M_{h_U}^{\rm can}|_V,
 \qquad
 w_{D,U}(z)
 :=\exp\!\left(
   \gamma\chi_{D,U}(z)
   -\frac{\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb E[\chi_{D,U}(z)^2]
  \right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 w_{D,U},\ w_{D,U}^{-1}\in C_b(V).
\end{equation}
In particular, the two measures in
(equation eq:interior-dirichlet-gmc-comparison of the paper) have the same null sets on $V$.

[Corollary 18 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\). For every \(x>0\), there exists a unique
\(\theta_a(x)\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
        \Lambda_a'(\theta_a(x))=x,
        \qquad
        J_a(x)=\theta_a(x)x-\Lambda_a(\theta_a(x)).
\]
Moreover, \(J_a\) is differentiable and strictly convex on \((0,\infty)\), with
\(J_a'(x)=\theta_a(x)\) and
\(J_a''(x)=1/\Lambda_a''(\theta_a(x))\). Finally, \(J_a\ge0\) on
\([0,\infty)\), and it vanishes uniquely at
\(\lambda_a=\frac{1}{4\pi}(1-\frac{1}{a})\).

[Lem limitXn of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] For all $x\in [0,\infty]$, all $n\geq 1$,
\[
X^{\mathrm{e}\infty,(n)}_t \leq X^{\mathrm{e}\infty,(n+1)}_t,\ \forall t\in [0,\infty)\quad \mathbb{P}_x\text{- a.s.}
\]
In particular, the sequence $\big(X^{\mathrm{e}\infty,(n)}\big)_{n\geq 1}$ admits an almost sure pointwise limit, and the following $[0,\infty]$-valued process is well-defined
\[X^{\mathrm{e}\infty}=\underset{n\rightarrow \infty}{\lim} \!\uparrow X^{\mathrm{e}\infty,(n)}.\]
title: Lem limitXn of arXiv:2605.06488

body:
[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $\chi$ is injective. Let $V$ be a $k[G]$-module with $\ell_V$ constant. Let $a\in C_m$ and $W:=U(a,1)$. We assume that $V$ is constant-indecomposable and we consider a direct sum decomposition into indecomposable $k[G]$-modules $V=\oplus_{i=1}^{\imath_V} U(a_i,b_i)$. Let 
$$J:=\{a_i+\epsilon|i\in\llbracket1,\imath_V\rrbracket\}.$$
Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} We have an identity
$$\dim_k\bigl(\Hom_{k[G]}(V,W)\bigr)=\begin{cases}1\quad\textup{if}\quad a\in J\\0\quad\textup{if}\quad a\notin J.\end{cases}$$

{\bf (2)} Let $(c,b)\in\mathbb J_{m,p^s}$. Then 
$$\dim_k\bigl(\Ext^1_{k[G]}(U(c,b),W)\bigr)=\begin{cases}1\quad\textup{if}\quad  a=c+\epsilon\;\textup{and}\;b<p^s\\0\quad\textup{if}\quad a\neq c+\epsilon\;\textup{or}\;b=p^s.\end{cases}$$

{\bf (3)} Suppose that $\jmath_V=0$. Then 
$$\dim_k\bigl(\Hom_{k[G]}(V,W)\bigr)=\dim_k\bigl(\Ext^1_{k[G]}(V,W)\bigr).$$
title: Proposition 17 of arXiv:2609.03191

[Definition def:inf-free-mom-cum of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $(\mathcal{A}, \varphi^{(0)}, \varphi^{(1)}, \ldots,
  \varphi^{(\nu)})$ be an infinitesimal non-commutative probability space of
  order $\nu$. The infinitesimal free cumulants of order $\nu$ are
  multilinear maps $(\kappa_n^{(0)}, \ldots, \kappa_n^{(\nu)} : \mathcal{A}^n
  \rightarrow \mathbb{C})$ uniquely determined by the following relation: For
  every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $i = 0, \ldots, \nu$ and $(a_1, \ldots, a_k) \in
  \mathcal{A}^k$,
  \begin{equation}
    \varphi^{(i)} (a_1 \ldots a_k) = \sum_{\pi = \{V_1, \ldots, V_p \} \in
    \ensuremath{\operatorname{NC}} (k)} \sum_{\lambda_1 + \cdots + \lambda_p = i}
    \frac{i!}{\lambda_1 ! \ldots \lambda_p !} \prod_{i = 1}^p \kappa_{|V_i
    |}^{(\lambda_i)} (a_1, \ldots, a_k |V_i) . 
  \end{equation}
title: Definition def:inf-free-mom-cum of arXiv:2412.09290

body:
[Definition def:biinf of arXiv:2607.05671, 'Bi-infinite systems of singularly interacting Brownian particles and the KPZ equation'] \normalfont

Let $X = \{X_i(t), t \in [0,\infty)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$, $L = \{L_{(i,i+1)}(t), t \in [0,\infty)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be collections of continuous, real-valued $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}$-adapted processes having the properties 
\begin{enumerate}[label = \arabic*.]

\item  For all $t \in [0,\infty), i \in \mathbb{Z}$,
\begin{equation} 
X_i(t) = x_i + B_i(t) + pL_{(i-1,i)}(t) - qL_{(i,i+1)}(t).
\end{equation} 

\item  For all $t \in [0,\infty)$, the sequence $\{X_i(t)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ is non-decreasing.

\item  For all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, $L_{(i,i+1)}$ is a continuous, non-decreasing process such that $L_{(i,i+1)}(0) = 0$ and $L_{(i,i+1)}$ can only increase at times $t \in [0,\infty)$ such that $X_{i+1}(t) = X_i(t)$, i.e. 
\[
\int_0^\infty (X_{i+1}(t) - X_i(t))dL_{(i,i+1)}(t) = 0.
\]
\end{enumerate}
We refer to $X = \{X_i\}$ as a \textit{bi-infinite system of singularly interacting Brownian particles with parameter $p$, initial condition $x$, and driving Brownian motions $\{B_i\}$.} The processes $\{L_{(i,i+1)}\}$ are called the \textit{local times} associated with the system $X$.

[Lem 31 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] There exists a constant $C > 1$ such that the following holds, whenever $q \in (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ and $a, b, c \in (1-\varepsilon, 1 + \varepsilon)$, for sufficiently small $\varepsilon \in (0, C^{-1})$. Fix $z_0 = (x_0,y_0) \in \mathfrak{L}_{q;a,b,c}$, and assume that $x_0\ge x^{SW}_{q;a,b,c}$ and that $\ell_{z_0}$ is the southwest edge of $\mathfrak{X}_{a,b,c}$. 
	 
	 \begin{enumerate} 
	 	\item We have that $C^{-1} (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2} \le -\partial_x \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2}$. 
	 	\item We have that $C^{-1} (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^{-1} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2} \le \partial_y \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^{-1} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2}$. 
		\item We have that $C^{-1} \mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^{1/2} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q}^{3/2} \le \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C \mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^{1/2} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q}^{3/2}$. 
		\item Assume that $z_0 = (x_0,y_0) \in \mathfrak{L}_{q;a,b,c}$ and $\ell_{z_0}$ is the southwest edge of $\mathfrak{X}_{a,b,c}$, but now $ x_0\le x^{SW}_{q;a,b,c}$. Then $C^{-1} (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2} \le -\partial_x \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2}$ remains valid, but now $C^{-1} \le \partial_y \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C$ and $C^{-1} \mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^2 \le \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C \mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^2$. 
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2604.19738, 'Phase Transitions in the Fluctuations of Functionals of Random Neural Networks \\'] Let $\kappa$ be such that $\kappa'(1)>1$ and assume that $\kappa'(0)\neq0$ if $\kappa$ is odd.
Then there exists a unique fixed point $b\in (-1,1)$.
Denote
\[
\rho= \kappa'(1),
\qquad
\lambda = \kappa'(b),
\qquad
\nu = \frac{-\log(\lambda)}{\log \rho},
\]
and define
\begin{equation}
\beta_L(x) = \frac{ \kappa_L(x) - b}{\lambda^L}.
\end{equation}

\noindent
If $\kappa$ is even or odd, set $K = (-1,1)$; otherwise, let $K= [-1,1)$.
Then the following properties hold:
Then the following properties hold:
\begin{align}

\beta_L(x) \longrightarrow \beta(x),
& \qquad x\in K,\\

\beta_L(1-x \nu^{-i}) \geq \lambda^i (1-x-b),
&\qquad x\in (1-c\nu^{-n},1), \quad c\in (0,1),\\

 -\beta(x) \asymp (1-x^2)^{-\nu},
& \qquad x\in (b,1), \\

 |\beta_L(x)| \lesssim  (1-x^2)^{-\nu},
&\qquad x\in K,\\

\kappa_L(x) \leq  1-c(1-\epsilon), &\qquad  x \in [0,1-c\mu^{-L}], \quad  c \in (0, \delta_\epsilon)
\end{align}
where $\delta_\varepsilon>0$.
Moreover, we have  $0\geq \beta_L(x)\uparrow \beta(x)$ for $x\geq b$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma Closure under subtraction of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:closure_under_subtraction}
Let $f,g \in \Sym$ with $\supp(g) \subseteq \supp(f)$. 
Let $C = \inf_{z \in \supp(g)} \frac{f(z)}{g(z)}$ and let $c \in [0,C]$. 
Then $h = \frac{f-cg}{1-c} \in \Sym$. 

Moreover, $\supp(h) \subseteq \supp(f)$, and if $\@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{\supp(f)} < \infty$ then the inclusion is proper if and only if $c = C$. 
\begin{proof}
Let $f,g \in \Sym$. 
First note that for $z \in \supp(g)$, $cg(z) \le Cg(z) \le f(z)$, so $f - cg \ge 0$ by construction. 
Also, $1-c = \sum_{z \in \supp(f)} (f(z) - cg(z))$, so $h$ is a PMF with $\supp(h) \subseteq \supp(f)$. 

Observe that for every $z \in \mathbb{R}$, both $\varphi = f$ and $\varphi = g$ solve the symmetry equation
\[ 

(\phi * f_X)(-z) = (\phi * f_X)(z) 

\]

This equation is linear in $\varphi$, so $\varphi = h$ is also a solution. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Closure under subtraction

[Proposition 17 (Continuity and stability of the $n$-atomic $q$-Bass map) of arXiv:2607.15872, 'Existence of $q$-Bass martingales in the semidiscrete setting'] Let $\nu \in \Prob_1(\RR)$ and let $q\in \Prob(\RR)$ be such that $q \ll \lambda$. Let $(\nu_k)_{k\in\NN}\subseteq \Prob_1(\RR)$ and $(q_k)_{k\in\NN}\subseteq \Prob(\RR)$ be such that
\[
    Q_{\nu_k}\to Q_\nu \quad\text{pointwise a.e.}, \qquad |Q_{\nu_k}|\le H \text{ for some } H\in L^1(0,1),
\]
and
\[
    q_k \ll \lambda, \qquad \rho_{q_k}\to \rho_q \quad\text{in } L^1(\RR).
\]
Let $f$ be the $n$-atomic $q$-Bass map with respect to $\nu$, $f^{(k)}$ be the $n$-atomic $q_k$-Bass map with respect to $\nu_k$ for $k\in\NN$, and $(h^{(k)})_{k\in\NN}\subseteq \RR_{\ge0}^{n-1}$. Then there exists a subsequence $(h^{(k_m)})_{m\in\NN}$, such that one of the following alternatives holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item there exists $h\in\RR_{\ge0}^{n-1}$ such that
    \[
        h^{(k_m)}\to h \qquad\text{and}\qquad f_j^{(k_m)}(h^{(k_m)})\to f_j(h) \quad\text{for every } j\in\{1,\dots,n-1\};
    \]
    \item there exists $i\in\{1,\dots,n-1\}$ such that
    \[
        h_i^{(k_m)}\to+\infty \qquad\text{and}\qquad f_i^{(k_m)}(h^{(k_m)})\to U_\nu(p_i^*).
    \]
\end{enumerate}
In particular, whenever $h^{(k)}\to h$ in $\RR_{\ge0}^{n-1}$, one has
\[
    f_j^{(k)}(h^{(k)})\to f_j(h) \qquad \text{for every } j\in\{1,\dots,n-1\},
\]
and any $n$-atomic $q$-Bass map is continuous. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Continuity and stability of the $n$-atomic $q$-Bass map

Version 1, Target 2; proof (unaudited). This supplies the named explicit remainder, not a new lognormal law. No novelty claim is made for the partition or connected-graph identities. The law itself is settled in the dossier and prior literature.

Fix k>=2 and c>=0. Let M_t=exp(-5t/2+sqrt(5t)Z), where Z is standard normal, 0<=t<=c. Set a_j=5j(j-1)/2, and let Pi_k denote partitions of [k]. For pi in Pi_k define

    w_pi=(-1)^(|pi|-1)(|pi|-1)!,
    H_pi=sum_(B in pi) a_|B|,
    W_k=sum_(r=1)^k S(k,r)(r-1)!,
    A_(k,s)=(1/s!) sum_(pi in Pi_k) w_pi H_pi^s.

Here S(k,r) is the Stirling number of the second kind and H^0=1 also at H=0. Define cumulants by the finite partition formula, not by an assumed finite moment-generating function. Then for every integer m>=0,

    |kappa_k(M_t)-sum_(s=0)^m A_(k,s)t^s|
       <= W_k exp(a_k c) (a_k t)^(m+1)/(m+1)! .       (1)

All constants are explicit finite sums. In particular, (1) is uniform over all integer L,n with 0<=L<=cn upon setting t=L/n. This is a statement about the limiting-law cumulant evaluated at that t, not a claim that it equals the exact finite-width cumulant.

Proof: E M_t^j=exp(a_j t). Finite moment-cumulant inversion gives

    F_k(t)=kappa_k(M_t)=sum_pi w_pi exp(H_pi t).

Since 0<=H_pi<=a_k, the exponential Taylor remainder for t>=0 is at most exp(a_k c)(a_k t)^(m+1)/(m+1)! termwise. Summing absolute weights proves (1). Every operation is on a finite partition set, so no analyticity of a probability MGF or interchange of an infinite moment series is used.

The coefficients of t^s vanish for s<k-1. To see this, put v=exp(5t)-1. The moment exp(a_jt)=(1+v)^(j choose 2) is the sum of v^|E| over all simple graphs on a fixed j-element set. Each graph uniquely decomposes into connected components. The finite partition moment-cumulant recursion therefore identifies F_k with the sum of v^|E| over connected simple graphs on [k]. Such a graph has at least k-1 edges. The first coefficient is 5^(k-1) times the number of labeled trees (equivalently k^(k-2), by the usual Prüfer encoding). This known identity explains cancellations; inequality (1) does not need tree enumeration.

For a scalar final preactivation Y_t=sqrt(q0 M_t) xi, q0>=0 deterministic and xi an independent standard Gaussian, all odd cumulants vanish and

    kappa_(2k)(Y_t)=(2k-1)!! q0^k F_k(t).

The same factor multiplies (1). This relation follows by substituting the finite-order formal moment series of q0 M into the Gaussian even-moment series; it does not require the actual series to converge.

Scope: for each fixed k, F_k is a finite sum of exponentials and is entire as a function of t; (1) is therefore stronger than a merely asymptotic fixed-k statement. [Lem cor:criticalptofGlo of arXiv:2508.04954, 'Conditional exponential directed last passage percolation under a one-point upper large de'] Let $\mathsf{z}_c=- \frac{\ell-a+b-\sqrt{D}}{2\ell}$, as in Lemma (lem:general_crit_behavior of the paper). 
Let  $z_{*}^{-} \le z_{*}^{+}$ denote the critical points of $\mathrm G_*$  for each $* \in \mathcal A_3$. Then, for every $\mathsf{q}\in \mathsf{R}_1\cup\cdots \cup \mathsf{R}_7$, 
\begin{equation} 
    z^+_{1} = z^+_3 = z^+_{12}  = z^+_{23}  = z_{123}^+ = \mathsf{z}_c. 
\end{equation}
Furthermore, the following results hold: 
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
    \item If $\mathsf{q}  \in \mathsf{R}_1$, then $ z^-_2<-1 < z^-_{23} < z^-_{3} < z_{123}^- < z^-_{12} < z^-_1 < \mathsf{z}_c = z^+_2 < 0$.
    \item If $\mathsf{q}  \in \mathsf{R}_2$, then $-1 < z^-_2 < z^-_{23} < z^-_{3} < z_{123}^- < z^-_{12} < z^-_1 < \mathsf{z}_c =z^+_2 < 0$.
    \item If $\mathsf{q}  \in \mathsf{R}_3$, then $-1 < z^-_3 < z^-_{23} < z^-_{2} < z_{123}^- < z^-_{12} < z^-_1 < \mathsf{z}_c = z^+_2 < 0$.
    \item If $\mathsf{q}  \in \mathsf{R}_4$, then $-1 < z^-_3 < z^-_{23} < z_{123}^- < z^-_{2} < z^-_{12} < z^-_1 < \mathsf{z}_c = z^+_2 < 0$.
    \item If $\mathsf{q}  \in \mathsf{R}_5$, then $-1 < z^-_3 < z^-_{23} < z_{123}^- < z^-_{1} < z^-_{12} < z^-_2 <  \mathsf{z}_c = z^+_2 < 0$.
    \item If $\mathsf{q}  \in \mathsf{R}_6$, then $-1 < z^-_3 < z^-_{23} < z_{123}^- < z^-_{1} < z^-_{12} < z^-_2 = \mathsf{z}_c  < z^+_2 < 0$.
    \item If $\mathsf{q} \in \mathsf{R}_7$, then $-1 < z^-_3 < z^-_{23} < z_{123}^- < z^-_{1} < z^-_{12} < z^-_2 = \mathsf{z}_c < 0 < z^+_2$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lem cor:criticalptofGlo of arXiv:2508.04954

[Corollary 22 (One-dimensional reduction and zero-field reference) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Under the model of Proposition~\ref{thm:conditional-gmm}, with \(\phi_r\) as in
\eqref{eq:conditional-cloning}, let
\begin{equation}

\kappa_t=a_t^2\delta^\top \Lambda_t^{-1}\delta,
\qquad
G_\pm(s)=\calN(s;\pm\sqrt{\kappa_t},1).
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}

\phi_r(t)
=
\int_{\R}
\frac{\alpha_+^2G_+(s)^2+\alpha_-^2G_-(s)^2}
{\alpha_+G_+(s)+\alpha_-G_-(s)}\,\dd s.
\end{equation}
In the zero-field reference case \(\eta(r)=0\), the origin \(z=0\) is a local
maximum of \(\log \widetilde p_t(z\mid r)\) if and only if
\(\kappa_t\le1\); for
\(\kappa_t>1\) it loses local maximality, becoming a local minimum in the
one-dimensional reduction and a saddle when \(d>1\).  Since
\(\kappa_t\) is nondecreasing along the reverse trajectory, and strictly
increasing whenever \(\delta\neq0\), the double-well landscape forms as
\(\kappa_t\) first crosses the threshold
\begin{equation}

\kappa_t=a_t^2\delta^\top \Lambda_t^{-1}\delta=1.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: One-dimensional reduction and zero-field reference

[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2604.13819, 'Convolution, cumulants and infinitesimal generators in the formal power series ring'] Let $\{X(s)\}_{s\ge0}$ be a one-dimensional L\'{e}vy process with the characteristic triplet $(\gamma,a,\nu)$ and $r>0$ such that $\int_{|x|>1} e^{r|x|}\nu(dx) <\infty$. For $A\in \mathcal{A}_r^{(-1)}$, we define $F(s,z):=A\boxplus^{-1} M_{X(s)}$. Then $F$ satisfies the $(-1,r)$-deformed Kolmogorov forward equation:
$$
\frac{\partial}{\partial s} \Phi_{-1} \bigl(F(s,\cdot)\bigr)(z) = \eta_{\gamma, a, \nu}(z) \Phi_{-1}\bigl(F(s,\cdot)\bigr)(z), \quad \text{on} \quad \mathbb{R}_{>0} \times \mathbb{D}_r.
$$
title: Proposition 21 of arXiv:2604.13819

[Prop 12 of arXiv:2606.04245, 'Properties of a Special Type of Filtration and its Martingale Criteria'] Assume $P(\gamma=+\infty)>0$, $\EE[\sup\limits_{t\in[0,+\infty)} |F(t)|]<+\infty$ and $\EE[|L|]<+\infty$. 
    Let $M$ be a local martingale on $\RRl_+$ defined by $M_t=F(t)\ind_{\{t<\gamma\}}+L\ind_{\{t\geq\gamma\}}$. 
    A necessary condition for the process $(M_t)_{t\in\RRl_+}$ to be a martingale is that the following equality holds on the set $\{\gamma=+\infty\}$: 
    $$
    \EE[L\mid\cH]\ind_{\{\gamma=+\infty\}}=F(0)\ind_{\{\gamma=+\infty\}}
    $$

body:
[Proposition prop:N-monotone of arXiv:2608.07042, 'Limit Points of Reflow with Minibatch Optimal Transport'] Let $\gamma\in\Gamma(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ be $N$-cyclically monotone and denote the corresponding velocities by $v_t=\argmin_{w_t\in L^2(\mu_t)}\mathcal L(w_t|\gamma)$. Then, the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $\mathcal L(v_t|\gamma)=0$.
    \item $\gamma$ is its unique rectified coupling, i.e., $\mathcal R(\gamma)=\{\gamma\}$.
    \item If $\mu_0$ is absolutely continuous, then $\gamma$ is rectifiable and there exists a monotone map $u$ such that $\gamma=(\mathrm{Id},u)_\#\mu_0$.
\end{enumerate}

body: Let g be a norm on R^2 that is even in the first coordinate (g(-h, m) = g(h, m)), as every lattice-symmetric FPP limit-shape norm is. For fixed m, the map h -> g((h, m)) is even and convex, hence minimized at h = 0, so g((h, m)) >= g((0, m)) = |m| g(e_2). Consequently, for a dogleg from (0,0) through v = (h, j) to (0, r) with j = r + m, m > 0 (longitudinal overshoot past the far endpoint): g(v) + g((0,r) - v) - g((0,r)) >= (r + m) g(e_2) + m g(e_2) - r g(e_2) = 2 m g(e_2), and symmetrically for j = -m < 0. The dogleg excess grows at least LINEARLY in the overshoot, with the explicit constant 2 g(e_2), using convexity and symmetry alone - no curvature hypothesis of any kind. The bound is tight as h -> 0. Use: in localization arguments it kills union sites with longitudinal overshoot at a rate no curvature assumption needs to fund, letting curvature windows be quoted only where they are literally assumed. Numerical attack: 0 violations in 300,000 trials on an anisotropic convex norm, worst ratio 1.000019.

[Theorem 1 (Inverse Riffle Shuffle with Concentrated Pile-Size Law) of arXiv:2605.19084, 'Limit Profiles for Separation Distance'] Let $f_n$ be a probability distribution on $[n]$, and consider the inverse riffle-type shuffle which chooses $K_n$ with law $f_n$, then moves a uniformly chosen set of $K_n$ cards to the top. Put $Y_n:=K_n/n$, and assume that $Y_n\to\alpha$ in probability for some $\alpha\in(0,1)$, with
$\operatorname{Var}(Y_n)=o\left(\frac1{\log n}\right).$
Define
$$q_{2,n}:=\sum_{k=1}^n f_n(k)\frac{\binom{k}{2}+\binom{n-k}{2}}{\binom{n}{2}}.$$
If $t_n$ is any sequence of integer times such that
$$t_n=\frac{2\log n+c+o(1)}{-\log q_{2,n}},$$
then
$$s_n(t_n)\to 1-\exp\left(-\frac12e^{-c}\right).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Inverse Riffle Shuffle with Concentrated Pile-Size Law

For d>=1, D=d(d+1)/2, noiseless IID standard Gaussian inputs and diagonal quadratic targets q_alpha=sum_i alpha_i x_i^2, any orthogonally equivariant measurable learner satisfying E||h-q_alpha||_L2^2<=epsilon||q_alpha||_L2^2 uniformly in alpha requires n>=ceil(D(1-epsilon)), 0<=epsilon<1. An equivariant minimum-norm quadratic least-squares learner recovers exactly at n=D, and a one-filter square CNN with only d readout coefficients trained recovers at n=d. Proof (unaudited), standard spherical-rank method specialized to a candidate source repair; no full minimax risk-curve equality or joint-GD claim.
d>=1, independent standard Gaussian inputs and noiseless targets with arbitrary real diagonal coefficients.
Population squared loss normalized by each individual target squared L2 norm; uniform expected guarantee.
Orthogonal equivariance is required for the D lower; the d-sample CNN upper uses coordinate patches and readout-only training.
Independent source-correction audit pending; no newness or frontier closure asserted.
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e171fa8587e4f09c53cdb48e0409d988c2e40c0c495318429a1a1a79d7447480","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e1/e171fa8587e4f09c53cdb48e0409d988c2e40c0c495318429a1a1a79d7447480.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:d298801d9e87ef8068b4206b4c0b86e44d799755f7a27d4b0928954567b699e8","bundle_entry_key":"li-zhang-arora-theorem54-norm-correct-replacement","bundle_id":"population.t407-draft-norm-correct-theorem54-replacement","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning theory","draft":"w693/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.sample_complexity:draft-norm-correct-source-theorem54-replacement-envelope","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Norm-correct replacement bound for the source quadratic regression problem

Status: proof (unaudited). This is a standard rank argument specialized to repair the source normalization, not a novel sample-complexity result. It makes explicit the expected-risk specialization already implicit in JOINT-005 and its queued brain card.

Let d>=1, D=d(d+1)/2, and P consist of x~N(0,I_d) with noiseless target q_alpha(x)=sum_i alpha_i x_i^2, alpha in R^d. The source expected complexity uses E_samples ||A(S)-q_alpha||_L2^2 <=epsilon ||q_alpha||_L2^2 uniformly in alpha.

For every orthogonally equivariant measurable learner A and 0<=epsilon<1, any n satisfying that guarantee necessarily obeys

    n >= ceil(D(1-epsilon)).

There exists an orthogonally equivariant learner that achieves zero error at n=D. Separately, a one-filter square-activation CNN with d scalar patches and only its d readout coefficients trained recovers every q_alpha at n=d. Thus the candidate replacement envelope is

    ceil(D(1-epsilon)) <= inf_(equivariant A) N_star(A,P,epsilon) <=D,
    inf_(specified CNN readout learners) N_star(A,P,epsilon) <=d.

The upper statement is existence of a learner, not an upper bound on every algorithm. No claim is made that the worst-case minimax risk curve equals1-n/D for intermediate n.

## Use the prediction norm, not the faulty source identity

For a real symmetric M, let q_M(x)=x^T M x. The true Gaussian inner product is

    <q_M,q_N>_L2 =2tr(MN)+tr(M)tr(N).

This follows by polarization of the corrected identity in SOURCE-011 (or direct fourth-moment expansion). It is positive definite on Sym(d), so the homogeneous quadratic subspace V has dimension D. Select any orthonormal basis phi_1,...,phi_D in this Hilbert space. The target q_theta=sum_j theta_j phi_j has prediction norm1 for every theta on S^(D-1). No ratio of expectations or uncertain source normalization is used.

Orthogonal equivariance under the Gaussian marginal transfers the learner's uniform normalized guarantee from diagonal targets to every homogeneous symmetric quadratic: diagonalize M and rotate inputs. Source Definition3.2 is sufficient, including for randomized algorithms. Hence a uniform prior on theta in S^(D-1) is a valid lower-bound prior, with exactly unit target prediction norm throughout its support. This transfer is used BEFORE averaging targets.

## Pair targets by a reflection fixing every observed label

Condition on the n input locations, independently of theta. Their evaluation matrix L has entries L_ij=phi_j(x_i) and rank r<=min(n,D). Let P be the Euclidean projection onto its row span, Q=I-P, and T=P-Q=2P-I. Then T is orthogonal, T^2=I and LT=L. The uniform spherical prior is invariant under T. This remains valid for D=1, where S^0 is the uniform two-point law.

Fix the learner's independent random coins. Targets theta and Ttheta produce identical labels and therefore exactly the same output h. If its L2 risk is infinite the lower bound is immediate. Otherwise orthogonally project h onto V, with coefficient vector gamma; projection cannot increase its squared distance from either target. Since theta=Ptheta+Qtheta and Ttheta=Ptheta-Qtheta,

    [||gamma-theta||^2+||gamma-Ttheta||^2]/2
       =||gamma-Ptheta||^2+||Qtheta||^2
       >=||Qtheta||^2.

Averaging over the spherical prior pairs theta and Ttheta without changing their law. Thus conditional average prediction risk is at least E_theta||Qtheta||^2=tr(Q)/D=(D-r)/D. The last equality uses E theta theta^T=I/D, valid also for D=1. Then average over inputs and coins. Since r<=n, the Bayes average risk is at least(1-n/D)_+. The uniform guarantee, transferred to every unit-norm quadratic, bounds that same average by epsilon, so n>=D(1-epsilon); integrality gives the ceiling. All integrands are nonnegative; Tonelli justifies averaging. No independence of conditional labels, posterior density formula, or product of conditional probabilities is assumed.

## Exact interpolation upper bounds

For the equivariant upper, minimize least-squares residual over Sym(d), choosing the unique minimum-Frobenius-norm minimizer. This is defined on every data set and commutes with orthogonal conjugation. At n=D its quadratic design is invertible almost surely: the D inputs e_i and e_i+e_j for i<j give an invertible evaluation matrix, first determining diagonals and then off-diagonals. Therefore its determinant is a nonzero polynomial in the sample coordinates; IID Gaussian inputs avoid its zero set almost surely. Exact recovery holds for every fixed quadratic target, yielding zero normalized expected risk. The zero target causes no division issue: the source guarantee is an inequality against epsilon times its squared norm.

For the CNN, one scalar shared filter w=1 with square activation and d independent readout weights represents sum_i alpha_i x_i^2. At n=d the design of squared coordinates is invertible almost surely, since inputs e_i give identity as a polynomial witness. Solving the readout linear system yields exact recovery for each fixed target. This is a readout-only upper, not a new claim about arbitrary joint-GD initialization. Joint-training candidates remain JOINT-005 and GD-006 v2.

## Verification and scope

The hardest imported source premise is only its model/algorithm definition, not its erroneous LemmaD.8 constant. The reflection identity is a finite algebraic identity and holds for any vector gamma, so it includes improper learners after Hilbert projection. If equivariance is removed, the lower transfer to all homogeneous quadratics fails: the coordinate-aware d-feature learner above is a counterexample to a universal D lower on diagonal targets. If inputs depend on theta, the independent fixed-input reflection prior argument fails. Noisy labels are not covered by the exact interpolation upper.

Primary context: Li-Zhang-Arora arXiv:2010.08515v2 Definition3.2, Theorem5.4 and AppendixD.6 pp21-22. The standard spherical-rank method was already in own JOINT-005/bundles003-004. x_1,\ldots,x_{p+q} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, we have
\begin{equation} 
\left| \rho^{(p+q)}(\bk x1{p+q}) - \rho^{(p)}(\bk x1p)\rho^{(q)}(\bk x{p+1}{p+q}) \right| \leq \omega_{p+q}(s),
\end{equation}
where $s := d(\bk x1p,\bk x{p+1}{p+q})$  is at (equation defs of the paper).
Denote 
$C_k:= \sup_s \omega_k(s)$ and observe 
that $(C_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ is non-decreasing.

\item  $\mathcal{P}$ has  {\em fast mixing  correlations} if 
$\omega_k$ is fast decreasing  for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$. 
\end{enumerate}

PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. Fix n>=1 integer, T>0, s in (0,1], c0 in [-1,1]. Start a two-input Gram chain with Q0=R0=s and C0=s*c0. Given each completed past, draw n iid centered Gaussian pairs (Ai,Bi) of covariance [[Ql,Cl],[Cl,Rl]], independently of previous layers, and update Qnew=mean tanh(Ai)^2, Rnew=mean tanh(Bi)^2, Cnew=mean tanh(Ai)tanh(Bi). Put Dl=1-Cl/sqrt(Ql*Rl), el=Ql-Rl, Hl=sum(j=1..l)1/j, H0=0; these variances are positive almost surely. Define K=32768*exp((105/2)*(4+T)), A=K*s*exp(3*T), B=264*exp(264*T)*A. For every integer 0<=l<=T*n: ||Ql*Rl*Dl||_2<=A*D0/(l+1), E(el^4)<=B^2*D0^2*Hl^2/n^2, E(el^2*Ql*Rl*Dl)<=A*B*D0^2*Hl/(n*(l+1)), and E(Ql^2*Rl^2*Dl^2)<=A^2*D0^2/(l+1)^2. Consequently sum(l=0..L-1)||el||_4^2<=B*D0*L*HL/n for 1<=L<=T*n. Norms are probability Lp norms. This uses the independently checked finite-width marginal bound T244-w691-C027 v1 and unaudited one-step lemma T250-w712-C013 v1. It closes the two radial mixed sources, not the stochastic angular gap or the full Tensor Programs rate. No Lean certificate is claimed.
Exact zero-bias critical tanh Gaussian Gram chain with fresh iid rows and layers
Deterministic equal initial variances s in (0,1], arbitrary c0 in [-1,1], n>=1 and l<=Tn
C013 v1 one-step fourth moment (unaudited); audited T244 C027 v1 finite marginal moments

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6438d50a85b4b0f985c1662c224b717d72d855a1551f851cd14c541d5ec9331c","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/64/6438d50a85b4b0f985c1662c224b717d72d855a1551f851cd14c541d5ec9331c.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:3a6490416b848b395f2baa9a7aed9d2f464c9bebbf32e151bc41dc071efbb6b1","bundle_entry_key":"tanh_radial_mixed_source_closure","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c014-radial-mixed-source-closure","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Quantitative Tensor Programs and stochastic two-input Gram propagation","draft":"w712/bundle_010.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:critical-tanh-two-input-radial-mixed-source-fourth-moment-closure","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C014 v1: closing the radial fourth-moment mixed sources

Kind: moved. Target: 1 (two-input critical tanh chain).
Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unverified. This closes a component of
C013, not the full Tensor Programs target or the stochastic angular error.

## Model and statement

Fix n>=1, horizon T>0, and deterministic initial Gram entries
Q_0=R_0=s in (0,1], C_0=s c_0, -1<=c_0<=1. Set D_0=1-c_0.
At each update the n Gaussian pairs (A_i,B_i), conditional on the past,
are iid with covariance matrix [[Q_l,C_l],[C_l,R_l]]. Define
Q_(l+1)=mean tanh(A_i)^2, R_(l+1)=mean tanh(B_i)^2,
C_(l+1)=mean tanh(A_i)tanh(B_i). All layers use fresh rows.
These matrices are positive semidefinite. Marginal variances are strictly
positive almost surely at each finite layer, and bounded by 1.
Write c_l=C_l/sqrt(Q_l R_l), D_l=1-c_l, e_l=Q_l-R_l,
H_l=sum_(j=1)^l 1/j, H_0=0. Norms below are probability Lp norms.

Use the following conservative explicit constants:

    K_T=32768 exp[(105/2)(4+T)],
    A_T=K_T s exp(3T), B_T=264 exp(264T) A_T.

For every integer 0<=l<=Tn,

    ||Q_l R_l D_l||_2 <= A_T D_0/(l+1),                  (1)
    E[e_l^4] <= B_T^2 D_0^2 H_l^2/n^2,                  (2)
    E[e_l^2 Q_l R_l D_l]
       <= A_T B_T D_0^2 H_l/[n(l+1)],                   (3)
    E[Q_l^2 R_l^2 D_l^2] <= A_T^2 D_0^2/(l+1)^2.       (4)

The constants are not claimed sharp. All expectations refer to the actual
coupled chain; Q and R, and their angular gap, are not independent.

## 1. Settled marginal input

We use T244-w691-C027 v1, equations (11)-(12) of
urn:mb-local:70868895e24d4cc2
The exact version has reviewer urn:mb-agent:d6ca7a10ae76247b PASS in its CLAIMS record;
the proof file retains its historical unaudited heading. Only its
unconditional finite-width moment bound is used, not its conditional
limiting-law consequence. It applies separately to both marginals here:
their shared rows across inputs do not change either marginal kernel.

For order 4, its nonsingleton partition constant is
C_4=6*3+3*3^2+4*15+105=210, and its c=1/2048.
Equation (12) gives, for 2<=l<=Tn,

    ||Q_l||_4 <= [8/(c l)] exp[C_4(4+T)/4]
                <= K_T/(l+1),

because (l+1)/l<=2. At l=0 and 1 the same last bound follows from
Q_l<=1 and K_T>=2. Identical bounds hold for R_l. We take this audited
scalar result as ground; the argument below concerns the coupled gap.

## 2. Unnormalized distance retains its initial-gap scale

Set P_l=Q_l+R_l-2C_l. This is the empirical squared distance and

    P_l=(sqrt(Q_l)-sqrt(R_l))^2+2sqrt(Q_l R_l)D_l >=0.

Given the past, A_i-B_i are iid N(0,P_l). Since tanh is 1-Lipschitz,

    P_(l+1) <= mean (A_i-B_i)^2.

For any integer p>=1, conditionally on the past,

    E[P_(l+1)^p | past]
       <= P_l^p product_(k=0)^(p-1)(1+2k/n)
       <= P_l^p exp[p(p-1)/n].                         (5)

The product is the exact pth moment of chi-square_n divided by n^p:
it follows from the Gaussian-square mgf (1-2t)^(-n/2), differentiating
p times at zero. When P_l=0 the difference is identically zero and (5)
continues to hold. Iterated conditional expectation, not independence of
states at distinct layers, proves

    E P_l^4 <= P_0^4 exp(12l/n),
    ||P_l||_4 <= P_0 exp(3T)=2sD_0 exp(3T).            (6)

## 3. The second mixed source

Let M_l=||Q_l R_l D_l||_2. The nonnegative distance identity gives
2sqrt(Q_l R_l)D_l<=P_l. Hence, pointwise,

    (Q_l R_l D_l)^2 <= Q_l R_l P_l^2/4
                        <= (Q_l+R_l)^2 P_l^2/16.

Cauchy-Schwarz and the triangle inequality now give

    M_l <= (1/4)||Q_l+R_l||_4 ||P_l||_4
          <= K_T s exp(3T)D_0/(l+1).

This proves (1) and (4), without separating dependent factors.

## 4. Closing C013 and the first mixed source

Use C013 v1 equation (1), with its B=e_l^2+8Q_lR_lD_l and a<=1.
C013 is an explicitly identified unaudited dependency; its finite
one-step estimate is not re-proved here. Put z_l=(E e_l^4)^(1/2).
Cauchy-Schwarz bounds E[e_l^2 Q_lR_lD_l]<=z_l M_l.
Expand C013's B and B^2 and take total expectations to obtain

    z_(l+1)^2 <= (1+18/n+1079/n^2)z_l^2
                  +(144/n+17264/n^2)z_l M_l
                  +69056 M_l^2/n^2.                  (7)

All coefficients and variables on the right are nonnegative. Since
528>=18, 69696>=1079, 528>=144, 139392>=17264, and 69696>=69056,
the right side is at most [(1+264/n)z_l+264M_l/n]^2. Thus

    z_(l+1) <= (1+264/n)z_l+264M_l/n.                 (8)

The equal initial variances give z_0=0. Iterating the deterministic
inequality (8), then applying (1), yields for l<=Tn

    z_l <= (264/n) sum_(j=0)^(l-1)
                    (1+264/n)^(l-1-j) M_j
         <= 264 exp(264T) A_T D_0 H_l/n.

Squaring proves (2). The same Cauchy-Schwarz estimate with (1) gives
(3). At l=0 these statements hold directly. If D_0=0 the paired features
coincide at every layer and all four inequalities hold with zero sides.
The case c_0=-1 is permitted and does not require a positive lower gap.

## Scope and remaining obstruction

The two mixed sources named at the end of C013 are now bounded entirely
in terms of the deterministic initial gap and explicit constants.
For L>=1, sum_(l=0)^(L-1) z_l <=B_T D_0 L H_L/n.
In particular H_L<=1+log L. For 0<eps<1 and L<=n^(1-eps),

    (L/n)(1+log L)
       <= [1+2/(exp(1) eps)] sqrt(L/n),

because sqrt(L/n)<=n^(-eps/2), log L<=log n, and
x exp(-eps x/2)<=2/(exp(1)eps) for x>=0.
Thus this accumulated radial source fits the requested sqrt(L/n)
scale, with eps-dependent constants. It does not by itself prove the
angular recursion, a readout Wasserstein bound, or all of Target 1.
The remaining hard step is the stochastic angular-gap recursion with
predictable products and their inverses: a final product depends on
future innovations, so its moment bound cannot simply be multiplied by
a martingale variance. A valid higher-moment martingale argument (or a
different coupling) is still required. No independence shortcut is used
in (1)-(8), and no Lean certificate or independent audit is claimed.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:216feb3ea89ec3c4c6ae401efd620ec0b5af7fa200bbd80b0095a2a64381ed0a","revision_digest":"sha256:a14105e6aaf1d0d303ba0f8c3af54056684b7bb7fa0880d7faa3310a92b82ab0","source_id":"own-work:T250-w712-C014-v1","source_revision":"C014-v1-2026-10-20","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Prp 2 of arXiv:2506.12755, '{\bf Stochastic intrinsic gradient flows on the Wasserstein space}\footnote{Supported in p'] Assume $(C_1)$. Let $\Lam$ be as in \eqref{eq:Lam}, $\gamma:\RR^d\times\scr P\to (0,\infty)$ be measurable such that $c^{-1}\leq\gamma(\cdot,\cdot)\leq c$
	for some constant $c\in(0,\infty)$ and $\Gamma$ be as in \eqref{eq:Gammadef}.
	
	
	(i) The bilinear form $(\EE^{\gamma,\Lam},C_b^1(\scr P_p))$, defined 
	\begin{equation*}\EE^{\gamma,\Lam}(u,v):=\int_{\scr P_p}\Gamma(u,v)(\mu)\LL(\d\mu),\qquad u,v\in C_b^1(\scr P_p),
	\end{equation*} 
	has a closed extension in $L^2(\scr P_p,\LL)$. Its minimal closed extension yields a quasi-regular, strongly local Dirichlet form $(\EE^{\gamma,\Lam},\D(\EE^{\gamma,\Lam}))$.
	In particular, there exists a non-terminating diffusion $(\Omega, \scr F,$ $(\mu_t)_{t\geq 0}, (\P^\mu)_{\mu\in \scr P_p})$ on $\scr P_p$ which is associated with $\EE^{\gamma,\Lam}$.
	
	(ii) There exist $\phi_{\mu,k}\in L^2(\RR^d\to\RR^d,\mu)$, $k=\N$, $\mu\in\scr P_p$, such that $D_{\phi_{\mu,k}}u:\scr P_p\to\RR$ is measurable for $u\in C_b^1(\scr P_p)$ and 
	\begin{equation*}
		\Gamma(u,v)(\mu)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty D_{\gamma_\mu\phi_{\mu,k}} u(\mu)D_{\phi_{\mu,k}}v(\mu)
	\end{equation*}
	for $\Lam$-a.e.~$\mu\in\scr P_p,$ $u,v\in C_b^1(\scr P_p)$.

[Lem 65 of arXiv:2608.28200, '\textbf On the Formality of Configuration Spaces of $\aka$'] Let $A,B$ be non-negatively graded CDGAs, and let $f:B\to A$ be a quasi-isomorphism. Assume there exist $z, \mu_1,\mu_2\in A^0$ and $\omega^1\in A^1$ such that 
$$
\omega^1=3\mu_1 d\mu_2 +d(-), \quad
z\omega^{1}= -2d\mu_1, \quad
\mu_1\omega^1=d\mu_2.
$$
Moreover, $z,\omega^1$ are $d$-closed and represent nontrivial cohomology classes in $H^\bullet(A)$. 

Then there exist elements $z_B, \mu_{1,B},\mu_{2,B},\omega^1_B \in B$ such that $z_B,\omega^1_B$ are $d$-closed, and
$$
f(z_B)=z, \quad 
f(\omega^1_B)=\omega^1+d(-), \quad
z_B\omega^{1}_B= -2d\mu_{1,B}, \quad
\mu_{1,B}\omega^1_B=d\mu_{2,B}, \quad
\omega^1_B=3\mu_{1,B} d\mu_{2,B} +d(-).
$$

If \(\beta_2<\infty\), then for any \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\),

 |\mathbb{E}[f(W)]-\mathbb{E}[f(Z)]| \leq \beta_{234}(1.8,3.58+0.55 \log d, 3.5) [f]_{\operatorname{Lip},1} .

body:
Every continuous map f from the closed unit ball B^n in R^n to itself has a fixed point: some x with f(x) = x. Convexity and compactness are what matter: the theorem holds for any nonempty compact convex subset of R^n in place of the ball.

In particular any continuous map of a nonempty closed interval [a,b] into itself has a fixed point. The hypotheses cannot be dropped in general: on S^1 in R^2, the half-turn f(x)=-x is continuous and has no fixed point although S^1 is compact; on R^n for n>=1, f(x)=x+v with v nonzero is continuous and has no fixed point although R^n is convex.

Then the map sending x to the point where the ray from f(x) through x exits the ball is a continuous retraction of the ball onto its boundary sphere. But no such retraction exists: it would induce, on the level of homology (or the fundamental group for n = 2), a factorization of the identity of the sphere through the trivial group of the contractible ball, a contradiction. Hence a fixed point exists. For the interval, g(x)=f(x)-x satisfies g(a)>=0 and g(b)<=0, so the intermediate value theorem gives a zero (the singleton case is immediate). The half-turn fixed-point equation x=-x forces x=0, outside S^1; the translation equation x+v=x forces v=0, a contradiction. To justify the general compact-convex case already stated by the keeper, choose a closed ball containing K and its nearest-point projection P onto K: existence follows from compactness, uniqueness from strict convexity of squared distance, and the projection variational inequalities give ||P(x)-P(y)||<=||x-y||. [Corollary 23 (Convergence forces both singular masses to vanish) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Assume \hyp{A1}{A1} and let $\alpha, \rho \in \Prob$. Then the distance splits, in
either order, as
\begin{equation}
  \tv{\alpha - \rho}
  \;=\; \sing(\alpha \mid \rho) + \bigl( \alpha_{\acp{\rho}} - \rho \bigr)^{+}(\XX)
  \;=\; \sing(\rho \mid \alpha) + \bigl( \rho_{\acp{\alpha}} - \alpha \bigr)^{+}(\XX) ,
  
\end{equation}
and consequently
\[
  \sing(\alpha \mid \rho) \;\le\; \tv{\alpha - \rho}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \sing(\rho \mid \alpha) \;\le\; \tv{\alpha - \rho} .
\]
In particular, under \hyp{A}{A}, if $\tv{T^{n}_{x} - \pi} \to 0$ for some $x \in \XX$,
then $\sing(T^{n}_{x} \mid \pi) \to 0$ and $\sing(\pi \mid T^{n}_{x}) \to 0$ for that
same $x$.

$(Z,U)$ and of the Borel representatives.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The variance of a variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ is given by
$$V(f)=E(f^2)-E(f)^2$$
with $E$ denoting as usual the expectation.

[Definition of arXiv:2504.03627, 'Richardson’s model and the contact process with stirring: long time behavior.'] A Markov process $(\eta_t)_{t\ge 0}$, taking values in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb Z^d)$, is called a \emph{growth model} if:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The law of the process is invariant by the translation $T_x$, for all $x\in \mathbb Z^d$. 
        \item The process is \emph{additive}, that is: if $A,B\subset \mathcal{P}(\mathbb Z^d)$, then $\eta^{A\cup B}=\eta^A\cup \eta^B$. 
        \item The process has \emph{nearest neighbor interactions}, which means that the process is local for $L=2$.
        \item The empty set is an absorbing state.
    \end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $\mathbf a_*\in D$ be a strict local minimum point of $H$, and choose
$\rho>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_*)\Subset D,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  H(\mathbf b)>H(\mathbf a_*)
  \quad
  \bigl(
  \mathbf b\in\overline{B_\rho(\mathbf a_*)}
  \setminus\{\mathbf a_*\}
  \bigr).
\end{equation}
Fix $\kappa,M,R>0$.  Then there exist positive constants
$C$, $\eta_0$, and $\varepsilon_0$, depending only on
$D,\mathbf a_*,\rho,\kappa,M$, and $R$, such that the following holds.

For every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, let
$\mathbf a_\varepsilon\in B_\rho(\mathbf a_*)$, and let
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(D)$ be nonnegative and satisfy
\[
  \int_D\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=\kappa,
  \qquad
  \|\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty\leq M\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R\varepsilon}(\mathbf a_\varepsilon).
\]
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of (equation eq:euler-intro of the paper).  If
\begin{equation}
  \eta_{\varepsilon,0}
  :=\mathcal D(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})
  +\kappa^2[H(\mathbf a_\varepsilon)-H(\mathbf a_*)]
  +\varepsilon
  \leq\eta_0,
\end{equation}
then, for every $t\in\mathbb R$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})\subset B_\rho(\mathbf a_*)
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal D(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})
  +\kappa^2\sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  [H(\mathbf b)-H(\mathbf a_*)]
  \leq C\eta_{\varepsilon,0}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: The Feynman–Kac formula, named after Richard Feynman and Mark Kac, establishes a link between parabolic partial differential equations and stochastic processes. In 1947, when Kac and Feynman were both faculty members at Cornell University, Kac attended a presentation of Feynman's and remarked that the two of them were working on the same thing from different directions. The Feynman–Kac formula resulted, which proves rigorously a real-valued analogy to Feynman's path integrals. The complex case, needed in quantum mechanics, is still an open question.
title: Feynman–Kac formula

[Proposition 7 (Quadratic local objective under scalar CFG) of arXiv:2608.29107, 'PathGuide: Dynamic Classifier-Free Guidance via On-Policy Transport Alignment'] Assume scalar CFG:
\begin{equation}
    v_t^\theta(x\mid y;\omega)
    =
    v_t^\theta(x\mid \varnothing)
    +
    \omega
    \Bigl(
        v_t^\theta(x\mid y)-v_t^\theta(x\mid \varnothing)
    \Bigr).
\end{equation}
For fixed \(y,\vec\omega_i,\psi\), define
\begin{equation}
    A_i(\psi)
    :=
    \int_{\R^d}
    \Bigl(
        u_{t_i}(x\mid y)
        -
        v_{t_i}^\theta(x\mid \varnothing)
    \Bigr)\cdot
    \grad\psi(x)\,
    \hat p_{t_i}(x\mid y;\vec\omega_i)\,\dd x
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
    B_i(\psi)
    :=
    \int_{\R^d}
    \Bigl(
        v_{t_i}^\theta(x\mid y)
        -
        v_{t_i}^\theta(x\mid \varnothing)
    \Bigr)\cdot
    \grad\psi(x)\,
    \hat p_{t_i}(x\mid y;\vec\omega_i)\,\dd x .
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal L_i(\omega_i\mid y;\vec\omega_i,\psi)
    =
    \bigl|A_i(\psi)-\omega_i B_i(\psi)\bigr|^2 .
\end{equation}
In particular, the exact local objective is quadratic in \(\omega_i\).

body:
[Defn def-geodesic of arXiv:2510.26123, 'Directed distances in bipolar-oriented triangulations:\\ exact exponents and scaling limit'] Let ${\operatorname{XDP}} \in \{\operatorname{LDP}, \operatorname{SDP}\}$. 
Let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a finite planar map equipped with an acyclic orientation of its edges and let $x,y\in\mathcal V(\mathfrak{m})$. 
We say that a directed path $\mathfrak{p} : [1,|\mathfrak{p}|]\cap\mathbbm Z \to \mathcal E(\mathfrak{m})$ from $x$ to $y$ is an \textbf{${\operatorname{XDP}}$ geodesic} if the length $|\mathfrak{p}|$ of $\mathfrak{p}$ is equal to ${\operatorname{XDP}}_\mathfrak{m}(x,y)$ (Definition~(def-ldp of the paper)). We say that $\mathfrak{p}$ is the \textbf{leftmost ${\operatorname{XDP}}$ geodesic} from $x$ to $y$ if every ${\operatorname{XDP}}$ geodesic in $\mathfrak{m}$ from $x$ to $y$ lies weakly to the right of $\mathfrak{p}$ if we stand at $x$ and look toward $y$. That is, every ${\operatorname{XDP}}$ geodesic from $x$ to $y$ lies in the submap of $\mathfrak{m}$ bounded by $\mathfrak{p}$, the rightmost directed path started from $x$, and the rightmost directed path ending at $y$ (including the vertices and edges lying on the three paths).
title: Defn def-geodesic of arXiv:2510.26123

[Prop 7 of arXiv:2607.28578, 'On two differing geometric descriptions of the passage from microscopy to macroscopy in Ma'] The form
	\[
		\langle f,h\rangle_{T^{*}_{\rho,V}}=\langle\Bop_{\rho}f,\Bop_{\rho}h\rangle_{V_{\rho}}
	\]
	is positive semidefinite on $\mathcal C_{\rho}$. Quotienting by $\Ker\Bop_{\rho}$ and completing gives a Hilbert cotangent $T^{*}_{\rho,V}$. The operator $\Kop_{\rho}$ extends uniquely to an isometric isomorphism
	\[
		\Kop_{\rho}\colon T^{*}_{\rho,V}\to\Aop_{\rho}\overline{\Bop_{\rho}(\mathcal C_{\rho})}^{V_{\rho}}\subseteq T_{\rho,V}.

	If the only $w\in H_{\rho}$ satisfying $\int_M\rho\langle\grad f,w\rangle_g\,\dd{\mathrm{vol}}=0$ for every $f\in\mathcal C_{\rho}$ is $w=0$, then $\Bop_{\rho}(\mathcal C_{\rho})$ is dense in $H_{\rho}$ and $\Kop_{\rho}$ is onto the full tangent $T_{\rho,V}$.

[Lemma lem:independence of arXiv:2606.11951, 'On Skorokhod Problems for Reflected and Singular Stochastic Heat Equations'] Let $x\in (0,1)$. Then it holds that $\beta_x$ and $\beta^{\mathrm{pin},x}$ (as introduced in Definition (def:l_and_bb_pin of the paper)) are independent. Further, the integration formula
    \begin{align}
    	\mathbb{E}\left[ F(\beta) \psi (\beta_x) \right]
    	&= \int_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{E}\left[ F(\beta^{\mathrm{pin},x}+y l^x)\right] \psi (y) \, \mathcal{N}(0,x(1-x))(dy) \nonumber\\
    	&= \int_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{E}\left[ F(\beta+(y-\beta_x) l^x)\right] \psi (y) \, \mathcal{N}(0,x(1-x))(dy)

[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2608.29972, '\bf Cram\'er transform, half-space depth and threshold phenomena for convex bodies'] Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then, for every $a\in(0,1/5)$,
$$\mathbb{E}_\mu\left[\exp\left(\frac{a}{n}\Lambda_\mu^*\right)\right]\leq C(a)n^{3a/2},$$
where $C(a)>0$ depends only on $a$.

More precisely,
$$\|\Lambda_\mu^*\|_{L^{\psi_1}(\mu)}\leq Cn\log n.$$

[Theorem 24 (Uniform convergence in probability) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:baseline}--\ref{ass:solutions} and suppose $B,A,S<1$. Then there exists a constant $C>0$, independent of $h$, such that, for every $h>0$, if $\wt\eta\in(1/\alpha,1]$, then
\[
\Pbb\left(\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-\wt X_t|^{\alpha-1}>h\right)
\le \frac{C}{h}\left[|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}
+\max\left\{
B^{\frac{\alpha\wt\eta-1}{\alpha\wt\eta-\alpha+1}},
A^{\frac{2(\alpha\wt\eta-1)}{\alpha\wt\eta-\alpha+2}},
S^{\alpha-1/\wt\eta}
\right\}\right].
\]
If $\wt\eta=1/\alpha$ and $\Theta=\max\{B,A,S\}\in(0,1)$, then
\[
\Pbb\left(\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-\wt X_t|^{\alpha-1}>h\right)
\le \frac{C}{h}\left[|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}
+\left(\log\frac1\Theta\right)^{-1}\right].
\]
When $\Theta=0$, the right-hand side is interpreted as $C|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}/h$.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit model calculation and hypothesis obstruction Result: For constant divergence-free transport fields on a torus or R3, write the equation in Stratonovich form with the matching second-order Ito correction. Let Z_t=sum b_n W_t^n. If v is a deterministic Navier-Stokes solution, u(t,x)=v(t,x+Z_t) solves the corresponding stochastic equation by Ito-Wentzell. Translation is an isometry on Lq and homogeneous Besov norms. Hence in this special commuting case a deterministic local theory transfers without any loss of its spatial smoothness threshold. Check: The quadratic-variation drift is (1/2)sum (b_n dot grad)^2u. Stating this correction is essential: deleting Ito transport without correcting viscosity would solve a different equation. The Leray projection commutes with constant translations. Obstruction: For spatially varying coefficients the flow is not a translation, the transformed Laplacian has random variable coefficients, and the pressure projection no longer simply commutes. No general endpoint estimate or optimality proof is obtained. The2026 high-probability global result uses chosen noise and smoother initial spaces, so its abstract does not settle this question.

\[
   \mathbb P\big(\0\ \text{belongs to an infinite open cluster}\big)\ \ge\
   1-5\varepsilon\ \ge\ \tfrac{123}{128} .
\]

consecutive integers.  Then

  \bigg|\sum_{n\in I}\e(\theta n)\bigg|\le\min\left(Y,\frac1{2\|\theta\|}\right).
\]

Let X be a variety over a number field k. The set of rational points X(k) diagonally embeds into the Brauer-Manin set X(A_k)^{Br}. Consequently, if X(A_k) is non-empty but X(A_k)^{Br} is empty, then X(k) is empty, providing a Brauer-Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle.

[Lem Derivative-via-image-diameter of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Let $D$ be a disc centred
    on the real line and $K\subseteq D$ a compact subset. Let $c_{1}$
    and $c_{2}$ be the two points where the boundary of $D$ intersects
    the real line $\mathbb{R}$. Then there exists a constant $C>0$ such
    that for any real Möbius transformation $F$ with $F(D)\subseteq\mathbb{C}$,
    we have 
    \[
    |F(z)-F(w)|<C|F(c_{2})-F(c_{1})|\cdot|z-w|
    \]
    for all $z,w\in K$.

[Lemma 7 (Polynomial conditioning cost) of arXiv:2604.26298, 'The Expiring Coupon Collector\\ Sliding-Window Surjection Flux and Rare-Entry Laws'] Let \(N\ge2\), \(m\ge N+1\), and \(1\le u\le m-1\), with \(m/N\le 2\log N\).  Let \(\tau>0\) be determined by
\[
        \frac{\tau}{1-e^{-\tau}}=\frac{m}{N}.
\]
For each color \(c\), let \((A_c,B_c)\) be independent split Poisson variables with means \(\tau u/m\) and \(\tau(m-u)/m\), conditioned on \(A_c+B_c\ge1\).  Write \(\Pbb_*\) for this product law and set
\[
        \mathcal C_u:=\left\{
        \sum_{c=1}^N A_c=u,
        \quad
        \sum_{c=1}^N(A_c+B_c)=m
        \right\}.
\]
There is an absolute constant \(C<\infty\) such that, uniformly in \(N,m,u\) in this range,
\[
        \Pbb_*(\mathcal C_u)\ge m^{-C}.
\]
Consequently, for every nonnegative functional \(H\) of the split occupancy configuration,
\[
        \Ebb_{\mathrm{onto}}H
        =\Ebb_*(H\mid \mathcal C_u)
        \le m^C\Ebb_*H.
\]

body: In mathematical logic and descriptive set theory, the analytical hierarchy is an extension of the arithmetical hierarchy. The analytical hierarchy of formulas includes formulas in the language of second-order arithmetic, which can have quantifiers over both the set of natural numbers, , and over functions from to . The analytical hierarchy of sets classifies sets by the formulas that can be used to define them; it is the lightface version of the projective hierarchy.

PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. Under (IID)+(UE) transience in direction l gives the Sznitman-Zerner regeneration structure with tau_1 < infinity a.s.; ballisticity is E[tau_1 | D = infinity] < infinity (Drewitz-Ramirez Open Question 2.20). Under (UE) a trap of diameter r holds the walk at most exponentially long in r, so sub-ballistic behaviour needs polynomially rare traps of logarithmic size along the path, which i.i.d. environments do allow; the question is whether the tail P(tau_1 > n) can be as heavy as n^{-1+eps}. Open Question 3.20 (does positive velocity imply (P)_M for M > 15d + 5) is then the question whether a finite first moment of tau_1 self-improves to moments of order about M/d, because (P)_M is equivalent through the slab decomposition to high moments of tau_1. The Guerra-Ramirez theorem (T) <=> (T') (2018) settles Open Question 3.28 but neither of these. Recorded as the moment-self-improvement reformulation.

body:
[Definition def: generalized resnet of arXiv:2609.03589, 'Correlated initialization of deep residual networks'] A generalized residual network \(F=F_{A, B,
    (v_l)_{l=0}^{L-1}, (w_l)_{l=0}^{L-1}}\) 
    with parameters \((A, B, (v_l)_{l=0}^{L-1}, (w_l)_{l=0}^{L-1})\)
    maps an input \(x\in \mathbb{R}^{{d_\mathrm{in}}}\) through a series of hidden layers
    \begin{align}
        h_0 &\coloneq A x
        \\
        h_{l +1} &\coloneq h_l + \lambda_L \sigma(w_l, h_l) v_l 
        && l \in \set{0, \dots, L -1}
    \end{align}
    to an output \(F(x) \coloneq Bh_{L} \in \mathbb{R}^{{d_\mathrm{out}}}\),
    with
    \begin{itemize}[noitemsep]
        \item \(\lambda_L\in [0, \infty)\), a scaling factor that depends on the depth
        \(L\) of the ResNet,
        \item input and output processing matrices
        \(A\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times{d_\mathrm{in}}}\)
        and
        \(B\in \mathbb{R}^{{d_\mathrm{out}}\timesd}\),
        \item parameters \(w_l\in\banachSpace[W]\), where
        \(\banachSpace[W]\) is a fixed Banach space, and
        \(v_l\in\mathbb{R}^r\), which determine the residual update through the
        continuous map
        \[
            \sigma\colon
            \banachSpace[W]\times\mathbb{R}^d
            \longrightarrow
            \mathbb{R}^{d\times r}.
        \]
\end{itemize}
title: General ResNet

 every sequence $\alpha=\alpha(n)$ and every increasing sequence $n_1,n_2,\dots \in N$: 
 
 $$ \lim_{i\to\infty} \ensuremath{{\mathbb P}}\left( \chi\left( G(n_i,\alpha) \right) > k \right) =
 \begin{cases}
 1 & \text{ if $\alpha > (1+\varepsilon)\alpha_k$, } \\
 0 & \text{ if $\alpha < (1-\varepsilon)\alpha_k$. }
 \end{cases} $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2511.09930, 'Martingale dimensions for a class of metric measure spaces'] Let $Y$ be a separable metric space.
Suppose that a sequence of finite Borel measures $\{\eta_k\}_{k=1}^\infty$ on $Y$ converges weakly to a non-zero finite measure $\eta_\infty$.
Let $a\in Y$ belong to the support of $\eta_\infty$.
Then, there exists $k_1\in\N$ and a sequence $\{a^{(k)}\}_{k=k_1}^\infty$ in $Y$ such that $a^{(k)}$ converges to $a$ as $k\to\infty$ and $a^{(k)}$ belongs to the support of $\eta_k$ for any $k\ge k_1$.

[Definition Total Variation Norm of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Given a complex Radon measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), its \emph{total variation norm} is defined by
\[
  \bigl\|\mu\bigr\|
  \;=\;
  \lvert \mu\rvert\!\bigl(\mathbb{R}^d\bigr),
\]
i.e.\ the total variation of \(\mu\) evaluated on the whole space. In particular, \(\|\mu\|\) is finite if and only if \(\lvert \mu\rvert\) is a finite (real) measure on \(\mathbb{R}^d\).

[Proposition 22 (Isotropic range evolution) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] At level $t$, conditionally on
$(L_t,R_t)=(\ell,r)\in\N^2$, the proposed graft rate is
$\ell+r+1$. If $U$ is uniform on $\{-\ell,\ldots,r\}$ and
$(L_t',R_t')$ is an independent copy of $(L_t,R_t)$, then the proposed
update is
\begin{equation}

        (\ell,r)
        \longmapsto
        \bigl(\max\{\ell,L_t'-U\},\max\{r,R_t'+U\}\bigr).
\end{equation}
Null updates are allowed.

\slope:=\frac{\lv-\ac-\bc+\sqrt{\discr}}{\lv-\ac-\bc-\sqrt{\discr}},
\eeq
where $\discr$ is given in \eqref{eq:Ddefn}. Define the regions 
\beqq
\begin{aligned}
U_1&:=\left\{(x,y)\in(1,\infty)^2:(x-1)/\slope<y-1<\slope(x-1)\right\},\\
U_2&:=\left\{(x,y)\in\R_+^2:x/\slope<y<\slope x\right\}\setminus\left(\overline{U}_1\cup\{(t,t):t\in(0,1)\}\right),\\
U_3&:=\R_+^2\setminus\left(\overline{U}_1\cup\overline{U}_2\right).
\end{aligned}
\eeqq
For $i=2,3$, also set
\beqq
U_i^{<}:=U_i\cap\{(x,y)\in\R_+^2:y<x\},\qquad U_i^{>}:=U_i\cap\{(x,y)\in\R_+^2:y>x\}.
\eeqq
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2608.20552

body:
[Theorem 17 (Log-Lipschitz stability of the PF-ODE) of arXiv:2607.25685, 'Mimicking diffusion processes with differential equations'] Assume \textup{(E1)}, \textup{(D$_{\mathrm S}$)}, \textup{(I)}, \textup{(S)} with \textup{(S2$_p$)}, and
\textup{(A)}. Fix $r>0$ and set
\[
  R:=(1+r)\,\exp\Big(\|G\|_{L^1}+\|G_\theta\|_{L^1}\Big),\qquad
  \mathcal{E}_v:=\big\|v-v_\theta\big\|_{L^1([\delta,T]\times B_R)},
\]
where $G,G_\theta\in L^1$ are the linear-growth rates of $v,v_\theta$ from
Theorem~\ref{thm:lagrangian}\textup{(i)} and \textup{(A3)}. Then for every $\lambda>0$ and
$\eta>0$,
\begin{equation}
  \Leb\Big(\big\{x\in B_r:\ \big|Z^\delta(T,x)-Z^\delta_\theta(T,x)\big|>\eta\big\}\Big)
  \;\le\;\frac{1}{\log\!\big(1+\eta/\lambda\big)}
  \Big[\,\mathcal C_p\;+\;\frac{L_\theta}{\lambda}\,\mathcal E_v\,\Big],
\end{equation}
where
\[
  \mathcal C_p:=C_{d,p}\,(L+L_\theta)\,|B_R|^{1/p'}\int_\delta^T\!\big\|\nabla v(\cdot,s)\big\|_{L^p(B_{3R})}\dd s,
  \qquad \tfrac1{p'}=1-\tfrac1p .
\]
Optimising with $\lambda=\sqrt{\mathcal E_v}$ gives, for $\mathcal E_v<\eta^2$,
\begin{equation}
  \Leb\Big(\big\{x\in B_r:\ |Z^\delta(T,x)-Z^\delta_\theta(T,x)|>\eta\big\}\Big)
  \;\le\;\frac{\mathcal C_p+L_\theta\sqrt{\mathcal E_v}}{\log\!\big(1+\eta\,\mathcal E_v^{-1/2}\big)}
  \;\xrightarrow[\ \mathcal E_v\to0\ ]{}\;0 .
\end{equation}
The convergence is \emph{logarithmic} in $\mathcal E_v$.

[Lemma 1 (Convexity and concavity facts) of arXiv:2607.09499, 'Log-convexity and log-concavity of noncentral gamma sums and differences'] Let $(E,\mathcal{E},\eta)$ be a positive measure space. Suppose that, for every $x\in I$, the map $y\mapsto h_y(x)$ is measurable. If $h_y:I\to(0,\infty)$ is log-convex for every $y\in E$ and
\[
H(x) \leqdef \int_E h_y(x)\,\eta(\rd y)
\]
is finite and strictly positive for every $x\in I$, then $H$ is log-convex on $I$. Also, if $G$ is convex on $[x_0,\infty)$ and $G(x)/x\to0$ as $x\to\infty$, then $G$ cannot satisfy $\limsup_{x\to\infty}G(x) = \infty$. Finally, the convolution of two log-concave densities, extended by zero outside their supports, is log-concave. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convexity and concavity facts
