body:
[Thm 27 of arXiv:2607.03924, 'Tree Coordinates and Range Martingales for Positive Operator-Valued Measures'] Let $X=\left\{ X_{w}\right\} $ be a bounded self-adjoint
range martingale. Then 
\begin{equation}
Q_{n+1}\left(X\right)-Q_{n}\left(X\right)=\sum_{\left|w\right|=n}E^{1/2}_{w}\Gamma_{w}\left(X\right)E^{1/2}_{w}
\end{equation}
for every $n\geq0$. In particular, $\left\{ Q_{n}\left(X\right)\right\} _{n\geq0}$
is an increasing sequence of positive operators. If 
\[
M=\sup_{w}\left\Vert X_{w}\right\Vert ,
\]
then 
\[
0\leq Q_{n}\left(X\right)\leq M^{2}I
\]
for every $n$. Hence $Q_{n}\left(X\right)$ has a strong limit.

[Proposition of arXiv:2604.17253, 'Large Deviations for the Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation with Randomized Quasi-Periodic Ini'] The domain ${\mathrm D}^{(k,\gamma^{(k)})}$ admits a canonical identification with
\begin{align*}
{\mathscr D}^{(k,\gamma^{(k)})}=
\begin{cases}
\prod_{j=1}^d \mathbb{Z}^{\nu_j}, & \gamma^{(k)}=0,\ k\ge1;\\
\prod_{j=1}^d (\mathbb{Z}^{\nu_j})^3, & \gamma^{(1)}=1;\\
\prod_{j=1}^3 {\mathscr D}^{(k-1,\gamma_j^{(k-1)})}, & \gamma^{(k)}\in(\Gamma^{(k-1)})^3,\ k\ge2.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
This identification is induced by coordinate-wise projection.

More precisely, for each $j=1,\dots,d$, we define the projection
\[
\iota_{x_j}:\left(\prod_{j=1}^d \mathbb{Z}^{\nu_j}\right)^s \to (\mathbb{Z}^{\nu_j})^s,
\quad
\iota_{x_j}\big((q_1^1,\dots,q_d^1),\dots,(q_1^s,\dots,q_d^s)\big)
= (q_j^1,\dots,q_j^s).
\]
The full map $\iota=(\iota_{x_1},\dots,\iota_{x_d})$ induces the above identification. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.21669, 'Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts:\\ II. order-order interface convergence'] Let~$q>4$ be integer and take~$T=T_c(q)$.
	For~$n\in\N$ and~$s\in \{1,2\}$, sample~$\Gamma_{\potts}^{s\pm,n}$ and~$\tilde{\Gamma}_{\potts}^{s\pm,n}$ from~$\potts_{\Lambda_n;T_c(q),q}^{1/2}$ as described above.
	Then, as~$n$ tends to infinity,
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item the envelops~\(\big(\tilde{\Gamma}_{\potts}^{1\pm,n}(t),\tilde{\Gamma}_{\potts}^{2\pm,n}(t)\big)_{t\in [0,1]}\), for any choice of~$+$ and~$-$, converges in law to~$(c_q\mathrm{BW}^(2)_{t\in[0,1]}$, where~\(c_q >0\) is some constant;
		\item the probability that~$\max_{k \leq n, s\in\{1,2\}} \left|\Gamma_{\potts}^{s+,n}(k) -\Gamma_{\potts}^{s-,n}(k)\right|\geq C\ln^{111}(n)$ tends to zero.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:canonical-covariance of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] Let
\[
\rho_k=\sum_i p_i(k)\lambda_i^2.
\]
Then
\[
\mathrm{Cov}_{p_k}
(\lambda^2,\log(1/p_k))
=
\frac1{E_k}
\sum_{i\ge3}
n_i(k)
\bigl(
\rho_k-\lambda_i^2
\bigr)
\log\frac{n_i(k)}{n_2(k)}.
\]
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}

\mathrm{Cov}_{p_k}
(\lambda^2,\log(1/p_k))
=
\sum_{i\ge3}
J_i(k)\,A_i(k).
\end{equation}

body: Given a parametric family {f(.;theta): theta in Theta} and data X, a statistic T(X) is sufficient for theta if the conditional distribution of X given T(X) = t does not depend on theta, for (almost) every value t in the range of T. Equivalently, by the Fisher-Neyman factorization criterion, T is sufficient for theta if and only if the density or pmf factors as f(x;theta) = g(T(x), theta) * h(x) for some functions g >= 0 and h >= 0, where h does not depend on theta.

body:
[Definition def5.2 of arXiv:2411.03528, '\textbf{On a boundary of the central limit theorem for strictly stationary, reversible Mar'] Suppose $\varepsilon$ and $\theta$ satisfy ((eq5.111 of the paper)).
Refer to ((eq5.112 of the paper)).
A Markov chain $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ 
is said to satisfy ``Condition ${\cal H}(\varepsilon, \theta)$'' if 
$X$ is a strictly stationary Markov chain such that \hfil\break
(i) its state space is $\{-1, 0, 1\}$, \hfil\break
(ii) its (invariant) marginal probability vector is the vector 
$\pi^{(\varepsilon)}$ in ((eq5.131 of the paper)), and \hfil\break
(iii) its one-step transition probability matrix is the matrix
$\mathbb P^{(\varepsilon, \theta)}$ in ((eq5.141 of the paper)).     
\smallskip

   That is [under Condition ${\cal H}(\varepsilon, \theta)$],
for $i,j \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$, 
$P(X_0 = i) = \pi_i^{(\varepsilon)}$ from ((eq5.131 of the paper)), 
and $P(X_1=j|X_0 = i) = p^{(\varepsilon, \theta)}_{i,j}$ from
((eq5.141 of the paper)).  
The requirements (ii) and (iii) in this definition are
compatible by ((eq5.143 of the paper)).
In fact Condition ${\cal H}(\varepsilon, \theta)$ uniquely 
determines the distribution of the entire Markov chain $X$
on $(\mathbb R^\mathbb Z, \mathcal R^\mathbb Z)$.
title: Definition def5.2 of arXiv:2411.03528

body:
[Theorem thm:FDT of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] For each mode $i \ge 2$, define $C_i(k) = |c_i|^2 \lambda_i^{2k}$ and $R_i(k) = c_i \lambda_i^k$. Then
\[
\frac{C_i(k+1) - C_i(k)}{C_i(k)} = \lambda_i^2 - 1 = -2\mu_i + \mu_i^2, \qquad
C_i(k) = |R_i(k)|^2,
\]
and summing over $i$ recovers the exact dissipation law (equation eq:modewise-dissipation of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Spectral fluctuation-dissipation theorem

[Definition of arXiv:2609.03731, 'Weightings and Lie groupoids'] The \emph{Rees algebra} associated to the filtration $\ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_\bullet$ of $C^\infty_M$ is the sheaf of $C^\infty_M$-algebras
\[ \ensuremath{\mathcal{R}}_{N,w}(C^\infty_M)=\{\sum t^{-k}f_k\mid f_k\in \ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_k\},\]
where $t$ is an auxiliary variable, a subalgebra of Laurent polynomials in $t$ with coefficients in $C^\infty_M$ ($\ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_k\ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_l\subset \ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_{k+l}$ guarantees that this is a subalgebra). The \emph{weighted deformation to the normal cone} or \emph{weighted deformation space} is the differential space
\[ \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_w(M,N)=\ensuremath{\textnormal{Spec}}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{R}}_{N,w}(C^\infty_M)).\]
The inclusions $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}[t],C^\infty_M\hookrightarrow \ensuremath{\mathcal{R}}_{N,w}(C^\infty_M)$ induce a morphism of differential spaces $(t,\hat{\pi})\colon \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_w(M,N)\rightarrow \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\times M$. The algebra automorphisms $t\mapsto \lambda^{-1} t$, $\lambda \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^\times$ determine an action (by morphisms of differential spaces) $\hat{\kappa}_\bullet\colon \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^\times \times \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_w(M,N)\rightarrow \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}_w(M,N)$ called the \emph{zoom action}.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2609.03731, 'Weightings and Lie groupoids'

[Theorem 27 (Fourier CLT for ball windows) of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] Let $\eta$ be a stationary random measure with local second moments whose
translation action is essentially free and CPE. Then, for every
$\xi\in E_\eta$,
\begin{equation}

    Z_R^{B}(\xi)
    \dto \mathcal{CN}\bigl(0,s_\eta(\xi)\lambda_d(B_1)\bigr).
\end{equation}
If $(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_q)$ belongs to the conull set
$E_\eta^{(q)}$ from Corollary~\ref{cor:continuum-several-frequencies}, then the
ball transforms at these frequencies converge jointly, and their Gaussian
limits are independent.

[Lemma lem:prelimit-enlargement of arXiv:2605.03703, 'Scaling Limits of Bivariate Nearly-Unstable Hawkes Processes and Applications to Rough Vol'] Work under the construction of Remark~(rem:thinning of the paper) and define the
initially enlarged filtration
\[
\mathbb G_t^T:=\sigma(\pi^1)\vee
\sigma\bigl(\pi^2((0,s]\times B):s\le t,\ B\in\mathcal B(\mathbb{R}_+)\bigr),
\qquad t\ge0,
\]
augmented by the $\mathbb P$-null sets.  Then $M^{T,2}$ is a
square-integrable $\mathbb G^T$-martingale with predictable bracket
$\langle M^{T,2}\rangle_t=\int_0^t\lambda_s^{T,2}\,ds$ and optional
bracket $[M^{T,2}]_t=N^{T,2}_t$.  Consequently, with
$c_T:=\bigl((1-a_T^2)/(m_2T^{\alpha_2})\bigr)^{1/2}$ as in
(equation eq:Mhat-def of the paper), the renormalized martingale
$\widehat M^{T,2}_t=c_TM^{T,2}_{Tt}$ is a square-integrable martingale for
the filtration $(\mathbb G_{Tt}^T)_{t\in[0,1]}$, and both
\begin{equation}
\widehat M^{T,2}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
(\widehat M^{T,2})^2-\int_0^\cdot V_u^{T,2}\,du
\end{equation}
are $(\mathbb G_{Tt}^T)$-martingales.

[Lemma 12 (Kneser) of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $A,B$ be subsets of a locally compact, abelian group $G$ and let $\mu$ 
denote (a version of) the Haar measure on $G$. If there exists an open 
subgroup $H$ such that 
$$
A+B+H=A+B \quad\text{and}\quad \mu(A+B+H) = \mu(A+H) + \mu(B+H)-\mu(H),
$$
then 
$$
\mu(A+B) \geq \mu(A)+\mu(B)-\mu(H).
$$
Otherwise, 
$$
\mu^*(A+B) \geq \mu(A)+\mu(B),
$$
where $\mu^*$ denotes the inner measure induced by $\mu$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 40 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] Let $\tau$ be a GW($\mu$)-tree, where $\mu$ is a non-trivial critical offspring distribution.  
Let $\nu$ be a supercritical offspring distribution whose mean is denoted by $\ttm_\nu$. 
Let $\ttb\ino (1, \infty)$. We assume that $\sum_{k\in \bbN} k^{2\ttb +1}\nu(k) \leko \infty$. Let $(\bT, \boo)$ be an invariant 
GW($\nu$)-tree. Let $(Y'_u)_{u\in \tau}$ be a $\tau$-indexed, $\bT$-valued $\ttm_\nu$-biased BRW whose conditional law given $(\bT, \boo)$ and $\tau$ is $Q^{_{(\bT, \boo)}}_{^{(\tau, \varnothing)}}$ 
as in Definition \ref{biasedbfRWdef}. 
We recall from (\ref{spinedfbis}) 
the pieces of notation $\boo (p)$ and $L_\boo$. Let 
$ (S_x)_{x\in \bT}$ be the harmonic coordinates as in (\ref{defSx}) and we recall from (\ref{vutchi}) the notation $\sigma_\nu$. For all $q\ino \bbN$, all $\lambda \ino (0, \infty)$ and all $\beta \ino 
(\tfrac{1}{2} +\tfrac{1}{2\ttb} , 1)$, we define the following subset of $\bT$ 
$$ B_{q, \lambda, \beta}= \Big\{ x\ino \bT\backslash L_\boo\,  : \bbn \boo \wedge x\bbn \geqo -q \;\,  \textrm{and}  \;\,  \big| 
\frac{_{_1}}{^{^{\sigma^2_\nu}}} (S_x\! -\! S_{\boo \wedge x}) \! -\!  \big( \bbn x\bbn\! -\!  \bbn \boo \wedge x\bbn\big) \big| \geqo \lambda \big( 1+  \big( \bbn x\bbn\! -\!  \bbn \boo \wedge x\bbn\big)^\beta \big) \Big\}. $$
Then, there exists $c\ino (0,\infty)$, which only depends on $\nu, \ttb, \beta$, such that 
$\bP \big( \exists u\ino \tau: Y'_u \ino B_{q, \lambda, \beta}) \leqo cq \lambda^{-2\ttb}.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 40 of arXiv:2605.02430

[Theorem cor:superprocess_main_CD of arXiv:2508.18809, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation III: The upper critical dimension}'] If $d= 3\alpha<6$ then there exist functions $\zeta(r)\to\infty$ and $\eta(r)\to 0$ such that
\[
\frac{1}{\eta(r)}\mathbb P_{\beta_c}\Biggl(|K|\geq \lambda \zeta(r),\; \frac{1}{\zeta(r)}\sum_{x \in K} \delta_{x/r}\in\cdot\Biggr) \to \mathbb{N}\Bigl(\mu(\mathbb R^d)\geq \lambda, \mu \in \cdot\Bigr)
\]
weakly as $r\to \infty$ for each fixed $\lambda>0$, where $\mathbb{N}$ denotes the canonical measure of the integrated symmetric $\alpha$-stable L\'evy superprocess excursion associated to the L\'evy measure with density $\frac{\alpha}{d+\alpha}\|x\|^{-d-\alpha}$. Moreover, the normalization factors $\zeta$ and $\eta$ are given asymptotically by
\[
\zeta(r) \sim \text{\emph{const.}}\;r^{2\alpha} (\log r)^{-1/2} 
\quad \text{ and } \qquad
\eta(r) \sim \text{\emph{const.}}\; r^{-\alpha} (\log r)^{1/2} 
\]
as $r\to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Superprocess limits at the critical dimension

[Prop 10 of arXiv:2609.03791, 'Canonical Bochner--K\"{a}hler potentials via the Sasaki--K\"{a}hler correspondence'] Let $V_1,\dots,V_{\mu}$ be the eigenspaces with eigenvalues $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{\mu}$ of $X$. Let $a_{V_k}$ be the components of $a$ with respect to the eigenspace decomposition of $X$. Then,
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The blocks $\hBlock_{ij}$ of the matrix $\hBlock$ that correspond to different eigenspaces $V_i$ and $V_j$ are uniquely determined by a choice of $\beta$.
        \item If $a_{V_k}\neq 0$ then $\beta_{V_k}=\I \lambda_k a_{V_k}$ where $\lambda_k$ is a real parameter and $H_{kk}$ satisfies $n_k$ equations, which reduces its freedom to $(n_k-1)^2$. This contributes $(n_k-1)^2+1$ parameters.
        \item If $a_{V_k}= 0$ then $H_{kk}$ is unrestricted and $\beta_{V_k}$ is either unrestricted, or vanishing.  
        This contributes  either $n_k^2$, or $n_k^2+2n_k$ parameters.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 10 of arXiv:2609.03791

body:
[Lemma 20 ($\kappa_{\delta,R}<\infty$ for linear drift) of arXiv:2607.25685, 'Mimicking diffusion processes with differential equations'] Assume \textup{(E1)} and $f(x,s)=-\beta(s)x$ with $\beta\in L^\infty(0,T)$ --- the
variance-preserving and variance-exploding models of Corollary~\ref{cor:diffusion}. Let $p_0$
be any probability density. With $m_s:=e^{-\int_0^s\beta}$ and
$\varsigma_s^2:=m_s^2\int_0^s\sigma(r)^2m_r^{-2}\dd r$, set
$\varsigma_{\min}^2:=\inf_{s\in[\delta,T]}\varsigma_s^2>0$,
$\varsigma_{\max}^2:=\sup_{s\in[\delta,T]}\varsigma_s^2<\infty$ and
$m_{\max}:=\sup_{s\le T}m_s$. Fix any $\rho>0$ with $\mu_\rho:=\int_{B_\rho}p_0\,\dd x>0$.
Then for all $s\in[\delta,T]$ and $|x|\le R$,
\begin{equation}
  p_s(x)\;\ge\;\frac{\mu_\rho}{(2\pi\varsigma_{\max}^2)^{d/2}}
  \exp\!\Big(-\frac{(R+m_{\max}\rho)^2}{2\varsigma_{\min}^2}\Big)\;>\;0 ,
\end{equation}
and consequently
\[
  \kappa_{\delta,R}\;\le\;(T-\delta)\,|B_R|\,
  \frac{(2\pi\varsigma_{\max}^2)^{d/2}}{\mu_\rho}\,
  \exp\!\Big(\frac{(R+m_{\max}\rho)^2}{2\varsigma_{\min}^2}\Big)\;<\;\infty .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: $\kappa_{\delta,R}<\infty$ for linear drift

[Definition Cirr of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] A complex C-space $(M=G_f/K\times T^z,J)$ without flag factor is called {\it reducible} if there exists a $J_\ag$-invariant decomposition $\ag=\ag_1\oplus\ag_2$ such that 
$$
\ag_1=\zg(\ggo)_1\oplus\underline{\ag}_f\oplus\tg_{i_1}\oplus\dots\oplus\tg_{i_{s_1}}, \qquad 
\ag_2=\zg(\ggo)_2\oplus\tg_{j_1}\oplus\dots\oplus\tg_{j_{s_2}},
$$
$\zg(\ggo)=\zg(\ggo)_1\oplus\zg(\ggo)_2$ and $\{ u+1,\dots,s\}=\{i_1,\dots,i_{s_1}\}\sqcup \{j_1,\dots,j_{s_2}\}$.  Otherwise, we say that $(M=G/K,J)$ is {\it irreducible}.
title: Definition Cirr of arXiv:2608.30747

body:
[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2604.15191, 'Quantitative Stability of Many-Marginal Schr\"odinger Bridge'] Let $\phi_t$ and $\psi_t$ be the Kantorovich potentials for solving the optimal transport problem between $\rho_0^\mu$ and $\rho_t^\mu$. That is, 
\begin{align*}
(\id - \nabla\phi_t)_\# \rho_0^\mu = \rho_t^\mu
\qquad\mx{and}\qquad
(\id - \nabla\psi_t)_\# \rho_t^\mu = \rho_0^\mu,
\end{align*}
where the sums $\id - \nabla\phi_t$ and $\id - \nabla\psi_t$ are
to be intended modulo $2\pi\mb Z^d$.
Then for any $\alpha\in(0, 1)$, there exists $\sigma_{\rm min},\sigma_{\rm max} > 0$ depending on $d$, $L_\rho$,  $\|\rho_0^\mu\|_{\m C^{0,\alpha}}$, and $\|\rho_t^\mu\|_{\m C^{0,\alpha}}$, 

such that
\begin{align*}
\sigma_{\rm min} I_d \leq  I_d - \nabla^2\phi_t(x) \leq \sigma_{\rm max}I_d
\qquad\mx{and}\qquad
\sigma_{\rm min} I_d \leq  I_d - \nabla^2\phi_t(x) \leq \sigma_{\rm max}I_d
\end{align*}
hold for every $(t, x)\in[0, 1]\times \mb T^d$.
\myqed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 32 of arXiv:2604.15191

body:
Choose positive integers n,L,M,D and D'>=0, parameter bound B>0, token clipping radius R>0, a label bound B_y>=1, and confidence 0<xi<1. Consider fixed-length in-context prediction instances Z=(H,y), with |y|<=B_y almost surely, drawn independently from one meta-distribution. In the paper's setting one first draws a task distribution P, then draws the context and query example iid from P. A transformer has L residual blocks, each consisting of normalized ReLU attention followed by a residual two-layer ReLU MLP; it has token dimension D, at most M attention heads per block, and MLP hidden width at most D'. For S tokens, attention sends h_i to h_i+(1/S) sum_m sum_j ReLU(<Q_m h_i,K_m h_j>) V_m h_j. The MLP sends h to h+W_2 ReLU(W_1 h). Project every input token and every block's output token onto the Euclidean radius-R ball. Read out the designated label coordinate of the final query token and clip it to [-B_y,B_y]. Restrict parameters to the class Theta with norm max_block(max_m{||Q_m||op,||K_m||op}+sum_m ||V_m||op+||W_1||op+||W_2||op)<=B. Write L(theta)=E[(y-prediction_theta(H))^2/2] and let hat theta be any exact empirical minimizer of the same loss over Theta on n independent instances. There is a universal C such that, with probability at least 1-xi, L(hat theta)<=inf_(theta in Theta) L(theta)+C B_y^2 sqrt((L^2(M D^2+D D') log(2+max{B,R,B_y})+log(1/xi))/n). This is an expected loss over the meta-distribution. Source: arXiv:2306.04637, Section 5.1 and Theorem 20, PDF pages 14–15; proof Appendix J.2, PDF page 89. The harmless choice B_y>=1 is stated explicitly here; any smaller valid label bound may be enlarged to one.
n,L,M,D positive integers; D'>=0; B,R>0; B_y>=1; 0<xi<1
The n pretraining instances are iid from the same meta-distribution and the query label is bounded by B_y
Normalized ReLU attention, residual ReLU MLP, input and hidden-token Euclidean projection at radius R, and prediction clipping at B_y
The specified transformer parameter norm is at most B and hat theta is an exact constrained empirical risk minimizer

Own-work draft; status independently checked proof. For iid finite nonnegative tooth heights with P(H_0>t)~C t^(-1/3), C>0, two independent discrete-time simple random walks started together at the backbone origin have infinitely many backbone collision times almost surely for almost every environment. The candidate proof counts only collisions at the positive-density good roots of I0012-L1 v1. Source Lemma 4.9 supplies a constant first moment in a scale-N time window of order N^3; the good-root collision Green sum gives E[Z_N^2]<=E[Z_N] O(1+log N), hence P(Z_N>0)>=c/(1+log N). Adapted geometric exit blocks and an explicit conditional product argument yield infinitely many successes. No independence of different blocks is assumed. The result is conditional on source Lemmas 4.9 and 4.10 and Proposition 4.11 at gamma=1/3 and on a nonempty Lemma 4.9 time window; Lemma 4.8, on which that window rests, prints an impossible unrestricted time range (see the Lemma 4.8 caveat card). Complete proof: proofs/I0012-C1_v1.md. Audit dispositions: w667 PASS on version 1; w668 PASS on version 1.

[Lemma lem:mellin of arXiv:2605.03703, 'Scaling Limits of Bivariate Nearly-Unstable Hawkes Processes and Applications to Rough Vol'] Let $f,g:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be locally integrable with
$f(\tau)=A\tau^{p-1}+r_f(\tau)$, $g(\tau)=B\tau^{q-1}+r_g(\tau)$, where $p,q>0$ and the
remainders satisfy $|r_f(\tau)|\le \epsilon(\tau)\tau^{p-1}$, $|r_g(\tau)|\le\epsilon(\tau)\tau^{q-1}$
with $\epsilon(\tau)\to0$ as $\tau\downarrow0$ and $\epsilon$ bounded on $(0,1]$. Then
\[
\int_0^t f(t-u)g(u)\,du = AB\,\mathrm{B}(p,q)\,t^{p+q-1}+o(t^{p+q-1}),\qquad t\downarrow0,
\]
where $\mathrm{B}(p,q)=\Gamma(p)\Gamma(q)/\Gamma(p+q)$.

body: In first-passage percolation on Z^2 with edge weights confined to [a, b] with a > 0, any geodesic from the origin to (0, r) satisfies a DETERMINISTIC bound on its transversal excursion: it never attains transversal level D > r(b - a)/(2a). The proof is elementary counting: reaching transversal level D forces at least r + 2D edges, each of weight at least a, giving passage time at least a(r + 2D), while the straight path gives at most b r; the two are incompatible beyond the stated level. No probabilistic input is used, so the bound holds for every realisation.

\end{equation}
Moreover, the maximal polygonal interpolation error converges to
zero in probability.

body:
Agresti and Veraar, Nonlinear parabolic stochastic evolution equations in critical spaces (journal version 2025, p. 130), Problem 4 asks whether in the variational setting of their Theorem 6.4 there is a constant C_T with E sup_{t <= T} ||u(t)||_H^2 <= C_T (1 + E ||u_0||_H^2) for all u_0 in L^2(Omega; H). Our result (id P0266, 2026-09-08): the bound FAILS, on the authors' own named unresolved example - Allen-Cahn on the one-dimensional torus with one-dimensional quadratic noise, du = (Laplacian u + u - u^3) dt + gamma u^2 dW, at the critical gamma^2 = 2. With deterministic constant data u_0 = a > 0 the solution stays spatially constant, and the substitutions Y = 1/U, Y = e^{-t} V, time change s = (e^{2t} - 1)/2 and R = V / sqrt 2 turn the SDE into R being a four-dimensional Bessel process started at R_0 = 1/(sqrt 2 a), with U_t = e^t / (sqrt 2 R_s). Since sup_{t <= T} U_t^2 >= 1/(2 inf_{s <= S} R_s^2) and a BES(4) enters a ball of radius x with probability of order x^2 (Newtonian capacity), P(sup U^2 > y) is of order 1/y - tail index one - so E sup_{t <= T} ||u(t)||_H^2 = infinity for every T > 0 while E ||u_0||_H^2 = a^2 is finite. Verification as the source words it: checked in the reverse direction by Ito as well; and an instrument note - a first simulation appeared to contradict the x^2 scaling, but refining the steps at fixed x drives P/x^2 toward the exact constant 2.0 (1.204, 1.579, 1.697 at x = 0.2 and 0.725, 1.285, 1.455 at x = 0.1), so the scaling is real. NOT Lean-checked: this one has no finite arithmetic core, being Ito calculus plus a capacity estimate. Prior art not cleared; the source is a year old, so the memo rates this among the likeliest to be genuinely new.
Allen-Cahn on the 1-d torus with 1-d quadratic noise, critical gamma^2 = 2
deterministic constant initial data u_0 = a > 0

body:
[Corollary cor:iterated-suspension of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $t\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ and put $A^{(0)}=A$.  For each $1\leq i\leq t$, choose an
integer $\ell_i\geq2$ and a specified $c_i$ having a length-$\ell_i$
representation by points of $A^{(i-1)}$ with $\gcd(c_i,\ell_i)=1$, and set
$A^{(i)}=\Sigma_{\ell_i,c_i}A^{(i-1)}$.  Put
$R=\prod_{i=1}^t\ell_i$, with the empty product equal to one.  Then, for
$q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$,
\begin{align}
 \mathcal H_{A^{(t)}}(z)
 &=\mathcal H_A(z)\prod_{i=1}^t[\ell_i]_z,
 \\
 |qA^{(t)}|
 &=\sum_{\substack{0\leq j_i<\ell_i\\
                    j_1+\cdots+j_t\leq q}}
   |(q-j_1-\cdots-j_t)A|,
 \\
 \mathcal K_{A^{(t)}}(z)
 &=\mathcal K_A(z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1-z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 \mathcal B_{A^{(t)}}(\xi,z)
 &=\mathcal B_A(\xi,z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1+\xi z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 \operatorname{ndiam}(A^{(t)})&=R\operatorname{ndiam}(A).
 
\end{align}
If every $\ell_i\leq q$, then
\[
 r_q(A^{(t)})=r_q(A)+t,\qquad
 \operatorname{fdim}_q(A^{(t)})=\operatorname{fdim}_q(A).
\]
If the starting projective coordinate ring is ACM, then the ACM property
and Cohen--Macaulay type are preserved.

Kind: route-failure. Target1. Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unresolved.

For every 0<mu<1, rank r=2 and p=3, the C029 reduced weighted-Stiefel flow has an open positive-Gaussian-probability set of initially full-rank signal overlaps whose determinant crosses zero at a finite positive time. The construction embeds into every r>=2,p>r and any unequal pair of positive target singular values. This is not a counterexample to eventual convergence; it blocks quantitative arguments that require signal overlap to remain invertible or its determinant to stay positive throughout the reduced trajectory.

Take H=diag(1,mu^2,0), M=[[2,-1],[-1,2]], M^(-1)=(1/3)[[2,1],[1,2]], and

Y_*=[[3/5,4/5,0],[0,0,1]].

This is an exactly row-orthonormal frame. Its two-by-two target-signal block S_* is [[3/5,4/5],[0,0]], so det(S_*)=0. Let v=(3/5,4/5), x=(-4/5,3/5), and follow the smooth autonomous flow

Y'=M^(-1)Y H(I-Y^TY).

The signal block obeys S'=M^(-1)S diag(1,mu^2)(I-S^TS). At Y_*, the derivative of its determinant is the component of the second row derivative along x:

D'(0) = (1/3) v diag(1,mu^2) x^T
      = (4/25)(mu^2-1) <0.

Compactness of St ensures that the flow through Y_* exists both forward and backward in time. Since D(0)=0 and D'(0)<0, for all sufficiently small delta>0 its determinant is positive at time -delta and negative at time +delta. Start instead at the full-signal-rank frame Y(-delta): it crosses zero after a finite positive time. Strict signs at the two endpoints persist under perturbations of both the initial frame and the SPD parameter M, by continuous dependence on initial conditions and parameters. Thus the crossing is present on an open subset of SPD_2 times St(2,3).

The smooth polar map G=M^(1/2)Y takes this to an open set of full-row-rank 2-by-3 matrices. Every nonempty open subset has positive iid-Gaussian probability. The initial signal block of G is invertible because both M^(1/2) and S_initial are invertible. This is therefore an obstruction on a positive-probability Gaussian set, rather than just a specially chosen measure-zero initialization.

For an exact algebra fixture mu=1/2, the derivative is -3/25. A nearby rational full-signal-rank frame is obtained by keeping the first row v and replacing the second by (a x_1,a x_2,b), with a=2q/(1+q^2), b=(1-q^2)/(1+q^2), q=1/10^6. Its determinant is a>0 and its instantaneous determinant derivative is strictly negative by exact rational arithmetic. This fixture checks the local derivative; the analytic transverse-crossing argument above proves existence of a crossing. No floating-point trajectory or interval integration is used.

For r>2, append signal-aligned orthonormal rows, identity blocks to M, and arbitrary additional positive diagonal target singular values; add zero input columns if p>r+1. Those aligned rows are stationary and the two-by-two crossing is unchanged. The open-set argument again gives positive probability in the full-dimensional Gaussian model. For unequal positive values lambda_i>lambda_j, the derivative scales to (4/25)(lambda_j^2-lambda_i^2)<0. Output dimensions m>=r only require embedding the target's positive output coordinates.

If M is scalar, or the two positive singular values coincide, the displayed transverse derivative vanishes. This explains why the flat-spectrum arguments do not supply this unequal-spectrum barrier automatically. C029's convergence proof does not require signal overlap to stay nonsingular, so C030 does not contradict that claim.

Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces, 1 <= p_0 < p_1 <= infinity, and let T be a SUBLINEAR operator defined on L^{p_0}(mu) + L^{p_1}(mu) with values in the measurable functions on Y, which is of WEAK type (p_0, p_0) with constant A_0 and of weak type (p_1, p_1) with constant A_1 (for p_1 = infinity this means ||Tf||_infinity <= A_1 ||f||_infinity). Then for every p with p_0 < p < p_1, T is of strong type (p,p): ||Tf||_{L^p(nu)} <= C ||f||_{L^p(mu)} for all f in L^p(mu), where one may take C = 2 (p/(p - p_0) + p/(p_1 - p))^{1/p} A_0^{1-theta} A_1^{theta} with 1/p = (1-theta)/p_0 + theta/p_1, and the term p/(p_1 - p) is read as 0 when p_1 = infinity. The constant blows up as p tends to p_0 or to p_1, and the conclusion genuinely fails at the endpoints. Off-diagonal version: if T is of weak types (p_0, q_0) and (p_1, q_1) with p_0 not equal to p_1, q_0 not equal to q_1, and p_i <= q_i for i = 0,1, then T is of strong type (p_theta, q_theta) for 0 < theta < 1, with 1/p_theta and 1/q_theta the interpolated exponents.

body: [Theorem 11 of arXiv:2512.19063, 'Sharp Decoupling Inequalities for the Variances and Second Moments of Sums of Dependent Ra'] With the same setting as Theorem 6, we have a Chebyshev-type inequality for any $t>0$, $\mathbb{P}\left(|S_{n}-\mathbb{E} S_{n}|>t\right)\leq\frac{2\operatorname{Var}(S^{\prime}_{n})}{t^{2}}.$ (15) If in addition $S_{n}\geq 0$ a.s., we have a Paley-Zygmund-type inequality for any $0<\theta<1$, $\mathbb{P}(S_{n}>\theta\,\mathbb{E} S_{n})\geq(1-\theta)^{2}\,\frac{(\mathbb{E} S_{n})^{2}}{2\mathbb{E}{S^{\prime}}_{n}^{2}-(\mathbb{E} S_{n})^{2}}=(1-\theta)^{2}\,\frac{1}{\frac{2\mathbb{E}{S^{\prime}}_{n}^{2}}{(\mathbb{E} S_{n})^{2}}-1}.$

Put
\[
  \Gamma := \Bigl\{ \omega \in \XX^{\Nz} :\
     \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f\bigl( X_{k}(\omega) \bigr) = L \Bigr\} .
\]
Then $\Gamma \in \XXA^{\otimes\Nz}$ and $\vartheta^{-1}\Gamma = \Gamma$, with equality
of sets and not merely up to a null set.

[Definition 12 (Size-biased measure) of arXiv:2608.13359, 'Fractional moments of the Stochastic Heat Flow and\\2D Directed Polymers'] For every probability mass function \(f\) on \(\Z^2\), we define the \emph{size-biased measure}  on \((\Omega, \cF, \PP)\), corresponding to initial distribution of the polymer~\(f\) by \(\dd \tPP_f = Z_{N}^{\beta,\w}(f) \dd \PP\), \textit{i.e.}\
  \[
    \tPP_f(A)
    = \tPP_{f,N}^{\beta} (A)
    \coloneqq \EE\bigl[ \indic_{A} \, Z_{N}^{\beta,\w}(f) \bigr] \qquad \text{for any } A\in \cF \,.
  \]

body:
[Lemma 2 (Theorem 7.11, \cite{Fen10}) of arXiv:2605.12475, 'Central limit theorem for the homozygosity of the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process'] Suppose $\bm{X} = (X_1, X_2, \ldots) \sim \PD(\alpha, \theta)$. Let 
\bal
\tilde{H}_m(\alpha, \theta) = \sqrt{\theta}\left( \frac{\theta^{m-1}}{(1 - \alpha)_{(m-1)}}  \sum_{i = 1}^\infty X_i^m - 1 \right), \qquad m \geq 2,
\eal
be the scaled $m$th order homozygosity. Then
\bal
(\tilde{H}_2(\alpha, \theta), \tilde{H}_3(\alpha, \theta), \ldots) \xrightarrow{D} (H_2(\alpha), H_3(\alpha), \ldots)
\eal
as $\theta \to \infty$, where $\bm{H} = (H_2(\alpha), H_3(\alpha), \ldots)$ is a $\R^\infty$-valued random vector such that for all $r \geq 2$, $(H_2(\alpha), \ldots, H_r(\alpha))$ has a multivariate normal distribution with zero mean and covariance matrix
\bal
\cov(H_i(\alpha), H_j(\alpha)) = \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(i+j-1)}}{(1 - \alpha)_{(i-1)}(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}} + \alpha - ij, \qquad i,j = 2, \ldots, r.
\eal (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 7.11, \cite{Fen10}

body: [Corollary adj8 of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $1\leq p<\infty$. Suppose that $B_X$ is relatively weakly $p$-precompact and that $Y$ is a Banach space with the $\mathrm{DP}^*\mathrm{P}_p$ such that $B_{Y^*}$ is weak$^{*}$ sequentially compact. Then $(X,Y)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_p$ if and only if $(Y^*,X^*)$ has the weak$^*$-to-weak$^*$ maximizing property. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary adj8 of arXiv:2609.03988

[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] When $G = \mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}$, the distributions which are symmetric about zero are exactly 
\[ \conv\left(\left\{\mathbb{1}_0, \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{-1} + \mathbb{1}_{1}), \dots, \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{-q} + \mathbb{1}_{q})\right\}\right) . \]
When $G = \mathbb{Z}_{2q}$, the distributions which are symmetric about zero are exactly 
\[ \conv\left(\left\{\mathbb{1}_0, \mathbb{1}_q, \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{-1} + \mathbb{1}_{1}), \dots, \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{-q+1} + \mathbb{1}_{q-1})\right\}\right) . \]

Immediate.

[Theorem 28 (Brascamp--Lieb {\cite{brascamp-lieb1976}; see
	\cite{ball1989volumes}}) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $u_1,\ldots, u_n \in\R^m$ be a finite family of unit vectors, and let $c_1,\ldots, c_n>0$ be real number 
		satisfying 
		$$
		\sum_i c_i u_i u_i^\top=I_m.
		$$
		Then, for every nonnegative measurable functions
		$F_1,\ldots, F_n:\R\to[0,\infty]$,
		$$
		\int_{\R^m}\prod_i F_i(\langle u_i,\theta\rangle)^{c_i}\,d\theta
		\le
		\prod_i\left(\int_\R F_i(t)\,dt\right)^{c_i}.
		$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title:
Brascamp--Lieb {\cite{brascamp-lieb1976}; see
	\cite{ball1989volumes}}

[Prop scale of arXiv:2608.12954, 'Rainbow percolation'] For $k\ge1$ let $g=g_k=8^{2k-1}$, with the blocks of
(def:blocks of the paper), and let $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_k$ be the event that in each of
the four blocks exactly one vertex qualifies (radius $\ge32g$ in
$\mathsf a_k,\mathsf b_k$; radius in $[4g,5g]$ in
$\mathsf c_k,\mathsf d_k$) while every other block vertex has radius $<g$
(``quiet blocks''); the selected vertices are called $a,c,d,b$. Define
\[
   D_k:=\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_k\cap B_k\cap\mathcal N_k
        \cap\mathcal Q^L_k\cap\mathcal Q^R_k,
\]
where $B_k$, $\mathcal N_k$ are the containment and no-cross-edge events of
the reduction for the selected rainbow at scale $k$, and $\mathcal Q^L_k$ is the event
that some cut position $\tau$ in the middle third of $(a,c)$ carries the
cut-point certificate: $R_u<\tau+1-u$ for all non-block $u\in(a,\tau]$,
$R_{\tau+1}<1$, and $R_w<w-a$ for all non-block $w\in(\tau+1,c)$
($\mathcal Q^R_k$ is the mirror image in $(d,b)$). Thus $\mathcal Q^L_k$ is
the analogue in $(a,c)$ of the certificate event
$\{N^\sharp_{\mathcal C}\ge1\}=\{\exists\,\text{gap}^\sharp\}$ of
(lem:cutmarked of the paper), and not of the disconnection event $\mathcal D^L$: it
provides an explicit cut position $\tau$, which is what (lem:confine of the paper)
requires. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] on $D_k$ the hypotheses of (lem:confine of the paper) hold for some
  $i\in(a,c)$, $i'\in(d,b)$, and $(-g,g)\subseteq(c,d)\subseteq(i,i']$;
\item[(ii)] $\mathbb P(D_k)\ge\delta(x_m)>0$, uniformly in $k$;
\item[(iii)] the events
  $E_k:=\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_k\cap\mathcal N_k\cap\mathcal Q^L_k\cap\mathcal Q^R_k$,
  $k\ge1$, are independent, being measurable with respect to the radii in
  the disjoint annuli $\{u: g_k\le|u|<9g_k\}$.
\end{enumerate}

On the uniform cube {-1, 1}^n let f be real, f^(S) = E[f chi_S] its Walsh coefficients and W_k = sum over |S| = k of f^(S)^2. For rho in [-1, 1], T_rho is the noise operator: T_rho f(x) = E[f(Y)] where the Y_i are independent with P(Y_i = x_i) = (1 + rho)/2, so T_rho chi_S = rho^|S| chi_S. For 0 <= rho <= 1, (1 - rho) Var(f) <= D_rho(f) <= (1 - rho^n) Var(f). For 0 < rho < 1 and nonconstant f, equality on the left holds iff all the nonconstant Walsh mass is at level 1, and on the right iff it is at level n; at rho = 0 and rho = 1 both bounds are equalities for every f. If 0 <= rho < sigma <= 1 then D_rho(f) >= D_sigma(f), strictly when f is not constant. No such monotonicity holds on [-1, 1]: D_rho(x_1 x_2) = 1 - rho^2 increases on [-1, 0].

[Corollary 2 (Voter consensus) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] Consider the continuous-time voter model on the component specified below,
where each vertex updates at rate $1$ by copying a uniformly chosen neighbor,
and suppose that the initial opinions are all distinct. Let $\cons$ be the
consensus time. There are absolute constants $0<c<C_{\rm sup}<\infty$ such that
the first two assertions below hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item In the fixed-supercritical case, let $H_\lambda$ be the giant component of
$G(n,\lambda/n)$ for a fixed $\lambda>1$. Then, with high probability,
\[
        c n \le \E^{H_\lambda}\cons \le C_{\rm sup} n.
\]

\item In the slightly supercritical case, let $H_{\rm ER}$ be the giant component
of $G(n,(1+\eps)/n)$, where $\eps\to0$ and $\eps^3n\to\infty$. Then, with high
probability,
\[
        c n \le \E^{H_{\rm ER}}\cons \le C_{\rm sup} n.
\]

\item In the critical window, fix $A_0\ge0$ and suppose that
$|n^{1/3}(np_n-1)|\le A_0$. Let $\mathcal C_1$ be the largest component of $G(n,p_n)$.
For every $\eta>0$ there are constants
$0<c_{A_0,\eta}<C_{A_0,\eta}<\infty$, depending only on $A_0$ and $\eta$, such
that, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\[
        \Pbb\left(
        c_{A_0,\eta} n
        \le \E^{\mathcal C_1}\cons
        \le C_{A_0,\eta} n
        \right)\ge1-\eta .
\]
\end{enumerate}
In all three cases, the same displayed bounds hold for the full coalescence
time of coalescing random walks started with one particle at every vertex. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Voter consensus

=

$$

Then, a copula $C_{\psi}$ is called an Archimedean copula with generator $\psi$ if it can be written as $C_{\psi}\left(v_{1}, \ldots, v_{n}\right)=\psi\left(\phi\left(v_{1}\right)+\cdots+\phi\left(v_{n}\right)\right)$ for all $v_{i} \in[0,1]$, $i =1, \ldots, n$, 
where $\phi=$ $\psi^{-1}=\sup \{x \in \mathbb{R}: \psi(x)>v\}$ is the right continuous inverse of the generator $\psi$.
title: Definition 31 of arXiv:2604.26026

Let N=N(n) with N/n->c in (0,infinity). For all n,i,j let X_ij^(n) be real independent identically distributed random variables with mean zero, variance one, and E|X_ij^(n)|^(4+epsilon)<infinity for some epsilon>0. Let sigma_ij(n) be deterministic real numbers uniformly bounded in absolute value. Let A_n be deterministic real N-by-n matrices whose row Euclidean norms and column Euclidean norms are uniformly bounded over all n and all rows and columns. Put (Y_n)_ij=sigma_ij(n) X_ij^(n)/sqrt(n) and Sigma_n=Y_n+A_n. For the relevant N,n, write A=A_n and sigma_ij=sigma_ij(n), D_j=diag(sigma_1j^2,...,sigma_Nj^2), and Dtilde_i=diag(sigma_i1^2,...,sigma_in^2). Let S_plus consist of the functions z->integral_[0,infinity) (lambda-z)^(-1) nu(dlambda) for probability measures nu on [0,infinity), analytically continued to C minus [0,infinity). Define the unique S_plus-valued solution psi_i,psitilde_j by psi_i(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(Dtilde_i Ttilde(z))/n)] and psitilde_j(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(D_j T(z))/n)], where Psi=diag(psi_i), Psitilde=diag(psitilde_j), T(z)=[Psi(z)^(-1)-z A Psitilde(z) A^T]^(-1), and Ttilde(z)=[Psitilde(z)^(-1)-z A^T Psi(z) A]^(-1). Both trace terms in these canonical equations use division by n. Let P_n be the empirical eigenvalue probability measure of Sigma_n Sigma_n^T and pi_n the deterministic probability measure with Stieltjes transform tr(T_n(z))/N. Then, for every n, E integral lambda P_n(dlambda) = integral lambda pi_n(dlambda) = (1/(N n)) sum_{i=1}^N sum_{j=1}^n sigma_ij(n)^2 + tr(A_n A_n^T)/N. In particular both first moments are bounded uniformly in n by sigma_max^2+a_max^2, where sigma_max bounds all |sigma_ij(n)| and a_max bounds all row and column Euclidean norms of A_n. The empirical first moment appears under expectation in this equality; the deterministic first-moment identity is exact, not merely asymptotic.

[Definition zerohypdef of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] A metric space $(S, d)$ is called a \textit{$0$-hyperbolic space} if for all $\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_3, \sigma_4 \! \in \!  S$,  
\begin{equation}

d(\sigma_1 , \sigma_2 ) + d(\sigma_3 , \sigma_4 ) \leq \max \big( d(\sigma_1 , \sigma_3 ) + d(\sigma_2 , \sigma_4 ) 
 \, , \, d(\sigma_1 , \sigma_4 ) + d(\sigma_2 , \sigma_3 ) 
\big) \, , 
\end{equation}
which is called the \emph{four-point condition}. $\hfill \square$
title: Definition zerohypdef of arXiv:2608.09856

body:
[Definition 7 of arXiv:2608.26084, 'Localic Esakia Duality\\via Conic Frames'] Let~$(X,\leq)$ be a Priestley space. A subset~$C\subseteq X$ is called a \emph{clopen upper set} if~$C$ is clopen and~$\up C= C$. The collection of clopen upper sets is denoted~$\ClopUp(X)$, and forms a distributive lattice under set-theoretic intersections and unions.

	If~$(X,\leq)$ is an Esakia space, then~$\ClopUp(X)$ moreover forms a Heyting algebra, with implication given for clopen upper sets~$A,B\subseteq X$ by~(\cite[\S 2]{bezhanishvili2023FrametheoreticPerspectiveEsakia}):
	\[
	A\to B
	:=
	X\setminus \down (A\setminus B).
	\]
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2608.26084

body:
[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2607.15872, 'Existence of $q$-Bass martingales in the semidiscrete setting'] Let $h\in\RR^{n-1}_{\ge 0}$, $\nu\in\Prob_1(\RR)$, $q\in \Prob(\RR)$, such that $q \ll \lambda$ and  Assumptions \ref{ass:A1}--\ref{ass:A2} hold. Let $f$ be the corresponding $n$-atomic $q$-Bass map and fix $i \in \{1, \dots, n-1\}$. 
Then $h_i = 0$ if and only if
\begin{equation}

	f_i(h) = f_{i-1}(h)+\frac{f_{i+1}(h)-f_{i-1}(h)}{p_{i+1}^*-p_{i-1}^*}p_i,
\end{equation}
where we set $f_0 = f_n = 0$.
Additionally, $h_i \geq \diam(\supp(q))$ if and only if
\begin{equation}

	f_i(h)= U_\nu(p^*_i).
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
	\Lambda_f \subseteq \Lambda^{p_1, \dots, p_n}_\nu.
\]
title: Proposition 23 of arXiv:2607.15872

$\gamma\geq\tau$, and set   
$$

B=E_{\cF_{\tau}}\int_{\tau}^{\gamma}e^{-\phi_{\tau,t}}\,|dB_{t}|.
$$
Then for any Borel $f(t,x)\geq0$ we have
$$
E_{\cF_{\tau}}\int_{\tau}^{\gamma}e^{-\phi_{\tau,t}}(r_{t}\det a_{t})^{1/(d+1)}
f(\sft_{t},x_{t})\,dA_{t}
$$
\begin{equation}
                                            
\leq N(d) (B^{2}+A)^{d/(2d+2)}\|f\|_{L_{ d+1} }.

[Thm ConvSegalAmp of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $(\mathcal{T}_n\coloneq (\mathbb{V}_n,\mathbb{E}_n,\mathbb{F}_n))_{n\ge 0}$ be a sequence of triangulations of $\Sigma$ such that there exist constants $a,A>0$ for which 
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty} 
\frac{\Bigl\lvert \bigl\{f\in \mathbb{F}_n : \tfrac{a^2}{\lvert \mathbb{F}_n\rvert}\leqslant \sigma(f)\leqslant \tfrac{A^2}{\lvert \mathbb{F}_n\rvert}\bigr\}\Bigr\rvert}{\lvert \mathbb{F}_n\rvert} > 0.
\]
Then, for all $(g_1,\dots,g_k)\in G^k$,
$Z_{\mathcal{T}_n} \underset{n\to\infty}{\xrightarrow{C^\infty(G^k)}}Z_{\Sigma}$ in the 
 $C^{\infty}(G^k)$ topology. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theo thm:Frostman-gauge of arXiv:2512.06984, 'Infinite Dimensional Multifractal Analysis of the Wiener measure'] Let $(X,d)$ be a separable metric space and let $h:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be a Hausdorff function
	(continuous, increasing, $h(0)=0$) such that the increasing sets lemma holds on $X$.
	If $A\subset X$ is analytic and $\mathcal H^h(A)>0$, then there exist a compact set $K\subset A$,
	a Borel probability measure $\mu$ supported on $K$, and a constant $C\in(0,\infty)$ such that
	\[
	\forall B\,  ({\rm ball \ in} \ X), \quad 
	\mu\bigl(B\bigr)\ \le\ C\,h( 3\, \mathrm{diam\, } B ).
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Frostman Lemma for a gauge $h$ on a metric space

[Lemma lem:reverse-hazard-ratio of arXiv:2604.25108, 'Terminal Defects, Growing Multiplicity, and Variance Extremality\\in the Double Dixie Cup '] For every $m\ge1$, the function
\[
        e(y):=\frac{d}{d\log y}\log\phi(y)
\]
is strictly negative and strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$.  Consequently, $\phi$ is strictly decreasing, and for every $c>1$ the ratio
\[
        y\mapsto \frac{\phi(cy)}{\phi(y)}
\]
is strictly decreasing.

[Lemma 4 (Stopped physical-state stability) of arXiv:2608.19151, 'Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning for Controlled Hawkes Jump-Diffusions'] Suppose that Assumption~\ref{ass:standing}(S1) holds. Fix
$K\geq1$ and $a\in\mathcal A$. Let
\[
    (X^a,N^a,\lambda^a)
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    (X^{K,a},N^{K,a},\lambda^{K,a})
\]
be constructed with the same Brownian motion, the same Poisson random
measures, the same initial condition, and the same admissible control
process $a$. For $R\geq1$, define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_R^{K,a}
:=
\inf\Bigl\{
t\in[0,T]:\;&
\norm{N_t^{K,a}}_1+\norm{N_t^a}_1>R
&\text{or }\norm{X_t^{K,a}}>R
\text{ or }\norm{X_t^a}>R
\Bigr\}
\wedge T.
\end{aligned}
\]
Set
\[
D_{X,R}^{K,a}(t)
:=
\E\left[
    \sup_{0\leq u\leq t}
    \norm{
        X_{u\wedge\tau_R^{K,a}}^{K,a}
        -
        X_{u\wedge\tau_R^{K,a}}^a
    }
\right],
\]
and
\[
D_{\lambda,R}^{K,a}(t)
:=
\E\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_R^{K,a}}
\norm{\lambda_s^{K,a}-\lambda_s^a}_1\,\dd s.
\] Then, for every $R\geq1$, there exists
$C_{T,R}<\infty$, independent of $K$ and
$a\in\mathcal A$, such that
\begin{equation}

D_{X,R}^{K,a}(t)
\leq
C_{T,R}\int_0^tD_{X,R}^{K,a}(s)\,\dd s
+
C_{T,R}D_{\lambda,R}^{K,a}(t),
\qquad
0\leq t\leq T.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}

D_{X,R}^{K,a}(t)
\leq
C_{T,R}D_{\lambda,R}^{K,a}(t),
\qquad
0\leq t\leq T.
\end{equation}

body: [Lemma 6 (Bennett's integral \citep{bennett1948spectra}) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] For a high-resolution quantizer with local step $\Delta(x)$ and input density $p$ whose overload distortion is negligible, as holds in particular when $p$ is supported within the quantizer's granular range, the distortion is $D=\tfrac{1}{12}\int \Delta(x)^2 p(x)\,dx$, the integral taken over that range. For a uniform quantizer ($\Delta$ constant, overload negligible) this reduces to the additive-white-noise model $D=\Delta^2/12$, with quantization error approximately uniform on $[-\Delta/2,\Delta/2]$ and decorrelated from the signal. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bennett's integral \citep{bennett1948spectra}

body: [Definition of arXiv:2607.06952, 'Universality for cokernels of partially random integral matrices'] Let $p$ be a prime, $\varepsilon >0$ a real number, and $X$ a random variable valued in $\mathbb{Z}_p$ or a finite quotient of $\mathbb{Z}_p$. Then $X$ is \emph{$\varepsilon$-balanced} if $\mathbb{P}(X \equiv t \pmod{p}) \leq 1- \varepsilon$ for all $t \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Otherwise, $X$ is \emph{$\varepsilon$-degenerate}.

[Lemma lem:cyclic_order_same of arXiv:2605.03896, 'Dimer models on astroidal zig-zag graphs'] {BCdTiso}}; see also {[GK13]}]

Let $\mathsf G$ be a minimal graph, and let $\mathsf x\in B(\mathsf G)\sqcup W(\mathsf G)$ be a vertex. Then the strands that $\mathsf x$ lies on are parallel to distinct edges of $N$. Moreover, the cyclic order of these strands (or the corresponding zig-zag paths) around $\mathsf x$ agrees with the cyclic order of the corresponding edges along $\partial N$ if $\mathsf x$ is white, and with the opposite cyclic order if $\mathsf x$ is black. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma D-inverse of arXiv:2608.21805, 'Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equati'] Let $K: \Omega \to L_1(H)$ be a trace-class self-adjoint non-negative operator which, viewed as an $L_2(H,H)$-valued random variable, satisfies $K \in \mathbb{D}^{1,2}(L_2(H,H))$. For each $\varepsilon > 0$ and each deterministic $h \in H$, the random variable
\[
  G^{(\varepsilon)} \;:=\; (K + \varepsilon I)^{-1}\,h \;\in\; H
\]
satisfies the following:

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=2.2em, itemsep=2pt]
 \item There is first a deterministic bound, $\norm{G^{(\varepsilon)}}_H \leq \varepsilon^{-1}\lVert h \rVert_H$ a.s., hence $G^{(\varepsilon)} \in L^\infty(\Omega; H) \subset \bigcap_{p \geq 1} L^p(\Omega; H)$.
  
 \item $\mathbb{D}^{1,2}$-membership and Leibniz formula. $G^{(\varepsilon)} \in \mathbb{D}^{1,2}(H)$, with
  \begin{equation}
    \mathcal{D}_r G^{(\varepsilon)} \;=\; -(K + \varepsilon I)^{-1}\,(\mathcal{D}_r K)\,(K + \varepsilon I)^{-1}\,h
    \quad \text{in } L_2(U, H), \text{ for a.e.\ } r \in [0, T].
  \end{equation}
  More generally, if $K \in \mathbb{D}^{1,p}(L_2(H,H))$ for some $p \in [2, \infty)$, then $G^{(\varepsilon)} \in \mathbb{D}^{1,p}(H)$ and the same formula~(equation eq:D-inverse of the paper) holds in $L^p$.
  
 \item There is next a pathwise bound on the derivative, valid almost surely and for almost every $r$,
  \[
    \norm{\mathcal{D}_r G^{(\varepsilon)}}_{L_2(U, H)} \;\leq\; \varepsilon^{-2}\,\lVert h \rVert_H\,\norm{\mathcal{D}_r K}_{L_2(U, L_2(H,H))} ,
  \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 1 of arXiv:2607.16145, 'The Memoryless Best-Choice Problem'] Every memoryless stopping rule has the form
$$\tau=\min\{k\in [n]: X_k\in D_k\},$$
where $D_k\subset [0,1]$ are Borel sets. This representation is essentially unique if ${\mathbb P}[\tau=n]>0$, in which case  $D_n=[0,1]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def-rr2 of arXiv:2507.01406, '{\Large On Iterated Lorenz Curves with Applications: The Multivariate Case }'] A density $h(u,v)$ on $[0,1]^{2}$ is \textit{reverse regular
of order 2} ($RR_{2}$) if for all $0\leq u_{1}<u_{2}\leq 1$ and $0\leq
v_{1}<v_{2}\leq 1$, 
\begin{equation}
h(u_{1},v_{1})\,h(u_{2},v_{2})\;\leq \;h(u_{1},v_{2})\,h(u_{2},v_{1}).

\end{equation}
Equivalently (under standard regularity so that conditional expectation and
density exist), for $H$ a bivariate distribution with density $h$, the
conditional mean $x\mapsto m_{2|1}^{H}(x)=E[\,X_{2}^{H}\mid X_{1}^{H}=x\,]$
is non-increasing.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] There exist $c > 0$ and $\delta > 0$ such that for any $n \geq 0$, 
\[
\P[ \mathsf{NC}(n,n,\geq \delta n) ] \leq 100 \delta n  \P[ \mathsf{NC}(n,n(1-\delta)) ] + \exp(- cn). 
\]
The same result holds when replacing $\mathsf{NC}(n,n,\geq \delta n)$ (resp. $ \P[ \mathsf{NC}(n,n, \delta n) ] $) by $\lfloor\mathsf{NC}(n,n,\delta n)\rfloor_k$ (resp. $\lfloor\mathsf{NC}(n,n,\geq \delta n)\rfloor_k$).

body: [Definition1 strong_ball of arXiv:2606.27357, '\textbf{Typical distances in high-genus triangulations}'] Fix $n,g \ge 0$ such that $n \ge 2g-1$. Also fix $\ell \ge 0$ and $\mathbf{p} = (p_1,\ldots,p_{\ell}) \in (\mathbb{N}^{*})^{\ell}$. Given $t \in \mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{p}}(n,g)$ and a subset $E$ of oriented edges of $t$, for any $r \ge 0$ we define the strong ball $B_r^{+}(t,E)$ of radius $r$ centered at $E$ as the family of triangulations with holes obtained by keeping all faces having a vertex at graph distance at most $r-1$ from the starting point of an edge in $E$.
title: Definition1 strong_ball of arXiv:2606.27357

body:
Let (X_n) be a martingale for (F_n) and let (H_n)_{n >= 1} be PREDICTABLE, meaning H_n is F_{n-1}-measurable. Define the transform (H . X)_n = sum_{k=1}^{n} H_k (X_k - X_{k-1}), with (H . X)_0 = 0. If each H_n is bounded (or, more generally, if H_n (X_n - X_{n-1}) is integrable for every n), then (H . X) is a martingale. If (X_n) is a SUPERMARTINGALE and in addition H_n >= 0 for every n, then (H . X) is a supermartingale; the same with submartingale. Predictability is the load-bearing hypothesis: H_n may depend on everything known strictly before time n but not on the outcome at time n. Without it the conclusion is false - taking H_n = sgn(X_n - X_{n-1}) gives (H . X)_n = sum |X_k - X_{k-1}|, which is nondecreasing and not a martingale unless the increments vanish. The nonnegativity requirement in the supermartingale case is also necessary, since multiplying by -1 turns a supermartingale into a submartingale. [standard; e.g. Williams, Probability with Martingales, Section 10.6]

[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:direct_sum_lifting}
Take $G = H \otimes I$ with respective Haar measures $\mu_G$, $\mu_H$, and $\mu_I$ such that $\mu_G = \mu_H \otimes \mu_I$. 

Let $f_H$ and $f_I$ be probability densities with respect to $\mu_H$ and $\mu_I$, respectively. 
Then $(g_H,g_I) \in \Sym(f_H) \times \Sym(f_I)$ implies $g_Hg_I \in \Sym(f_Hf_I)$.  
\begin{proof}
For all $a \in H$, $(g_H * f_H)(a) = (g_H * f_H)(a^{-1})$, and for all $b \in I$, $(g_I * f_I)(b) = (g_I * f_I)(b^{-1})$, so
\[
(g_H * f_H)(a)(g_I * f_I)(b)
= (g_H * f_H)(a^{-1})(g_I * f_I)(b^{-1}). \]
Applying Fubini-Tonelli,

\begin{multline*}
\int_{G} g_H(r)g_I(s) f_H(r^{-1}a)f_I(s^{-1}b) \,d\mu_G((r,s)) \\
= \int_{G} g_H(r)g_I(s) f_H(r^{-1}a^{-1})f_I(s^{-1}b^{-1}) \,d\mu_G((r,s)) .
\end{multline*}
Thus, writing $f \coloneqq f_H f_I$ and $g \coloneqq g_H g_I$, 
\[
\int_G g(r,s) f(r^{-1}a,s^{-1}b) \,d\mu_G((r,s))
= \int_G g(r,s) f(r^{-1}a^{-1},s^{-1}b^{-1}) \,d\mu_G((r,s)) ,
\]
so $(g * f)(a,b) = (g * f)(a^{-1},b^{-1})$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2605.15066, 'The critical activation density in graph bootstrap percolation'] Let $S\subset F$. Naturally, we say that  $(S,F)$ is 
{\it $\alpha$-sparse} if $\rho^{\rm max}(S,F)<\alpha$; that is, 
if 
\[
e(F')-e(S)<\alpha(v(F')-v(S)), 
\]
for {\it every} $S\subset F'\subseteq F$.

\[

\qquad

\]
\[
\mu_{+,N}
=
\frac{(\sqrt{M_N}+\sqrt N)^2}{N},
\qquad
\sigma_{+,N}
=
\frac{\sqrt{M_N}+\sqrt N}{N}
(M_N^{-1/2}+N^{-1/2})^{1/3},
\]
\[
\chi_{N,G}^+
=
\frac{\lambda_{1,G}^{(N)}-\mu_{+,N}}{\sigma_{+,N}},
\qquad

\qquad
s_N=(\log N)^{1/3},
\]
and
\[
A_2=\left(\frac14\right)^{2/3},
\qquad
B_2=4^{1/3}.
\]
Then:

\begin{enumerate}
\item For every \(q>A_2\), there are
\(\eta_q^{G,+}>1/3\) and \(N_q^{G,+}\) such that
\[
\Prob(\chi_{N,G}^+\geq qr_N)
\leq
N^{-\eta_q^{G,+}},
\qquad
N\geq N_q^{G,+}.
\]

\item For every \(q>B_2\), there are
\(\eta_q^{G,-}>1/3\) and \(N_q^{G,-}\) such that
\[
\Prob(\chi_{N,G}^+\leq-qs_N)
\leq
N^{-\eta_q^{G,-}},
\qquad
N\geq N_q^{G,-}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Definition 2 of arXiv:2604.14427, 'A criterion for proving entropy chaos on path space'] (see, e.g., \cite{CarlenCD,Carlen:162610})    
  The space of \emph{proper infinitesimal characteristics} is the set of pairs $(\rho(t),v(t))$,
  with $\rho: \RR^d \times \RR_+\rightarrow \RR_+$, $v:\RR^d\times \RR_+\rightarrow\RR^d$ functions
  satisfying the following properties:
  a \textit{continuity equation} in weak form,
  \begin{equation} 
    \int_{\R^d}f(x,T)\rho(x,T)dx-\int_{\R^d}f(x,0)\rho(x,0)dx=\int_0^T\int_{\R^d}(v(t)\cdot\nabla
    f)\rho(x,t)dx,
  \end{equation}
  and a \textit{finite energy condition},
  \begin{equation}
    \int_0^T\int_{\R^d} (|u(x,t)|^2+|v(x,t)|^2){\rho}(x,t)\dd x\dd t
    <+\infty,
  \end{equation}
  \noindent  with $u(x,t)=\frac{\nabla \rho(x,t)}{2\rho(x,t)}$, for all $T\geq 0$ and all $f\in
  C_0^{\infty}(\R^{d+1})$.
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2604.14427

[Definition def:shiftable-kernel of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] Let $K$ denote the NURS transition kernel induced by a shiftable direction law
$q$, and let $K^t$ denote its $t$-step iterate.
Given a current state $\sigma \in S_n$, one step of $K$ is constructed as
follows:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Sample an index pair $(I,J)$ uniformly from
  $\{(i,j):1\le i<j\le n\}$, and then sample a direction
  $\eta \in \Omega_{IJ}$ according to a fixed, state-independent law.
  \item Let $2m := \ord(\eta)$ and set $W := \{0,1,\dots,2m-1\}$.
  Sample an index $r \in W$ with probability proportional to
  $w(\sigma \eta^{r})$, and update the state to $\sigma' = \sigma \eta^{r}$.
\end{enumerate}
For the coupling across an edge $(\sigma,\sigma\circ\tau_{ij})$ we use the same
random choices $((I,J),\eta)$ for both chains.
title: Shiftable kernel

body: [Definition 4 (Global solution) of arXiv:2506.12834, 'Space-time fractional stochastic partial differential equations driven by L\'evy white noi'] We say that an $\{\cF_t\}$-adapted stochastic process $u(t,x):[0,T]\times\R^d\mapsto\R$ is a global solution of \eqref{e:fde-white} for L\'evy space-time white nosie (resp. \eqref{e:fde-jump} for pure jump L\'evy noise), if for any $T>0$, $\{u(t,x)\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ satisfies the integral equation \eqref{e:de-solution} (resp. \eqref{e:de-solution2}) for each $t\in[0,T]$. Furthermore, we say that the solution is unique, if $u$ and $v$ are any two global solutions, then for all $(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\R^d$, $u(t,x)=v(t,x)$ almost surely.
title: Global solution

[Lem Kemperman of arXiv:2412.03415, 'Critical first passage percolation on random graphs'] Suppose that for any $m\geqslant 1$, $ (\eta_1, \ldots \eta_m)$ are cyclically exchangeable integer valued random variables with $\eta_i\geqslant -1$ a.s. Define $W_j = \sum_{i=1}^j \eta_i$ and
$$
T_{-k} = \inf\{ j > 0 : W_j-j = -k\}.
$$
Then, 
$$
\pr( T_{-k}=m) = \frac{k}{m} \pr(W_m-m=-k).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Kemperman's formula

[Theorem 4 (Local-in-time theory) of arXiv:2609.02019, '2609.02019'] Under Assumption~\ref{Hypo-Q}, let
		\[
		s>\frac{3}{2}+\max\{2\delta_{\mathcal Q},1\}.
		\]
		For every $H^s$-valued $\mathcal F_0$-measurable random variable $v_0$,
		the Cauchy problem \eqref{Target problem SCCF} admits a pathwise unique maximal
		$H^s$ classical solution $(v,\tau^*)$ in the sense of
		Definition~\ref{Def : solution}.
		Moreover,  the maximal lifetime $\tau^*$ is independent of the Sobolev index $s$: if $v_0$
		belongs to two admissible Sobolev spaces, then the corresponding maximal
		lifetimes coincide; and
		the following blow-up criterion also holds:
		\begin{equation}
			\limsup_{t\uparrow\tau^*}
			\left(
			\|\partial_xv(t)\|_{L^\infty}
			+
			\|\Lambda v(t)\|_{L^\infty}
			\right)
			=\infty\quad
			\text{a.s. on}\ \left\{\tau^*<\infty\right\},
		\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Local-in-time theory

[Theorem teo_fey_kac of arXiv:2605.07832, 'A Bismut -Elworthy formula for BSDEs with degenerate noise'] Let hypotheses (ip_forward of the paper), (ip_forward_agg of the paper) and (ip-psiphi of the paper)
hold true.  Moreover assume that $\phi$ is G\^ateaux differentiable with bounded derivative and that $\psi$ is G\^ateaux differentiable with respect to $x$, $y$ and $z$ \textcolor{red}{with bounded derivatives}. The nonlinear Kolmogorov equation ((Kolmo of the paper)) has a unique mild solution $v$ given by the formula
$$v(t, x) = Y_t^{t,x} ,\qquad     (t, x) \in [0, T ] \times H,$$
where $(X^{t,x},Y ^{t,x} , Z^{ t,x} )$ is the solution to the FBSDE (equation fbsde of the paper). Moreover, we
have, $\mathbb P$-a.s.,
\begin{align}

Y_s^{t,x} = v(s, X_s^{t,x} ),\quad       Z_s^{t,x} =\nabla_x v(s, X_s^{t,x} )\nabla_x  X_s^{t,x}G(s)
\end{align}
and, under our assumptions, there exists a constant $C$, that may depend also on $\nabla_x\phi$,
$\nabla_x\psi$ and $L_\psi$, such that
\begin{equation}
\vert Z_s^{t,x}\vert \leq C.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:ik-model-validates-cdia-and-fs2 of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] {fischer_axiomatizations_1984}}] 
  Both $\textsf{C}_\Diamond$ and $\textsf{FS2}$ are valid in every IK-model.
  \begin{proof}
    The former is proven similarly to Proposition (prop:separation-cdia of the paper) (1), without using any frame condition on $\mathfrak{M}$.
    For the latter, take any IK-model $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$, any $\varphi, \psi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$, and any $x, x'$ such that $x \leq x' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \varphi \to \Box \psi$,
    and it suffices to show that $x' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box (\varphi \to \psi)$.
    To do so, take any $x'', y'', y'''$ such that $x' \leq x'' \sqsubset y'' \leq y''' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$,
    and we shall show that $y''' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$.
    By the FS2 condition, there is $x'''$ such that $x'' \leq x''' \sqsubset y'''$,
    then $y''' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ implies $x''' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \varphi$.
    Here, $x'' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \varphi \to \Box \psi$ by persistency,
    so $x''' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$. Therefore, $y''' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma 71 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Suppose that we have the setup of Section~\ref{se:bilipschitz_setup} but condition on the event that $\CL \cap \partial\D = \emptyset$.\footnote{This conditioning implies that for each $\lambda \in (0,1]$, the law of~$\lambda\Gamma$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the law of~$\Gamma$, see \cite[Lemma~7.2]{my2025geouniqueness}.} Let $(\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions}$ be a weak \clekp{} resistance form. Then there exists $\resexp \in [\ddouble,\dsle]$ such that the following holds. body:
[Theorem thm:from-r-to-l of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] Let the graph $G$ be finite and take $0\le l\le r$. We endow the subdivided graph $G_r$
  with i.i.d.\ edge weights $W_e>0$, $e\in E_r$. Consider the family $W^{(l)}$ of
  corresponding random weights
from Theorem (thm:vrjp-on-G-r-pos-rec of the paper), all realized on the same probability space
with expectation operator ${\mathbb E}$. We abbreviate
$C_\alpha:=2^{-\alpha}\Gamma(\tfrac12-\alpha)/\sqrt{\pi}$
for $0\le\alpha<\frac12$ and ${c_2}:=\gamma+\log 2=1.27036\ldots$, where 
\begin{align}
  
  \gamma=-\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\log t\, dt=0.57721\ldots
\end{align}
denotes the Euler Mascheroni constant. 
For all $\bar e\in E_l$ and $e'\in E_r$, one has
  \begin{align}
    
    {\mathbb E}[(W^{(l)}_{\bar e})^\alpha]
    &\le (2^{-\alpha})^{r-l}{\mathbb E}[W_{e'}^\alpha]
    &\hspace{-1cm}\text{ for } \alpha\in[0,1],\\
    
    {\mathbb E}[(W^{(l)}_{\bar e})^\alpha]
     &\le \frac{1}{C_\alpha}\min_{m\in\{l,\ldots,r\}}\left(C_\alpha 
       (2^{-\alpha})^{r-m}{\mathbb E}[W_{e'}^\alpha]\right)^{2^{m-l}}
     &\hspace{-1cm}\text{ for } \alpha\in[0,\tfrac12),
    \\
      
    {\mathbb E}[\log W^{(l)}_{\bar e}]
    &\le \min_{m\in\{l,\ldots,r\}}
      2^{m-l}\left({\mathbb E}[\log W_{e'}]-(r-m)\log 2+{c_2}\right)-{c_2}.
  \end{align}
  Set $m_0:=r-2-\lfloor\alpha^{-1}\log_2(C_\alpha {\mathbb E}[W_{e'}^\alpha])\rfloor$
  and $m_1:=r-2-\lfloor(\log 2)^{-1}({\mathbb E}[\log W_{e'}]+{c_2})\rfloor$.
  If $m_0\in\{l,\ldots,r\}$, a minimizer in (equation eq:combined-alpha of the paper)
  is given by $m=m_0$. If $m_0<l$ or $m_0>r$, it is given by
  $m=l$ or $m=r$, respectively. The analogous statement holds for $m_1$
  with (equation eq:combined-alpha of the paper) replaced by (equation eq:combined-log of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Decay of the effective weights by restriction

body:
[Lemma 15 (Finite-product cutoff reduction) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $(E,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $J\in\N$, and let
$\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_J:E\to\R^3$ be measurable.  For
$\boldsymbol\epsilon=(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_J)\in\{0,1\}^J$, set
\[
 \mathcal I_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}:=
 \{\nu: \epsilon_\nu=1\},
 \qquad
 M_{\Lambda}^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}(z)
 :=\prod_{\nu\in\mathcal I_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}}
 m_\Lambda(\zeta_\nu(z)),
\]
with the empty product equal to one.  If
$\mathcal I_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}=\varnothing$, the maxima and indicators below
are understood as zero.  There is a constant $C_J$, depending only on $J$ and
the uniform zeroth-order cutoff bound, such that
\begin{align}
 |M_{\Lambda}^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}(z)-1|^2
 &\le C_J\,
 \one_{\{\max_{\nu\in\mathcal I_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}}
              |\zeta_\nu(z)|\ge c_0\Lambda\}},
 \\
 |M_{\Lambda}^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}(z)
   -M_{\Lambda'}^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}(z)|^2
 &\le C_J\left(
 \one_{\{\max_{\nu\in\mathcal I_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}}
              |\zeta_\nu(z)|\ge c_0\Lambda\}}
 +
 \one_{\{\max_{\nu\in\mathcal I_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}}
              |\zeta_\nu(z)|\ge c_0\Lambda'\}}
 \right).
 
\end{align}
Consequently, for every nonnegative measurable $F$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_E |M_{\Lambda}^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}-1|^2F\,\dd\mu
 \le C_J
 \int_{\{\max_{\nu\in\mathcal I_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}}
              |\zeta_\nu|\ge c_0\Lambda\}}F\,\dd\mu,
\end{equation}
and the analogous two-tail bound follows from
\eqref{eq:finite-product-two-cutoffs}.  The same statement compares products
formed from two different admissible cutoff families, after replacing $c_0$
by the smaller plateau constant and using a common zeroth-order bound.  The
conclusion applies with $F$ equal to a static squared kernel or to a normalized
time-increment majorant.  Repeated frequency legs are included by listing them
with multiplicity.

[Definition defextgraph of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] Let $f\in \mathcal D_I$.
  \begin{enumerate}[a)]
    \item 
      The  {\em extended graph} of $f$ is defined as
      $$
        \mathbb G(f)
         := \bigcup_{t\in I}\big(\{t\} \times [\min(f(t-),f(t)), \max(f(t-),f(t))]\big).
      $$
      Thus, in  words from~[K23], the extended graph  ``contains the graph together with the straight lines connecting the two ends of a jump discontinuity''.
    \item 
      A~{\em parametric representation} of (the extended graph of) $f$ is a mapping $\phi$ which maps $[0,1]$ onto $\mathbb G(f)$ and for which $u \mapsto \phi(u)$ is increasing with respect to the total order $\preceq$ on $\mathbb G(f)$ defined by
      $$
        (t_1,x_1)\preceq (t_2,x_2) :\Longleftrightarrow t_1\le t_2
          \mbox{ and } \left(t_1=t_2 \Rightarrow |x_1 - f(t_1-)| \le |x_2 - f(t_1-)|\right).
      $$
  \end{enumerate}
title: Definition defextgraph of arXiv:2605.10617

        $$|\tilde{\mu}_{\mathcal{C}_n}(\mathbf{I})-\varrho_{\mathrm{MP}_y}(\mathbf{I})| \prec n^{-1/4}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem description-of-Pinv of arXiv:2607.05097, 'Asymptotics of Lyapunov Exponents and Phase Transitions for Fluids with Degenerate Forcing'] Let $\mu \in P_{\mathrm{inv}}$ be ergodic. Then there is some $z_0$ such that $\mu(\{z = z_0\}) = 1$. Furthermore, there is some $i$ such that $\mu(\{v \in \operatorname{Span}(\{V_j \mid \Re \lambda_j = \Re \lambda_i\})\}) = 1$, where $V_1,\dots,V_k$ are the generalized eigenspaces of $A(z_0)$ corresponding to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k$. Additionally, we have
$$\int \Lambda(z,v)d\mu(z,v) = \Re \lambda_i \,.$$
In particular, if $\mu(\{P_0(z)v = 0\}) = 0$ then
$$\int \Lambda(z,v)d\mu(z,v) = \lambda(A(z_0)) \,.$$
title: Lem description-of-Pinv of arXiv:2607.05097

[Prop mySp-vs-mySp-gl of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The inclusion of equivariantly cofibrant orthogonal $G$-spectra induces a fully faithful global functor ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}$. Moreover, its underlying ${\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}$-functor admits a right adjoint which is levelwise a localization at the equivariant weak equivalences.
    \begin{proof}
        Lemma~(lemma:equiv-spectra-vs-gl-spectra of the paper) already shows that ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}$ is fully faithful and admits a pointwise right adjoint which is a localization at the equivariant weak equivalences.
        To complete the proof, it remains to verify the Beck--Chevalley condition for the pointwise right adjoints with respect to \emph{injective} homomorphisms. As the right adjoints are localizations, this amounts to saying that $\alpha^*\colon{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\text{$G'$-gl}\to{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\text{$G$-gl}$ sends $G'$-equivariant weak equivalences to $G$-equivariant ones for any injective $\alpha\colon G\to G'$. This is however immediate from Proposition~(prop:i!-left-Quillen-equiv-sp of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop mySp-vs-mySp-gl of arXiv:2608.28504

    \item 
    \[
        \mathrm{Vol}\Bigl( B\bigl(x_A,  R''\bigr) \setminus B\big(x_A,  R'\big) \Bigr)
        = \mathrm{Vol}\Bigl( B\bigl(x_A,  R\bigr) \Bigr)= \kappa_{k} \frac{r_2}{ 10^k n} \geq  \kappa_{k} \frac{2\tau}{10^k n} .
    \]
    where $\kappa_{k}$ is the volume of a ball of unit radius in $\mathbb{R}^k$.
    
    \item  
    Consider any two points $x_0,x_1$ with $x_0 \in B\left(x_A,R\right)$ and $x_1 \in B(x_A,R'')\setminus B(x_A,R')$. Define, for $\ell\ge 0$,
    \[
        I(\ell;x_0,x_1)\triangleq \mathrm{Vol}\Big( B\big(x_0,(\ell/n)^{1/k}\big)\,\mathbin{\scalebox{1.2}{\ensuremath{\cap}}}\,B\big(x_1,(\ell/n)^{1/k}\big)\Big).
    \]
    Then the map $\ell\mapsto I(\ell;x_0,x_1)$ is convex on $[r_2-2\tau,r_2]$, and there exists a constant $\alpha^{(lmm:gainonepattern of the paper)}_{\gamma ,k}>0$ such that
    \begin{align} 
        I(r_2)-2I(r_2-\tau)+I(r_2-2\tau)
        \ge \frac{\alpha^{(lmm:gainonepattern of the paper)}_{\gamma ,k}}{n}\,\tau^{\,2} \, .
    \end{align}
    
    \item  
    \[
        B\left(x_A,\,R'' + (\gamma /n)^{1/k}\right)  \subseteq  A, \qquad A  \subseteq  B(x_A, R''').
    \]
    
    \item 
    Any point $d \in [0,1]^k \setminus B(x_A,R''')$ satisfies\footnote{The distance from a point $d$ to a cell $A$ is defined as $\operatorname{dist}(d,A) = \inf_{a\in A} \| d-a\|_2$.}
    \[
        \operatorname{dist}(d,A) > 2\left(\frac{\gamma }{n}\right)^{1/k}.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'] For each one-variable meet APS term $\triangle v$, we define $\mu(\triangle)\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ recursively as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\mu(v)=\infty$, 
    \item $\mu(\Box\triangle)=\mu(\triangle)+1$, 
    \item $\mu(\boxtimes\triangle)=0$, 
    \item $\mu(\triangle_0\land\triangle_1) = \min\{\mu(\triangle_0), \mu(\triangle_1)\}$.
\end{enumerate}
Here, $\infty+1=\infty$.

[Proposition prop:vertical of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] There is $c=c(d)>0$ such that the following holds. Let $\eta>0$, $\epsilon\in(0,1)$,
$0<\Delta\le\Lambda$ and $W>0$, and let $\ell$ satisfy
\begin{equation}

  \Delta\ge c_0\ell^2(\epsilon/3)^{-4/\kappa}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\eta\ell^d\ge1 .
\end{equation}
Let $\mathsf G\ge\max\{c_1\Delta^{1/2}(\epsilon/3)^{-1/d},\,12r\}$, and put $K'=W+2\mathsf G$ and
$K=K'+2\mathsf G$. Let
$B\subseteq Q_W\times[0,t_0]$ and $B'\subseteq Q_W\times[t_0+\Delta,\Lambda]$, and let $A,A'$ be
increasing events determined by $B$ and $B'$ in the sense of (lem:Hprops of the paper). Then
\begin{equation}

  \mathbb{P}_\eta(A\cap A')\le\mathbb{P}_\eta(A)\Big[\mathbb{P}_{\eta(1+\epsilon)}(A')
  +\Gamma\,e^{-c\eta\epsilon^2\Delta^{d/2}}\Big]
  +\Big(\tfrac K\ell\Big)^de^{-c\eta\epsilon^2\ell^d}
  +C_d\,\eta\,(K+\Lambda^{1/2})^de^{-\mathsf G^2/(8d\Lambda)} ,
\end{equation}
where $\Gamma=C_d\,\epsilon^{-d}\big(K\Delta^{-1/2}\big)^{d(d+1)}$ is the factor
(equation eq:Gamma of the paper) of (thm:mixingupper of the paper) at mixing parameter $\epsilon/3$.

body:
[Pro Pro1 of arXiv:2606.22183, 'Expected loss of quasi-arithmetic means of exchangeable random variables'] The following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
 \item[(i)] If $n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{1\}$ and $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n$ are exchangeable random variables, then the $(n-1)$-dimensional random vectors
 \[
   (\xi_2,\xi_3,\ldots,\xi_n), \quad (\xi_1,\xi_3,\ldots,\xi_n),\quad \ldots\quad (\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots,\xi_{n-1})
 \]
 have the same distributions.
 
\item[(ii)]
If $h:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a Borel measurable function and $(\xi_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of exchangeable random variables, then $(h(\xi_n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is also exchangeable.

\item[(iii)]
If $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\in\mathbb{R}$, and $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n$ are exchangeable random variables,
 then, for each permutation $\sigma$ of $(1,\ldots,n)$, we have $\sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_{\sigma(i)} \xi_i$ has the same distribution as $\sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_i \xi_i$.
\end{itemize}

body:
[Corollary 8 of arXiv:2609.01402, 'Parabolic Lie algebroid connections on parabolic principal bundles over curves'] Let $X$ be a compact connected Riemann surface and $G$ a connected complex reductive affine algebraic group.
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group of biholomorphisms of $X$ and $E_{G}$ a $\Gamma$--equivariant holomorphic 
principal $G$--bundle on $X$ such that $E_G$ is not semistable. Take any $\Gamma$--equivariant holomorphic Lie 
algebroid $(V,\, \phi)$ on $X$ that satisfies the condition that the anchor map
$\phi$ not surjective. Then the Harder--Narasimhan reduction $E_{P}\,\subset\, 
E_{G}$ of $E_G$ admits a $\Gamma$--equivariant holomorphic $(V,\, \phi)$--connection.

[Conjecture of arXiv:2603.27144, 'On the critical fugacity of the hard-core model on regular bipartite graphs'] There are $c,C>0$ such that for every integer $\delta\ge2$ there
is a simple $\delta$-regular bipartite finite graph $G$, with bipartition
$(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{O})$ satisfying $h(G)\ge c$ and local expansion property
with $C_{\mathrm{LE}}\le C$ and $M_{\mathrm{LE}}\ge\frac{|V|}{\delta}$ such that
for $\lambda=c\frac{\log\delta}{\delta}$ it holds that $\mu^{G}(\mathcal{M}>c\lambda|V|)\ge c$. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

body:
[Thm BE3 of arXiv:2411.08725, 'Berry-Esseen bounds for large-time asymptotics of one-dimensional diffusion processes via '] Let Assumption~{\rm (ass3 of the paper)} with $\alpha >\frac{1}{2}$ and $\beta >1$ hold.
Let $x\in (l,\infty )$, and let $X_t^x$ be the solution to (equation eq:SDE12 of the paper). 
Assume that $X_t^x$ does not hit $l$ almost surely.
Furthermore, assume that there exists a constant $q\in (1,\infty )$ such that 
\begin{equation}
\limsup _{y\rightarrow \infty} \sup _{t\in [0,\infty )} \left( \frac{q(q+1)}{q-1} \left( \frac{\partial \sigma }{\partial y} (t,y) \right) ^2 +2q \frac{\partial b}{\partial y} (t,y) \right) < \frac{\sigma _1^2 b_1^2}{2}.
\end{equation}
Then there exists a positive constant $C$ such that 
\[
d_{\rm  TV} \left( {\rm Law} \left(\frac{X_t^x -x - t \overline{b _\infty}(t)}{\overline{\sigma _\infty}(t) \sqrt{t}} \right) , {\rm Law}(Z)\right) \leq \frac{C\log t}{\sqrt{t}}, \quad t\geq 2,
\]
where $Z$ is a random variable with the standard normal distribution.
title: Thm BE3 of arXiv:2411.08725
