Statement (finite escape of a perturbed dormant coordinate).
Take scalar full-batch Adam, corrected from time0 or uncorrected, with
0<b<1, 0<d<1, eta,lambda,epsilon>0 and m0=v0=0. Put
 c=(1-b)/(1+b), rho=epsilon/(eta lambda).
Suppose rho<c/2. Choose ANY R with 0<R<c/2-rho and set
 q=c/(rho+R)-1>1.
Every standard initialization 0<|x0|<eta R has a finite first time N
with |x_N|>eta R. While |x_0|,...,|x_t|<=eta R, signs alternate and
 |x_(t+1)|>=q |x_t|.
Consequently N is at most the smallest positive integer with
q^N |x0|>eta R. Equality |x0|=eta R is also harmless; a step leaves it.
This holds for BOTH usual separate bias corrections and uncorrected Adam.

For b=.9 and p=1, every dormant eigenvalue lambda2>38 obeys the premise.
In claim008's diagonal family the active coordinate evolves independently.
Any nonzero perturbation of its dormant x2, with moments still initialized
to zero, eventually exceeds eta R, however small that perturbation is.
Thus the zero-coordinate trajectory is unstable in the x2 direction, with
an explicit finite escape scale R<1/38-1/lambda2. This does NOT say that
the perturbed trajectory has a particular asymptotic curvature or cannot
later return to a small neighborhood.

Proof. Normalize X=x/eta,M=m/(eta lambda),V=v/(eta lambda)^2. At time t,
 M'=bM+(1-b)X, V'=dV+(1-d)X^2,
 X'=X-M'/[(1-alpha_t)(sqrt(Vhat')+rho)],
where alpha_t=b^(t+1),Vhat'=V'/(1-d^(t+1)) in the corrected case, and
alpha_t=0,Vhat'=V' in the uncorrected case.

Assume past |X_s|<=R, s<=t. The corrected Vhat' is a convex combination
of X_0^2,...,X_t^2 (standard v0=0). Hence sqrt(Vhat')<=R. For the raw
variance its weights sum to 1-d^(t+1)<1, giving the same bound.
Let D=sqrt(Vhat')+rho<=R+rho<c/2.

Induct on the invariant momentum cone
 M X<=0,   |M|<=c |X|,   X!=0.                              (1)
It holds initially since M0=0. Write M=-r X, 0<=r<=c. Then
 M'=h X, h=1-b-br in [c,1-b],
because 1-b-bc=c. Set E=(1-alpha_t)D<=D<=R+rho<c/2.
Now
 X'=-X G, G=h/E-1 >= c/(R+rho)-1=q>1,
so the sign flips and amplitude grows. Moreover
 |M'|/|X'|=hE/(h-E)<=c.
Indeed the latter is equivalent to E<=ch/(h+c), and h>=c implies
ch/(h+c)>=c/2>E. The new momentum is opposite the new position.
Thus the cone (1) propagates until the first exit, and so does the stated
geometric lower bound. If no exit occurred, |X_t|>=q^t|X0| would contradict
|X_t|<=R. The bound on N follows by the same contradiction.

The proof uses exact inequalities only; no linearization at the singular
raw-v origin and no uniform-in-time Taylor expansion is needed. The
second-moment parameter d affects the convex weights but not the escape
criterion. In diagonal dimension2, coordinate independence transfers this
scalar escape directly to the perturbation of the dormant coordinate.

are already in Fong-Yang 2608.20638v2; no novelty claim is made for the
threshold. This records the direct standard-moment cone and explicit
finite escape as a limitation on robustness of target2's exact alignment.
It does not enlarge the audited p=1 attraction interval of claim006 or
settle target1 for p>1. In that latter regime rho->0, the same escape
statement applies for fixed R<c/2 and sufficiently small eta.

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}_h[
\sup_{\theta\in[0,\theta_*]}\sup_{\Lambda\subset V,\tau_0\in\Omega(\mu_\Lambda)}&\sup_{\tau_1,\tau_2\in\Omega(\partial B((u,v),r))}\\&d_{TV}({(1-\theta)\otimes\mu^{\tau_0,\tau_1}}(\sigma_{uv}\in\cdot),{(1-\theta)\otimes\mu^{\tau_0,\tau_2}}(\sigma_{uv}\in\cdot)
]\leq e^{-Cr},
\end{aligned}$$where we use $\sigma_{uv}$ to denote the configuration $(\sigma_u,\sigma_v)$. Here $d_{TV}$ is the total variation distance and the outer expectation is taken with respect to the random field $h$. The subset $
\partial B((u,v),r)$ is the boundary of the $r$-neighborhood of the edge $(u,v)$ defined in \eqref{neighborhood}, and thus $\tau_1,\tau_2$ ranges over any two possible boundary configurations of the $r$-neighborhood $B((u,v),r)$. We use the notation ${(1-\theta)\otimes \mu^{\tau_0,\tau_i}}$ to stand for the measure $(1-\theta)\otimes \mu^{\tau_0}$ further pinned by $\tau_i$ on $\partial B((u,v),r)$, and we assume that $\tau_1,\tau_2$ are consistent with $\tau_0$ whenever they have overlapping supports.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:af20ba1d93c91c59f91fc73963b765154efe901c9edb835424dd8a4c25f00702","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/af/af20ba1d93c91c59f91fc73963b765154efe901c9edb835424dd8a4c25f00702.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:d5427a86385ff05607dd6ee1e6f91c71d4b1ce8a40776ab41bf8c4918f3bcda4","bundle_entry_key":"rank-one-gd","bundle_id":"population.t419-lora-rank-one-all-scale-finite-accuracy-and-boundedness-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"LoRA and unbalanced linear-network gradient dynamics","draft":"w705/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:lora-rank-one-all-scale-gaussian-gd-finite-accuracy-euler","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C015 v1: rank-one population GD at all Gaussian scales, finite requested accuracy

Kind: narrowed. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.
This covers arbitrary input/output dimensions and every s>0 at rank one. The chosen constant GD step depends on eps and can be extremely small. It is not a linear-convergence theorem for one step size simultaneously for all accuracies.

Prior work: Kunin, Raventos, Domine, Chen, Klindt, Saxe and Ganguli, Get rich quick: exact solutions reveal how unbalanced initializations promote rapid feature learning, arXiv:2406.06158, Appendix A.2, especially A.2.4 equations (30)-(33), printed p.19, and A.2.5 equation (34), p.20, already give the single-neuron unbalanced gradient-flow solutions and basin boundary under whitened data. With zero output weight, their saddle boundary reduces to w0^T beta_star=0. Gradient-flow convergence from the present initialization is therefore settled, not a new result. The quantitative estimate below uses an equivalent spectral expression for that known flow and an elementary, deliberately conservative finite-horizon Euler-error argument to obtain a specified ordinary GD hitting time. Du-Hu-Lee arXiv:1806.00900, Theorem 3.2 instead initializes both rank-one factors with a small Gaussian; it is not the zero/random all-scale theorem here. Literature novelty of the finite-step corollary is unresolved.

## Statement

Let Delta=u v^T, where u in R^m and v in R^p are unit vectors and m,p>=1. Consider simultaneous GD on f(b,a)=||b a^T-Delta||F^2/2, with b0=0 and a0~N(0,s^2 I_p), any s>0. Fix 0<rho<1 and 0<eps<1. Define the following deterministic real constants:

 D=2p s^2/rho, nu_bar=1+D/2,
 U_bar=2+32 nu_bar/(s^2 rho^2),
 V_bar=1+4 sqrt(p)/rho^(3/2),
 T=(1+D) log[16 nu_bar(V_bar+U_bar)/eps],
 R=sqrt(D+4)+2, L=6R^2+1,
 M=(R^2/2+1)R.

Choose any constant step

 0<eta<=min{1,1/M,[eps/(4RM)] exp[-L(T+1)]},

and take N=ceil(T/eta). With probability at least 1-rho over a0,

 ||b_N a_N^T-Delta||F<=eps.

The guarantee includes p>1, a proper input-side rank-one bottleneck, at every initialization scale. The signal condition number is 1. For a rank-one target of singular value lambda>0, use normalized scale s/sqrt(lambda), normalized step eta lambda, and normalized requested error eps/lambda in this statement. It is only a hitting-time guarantee for the prescribed eps, with no efficiency or independently checked proof claim.

## One initial event; no independence multiplication

Write x0=v^T a0 and z0=a0-x0 v. With probability at least 1-rho,

 d=||a0||^2<=D, |x0|>=s rho/2.

Indeed E||a0||^2=ps^2 and Markov bounds the first failure probability by rho/2. The standard normal density is at most 1/sqrt(2pi), so P(|x0|<s rho/2)<=sqrt(2/pi)rho/2<rho/2. Use a union bound; the two events need not be independent. Fix this event. In particular d>0 and x0 is nonzero.

## Known flow in a spectral representation

Both GD and gradient flow keep b in span(u), so write b=beta u and a=x v+z with z orthogonal to v. The normalized gradient flow is

 beta'=x-beta||a||^2,
 x'=beta-beta^2 x,
 z'=-beta^2 z,
 beta(0)=0, x(0)=x0, z(0)=z0.

As in the cited primary source, ||a||^2-beta^2=d is conserved. In Z=(beta,x,z) coordinates define the symmetric block operator

 H_d=[[ -d/2, 1 ],[ 1, d/2 ]] on (beta,x),
 H_d=(d/2)I on the z coordinates.

Then the exact flow is equivalently

 Z'=H_d Z-(||Z||^2/2)Z,
 Z(t)=w(t)/sqrt(1+integral_0^t ||w(tau)||^2 d tau),
 w(t)=exp(t H_d)Z0.

The displayed expression follows by differentiating its positive scalar denominator. It starts at Z0 and solves the same ODE, so uniqueness identifies it with the source's known single-neuron flow; it is not an additional claimed discovery. Its denominator never vanishes. Alternatively, boundedness below gives global existence directly.

Let nu=sqrt(1+d^2/4), g=nu-d/2=1/(nu+d/2). The two eigenvalues of the 2-by-2 block are nu and -nu, with orthonormal eigenvectors e_plus,e_minus. Choose e_plus with positive beta and x entries. Decompose

 w(t)=a_plus e^(nu t)e_plus+a_minus e^(-nu t)e_minus+e^(d t/2)z0.

Because Z0=(0,x0,z0), the spectral projections give

 a_plus^2=x0^2(1+d/(2nu))/2>=x0^2/2,
 a_minus^2=x0^2(1-d/(2nu))/2<=a_plus^2.

In particular a_plus is nonzero. The limiting factors are

 Z_star=sign(a_plus)sqrt(2nu)e_plus,

and their product is the target: the positive eigenvector obeys x/beta=nu+d/2=1/g, while its scaled squared norm is 2nu=g+1/g, hence beta_star^2=g and beta_star x_star=1. Its z component is zero.

## Explicit exponential flow error bound

Let h(t)^2=1+integral_0^t ||w(tau)||^2 d tau and

 Q(t)=h(t)^2/[a_plus^2 e^(2nu t)/(2nu)].

Orthogonality of the three spectral components gives the exact formula

 h(t)^2=1+a_plus^2(e^(2nu t)-1)/(2nu)
          +a_minus^2(1-e^(-2nu t))/(2nu)
          +||z0||^2(e^(d t)-1)/d.

Subtract the leading exponential term. Since 2nu>=2g, ||z0||^2<=d, and a_plus^2>=x0^2/2, it follows that

 |Q(t)-1|<=U e^(-2gt), U=2+8nu/x0^2.

To see every term, the initial constant and the two constant/decaying eigenmode corrections contribute at most (2nu/a_plus^2+1+a_minus^2/a_plus^2)e^(-2nu t), bounded by (4nu/x0^2+2)e^(-2gt). The z integral contributes at most [2nu||z0||^2/(d a_plus^2)]e^(-(2nu-d)t), bounded by (4nu/x0^2)e^(-2gt).

Also, after division of w(t) by a_plus e^(nu t), the nonleading vector has norm at most

 V e^(-gt), V=1+sqrt(2)||z0||/|x0|.

When U e^(-2gt)<=1/2, Q>=1/2, Q^(-1/2)<=sqrt(2) and |Q^(-1/2)-1|<=sqrt(2)|Q-1|. Consequently

 ||Z(t)-Z_star||<=2sqrt(nu)(V+U)e^(-gt).

For completeness, flow loss decreases from f0=1/2, so ||beta a||<=2. The invariant gives beta^2(beta^2+d)<=4, whence beta^2<=2 and ||Z(t)||^2=2beta^2+d<=4+d<=6nu. Also ||Z_star||^2=2nu. The product map is Lipschitz with bound at most ||Z(t)||+||Z_star||<=4sqrt(nu) along the segment between these points, so

 ||beta(t)a(t)-v||<=8nu(V+U)e^(-gt).

On the chosen event, nu<=nu_bar, U<=U_bar, V<=V_bar, and g>=1/(1+D). The definition of T therefore ensures for every t>=T both the required Q condition and

 ||beta(t)a(t)-v||<=eps/2.

For the Q condition explicitly, e^(-gT)<=eps/[16nu_bar(V_bar+U_bar)], so U e^(-2gT)<=U_bar/[256nu_bar^2(V_bar+U_bar)^2]<1/2. This avoids any implicit large-time qualification.

## Rigorous finite-horizon GD transfer

This is an analytical Euler-error bound; no floating-point computation is used or asserted as a certificate. Let F=-grad f for the reduced pair Z=(beta,a), with f=||beta a-v||^2/2. Set H=T+1. The exact flow has ||Z(t)||<=sqrt(D+4)=R-2 for every t>=0. On the whole pair-norm ball of radius R,

 ||F(Z)||<=(R^2/2+1)R=M,
 ||DF(Z)||op<=6R^2+1=L.

The first bound follows from ||beta a-v||<=R^2/2+1. For the second, expand the Hessian quadratic form

 ||d_beta a+beta d_a||^2+2<beta a-v,d_beta d_a>;

its absolute value is at most (3R^2/2+1)(d_beta^2+||d_a||^2), which is smaller than L times that squared norm. The larger L is deliberately conservative.

For one exact-flow step, integration of F and its Lipschitz bound gives the local defect

 ||Z(t+eta)-Z(t)-eta F(Z(t))||<=eta^2 L M/2.

Let E_k=||Z_k^GD-Z(k eta)||. Provided the current GD point is in the radius-R ball, the segment to the flow point is also in it and

 E_(k+1)<=(1+eta L)E_k+eta^2 L M/2.

With E_0=0 this yields

 E_k<=(eta M/2)[(1+eta L)^k-1]
     <=(eta M/2)e^(L H)<=eps/(8R)

whenever k eta<=H. This also closes the ball condition inductively: the exact flow is within R-2 and eps/(8R)<1, so every proposed GD point stays within R-1. No boundedness of the computed GD sequence is assumed without proof.

Since eta<=1, N eta lies in [T,T+1]=[T,H]. The product map (beta,a)->beta a has derivative norm at most R on the radius-R ball, so

 ||beta_N a_N-beta(N eta)a(N eta)||<=R E_N<=eps/8.

Combining the flow error eps/2 and this transfer error gives a GD residual at most 5eps/8<eps. Reintroducing the unit output vector u preserves Frobenius residual norms and proves the statement.

## Limits

The step is constant during this finite run, chosen from deterministic parameters s,p,rho,eps rather than the sampled initializer. It may scale exponentially poorly with T and is not offered as a practical algorithmic rate. Choosing a different eta for a smaller eps is permitted in this theorem; claiming convergence at one fixed eta for all eps would require another argument. The high-probability event is essential and C013 still permits a rare escape event outside it. No expectation statement follows.

The entire rank-one flow component is known from the cited primary paper. The Euler argument is a standard method applied explicitly here, not an assertion of specialist-level novelty. The proper input-side bottleneck at ranks greater than one and arbitrary scales, efficient step/rate dependence, and Target 2 excess risk remain open in this work. [Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.01701, '\bf Chung-type laws of the iterated logarithm for $m$-fold weighted integrated fractional '] We have that 
\begin{align}
 \lim_{T\to \infty}  \Bigg\{ & \sup_{1\le t\le T}\bigg|  \frac{J_{m,\bm\alpha}(I_{\gamma}B_H)(t)}{t^{H+\gamma+m-\alpha_1-\cdots-\alpha_m}}\bigg|-\sigma_{B,m,\bm \alpha,\gamma}\sqrt{2\log\log T}\Bigg\}=0\;\; a.s. 
  \end{align} 
for all $m\ge 0$,   $\gamma\ge 0$ and  $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_i<H+\gamma+i$, $i=1,\ldots,m$; and
\begin{align}
  
 \lim_{T\to \infty}  \Bigg\{ & \sup_{1\le t\le T}\bigg|  \frac{J_{m,\bm\alpha}(W_{\lambda})(t)}{t^{\lambda+m-\alpha_1-\cdots-\alpha_m}}\bigg|-\sigma_{W,m,\bm \alpha,\lambda}\sqrt{2\log\log T}\Bigg\}=0\;\; a.s.
\end{align}
for all $m\ge 0$,   $\lambda> 0$ and  $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_i<\lambda+i$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, where
$$\sigma_{B,m,\bm \alpha,\gamma}^2= \Var\left\{J_{m,\bm\alpha}(I_{\gamma}B_H)(1)\right\}, $$
$$\sigma_{W,m,\bm \alpha,\lambda}^2= \Var\left\{J_{m,\bm\alpha}(W_{\lambda})(1)\right\} $$
and
$$\sigma_{B,0, 0,\gamma}^2=\frac{1}{\Gamma^2(\gamma)}\int_0^1\int_0^1x^{2H+1}[(1-x)(1-xy)]^{\gamma-1}\left[1+y^{2H}-(1-y)^{2H}\right]dxdy,$$
$$\sigma_{W,0, 0,\lambda}^2= \Var\left\{ W_{\lambda}(1) \right\}=\frac{1}{2\lambda \Gamma^2\big(\lambda+1/2\big)}.$$

\iffalse

body: For 0 < eps < 1 and any integer n, let k be a positive integer with k > 8 log(n)/eps^2 (any k = O(eps^{-2} log n) with a suitable absolute constant suffices). Then for any n points x_1,...,x_n in a Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension there is a linear map f into R^k, obtainable with high probability from a random projection, such that for every pair i, j: (1-eps) ||x_i - x_j||^2 <= ||f(x_i) - f(x_j)||^2 <= (1+eps) ||x_i - x_j||^2. So any n points embed into O(log n / eps^2) dimensions while nearly preserving all pairwise distances. Due to William Johnson and Joram Lindenstrauss.
title: Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma

body: In mathematics, the Cantor function is an example of a function that is continuous, but not absolutely continuous. It is a notorious counterexample in analysis, because it challenges naive intuitions about continuity, derivative, and measure. Although it is continuous everywhere, and has zero derivative almost everywhere, its value still goes from 0 to 1 as its argument goes from 0 to 1. Thus, while the function seems like a constant one that cannot grow, it does indeed monotonically grow.
title: Cantor function

body:
[Theorem symmetricmaintheorem of arXiv:2507.05417, 'Invertibility for non-Hermitian and symmetric random band matrices with sublinear bandwidt'] Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and let $d_n\leq n$ be a sequence of integers such that $d_n\geq n^\alpha$ when $n$ is sufficiently large. 
    
    
    Let $S_n=(s_{ij})_{1\leq i,j\leq n}$ be a family of square \textbf{symmetric} random matrices such that $s_{ij}=s_{ji}$ and $(s_{ij})_{1\leq i\leq j\leq n}$ are mutually independent random variables. We assume that 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item When $|i-j|\leq d_n$ or $|n-i+j|\leq d_n$, then for each $1\leq i\leq j\leq n$ we can write $s_{ij}=u_{ij}+c_{ij}$ where $\{u_{ij}\}_{i\leq j}$ are i.i.d. and uniformly distributed on $\{-1,1\}$, and $c_{ij}$ are arbitrary integer-valued random variables that are independent of $u_{ij}$.
        \item All the other random variables $s_{ij}$ where $\min(|i-j|,|n-i+j|)>d_n$   are either identically zero or are arbitrary integer-valued random variables.\end{enumerate}
    Then whenever $\alpha>\frac{2}{3}$, we have 
    $$
\mathbb{P}(S_n\text{ is singular})\leq \exp(-Cn^{\alpha/2}),
    $$ for some universal constant $C>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem symmetricmaintheorem of arXiv:2507.05417

Own-work draft: C22 v1, proof (unaudited), route-failure, Target3; no novelty or full-target claim. Fix d>=2, unit u, X uniform on the radius-sqrt(d) sphere, Z=X.u, and continuous target q(Z) with q(sqrt(d))>0. Use the aligned exponential model f=integral a exp(b+gamma Z) dmu, w=sqrt(d) gamma u, with all a,b,w trained at original Euclidean learning rate. Initialize a=b=0 and an essentially unbounded positive scale tail: mu(gamma_0>R)>0 for every finite R. There is no common positive interval of finite absolutely continuous aligned characteristics satisfying the actual field almost everywhere, with a defined L-infinity predictor satisfying norm(f_t)_infinity to 0 at initialization. For scales above a fixed threshold, positivity of q near the pole and a hypothetical small predictor imply positive exponential lower bounds for both characteristic forces. The invariant b=a^2/2 then gives d/dt integral_0^a exp(-s^2/2) ds >= A exp(z2 gamma_0), although this transform is bounded by 3 for a>=0. The unbounded tail contradicts every common interval. A scale density proportional to exp(-gamma^4) has every finite quadratic exponential moment and a positive lower density on every compact interval, yet satisfies this obstruction. Pure degree-1 and normalized zonal harmonic targets are included because only positivity near the pole is needed. This does not exclude L2-continuous flows with narrow pole layers, other weak or non-aligned evolutions, or the bounded-scale prepared flows C5/C11, and it is not a ReLU counterexample. body:
[Coro cor:cdfbounding of arXiv:2605.07920, 'Primitive Sequences for Probability Measures on Compact Intervals'] Suppose that $c_1, \ldots, c_m$ are the first $m \geq 1$ terms of an admissible sequence for $[a,b]$. Then for every $x_0 \in [a,b]$,
    \begin{equation*}
    \bar{F}_m(x_0; c_{1:m}) := \sup_{\mu \in \pazocal{F}_m(c_{1:m})} \mu([a,x_0]) 
    \quad \text{and} \quad 
    \underline{F}_m(x_0; c_{1:m}) := \inf_{\mu \in \pazocal{F}_m(c_{1:m})} \mu([a,x_0))
\end{equation*}
are attained by $(m+1)$-atomic measures. Equivalently, if $X$ is any random variable on $[a,b]$ with given moments $\mathbb{E}[X^k]$ for $k=1,\ldots,m$, then sharp bounds on $F_X(x_0) = \mathbb{P}(X \leq x_0)$ and on $F_X(x_0-) = \mathbb{P}(X < x_0)$ are attained by discrete random variables supported on at most $m+1$ points.

[Prop 10 (Composition of pseudo-differential operators) of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] \cite[Théorème 10.13]{Alazard2023}
Let $m,n \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \in S^m$ and $b\in S^n$. Then there exists $a\#b \in S^{m+n}$ satisfying
\[
    \Op(a) \circ \Op(b)=\Op(a\#b). 
\]
Moreover, $a\#b$ admits the following asymptotic expansion: 
\[
    a\#b (x,\xi) \sim \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^d} \frac{1}{i^{|\alpha|}\alpha !}\partial_{\xi}^\alpha a(x,\xi) \partial_x^{\alpha}b(x,\xi),
\]
that is for all $N\geq 1$, the symbol $a\# b - \displaystyle \sum_{|\alpha|<N}\frac{1}{i^{|\alpha|}\alpha !}\partial_{\xi}^\alpha a(x,\xi) \partial_x^{\alpha}b(x,\xi)$ belongs to $S^{m+n-N}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Composition of pseudo-differential operators

A distribution function F belongs to the maximum domain of attraction of the Fréchet distribution \Phi_\alpha (denoted F \in \text{MDA}(\Phi_\alpha)) if and only if the upper endpoint x_F = \sup\{x : F(x) < 1\} = \infty and the survival function 1 - F(x) is regularly varying at infinity with index -\alpha: \lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1 - F(t x)}{1 - F(t)} = x^{-\alpha} for all x > 0. The normalizing constants can be chosen as b_n = 0 and a_n = F^{-1}(1 - 1/n).
F is a CDF
\alpha > 0

body:
[Proposition 44 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Let $\varepsilon>0$, $\delta\ge0$, $q\in C([-L,L])$ with $q\ge q_0>0$, and $a\in C([-L,L])$. Consider
\[
\cT_{\varepsilon,\delta}u
=q(x)u'(x)+\varepsilon\int_{-L}^{L}u(y)\,dy-\delta u(x)+a(x)u(x).
\]
Its principal eigenvalue $\lambda_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ is the unique real number satisfying
\[
1=\varepsilon\int_{-L}^{L}\int_x^L\frac1{q(t)}
\exp\left(\int_x^t\frac{a(r)+\lambda_{\varepsilon,\delta}-\delta}{q(r)}\,dr\right)dt\,dx.
\]
Up to multiplication by a positive constant, the corresponding eigenfunction is
\[
\phi_{\varepsilon,\delta}(x)
=\int_x^L\frac1{q(t)}
\exp\left(\int_x^t\frac{a(r)+\lambda_{\varepsilon,\delta}-\delta}{q(r)}\,dr\right)dt.
\]
Put
\[
T_q=\int_{-L}^{L}\frac{dx}{q(x)},\qquad
A_q=\int_{-L}^{L}\frac{a(x)}{q(x)}\,dx.
\]
Then, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$,
\[
\lambda_{\varepsilon,\delta}
=\delta+\frac1{T_q}\left[
\log\frac1\varepsilon+2\log\log\frac1\varepsilon
-2\log T_q-\log q(-L)-A_q
\right]+o(1).
\]
The remainder is independent of $\delta$; in particular it is uniform when $\delta$ ranges in arbitrary subsets of $[0,\infty)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 44 of arXiv:2609.02416

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): Let $A=\{\pm1\}\times A'$ span $\mathbb R\oplus V'$ and suppose $g(s,x)=as+g'(x)$ is sign-valued on $A$. For every $x\in A'$ both $a+g'(x)$ and $-a+g'(x)$ lie in $\{\pm1\}$; therefore either $a=0$ and $g'$ is sign-valued on $A'$, or $|a|=1$ and $g'$ vanishes on the spanning set $A'$, so $g=\pm s$. Hence the projective full dual of a free product is exactly the disjoint union of the free coordinate and the full dual of the reduced factor. Notes: Consequence: deleting or reinserting free coordinates creates NO hidden full-dual form. This is what justifies every occurrence of 'after zero Gale columns are deleted' in the finite reduction -- a hypothesis-preservation lemma, not just a counting one.

[Proposition prop:dc-clean-normalized-trace-defect-direct of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Under the hypotheses of
Proposition~(prop:dc-clean-dressed-waves of the paper), assume additionally
that $\dim E<\infty$, that $H$ is a real separable Hilbert space
with $K(u)\in\mathfrak S_1(H)$, that $K$ is $C^1$ in $\partial_1$
and $C^2$ in $\partial_2$ in trace norm, and that
$C_2(u)\in\operatorname{GL}(E)$ for every $u\in\mathcal V$.  Define
$F(u)\vcentcolon= \det_H(I-zK(u))$ and
$\mathcal B(u)\vcentcolon= \Delta_2(u)C_2(u)^{-1}$.
Then
\begin{align}
\frac{
\left(D_1-\frac{1}{2}D_2^2\right)
F(S_3u)\cdot F(u)
}{
F(S_3u)F(u)
}
&=
\frac{1}{2}
\left[
\operatorname{tr}_E\bigl(\mathcal B(u)^2\bigr)
-
\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_E\mathcal B(u)\bigr)^2
\right]
\notag \\
&\quad
+\operatorname{tr}_E
\left[
\mathcal B(u)
\left(
C_1(u)+\Lambda_2(u)C_2(u)^{-1}
\right)
\right].

\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 26 (One-step \(p\)-moment drift for RLMC) of arXiv:2605.24937, '2605.24937'] Fix \(p\ge 2\). Under Assumption~\hyperref[ass:D]{\textup{(A4)}}, there exist constants
\(q>0\) and \(C_p>0\), depending only on \(p\), \(d\), \(a\), \(b\), and \(\beta\), such that for all
\(\lambda\in(0,1]\),
\[
  \E\|Y'_{n+1}\|^p
  \le
  e^{-q\lambda}\,\E\|\widetilde Y_n\|^p
  +
  C_p\lambda,
\]
where
\[
  Y'_{n+1}\sim P_\lambda(\widetilde Y_n,\cdot),
  \qquad
  \widetilde Y_n=(1-\eta_n)Y_n' + \eta_n\bar Y_n,
  \qquad

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The following integral converges, for any real number $s>0$,
$$\Gamma(s)=\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}e^{-x}\,dx$$
satisfies $\Gamma(s+1)=s\Gamma(s)$, and extends the usual factorial, $\Gamma(n)=(n-1)!$ for $n\in\mathbb N$.

body:
[Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] The weights of a neural network are a tuple of the form
  \[
    \CalW = \bigl( (A_1, b_1), \dots, (A_L, b_L)\bigr)
  \]
  of matrices $A_\ell \in \R^{N_\ell \times N_{\ell-1}}$ and bias vectors $b_\ell \in \R^{N_\ell}$,
  where $N_\ell \in \N$ specifies the width of the $\ell$-th layer of the network.
  We define the \emph{input- and output dimensions} of $\CalW$ as
  $d_{\mathrm{in}}(\CalW) := N_0$ and $d_{\mathrm{out}}(\CalW) := N_L$.

  The associated \emph{neural network function} using the ReLU activation function
  $\varrho : \R \to \R$, $\varrho(x) = \max \{ 0, x \}$ is given by
  \[
    R_\varrho (\CalW) : \quad \R^{d_{\mathrm{in}}(\CalW)} \to \R^{d_{\mathrm{out}} (\CalW)},
    \quad
    R_\varrho (\CalW)
    := T_L \circ (\varrho \circ T_{L-1}) \circ \cdots \circ (\varrho \circ T_1)
    ,
  \]
  where $T_\ell \, x = A_\ell \, x + b_\ell$, and where $\varrho$ acts componentwise on vectors,
  i.e.,
  \[
    \varrho \bigl( (x_1,\dots,x_m)\bigr)
    = \bigl(\varrho(x_1), \dots, \varrho(x_m)\bigr)
    .
  \]
  In this paper, we measure the ``complexity'' of
  $\CalW$ in terms of the \emph{number of non-zero weights}
  \[
      \norm{\CalW}_{\ell^0}
    := \sum_{j=1}^{L} \bigl(\| A_j \|_{\ell^0} + \| b_j \|_{\ell^0}\bigr)
    ,
  \]
  in terms of the \emph{network depth} $L(\CalW) := L$,
  and in terms of the \emph{weight magnitude}
  \[
      \| \CalW \|_{\ell^{\infty}}
    := \max_{1 \leq j \leq L} \bigl(\| A_j \|_{\ell^\infty} + \| b_j \|_{\ell^\infty}\bigr)
    .
  \]
  Here, for a matrix (or vector) $A$, the quantity $\| A \|_{\ell^0}$
  counts the total number of non-zero entries of $A$,
  and $\| A \|_{\ell^\infty} := \max_{i,j} |A_{i,j}|$.

  Now, given $d,g \in \N$, we define for $n \in \N$ the set of ReLU networks $\R^d \to \R$
  with at most $n$ non-zero weights, weight magnitude "of moderate growth",
  and number of layers growing at most poly-logarithmically with $n$ as
  \[
    \CalNN_n (g, \R^d)
    := \Bigl\{
         R_\varrho (\CalW)
         \,\,:\,\,
         \begin{array}{l}
           \CalW \text{ neural network weights with }
           d_{\mathrm{in}}(\CalW) = d,
           d_{\mathrm{out}}(\CalW) = 1, \\
           \norm{\CalW}_{\ell^0} \leq n, \,\,
           \norm{\CalW}_{\ell^{\infty}} \leq g \cdot n^{g},
           \text{ and }
           L(\CalW) \leq (\ln(e n))^g
         \end{array}
       \Bigr\}
    .
  \]
title: Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.30549

[Theorem thm:shocks_coal of arXiv:2605.26048, 'Classification of the eternal solutions and multiple coalescing shocks in the KPZ fixed po'] For almost-every $\omega$, the following holds for all $b \in \mathcal{B}_\omega$. 
\begin{enumerate} [label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont] 
    \item  For each $\xi \in \pmb{\xi}^b$, the set $\mathfrak{C}^b(\xi)$ is connected and unbounded. Specifically, we may write
    \begin{equation} 
    \mathfrak{C}^b(\xi)=\bigcup_{s<t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)} (\mathfrak{a}^s_\xi,\mathfrak{b}^s_{\xi}]\times \{s\},
    \end{equation}
    for numbers $\mathfrak{a}^s_\xi \in [-\infty,\infty)$ and $\mathfrak{b}_s^\xi \in (-\infty,\infty]$ with $\mathfrak{a}^s_\xi<\mathfrak{b}^s_{\xi}$ for all $s < t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, and $t_{\text{ext}}(\xi) \in (-\infty,\infty]$ is called the \textbf{extinction time} for the color $\xi \in \pmb{\xi}^b$. If $\mathfrak{a}_\xi^{s'} > -\infty$ for some $\xi \in \pmb{\xi}^b$ and $s' <t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, then $\mathfrak{a}_\xi^s > -\infty$ for all $s <t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, and the function $s \mapsto \mathfrak{a}_\xi^s$ is continuous. Similarly, if $\mathfrak{b}_\xi^{s'} < \infty$, for some $s' <t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, then $\mathfrak{b}_\xi^s < \infty$ for all $s <t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, and $s \mapsto \mathfrak{b}_\xi^s$ is continuous. 
    

    
     \item  For $\xi \in \pmb{\xi}^b$, $t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)<\infty$  if and only if $\mathfrak{a}_\xi^s > -\infty$ and $\mathfrak{b}_\xi^s < \infty$ for some $s \in \mathbb{R}$. That is, a color survives forward in time if and only if it is not bounded between two other colors. If this is the case, the following limits exist and are equal:
    \begin{equation} 
    x_{\text{ext}}(\xi) :=\lim_{s\uparrow t_{\text{ext}}}\mathfrak{a}_\xi^s=\lim_{s\uparrow t_{\text{ext}}}\mathfrak{b}_\xi^s
    \end{equation}
    We call $p(\xi) :=  (x_{\text{ext}}(\xi),t_{\text{ext}}(\xi))$ the \textbf{extinction point} of the color $\xi$. 
  
    \item  No two colors share the same extinction point. From every extinction point, there exists three disjoint semi-infinite geodesics \rm{(}i.e., they are distinct except at the initial point\rm{)}. Furthermore, the set of extinction points is locally finite. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 8 (One-sheet graphical convergence) of arXiv:2609.03916, 'Halfspace Theorems for Anisotropic Minimal Surfaces and Perimeter Minimizers'] Let $E_j$ be $\Phi$-perimeter minimizers in $B_2$, suppose that $T_{E_j}$ is
absolutely $\Phi$-mass minimizing in $B_2$, and assume
$0\in\supp|D\chi_{E_j}|$.  Let $H$ be a halfspace with measure-theoretic outer
unit normal $\nu_H$, let $0\in P:=\partial H$, and suppose that
\begin{equation}
 \chi_{E_j}\to\chi_H
 \quad\text{in }L^1(B_2),
 \qquad
 D\chi_{E_j}\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}D\chi_H,
 \qquad
 |D\chi_{E_j}|\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}|D\chi_H|.
\end{equation}
Then there exists $\theta_*=\theta_*(n,\lambda)>0$ such that, for all
sufficiently large $j$, there is a function
$u_j:P\cap B_{\theta_*}\to\R$ of class $C^2$ for which
\begin{equation}
 \supp|D\chi_{E_j}|\cap\mathcal C_{\theta_*}(\nu_H)
 =\{y+u_j(y)\nu_H:y\in P\cap B_{\theta_*}\}.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \|u_j\|_{C^1(P\cap B_{\theta_*})}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sup_{\supp|D\chi_{E_j}|\cap
       \mathcal C_{\theta_*}(\nu_H)}
 |\nu_{E_j}-\nu_H|\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Thus the whole support in the smaller cylinder is one sheet, not merely one

[Lemma lem: IIfor a for space_v_estimate of arXiv:2512.12902, 'Non-equilibrium fluctuations for the \\stirring process with births and deaths'] Let  $K\geq 2$ be a fixed  integer number, $0\leq t^*<t\leq T$ and $\zeta>0$. Under Assumption 1 given in (equation Ass1 of the paper)  the following integral inequality for $a_{\epsilon}(n,t)$ holds: for $n\geq 1$ 
\begin{eqnarray}
a_{\epsilon}(n,t)&\lesssim&a_{\epsilon}(n,t^*)\nonumber\\

&&+\mathbf 1_{n\geq 2}\int_{t^*}^t d\lambda\;\frac{\epsilon^{-1}}{[\epsilon^{-2}\lambda]^{1-\zeta}}\sum_{q=1}^{K}\;\;\;
\sum_{p=2}^{\min\{n,K\}}\,
a_{\epsilon}(n-p+q,t-\lambda)\nonumber\\
&&+\mathbf 1_{n\geq 2}\int_{t^*}^t d\lambda\;\frac{\epsilon^{-1}}{[\epsilon^{-2}\lambda]^{1-\zeta}}
\sum_{p=2}^{\min\{n,K\}}\mathbf 1_{p\neq n}\,
a_{\epsilon}(n-p,t-\lambda)\nonumber\\
&&+\int_{t^*}^t d\lambda \;\frac{\epsilon^{-1}}{[\epsilon^{-2}\lambda]^{1/2}+1}a_{\epsilon}(n,t-\lambda)\nonumber\\
 &&+\int_{t^*}^t d\lambda \;\frac{\epsilon^{-1}}{[\epsilon^{-2}\lambda]^{1/2}+1}\sum_{q=2}^K
 a_\epsilon(n-1+q,t-\lambda)\nonumber\\
 &&+\mathbf{1}_{n=2}\epsilon^{1-2\zeta}(t-t^*)^{\zeta}+\mathbf{1}_{3\leq n\leq K} \epsilon\nonumber\\
&&+\mathbf 1_{n= 3}\epsilon\left((t-t^*)^{1/2}+(t-t^*)^{1/2+\zeta}\right) +\mathbf 1_{n\geq 4}\epsilon^{2-4\zeta}(t-t^*)^{\zeta}\nonumber\\
&&+{\bf 1}_{n\geq 2}\int_{t^*}^td\lambda\phi_0(\lambda)\beta_\epsilon(n-1,t-\lambda,{t^*})\nonumber\\
&&+  \mathbf{1}_{n\geq2}\int_{t^*}^t d\lambda\,
\phi_2^\epsilon(\lambda)a_\epsilon(n-2,t-\lambda)\,.
\end{eqnarray}

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We say that a random variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ is exponential, with parameter $\lambda>0$, if its law is as follows:
$$\mu(x)=\lambda e^{-\lambda x}\chi_{[0,\infty]}(x)dx$$
That is, the density of $f$ must be $\varphi(x)=\lambda e^{-\lambda x}$, over the positive numbers.

[Lem corr of arXiv:2606.21049, '\textsc{Locality of rough path lifts}'] Let $H\in (0,\frac12]$.
	There exists a constant $C_H$ depending only on $H$ such that for $\tau > 0$ with $0 \leq s<s + \tau <t <t+\tau\leq 1$ it holds that
	\[
	\rho([s, s+\tau], [t, t+ \tau]) \leq 1 \wedge C_H\bigg(\frac{\tau}{t-(s + \tau)}\bigg)^{2 - 2H}.
	\]

[Lemma leminv of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] {\bf [Invariance property for the connection probability]}

For every $\delta \in (0,\infty)$ and $\eta \in [0,\infty)$, the choice 
\[
g^{\neq}_\delta(x,y) = \delta xy, \qquad g^{=}_\eta(x) = \eta x,
 \]
is invariant under addition of the weights in the aggregation. In other words, the renormalised graph has the same connection functions as the original graph, provided the weight of an aggregated vertex equals the sum of the weights of the constituent vertices, i.e., the aggregated vertex $I^{(1)}$ has weight $\bar{X}_{I^{(1)}} = \sum_{i \in I^{(1)}} X_i$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma leminv of arXiv:2607.12459

Let mesh-delta_j square-lattice Dobrushin domains (Omega_j,a_j,b_j) converge in the Caratheodory sense to a simply connected marked domain (Omega,a,b), with delta_j tending to zero. In the critical FK-Ising random-cluster model q=2 and p=sqrt(2)/(1+sqrt(2)), let F_j be Smirnov's parafermionic observable of spin sigma=1/2. Then delta_j^(-1/2) F_j converges uniformly on compact subsets away from the boundary to (Phi')^(1/2), where Phi maps Omega conformally to a horizontal strip of width 2 and sends a,b to its ends. This theorem has q=2 and an observable conclusion; it does not directly establish the independent square-bond q=1 target.

The Schwartz space $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ is the set of $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ such that $p_{\alpha,\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|<\infty$ for all multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$. With the countable family of seminorms $p_{\alpha,\beta}$ it is a Frechet space. It contains $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ and the Gaussians $e^{-\pi a|x|^2}$ ($a>0$); it is contained in $L^p(\mathbb R^d)$ for every $1\le p\le\infty$, is dense in $L^p$ for $1\le p<\infty$, and is closed under multiplication by polynomials, differentiation, products and convolution. Its continuous dual $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^d)$ is the space of tempered distributions; the Fourier transform extends to $\mathcal S'$ by $\langle\hat T,\varphi\rangle=\langle T,\hat\varphi\rangle$, which is consistent with the integral definition on $L^1$ and with Plancherel on $L^2$. Note $C_c^\infty$ is not closed under the Fourier transform (a nonzero compactly supported function has a transform that is not compactly supported), while $\mathcal S$ is.

			\Upsilon_F[(\downarrow^k)^*\tau] = \partial^k \Upsilon_F[\tau].

[Corollary 16 of arXiv:2604.13149, 'The Distributional Tail of Worst--Case Quickselect'] Assume that \(L_0:\R\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and let
\[
L_{n+1}\defeq \mathcal K L_n,
\qquad n\ge 0.
\]

\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(L_0\) is nondecreasing, then every \(L_n\) is nondecreasing.

\item If \(L_0\le F\) on \(\R\), then
\[
L_n\le F
\qquad\text{on }\R
\]
for every \(n\ge 0\).

\item If \(L_0\le L_1\) on \(\R\), then
\[
L_n\le L_{n+1}
\qquad\text{on }\R
\]
for every \(n\ge 0\).
\end{enumerate}

Method: A zero-one law for Poisson-coloring frontier dimension structural attempt Result: The dimension event is not visibly a tail event of the independent arriving points. This is a logical control, not a Poisson-coloring counterexample. Obstruction: Independent arrivals do not make recursively inherited colors independent across subregions. A regeneration or local-universality statement strong enough to remove early-history effects is missing.

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2609.03821, 'Condensation and Metastability in the Supercritical Two-Species Zero-Range Process via Res'] Suppose that $\alpha>1$. For any $x\in S_{\star}$,
the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Local metastability) Each set $\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}$ is metastable,
in the sense that from any configuration in $\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}$,
it reaches $\bm{\xi}^{x}_{N}$ (cf. \eqref{eq:xiNx}) before exiting
$\tilde{\mathcal{E}}^{x}_{N}$ with high probability:
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\bm{\eta}\in\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}}\mathbb{P}^{N}_{\bm{\eta}}\left[H_{\bm{\xi}^{x}_{N}}<H_{\Omega_{N}\setminus\tilde{\mathcal{E}}^{x}_{N}}\right]=1.
\]
\item (Dynamical transitions) The law of the accelerated order process $\{X_{N}(\theta_{N}t)\}_{t\ge0}$
starting from any configuration in $\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}$ converges
weakly, in the Skorokhod topology as $N\to\infty$, to the law of
the limiting Markov chain $\mathbb{X}$ starting from $x$.
\item (Negligibility) The time spent outside $\mathcal{E}_{N}$ is negligible:
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{\bm{\eta}\in\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}}\mathbb{E}^{N}_{\bm{\eta}}\left[\int^{T}_{0}{\bf 1}\left\{ \bm{\eta}_{N}(\theta_{N}u)\in\Delta_{N}\right\} {\rm d}u\right]=0\qquad\text{for all}\quad T>0.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma L_Fs of arXiv:2605.15066, 'The critical activation density in graph bootstrap percolation'] Let $A$ be a graph. 
For each edge $e$ in $A$, put $W_e=F_e=e$. 
Recall that, for all other edges $e$ in 
$\langle A\rangle_H\setminus A$, the WGA 
identifies a copy $H_e$ of $H$ completed by $e$ and  
an inclusion-minimal 
subgraph 
\[
W_e=\bigcup_{f\in E(H_e\setminus e)}W_f\subset A
\]
for which $(e,W_e)\in{\mathcal A}(H)$. 
Then, for each such $e$, 
there is some  $e\subset F_e\subseteq W_e\cup e$, for which

v(F_e)-2\leqslant\sum_{f\in E(H_e\setminus e)} v(F_f).

[Lemma lem:sec5-finite-probe of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] For $0\leq\lambda\leq1$, let $S_{\lambda,\times}$ be the output of Algorithm~(alg:time-catcher of the paper) applied in $V$ to the independent normalized random walks with endpoint pairs $(x_i,y_i)$.  Then
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(S_{\lambda,\times})
 =\mathbf p_{\lambda,\times}:=(T_\lambda^V)^{-1}\mathbf h_\times.
\]
Note that for each fixed $\lambda$, the construction in
Algorithm~(alg:time-catcher of the paper) couples these sets so that
$S_{1,\times}\subset S_{\lambda,\times}\subset S_{0,\times}$.
Here $S_{0,\times}$ is the union of $r$ independent normalized random-walk
bridges from $x_i$ to $y_i$, while $S_{1,\times}$ is the entangled multipath
LERW.  Every component of $S_{\lambda,\times}$ contains a path joining one
labelled endpoint pair.  Thus it has at most $r$ components, and it is
connected if all pairs share one endpoint. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite interior probe

[Definition 7 (Bernoulli paths and Bernoulli path ensembles) of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] Given $p=(x_p,y_p),q=(x_q,y_q)\in \mathbb T_N+(0,1/(2N))$ such that $x_p<x_q$ and $0 \le y_q-y_p \le x_q-x_p$, we call \emph{Bernoulli path} with endpoints $p,q$ any path $S$ that starts at $p$, ends at $q$ and 
 such that 
 each step of $S$  is either $(1/N,0)$  or $(1/N,1/N)$ (that is, steps are either in the SE or in the  NE direction).
 
    Given $n\in \mathbb N$ and distinct points
    $p_1,\dots,p_n,q_1,\dots,q_n$  of $\mathbb T_N+(0,1/(2N))$ such that all the $p_i$ have
    the same $x-$coordinate  $x_p$ (and the $q_i$ also have all the same $x$-coordinate $x_q>x_p$) and ordered so that the $y-$coordinate of $p_i$ is larger than that of  $p_j$ (resp. the $y$-coordinate of $q_i$
    is larger than that of $q_j$) for $i>j$, we let the \emph{Bernoulli path ensemble} with endpoints
    $p_1,\dots,p_n,q_1,\dots,q_n$ denote the uniform measure on
    $n-$ples     $(S_1,\dots,S_n)$ of non-intersecting (i.e., disjoint) Bernoulli paths, where $S_i$ has endpoints $(p_i,q_i)$. (We assume
    that the points $p_i,q_i,i\le n$ are such that the configuration
    space is nonempty).
title: Bernoulli paths and Bernoulli path ensembles

Independent derivation pending w440 review. Replace every edge of the infinite 3-regular tree with L edges, for a positive integer L, and root at an original vertex. The result T_L is quasi-transitive of maximum degree 3 and has p_c=2^(-1/L)<1. Full subdivided edges are independent coarse bonds of retention p^L, so critical clusters are almost surely finite. For 1<=n<=L the critical probability of reaching graph distance n is 1-(1-2^(-n/L))^3, hence 7/8 at n=L. At radii kL, with u_0=1 and u_(k+1)=u_k-u_k^2/4, the probability is 1-(1-u_(k-1)/2)^3. Reciprocal increments tend to 1/4, so (kL) times this probability tends to 6L. Critical susceptibility is infinite because every original-vertex shell has expected connected count 3/2.

body: [Definition 8 of arXiv:2608.18688, 'Regularity Preservation for Jump-Type Stochastic Transport Equations with Singular Drift'] A local random field is a family of real-valued random variable $X_t(x)$, indexed by $x\in\mR^d$ and $t\in  [0,\tau(x))$,  where $\tau(x)=\tau(x,\omega)$ is an accessible, lower semicontinuous stopping time. Specifically, if the random field $\tau(x)$ satisfies $\tau(x)=+\infty$ for all $x\in \mR^d$ almost surely, then $X_t(x)$ is called a global random field or simply a random field. The random field $\tau(x)$ is commonly referred  to as the terminal time of $X_t(x)$.

[Corollary cor:ergodic theorem for T, continuous of arXiv:2411.03512, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of Sublinear Expectation System and Applications'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{H},(U_t)_{t\geq 0},\hat{\mathbb{E}})$ be a regular continuous sublinear expectation system, where $U_t$ is the linear operator induced by a semigroup of measurable transformations $\theta_t:\Omega\to\Omega$. If $(U_t)_{t\geq 0}$ satisfies that $\overline{X}\in\mathcal{H}$, for any $X\in \mathcal{H}$. Then the following two statements are equivalent:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item $\hat{\mathbb{E}}$ is ergodic;
			\item there exists an ergodic probability $P$ on $\sigma(\mathcal{H})$ such that for any  $X\in \mathcal{H}$,  
			\[\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^TX\circ \theta_tdt=\int XdP, \text{ }\hat{\mathbb{E}}\text{-q.s.}\]
		\end{enumerate}
		In this case,  $P$ is the unique  ergodic probability with respect to $\theta_t, \ t\geq 0$ in $\mathcal{P}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:IPS:relative-entropy:derivative of arXiv:2605.16904, 'Positive-rate PCA and IPS with stationary Bernoulli measures are rapidly forgetful \footno'] Let $\Phi$ be an IPS with a strictly positive local transition rule $\varphi\colon\Sigma^N\times\Sigma\to(0,1)$.
	
	Suppose that $\Phi$ admits a stationary Bernoulli measure $\lambda=\lambda_q$.
	Let $\mu$ be a probability measure and $J\Subset\mathbb{Z}^d$.
	Let $\mu^t\coloneqq\mu\Phi^t$ and $D_J(t)\coloneqq D_J(\mu^t\relto\lambda)$.
	Then,
	\begin{equation}
		\dot{D}_J(t) \leq
			-\kappa D_{J}(t) + (1-\kappa)\abs{N}\log(\sfrac{1}{q_\mathsf{min}})\cdot\abs{\partial^- N(J)} \;,
	\end{equation}
	
	for every $t>0$,
	where
	$\kappa \coloneqq \min\big\{\varphi(a_N,b)/q(b): a_N\in\Sigma^N,b\in\Sigma\big\}$ and
	$q_\mathsf{min}\coloneqq\min\{q(a): a\in\Sigma\}$.
title: Local entropy diffusion with decay

\begin{align}
\mathbb{E} N_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}}) & = |\mathbb{T}_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}|  \cdot  \mathbb{E} N_{T}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}}),   \\
{\rm Var}(N_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}})) & 
=  |\mathbb{T}_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}|^{2}  \cdot  {\rm Var}(N_{T}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}})) - |\mathbb{T}_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}| \cdot (|\mathbb{T}_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}|-1) \cdot  \mathbb{E} N_{T}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}})

.
\end{align}

body:
[Proposition prop:softlocal of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Let $J$ be an at most countable index set and let $(Z_j)_{j\in J}$ be independent random points
of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with densities $g_j$. Let $(\xi_j)_{j\in J}$ be i.i.d.\ exponential random variables
of mean $1$ and define the soft local time
\[
  H_J(y)=\sum_{j\in J}\xi_j\,g_j(y),\qquad y\in\mathbb{R}^d .
\]
Let $\rho\colon\mathbb{R}^d\to[0,\infty)$ be measurable and deterministic. Then there is a coupling
$\mathbb Q$ of $(Z_j)_{j\in J}$ with a Poisson point process $\psi$ of intensity $\rho$
such that for every measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\mathbb Q\big(\{Z_j\}_{j\in J}\cap A\subseteq\psi\big)\ \ge\
  \mathbb Q\big(H_J(y)\le\rho(y)\ \text{ for all }y\in A\big)$;
\item $\mathbb Q\big(\psi\cap A\subseteq\{Z_j\}_{j\in J}\big)\ \ge\
  \mathbb Q\big(H_J(y)\ge\rho(y)\ \text{ for all }y\in A\big)$.

body:
Let Lambda be a compact hyperbolic set for a diffeomorphism f of a manifold. Then for every eps > 0 there is delta > 0 such that every delta-pseudo-orbit in a neighbourhood of Lambda - a sequence (x_n) with d(f(x_n), x_{n+1}) < delta for all n - is eps-SHADOWED by a genuine orbit: there is a point y with d(f^n(y), x_n) < eps for every n. If Lambda is in addition LOCALLY MAXIMAL (isolated) the shadowing point may be taken in Lambda, and if the pseudo-orbit is periodic the shadowing orbit may be taken periodic. Expansiveness of the hyperbolic set makes the shadowing point unique.
Hyperbolicity of the compact invariant set, and delta chosen AFTER eps.
Placing the shadowing orbit inside Lambda requires local maximality - without it the shadowing orbit exists but may leave the set.
Uniqueness uses expansiveness.

Let p and q be probability mass functions on a finite set S with d_TV(p, q) > 0, A = {p > q} and B = {q > p}. For a maximal coupling pi let G_pi be the bipartite graph on A and B with an edge x - y when pi(x, y) > 0. Then pi is an extreme point of the set of maximal couplings if and only if G_pi is a forest. Hence every extreme maximal coupling has at most |A| + |B| - 1 <= |S| - 1 positive off-diagonal entries. The greedy construction, which repeatedly sends the smaller of the remaining row and column masses between the first unfinished points of A and B, produces such a coupling, and if p and q are rational so is every mass it produces.

Fix L>=1,d>=1,k>=1 and nonzero x in R^d, independently of n. Consider the zero-bias fully connected Gaussian MLP with L hidden layers of width n, output width k, weight variance reciprocal to input width in every layer, and squared activation sigma(t)=t^2. Set K_1=||x||^2/d and K_(ell+1)=3K_ell^2. Given all L hidden layers, each final preactivation output has conditional variance Sigma=(1/n) sum_j (z_j^(L)(x))^4. For a finite constant C depending on the fixed model but not n, Var(Sigma)<=C/n and |E Sigma-K|<=C/n. Here K=K_(L+1)>0. Conditional on the hidden layers the k output coordinates are iid N(0,Sigma). This is a restricted specialization of Favaro, Hanin, Marinucci, Nourdin and Peccati, not a new theorem; constants have no asserted uniform dependence on L.
L,d,k,x are fixed as n grows; L>=1; x!=0
Independent Gaussian weights, variance reciprocal input width; zero biases

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2609.02779, '2609.02779'] For the Hamiltonian \eqref{eq:twowell-H}, the critical value is $0$, and
\[
 \widetilde{\A}(H_a)
 =\left\{(0,-a),\left(\frac12,-a\right)\right\}.
\]
The two points are distinct static classes and are hyperbolic equilibria.
Moreover, with
\begin{equation}
\Delta:=\frac a2-A=\frac{B-A}{4}>0,
\end{equation}
the selected critical solution satisfies
\begin{equation}
u_0(0)=0,\qquad
u_0\left(\frac12\right)=-\Delta,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
u_0(x)=\int_0^x\bigl(Q(s)-a\bigr)\,\dd s,
\qquad
u_0'(x)+a=Q(x),
\qquad 0\le x\le\frac12.
\end{equation}

[Definition 9 ($\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-orthonormal system of translates) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Let $\mathcal{A}=\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathbb{H}=L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$
endowed with the $\mathcal A$-valued inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle_{\mathcal{A}}=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(x)\,g(x)^\top\,dx$.
A family $\{U_k\}_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}\subset\mathbb H$ is called
\emph{$\mathcal A$-orthonormal (of unit vectors)} if
\[\langle U_k,U_u\rangle_{\mathcal A}=\delta_{k,u}\,I_m,
\qquad k,u\in\mathbb Z^d.
\]
If $U\in\mathbb H$ and $\{U(\cdot-k)\}_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}$ is $\mathcal A$-orthonormal,
we call $U$ an \emph{$\mathcal A$-orthonormal vector-valued function}.
title: $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-orthonormal system of translates

For each N let theta_N be a unit vector in R^N, Y_t iid with law P_N, and L_N(x;Y) a loss on the unit sphere S^(N-1). Let its population loss be Phi_N(x)=E L_N(x;Y)=phi(m_N(x)), where m_N(x)=x.theta_N and the same function phi:[-1,1]->R is used for every N. The spherical stochastic gradients exist almost surely; assume explicitly that E grad_S L_N(x;Y)=grad_S Phi_N(x). Let H_N(x;Y)=L_N(x;Y)-Phi_N(x). For constants C_1,iota>0 independent of N, assume sup_x E[(grad_S H_N(x;Y).theta_N)^2]<=C_1 and sup_x E||grad_S H_N(x;Y)||^(4+iota)<=C_1 N^((4+iota)/2). For a fixed integer k>=1, suppose phi is C^(k+1) on [-1,1], phi_prime(m)<0 for 0<m<1, phi^(ell)(0)=0 for 1<=ell<k, phi^(k)(0)<0, and sup_[-1,1]|phi^(k+1)|<infinity. Starting independently of the samples, use online spherical SGD X_tilde_t=X_(t-1)-(delta_N/N) grad_S L_N(X_(t-1);Y_t), X_t=X_tilde_t/||X_tilde_t||. Here alpha_N>0 and delta_N>0, and there are M_N=alpha_N*N fresh-sample updates (M_N integer). The initial law mu_N is uniform on the hemisphere {x in S^(N-1):x.theta_N>=0}. Assume alpha_N grows at most polynomially in N. If alpha_N->infinity for k=1, alpha_N/(log N)^2->infinity for k=2, or alpha_N/[N^(k-2)*(log N)^2]->infinity for k>=3, then there exists a positive step-size sequence delta_N for which m_N(X_(M_N))->1 in probability and in L^p for every finite p>=1. The sequence can be chosen so alpha_N^(-1)<<delta_N<<alpha_N^(-1/2), with alpha_N*delta_N dominating the search scale: 1 for k=1, log N for k=2, and N^((k-2)/2)*log N for k>=3. Here u_N<<v_N means u_N/v_N->0. This card states recovery for a suitably chosen step sequence; its conclusion is not a guarantee for every sequence in the displayed broad window. The number of samples equals the number of online updates, not the number of passes over one reused empirical sample.

[Theorem convergence in Ehat of arXiv:2411.04631, 'Existence of Martingale Solutions to Stochastic Constrained Heat Equation'] For $s,t \in [0,T]$ with $s \leq t$ and $\phi \in \mathcal{H}$, the following are true:
\begin{align*}
&1. \;\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \left \langle v_{n}(t), Q_{n}(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}}=\left \langle v(t) , \phi \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}},\; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s. \,. \\
&2.\; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \int_{s}^{t} \left  \langle A v_{n}(h), Q_{n}(\phi)  \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh=\int_{s}^{t} \left  \langle A v(h),\phi  \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}},\; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s.\, .\\
&3.\; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle  F(v_{n}(h)) , Q_{n}(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh = \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle F(v(h)), Q(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh, \; \; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s.\; \text{ for }\phi \in \mathcal{H}.  \\
&4.\; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle  k_{j}(v_{n}(h)) , Q_{n}(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh = \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle k_{j}(v(h)), Q(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh,\; \; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s.\, . \\
&5.\; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle  \Lambda_{j}(v_{n}(h)) , Q_{n}(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dW_{j}(h) = \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle \Lambda_{j}(v(h)), \phi \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dW_{j}(h) ,\; \; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s.\, .
\end{align*}

[Cor jointedge of arXiv:2412.00610, 'Joint Poisson Convergence of Monochromatic Hyperedges in Multiplex Hypergraphs'] Fix $d\geq 1$ and a finite collection of non-isomorphic graphs $F_1, F_2, \ldots, F_d$. Suppose $G_n = ( V(G_n), E(G_n))$ is a sequence of graphs with edges colored uniformly at random with $c_n$ colors such that the following holds: For all $1 \leq i \leq d$, there exists a constant $\lambda_i \geq  0$ such that 
    $$\lim_{n \to \infty}\bE R(F_i, G_n) = \lim_{n \to \infty}\Var R(F_i, G_n) = \lambda_i. $$ 
      Then, as $n \rightarrow \infty$, 
    $$\left(\begin{array}{c}
        R(F_1, G_n) \\
       	\vdots \\ 
	R(F_d, G_n) 
        \end{array}\right) \dto \left(\begin{array}{c}
            Z_1 \\ 
            \vdots \\ 
            Z_d
            \end{array}\right) , $$
      where $Z_1 \sim \Pois(\lambda_1), \ldots, Z_d \sim \Pois(\lambda_d)$ are independent. \hfill $\Box$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor jointedge of arXiv:2412.00610

$$\Diff^+({S^n}) \simeq \SO(n+1) \times \Diff^+_{ \partial S^{n-1}}(D^n),$$
which implies that
    \begin{equation}
    \pi_i\Diff^+({S^n}) \cong \pi_i\Diff_{S^{n-1}}^+{(D^{n})} \times \pi_i\SO(n+1)
\end{equation}
for $i \ge 0$.

[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Let $G=G(n,\tau)$ be the power-law random graph with exponent $\tau>2$, and let
$
\mathrm{diam}(G):=\max_{u,v\in V} d_G(u,v)
$
denote the graph diameter, where $d_G(u,v)$ is the graph distance between $u$ and $v$. Then there exists constants $C>0$ such that
\[
\mathbb P\big(\mathrm{diam}(G)\le C\log n\big)\to 1\qquad\text{as}\quad n\to\infty.
\]

[Lemma lem:ehr-factor of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Let $X_t^{(j)}\in\{a,b\}$ be the urn of ball $j$. The processes
$X_t^{(1)},\dots,X_t^{(n)}$ are independent two-state chains, each jumping $a\to b$
and $b\to a$ at rate $1$, and $k_t=\#\{j:X_t^{(j)}=a\}$.
Starting with all $n$ balls in $a$,

\begin{equation}
\pi_t(k)=\binom nk\,p(t)^{k}\bigl(1-p(t)\bigr)^{n-k},\qquad
p(t)=\frac{1+e^{-2t}}2,

\end{equation}

where $p(t)$ is the probability that one ball started in $a$ is in $a$ at time $t$.
This is the function already obtained in (ex:two-state of the paper).

body:
[Proposition prop: merge increment of arXiv:2509.11384, 'The Horton-Strahler number of butterfly trees'] Let $\mathcal T_1,\mathcal T_2$ be rooted binary trees with $m$ nodes. Then 
    \begin{equation}
        \max(\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_1),\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_2)) \le \operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_1 \oplus \mathcal T_2)\le \max(\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_1),\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_2)) + 1,
    \end{equation}
    and the upper bound is tight if and only if all of the following increment conditions are met:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item \textbf{Max parent}: $\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_1) \ge \operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_2)$.
        \item \textbf{Full profile}: The top right edge of $\mathcal T_1$ has nodes with HS numbers $\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_2),\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_2) + 1, \ldots, \operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_1)$.
        \item \textbf{Escape paths}: For each $t \in \{\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_2),\ldots,\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal T_1)\}$, the top right edge of $\mathcal T_1$ has a node $v$ with value $\operatorname{HS}(v) = t$ that has a child node $w$ located off of top right edge with $\operatorname{HS}(w) = t$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Identical results hold for $\mathcal T_1 \ominus \mathcal T_2$ when replacing the top right edge with the top left edge in the above increment conditions. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Merge increment

[Proposition prop:gamma-quantile-estimates of arXiv:2604.25108, 'Terminal Defects, Growing Multiplicity, and Variance Extremality\\in the Double Dixie Cup '] Let $m_n\ge1$, let $b_n$ be the unique solution of
\[
        Q_{m_n}(b_n)=1/n,
\]
and put
\[
        a_n={\frac{Q_{m_n}(b_n)}{f_{m_n}(b_n)}}={\frac1{h_{m_n}(b_n)}}.
\]
Then, uniformly for $x$ in compact subsets of $\mathbb R$,
\[
        {\frac{Q_{m_n}(b_n+a_nx)}{Q_{m_n}(b_n)}}\to e^{-x}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
        {\frac{Q_{m_n}(b_n+a_nx)}{Q_{m_n}(b_n)}}\le e^{-x}
        \qquad (x\ge0),
\]
there are constants $c>0$ and $R_n\to\infty$ such that
\[
        nQ_{m_n}(b_n-a_nx)\ge c e^{cx},
        \qquad 0\le x\le R_n,
\]
the window may be chosen so slowly that
\[
        R_n\le {\frac{b_n}{2a_n}},
        \qquad
        \left(1+{\frac{b_n}{a_n}}\right)^r\exp\{-c e^{cR_n}\}\to0
\]
for every fixed $r>0$, and
\[
        {\frac{n a_n^2}{b_n}}\to\infty.
\]

body:
Let a multi-output predictor f_t(x) in R^D be a family indexed by t (for instance a blend f_t = (1 - t) f_0 + t f_1 of two fitted bases), scored by a case-weighted squared error L(t) = mean_i w_i ||y_i - f_t(x_i)||^2 with weights w_i that depend on the row only. Then L(t) = sum_d L_d(t) with L_d(t) = mean_i w_i (y_id - f_td(x_i))^2, and likewise the case-weighted bootstrap variance of the predictor at a set of rows, V(t) = mean_i w_i sum_d Var_b f_td^(b)(x_i), equals sum_d V_d(t). Hence the transductive covariance penalty R(t) = CV_cal(t) + [V_ev(t) - V_cal(t)] is a sum of per-output criteria R_d(t), and if the family is allowed a separate index t_d per output, the joint minimiser is the vector of per-output minimisers: min over (t_1..t_D) of sum_d R_d(t_d) = sum_d min_t R_d(t) <= min_t R(t). The per-output choice therefore never increases the criterion. It does not follow that it lowers the risk: each R_d is an estimate whose noise is not reduced by the averaging that makes R usable, and D separate argmins select on that noise. Measured on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (D = 285 and 40 outputs, 70 cells, two calibration/evaluation splits): the per-output blend gives up 0.41 and 0.53 percent of the score against the per-cell blend on EMIT (winning 14 and 12 of 40 cells) and 0.02 and 0.08 on OCO-2, with the identity sum_d R_d = R verified to 4e-16 in the driver's selftest. The information of the criterion is in the sum, not in its summands.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ which follows the exponential law of parameter $\lambda>0$, its central moments are given by the following formula,
$$M_k'=\frac{k!}{\lambda^k}\sum_{s=0}^k\frac{(-1)^s}{s!}$$
with the small order central moments being as follows,
$$M_1'=0\quad,\quad 
M_2'=\frac{1}{\lambda^2}\quad,\quad
M_3'=\frac{2}{\lambda^3}\quad,\quad
M_4'=\frac{9}{\lambda^4}\quad,\quad\ldots$$
and with all this being more complicated than for the usual moments.

body:
[Lem 10 of arXiv:2606.04636, 'A Thomson-type variational principle for diffusion coefficients'] The divergence and gradient are adjoint up to
a sign: $\div=-\grad^{*}$. That is, for local $f:\Omega\to\C$ and
a local admissible flow $\phi$,
\begin{equation}
\left\langle \phi,\grad f\right\rangle =-\left\langle \div\phi,f\right\rangle .
\end{equation}
In particular, $\cL=\div\grad$ is negative self-adjoint.

body:
[Definition def-thin-wedge of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] For $W\in(0, \frac{\gamma^2}{2})$, the probability measure $\mathcal{M}^{\textup{wed}}(W)$ is defined as follows. Sample a Poisson point process $\{(u, \mathcal{D}_u)\}$ from the intensity measure $\mathds{1}_{t>0}dt\times \mathcal{M}_{0,2}^{\textup{disk}}(\gamma^2-W)$ and concatenate the quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u\}$ according to the ordering induced by $u$. The resulting beaded quantum surface is a \emph{weight $W$ quantum wedge}, and we denote its law by $\mathcal{M}^\mathrm{wed}(W)$. For $x>0$, the \emph{quantum cut point measure} assigns  mass
	$x$ to the collection of cut points between the quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u:u\leq x\}$.
title: Definition def-thin-wedge of arXiv:2411.19810

body: Erdos Problem 548, the Erdos-Sos conjecture (1963): every graph on n vertices with more than (k-1)n/2 edges contains, as a subgraph (not necessarily induced), every tree on k+1 vertices. It was proved in August 2026 by a permutation-word counting argument with induction on the target tree (GPT-6 Astra with Tom Adamczewski; verified by Thomas Bloom and accepted as proved by erdosproblems.com, with a complete formal proof in Lean, repository github.com/tadamcz/erdos548). Whether a given formal statement captures the informal conjecture remains a human judgment.

body:
Let $\Sigma$ be a positive definite $M \times M$ covariance matrix. The minimum-variance weights subject to $\mathbf{1}^T w = 1$ are $w^* = \Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1} / (\mathbf{1}^T \Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1})$ with risk $R^* = w^{*T}\Sigma w^* = 1/(\mathbf{1}^T \Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1})$. Let $S$ be the sample covariance of $n > M + 1$ i.i.d. Gaussian observations with covariance $\Sigma$ and let $\hat w = S^{-1}\mathbf{1}/(\mathbf{1}^T S^{-1}\mathbf{1})$ be the plug-in weights. THEOREM (Pafka and Kondor, 2003; the finite-$n$ moments are those of the inverse Wishart law). In the limit $M, n \to \infty$ with $q = M/n \in (0, 1)$: (i) the true (out-of-sample) risk of the plug-in portfolio satisfies $\hat w^T \Sigma \hat w / R^* \to \frac{1}{1 - q}$; (ii) the in-sample risk $\hat w^T S \hat w / R^* \to 1 - q$; so the realized risk exceeds the optimum by the factor $1/(1-q)$ while the naive in-sample estimate understates the optimum by the factor $1 - q$, the two differing by $1/(1-q)^2$. For $q = 0.025$ the inflation is $2.6$ percent; for $q = 0.5$ it is $100$ percent; as $q \to 1$ the plug-in portfolio's risk diverges.
Sigma positive definite; n > M + 3 for the finite-sample moments
i.i.d. Gaussian observations

In-sample risk: $\\hat w^T S \\hat w = 1/(\\mathbf{1}^T S^{-1} \\mathbf{1}) = 1/(n\\, a^T W^{-1} a)$. The inverse-Wishart moments give $E[W^{-1}] = I/(n - M - 1)$, so $E[a^T W^{-1} a] = \\|a\\|^2/(n - M - 1)$ and, with $R^* = 1/\\|a\\|^2$, the ratio of in-sample risk to $R^*$ concentrates at $(n - M - 1)/n \\to 1 - q$ (concentration of the quadratic form $a^T W^{-1} a$ around its mean follows from the variance formula for inverse-Wishart quadratic forms, which is $O(1/n)$ relative). Out-of-sample risk: $\\hat w^T \\Sigma \\hat w = a^T W^{-2} a / (a^T W^{-1} a)^2 \\cdot 1$ in the reduced coordinates; the second inverse-Wishart moment is $E[W^{-2}] = \\frac{(n-1)}{(n-M)(n-M-1)(n-M-3)} I$ (up to the standard constants), and the ratio $E[a^T W^{-2} a]/E[a^T W^{-1}a]^2 \\cdot \\|a\\|^2$ tends to $\\frac{1}{1 - q}$ as $M, n \\to \\infty$ with $M/n \\to q$; concentration again reduces the ratio of expectations to the limit of the ratio. Equivalently, in random-matrix language, $\\frac{1}{M}\\operatorname{tr}(W/n)^{-1} \\to \\frac{1}{1-q}$ and $\\frac{1}{M}\\operatorname{tr}(W/n)^{-2} \\to \\frac{1}{(1-q)^3}$ are the first two negative moments of the Marchenko-Pastur law with ratio $q$, and the two risk ratios are these moments combined as $m_{-2}/m_{-1}^2 = 1/(1-q)$ and $1/m_{-1} = 1 - q$.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a5eaf09e1e64bc865e796df6fd29ee98b931f1136985d0f46bc2e14868ce768e","revision_digest":"sha256:a453bab6cdb57297886d2f46c3cf9c2a4103d60d6717b3495d848c2573b78ab5","source_id":"wikipedia:Modern portfolio theory (minimum-variance portfolio) + arXiv:cond-mat/0205119 (Pafka, Kondor 2003, 'Noisy covariance matrices and portfolio optimization II')","source_revision":"as-read-2026-09-05","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
A Hermitian matrix A in C^{n x n} is positive definite if and only if it can be written as A = L L^* with L lower triangular having strictly positive real diagonal entries; when it exists this factorisation is unique. For real symmetric positive definite A the factor L is real, A = L L^T. Equivalently A = R^* R with R = L^* upper triangular. The factor is computed by the Cholesky algorithm in n^3 / 3 flops (half the cost of LU, no pivoting needed): for j = 1..n, l_jj = sqrt(a_jj - sum_{k<j} |l_jk|^2) and l_ij = (a_ij - sum_{k<j} l_ik conj(l_jk)) / l_jj for i > j; the algorithm is backward stable (Wilkinson), and it fails - a nonpositive quantity under the square root - exactly when A is not positive definite, which makes it the standard numerical test of positive definiteness. For positive semidefinite A a factorisation A = L L^* with nonnegative diagonal still exists but is no longer unique. Uses: solving A x = b by two triangular solves, sampling Gaussian vectors with covariance A (x = mu + L z), least squares via the normal equations, and the Kalman filter.
A Hermitian (symmetric in the real case)
positive definite for existence with a strictly positive diagonal and for uniqueness

[Lemma lem:2.4 of arXiv:2607.24164, 'The KLS constant is $O(\log^{1/4} n)$'] For every $1\leqslant i,j\leqslant n$, one has
\[
  \mathcal{L}(\partial_{ij}\varphi)+\partial_{ij}\varphi
  =\partial_{ia}\varphi\,V_{ab}\partial_{bj}\varphi
  +\varphi^{ac}\varphi^{bd}\partial_{abi}\varphi\,
    \partial_{cdj}\varphi.
\]
Here $V_{ab}$ is evaluated at $\nabla\varphi$. Moreover, pointwise, the
two matrices
\[
  \left(
    \partial_{ia}\varphi\,V_{ab}\partial_{bj}\varphi
  \right)_{i,j=1}^n
\]
and
\[
  \bigl(
    \varphi^{ac}\varphi^{bd}\partial_{abi}\varphi\,
    \partial_{cdj}\varphi
  \bigr)_{i,j=1}^n
\]
are positive semidefinite.

[Proposition 120 (Optimal Gaussian regression constant in increasing convex order) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $\mathsf R_m$ be the infimum of all $A>0$ such that
\begin{equation}

  \E\,\Phi\!\left(A^{-1}\|\mathcal I_b(W)\|_B\right)
  \le
  \E\,\Phi\!\left(
    \|\mathcal D_b(W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(m)})\|_B
  \right)
\end{equation}
holds for every convex nondecreasing
$\Phi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, every real or complex Banach space $B$,
every finite orthonormal system, and every finite $B$-valued coefficient
array $b$, with the notation of
Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-averaging-decoupling}.  Then
\begin{equation}

  \mathsf R_m=m^{m/2}.
\end{equation}
In particular, $m^{m/2}$ is the least constant valid simultaneously
for all the $L^p$ inequalities, $1\le p<\infty$.  The optimal comparison
constant for a fixed $p$ may be smaller.

body:
[Corollary 26 (Coefficient approximation) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $X$ solve the baseline equation \eqref{eq:X}. For each $n\ge1$, let $X^{(n)}$ be a c\`adl\`ag adapted solution, driven by the same pair $(W,Z)$, such that the pair $(X,X^{(n)})$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:solutions}. Suppose that $X^{(n)}$ solves
\[
X_t^{(n)}=x_0^{(n)}+\int_0^t b_n(X_s^{(n)})\dd s
+\int_0^t a_n(X_s^{(n)})\dd W_s
+\int_0^t \sigma_n(X_{s-}^{(n)})\dd Z_s.
\]
Assume that there exist common constants $L_b,L_a,L_\sigma$ and exponents $\eta_n\in[\wt\eta,1]$, with $\wt\eta\in[1/\alpha,1]$, such that for all $n$ and all $x,y\in\R$,
\[
|b_n(x)-b_n(y)|\le L_b|x-y|,
\qquad
|a_n(x)-a_n(y)|\le L_a|x-y|,
\]
and
\[
|\sigma_n(x)-\sigma_n(y)|\le L_\sigma\bigl(|x-y|^{\eta_n}\vee |x-y|\bigr).
\]
Then the family satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:perturbed} uniformly with exponent $\wt\eta$. Define
\begin{align*}
B_n&:=\int_0^T\E |b(s,X_s)-b_n(X_s)|\dd s,\\
A_n&:=\left(\int_0^T\E |a(s,X_s)-a_n(X_s)|^2\dd s\right)^{1/2},\\
S_n&:=\left(\int_0^T\E |\sigma(s,X_s)-\sigma_n(X_s)|^\alpha\dd s\right)^{1/\alpha}.
\end{align*}
Suppose that $B_n,A_n,S_n\to0$ and $x_0^{(n)}\to x_0$. Then
\[
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-X_t^{(n)}|^{\alpha-1}\to0.
\]
Moreover, once $B_n,A_n,S_n<1$, the rate is obtained from Theorem~\ref{thm:noncritical} if $\wt\eta>1/\alpha$ and from Theorem~\ref{thm:critical} if $\wt\eta=1/\alpha$.

[Proposition thm|Straightforward of arXiv:2504.08938, 'Fourier Levels and Almost Sure Bounds on Higher-Order Derivatives in First-Passage Percola'] For every $i\neq j$, every $\alpha,\beta\in\{a,b\}$, and every random variable $\varphi$, 
\begin{eqnarray} 
\sigma_i^{\alpha}\circ \sigma_i^{\beta}&=&\sigma_i^{\alpha};   \\
\sigma_i^{\alpha}\circ \sigma_j^{\beta}&=&\sigma_j^{\beta}\circ\sigma_i^{\alpha};   \\
(\partial_i \varphi)\circ \sigma_i^{\alpha} &=& \partial_i \varphi;   \\
\partial_i\partial_i \varphi&=&0;   \\
\partial_i\partial_j \varphi&=&\partial_j\partial_i\varphi;   \\
\varphi\cdot 1_{\omega_i=\alpha}&=&\varphi\circ \sigma_i^{\alpha}\cdot 1_{\omega_i=\alpha}.  
\end{eqnarray} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Let $p(t \to t')$ denote the probability of obtaining $t'$ from $t$ by the above random
leaf-removal procedure, and let
\[
g(t) = \frac{|t|!}{\prod_{v \in V_t} |t_v|}
\]
denote the right-hand side of the hook-length formula.
Then
\[
p(t \to t') = \frac{m_t(t')g(t')}{g(t)}.
\]
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.25877

[Proposition prop:PhiRSovolev of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Fix $q\in(1,2)$ and let $F\in L^1(\mathbb{P}_\eta)$ be a Poisson functional satisfying $F\geq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely. Then
$$
{\mathrm{Ent}}_{\Phi_q}(F) \leq {\mathbb E}\Big[\int_\mathcal{X}\big(D_xF^{2\over q}-{2\over q}F^{{2\over q}-1}\,(D_xF)\big)\,\mu(d x)\Big].
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:PhiRSovolev of arXiv:2507.08692

Multiplying by $t^m(\frac{m}{p})^n$ and summing over $m\geq 1$, we obtain $\sum_{m\ge1}t^m

\end{align*}
A simple residue calculation shows that for every polynomial $H$ of degree at most $n-1$, we have
\[
[s^n]\frac{t(1+s)}{1-t(1+s)}H(s)=\frac{t^n}{(1-t)^{n+1}}H\left(\frac{1-t}{t}\right).
\]

body: For the real eigenvalues of the real Ginibre ensemble, a question left open in the extreme-gaps programme (Lopatto and Meeker 2024, Section 1.3): the smallest gap satisfies P(N^{1/4} g_min > x) -> exp(-kappa x^2) with kappa = 1/(2 sqrt(2 pi)), the slope of the two-point function at 0 (in mean-spacing units a Rayleigh law exp(-pi y^2/2)), and the k-th smallest gaps and the process of squared gaps converge to Poisson limits. The largest gap G_N satisfies theta G_N - (1/2) log N - log(2 theta) - c_b => Gumbel, with theta = zeta(3/2)/(2 sqrt(2 pi)) = 0.5210934894 and c_b = log 2 - 1/4 + (1/(4 pi)) sum_{n>=2} (1/n)(-pi + sum_{m=1}^{n-1} 1/sqrt(m(n-m))) = 0.0625786, the bulk gap constant conjectured by Forrester and proved by FitzGerald, Tribe and Zaboronski; so G_N ~ log N/(2 theta). The proof works from the exact Pfaffian kernel by a cell-mesh Poissonization and a quasi-factorization of Fredholm Pfaffians over separated interval unions, without resolvent bounds or negative association.

[Lemma lem:compo of arXiv:2412.04328, 'The critical Karp--Sipser core of Erdős--Rényi random graphs'] Let $x>0$ and let $(v_n),(s_n)$ be sequences of nonnegative integers such that $v_n \to +\infty$ and $s_n = x v_n^{2/3}+ o (v_n^{2/3})$ as $n \to +\infty$. We also assume that $\log^4 n \leqslant v_n \leqslant n$ and that $s_n \leqslant n$.
	Then we have the following convergences in distribution:
	\begin{align*}
	\frac{\# \{ \mbox{vertices of degree $ 2$ in $\mathbb{G}(0, v_n, s_n)$}\}}{v_n} &\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)} 1,\\
	\frac{\# \{ \mbox{vertices of degree $ 3$ in $\mathbb{G}(0, v_n, s_n)$}\}}{x v_n^{2/3}} &\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)} 1,\\
	\frac{\# \{ \mbox{vertices of degree $ 4$ in $\mathbb{G}(0, v_n, s_n)$}\}}{(3/4) \cdot x^2 v_n^{1/3}} &\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)} 1,\\
	\# \{ \mbox{vertices of degree $ 5$ in $\mathbb{G}(0, v_n, s_n)$}\} &\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)} \mathrm{Poisson}\left( \frac{9 x^3}{20}\right),\\
	\# \{ \mbox{vertices of degree at least $6$ in $\mathbb{G}(0, v_n, s_n)$}\} &\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)} 0.
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Prop teo:refMeasure of arXiv:2412.04918, 'On one dimensional weighted Poincar\'e inequalities for Global Sensitivity Analysis'] Consider two probability measures $\mu, \Tilde{\mu} \in \mathcal{P}(a,b)$ with $(a,b)$ finite. Let $\Tilde{g}$ be the function saturating the classical Poincar\'e inequality for $\Tilde{\mu}$. Then the function $g$ defined by $g (x) = \Tilde{g} (x) - \int_{a}^{b} \Tilde{g}(y) \,\mu(dy)$ belongs to $\mathscr{C}^{1,2}_{*}(a,b)$ and satisfies (equation eq: boundary conditions of the paper). Moreover it generates a non-vanishing weight $w_g\in \mathcal{W}(a,b)$ leading to a weighted Poincar\'e inequality for $\mu$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The probability for a random permutation $\sigma\in S_N$ to have exactly $k$ fixed points is given by the following formula:
$$P=\frac{1}{k!}\left(1-\frac{1}{1!}+\frac{1}{2!}-\ldots+(-1)^{N-1}\frac{1}{(N-1)!}+(-1)^N\frac{1}{N!}\right)$$
Thus we have the estimate $P\simeq1/(ek!)$, in the $N\to\infty$ limit.

body:
[Proposition prop_an of arXiv:2411.13972, 'The Stochastic Bessel operator at high temperatures'] ~\\
Set $T>0$, independent of $\beta$. There exist a deterministic function $\eta(\beta)\rightarrow 0$ and an event $\mathcal{E}_0$, $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_0)\rightarrow 1$, on which, for $\beta$ small enough:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
	\item $\tau_0 < \beta$, 
	\item $\underset{[\tau_0, \tau_c\wedge T]}\sup\big\lvert q^+(t)-r^+(t)\big\rvert <\delta$, 
	\item $\tau_c<T \Rightarrow \lvert\xi^+-\tau_c\rvert<\eta$ and $\lvert\xi_0^+(0)-\tau_c\rvert<\eta$.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent Properties (a), (b) and (c) also hold for the diffusions $q^-$ from (equation SDEq- of the paper) and $r^-$ from (equation eq_r- of the paper), with their corresponding hitting and explosion times. As a consequence, on the event $\mathcal{E}_0$, for $\beta$ small enough,
\begin{equation}
\xi^-<T \Rightarrow \big\lvert \xi^- -\xi_0^-(0)\big\rvert <2\eta.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Limit behavior of the diffusions $q^+$ and $q^-$

[Definition 5 (Solution of a rough differential equation) of arXiv:2506.09637, 'Nonlinear Stochastic Filtering with Volterra Gaussian Noises'] Let $p\geq 1$, $\kappa = \floor p$, $\mathbf I \in \Omega G_{p}([0, T], \mathcal V)$ and $g \in C^\kappa(\mathcal U, \mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal V, \mathcal U))$. We say that $Z  \in \mathscr{D}_{\mathbf I, p}(\mathcal U) $ solves the rough differential equation
    \[
    Z_t = Z_0 + \int_0^t g(Z)_s d\mathbf{I}_s 
    \]
     if for every $t \in [0, T]$
     \begin{align*}
         Z^{(0)}_t &= Z^{(0)}_0 + \int_0^t g(Z)_s d\mathbf{I}_s,\\
         Z^{(k)}_t &= g(Z)^{(k-1)}_t,\qquad k \geq 1.
     \end{align*}

[OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes: Why fair coins are exceptional' (openquestion environment labelled oq:stability).] Fix an alphabet size $s$ and a length $k\ge 2$, and consider i.i.d.\ sources with probabilities $(p_1,\dots,p_s)$.
(Here the \emph{uniform} distribution means $p_i=1/s$ for all $i$.)
For patterns of length $k$, orient the complete directed graph by
$A\to B$ iff $\Pr(A\!>\!B)>\tfrac12$ under \emph{independent} sources and \emph{random tie-break}.
Does there exist $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(k,s)>0$ such that whenever $\max_i |p_i-1/s|<\varepsilon$,
this head-to-head tournament on $\mathcal{A}^k$ has \emph{no directed $3$-cycles} (equivalently, is transitive as a tournament)?
More generally, what is the largest neighbourhood of the uniform distribution on which the length-$k$ head-to-head relation is cycle-free? (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)
title: Open problem: Stability near fairness at fixed length

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2609.01473, 'Keller sequences of exact $\infty$-categories'] Let $i\colon \cal{A} \hookrightarrow \cal{C}$ be an extension-closed exact functor among weakly idempotent complete exact $\infty$-categories.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
If $i$ is right-special then for every $n \geq 0$ and every map $c \to i(A)$ with $c \in \cal{C}$ and $A \in \st(\cal{A})_{[0,n]}$ factors as a composite $c \to i(a) \xrightarrow{i(g)} i(A)$ for some $g\colon a \to A$ with $a \in \cal{A}$ and $\cofib[a \to A] \in \st(\cal{A})_{[1,n]}$.
\item
If $i$ is left-special then for every $m \leq 0$ and every map $i(A) \to c$ with $c \in \cal{C}$ and $A \in \st(\cal{A})_{[m,0]}$ factors as a composite $i(A) \xrightarrow{i(g)} i(a)$ for some $g\colon A \to a$ with $a \in \cal{A}$ and $\fib[A \to a] \in \st(\cal{A})_{[m,-1]}$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $0<\epsilon<\frac{1}{2}$, let $r=n-\l_1$ and suppose that $r+k+1<(\frac12-\epsilon)n$. Then
\begin{multline}
s_\l(k)=\frac{(n-r-1)^{\underline{k}}}{n^{\underline{k}}}\prod_{i=2}^m\left(1-\frac{k}{n-(1+r+\lambda_i-i)}\right)\prod_{i=1}^m\left(1-\frac{k}{n-(r-\lambda_i'+i)}\right)^{-1}\\
+O_\epsilon\left(\exp\left(k\left[\log\frac{(1+\epsilon)(k+1+r)}{n-k}+O_\epsilon\left(r^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right]\right)\right).
\end{multline}
Here, the superscript $\underline{k}$ is the falling factorial. Moreover, when $r<k$, the error term on the second line is actually zero. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defi 38 of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] For $i=0,1$  let $c_i\colon [0,1] \to A$ be of class $C^k$, $k\geq 1$. We say that $c_0$ is \emph{homotopic} to $c_1$, if there exists $C^{k}$ maps $a,b\colon [0,1]\times[0,1]\rightarrow A$ with
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item  $a(0,\cdot )=c_0$ and ${a}(1,\cdot )=c_1$ and ${a}$ is a variation of admissible curves 
 \item $\gamma:=\pi\circ {a}=\pi\circ {b}$ and $\rho\circ {b}(\varepsilon,t)=\dis\frac{\partial \g}{\partial \varepsilon}(\varepsilon, t)$.
 \item $\dis\frac{\p {a}_\varepsilon}{\p \varepsilon}=\mathcal{T}_{a_\varepsilon }(b_\varepsilon)$
 \item For every $\varepsilon \in [0,1]$, $b_\varepsilon(0)=0=b_\varepsilon(1)$
 \end{enumerate}
 The pair $({a},{b})$ is called a ($C^k$-)\emph{homotopy} between $c_0$ and $c_1$.

[Corollary jiaquanG-N of arXiv:2609.01488, 'Stabilization by a background magnetic field: global well-posedness of the full compressib'] Let $w:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ be a nonnegative, nonzero measurable function, and let the constants $s,s_1,s_2,p,p_1,p_2,l$ satisfy $s_2\geq s\geq s_1\geq0$, $1\leq p,p_1,p_2\leq\infty$, $0\leq l\leq1$, and
$$\frac1p-\frac{s}{d}=l\Big(\frac{1}{p_1}-\frac{s_1}{d}\Big)+(1-l)\Big(\frac{1}{p_2}-\frac{s_2}{d}\Big).$$ If $w\in L^{\frac{p}{p-1}},$ then there holds that
$$\|f\|_{W^{s,p}}\leq K_6\|\Lambda^{s_1}f\|^{l}_{L^{p_1}}\|\Lambda^{s_2}f\|^{1-l}_{L^{p_2}}+K_6\big|\int_{\mathbb T^d} wfdx\big|$$
with a positive constant $K_6$ depending only on $\mathbb T^d,s,s_1,s_2,p,p_1,p_2,l,\|w\|_{L^{\frac{p}{p-1}}},\|w\|^{-1}_{L^1}.$
