body: [Theorem 16 of arXiv:2608.18688, 'Regularity Preservation for Jump-Type Stochastic Transport Equations with Singular Drift'] Let $h(x)$ be a function belonging to the $\mH^{l+1,\alpha}$-class on $\mR^d$, where $m\geq l\geq2$, $\alpha>0$. Consider the processes $\bar{\xi}_t(x)$, $\bar{\eta}_t(x)$ and $\bar{\zeta}_t(x)$ defined by  (\ref{char-equ-1}) and let $\varGamma(x)$ be the stopping time defined by (\ref{stopping-time1}). Define $u_t(x)$ as  $u_t(x):=\bar{\eta}_t(\bar{\xi}_t^{-1}(x))$, $t\in [0,\varGamma(x))$. It follows that $u_t(x)$  is a local solution to equation (\ref{SPDE-2}). Furthermore, this solution is a local   $\mH^{l-1,\beta}$-semimartingale for any $\beta<\alpha$.

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $(\Omega,\FF)$. Then:
	\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
		\item $\mu$ is additive: $\mu(A\cup B)=\mu(A)+\mu(B)$ whenever $\{A,B\}\subset \FF$ and $A\cap B=\emptyset$.
		\item $\mu$ is monotone: $\mu(A)\leq \mu(B)$ whenever $\{A,B\}\subset \FF$ and $A\subset B$.
		\item $\mu$ is continuous from below: $\mu(\cup_{n\in \mathbb{N}}A_n)=\uparrow\!\!\text{-}\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A_n)$ whenever $(A_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is a nondecreasing (w.r.t. inclusion) sequence in $\FF$.
		\item $\mu$ is countably subadditive: $\mu(\cup_{n\in \mathbb{N}}A_n)\leq \sum_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mu(A_n)$ whenever $(A_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence in $\FF$.
		\item Suppose $\mu$ is finite. $\mu(\Omega\backslash A)=\mu(\Omega)-\mu(A)$ for all $A\in \FF$. Further, $\mu$ is continuous from above: $\mu(\cap_{n\in \mathbb{N}}A_n)=\downarrow\!\!\text{-}\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A_n)$ whenever $(A_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is a nonincreasing (w.r.t. inclusion) sequence in $\FF$. 
		\item For  $A\in \FF$: put $\FF\vert_A:=\{B\cap A:B\in \FF\}$; then $\mu_A:=\mu\vert_{\FF\vert_A}$ is a measure on $\FF\vert_A$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 4 of arXiv:2604.01685

body:
[Lem 236 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $1\le \fq < \fp$ and $C > 0$, the spaces $\cP_\fp(\R,C)$ and $\cP_\fp(\R_{\ge0},C)$, endowed with the $\bbW_\fq$ metric,
are compact.

\begin{proof}
	We will show compactness of $\cP_\fp(\R,C)$, as compactness of $\cP_\fp(\R_{\ge0},C)$ is proved analogously.
	It suffices to show that every sequence $(\mu_n)_{n\ge 1}$ in $\cP_\fp(\R,C)$ has a subsequence converging in $\bbW_\fq$ to a measure in $\cP_\fp(\R,C)$.
	Consider any such sequence $(\mu_n)_{n\ge 1}$.
	The set of measures $\cP_\fp(\R,C)$ is clearly tight, so by Prohorov's theorem there exists a weakly convergent subsequence $(\mu_{n_j})_{j\ge 1}$. 
Let $\mu$ be its weak limit. By Skorokhod's theorem, we can find a coupling of random variables $X_j\sim\mu_{n_j}$ and $X\sim\mu$ such that
$X_j\to X$ almost surely. Then, by Fatou's lemma, we have
	\[
		\|\mu\|_{L^\fp}^\fp 
	=\E[|X|^p]^{1/p}
		\le
		\liminf_j \E[|X_j|^p]^{1/p}
		= \liminf_{j\to\infty} \|\mu_{n_j}\|_{L^\fp}^\fp
		 \le C\,,
	\]
	so $\mu \in \cP_\fp(\R,C)$. 
	It remains to show $(\mu_{n_j})_{j\ge 1}$ converges to $\mu$ in the $\bbW_\fq$ metric.
	 Note that for any $\nu \in \cP_\fp(\R_{\ge0},C)$, Markov's inequality implies
	\[
	\nu(|x|>K) 
	\le \frac{1}{K^\fp}\int
		|x|^\fp \,d\nu
		 \le \frac{C}{K^\fp}\,.
	\]
Combining this with H\"older's inequality gives
	\beq
		\int_{|x|>K} |x|^\fq \,d\nu
		\le \nu(|x|>K)^{1 - \fq/\fp} \bigg(
			\int |x|^\fp \,d\nu
		\bigg)^{\fq/\fp}
		\le \frac{C}{K^{\fp - \fq}}\,.
	\eeq
	By \eqref{e:confinement.cPp.compact.Wq.tail} and the weak convergence $\mu_{n_j} \rightarrow \mu$,
	\begin{align*}
		\limsup_{j\to\infty} \bigg|
			\int |x|^\fq \,d\mu_{n_j}
			- \int |x|^\fq \,d\mu
		\bigg|
		&\le \limsup_{j\to\infty} \bigg|
			\int
			\max\{|x|,K\}^\fq
			\,d\mu_{n_j}
			- \int
			\max\{|x|,K\}^\fq
			 \,d\mu
		\bigg|\\
		&\qquad + \limsup_{j\to\infty} \int_{|x| > K} |x|^\fq \,d\mu_{n_j}
		+ \int_{|x| > K} |x|^\fq \,d\mu
		\le \frac{2C}{K^{\fp-\fq}}\,.
	\end{align*}
	Since $K$ was arbitrary, we infer the convergence of $\fq$-th moments
	\[
		\lim_{j\to\infty} 
		\E[|X_j|^p]
		=\lim_{j\to\infty} 
		\int |x|^\fq \,d\mu_{n_j}
		= \int |x|^\fq \,d\mu
		= \E[|X|^p]\,.\]
This implies that the random variables $\{X_j\}$ are uniformly integrable, so
	\begin{align*}
	&\bbW_\fq(\mu_{n_j}, \mu)^\fq
	\le \E[|X_j-X|^\fq]\\
	&\le\E\Big[
	\max\{|X_j-X|,2K\}^\fq\Big]
	+\E\Big[|X_j| ; |X_j|\ge K\Big]
	+ \E\Big[|X| ; |X|\ge K\Big]
	\\
	&\le o_j(1) + o_K(1)+ o_K(1)\,.
	\end{align*}
Since the left-hand side does not depend on $K$, we conclude that
$\mu_{n_j} \rightarrow \mu$ in the $\bbW_\fq$ metric.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 236 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Theorem thm:joint_invm_class of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] Let $c \in [0,q^{-1})$. If $m \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\nu$ is an extremal $m$-invariant measure for $\operatorname{GLPP}_c$, then there exist $s_1,\ldots,s_m \in [r_c,q^{-1})$ such that 
     \[
      \nu = \mu_{c,s_1,\ldots,s_m}.
     \]
     Furthermore, for any $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m \in (0,\xi_{\max}^c]$,
\[
\Bigl(W^c_{\xi_1}\bigl((0,0),(k,0)\bigr),\ldots,W^c_{\xi_m}\bigl((0,0),(k,0)\bigr)\Bigr)_{k \in \mathbb{N}} \sim \mu_{c,s_1,\ldots,s_m},
\]
where, for $i \in \llbracket 1,m \rrbracket$,
\[
s_i = \begin{cases}
    (X_c \circ T_c)^{-1}(\xi_i) &\xi_i < \xi_{\max}^c \\
    r_c &\xi_i = \xi_{\max}^c.
\end{cases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:joint_invm_class of arXiv:2605.22787

body:
[Definition def:cp-irred of arXiv:2606.14687, 'Lehner's operator norm formulas, semidefinite programming, and spiked matrix models'] Suppose $\mathcal{L}: \mathbb{C}^{d \times d} \to \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ is completely positive and has the form
    \[
        \mathcal{L}(\bm S) = \sum_{i = 1}^n \bm B_i \bm S \bm B_i^*,
    \]
    sometimes called a \emph{Kraus representation}.
    We say that $\mathcal{L}$ is \emph{irreducible} if there is no nonzero proper subspace $L \subset \mathbb{C}^d$ such that $\bm B_i L \subseteq L$ for every $i \in [n]$.
    We say that $\mathcal{L}$ is \emph{primitive} if there is some $m \geq 1$ such that $\mathcal{L}^m(\bm S) \succ \bm 0$ for every nonzero $\bm S \succeq \bm 0$.
title: Irreducibility and primitivity

body:
[Proposition cond:subcrit of arXiv:2606.01866, 'Phase Transition of a Semiflexible Membrane in Two Dimensions'] \label[proposition]{thm:massiveanalysis}
    For a fixed $M>0$, let $0<m\le M$ be a mass parameter. Suppose $x\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ satisfies $\|x\|\to\infty$. Let $G^m$ be the massive Green function with mass $m$. Then we have the following estimates:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*), ref=(\alph*)]
        \item 
        If $m\|x\|\to\infty$, then there exists $c,C>0$, depending only on $M$, such that
        \[G^m(x,0)\le C (m\|x\|)^{-1/2}e^{-cm\|x\|}.\]
        
        \item 
        If $m\|x\|\to s>0$ with $\|x\|\to\infty$, then for any multiindex $\alpha$ including $\alpha=0$,
        \[|\nabla^\alpha G^m(x,0)|\lesssim \|x\|^{-|\alpha|}.\]
        
        \item 
        If $m\|x\|\to 0$, then 
        \[|G^m(x,0)-G^m(0,0)-\mathfrak{a}(x)|=o(1).\]
        Moreover, the asymptotic (cond:supercrit of the paper) remains valid without the assumption $\|x\|\to\infty$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Uniform estimate for massive Green functions

\]

body:
[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Let $m_1,m_2$ be measures on $\Omega$ with $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcalorig{F}$. The following are also measures on $\Omega$. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $m_1+m_2$ given by pointwise addition (of sets).
\item For $\alpha \geq 0$, $\alpha m_1$ given by $(\alpha m_1)(A) = \alpha m_1(A)$.
\item For $m_1,m_2$ finite and $\forall U \in \mathcalorig{F}$, $m_1(U) \geq m_2(U)$, $m_1 - m_2$ given by pointwise subtraction.
\item For $U \in \mathcalorig{F}$, the restriction of $m_k$ to $U$. That is, $m_k\big|_U(A) := m_k(A \cap U), \forall A \in \mathcalorig{F}$.
\end{enumerate}

$$T=U^*M_fU$$
with $U:H\to L^2(X)$ being a unitary operator from $H$ to a certain $L^2$ space associated to $T$, with $f:X\to\mathbb R$ being a certain function, once again associated to $T$, and with
$$M_f(g)=fg$$

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] \textbf{(Rooted ordered trees, subtrees, forests)}
$(\textbf{a})\, $ A \textit{rooted ordered tree} is a subset $ \fftree\! \subset \! \bbU$ satisfying the following conditions: 
\begin{compactenum}
\item[] \textbf{(1):} $\varnothing \ino \fftree$. \textbf{(2):} If $u\ino  \fftree\backslash \{ \varnothing\}$ 
then $\overleftarrow{u}\ino  \fftree$. \textbf{(3):} For all $u\ino  \fftree$, there exists $k_u ( \fftree)\ino \bbN\cup \! \{ \infty\}$ such that: $u \! \ast \!  (j)\ino  \fftree$  if and only if  $1\! \leq \! j \! \leq \! k_u ( \fftree)$. 
\end{compactenum}
Here, $k_u ( \fftree)$ is interpreted as the \textit{number of children of $u$} and if 
$1\! \leq \! j \! \leq \! k_u ( \fftree)$, then $u\ast (j) $ is the \emph{$j$-th child of $u$.}
We denote by $\bbT$ the set of rooted ordered trees.

\smallskip

\noindent
$(\textbf{b})\, $
Let $ \fftree\ino \bbT$ and $u\ino t$. Then 
$\theta_u  \fftree\!  = \! \{ v\ino \bbU: u\ast v\ino  \fftree \}$ is the \emph{subtree of $ \fftree$ stemming from $u$}. 
Note that $\theta_u t\ino \bbT$. 

\smallskip

\noindent
$(\textbf{c})\, $ A \emph{fores}t is a sequence of trees 
$(t^{_{(k)}}_{^{\,}} )_{k\in \bbN^*}$. It is sometimes convenient to view it as a single tree $t\ino \bbT$ with $k_\varnothing(t)\eqo\infty$ such that 
$t^{_{(k)}}_{^{\,}}$ is the subtree stemming from the $k$-th child of $t$: $t^{_{(k)}}_{^{\,}}\eqo \theta_{(k)}t$. \cq

body:
Let U subset R^n be open, bounded, with Lipschitz boundary, n>=1, and H^1(U)=W^{1,2}(U). Then: (i) if n=1, H^1(U) embeds continuously into C^{0,1/2}(closure(U)); (ii) if n=2, H^1(U) embeds continuously into L^q(U) for every finite q in [1,infinity), but not into L^infinity(U) or C^0(closure(U)) in general; (iii) if n>=3, H^1(U) embeds continuously into L^{2*}(U), 2*=2n/(n-2), i.e. there is C=C(n,U) with ||u||_{L^{2*}(U)} <= C||u||_{H^1(U)} for all u in H^1(U). In every dimension the embedding of H^1(U) into L^q(U) is compact for every q strictly below the borderline exponent (q<2* for n>=3, any finite q for n<=2), by the Rellich-Kondrachov theorem.
U is open, bounded, with Lipschitz boundary
n = dimension >= 1

Let G = (X, Y, E) be a finite bipartite graph and, for S a subset of X, let N(S) be the set of vertices of Y adjacent to some vertex of S. There is a matching saturating every vertex of X if and only if |N(S)| >= |S| for every subset S of X. Equivalently, a finite family of finite sets (A_1, ..., A_m) has a system of distinct representatives (distinct a_i with a_i in A_i) if and only if every k of the sets have a union with at least k elements.

body:
Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. For 0 <= t <= n let H_t be the average of Var(E[f | X_T]) over the t-element sets T. Then H_t = sum_{k=1}^t [binom(t, k)/binom(n, k)] W_k, so H_0 = 0, H_n = Var(f) and H_t is nondecreasing in t; and for 1 <= k <= n, W_k = binom(n, k) sum_{t=0}^k (-1)^(k - t) binom(k, t) H_t = binom(n, k) Delta^k H_0 >= 0. The n + 1 averages determine the variance at every interaction order, though not the individual w_S.

[Theorem thm:massive_limit of arXiv:2605.15545, 'Crossover from subcritical to critical decay: \\ random walk, self-avoiding walk, percolat'] Let $d \ge 1$. Suppose $D(x)$ has finite support $\mathcal{U}$.
Let $x \in {\mathbb R^d}$ be on the boundary of $\mathrm{Conv}(\mathcal{U})$.
Then as $z \to 0$, we have
\begin{equation}
\abs x_{z} = \mathrm{rad}(\mathcal{U}) + O(m_z^{-1}) .
\end{equation}
In particular, $\lim_{z\to 0} | \cdot |_z$ defines a norm on ${\mathbb R^d}$, with its unit ball being $\mathrm{Conv}(\mathcal{U}) / \mathrm{rad}(\mathcal{U})$.
title: Theorem thm:massive_limit of arXiv:2605.15545

[Corollary 33 (Fixed reset probability) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Assume $\rho_n\equiv\rho\in(0,1)$ and put $q=1-\rho$.  Then
\[
        s_n
        \sim
        \sqrt{2\pi\rho n}\left(q\rho^{\rho/q}\right)^n.
\]
Consequently
\[
        \rho\sqrt{2\pi\rho n}\left(q\rho^{\rho/q}\right)^nT_n
        \Rightarrow \Exp(1),
\]
and for every fixed integer $r\ge1$,
\[
        \Ebb\left[\rho\sqrt{2\pi\rho n}\left(q\rho^{\rho/q}\right)^nT_n\right]^r
        \longrightarrow r!.
\]
In particular,
\[
        \Ebb T_n
        \sim
        \frac{1}{\rho\sqrt{2\pi\rho n}}
        \left(q\rho^{\rho/q}\right)^{-n}.
\]

body:
[Theorem thmFi of arXiv:2411.05534, 'Inverse problems for stochastic partial differential equations'] Let $\phi \in C^1((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n)$, $b^{jk}=b^{kj}\in
C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $j,k=1,2,\cdots,n$, 
and $\ell,\Psi \in C^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n)$. 
Let $u$ be an $H^2(G)$-valued, $\mathbf{F}$-adapted process such that $u_t$ is an $L^2(G)$-valued It\^o process. 
Set $\theta = e^\ell$ and $w=\theta u$. 
Then, for a.e.     $x\in G$ and ${\mathbb{P}}$-a.s. $\omega \in \Omega$,

\begin{align}
    \notag
      
    &   \theta \Big ( -2\phi\ell_t w_t + 2\sum_{j,k=1}^n b^{jk}\ell_{x_j} w_{x_k} + \Psi w \Big )
    \Big[ \phi du_t - \sum_{j,k=1}^n (b^{jk}u_{x_j})_{x_k} dt \Big]  
    \\ \notag
    & \quad+\sum_{j,k=1}^n \Big[ \sum_{j',k'=1}^n \Big (
    2b^{jk}b^{j'k'}\ell_{x_{j'}}w_{x_j}w_{x_{k'}} -
    b^{jk}b^{j'k'}\ell_{x_j} w_{x_{j'}}w_{x_{k'}}
    \Big )   
    \\ \notag
    &\quad  - 2 \phi b^{jk}\ell_t w_{x_j} w_t + \phi b^{jk}\ell_{x_j} w_t^2  +
    \Psi b^{jk}w_{x_j} w - \Big({\cal A}\ell_{x_j} +
    \frac{\Psi_{x_j}}{2}\Big)b^{jk}w^2 \Big]_{x_k} dt
    \\ \notag
    &\quad +d\Big\{ \phi\sum_{j,k=1}^n b^{jk}\ell_t w_{x_j} w_{x_k}-
    2\phi\sum_{j,k=1}^n b^{jk}\ell_{x_j}w_{x_k}w_t  + \phi^2\ell_t w_t^2
    - \phi\Psi w_t w 
    \\ \notag 
    & \quad \quad \quad 
    + \Big[ \phi {\cal A}\ell_t +
    \frac{1}{2}(\phi\Psi)_t\Big]w^2 \Big\}   
    \\ \notag
    &   =  \bigg\{ \Big[(\phi^2\ell_{t})_t + \sum_{j,k =1}^n (\phi
    b^{jk}\ell_{x_j})_{x_k} - \phi\Psi \Big]w_t^2   d t
    \\ \notag
    & \quad - 2\sum_{j,k=1}^n \big[(\phi
    b^{jk}\ell_{x_k})_t +
    b^{jk}(\phi\ell_{t})_{x_k}\big]w_{x_j}w_t   d t   
    +\sum_{j,k=1}^n c^{jk}w_{x_j}w_{x_k} d t + Bw^2 d t
    \\
    & \quad 
    + \Big(   -2\phi\ell_tv_t 
    + 2\sum_{j,k=1}^n b^{jk}\ell_{x_j}w_{x_k} + \Psi w
    \Big)^2\bigg\} dt + \phi^2\theta^2 \ell_t(du_t)^2,  
\end{align}

where 
\begin{align} \notag
    & {\cal A}\mathop{\buildrel\Delta\over=}\phi (\ell_t^2-\ell_{tt})-\sum_{j,k=1}^n
    (b^{jk}\ell_{x_j}\ell_{x_k}-b^{jk}_{x_k}\ell_{x_j}
    -b^{jk}\ell_{x_jx_k})-\Psi,\\ \notag
       & {\cal B}\mathop{\buildrel\Delta\over=}{\cal A}\Psi+(\phi {\cal A}\ell_t)_t\!-\! \sum_{j,k=1}^n\!({\cal A}
    b^{jk}\ell_{x_j})_{x_k}\! +\!\dfrac 12
    \Big[\big(\phi\Psi\big)_{tt}\!-\!\sum_{j,k=1}^n\!
    \big(b^{jk}\Psi_{x_j}\big)_{x_k}\Big],\\  
      & c^{jk}\mathop{\buildrel\Delta\over=} \big(\phi b^{jk}\ell_t\big)_t\! +\!
    \sum_{j',k'=1}^n\! \Big[2b^{jk'}(b^{j'k}\ell_{x_{j'}})_{x_{k'}}
    \!-\!\big(b^{jk}b^{j'k'}\ell_{x_{j'}}\big)_{x_{k'}}\Big] \!+\! \Psi
    b^{jk}.
\end{align}

[Defn 16 of arXiv:2608.28200, '\textbf On the Formality of Configuration Spaces of $\aka$'] A structure on the real field $(\mathbb{R}, +, \cdot, <)$ is a sequence $\mathcal{S} = (S_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, where each $S_n$ is a collection of subsets of $\R^n$,  satisfying the following: 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $S_n$ contains all algebraic subsets, i.e., sets defined by polynomial equalities and inequalities.
    \item $S_n$ is closed under finite union, finite intersection, and complement.
    \item If $A \in S_m$ and $B \in S_n$, then $A \times B \in S_{m+n}$.
    \item If $p:\R^{n+1}\to \R^n$ is a linear projection and $A \in S_{n+1}$, then $p(A)\in S_n$.
\end{enumerate}
The elements of $S_n$ are called  $\mathcal S$-definable subsets of $\R^n$. A map (or function) $f:A\to B$ between $\mathcal S$-definable sets is called definable if its graph is $\mathcal S$-definable.

[Lem 102 of arXiv:2511.20322, 'Dissertation'] Let $T > 0$ and $B, l\in \N$.
Suppose $u : [0,T]\to [0,1] \in \Lip^l$ and $R \in \dC l(\R^d, L^\infty(\cZ,\R))$ with $\nabla R \in \Lip^l(\R^d, L^\infty(\cZ,\R^d))$. Define
\begin{align*}
F(h,t,\thet,z) := &  -\frac{u_t} B\sum_{k=0}^{B-1}\nabla R_{z(k)}(\thet), \quad h\in (0,1),t\in [0,T], \thet \in \R^d, z = (z_0,\dots, z_{B-1})\in \cZ^B,\\
Z_n := & (\bz(0 + Bn),\dots, \bz((B-1) + Bn)), \quad n\in \N,\\
f_t^h(\thet) := & F(h,t,\thet, Z_{\floor{t/h}}), \quad h\in (0,1),t\in [0,T], \thet \in \R^d.
\end{align*}
Then 
\[|F(h,t,\thet,z)| \lesssim 1 + |\thet|,\unfovr h\in (0,1),t\in [0,T],\thet \in \R^d, z\in \cZ^B,\]
and $f_t^h \in \Lip^l(\R^d, L^\infty(\Om, \R^d))$ uniformly in $t\in [0,T]$ and $h\in (0,1)$.
Further, by defining
\[\bar f_t(\thet) := -u_t \nabla \cR(\thet), \quad \Si_t(\thet) := \frac{u_t^2}{B}\E[(\nabla R_{\bz(0)}(\thet) - \nabla \cR(\thet))^{\otimes 2}],\]
for all $\thet\in \R^d$ and $t\in [0,T]$, we have $\bar f\in \Lip^l([0,T]\times \R^d, \R^d), \Si \in \wC l 2([0,T]\times \R^d, \R^{d\times d})$, and
\[\bar f_t(\thet) = \E[f_t^h(\thet)], \quad  \Si_t(\thet) = \Cov f_t^h(\thet),\]
for all $\thet\in \R^d, h \in (0,1)$ and $t\in [0,T]$.

[Theorem 43 (Convergence under a strictly positive density after finitely many steps) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Assume \hyp{A}{A} and \hyp{E}{E}. Then
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\ \sup_{A \in \XXA} \bigl| (T^{n}\circ\mu)(A) - \pi(A) \bigr| = 0
  \qquad\text{for every } \mu \in \Prob,
\]
and $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$. More precisely, the
singular mass is bounded by the mass that has not yet entered the good sets:
\[
  \sing\bigl( T^{n}\circ\mu \bigm| \pi\bigr) \;\le\; 1 - \mu(\XX_{n})
  \qquad (\mu \in \Prob,\ n \in \N) ,
\]
and the right-hand side tends to $0$ for every $\mu \in \Prob$.

Let D be an abelian (v, k, lambda)-difference set in group G. Let p be a prime divisor of k - lambda such that p is coprime to v and p > lambda. Then the map x -> x^p is a multiplier of D: there exists an element g in G such that D^p = {d^p : d in D} = g D.
G is abelian
p divides k - lambda
gcd(p, v) = 1
p > lambda

[Corollary 4 of arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes \\ Why fair coins are exceptional'] Assume the coin (die) is \(s\)-sided and each side occurs with probability \(1/s\). Then
\[
c_T(x)= \frac{1}{1+(1-x) \left(\left(\tfrac{s}{x}\right)^{\ell_1} +  \left(\tfrac{s}{x}\right)^{\ell_2} + \cdots +  \left(\tfrac{s}{x}\right)^{\ell_r}\right)}.
\]
In particular, \(\mathbb{E}[\tau_T]=s^{\ell_1} + s^{\ell_2}+ \cdots + s^{\ell_r}\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 6 ({\cite[Theorem~17.6) of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] {bhattacharya-rao}}] 
Fix $k, n  \in \N$. Let $(X_i)_{i\in \N}$ denote a sequence of  independent random variables taking values in $\R^k$ such that
\[
  \E X_j = 0 \,,\, 1 \leq j \leq n\qquad \text{and} \qquad \sum_{j=1}^n \Cov(X_j) = \mathrm{Id}\,.
\]
Let $Z$ denote a standard Gaussian in $\R^k$. There exist constants $c,C>0$  such that if 
\[

[Definition def:grafting0 of arXiv:2411.07157, 'Rough differential equations in the flow approach'] Given $\ell \in\N$ and a labelled tree $\underline{\sigma}\in\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{T}}$, we define a new labelled tree ${\underline{\sigma}}+\ell \in\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{T}}$ to be the labeled tree with node set ${N}(\underline{\sigma}+\ell) \eqdef \{ j + \ell : j \in N(\underline{\sigma})\}$ and such that the \textit{shift by $\ell$} defined as $ N(\underline{\sigma})\ni j \mapsto j+ \ell \in{N}(\underline{\sigma}+\ell)$ belongs to $\mathrm{Iso}(\underline{\sigma},\underline{\sigma}+\ell)$ -- in particular, we have $ r(\underline{\sigma}+\ell)= r(\underline{\sigma})+\ell$. 
Note that $\underline{\sigma} + 0 = \underline{\sigma}$. 

Finally, given two labelled trees $\underline{\tau},\underline{\sigma}\in\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{T}}$, we set 
\[
\ell_{\underline{\tau},\underline{\sigma}}
\eqdef 
 \begin{cases}  
    \max N(\underline{\tau}) + 1& \text{if} \;N(\underline{\tau}) \cap N(\underline{\sigma}) \not = \emptyset\,, \\
    0 & \text{otherwise} \,. \\
\end{cases}
\]
We overload notation, identifying $\ell_{\underline{\tau},\underline{\sigma}}$ with the shift-isomorphism and write $\ell_{\underline{\tau},\underline{\sigma}} \in \mathrm{Iso}(\underline{\sigma}, \underline{\sigma} + \ell_{\underline{\tau},\underline{\sigma}})$.

Let (X,d) be a metric space, A a nonempty subset, and 0<kappa<=1. Let f:A->R have finite M_inf=sup_(a in A)|f(a)| and finite Holder seminorm L=sup_(a!=b in A)|f(a)-f(b)|/d(a,b)^kappa, with the seminorm set to zero for a singleton. Then there is F:X->R with F|A=f, sup_X|F|=M_inf and [F]_(kappa,X)=L. Consequently the sum norm ||F||_(BL^kappa(X))=||F||_infinity+[F]_(kappa,X) equals ||f||_(BL^kappa(A)). A construction is g_sup(x)=sup_(a in A)(f(a)-L d(x,a)^kappa), followed by clipping to [inf_A f,sup_A f]. Equivalently, clipping g_inf(x)=inf_(a in A)(f(a)+L d(x,a)^kappa) gives such an extension. In particular kappa=1 gives a globally Lipschitz real-valued extension with the same bound. No closedness of A, completeness of X, compactness, or attainment of the extrema is required.
Arbitrary metric space with finite real-valued distances and a nonempty subset A
Real-valued f bounded on A with finite kappa-Holder seminorm
Exponent 0<kappa<=1, as fixed in primary Definition2.1
Classical real supremum and infimum; singleton seminorm convention zero
For preserving the supremum norm, clip the cone extension to the bounded range interval

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The following happen:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The Dirac masses are infinitely divisible.

\item The measures supported by $2\leq n<\infty$ points are not infinitely divisible.

\item In particular, the binomial laws are not infinitely divisible.

\item The negative binomial laws, including the geometric ones, are infinitely divisible.

\item The Poisson laws are infinitely divisible, and so are their compound versions.

\item The uniform laws are not infinitely divisible, while the exponential laws are.
\end{enumerate}

 \\
 \mathfrak H_Q(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})
 &\le\frac{dQa_QR^4}{J},
 \\
 \Delta_{\mathrm{res}}(r^{[J]})
 +\Delta_{\mathrm{mix}}(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})
 &\le\frac{dQ\mu_Qa_QR^4}{J}.
 
\end{align}
At every promotion made before the end of level $J$, the synthesis map
in \eqref{bridge:eq:reduced-promotion} has smallest singular value strictly
larger than
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\delta_J}{dQR}
 =\frac{a_QR^3}{J}.
 
\end{equation}
Thus no Gram mode which vanishes along a fixed level can be promoted after
renormalization.

Own-work draft; independently checked proof; D0010-C002 v1; audits w667:PASS, w668:PASS. On [0,1], f(x)=846x/37 for x<=1/6, (264-738x)/37 for 1/6<=x<=1/3, and 18/37 for x>=1/3 is continuous and unimodal with mean 1/3. It satisfies 3P(X>x)<=ceil(1/x)-1 for every x>0, but violates 2P(X>1-t)<=P(X<t) whenever 0<t<4/47 and is not 3-CM. Thus integer tail tests plus unimodality and boundary mean are insufficient.
As stated in the linked proof

Define f on [0,1] by

    f(x)=846x/37                 for 0<=x<=1/6,
    f(x)=(264-738x)/37           for 1/6<=x<=1/3,
    f(x)=18/37                  for 1/3<=x<=1.

It is continuous: both first formulas give 141/37 at 1/6 and the second gives 18/37 at 1/3. It is strictly increasing up to 1/6, strictly decreasing until 1/3, then constant. Thus it is unimodal, nonnegative, with essential support [0,1].

An easy integration check uses f=H T+c R with H=123/37,c=18/37. The triangle T is 6x on [0,1/6], 2-6x on [1/6,1/3], and zero thereafter. The ramp R is 6x on [0,1/6] and one thereafter. Their masses are 1/6 and 11/12; first moments are 1/36 and 107/216. Thus integral f=123/(37*6)+18*11/(37*12)=1 and integral x f=123/(37*36)+18*107/(37*216)=1/3.

For every x>0 the earlier necessary integer tail bound

    3 P(X>x) <= ceil(1/x)-1

holds (for x>1 both sides are zero). For 0<x<1/3 the right side is at least 3 and the inequality is automatic. At x=1/3, P(X>x)=12/37<2/3. For 1/3<x<1/2, the right side is 2 and the tail is <=12/37<2/3. At x=1/2 the right side is 1 and the tail is 9/37<1/3. For 1/2<x<=1 the right side is 1 for x<1, the tail <=9/37<1/3, and at x=1 both sides are zero.

Nevertheless the law is not 3-CM. For 0<t<=1/6, P(X<t)=423 t^2/37 and P(X>1-t)=18t/37. The endpoint-balance inequality from D0010-C001 would require 423t^2>=36t, which fails for 0<t<4/47. [Proposition 15 of arXiv:2608.27374, '\Large \bf Distribution-constrained optimal multiple stopping: the Root-type solution'] We have $u^\beta(t_0,\cdot)-v^\xi(t_0,\cdot) = 0$. 
For \(i=1,\ldots,n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R\), we have
\begin{equation}

\begin{aligned}
    u^\beta(t_i,y)-v^\xi(t_i,y)
    =
    \min\Bigg\{
        w^\beta(t_i),\,
        &\E^y\!\left[
            u^\beta\!\left(
                t_{i-1},Y_{t_i-t_{i-1}}
            \right)
            -
            v^\xi\!\left(
                t_{i-1},Y_{t_i-t_{i-1}}
            \right)
        \right]\\
        &\quad+
        \P\!\left(
            t_{i-1}<\sigma^\xi\le t_i,\,
            X_{t_i}>y
        \right)
    \Bigg\}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For every \(i=0,\ldots,n\), the map $
    y
    \longmapsto
    u^\beta(t_i,y)-v^\xi(t_i,y)$
is continuous and non-increasing, with
\[
    \lim_{y\to-\infty}
    \bigl[
        u^\beta(t_i,y)-v^\xi(t_i,y)
    \bigr]
    =
    w^\beta(t_i),
    \qquad
    \lim_{y\to+\infty}
    \bigl[
        u^\beta(t_i,y)-v^\xi(t_i,y)
    \bigr]
    =
    0.
\]
Set \(b_0:=+\infty\). For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), let $
    b_i
    :=
    \sup\left\{
        y\in\mathbb R:
        u^\beta(t_i,y)-v^\xi(t_i,y)=w^\beta(t_i)
    \right\}$. Then 
   $\Rc^\beta_t
    =
    (-\infty,b_i]$.

body: [Lemma lem-resample-inside-ns of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] For $(\phi, \eta) \sim M_W$, the conditional law of $\eta$ given $\phi$ is radial $\mathrm{SLE}_{\kappa'}(\rho)$ in $\mathbb{H}$ from $\infty$ to $i$ with force point infinitesimally counterclockwise of $\infty$, where $\rho = \frac4{\gamma^2}W + \frac8{\gamma^2} - 4$.  Furthermore, consider a bounded neighborhood $A\subset \mathbb{H}$ of $i$ such that $\overline A \cap \partial \mathbb{H} = \emptyset$, and let $\alpha = Q - \frac1{2\gamma} (W + 2-\frac{\gamma^2}2)$. Conditioned on $\phi |_{\mathbb{H} \backslash A}$, we have $\phi|_A \stackrel d= h + \mathfrak h + \alpha G_A(\cdot, i)$, where $\mathfrak h$ is the harmonic extension of $\phi|_{\mathbb{H} \backslash A}$ to $A$, $h$ is a zero boundary GFF on $A$ and $G_A$ is the Green function of $h$.

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Salez, Modern aspects of Markov chains: entropy, curvature and the cutoff phenomenon (arXiv:2508.21055), Problem 2.4 (p. 27) asks to prove that cutoff is equivalent to the product condition for random walks on Cayley graphs of abelian groups, presented as a workshop prediction reiterated as [52, Conjecture 1], with no degree bound stated in the printed question. Our result (id P0276, 2026-09-08): the literal statement is FALSE. Take G_d = (Z/2)^d x (Z/m_d) with m_d = 1 + ceil(2^d log d / 4) and S_d = {(e_i, k): i <= d, k nonzero} union {(x, 0): x in the cube, x nonzero} - a simple, connected, undirected, vertex-transitive, unweighted abelian Cayley graph. The cube generators act as a reset Q_d = (2^d Pi_d - I)/(2^d - 1), giving the exact identity q_d(t) = e^{-beta_d t} c_d(alpha_d t) with beta_d chosen so that beta_d T_d tends to 1 (T_d the cube's mixing scale); the distance profile is e^{-s} on 0 < s < 1 and 0 beyond, a continuous decay with NO cutoff, while gap times t_mix is asymptotic to (1/2) log d, which diverges, so the product condition HOLDS. Verification as the source words it: alpha_d tends to 1 and beta_d ~ 4/(d log d) so beta_d T_d tends to 1; the character computation puts the slowest sector at a = 1 giving gap = 2 alpha_d/d + beta_d ~ 2/d; the profile yields t(3/4)/t(1/4) tending to log(4/3) = 0.288, not 1; and the whole-graph error bound |v_d - q_d| <= e^{-alpha_d t} + 1/m_d is correct with both terms vanishing on the relevant scale. A scoped independent review by another agent is on file, checking the full character spectrum, the coupling and the mixing-time brackets, and found no gap in scope. CAVEAT in the memo's own words: the degree is unbounded; Salez's Problem 2.4 as printed carries no degree bound, so the literal statement falls, but whether the workshop question and [52, Conjecture 1] carry one is unchecked. G_d = (Z/2)^d x (Z/m_d), m_d = 1 + ceil(2^d log d / 4) S_d as specified; degree unbounded in d simple, connected, vertex-transitive, unweighted abelian Cayley graph

body:
Let mu_sc be the semicircle law with density (1/(2 pi)) sqrt(4 - x^2) on [-2, 2]. Its Stieltjes transform m(z) = integral (x - z)^{-1} mu_sc(dx) satisfies the self-consistent equation m(z)^2 + z m(z) + 1 = 0 for every z in C^+, equivalently m(z) = -1/( z + m(z) ), and is the UNIQUE solution of that equation with Im m(z) > 0 for z in C^+; explicitly m(z) = ( -z + sqrt(z^2 - 4) )/2 with the branch of the square root chosen so that m(z) is asymptotic to -1/z as |z| tends to infinity. This equation is the fixed point that resolvent proofs of Wigner's theorem converge to: the Schur complement identity applied to the resolvent of a Wigner matrix gives (1/n) tr (H - z)^{-1} approximately equal to -1/(z + (1/n) tr (H - z)^{-1}) up to errors that vanish as n grows, and stability of the fixed point then forces the empirical Stieltjes transform to converge to m. For the Marchenko-Pastur law the analogous equation carries the aspect ratio and reads m(z) = 1/( 1 - y - y z m(z) - z ), a different fixed point that must not be substituted for this one. [standard; e.g. Anderson, Guionnet and Zeitouni, An Introduction to Random Matrices, Section 2.4]
the semicircle law normalised to [-2,2], corresponding to Wigner matrices with entry variance 1/n
the convention m(z) = integral (x - z)^{-1} d mu(x); the opposite sign convention changes the equation

[Theorem 34 of arXiv:2604.13454, 'Invariant and periodic measures in classical spin systems on infinite lattices with highly'] (Harris-Meyn-Tweedie). Let $X(t)$ be a time-homogeneous Markov process on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ with transition probability kernel $\mathcal{P}_t$ and infinitesimal generator $\mathscr{L}$. Suppose that following hypotheses are satisfied
		\item[(i)] The Markov process is irreducible, that is, there exists $t_0$(and then for all $t > t_0 $ ) such that
		$$
		\mathcal{P}_{t_0}(x,\Gamma)> 0,
		$$
		for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and nonempty open sets $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^n$.
		\item[(ii)] For any $t> 0$ the Markov semi-group $\mathcal{P}_t(x,dy)$ has a density $p_t(x,y)$, which is a continuous function of $(x,y)$.\\
		Assume there exists a Lyapunov function
		$$
		V:\mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \left[ 0,\infty\right) \xrightarrow{\Vert x \Vert_{\mathbb{R}^n} \rightarrow +\infty}+\infty
		$$
		and constants $C,c> 0$ such that 
		$$
		\mathscr{L}V+cV\leq C.
		$$
		Then there exists unique invariant measure $\mu$ for the process $X(t)$ and there exist constants $K,\alpha > 0$ such that
		$$
		\sup\limits_{\{f:\vert f(x) \vert \leq V(x)\}}\vert \mathcal{P}_tf(a)-\mu (f) \vert \leq KV(a)e^{-\alpha t}
		$$
		for any $a\in \mathbb{R}^n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 1 (Operator-domain regularity) of arXiv:2608.29854, '2608.29854'] Let $J$ be an open interval and let $w:J\to(0,\infty)$ be Borel with
$w\in L^1_{\loc}(J)$.  Let $\cV$ be admissible in
$H=L^2(J,w(y)\,\dd y)$, and let $\cE$ and $A$ be as above.
Then every  $v\in\Dom(A)$ belongs to $C^1(J)$, with
$v'\in\AC_{\loc}(J)$, and
\begin{align} 
  v''=wAv,
  \quad\text{almost everywhere}.
\end{align}
Moreover, for every compact interval $K\subset J$, the restriction map
$\Dom(A)\to C^1(K)$, where $\Dom(A)$ is equipped with the graph norm,
is continuous.

Let $\bm{\mathcal{Y}}_N = ((\bm{X}_i)_{i \in [N]}, (\bm{W}_{i, j})_{i, j \in [N]})$ be a dissociated array of particle states and pairwise weights. An Aldous-Hoover representation of $\bm{\mathcal{Y}}_N$ is a triple $((\Omega, \mathcal{A}, \pi), \mathsf{X}, \mathsf{W})$ consisting of a latent probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{A}, \pi)$ and measurable functions $\mathsf{X}: \Omega \to \mathbb{D}$ and $\mathsf{W}: \Omega \times \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ such that the array is equal in law to the sampling $\bm{X}_i \stackrel{d}{=} \mathsf{X}(\bm{\xi}_i)$ and $\bm{W}_{i, j} \stackrel{d}{=} \mathsf{W}(\bm{\xi}_i, \bm{\xi}_j)$, where $(\bm{\xi}_i)_{i=1}^N$ are independent random variables on $\Omega$ satisfying the averaging condition $\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \operatorname{Law}(\bm{\xi}_i) = \pi$.
\bm{\mathcal{Y}}_N is a dissociated array
(\Omega, \mathcal{A}, \pi) is a probability space

body:
[Theorem 15 of arXiv:2608.26692, 'Many Facets in Random Polytopes from Product and Log-Concave Measures'] There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ with the following property. For
$n\geq2$, let $\mu$ be a full-dimensional log-concave probability measure on
$\R^n$ with density $f$, and  $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ be independent random
vectors with law $\mu$, where $N\geq2n$.  If
\[
    P_N=\conv\{X_1,\ldots,X_N\},
\]
then
\begin{equation}
    \E f_{n-1}(P_N)
    \leq
    C^n N n^{(n-3)/2}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for every fixed $b>0$, if
\[
    N\leq e^{bn}n^{3/2},
\]
then
\begin{equation}
    \E f_{n-1}(P_N)
    \leq C_b^n n^{n/2}.
\end{equation}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.29327, 'Fractal Random Variables\\ Defined by Probability Distributions of Digits\\ of Their $G_2$'] For any number $x\in [0;g_0]$,
  there exists a sequence $(\alpha_n)\in L$ such that
  \begin{equation}
    
    x = \delta_{\alpha_1}
      + \sum_{k=2}^\infty (\delta_{\alpha_k} \prod_{j=1}^{k-1} g_{\alpha_j})
    \equiv \Delta^{G_2}_{\alpha_1\alpha_2...\alpha_k...},
    \quad
    \delta_{\alpha_k}=\alpha_kg_{1-\alpha_k}.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 9 of arXiv:2511.21496, 'Optimal local central limit theorems on Wiener chaos'] Let $F, G \in \bD^{1,2}$. 
Let $\psi \colon \R \to \R$ be a continuously differentiable function with a bounded derivative. 
Then 
\begin{equation}
    \E[F\psi(G)] = \E[F]\E[\psi(G)] + \E[\psi'(G)\abra{DG, -DL^{-1}F}_{\fH}].
\end{equation}
Here, $L^{-1}$ is extended to a contraction operator on $L^2(\Omega)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 9 of arXiv:2511.21496

[Proposition 40 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Let  $\widetilde{X}^n$ satisfy (\ref{formula1+12+1}). Suppose that $f\in \mL_{p}^q([0,1])$ and $h\in \mH_{1,p}^q([0,1])\cap \mL^{\infty}([0,1])$, where $q\in [2,\infty)$ and $ p\in(2d/\beta\vee 2,\infty]$ are such that  $\frac{d}{p}+\frac{2}{q}<1$. Let $u\in[0,1-4/n]$ be a fixed number, $n\geq 4$ is an integer. Then for every $u+4/n\leq S\leq T\leq 1$, ones has the bound
	\be 
	&&\|\int_{S}^{T}h(r,\widetilde{X}_r^{n})(f(r,\widetilde{X}_r^{n})-f(r,\widetilde{X}_{r_n}^{n}))dr\|_{L_p(
		\Omega|\sF_u)}\no\\
	&\leq &N[(1/n)^{\alpha/2}+(1/n)^{ 1-\beta/2}+(1/n)^{1/2}\log(n)]T(f,h),
	\ee
	where the constant $N$ only depends on $d,p,q,c_1,c_0$ and $$T(f,h)=(\|h\|_{\mL^{\infty}([S,T])}+\|h\|_{\mH_{1,p}^{q}([S,T])})\|f\|_{\mL_{p}^{q}([S,T])}.$$
    In particular,
	\be

body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2512.10761, 'Special times for the point set process of the Brownian Net'] There exists a $(\mathcal{H}^2, \mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{H}^2})$-valued random variable $(\mathcal{W}^l, \mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{r}})$, called the standard left-right Brownian web, whose distribution is uniquely determined by the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item For each deterministic $z \in \mathbb{R}^2$, almost surely there are unique paths $l_z \in \mathcal{W}^l(z)$ and $r_z \in \mathcal{W}^{r}(z)$.
        \item For any finite deterministic set of points $z_1, \ldots, z_n, z_1^{\prime}, \ldots, z_m^{\prime} \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the collection $\left(l_{z_1}, \ldots, l_{z_n} ; r_{z_1^{\prime}}, \ldots, r_{z_m^{\prime}}\right)$ is distributed as left-right coalescing Brownian motions.
        \item For any deterministic countable dense subset $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, almost surely $\mathcal{W}^l$ is the closure of $\mathcal{W}^l(\mathcal{D})$ and $\mathcal{W}^{r}$ is the closure of $\mathcal{W}^r(\mathcal{D})$ in the space $(\Pi, d)$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2607.21062, 'A new probabilistic approach for\\ mean field games of optimal stopping'] Suppose that Assumption \ref{assumption:1A} holds. Let $\{L^n\}_n\subset\mathcal V$ be a sequence weakly converging in $\mathbb H^2(\mathbb R)$ to some $L\in\mathcal V$. Let $\psi$ be as in Lemma \ref{L:m_BV}. Then, it holds that, up to a subsequence,
    \[
    \mathbb E[\psi(t,X_t)L_t^n] \rightarrow \mathbb E[\psi(t,X_t)L_t] \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb E[\psi(t,X_t^n)L_t^n] \rightarrow \mathbb E[\psi(t,X_t)L_t], \qquad \text{for a.e. }t\in[0,T],
    \]
    where $X^n$ is the solution to equation \eqref{MFG SDE} with $L^n$ in place of $L$. In particular, for every $p\geq1$, it holds that
    \[
    \int_0^T\big|\mathbb E[\psi(t,X_t)L_t^n] - \mathbb E[\psi(t,X_t)L_t]\big|^pdt\rightarrow0, \qquad
    \int_0^T\big|\mathbb E[\psi(t,X_t^n)L_t^n] - \mathbb E[\psi(t,X_t)L_t]\big|^pdt\rightarrow0.
    \]

body:
[Proposition 26 (Geometric axis and gate decomposition) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $0\neq v\in V$, and let $g,a\in\Sl(V)$ satisfy
\[
g=a\e^v a^{-1}.
\]
Equip $V$ with an auxiliary Euclidean norm, denoted by $\norm{\cdot}_{\mathrm{Euc}}$, and set
\[
\mathcal{A}=a\mathcal{A}_v
 =\set{a\e^{tv}:t\in\R},
\qquad L_g(x)=gx,
\]
and let $p$ be the metric projection of $1$ onto $\mathcal{A}$. Then, for every $x\in\Sl(V)$,
\begin{align}
 d_{\infty}(x,gx)
 &=2d_{\infty}(x,\mathcal{A})+\norm{v}_{\mathrm{Euc}},
 \\
 \mathcal{A}
 &=\set{x\in\Sl(V):d_{\infty}(x,gx)=\norm{v}_{\mathrm{Euc}}}.
 
\end{align}
Thus $\mathcal{A}$ is the unique minimum-displacement axis of $L_g$ and is independent of the chosen factorisation of $g$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}
[1,g]=[1,p]\cup[p,gp]\cup[gp,g],
\end{equation}
where the three pieces meet only at $p$ and $gp$, and
\begin{equation}
gp=p\e^v,
\qquad
g=p\e^v p^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Finally,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{A}\cap[1,g]=[p,gp].
\end{equation}
The first and third pieces in \cref{eq:conjugacy-geodesic-decomposition} degenerate simultaneously.

[Theorem thm:top2 of arXiv:2411.14556, 'Emergence in Graphs with near-extreme constraints'] For each fixed $e \in (0,1)$ and all $t$ sufficiently close to (but below) $e^{3/2}$, the 
optimal graphon with edge/triangle densities $(e,t)$ is unique and bipodal. Asymptotically, the Boltzmann entropy 
scales as $-(e^{3/2}-t)\ln(e^{3/2}-t)$
and the Lagrange multiplier $\beta$ scales as $\ln(e^{3/2}-t)$.

[Corollary 14 of arXiv:2609.03098, 'Standing waves for Schr\"odinger equations with Kato class potentials and $L^\infty$-bound'] Assume that for each $n \ge 0$, the mapping $F_n$ satisfies the Lipschitz condition \eqref{F-lip-cond} with the same constant $L>0$. Suppose, moreover, that the family $\{F_n\}_{n \ge 1}$ satisfies \eqref{k-set-for-seq} with $k < \inf \sigma_{ess}(A)-\lambda$ and that
\[
F_n(u) \to F_0(u) \quad \text{in } \ L^2(\mathbb{R}^N), \ \ \text{as } \ n \to +\infty,
\]
for every $u \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Let, for each $n \ge 1$, the mapping $u_n \colon [0,t_n] \to H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ be a solution of equation \eqref{A-Fn-eqn} with $t_n \to \infty$. If there exists $R > 0$ such that
\[
\|u_n(t)\|_{H^1} \le R \quad \text{for all } \ t \in [0, t_n] \ \text{ and } \ n \ge 1,
\]
then the sequence $\bigl(u_n(t_n)\bigr)$ contains a subsequence  converging in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$.

STATUS: proof (unaudited); own-work draft. For arbitrary n>=2 scalar three-token first-token-query self-attention examples with distinct signed values, negative minimum, positive maximum, and positive signed first token, joint-head logistic GD has two open endpoint-selection basins. Invariant subregions escape for every eta>0; for eta<=min(2/H^2,1/(2D)), every finite initialization outside a null saddle-stable set escapes to one endpoint pattern. Interior and mixed endpoint hard patterns are impossible. Normalized margins are min maxima and min negated minima, so unequal margins give a positive-measure inferior basin.

# Target 1: scalar three-token self-attention under joint training

Version 1, unaudited. Own work; novelty not established globally.
This extends the scalar family, not arbitrary vector-valued token geometry.

## Data, model and conclusions

For each i=1,...,n, n>=2, take a label y_i in {-1,+1} and three distinct
signed token values c_ij. Their minimum m_i is negative, maximum M_i positive,
and the FIRST token c_i1 is positive. Let raw tokens x_ij=y_i c_ij and use
the actual first token x_i1 as the self-attention query. With jointly trained
scalar head v and scalar attention weight p, signed prediction is v h_i(p),

 h_i(p)=sum_j c_ij exp(zeta_i c_ij p)/sum_j exp(zeta_i c_ij p),
 zeta_i=c_i1>0.

The loss is average logistic loss. Let
 H=max_i max(|m_i|,|M_i|), D=max_i zeta_i(M_i-m_i)^2,
 eta_*=min(2/H^2,1/(2D)).

For every fixed eta in (0,eta_*], simultaneous GD in (v,p) has precisely
three possible limits: the unique finite saddle (0,p_bar), where
mean_i h_i(p_bar)=0; matching-positive escape v,p->+infinity; or
matching-negative escape v,p->-infinity. The saddle's global stable set is
planar null. Both escaping basins are open and nonempty. Their hard selections
are respectively the maximum signed token in EVERY example and the minimum
signed token in EVERY example. No interior token, or mixed pattern of extrema,
is a hard-selection limit in this scalar model. On escaping trajectories
p=O(log |v|), loss->0 and the normalized joint directions are (+1,0),(-1,0).
The corresponding minimum signed margins, normalized by sqrt(v^2+p^2),
are Gamma_+=min_i M_i and Gamma_-=min_i(-m_i).

In addition, for EVERY eta>0 the regions
 Q_+={v>0,p>max_i rho_i}, Q_-={v<0,p<min_i rho_i},
where h_i(rho_i)=0, are forward invariant and satisfy the same respective
escape/margin conclusions. Thus if Gamma_+>Gamma_-, the inferior basin is
open and positive measure even without a step-size restriction. A sufficient
strict inequality is M_i+m_i>0 for every example.

## Scalar softmax link estimates

Write alpha_ij(p) for the three softmax weights. Direct differentiation gives
h_i'=zeta_i[sum alpha_ij c_ij^2-h_i^2]
     =zeta_i sum_{j<l} alpha_ij alpha_il(c_ij-c_il)^2>0.
Also |h_i|<=H, h_i'<=zeta_i(M_i-m_i)^2<=D, and h_i tends to m_i,M_i
at the two infinities. Thus each root rho_i exists uniquely.

Let delta be the minimum over i of zeta_i times either adjacent gap of its
sorted three token values. It is strictly positive. For p>=0, the total
softmax mass on nonmaximum tokens is <=2 exp(-delta p).
Variance is no larger than the second moment about the maximum token,
so h_i'(p)<=2D exp(-delta p). Reflecting yields the same upper bound
2D exp(-delta |p|) for p<=0. Every h_i is real analytic, strictly increasing,
bounded, and has exponentially decaying derivative.

## Full-plane trapping and escape

For g_i=(1+exp(v h_i(p)))^-1 put F=mean g_i h_i and G=mean g_i h_i'>0.
GD is v_+=v+eta F, p_+=p+eta vG. The following estimates are identical
to those needed in proof 005, now established for genuine three-token links:

 -H^2/4<=F_v<=0,
 F(0,p)=mean h_i(p)/2=:F_0(p), 0<F_0'<=D/2, G<=D.

There is a unique mean root p_bar. Set u=p-p_bar, A=H^2/4.
In v,u>0, v_+>=(1-eta A)v+eta F_0(p)>0 and p increases; reflecting gives
invariance in v,u<0. In a bad quadrant v>0,u<0, v decreases and u increases
until it exits or converges to the saddle. Double crossing would require

 (1-eta A)v<=eta(D/2)|u|<=eta^2 D^2 v/2,

impossible since eta A<=1/2 and eta D<=1/2. The other bad quadrant is the
reflection. An axis point other than the saddle enters a good quadrant after
one step. A bad-quadrant orbit staying there is bounded and monotone; continuity
of increments gives vG=F=0 at its limit, hence the saddle.

Consider a positive good-quadrant orbit. If p had a finite limit P and v were
bounded, compactness would give G bounded below; Delta p->0 would force v->0,
but F_0(P)>0 contradicts convergence of v to zero. If v were unbounded and
P<=R:=max rho_i, an example with root R has h_j(p)<=0 and therefore g_j>=1/2.
On the compact p interval its derivative is bounded below, so
Delta p>=eta d v/(2n), contradicting finite P. If P>R, eventually all links
are >=c>0; v then increases without bound and
Delta p/Delta v>=d v/H again contradicts finite P. Thus p->infinity.
Eventually all h_i>=c, forcing v->infinity (bounded v would keep the g_i
uniformly positive). Negative escape follows by reflection using -h_i(-p).

This proof also applies directly within Q_+ or Q_- at any eta>0: both
coordinates are monotone from the start and all signed links are positive
after reflection. Only the full-plane trapping argument uses eta_*.

## Rates, margin, and the null exceptional set

On a positive escaping trajectory, h_i>=c>0 eventually, so
Delta p<=eta D v exp(-cv)->0. Moreover
Delta p/Delta v<=2D v exp(-delta p)/c.
Once Delta p<=1, the mean value theorem gives
Delta exp(delta p)<=C v Delta v. Telescoping against v^2 gives
exp(delta p)<=C'(1+v^2), so p=O(log v). Reflection proves the other branch.
Loss and normalized margin limits now follow. For any parameter pair,
the endpoint bounds and sqrt(v^2+p^2)>=|v| show the normalized minimum
margin cannot exceed max(Gamma_+,Gamma_-); the larger branch attains it.

At the saddle, the update Jacobian is
[[1-eta A_s,eta B_s],[eta B_s,1]],
where A_s=mean h_i(p_bar)^2/4<=A and B_s=mean h_i'(p_bar)/2 in (0,D/2].
Its determinant >=7/16 and det(DT-I)<0: one eigenvalue lies in (0,1),
the other exceeds 1. The analytic update map has a Jacobian determinant
not identically zero; the zero set is null. Away from that set its local
inverse maps preserve null sets. By a countable cover, preimages of null
sets are null. The local stable-manifold theorem and countably many iterated
preimages therefore give a null global stable set. Each escaping basin is
the union of preimages of its open good quadrant, hence open. This is the
same null-preimage argument detailed in proofs/003 and 005, not an assumption
that the GD map is globally invertible.

## Which locally optimal selections, and comparison with prior art

For p->+infinity only the largest signed c_ij can dominate; for p->-infinity
only the smallest can dominate. Because all zeta_i>0 these choices must be
consistent across examples. At finite p all weights are strictly positive,
so an interior token cannot become a hard selection. For a fixed v>0, the
maximum-token pattern is the only locally optimal feasible hard selection;
for fixed v<0 the minimum-token pattern is the only one. Both are stable
under joint training, by the open basins above. The minimum pattern can
nevertheless be inferior when comparing the two JOINT normalized margins.

Tarzanagh et al., 2306.13596, Definition 2 (PDF p.5) compares the chosen token
score only to its active SVM neighbors, with a FIXED head. Their Theorem 3
(PDF p.6) gives convergence from cones C_{mu,R} around such locally optimal
directions. It already includes a three-token illustration immediately after
the theorem. The present scalar result is not the discovery of that phenomenon:
it classifies the scalar joint-head basins and excludes mixed/interior hard
patterns in this stated geometry. General vector-valued three-token locally
optimal selections and their joint-head basins remain open here.

## Explicit distinct mixed-label witness

Take signed triples (3/2,1/4,-1/2) and (3/2,1/8,-1), with labels +1,-1.
Raw triples are (3/2,1/4,-1/2),(-3/2,-1/8,1); actual first-token queries
are 3/2,-3/2. Both zeta_i=3/2. H=3/2, D=75/8, eta_*=4/75.
Gamma_+=3/2 and Gamma_-=1/2. The conditions are strict and persist in an
open neighborhood of these data. This witness is illustrative; the theorem
covers the whole family above rather than just this isolated case.
Raw tokens x_ij=y_i c_ij, y_i in {+1,-1}; query=x_i1; c_i1>0, min_j c_ij<0<max_j c_ij, all three c_ij distinct. H=max absolute signed endpoint, D=max_i c_i1(max c_i-min c_i)^2. Train scalar v,p by simultaneous fixed-step Euclidean GD on average logistic loss.

[Defination 4 of arXiv:2511.10814, '\Large \bf \boldmath\ \\ Convergence of the extended Kalman filter with small and state-de'] Let $L^q$ be the space of random variables with  finite moment of order $~q \geq 1$. 
			The \textbf{norm of a random variable} $X$ in $L^q,~q \geq 1$,  is denoted by  $\left\vert X \right\vert_{q}$  and is  defined  by  $\left\vert X \right\vert_{q}=\Big(\E[|X|^q]\Big)^{1/q}$.

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2606.14038, 'Trivariate Hypergeometric Series Formulas\\ for Pure Partition Functions of Multiple $3$-S'] (i) For any   $p\in (0,3\beta+1-(\beta\vee 1))$, there exists $ C_p>0$ such that $|A_{\u n}|\le C_p(N_{\u n}+1)^{-p}$  for all $\u n\in\N_0^3$.

(ii) If $\beta\in (1/2,1)$, then for any $s\in (1, (\beta+1/2)\wedge (2-\beta))$, there exists $ C_s>0$ such that $|A_{\u n}|\le C_s(a_{\u n}+1)^{-s}(b_{\u n}+1)^{-1}(c_{\u n}+1)^{-s}$  for all $\u n\in\N_0^3$.

[Corollary 20 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Suppose $\X$ satisfies Assumption \ref{assump:X-universal}.

\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item If Assumption \ref{assump:dynamics} holds,
$f:\R \to \R$ is odd, and $\theta^0$ is
sign invariant in law (i.e.\ $f(x)={-}f(-x)$ for all $x \in \R$, and
$\Law(\theta^0)=\Law({-}\theta^0)$),
then Theorem \ref{thm:dmft-approx} holds for the dynamics
$\{\btheta^t\}_{t \geq 0}$.
\item If $U(\cdot)$ and $\Lambda$ satisfy all conditions of
Corollary \ref{cor:hightemp}, and $U:\R \to \R$ is even
(i.e.\ $U(x)=U(-x)$ for all $x \in \R$),
then all statements of Theorem \ref{thm:replica} hold for $\mu_\Gibbs$.
\item If $h=0$ in the Ising model \eqref{eq:ising} and $\Lambda_{\max}<1/2$,
then all statements of Corollary \ref{cor:ising} hold.
\item If $f(\cdot)$ is not odd, $\theta^0$ is not sign-invariant in law,

body: In Vapnik–Chervonenkis theory, the Vapnik–Chervonenkis (VC) dimension is a measure of the size of a class of sets. The notion can be extended to classes of binary functions. It is defined as the cardinality of the largest set of points that the function class can shatter—that is, for which all possible binary labelings can be realized by some function in the class. It was originally defined by Vladimir Vapnik and Alexey Chervonenkis.
title: Vapnik–Chervonenkis dimension

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $K\subset\R$ be compact and let $a\in\R$.  Suppose that
\begin{equation}
 \inf_{u\in K}\inf_{\zeta\in\spec(H_{\beta-iu})}\Re\zeta>a

\end{equation}
and that
\begin{equation}
 \Re\mathfrak h_{\beta-iu}[f]
 \geq a\norm f_2^2,
 \qquad f\in\cD, u\in K.
 
\end{equation}
Then there are $C,\eta>0$ such that
\[
 \sup_{u\in K}\norm{S_u(t)}_{2\to2}
 \leq C \mathrm e^{-(a+\eta)t},
 \qquad t\geq1.
\]
The same conclusion holds for a norm-continuous family of complementary
spectral semigroups $S_u(t)(I-P_u)$, provided that the corresponding
complementary spectra satisfy \eqref{eq:abstract-uniform-spectral-gap} and
$\sup_{u\in K}\norm{P_u}_{2 \to 2}<\infty$.

Fix positive integers N,n, arbitrary finite real numbers sigma_ij, and a real N-by-n matrix A_n. For the relevant N,n, write A=A_n and sigma_ij=sigma_ij(n), D_j=diag(sigma_1j^2,...,sigma_Nj^2), and Dtilde_i=diag(sigma_i1^2,...,sigma_in^2). Let S_plus consist of the functions z->integral_[0,infinity) (lambda-z)^(-1) nu(dlambda) for probability measures nu on [0,infinity), analytically continued to C minus [0,infinity). The canonical equations define a unique S_plus-valued solution psi_i,psitilde_j by psi_i(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(Dtilde_i Ttilde(z))/n)] and psitilde_j(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(D_j T(z))/n)], where Psi=diag(psi_i), Psitilde=diag(psitilde_j), T(z)=[Psi(z)^(-1)-z A Psitilde(z) A^T]^(-1), and Ttilde(z)=[Psitilde(z)^(-1)-z A^T Psi(z) A]^(-1). Both trace terms in these canonical equations use division by n. Moreover there are positive matrix-valued measures M and Mtilde on [0,infinity), with total masses I_N and I_n, such that T(z)=integral (lambda-z)^(-1) M(dlambda) and Ttilde(z)=integral (lambda-z)^(-1) Mtilde(dlambda). Positivity here means that the measure of every Borel set is a positive-semidefinite matrix. In particular tr(T)/N and tr(Ttilde)/n are Stieltjes transforms of probability measures. Uniqueness is within this analytic Stieltjes class, rather than among all algebraic roots at one value of z.

all scalar unknown functions belong to the probability-measure Stieltjes class S_plus

body: [Corollary of arXiv:2608.30592, 'Infinite Matrix Operators and $E$-Frames in Hilbert Spaces'] Suppose that $E=(E_{n,k})_{n,k\geq 1}$ is an infinite complex diagonal matrix such that $0<\inf_n\left\vert\lambda_n\right\vert\leq\sup_n\left\vert\lambda_n\right\vert<\infty$ where $\lbrace\lambda_n\rbrace_{n=1}^{\infty}=\lbrace E_{n,n}\rbrace_{n\geq1}$. Then any frame $\Psi=\lbrace\psi_k\rbrace_{k=1}^{\infty}$ for $\mathcal{H}$ with bounds $A$ and $B$, is an $E$-frame for $\mathcal{H}$ with bounds $CA$ and $\lambda^2B$ where $\lambda=sup_n\left\vert\lambda_n\right\vert$ and $C$ is a positive number.

    (set $\theta = 0$ in comparison to (def:strong of the paper)-(def:mild of the paper)).  Fix $\eta \in (N/(2r), 1/2)$ and $\theta_F, \theta_G \leq 0$ that satisfy $\theta_F > \eta - 1$, $\theta_G > \eta - 1/2$. If $F: B \to \mathcal{B}_{\theta_F}$ and $G: B \to \gamma(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{B}_{\theta_G})$ are globally Lipschitz, then for all $p,T > 0$ the following statements hold:

        \item The problem (equation eq:gefx of the paper) has a unique mild solution $x_t \in L^p(\Omega; C([0,T];B))$ ((def:mild of the paper)) for any initial condition $x_0 \in B$.
        \item If $F_n: B \to \mathcal{B}_{\theta_F}$ and $G_n: B \to \gamma(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{B}_{\theta_G})$ are globally Lipschitz for each $n \geq 1$, $F_n \to F, G_n \to G$ pointwise, and $x_0^{(n)} \to x_0$ in $B$, then the solutions $x_t^{(n)}$ converge to $x_t$ in $L^p(\Omega; C([0,T];B))$.
    \end{enumerate}

Then, for any $h_1,h_2 \in [H]$
\[
\oint_{\gamma_{h_1}} \oint_{\gamma_{h_2}} \mathcal{F}_{h_1,h_2}(z_1,z_2) f_{h_1}(z_1) f_{h_2}(z_2) \frac{\dd z_1 \dd z_2}{(2\ii\pi)^2} = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_{\alpha_{h_1}}^{\beta_{h_1}}  \int_{\alpha_{h_2}}^{\beta_{h_2}} \textnormal{Gr}^{+}(p_1,p_2) \dd \tilde{f}_{h_1}(p_1) \dd \tilde{f}_{h_2}(p_2).
\]

body: Let A, B be n x n Hermitian matrices, with eigenvalues of each, and of A+B, listed in decreasing order lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ... >= lambda_n. Weyl's inequality states lambda_{i+j-1}(A+B) <= lambda_i(A) + lambda_j(B) whenever i+j-1 <= n, and lambda_{i+j-n}(A+B) >= lambda_i(A) + lambda_j(B) whenever i+j-n >= 1. Taking j=1 and j=n gives lambda_k(A) + lambda_n(B) <= lambda_k(A+B) <= lambda_k(A) + lambda_1(B) for every k, hence |lambda_k(A+B) - lambda_k(A)| <= ||B|| (operator norm) for all k: eigenvalues are 1-Lipschitz functions of the matrix.
title: Weyl's inequality

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2609.00483, 'On Embedding Hamming Spheres with Applications to Positive Curvature'] Assume $\Z_p^r$ acts effectively and isometrically on a closed, positively
curved manifold $M^n$ with a non-empty fixed-point set, where 
$p \in \{3,5,7,11,13,17,19\}$. 
Suppose
\begin{multline*}
r>
\frac12\Bigl(1-H_p(J_p(\tfrac14))\Bigr)n
+\frac32\log_p n
+\log_p\!\left(\frac{p-1}{2}+\frac1n\right)
-\frac12\log_p 2 \\
\qquad
+\frac12\log_p\!\left(\frac{8(1-J_p(\tfrac14))}{J_p(\tfrac14)}\right)
+\log_p(p-1).
\end{multline*}
Then the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists $\tau_1\in\Z_p^r$ such that $\codim(M^{\tau_1}_x)\le \frac{n+3}{4}$;
\item There exists $\tau_2\in\Z_p^r$ such that $\codim(M^{\tau_2}_x)\le \frac{n+1}{3}$, where $\tau_2\notin\langle\tau_1\rangle$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.02294, 'Existence and Blow-Up for Non-linear Fokker-Planck with Controlled Drift Divergence'] Assume condition \eqref{eq:assumptions2}. If $k>k_c$, any uniformly bounded solution $u$ in space and time, i.e. $u \in L^\infty_{t,x}$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
\max_{x\in\R^d}|u(t,x)|\le  \mathcal O(t^{-\frac{d}{2}}), \text{ for }t \to \infty.
\end{equation} If $k=k_c$, any well defined solution satisfies \eqref{eq:longtimeest}. Instead, for subcritical cases $k<{k_c}$, there are examples of stationary solutions. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm-order of arXiv:2604.17170, 'CaTherine wheels from trees and Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $f$ be as in Theorem~(thm-lqg-wheel of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}
\item 
Almost surely, $f^{-1}(\infty)$ consists of a single point, and there exists a continuous space-filling curve $g : \mathbb R\to \mathbb C$ which is a re-parametrization of $f|_{S^1- f^{-1}(\infty)}$ such that $g(0) = 0$ and $\mu(g[a,b]) = b-a$ for each $a,b\in\mathbb R$ with $a < b$, where $\mu$ is the LQG area measure. 
\item Let $z,w\in\mathbb C \setminus Z_\infty$ such that there is a unique $D$-geodesic from each of $z$ and $w$ to $\infty$ (by Proposition~(prop-geo-infty of the paper), this is a.s.\ the case for a fixed $z,w\in\mathbb C$). Then with $g$ as above, each of $z$ and $w$ has a unique preimage under $g$. Moreover, $z$ is hit before $w$ by $g$ if and only if the $D$-geodesic from $z$ to $\infty$ merges into the $D$-geodesic from $w$ to $\infty$ from the right side of the latter. 

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Properties the LQG CaTherine wheel

body: [Proposition prop:noncancellation of arXiv:2606.01937, 'Stationary fluctuations for an exclusion process with mass and energy conservation'] Assume that $\rho\in (0,1)$, $\mathcal{E}\in (\rho ,\kappa\rho )$, $\kappa >2$ and $\alpha_e\neq 0$. Then, the coefficients~$\mathbf{G}_{22}^1$ and $\mathbf{G}_{11}^2$ are always non-zero. Moreover, there exists some choice of parameters that makes all the diagonal entries of the coupling matrices non-zero, leading to the emergence of KPZ behaviour for both modes according to NLFH theory (\textit{cf.}~the red cell in (table:classification of the paper)).

[Lemma 21 (Local absolute continuity) of arXiv:2506.09609, 'Schramm-Loewner evolution contains a topological Sierpi\'nski carpet when $\kappa$ is clos'] Fix $0 < b < b' < 1$ and $T>0$. For any $M>0$ and $\alpha>0$, there exists a constant $C = C(b, b', T, \alpha, M)>0$ such that the following holds. Let $h$ be a zero-boundary GFF on $B(z,r)$. Let $g$ be any deterministic harmonic function in $B(z,r)$ satisfying $\sup_{u,v \in B(z,b'r)} |g(u) - g(v)| \leq M$, and let $s \in (0,T)$. Then, $(h+g)|_{B(z, br)}$ and $h|_{B(z,br)}$ are absolutely continuous with respect to each other viewed as random generalized functions modulo $s \mathbb{Z}$. Furthermore, the Radon-Nikodym derivative $H_g$ of the former with respect to the latter satisfies
        $$
        \max\{ \mathbb{E}[(H_g)^{-\alpha}], \mathbb{E}[(H_g)^\alpha] \} \leq C.
        $$

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.09248, '\bfseries Limit laws for longest edges in empty region graphs'] Assume the same set-up as in Theorem \ref{th:PoisConv}. Then, for any $t\geq 2$,
$$
\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{Kol}}\big(\gamma tL_{t,W}^d-\log(t)-\log(\kappa_d/(2\gamma)),G_W\big) \leq \begin{cases}
        c \log^{-(d-2)}(t), & d \ge 3,\\
        c \log^{-1/2}(t), & d=2,
    \end{cases}
$$
where $G_W$ is a Gumbel distributed random variable with $\PP(G_W\leq s)=\exp(-\vol(W)e^{-s})$ for $s\in\RR$. Here, $c\in(0,\infty)$ is a constant which only depends on $d$, $\vol(W)$, and the parameters of the particular example. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm 14 (Two-level kernel for orientation-reversing nested rectangles) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Suppose one physical side has size $p$ at the earlier rectangle and $Q$ at the later rectangle, while the other has size $q$ earlier and $P$ later, where
\[
 p<q\leq P<Q.
\]
Put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 r_0&=q-p,
 &C&=P-q,
 &B&=Q-q,\\
 A&=P-p=r_0+C,
 &r&=Q-P=B-C.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Define $\mathcal L_{d,\alpha}$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-orientation-kernel}.

Set $W(x,z)=0$ for $z\leq x$. If $C=0$, put
\begin{equation}
 W(x,z)
 =
 \ee^{-z}\frac{(z-x)^{r_0+B-1}}{(r_0+B-1)!}.
\end{equation}
If $C\geq1$, put
\begin{equation}
 W(x,z)
 =
 \ee^{-z}z^r
 \int_x^z
 \frac{(u-x)^{r_0+B-1}u^{-B}(z-u)^{C-1}}
 {(r_0+B-1)!(C-1)!}\,\dd u.
\end{equation}

The two-level positive squared-singular-value process is determinantal, with one exact kernel
\begin{align}
 K_{00}(x,y)
 &=
 \ee^{-x}x^{r_0}\mathcal L_{p,r_0}(x,y),
 \\
 K_{11}(x,y)
 &=
 \ee^{-y}y^r\mathcal L_{P,r}(x,y),
 \\
 K_{10}(x,y)
 &=
 \left(\frac{\dd}{\dd y}\right)^A
 (rI+E_y)^{\mathrm{fall}\,B}
 \mathcal L_{P,r}(x,y),
 \\
 K_{01}(x,y)
 &=
 -W(x,y)+
 \int_0^\infty W(x,z)K_{11}(z,y)\,\dd z.
 
\end{align}
The same statement holds with rows and columns interchanged.

body: In mathematics, the matrix exponential is a matrix function on square matrices analogous to the ordinary exponential function. It is used to solve systems of linear differential equations. In the theory of Lie groups, the matrix exponential gives the exponential map between a matrix Lie algebra and the corresponding Lie group.

Fix an integer l>=1, and let d_0=d tend to infinity, d_i=d_i(d) tend to infinity for each 1<=i<=l, and d_(l+1)=1. Independently for each layer, let W_i have independent N(0,1/d_(i-1)) entries. Let f_d(x)=W_(l+1) sigma(W_l sigma(...sigma(W_1 x)...)), with sigma applied coordinatewise. Assume sigma is nonconstant and locally Lipschitz, is differentiable almost everywhere with almost-everywhere continuous derivative, and satisfies |sigma'(t)|<=C_sigma(1+|t|^(k-1)) for some fixed integer k>=1. For deterministic x_d of norm sqrt(d), and every increasing positive sequence xi_d tending to infinity, there is a positive deterministic step sequence s_d<=xi_d such that x_s=x_d-sign(f_d(x_d))*s_d*grad f_d(x_d) has ||x_s-x_d||/||x_d|| tending to zero in probability and P(sign(f_d(x_s)) != sign(f_d(x_d))) tending to one. No relative growth restriction between diverging widths is imposed. The theorem does not supply an explicit finite-width rate for the sign-reversal probability. In particular ReLU and profiles d->floor(d^c)->m(d)->1, 0<c<1 and m(d)->infinity, are included.
Fixed depth l+1
Every hidden width diverges
Independent Gaussian entries with inverse incoming-width variance
Deterministic input of norm sqrt(d)
Nonconstant locally Lipschitz activation, a.e. differentiable, a.e. continuous derivative with polynomial growth; local Lipschitz is an explicit extra regularity hypothesis

body: [Corollary cor:consistency-mean of arXiv:2411.09516, 'Sharp Matrix Empirical Bernstein Inequalities\footnote{NeurIPS 2025 Poster}'] Let $\{  \mathbf{X} _n \}$ be adapted to $\mathcal{F}$ with constant conditional mean $ \mathbb E [ \mathbf{X} _n|\mathcal{F}_{n-1}] =  \mathbf{M} $ and $\delta \in (0,1]$. If $\sum_{n=1}^\infty n^{-1-\delta}  \mathbb E [ \| \mathbf{X} _n -  \mathbf{M}  \|^{1+\delta} | \mathcal{F}_{n-1} ] < \infty $ almost surely, then the sample mean $\overline{ \mathbf{X} }_n$ converges to $ \mathbf{M} $ almost surely.

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2605.27818, 'Exponential decay of mass for inertial coalescing particles with Hamiltonian noise'] At each midpoint $q\in\mathcal M$, the function $D_H$ vanishes at exact order $2$,
and is non-negative on a neighborhood of $q$ intersected with $\mathcal S$.
More precisely, for $q=(q_1,p_2)\in Z_1\times M_2$ there exist positive constants
$c_1(q), c_2(q), r_q$ such that
\begin{equation}c_1(q)(x_2-p_2)^2-c_2(q)|x_1-q_1|\;\leq\;D_H(x)\;\leq\;
c_2(q)\big((x_2-p_2)^2+|x_1-q_1|\big),
\end{equation}
for $|x-q|<r_q$.
An analogous statement  holds at the  midpoints in

[Lemma lemma-h0C of arXiv:2609.00108, 'The double sphere solution in the liquid drop model'] Let \(0<b<\frac14\) be fixed and sufficiently small, and let
		\(\delta>0\) be fixed and sufficiently small. Then the function
		\(h_C^0\) defined in (equation def-hC0 of the paper)--(equation def-psiC0 of the paper) has the
		following properties.
		First,
		\begin{equation}
			h_C^0(r)=0,
			\qquad
			1<r\le r_0 :=\delta\varepsilon^{-3/4}.
		\end{equation}
		In the transition region
		\[
		r_0<r<2r_0
		\]
		one has
		\begin{equation}
			|h_C^0(r)|
			\le C_\delta,
			\qquad
			|(h_C^0)'(r)|
			\le
			\frac{C_\delta}{r_0},
			\qquad
			|(h_C^0)''(r)|
			\le
			\frac{C_\delta}{r_0^2}.
		\end{equation}
		Moreover, uniformly for
		\[
		2r_0<r<\varepsilon^{-1+b},
		\]
		one has
		\begin{equation}
			r(h_C^0)'(r)
			=
			-\left(
			1+O(\delta^4)+O(\varepsilon^b)
			\right),
		\end{equation}
		and consequently
		\begin{equation}
			h_C^0(r)
			=
			-\left(
			1+O(\delta^4)+O(\varepsilon^b)
			\right)
			\log\frac r{r_0}
			+
			O_\delta(1).
		\end{equation}
		In addition,
		\begin{equation}
			|(h_C^0)''(r)|
			\le
			\frac{C_\delta}{r^2},
			\qquad
			2r_0<r<\varepsilon^{-1+b},
		\end{equation}
		and
		\begin{equation}
			\|h_C^0\|_*
			\le
			C_\delta
			\varepsilon^{3/2}|\log\varepsilon|.
		\end{equation}
		Finally,
		\begin{equation}
			J_{\Sigma_0^\varepsilon}[h_C^0]-E_{02}
			=
			0
			\qquad
			\text{for }
			r\notin(r_0,2r_0),
		\end{equation}
		while
		$$
		\left|
		J_{\Sigma_0^\varepsilon}[h_C^0]-E_{02}
		\right|
		\le
		C_\delta
		\varepsilon^2|\log\delta|
		\qquad
		\text{for }
		r \in (r_0,2r_0).
		$$
		In particular,
		\begin{equation}
			\left\|
			J_{\Sigma_0^\varepsilon}[h_C^0]-E_{02}
			\right\|_{L^\infty(1,\varepsilon^{-1+b})}
			\le
			C_\delta
			\varepsilon^2|\log\delta|.
		\end{equation}

[Defin 15 of arXiv:2608.00811, 'Comparison of Dirichlet forms for stable-like random walks on groups of polynomial volume '] Let $\widetilde{S_N}$ be the formal concatenation of $\Sigma_0$ and $S_N$. 
Define the weight system $w_N$  by setting 
$$w_N(\sigma) = 
 \begin{cases}
\frac{1}{2} &\text{if }\sigma \in \Sigma_0\\
v_i &\text{if }\sigma =x_j s_i^{\epsilon_i}  x_j^{-1}  \subseteq S_N.\\
\end{cases}
$$  Set 
$$    \|g\|_N =  \|g\|_{N,S,\mathbf{v}} = \inf \left\{ \max_{\sigma \in \widetilde{S_N}}\left\{ \mbox{deg}_\sigma(\theta)^\frac{1}{w_N(\sigma) } \right\}:  \theta = g \in G, \theta \in \bigcup_{m=0}^\infty \widetilde{S_N}^m\right\}\\ $$
Regard $S_N$ as a tuple and denote by $\mathbf{v}_N$ the tuple given by $(w_N(\sigma))_{\sigma \in S_N}$.

[Corollary 142 (Fixed-interface, fixed-driver response-completion extension) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Fix the law family $\cP$, one backward-compatible continuation interface
$(\mathcal E_{s,t})$, and one admissible driver $F$ in the sense of
\Cref{def:admissible-backward-driver}.  Let $\mathscr D_0$ be a
response-quotiented operational data core for this fixed triple and suppose
every $d\in\mathscr D_0$ carries a backward first-jet trajectory with terminal
response $\xi^d$.  Assume that $d\mapsto\xi^d$ is part of the declared data
metric and is Cauchy-continuous into $\mathcal L_{\cP}^2$.  If the
operational solution map
\[
 \Phi_{\rm bw}^{\rm op}:d\longmapsto(Y^d,Z^d)
\]
is Cauchy-continuous from the declared data metric into
$\mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}$, then it extends uniquely to the metric completion
$\overline{\mathscr D_0}$:
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{\rm bw}:\overline{\mathscr D_0}
 \longrightarrow\mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}.
\end{equation}
Assume also that $\mathscr D_0$ carries declared truncations
$\rho_u^{\mathscr D}$ which preserve $\mathscr D_0$, are Cauchy-continuous
for the data metric, and form a truncation system:
\[
 \rho_T^{\mathscr D}=I,
 \qquad
 \rho_u^{\mathscr D}\rho_v^{\mathscr D}
 =\rho_{u\wedge v}^{\mathscr D},
 \qquad u,v\in[0,T].
\]
Assume, moreover, that
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{\rm bw}^{\rm op}(\rho_u^{\mathscr D}d)
 =\rho_u^{\mathscr W}\Phi_{\rm bw}^{\rm op}(d),
 \qquad d\in\mathscr D_0,\quad u\in[0,T].
\end{equation}
Then the truncations and the displayed compatibility extend to the two
completions; the extended maps still satisfy the truncation identities.
The terminal response extends simultaneously; writing its extension again as
$d\mapsto\xi^d$, continuity of terminal evaluation gives
$Y_T^d=\xi^d$ on $\overline{\mathscr D_0}$.  Thus the limit is independent of
the operational approximation in the declared data metric and retains the
terminal condition.  The running sources $B^F[Y^d,Z^d]$, common stochastic integrals,
and intrinsic defects converge as continuous readouts, and the limiting defect
remains in $\mathbb K_{\cP}^{2,\uparrow}$.  For every declared seam $s\le t$
put
\[
 \mathscr G_{s,t}^0
 :=\{G_{s,t}[Y^d,Z^d]:d\in\mathscr D_0\}.
\]
If $\mathcal E_{s,t}$ extends continuously from $\mathscr G_{s,t}^0$ to its
closure in $\mathcal L_{\cP}^2$, with values in
$\mathcal L_{\cP}^2$, and these extensions preserve the exact tower on their
common closed seam domains, then the seam identity
\eqref{eq:backward-response-law} passes to the limit and remains
consistent with that closed deterministic tower.

Let
\[
 \mathscr S_{\rm sol}
 :=\overline{\Phi_{\rm bw}(\overline{\mathscr D_0})}
 ^{\,\mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}}.
\]
Assume in addition that this completed solver range is invariant under the
first-jet truncations.
If the equivalent conditions of
\Cref{prop:nonlinear-solver-range-compression} hold on
$\mathscr S_{\rm sol}$, then the completed solution map admits the value-only
realization
\[
 \Phi_{\rm bw}(d)
 =\bigl(Y^d,\mathcal Z_{\rm sol}(Y^d)\bigr).
\]
Only when the solver range is a closed linear relation does this reduce to the
vertical-space and closed-value-domain criterion of
\Cref{thm:backward-compression-retention}.

[Proposition 4 (Positivity implies a genuine measure) of arXiv:2604.20634, 'Distributional Statistical Models:\\ \large Weak Moments, Cumulants, and a Central Limit T'] Let $(T,\varphi)$ be a generalised probability measure with
$\varphi(x)>0$ for all~$x$.  Then the distributional product
$T\varphi\in\mathcal{S}'(\R)$ is a positive Radon measure: there
exists a unique positive Borel measure~$\mu$ on~$\R$ with
$\langle T,\psi\varphi\rangle = \int\psi\,d\mu$ for all
$\psi\in\mathcal{A}_\varphi$.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2506.22040, '\vspace{-3em} Khinchin inequalities for uniforms on spheres with a deficit'] Let $p \geq 2$. For $a \in \R, v \in \R^d$, $d \geq 2$, we have
\[ 
D_p(a, v) \geq \kappa_{p,d}a^4\cdot\begin{cases}
(|v|^2+2a^2)^{\frac{p-4}{2}}, & 2 \leq p \leq 4, \\
|v|^{p-4}, & p > 4,
\end{cases}
 \]
where 
\[
\kappa_{p,d} = \frac{p(p-2)(p+d-2)(p+d-4)}{4d^2(d+2)}.
\]

[Definition 36 (Homotopy pro-groups) of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \((X,x_0)\) be a pointed compact metric space embedded in an absolute
neighborhood retract \(P\). Let
\(V_1\supset V_2\supset V_3\supset\cdots\supset X\)
be a nested cofinal sequence of open neighborhoods of \(X\) in \(P\). For
\(q\ge 1\), the inclusions \(V_j\hookrightarrow V_i\), \(j\ge i\), induce
homomorphisms
\(p_{ij}\colon\pi_q(V_j,x_0)\to \pi_q(V_i,x_0)\).
The \(q\)-th homotopy pro-group of \((X,x_0)\), denoted
$\operatorname{pro}\text{-}\pi_q(X,x_0),$
is the inverse system
$\bigl\{\pi_q(V_i,x_0),p_{ij}\bigr\}_{j\ge i},$
viewed as an object of the pro-category \(\operatorname{pro}\text{-}\mathbf{Grp}\).
title: Homotopy pro-groups

[Thm 40 (Corollary 1.12 of \cite{St83}) of arXiv:2609.00758, 'Deformations of Compact Calabi--Yau and Fano Varieties with Isolated Singularities'] Let $X$ be a complex $n$-fold, $x\in X$ an isolated singularity and $f:(Y,E)\to(X,x)$ a good resolution. Then for integers $p<n$ and $q>n$ there are exact sequences
\[\begin{split}
0\to H^p(Y,Y\-E;\C)\to H^p(E,\C)\to H^{p+1}(X,X\-\{x\};\C)\to 0,\\ 0\to H^q(X,X\-\{x\};\C)\to H^q(Y,Y\-E;\C)\to H^q(E,\C)\to 0
\end{split}\]
consisting of the morphisms of mixed Hodge structures. Also the map $H^n(Y,Y\-E;\C)\to H^n(E,\C)$ is an isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures. \qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let R be a unique factorization domain with fraction field K. The product of two primitive polynomials in R[x] is primitive; consequently, every primitive polynomial of positive degree is reducible in R[x] if and only if it is reducible in K[x], and R[x] is itself a unique factorization domain.
R is a unique factorization domain
K is the fraction field of R

Thus a product of primitive polynomials is primitive and c(fg) is associated to c(f)c(g). body:
Symmetric form: let A_1, ..., A_n be events in a probability space, each with P(A_i) <= p, and suppose each A_i is mutually independent of all but at most d of the other events. If e p (d + 1) <= 1 (e the base of natural logarithms), then P(none of the A_i occurs) > 0. General form: if there are numbers x_1, ..., x_n in [0, 1) with P(A_i) <= x_i prod_{j in Gamma(i)} (1 - x_j) for every i, where Gamma(i) is the set of events A_i is not mutually independent of, then P(intersection of the complements) >= prod_i (1 - x_i) > 0.
mutual independence from the events outside the dependency neighbourhood, not merely pairwise independence
e p (d + 1) <= 1 in the symmetric form; the constant e cannot be improved in general

[Proposition prop:LocalUD of arXiv:2509.04155, 'An Approach to Sub-Gaussian Heat Kernel Estimates via Analysis on Metric Spaces'] Let $1 \leq p \leq q$, $(\mathcal{F}_p,\Gamma_p,\Psi)$ be a $p$-energy structure and $\nu$ be a Borel measure of $X$.
    Assume that the pair $x_0 \in X$ and $R_0 \in (0,\diam(X))$ satisfies the following condition. There are constants $L_0\geq 1$ and $\delta > 0$ such that the inequality
    \begin{equation}
        \nu(B(x,r))^{\frac{1}{q}} \leq L_0 \left(\frac{r}{R_0}\right)^{\delta}\left(\frac{\mu(B(x,r))}{\Psi(x,r)}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}
    \end{equation}
    holds for all $x \in X$ and $r > 0$ satisfying
    \[
        B(x,r) \cap B(x_0,R_0) \neq \emptyset \text{ and }0 < r \leq R_0.
    \]
    Then there are constants $C,\sigma \geq 1$ such that for all $f \in \mathcal{F}_p$,
    \[
        \left(\int_{B(x_0,R_0)} \abs{\tilde{f} - f_{B(x_0,R_0)}}^{q} \, d\nu \right)^{\frac{1}{q}} \leq C L_0 \left(\int_{B(x_0,\sigma R_0)} d\Gamma_p\Span{f} \right)^{\frac{1}{p}}.
    \]
    This result is quantitative in the sense that $C$ and $\sigma$ depend only on the constants in (eq:PI of the paper), (equation eq:muDoubling of the paper), (equation eq:RadDiam of the paper), the constant associated to $\Psi$ in (equation eq:Psi of the paper), $\delta, \, p$ and $q$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2609.01333, '2609.01333'] The mapping $\cF_0: \mathcal{B}_\delta \to C^{0,\alpha}$ is Fr\'echet $C^\infty$. Moreover, for $\varphi\in  \mathcal{B}_\delta$, the first derivative the linear map  $D\cF_0(\varphi) : C^{2,\alpha}(\R )\to C^{0,\alpha}(\R)$  is given

$$D\cF(\varphi)(w)= L_\varphi(w)  =-\frac{w''}{(1+\varphi'^2)^{3/2}} + \frac{3\varphi''\varphi'w'}{(1+\varphi'^2)^{5/2}} -\frac{\varphi'w'}{\varphi (1+\varphi'^2)^{3/2}} -\frac{w}{\varphi^2(1+\varphi'^2)^{1/2}},$$
while the  Hessian $D^2\cF_0(\varphi):C^{2,\alpha}(\R )\times C^{2,\alpha}(\R )\to C^{0,\alpha}(\R) $ is  given by polarization
\begin{align*}
D^2\cF_0(\varphi)(w,v) =
\left(B_\varphi(w+v,w+v) -B_\varphi(w,w)-B_\varphi(v,v)
\right).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Owner campaign draft, proof (unaudited); no independent audit or novelty assessment. Let d>=5, n>=1, 0<r<=1, h>=0, P0=P on R^d, and M=integral |x-c|^q P(dx)<infinity for fixed c and q>2d/(d-2). Each round draws n conditionally iid centers from rP+(1-r)Pt, with fresh real draws, and Pt+1 is their equal-weight isotropic Gaussian KDE of covariance h^2 I_d. Put z=2^(d/2-2), B=z/(z-1)+8/3, G=1+4/[1-2^(2-q(1-2/d))]. Then sup_t E W2^2(Pt,P) <= [16d B G M^(2/q)n^(-2/d)+2d h^2]/r, including M=0. The same bound holds for independently sampled weighted n+n groups, Pt+1=(r Phat_n+(1-r)Pt_hat_n)*N(0,h^2 I_d), and for exactly m fresh of n total points when r=m/n. The method labels every center by its fresh real-data ancestor. For every cell A, E Lt(A)=P(A) and Var Lt(A)<=P(A)/(n alpha), alpha=1-(1-1/n)(1-r)^2; Gaussian displacement has expected coupling cost at most d h^2/r. An annular dyadic transport bound transfers these dependent-label estimates into the displayed W2 bound. Gaussian increments must be centered, independent, and parent selection must use the KDE weights; real data must be fresh, not a fixed reused dataset. Proofs: C004 v2 and C005 v2, T356/proofs/review/. Classical dyadic architecture is credited to Fournier and Guillin, arXiv:1312.2128v1, Lemmas 5-6 and proof of Theorem 1.
