[Corollary 27 of arXiv:2608.30059, 'Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations'] For the fixed admissible gauge \(\tau\), with
\(C_\star=(1,2]^q\) and \(d_\alpha=m_\alpha(C_\star)\), set  
\begin{equation}

s_\tau
:=
\varsigma_\tau(\Sigma_\tau)
=
\frac{1}{d_\alpha}
\int_{\{\tau\in C_\star\}}
\chi_\alpha(\tau(x))\,\nu(dx)
=
\frac{\nu\{\tau\in C_\star\}}
{\vartheta_\alpha(C_\star)}
\in(0,\infty].
\end{equation}
Every stochastic representer \(Z\) of \(\nu\) satisfies
\[
\E{\chi_\alpha(R_Z)}=s_\tau.
\]
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm(i)]
\item
Some stochastic representer \(Z\) has \(R_Z\perp Y_Z\).

\item
\(s_\tau<\infty\).

\item
\(\nu\{\tau\in C_\star\}<\infty\).
\end{enumerate}

If \(s_\tau<\infty\), put
\[
\bar\alpha:=\sum_{i=1}^q\alpha_i,
\qquad
a_\tau:=s_\tau^{1/\bar\alpha}\boldsymbol1 
\]
and  for any stochastic representer \(Z\)  define
\begin{equation}

\frac{d\mathbb P_Z^\tau}{d\mathbb P}
:=
\frac{\chi_\alpha(R_Z)}{s_\tau},
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}

Z_\tau^\circ
:=
S_{a_\tau}Y_Z
=
S_{a_\tau R_Z^{-1}}Z.
\end{equation}
Under \(\mathbb P_Z^\tau\),
\[
Y_Z\sim\frac{\varsigma_\tau}{s_\tau},
\qquad
\tau(Z_\tau^\circ)=a_\tau,
\qquad
\nu_{Z_\tau^\circ}=\nu,
\]
and
\[
\mathcal L(Z_\tau^\circ)
=
(S_{a_\tau})_\#
\left(\frac{\varsigma_\tau}{s_\tau}\right).
\]
Consequently, every stochastic representer \(W\) satisfying
\(\tau(W)=a_\tau\) almost surely has this law.

Finally, for \(Z\) concentrated on \(E_\tau\) with \(R_Z\perp Y_Z\),
\[
\nu_Z=\nu
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
Y_Z\sim\frac{\varsigma_\tau}{s_\tau}
\ \text{ and }\
\E{\chi_\alpha(R_Z)}=s_\tau.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 35 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $j,\ell\in[3]$ with $j\neq\ell$. Recall the functions $m_1,m_2,m_3$ from \eqref{e:freeprob.m.z}, \eqref{e:freeprob.m2.z}, and \eqref{e:freeprob.m3.z}; and let $s_\ell$ denote the inverse of $m_\ell$. For any $z>0$, we have the bounds
    \[
        \iota z^{j/\ell} 
        \le m_j(s_\ell(z))
        \le \bigg(\frac{z}{\iota}\bigg
            )^{j/\ell}\,.
    \]

\begin{proof}
From the definitions \eqref{e:freeprob.m.z}--\eqref{e:freeprob.m3.z}, 
for each $\ell\in[3]$ and for any $z>\hw_1$ we have
    \[
    \frac{\mu_1}{(z-\hw_1)^\ell}
    \le m_\ell(z)=\sum_{j=1}^s
    \frac{\mu_j}{(z-\hw_j)^\ell}
    \le \frac{1}{(z-\hw_1)^\ell}\,.
    \]
Thus, for $t_- = \hw_1 + (\mu_1/z)^{1/\ell}$ and $t_+ = \hw_1 + z^{-1/\ell}$, we have
    \[
        m_\ell(t_+) 
        \le \frac{1}{(t_+ - \hw_1)^\ell}
        = z 
        = \frac{\mu_1}{(t_- - \hw_1)^\ell}
        \le m_\ell(t_-)\,.
    \]
    Since $m_\ell$ is strictly decreasing, this implies $t_- \le s_\ell (z) \le t_+$. Then, since $m_j$ is also strictly decreasing, it follows that
    \[
        \mu_1 z^{j/\ell}
        = \frac{\mu_1}{(t_+ - \hw_1)^j}
        \le m_j(t_+)
        \le m_j(s_\ell (z))
        \le m_j(t_-)
        \le \frac{1}{(t_- - \hw_1)^j}
        = (z/\mu_1)^{j/\ell}\,.
    \]
The conclusion follows by recalling that $\mu_1 \ge \iota$ because $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 35 of arXiv:2608.29416

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare the short cycle structure of Z^d and the hypercube to predict the first differing coefficient. Result: The coefficients a_i are determined by the counts of closed non-backtracking walks of length up to 2i in the graph (the lace-expansion diagrams at order i involve random-walk loops of length up to 2i, up to the normalisation by (2d)^i). Z^d and the hypercube both have degree 2d (resp. d, with the appropriate rescaling) and both have girth 4; the number of 4-cycles through a vertex is d(d-1)/2 ... for Z^d: choose two distinct directions, 4 sign patterns give (2d)(2d-2)/2 cycles; for the hypercube choose two coordinates: d(d-1)/2 cycles; after the normalisation by degree these agree to leading order, which is why a_2 agrees. 6-cycles: in Z^d a 6-cycle uses three directions (counts (2d)(2d-2)(2d-4)/...), or two directions with a back-and-forth (which is backtracking-free? a 6-cycle in two directions like ++-+-- exists in Z^2: no, in Z^2 6-cycles do not exist since the square lattice is bipartite with girth 4 and 6-cycles would need ... Z^2 has cycles of length 6? A closed walk of length 6 that is a simple cycle in Z^2 encloses 2 squares: yes, the 2x1 rectangle has perimeter 6. In the hypercube a simple 6-cycle uses exactly three coordinates (a 6-cycle in Q_3 exists); in Z^d a 6-cycle can use two directions (the 2x1 rectangle) or three. The hypercube has no 2x1 rectangle analogue (in Q_d, two coordinates span a 4-cycle only). So the 6-cycle counts differ at relative order 1/d^2: Z^d has extra 6-cycles using only two directions, of number of order d^2 versus the three-direction ones of order d^3; the 1/d^2-relative difference in the 6-cycle count enters the coefficient at order (2d)^{-3} x (1/d^2)... The source says a_3 agrees, consistent with the two-direction 6-cycles being of lower order; they enter at order 1/d beyond a_3's leading diagrams, i.e. at a_4 or a_5. Prediction: the first differing coefficient is a_4 (from the 2x1-rectangle 6-cycles, absent in the hypercube), unless their contribution cancels, in which case a_5. This is a heuristic prediction, not a proof; the source's hint that the proofs in [173, 174] suggest a difference at some i >= 4 is consistent. Key identity: The 2x1-rectangle 6-cycles exist in Z^d but not in the hypercube; their normalised count is one order in 1/d below the three-direction 6-cycles, predicting the first discrepancy at a_4. Obstruction: Not proved; requires the fourth-order lace diagrams on both graphs.

[Theorem 8 (Nekrasov equation) of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] For the discrete ensemble \eqref{eq_Hahn_cut_2}, the function
\begin{equation}
  R(z)= \Phi^-(z)
  \cdot \E\left[ \prod_{i=1}^N
  \bigg(1-\frac{1}{\N z-\ell_i+\frac{1}{2}} \bigg)
   \right]
  +
  \Phi^+(z)
    \cdot \E \left[ \prod_{i=1}^N
  \bigg(1+\frac{1}{\N z-\ell_i-\frac{1}{2}} \bigg)
   \right]
\end{equation}
is holomorphic on the complex plane, \textit{i.e.} it has no poles. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 (Poisson-regime profiles) of arXiv:2604.09933, 'Explicit cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles'] Fix \(p\ge1\) and \(c\in\R\). Assume \eqref{eq:intro-Poisson-assump}. Then
\[
\|M_n-U\|_{\TV}\longrightarrow f_p(c),
\qquad
\sep(M_n,U)\longrightarrow s_p(c).
\]
If in addition there exists \(B\ge1\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and all \(u\ge0\),
\[
0\le \mu_n(n-u)\,u!\,p^u\le B^u,
\]
then, for every \(1\le q<\infty\),
\[
\left\|\frac{M_n(\cdot)}{U(\cdot)}-1\right\|_{L^q(U)}^q
\longrightarrow H_{q,p}(c),
\qquad
D(M_n\|U)\longrightarrow h_p(c).
\]
In particular,
\[
\chi^2(M_n,U)\longrightarrow H_{2,p}(c)=g_p(c).
\]
Assume further, in the case \(r<1\), that there exists a summable \((b_u)_{u\ge0}\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and all \(u\ge0\),
\[
0\le \mu_n(n-u)\,u!\,p^u\le b_u.
\]
Then, with convergence understood in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\),
\[
\left\|\frac{M_n(\cdot)}{U(\cdot)}-1\right\|_{L^\infty(U)}
\longrightarrow H_{\infty,p}(c).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 10 of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Let $\lambda_0$ belong to a compact subinterval of
$(\lambda_{1,\Omega},\lambda^*)$ for the branch $u_\lambda^-$, or of
$(-\infty,\lambda^*)$ for the branch $u_\lambda^+$. Then there exist
$\delta>0$ and
$r_i^\pm(\lambda,\lambda_0)=o(|\lambda-\lambda_0|)$, $i=1,2$, such that,
whenever $0<\lambda-\lambda_0<\delta$,
\begin{align}
	-\frac{\lambda-\lambda_0}{2}\|u_\lambda^-\|_2^2+r_1^-(\lambda,\lambda_0)
	&\leq E_\lambda(u_\lambda^-)-E_{\lambda_0}(u_{\lambda_0}^-)
	\notag\\
	&\leq -\frac{\lambda-\lambda_0}{2}\|u_{\lambda_0}^-\|_2^2
	+r_2^-(\lambda,\lambda_0).
	
\end{align}
and
\begin{align}
	-\frac{\lambda-\lambda_0}{2}\|u_\lambda^+\|_2^2+r_1^+(\lambda,\lambda_0)
	&\leq E_\lambda(u_\lambda^+)-E_{\lambda_0}(u_{\lambda_0}^+)
	\notag\\
	&\leq -\frac{\lambda-\lambda_0}{2}\|u_{\lambda_0}^+\|_2^2
	+r_2^+(\lambda,\lambda_0).
	
\end{align}
Moreover, for every fixed
$\lambda_0\in(\lambda_{1,\Omega},\lambda^*)$, there exist
$\delta,c_0,C_0>0$ such that, whenever $|\lambda-\lambda_0|<\delta$,
\[
|H_\lambda(u_\lambda^-)|\geq c_0,
\qquad
\|u_\lambda^-\|\leq C_0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 49 (exceptional comparison) of arXiv:2609.03593, '\textbf{New Homogeneous Einstein Metrics from Detection}'] For each of
\[
 E_6^3/\Delta\Sp(4),\qquad
 E_7^3/\Delta\SU(8),\qquad
 E_8^3/\Delta\SO(16),
\]
the two asymmetriv Einstein metrics are pairwise non-homothetic and
non-isometric.  Neither is a product metric or naturally reductive, and no
larger connected naturally reductive presentation exists.  The cited
two-factor aligned and $H\times H/\Delta K$ classification theorems do not
classify these three-factor homogeneous pairs.  To the best of our knowledge, none of the six asymmetric Einstein metrics
occurs in the classifications cited above. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:mucs of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] We define the following family of measures.
 For $c \in [0,q^{-1})$ and $r_c \le s < q^{-1}$, let $\mu_{c,s}$ denote the law of the following function $f:\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$: 
\[
f(k) = S_2(k) + \Bigl(\max_{\ell \in \llbracket 1,k \rrbracket} [S_1(\ell) - S_2(\ell - 1)] - Y\Bigr)^+,
 \]
where $S_1$ is a $\operatorname{Geo}(qs)$ random walk, $S_2$ is a $\operatorname{Geo}\bigl(qs^{-1}\bigr)$ random walk, and $Y \sim \operatorname{Geo}\bigl(cs^{-1}\bigr)$ (a single geometric random variable). Here, we use the notation $x^+$ to denote $x \vee 0$.

body: [Proposition 5 (Characterization of an admissible process by its driver) of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] Let $\lambda_0$ be an admissible capacity on an interval $I$, let $g_0$ be a stretching morphism from $\lambda_0$ to the constant capacity $1$ on $\R$, and let $x_0\in \overline I$. Let $(D_t)_{0\leq t < T(D)}$ be an admissible driver. Then, there exists a unique process $(X_t)_{0\leq t < T(D)}$ (defined up to time-change) admissible at $x_0$ for the capacity $\lambda_0$ on $I$ such that $(D_t)_{0\leq t < T(D)}$ is the driver of the process $X$ for the target $x_0$ and initial uniformization $g_0$.

[Definition 11 (Thin quantum disk) of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] For $W\in(0, \frac{\gamma^2}{2})$, the infinite measure $\mathcal{M}_{2}^{\textup{disk}}(W)$ is defined as follows. Then sample a Poisson point process $\{(u, \mathcal{D}_u)\}$ with intensity $\mathds{1}_{t\in [0,T]}dt\times \mathcal{M}_{2}^{\textup{disk}}(\gamma^2-W)$. Finally consider the ordered (according to the order induced by $u$) collection of doubly-marked thick quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u\}$, called a \emph{thin quantum disk} of weight $W$.
		
		Let $\mathcal{M}_{2}^{\textup{disk}}(W)$ be the law of this ordered collection of doubly-marked quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u\}$.
		The left (resp.\ right) boundary length of a sample from $\mathcal{M}_{2}^{\textup{disk}}(W)$ is defined to be the sum of the left (resp.\ right) boundary lengths of the quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u\}$. A surface sampled from $\mathcal{M}_{2}^{\textup{disk}}(W)$ has two marked points; see Figure~\ref{fig-qt} (left).
title: Thin quantum disk

STATEMENT
Let 0<b<sqrt(d)<1 and rho>0. Consider a bounded full orbit indexed
by all integers of the raw scalar Adam map

 M_next=b*M+(1-b)*X,
 V_next=d*V+(1-d)*X^2,
 X_next=X-M_next/(sqrt(V_next)+rho), V>=0.

Put D=(1-b)/(2*(1+b)), a=D-rho, and assume 0<rho<D.
Suppose at EVERY integer time

 X_t^2 * [1/(sqrt(V_(t+1))+rho)-1/D] = 0.       (ZW)

Then the full orbit is either the origin, or the exact alternating
cycle (X,M,V)=(+/-a,-/+(1-b)/(1+b)*a,a^2).
No assumption that X stays nonzero, that curvature itself converges,
or that a cycle is hyperbolic is required. This is a zero-work path
classification, stronger than merely classifying constant-curvature
orbits; it is not a claim about all unrestricted Adam orbits.

HARDEST STEP
Exclude isolated exact position zeros on a full zero-work path. The
variance recurrence restricts nonzero amplitudes to two values, while
the momentum recurrence contracts across an isolated zero.

PROOF
If X_t=X_(t+1)=0, the position update gives M_(t+1)=0 and then M_t=0.
The inverse position update gives X_(t-1)=X_t+M_t/(sqrt(V_t)+rho)=0;
the inverse momentum update gives M_(t-1)=0. Repeating backwards and
forwards shows X=M=0 at all times. Then V_next=dV; boundedness at the
negative time end forces V=0. Hence a non-origin full path never has
two consecutive position zeros.

For any nonzero X_t, (ZW) gives V_(t+1)=a^2. If X_t=0, its predecessor
is nonzero, so V_t=a^2 and V_(t+1)=d*a^2. Consequently every variance
along a non-origin path is either a^2 or d*a^2. At any nonzero X_t,
the variance recurrence and V_(t+1)=a^2 imply

 |X_t|=a if X_(t-1)!=0,
 |X_t|=sqrt(1+d)*a if X_(t-1)=0.                 (1)

In particular all nonzero amplitudes are at most sqrt(1+d)*a<2a.

Suppose X_t and X_(t+1) are both nonzero. Their next denominators
are both D, |X_(t+1)|=a, and eliminating the momentum gives

 X_(t+2)=-(1+b)*X_(t+1)-b*X_t.                  (2)

If X_(t+2)=0, then |X_t|=(1+b)*a/b>2a, contradicting (1).
Otherwise |X_(t+2)|=a. If its sign equals that of X_(t+1), (2) requires
|X_t|=(2+b)*a/b>3a, also impossible. Therefore
X_(t+2)=-X_(t+1) and X_t=-X_(t+1). At time t+1 the complete state is

 (X_(t+1),M_(t+1),V_(t+1))
 = (X_(t+1),-2D*X_(t+1),a^2).

This is an exact cycle state. The raw map is injective on physical
states with rho>0: recover X_old=X_new+M_new/(sqrt(V_new)+rho),
then M_old=(M_new-(1-b)*X_old)/b and
V_old=(V_new-(1-d)*X_old^2)/d. Thus the FULL path is that cycle.

The remaining possibility is strict alternation between a nonzero
position and a zero position. Every nonzero amplitude is then the
same number sqrt(1+d)*a by (1). But at a nonzero time t followed by
X_(t+1)=0, the momentum and variance updates give

 X_(t+2)=-k*X_t, k=b*D/(sqrt(d)*a+rho)
                  <=b/sqrt(d)<1,              (3)

because sqrt(d)*a+rho>=sqrt(d)*(a+rho)=sqrt(d)*D.
This contradicts equality of the two nonzero amplitudes. The origin
and exact cycle are therefore the only bounded full (ZW) paths.

paper is invoked. Algebra (2) uses (1-b)/D=2(1+b). Argument (3) is
where b<sqrt(d) is needed. Both time ends and boundedness are essential

[Theorem thm:contiCZ of arXiv:2504.18739, 'discrete analogues of second-order Riesz transforms'] Define the kernels
\begin{align} 
   & \mathbf{K}^{(jk)}(x) = \mathcal{K}^{(jk)}(x)\mathds{1}_{\{|x|\ge 1\}} - K^{(jk)}(x)\mathds{1}_{\{|x|<1\}}\\
    &=-\left(\int_0^{\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}H_s(z)\frac{\partial}{\partial z_j} \left(\frac{P_s(z)}{H_s(z)}\right)\frac{\partial}{\partial z_k} \left(\frac{P_s(z-x)}{H_s(z)}\right)\,dz\,ds\right) \mathds{1}_{\{|x|\ge 1\}}\nonumber\\
    &-c_d \frac{x_j x_k}{|x|^{d+2}}\mathds{1}_{\{|x|<1\}}\nonumber
\end{align} 
These give Calder\'on-Zygmund operators $\mathbf{R}^{(jk)}:L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)\to L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with discrete analogues $\mathcal{R}^{(jk)}$. That is, 
\[
    \mathbf{R}^{(jk)}(f)(x) = \mathbf{K}^{(jk)}\ast f(x),
\]
where $\mathbf{K}^{(jk)}$ are Calder\'on-Zygmund kernels satisfying (equation ConCalZyg1 of the paper) and 
\[
    \mathcal{R}^{(jk)}(f)(n) = \sum_{m} \mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{dis}}^{(jk)}(m)f(n-m),\quad 
    \mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{dis}}^{(jk)}(m)=\mathbf{K}^{(jk)}(m)\mathds{1}_{\mathbb{Z}^d\setminus\{0\}}(m).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.02427, 'Ampleness in the Farey graph'] Let $A=\acl(\bar a)$ and $B=\acl(\bar b)$ be algebraically closed
subsets of a connected component of $\mathbb{M}\models Th(FG)$, with $A\cap B\neq \emptyset$. Then $\indep{A}{A\cap B}{B}$.

Moreover, for any $x\in\mathbb{M}$
\[
\depen{x}{A\cap B}{A}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\indep{x}{A\cap B}{B}.
\]

body:
Let G be a finite undirected graph with k>=3 distinct terminals. Its edges are independently open with probabilities in [0,1]. If the terminal partition is all separated with positive probability and all connected with positive probability, then some strictly intermediate terminal partition has positive probability. If its m optional-edge probabilities lie in [epsilon,1-epsilon], 0<epsilon<=1/2, its partition law has total-variation distance at least min(q,1-q,epsilon^m) from the selector law assigning probability q to all connected and 1-q to all separated, for 0<q<1.
Finite undirected graph; k>=3 distinct terminals.
Independent Bernoulli edge states.
Quantitative bound additionally assumes all m optional probabilities in [epsilon,1-epsilon].
No conclusion uniform in growing m.

[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] Let $Z$ be a locally finite random signed measure on $\sC$ (as
  defined in \eqref{eq:sCK}). Then
  \begin{equation}
    
    \Phi(K)=Z(\{F\in\sC\colon K\cap F\neq\emptyset\}),\quad K\in\Kd,
  \end{equation}
  is a $\sigma$-continuous random valuation. 
  Furthermore, $\Phi$ is a.s.~non-negative if $Z$ is
  a.s.~non-negative. In this case, $\Phi$ is necessarily monotone.

body:
[Theorem thm:universality of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] Let $\Sigma$ be a compact connected oriented Riemannian surface, possibly with boundary, endowed with a smooth positive area density $\mathrm{vol}$, and fix a base point $o\in\operatorname{int}(\Sigma)$. Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group, let $({\mathbb{G}}_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a universally stable sequence of embedded topological maps on $\Sigma$ based at $o$, and let $(Q_t)_{t>0}$ be scaling-admissible with L\'evy symbol $\psi$. In the case with boundary, fix the same prescribed boundary conjugacy classes $\mathfrak t$ for the lattice models and for the limiting Markovian holonomy field.
\par Then the lattice partition function is strictly positive for all sufficiently large $n$. For those $n$, let $H_n$ be the holonomy process on ${\mathbb{G}}_n$ associated with the plaquette weights $(Q_t)_{t>0}$ and boundary data $\mathfrak t$ when present. Then $(H_n)$ converges regularly to the holonomy process $H^\psi$ on $\Sigma$ induced by the regular Markovian holonomy field associated with the L\'evy process of symbol $\psi$ and the same boundary data. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Universality of holonomy processes

body: [Theorem thm_unimodularity_FCP of arXiv:2607.04002, 'Collisions of random walks in unimodular random graphs: applications to the random geometr'] Let~$(G,\rho)$ be a unimodular random rooted graph with~$\mathbf E[ \deg(\rho) \cdot \sum_{n \ge 0} p_n(\rho,\rho) ] <  \infty$. Then~$G$ has the discrete and continuous finite collision property almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$$
\forall T\geq 0,\quad [\blacksquare_T(\gamma)]:=\int_0^{T}\iota_V\varphi_f^{t*}[\gamma] dt\ \in\ L^\infty(\Sigma,\mathbb{R}),
$$
and, for every $1\leq p<\infty$,
$$
\lim_{T\rightarrow+\infty}\left\|[\blacksquare_T(\gamma)]-[\blacktriangle(\gamma)]\right\|_{L^p}=0.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:full-leading-chaos-increment of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Assume \(((A1 of the paper))\)--\(((A4 of the paper))\), \(\alpha m<1\), and \(2d+\alpha m<1\). Let
\(H=1-d-\alpha m/2\). For every \(T<\infty\) there exist constants
\(C_T<\infty\) and \(\beta>1\) such that the following estimates hold.

First, uniformly in \(n\ge3\) and in every interval
\(I\subset\{1,\ldots,\lfloor Tn\rfloor+2\}\),
\[
    \operatorname{Var}\left(
        \frac{J_m}{m!}\sum_{u\in I}a_uH_m(X_u)
    \right)
    \le
    C_T A_n^2\left(\frac{|I|}{n}\right)^\beta .
\]
Second, uniformly in \(0\le s<t\le T\),
\(
    \operatorname{Var}\bigl(\mathcal S_{n,m}(t)-\mathcal S_{n,m}(s)\bigr)
    \le
    C_T A_n^2 |t-s|^\beta .
\)
Equivalently,
\(
    \left\|
        \widetilde F^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,t}
        -
        \widetilde F^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,s}
    \right\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^m)}^2
    \le C_T |t-s|^\beta .
\)

\begin{equation}
 \ker\mathcal O=\mathsf V^\circ,
 \qquad
 \mathsf V\subseteq\mathsf R\subseteq G.
 
\end{equation}
If every $T_e$ is injective, then $\mathsf V=\mathsf R$; hence full Rees
support is equivalent to $\mathsf R=G$.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.01098, 'Gaussian upper bounds for averaged heat semigroups on graphs'] Let $n,r_0,C>0$. Assume that,
for all $x,y\in X$ and $t\geq r^2\geq r_0^2$, we have
\[
\mathcal{P}_r(t,x,y)
 \leq 

C 
\frac{\left(1\vee S^{-2}\sqrt{\rho(B_x(r),B_y(r))^2S^2+t^2}-t\right)^{\frac{n}{2}}}{\sqrt[\frac{2q(t)}{q(t)-1}]{m(B_x(\sqrt t))m(B_y(\sqrt t))}}
 \euler^{-S^{-2}t\zeta(\rho(B_x(r),B_y(r))S/t)}
\]
and  that,
for all $x\in X$ and $r_0\leq r_1\leq r_2$, we have
\begin{equation*}
m(B_x(r_2))\leq C
\left(\frac{r_2}{r_1}\right)^{n} m(B_x(r_1)).
\end{equation*}
Then there is a constant $C'=C'(C,n)>0$ such that, for all $\varepsilon\in[0,1)$, $r\geq 1\vee r_0$, and $U\subset B(r)$ satisfying $m(U)\geq \varepsilon m(B(r))$, we have 
\[
\lambda(U)
\geq 
\frac{C'}{r^{2+\varepsilon}}
\left(
\frac{m(B(r))}{m(U)}\right)^{\frac{2}{N}} \left[1\wedge \frac{1}{m(B(r))}\right] ^{\frac{1}{C'q(r^2)}}
\]
 where 
\[
N(r)= n\cdot \frac{q(r^2)}{q(r^2)-1}+ \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\ln \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\cdot \frac{1}{\ln r}+\frac{1}{q(r^2)-1}\cdot \ln(1\vee m(B(r))).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm Jankins--Neumann~\cite{JankinsNeumann1985}, Naimi~\cite{Naimi1994} of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Suppose $M=(\text{Pair of pants})\times S^1$, with $\Phi$ the periodic flow in the $S^1$ direction. Then the Jankins--Neumann ziggurat $\mathcal{Z}(\Phi)$ is the subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$ cut out by the following inequality (combined with its sibling obtained by inverting all three coordinates):
for $(r_1,r_2,r_3)\in \mathcal{Z}(\Phi)$,
$$r_3 \leq \sup_{q\geq 1}  \frac{-p_1 - p_2 + 1}q,$$
where $p_1/q \leq r_1$ and $p_2/q \leq r_2$ are the best rational subapproximants of $r_1$ and $r_2$ with denominator $q$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:one-point-gaussian-regression of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Under the hypotheses and notation of
		Proposition~(prop:one-point-conditional-hessian of the paper), whenever
		\(m=\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(r,x)\), write
		\[
		u(r,m):=\partial_{xx}\Phi_\zeta(r,x)
		=\frac1{\partial_{mm}h_\zeta(r,m)}.
		\]
		Set \(e=\mathbf{m}/\sqrt{Nq}\), and let \(P\) be the orthogonal
		projection onto \(\mathbf{m}^\perp\). Define
		\[
		z_i
		:=
		\xi''(q)\left(
		\frac{b_i}{\xi'(q)}-\partial_m u(q,m_i)
		-2\zeta(\{0\})m_i
		\right).
		\]
		There exist a GOE matrix \(W_N\), with off-diagonal entries of
		variance \(N^{-1}\), and a standard Gaussian vector \(g_N\) in
		\(\mathbf{m}^\perp\), independent of \(W_N\), such that, under
		\(\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf{m},f_N}\) and relative to
		\(\mathbb R e\oplus\mathbf{m}^\perp\),
		\begin{equation}
			\nabla_-^2F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})
			=
			\begin{pmatrix}
				a_N&y_N^{\mathsf T}P\\
				Py_N&C_N
			\end{pmatrix}
			+o(1),
		\end{equation}
		where the error converges to zero in operator norm in probability,
		and
		\begin{equation}
			C_N
			=
			P\left(
			\sqrt{\xi''(q)}\,W_N
			-\operatorname{diag}\left(
			\frac1{u(q,m_i)}
			+\frac{\xi''(q)}N\sum_{j=1}^Nu(q,m_j)
			\right)_{i\le N}
			\right)P\big|_{\mathbf{m}^\perp},
		\end{equation}
		\[
		\begin{aligned}
			y_N={}&
			\frac1{\sqrt N}\left(
			-\frac{m_i}{\sqrt q\,u(q,m_i)}+\sqrt q\,z_i
			+\sqrt q\,\zeta(\{0\})\xi''(q)m_i
			\right)_{i\le N}\\
			&+\left(
			\frac{\xi''(q)+q\xi'''(q)-q\xi''(q)^2/\xi'(q)}N
			\right)^{1/2}g_N,
		\end{aligned}
		\]
		and
		\[
		\begin{aligned}
			a_N={}&
			-\frac1{Nq}\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{m_i^2}{u(q,m_i)}
			-\frac{\xi''(q)}N\sum_{i=1}^Nu(q,m_i)
			+\frac2N\sum_{i=1}^Nm_iz_i\\
			&+q\left(
			-\frac{\xi'''(q)}N\sum_{i=1}^Nu(q,m_i)
			+\zeta(\{0\})\xi''(q)
			-\frac{2\xi''(q)}N\sum_{i=1}^N\partial_q u(q,m_i)
			\right).
		\end{aligned}
		\]

[Theorem 16 (Mean) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The expectation of $T_{m,p}$ is
  \[
    \E T_{m,p} = m \sum_{\ell = 1}^m \frac{1}{\ell\left(1-p\right)^\ell}.
  \]
  This quantity increases in both $m$ and $p$. Moreover,
  each function $p \mapsto \E T_{m,p}$ is convex.
  \begin{proof}
    Simply take $\E T_{m,p} = M_{T_{m,p}}'(0) = -\Lambda'(0) \, \Lambda(0)^{-2}$.
    The two claims are trivial.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Cor joint distribution of corner of arXiv:2411.01104, 'Gaussian universality of $p$-adic random matrix products via corners'] Let $A\in\Mat_{n\times n}(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ be random with $\SN(A)=\mu^{(1)}$ fixed and distribution invariant under the action of $\GL_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)\times\GL_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)$ acting on the right and left. For every $1\le i\le n$, let $A^{(i)}$ be the submatrices of $A$, consisting of the last $n-i+1$ rows and all $n$ columns. Then the joint distribution of $(\SN(A^{(2)}),\ldots,\SN(A^{(n)}))$ has the form 
$$\mathbf{P}(\SN(A^{(2)})=\mu^{(2)},\ldots,\SN(A^{(n)})=\mu^{(n)})=\frac{P_{\mu^{(1)}/\mu^{(2)}}(1;t)\cdots P_{\mu^{(n-1)}/\mu^{(n)}}(t^{n-2};t)P_{\mu^{(n)}}(t^{n-1};t)}{P_{\mu^{(1)}}(1,t,\ldots,t^{n-1};t)}.$$

In particular, for all $2\le k\le n$, the distribution of $\SN(A^{(k)})$ has the form
$$\mathbf{P}(\SN(A^{(k)})=\mu^{(k)})=\frac{P_{\mu^{(1)}/\mu^{(k)}}(1,t,\ldots,t^{k-2};t)P_{\mu^{(k)}}(t^{k-1},t^k,\ldots,t^{n-1};t)}{P_{\mu^{(1)}}(1,t,\ldots,t^{n-1};t)}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2604.07207, 'Mixing times of step-reinforced random walks'] Under Assumption \ref{mainassum}, if $ \langle \Gamma \cdot \Gamma^{-1}  \rangle=G$, then there exist two positive constants $C=C(G,\mu)$ and $\rho=\rho(G,\mu)\in (0,1)$ such that for any $n\geq 1$, 
 $$
d_{\infty}(n) \leq C\rho^{(1-\alpha)n}.
 $$
 In particular, this holds in the following cases:
\begin{enumerate}[\bf (i)]
\item $\Gamma$ is symmetric, i.e., $\Gamma=\Gamma^{-1}$;
\item   $\Gamma$ is  a union of conjugacy classes of $G$, which contains case when $G$ is abelian.
\item  $e_G \in \Gamma$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm 2 of arXiv:2609.03185, 'Uniqueness of tangent flows in free boundary flow'] There exist constants $\beta_0=\beta_0(n)>0$ and $A=A(n)>0$ such that, for $\kappa$ sufficiently small, if
\[
\mathcal E_0\geq e^{-\frac{n\tau_0}{2}} \int_{M_{\tau_0}}\phi(x,\tau_0)\, d\mathcal H^n_{g_{\tau_0}}, \qquad \tau_0=-\log(\beta_0\kappa^2),
\]
then
\[
\tau\longmapsto e^{A e^{-\frac{\tau}{4}}} \int_{M_\tau} \Phi(x,\tau)\,d\mathcal H^n_{g_\tau} + A\mathcal E_0e^{-\tau}
\]
is decreasing on $[\tau_0,\infty)$.

Moreover, if $\partial M_\tau\subset S_\tau=S=\{x_{n+1}=0\}$ and the corresponding coordinates are Euclidean, so that $g_\tau = \delta$, then one may take $A=0$, and no $\mathcal E_0$ is needed. More precisely, for any fixed $T$,
\[
\frac{d}{d\tau} \int_{M_\tau} \Phi(x,T+\tau) \,d\mathcal H^n \leq -\int_{M_\tau} \left|H+\frac{x^\perp}{2}\right|^2 \Phi(x, T+\tau) \,d\mathcal H^n.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 2 of arXiv:2609.03185

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2604.11682, 'Semilocalization for inhomogeneous random graphs'] A \emph{path} $\gamma$ in a graph $G$ is a sequence of vertices
  $\gamma = (\gamma_{0}, \gamma_{1}, \ldots, \gamma_{l})$, with
  $\left\{ \gamma_{i-1}, \gamma_{i} \right\} \in G$ for $i\in[n]$. The length of the
  path is $l(\gamma) = l$. A path is said to be \emph{simple} if $\gamma_{i} \neq \gamma_{j}$
  for $i \neq j, \{i, j\} \neq \{0, l\}$.

  The set of paths $\gamma$ in $G$ satisfying $\gamma_0 = x$ and
  $\gamma_{l(\gamma)} = y$ is denoted by $\mathcal{P}_{xy}(G)$, and
  its subset of simple paths is denoted by $\mathcal{P}^{*}_{xy}(G)$.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2605.22445, 'Generalized specific entropy on Wiener space with application to Martingale Optimal Transp'] Given $\Sigma(t,x)  \in \mathbb S^d_{+}$, a probability measure \(\mathbb P\) on the c\`adl\`ag path space
\(D([0,1],\mathbb R^d)\), equipped with its Borel \(\sigma\)-algebra,
is said to solve the martingale problem for the time-dependent generator
\begin{equation}
\mathcal L_t\varphi(x)
=
\frac12 \tr\!\big(\Sigma(t,x)D^2\varphi(x)\big),
\qquad (t,x)\in[0,1]\times\mathbb R^d,
\end{equation}
with initial distribution \(\delta_{x_0}\) if, denoting by \((X_t)\) the canonical process,
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[{\rm (i)}] \((X_0)_{\#}\mathbb P=\delta_{x_0}\);
    \item[{\rm (ii)}] for every \(\varphi\in C_b^2(\mathbb R^d)\), the process
    \[
    M_t^\varphi
    :=
    \varphi(X_t)-\varphi(X_0)-\int_0^t \mathcal L_s\varphi(X_s)\,ds
    \]
    is a martingale.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2605.22445

[Thm 3 of arXiv:2609.00922, 'The Morse Index, Nullity and Jacobi Fields of Constant-Curvature 2-Spheres in Complex Proj'] Let $N\ge n\ge1$ be integers, let $k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$, and put
	$\lambda=n-2k$.  The normal component of the differential of the directrix
	construction descends at $d_0$ to an $\SU(2)$-equivariant real-linear
	isomorphism
	\[
	\mathfrak d_{k,N}:T_{d_0}\mathscr D_{n,N}
	\longrightarrow\ker J_{\lambda,n}^{N},
	\]
	where the tangent space is regarded as a real vector space.  Consequently,
	for every $V\in\ker J_{\lambda,n}^{N}$ there is a smooth family of minimal
	immersions $\psi_t:S^2\to\CP^N$, obtained by deforming the rational normal
	directrix, such that $\psi_0=\phi_{\lambda,n}^{N}$ and the normal component of
	its variational field at $t=0$ is $V$.  Thus every normal Jacobi field along
	$\phi_{\lambda,n}^{N}$ is integrable.
	
	When $\lambda=0$, the theorem concerns the full normal Jacobi kernel of the
	two-fold covering immersion on $S^2$.  The integrating families need not
	preserve the antipodal deck transformation and hence need not descend to the
	totally real projective image. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 25 (Asymptotics along $\Gamma_{x,\alpha}$ and $\Gamma_{y,\alpha}$ in the red arc region at $\alpha_0 = 0, \pi$) of arXiv:2512.09136, 'On the Green's functions and Martin boundary structure of a planar diffusion in a disconti'] Suppose $x^+_{max} < x^-_{max}$ and let $\alpha_0 = 0$. If $r = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$ and $\alpha = \alpha(a,b) \in (0,\pi)$ is the angle such that $\cos(\alpha) = \frac{a}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$ and $\sin(\alpha) = \frac{b}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$, then the following asymptotics hold:
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{2i\pi}\int_{\Gamma_{x,\alpha}} \phi^{z_0}(x) \frac{\gamma(x, Y^+(x), Z^+(x))}{\partial_y \gamma_+(x, Y^+(x))} e^{-a x - b Y^+(x)} \, dx 
+ \frac{1}{2i\pi} \int_{\Gamma_{y,\alpha}} \frac{e^{(a_0 - a) X^+(y) + (b_0 - b) y}}{\partial_x \gamma_+(X^+(y), y)} \, dy
\end{equation}
\[
\underset{r \to +\infty, \ \alpha \to 0, \ \alpha \geq 0}{\sim} 
C_0 f_0(z_0) \left( \kappa \alpha + \frac{1}{r} \right) \frac{e^{-r(\cos(\alpha) x(\alpha) + \sin(\alpha) y(\alpha))}}{\sqrt{r}},
\]
where $\kappa > 0$ is an explicit constant (see \eqref{eq:kappa}) and $f_0(z_0)$ is given by \eqref{f(z_0)col}. Furthermore, 
\[
\partial_\alpha \bigl(C(\alpha) h_\alpha(z_0)\bigr) \big|_{\alpha = 0} = \kappa C_0 f_0(z_0).
\]

If $x^+_{min} > x^-_{min}$, the symmetric result holds for $\alpha \to \pi$ with $\alpha \leq \pi$.
title: Asymptotics along $\Gamma_{x,\alpha}$ and $\Gamma_{y,\alpha}$ in the red arc region at $\alpha_0 = 0, \pi$

[Lemma lem:nemytskii_lipschitz of arXiv:2505.14012, 'Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations'] Assume that $f$ is Lipschitz continuous and that $\rho\in L^1(U)$. Then the associated Nemytskii operator $F$ is a nonlinear, bounded, Lipschitz continuous operator on $H=L^2(U,\rho)$ with
\[\|F(u)\|\le \sqrt{1+\zeta}\operatorname{Lip}(f)\|u\|+\sqrt{1+C(\zeta)}|f(0)|\|\rho\|_{L^1(U)}^{1/2},\]
for any $\zeta>0$ and some $C(\zeta)>0$,
and we have that $\operatorname{Lip}(F)=\operatorname{Lip}(f)$. If $\zeta=1$, then $C(\zeta)=1$.

[Proposition 5 (Local extinction on bounded-degree graphs) of arXiv:2609.00292, 'Extinction, Survival and Fluctuations for the Spatial Maki--Thompson Model on Infinite Gra'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be an infinite, connected
    graph of bounded degree, and consider the spatial Maki--Thompson rumor
    model on $G$ with transmission rate $\lambda>0$ and stifling rate
    $\alpha>0$, started from an arbitrary deterministic initial configuration
    \(
    \eta_{0}\in\{0,1,2\}^{V}.
    \)
    Then, for every finite set $K\subset V$, there exists an almost surely finite
    random time $\tau_{K}$ such that
    \[
        \eta_{t}(x)\ne1 \qquad \text{for every $x\in K$ and every
            $t\ge\tau_{K}$}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Local extinction on bounded-degree graphs

body:
[Corollary 29 (Careless uniform exponential tails and moments) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Let $Y_n:=\mu_nT_{n,p}$ in the fixed-$p$ careless collector started from the empty collection, where
\[
        \mu_n=\Pbb_{\nu_n}(K_0<n,K_1=n)
\]
is the stationary-entry flux into the post-loss completion state.  There are constants $C,c\in(0,\infty)$, depending only on $p$, such that
\[
        \Pbb(Y_n>x)\le C e^{-cx},
        \qquad x\ge0,
\]
for all sufficiently large $n$.  Consequently, for every fixed $r\ge1$,
\[
        \Ebb Y_n^r\longrightarrow \Ebb Z^r=r!,
        \qquad Z\sim\Exp(1).
\]
In particular,
\[
        \Ebb T_{n,p}\sim \frac{1}{\mu_n},\qquad
        \Var(T_{n,p})\sim \frac{1}{\mu_n^2}.
\]
Together with Theorem~\ref{thm:careless-sharp-constant}, this gives the explicit constant
\[
        \mu_n\sim \frac{1}{(q;q)_\infty}
        \frac{n!}{n^n}q^{n(n+1)/2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
        \Ebb T_{n,p}
        \sim (q;q)_\infty\frac{n^n}{n!}q^{-n(n+1)/2},
\]
and
\[
        \Var(T_{n,p})
        \sim (q;q)_\infty^2\left(\frac{n^n}{n!}\right)^2q^{-n(n+1)}.
\]

[Theorem 26 (Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski) of arXiv:2607.22441, 'The martingale representation theorem for cylindrical martingale valued measures'] Let $E$ be a compact metric space and let $\psi: E \times \widetilde{\Omega} \rightarrow \R$ be a mapping such that $\psi(x, \cdot)$ is measurable for arbitrary $x \in E$ and $\psi(\cdot, \widetilde{\omega})$ is a continuous mapping for arbitrary $\widetilde{\omega} \in \widetilde{\Omega}$. Then there exist an $E$-valued measurable function $X:\widetilde{\Omega} \rightarrow E $ such that 
$$ \psi(X(\widetilde{\omega}),\widetilde{\omega})=\sup_{x \in E} \psi(x,\widetilde{\omega}), \quad \widetilde{\omega} \in \widetilde{\Omega}.$$

[Theorem thm:that-implies-wladhausens-thm of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Let $M$ be irreducible and boundary irreducible. Let $f \colon M \to M$, with $f^{-1}(\partial M) = \partial M$, be a homotopy equivalence.  Then either
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item $f$ is properly homotopic to a homeomorphism $g \colon M \to M$; or
        \item $f$ is properly homotopic to $g$ with $g(M) \subseteq \partial M$, and $M$ is an interval bundle over $F$ for some surface $F$, i.e.~$M \cong F \times I$ or $M \cong F \widetilde{\times} I$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:that-implies-wladhausens-thm of arXiv:2609.00233

\]
Thus
\[
X^{(2)}(-1,3) + \mathcal{B}^{(2)}(0,3;x,4) \ge \mathcal{B}^{(2)}(0,2;x,4),
\]
which implies that
\[
X^{(2)}\mathcal{B}^{(2)}(-1,3;x,4)\ge X^{(2)}\mathcal{B}^{(2)}(0, 2;x,4).
\]

\begin{equation}

[Proposition Thm : bound of arXiv:2609.00105, 'Weighted composition operators and classification of weighted Hardy spaces'] Let $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2$ be as above.
    For $\varphi: X_1\to X_2$ and $\lambda:X_1\to \mathbb{C}$ the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\set{\lambda \cdot f\circ\varphi:f\in\mathcal{H}_2 }\subseteq \mathcal{H}_1$.
        \item $W_{\lambda,\varphi}:\mathcal{H}_2\to \mathcal{H}_1$ is a bounded operator. 
        \item there exists a constant $c\ge0$, such that $c^2K_1(x,y)-\overline{\lambda(y)}K_2(\varphi(x),\varphi(y))\lambda(x)$ is kernel function on $X_1$. 
    \end{enumerate}
    Moreover, in these cases, $\norm{W_{\lambda,\varphi}}$ is the least constant, $c$, satisfying the condition in (3).

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2605.12269, 'It\^o integral for a two-sided L\'evy process'] Let $p\geq 2$ be an even integer such that $m_p<\infty$. Let $\Phi=\{\Phi(t,x);t\geq 0,x\in \bR\}$ be a random field such that $(\omega,x,t) \mapsto \Phi(\omega,t,x)$ is $\cP \otimes \cB(\bR_{+})$-measurable, and
\[
\sup_{t\leq T} \sup_{x\in \bR} \bE|\Phi(t,x)|^p<\infty \quad \mbox{for any $T>0$}.
\]
Let $(t,x)\mapsto \cG_t(x)$ be a measurable function on $\bR_{+} \times \bR$ such that 
\begin{equation}

\nu_T:=\int_0^T \int_{\bR} |\cG_{t}^p(x)|dxdt<\infty \quad \mbox{for any $T>0$}.
\end{equation}
Then, for any $t>0$ and $x \in \bR$,
\[
\bE \left| \int_0^t \int_{\bR} \cG_{t-s}(x-y) \Phi(s,y) ds L(dy) \right|^p \leq B_{t,p}^p
\int_0^t \int_{\bR} \big(\cG_{t-s}^2(x-y)+\cG_{t-s}^p(x-y)\big) \bE|\Phi(s,y)|^p dyds,
\]
where 
\begin{equation}

B_{t,p}^p=2^{p-1}\cC_p^p \big(t^{p/2}\nu_t^{p/2-1} + t^{p-1} \big),
\end{equation} 
and $\cC_p$ is the constant from \eqref{IXp}.

body:
[Theorem thm:limits of arXiv:2411.16913, 'Entropies of the Poisson distribution as functions of intensity: ``normal'' and ``anomalou'] \begin{itemize}
    \item[$(a)$]  The Shannon, R\'enyi and both generalised R\'enyi entropies of the Poisson distribution, for all admissible values of the parameters, converge to infinity as $\lambda$ tends to infinity. Moreover, for $\lambda\to\infty$,
    \begin{align}
    \mathbf H_{SH}(\lambda)&\sim \frac{1}{2}\log(2\pi\lambda)+\frac12;\\
    \mathbf H_R(\alpha,\lambda)&\sim \frac{1}{2}\log(2\pi\lambda)+\frac{\log\alpha}{2(\alpha-1)};\\
    \mathbf H_{GR}(\alpha,\beta,\lambda)&\sim \frac{1}{2}\log(2\pi\lambda)+\frac{\log\beta-\log\alpha}{2(\beta-\alpha)}.
\end{align}
    \item [$(b)$]  The Tsallis entropy of the Poisson distribution converges to infinity, as $\lambda$ tends to infinity, only for $\alpha \in (0,1)$, more precisely, 
    \[
    \mathbf H_{T} (\alpha, \lambda)\sim \frac{1}{ \sqrt{\alpha}(1-\alpha)}(2\pi\lambda)^{\frac{1-\alpha}{2}}, \qquad\lambda\to\infty, \ \alpha\in(0,1),
    \]
    and
    \[
    \lim_{\lambda\to\infty} \mathbf H_{T} (\alpha, \lambda) =
    \dfrac{1}{\alpha - 1}, \qquad \alpha > 1.
    \]
    \item [$(c)$]  The Sharma--Mittal entropy of the Poisson distribution converges to infinity, as $\lambda$ tends to infinity, only for $\beta \in (0,1)$, more precisely,  
    \[
        \mathbf H_{SM} (\alpha,\beta, \lambda)\sim \frac{1}{(1-\beta)\alpha^{\frac{1-\beta}{2(1-\alpha)}}}(2\pi\lambda)^{\frac{1-\beta}{2}}, \qquad\lambda\to\infty, \ \beta\in(0,1),
    \]
    and
    \[
    \lim_{\lambda\to\infty} \mathbf H_{SM} (\alpha, \beta, \lambda) =
    \dfrac{1}{\beta - 1}, \qquad \beta > 1.
    \]
    \end{itemize}
title: Theorem thm:limits of arXiv:2411.16913

Let N>=2,1<=K<=N-1,and1<=t<=N be integers. Let H=Hyp(N,K,t) be the number of successes in t draws without replacement from a population of N containing K successes,and B=Bin(t,K/N). With the usual zero masses outside the hypergeometric support, sum_{w=0}^t |H(w)-B(w)|<=2*(t-1)/sqrt(N-(t-1)). Consequently,for the convention TV(P,Q)=(1/2)*sum_x|P(x)-Q(x)|, TV(H,B)<=(t-1)/sqrt(N-t+1). If t=1 the two laws coincide. Theorem1 is phrased in the regime K/N=p fixed in(0,1) as N tends to infinity;the displayed finite bound follows from its likelihood-ratio proof for each valid N,K,t. In particular,for fixed t and fixed p along integers K=p*N,the L1 distance tends to zero. This is a known source result,not a new convergence theorem.
Finite integers N>=2,1<=K<N,1<=t<=N;standard hypergeometric and binomial count laws.
Natural-log KL;L1 sum differs from total variation by a factor2.
The asymptotic corollary holds t fixed and p=K/N fixed in(0,1) along an integer sequence.

Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. With R_r the block conditional variances, put D_m = (-1)^(m+1) Delta^m R_0 for 1 <= m <= n, and let H_<m be the functions whose Hoeffding components of order m or more vanish. Then D_m = binom(n, m)^(-1) sum_{k=m}^n binom(k, m) W_k and D_m <= dist_2(f, H_<m)^2 <= binom(n, m) D_m; so D_m = 0 if and only if f lies in H_<m. With nonzero tail, the left inequality is an equality exactly when all the tail mass sits at order n, and the right one exactly when it sits at order m. The same holds with Q_r, the average over |A| = r of E[(f(X) - f(X^(A)))^2], since Q_r = 2 R_r: for m = 1 it reads Var(f) <= (1/2) sum_i E[(f(X) - f(X^(i)))^2].

body: [Lemma distribution_v_i of arXiv:2607.22480, 'Distinguishability threshold for random geometric graphs'] Let $1\leq s< i\leq n$. Then, conditional on the coordinates $\boldsymbol{v}_i(1), \dots, \boldsymbol{v}_i(s-1)$, the value $\boldsymbol{v}_i(s)/r_i(s)$ is distributed as the first coordinate of a uniform random point $\boldsymbol{y}$ on the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-s}\subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d-s+1}$, where $r_i(s)=\sqrt{1-\sum_{k=1}^{s-1} \boldsymbol{v}_i(k)^2}$ is the residual length of the vector $\boldsymbol{v}_i$ after coordinate $s$. In other words, the first $i-1$ coordinates of $\boldsymbol{v}_i$ follow the same distribution as the first $i-1$ coordinates of a uniform random point on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$.

body:
[Lemma boundedorthogonal of arXiv:2609.01885, 'The Order of the Non-universal Tree of a Hilbert Space with Respect to the Haar Basis'] Suppose that $(u_0,\ldots, u_{m-1})\in \textbf{T}(C)$ is a family of pairwise-orthogonal vectors. Set $A = \inf_{n<m}\{||u_n||\}$, $B = \sup_{n < m} \{||u_n||\}$, and $C' = \max\{C B, \frac{C}{A}\}$. Then $m \leq 2^{(C')^2-2}$. 

In particular, for every sting $s\in \textbf{T}(C)$ consisting of pairwise-orthogonal vectors, $|s|\leq 2^{C^4-2}$.
title: Lemma boundedorthogonal of arXiv:2609.01885

body: [Thm 32 of arXiv:2609.00758, 'Deformations of Compact Calabi--Yau and Fano Varieties with Isolated Singularities'] Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper flat morphism of complex spaces and $s\in S$ a point over which the fibre $X_s$ has isolated Du Bois singularities and its resolutions satisfy the the $\partial\db$ lemma. [Prop 33 of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Suppose that $Z_1,Z_2\in\Z_p[x]$, at least one of which is monic. If their
reductions
$\overline{Z}_1,\overline{Z}_2\in\F_p[x]$ are relatively prime, then
$$
\val\left(\Res(Z_1,Z_2)\right)=0.
$$

body:
[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2609.03993, 'The Endpoint Fractional Riesz Estimate on the Hamming Cube'] Let $(X_0,X_1)$ and $(Y_0,Y_1)$ be compatible Banach couples.  Suppose
		$S_z:X_0+X_1\to Y_0+Y_1$, $0\le\Re z\le1$, is a family of linear maps
		that is norm-continuous on the closed strip, analytic in the open strip,
		and bounded there in the sum-space operator norm:
		\[
		\sup_{0\le\Re z\le1}
		\|S_z\|_{X_0+X_1\to Y_0+Y_1}<\infty.
		\]
		Assume also that
		\[
		\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\|S_{it}\|_{X_0\to Y_0}\le M_0,
		\qquad
		\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\|S_{1+it}\|_{X_1\to Y_1}\le M_1.
		\]
		Then
		\begin{equation*}
			S_\theta:[X_0,X_1]_\theta\longrightarrow[Y_0,Y_1]_\theta,
			\qquad
			\|S_\theta\|\le M_0^{1-\theta}M_1^\theta.
		\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 127 (Identification with the common martingale integrand) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $Y\in\mathscr C_{\rm bw}^{1,2}$ and suppose that its martingale part is
represented, under every $P\in\cP$, by the modelwise projection of one common
upper-energy class $Z\in\mathbb H_{\cP}^2$ and its integral class $I(Z)$.
If the pathwise covariation
algorithm agrees modelwise with classical covariation, then
\begin{equation}
 [D_Q^{\rm pw}Y]_{\mathbb H_{\cP}^2}=Z.
\end{equation}
Thus on the martingale-representation branch of the backward interface, the
response-generated covariance jet coincides with the conventional stochastic
integrand.

body:
A multi-species stochastic population model X_t = (X_t^1, ..., X_t^d) is stochastically persistent in probability if for every epsilon > 0, there exists delta > 0 such that liminf_{t -> infinity} P(min_{1 <= i <= d} X_t^i >= delta) >= 1 - epsilon whenever min_{1 <= i <= d} X_0^i > 0 almost surely.
Initial state in the strictly positive orthant almost surely
title: Stochastic Persistence in Population Dynamics

body:
[Proposition 27 of arXiv:2608.10183, '2608.10183'] Fix a time-independent reinforcement environment $\eta$. Assume that, for
every $M\geq 2$, the frozen $M$-replica process admits an invariant probability
measure $\pi_M^\eta$ with the exponential integrability required below.
Assume moreover that $\pi_M^\eta$ is exchangeable with respect to
permutations of the replica labels.

Assume further that the Poisson Hypothesis holds.

Let
\begin{align*}
\beta_i
&:=
\mathbb E_\eta[X_i+z_i].
\end{align*}

Assume moreover that, as $M\to\infty$,
\begin{align*}
\beta_i^M
&\longrightarrow
\beta_i,
\\
\Lambda_i^{M,m,\eta}(u)
&\longrightarrow
\Lambda_i^\eta(u),
\\
\Theta_i^{M,m,\eta}(u,v)
&\longrightarrow
\Theta_i^\eta(u,v),
\end{align*}
for $u$ in a common open interval $I$ containing $0$.

Assume in addition that, for every compact set $K\subset I$, there exists
$\delta_K>0$ such that $u+2\delta_K\in I$ for every $u\in K$ and
\begin{align*}
\sup_{M\geq 2}
\sup_{u\in K}
\mathbb E_{\pi_M^\eta}
\left[
e^{(u+2\delta_K)(X_i^m+z_i)}
\right]
&<\infty.
\end{align*}

Then, for every $u\in I$,
\begin{align}
0
=&
-(1+a_i u)
\bigl(\Lambda_i^\eta\bigr)'(u)
+
a_i u z_i\Lambda_i^\eta(u)
+
\beta_i e^{u(r_i+z_i)}+
\\
\nonumber +
&\sum_{j\in\mathcal P_i}
\beta_j Q_i^\eta(+1)
\bigl(e^{u w_{ji}}-1\bigr)
\Lambda_i^\eta(u)
+
\sum_{j\in\mathcal P_i}
\beta_j Q_i^\eta(-1)
\left[
\Theta_i^\eta(u,v_{ji})
-
\Lambda_i^\eta(u)
\right].
\end{align}

Moreover,
\begin{align*}
\beta_i
&=
\bigl(\Lambda_i^\eta\bigr)'(0).
\end{align*}

If $r_i=0$, the contribution arising from the reset mechanism before
combination with the deterministic drift is
\begin{align*}
\beta_i e^{u z_i}
-
\bigl(\Lambda_i^\eta\bigr)'(u).
\end{align*}

 	\beqnn
 	\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\mathbf{P}\big(  |N_s-   s | \geq Kb(t)\big) + 	\sup_{0< s\leq t} \mathbf{E}\Big[\frac{N_s}{s}\cdot \mathbf{1}_{\{ |N_s- s| \geq Kb(t)\}}\Big]\leq \frac{C}{K} .
 	\eeqnn (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:rigidity of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Let the features span $\mathbb{R}^d$ and suppose $\tau(D)=k:=(m+1)d$. Let $c$ be a
spanning zero certificate with $|\operatorname{supp} c|=k$ and support $S$. Then $S$ splits
uniquely (up to permutation) into $d$ pairwise disjoint blocks
$S=C_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup C_d$ with $|C_j|=m+1$, where each $C_j$ supports a
positive circuit of the dyads whose features span a one-dimensional line
$U_j$, and $U_1,\dots,U_d$ are linearly independent.

body:
[Proposition prop:well_defined_functional of arXiv:2608.22044, 'Structured Learning on Mapper Representations'] Let
$
F:\widetilde{\mathcal R}\to\mathbb R
$
be a functional satisfying
$
F(\mathcal R_1)=F(\mathcal R_2)
\quad
\text{whenever }
\mathcal R_1\sim\mathcal R_2.
$
Then $F$ induces a well-defined functional
\[
\bar F:\mathcal R\to\mathbb R
\]
on the quotient representation space by
$
\bar F([\mathcal R])=F(\mathcal R).
$

body:
[Lemma lem:absorber of arXiv:2609.00889, 'Dominant-Degree Conditions for Ramsey--Tur\'an Factors of Non-Directed Cycle Orientations'] {[LoMarkstrom,CHWY2024]}
Let $H$ be a fixed oriented graph on $h\ge2$ vertices. For every $\eta,\beta>0$ and $t\in\mathbb N$ there are $\xi>0$ and $n_0$ such that the following holds. If $D$ is a digraph with $n\ge n_0$, and $V(D)$ is $(H,\beta n,t)$-closed, then there is a set $A\subseteq V(D)$ with $|A|\le\eta n$ such that, for any set $U\subseteq V(D)\setminus A$ with $|U|\le\xi n$ and $h\mid |A\cup U|$, the digraph $D[A\cup U]$ has an $H$-factor. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Absorbing lemma

body:
[Definition 21 (Multivariate Gaussian) of arXiv:2605.14630, '2605.14630'] For $N\geqs1$, let $\R^N$ be equipped with the $\sigma$-algebra $\cB$ of Borel
sets and Lebesgue measure $\6x$. Let $m\in\R^N$ and let $C\in\R^{N\times N}$ be 
a symmetric, positive definite matrix. 
A random variable $X:\R^N\to\R$ is a (multivariate) Gaussian random variable 
with mean $m$ and covariance matrix $C$ if its law is 
\begin{equation}
 
 \mu(\6x) = 
 \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{N/2}\det(C)^{1/2}} \e^{-\pscal{(x-m)}{C^{-1}(x-m)}/2} \6x\;.
\end{equation} 
In that case, we write $X \sim \cN(m, C)$.
title: Multivariate Gaussian

body: The characteristic function of a random variable X is phi_X(t) = E[e^{itX}] for t real (the Fourier transform of its distribution). It satisfies phi_X(0) = 1, |phi_X(t)| <= 1, and phi_X is uniformly continuous. It DETERMINES the distribution (uniqueness theorem: equal characteristic functions imply equal laws, via the Fourier inversion formula), and X, Y independent implies phi_{X+Y} = phi_X phi_Y.
title: Characteristic Function

body: [Theorem thm: sbt of arXiv:2507.04505, 'Heights of butterfly trees'] Let $\pi \sim \operatorname{Unif}(\operatorname{B}_{n,s})$ and $h_n^{\operatorname{B}} = h(\mathcal T(\pi))$. Then $h_n^{\operatorname{B}} \sim 2^{X_n} + 2^{n - X_n} - 2$, where $X_n \sim \operatorname{Binom}(n,1/2)$, while $(\log_2 h_n^{\operatorname{B}} - n/2)/(\sqrt n/2)$ converges in distribution to $|Z|$ as $n \to \infty$, where $Z \sim N(0,1)$. In particular, $\mathbb{E} h_{n}^{\operatorname{B}} = 2(3/2)^n - 2 = c N^\alpha \cdot(1 + o(1))$ with $c=2$ and $\alpha = \log_2(3/2) \approx 0.58496$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm: sbt of arXiv:2507.04505

[Defn of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] A \textit{Cartan subalgebra} $\mathfrak{h}$ of $\mathfrak{g}$ is
a subspace which satisfies the following two properties:

\vspace{2mm}\noindent (i) $\mathfrak{h}$ is a maximal abelian subalgebra;

\vspace{2mm}\noindent (ii) ${\rm ad}_{H}\in{\rm End}(\mathfrak{g})$ is diagonalisable (over
$\mathbb{C}$) for each $H\in\mathfrak{h}$.

[Corollary 14 (Neutral reinforcement) of arXiv:2608.10183, '2608.10183'] If $
p=\frac12,
$ 
then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\left(S_t^j\right)
=
\mathbb E\left(S_0^j\right),

constant in expectation, although its sample paths continue to fluctuate.

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2512.03884, '2512.03884'] Let $\alpha$ be a quadratic irrational, and let $D$ be the discriminant of its minimal polynomial. Let $A=\mathbb{Z} + \mathbb{Z}\alpha$, and let $\varepsilon$ be the smallest totally positive unit in the order $\{ \xi \in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D}) : \xi A \subseteq A \}$ such that $\varepsilon>1$. Then
\[ c_1(\alpha) = \frac{2\zeta(A,-1)}{D^{1/2} \log \varepsilon} \quad \textrm{and} \quad c_2(\alpha) = \frac{4 \zeta(A,-3)}{9D^{3/2} \log \varepsilon} . \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 2 of arXiv:2512.03884

[Thm MPL of arXiv:2506.01746, '\bf Optimal Bregman quantization: existence and uniqueness of optimal quantizers revisited'] $(a)$ {\em General case}  (see e.g.~[Kav1993],~[Struwe1990]). If $\Lambda:\mathbb{R}^d\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}_+$ ($\Lambda$ for ``landscape'' when $d\!=\!2$) is
a continuously differentiable function satisfying $\displaystyle \lim_{|x|\to +\infty}\Lambda(x)$  $= +\infty$ and if two distinct zeros of $\nabla \Lambda$ are strict local
minima then $\nabla \Lambda$ has  a third zero  which can be in no case a strict  local minimum.

\smallskip
\noindent $(b)$  {\em  Compact case} (see [LambertonP1996],~[Cohort1998],~[LuPag23]). Let $K\!\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be   a
nonempty compact convex set with a nonempty interior $O$, $\mathring{K} = O$. If $\Lambda :K\longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is $C^1$
on $O$, $\nabla \Lambda$ admits a continuous extension  on $K$ satisfying $\{\nabla \Lambda=0\}\!\subset \,O$ 
and if, for every small enough $\varepsilon>0$, $(Id-\varepsilon \nabla \Lambda)(O)\!\subset O$, then $\nabla \Lambda$ has at least a third critical point in $K$ which is not a strict local minimum for $\Lambda$ on $K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Mountain Pass Lemma

body: [Lemma 52 (FIID sparse unique infinite clusters on the symmetric space) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a connected higher rank semisimple real Lie group with property (T) and let $(X,d_X)$ be its symmetric space. Let~$\mathbf Y$ be a Poisson point process $Y$ on $X$ of intensity $1$ together with iid ${\rm Unif}[0,1]$ marks. Then, for every $\eps>0$, there exists $\lambda>0$ such that if $\mathbf Y^{(\lambda)}$ is an independent Poisson point process on $X$ of intensity $\lambda$ equipped with iid ${\rm Unif}[0,1]$ marks,  there is a graph $\mathcal H$ on $Y$ defined as an isometry-equivariant factor of $(\mathbf Y,\mathbf Y^{(\lambda)})$ with a unique infinite cluster and $\mathbb E\big[ {\rm deg}_{\mathcal H(Y_0)}(o) \big]\le\eps$, where $Y_0:=Y\cup\{o\}$.
title: FIID sparse unique infinite clusters on the symmetric space

[Lemma 9 (\cite{Meurant,Usmani}) of arXiv:2607.08536, 'Soft edge limit of the Laguerre beta-ensemble at the lower edge'] Let $\ma{M}$ be an $n\times n$ tridiagonal matrix satisfying the assumptions above.
Then the following statements hold:
\begin{align}
u_{i}&= \det \ma{M}_{[1,i-1]} \cdot \prod_{k=1}^{i-1} e_k^{-1}, \qquad\qquad 1\le i\le n,\\
v_{j}&= \det \ma{M}_{[j+1,n]} \cdot \prod_{k=1}^{j-1} e_k \cdot (\det \ma{M})^{-1}, \qquad 1\le j\le n,\\ 
[\ma{M}^{-1}]_{i,j}&=u_{i} v_{j}= \det \ma{M}_{[1,i-1]}\det \ma{M}_{[j+1,n]} (\det \ma{M})^{-1} \prod_{k=i}^{j-1} e_k, \qquad \quad 1\le i\le j\le n,\\
\det \ma{M}&=v_n^{-1} \prod_{k=1}^{n-1}e_k= (d_n u_n-e_{n-1} u_{n-1})\prod_{k=1}^{n-1} e_k.
\end{align}
Note that by convention  the determinant of the empty matrix is equal to $1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{Meurant,Usmani}
Convergence orthogonal invariant bounded matrix

Let a_1, ..., a_n be real numbers with every |a_i| >= 1, and let eps_1, ..., eps_n be independent uniform signs. Then for any open interval I of length 2, the probability that sum eps_i a_i lies in I is at most C(n, floor(n/2)) / 2^n, which is Theta(1/sqrt(n)). The extremal case is all a_i equal.
|a_i| >= 1 for every i

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked with a scope caveat; NO independent review - the parent that reviewed it had itself supplied two of the argument's steps, so its review does not certify the amended proof; no Lean] van Handel, The strong convergence phenomenon, arXiv:2507.00346v2 (11 February 2026), Section 6.9, pp. 69-70, asks whether strong convergence of a family of random matrices forces the empirical complex-eigenvalue measures of every noncommutative polynomial to converge to the corresponding limiting Brown measure. Problem 6.9 states it for ARBITRARY strongly convergent families - no independence, no independent entries, no freeness of the limit - and that literal generality is what is addressed. CLAIM: no. Fix an irrational theta and reduced approximants p_j/q_j -> theta; with omega_j = exp(2 pi i p_j / q_j) put U_j e_k = omega_j^k e_k, S e_k = e_{k-1} and V_j = e^{pi i / q_j} S. Then V_j U_j = omega_j U_j V_j, U_j^{q_j} = I, V_j^{q_j} = -I, and det(z I - U_j - V_j) = z^{q_j} exactly, so A_j = U_j + V_j is nilpotent and every empirical eigenvalue measure is delta_0, while the Brown measure of u + v for the limiting irrational-rotation pair is Haar measure on the unit circle (Fang, Jiang, Lin and Xu, arXiv:1210.4771, Theorem 12.2 - a literature dependency, not proved here). The same example blocks any universal lower bound on the limiting spectral radius. Conjugating by an independent Haar unitary makes the family random without changing norms, traces, nilpotency or eigenvalues. THE LOAD-BEARING GAP, named by the record itself: the pair converges to a ROTATION-ALGEBRA pair, not a free pair, and the two have different Brown measures, so the citation has to match the limit the construction actually has; the strong-convergence step is recorded as one of three loose ends. WHAT IS NOT REFUTED: the narrower conjectures for independent Ginibre matrices with adjoints and for free limiting families. Yi Han, arXiv:2606.01664 (June 2026), claims the Ginibre case and is COMPATIBLE with this construction. Do not promote a general counterexample to a result about independent matrix ensembles. FULL CONSTRUCTION AND PROOF: the store holds it as the lemma math:probability.free:candidate-strong-convergence-does-not-force-brown-measure, under a title naming neither the problem nor the campaign; this node is what makes it reachable from the problem id.

body:
[Theorem 29 (Mean) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The first moment of $T_{m, p}$ is
  \[
    \E T_{m, p} = m \, H_m + 
      \frac{(1-p)^{-m}}{p}
      \left[
      (p\,m)^2\left(1-p\right)^{m-1}
      +
      \int_0^1 p^3 \, m^2 \left(m-1\right)
      \left(1-p\,x\right)^{m-2} L(x) \, dx
      \right]
  \]
  where $H_m$ is the $m^\text{th}$ harmonic number
  and $L(x) \coloneqq x + (1-x) \log(1-x)$.
  If $p = p_m$ is an $o(1/m)$ sequence then this becomes
  \[
    \E T_{m, p} = m\,H_m
    + p\,m^2 + \frac{1}{4} \, p^2 \, m^3
    + O\left(p^2 \, m^2\right) + O\left(p^3 \, m^4\right).
  \]
  as $m \to \infty$. If $p \sim c/m$ then
  \[
    \E T_{m, p} = m\,H_m + \left(1 + o(1)\right)
      m \left[ c + c^2 \int_0^1 e^{-cx} \, L(x) \, dx\right].
  \]
  If $p = \omega(1/m)$ then
  \[
    \E T_{m,p} = m\,H_m + \frac{(1-p)^{-m}}{p} \left(1
    + O\left(\frac{1}{p\,m}\right)\right).
  \]
  In particular, for $p$ constant,
  \begin{align*}
    \E T_{m,p}
    = m \, H_m
    + \frac{(1-p)^{-m}}{p}&\Bigg\{
      1 + \left(-6p + 5 + \frac{1}{p}\right) m^{-1}\\
    &\phantom{\Bigg\{} {} + \left(45\,p^2 - 62\,p + 8 + \frac{7}{p} + \frac{2}{p^2} \right) m^{-2}
      + O\left(m^{-3}\right)
    \Bigg\}.
  \end{align*}
  \begin{proof}
    The difference $T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}$ has \textsc{mgf}
    $I_{m, p}(t)$. Corollary~\ref{thm:mgf} implies
    the \textsc{mgf} of $T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}$
    exists on a neighbourhood of the origin, hence
    $\E [T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}] = \lim_{t \uparrow 0} I_{m,p}'(t)$.
    With the knowledge 
    \begin{equation}
      
      \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \left( 1 - x \right)^{m \exp(-t) - m}
      = \log\left(\frac{1}{1-x}\right) \, m \, e^{-t}
      \left( 1 - x \right)^{m \exp(-t) - m},
    \end{equation}
    we differentiate the integral expression of
    \eqref{eq:extra term} to find
    \begin{align}
      \notag
      \E \left[T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}\right]
      &= (1-p)^m

      &\quad \times \int_0^1 p\,m^2 \left(1-p\,x\right)^{m-1}

      integration by parts,}

      +

    uniform in $x$, within \eqref{eq:diff mean}.

    \begin{align*}

      + p^2\,m^3\,(1 + O(1/m))\,(1 + O(p\,m))\,\frac{1}{4}\\

body: Consider a nearly integrable Hamiltonian H(I,theta) = H_0(I) + eps H_1(I,theta) in action-angle coordinates, where H_0 is nondegenerate (its Hessian in I is nonsingular, so the frequency map I -> omega(I) = dH_0/dI is a local diffeomorphism) and H_1 is a sufficiently smooth, classically real-analytic, perturbation. The KAM theorem states that for eps small enough, invariant tori of the unperturbed system whose frequency vector omega(I) is Diophantine (|omega . k| >= c |k|^{-tau} for all nonzero integer vectors k) persist as slightly deformed invariant tori carrying quasi-periodic motion, and the surviving tori occupy a set of measure tending to full measure as eps -> 0. Due to Kolmogorov, Arnold, and Moser.
title: Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser theorem

Let $v, w$ be independent uniformly distributed (Haar) unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^D$ with $D \ge 3$, and let $\rho = \langle v, w\rangle$. Then $Y = 1 - \rho^2$ has the Beta distribution with parameters $\frac{D-1}{2}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$, and the singular kernel $(1-\rho^2)^{-1/2}$ has finite mean with the exact value $\mathbb{E}[Y^{-1/2}] = \dfrac{\Gamma(D/2)\,\Gamma((D-2)/2)}{\Gamma((D-1)/2)^2} = 1 + O(1/D)$. This is the benchmark that any corresponding estimate for non-Gaussian residual lines has to reproduce, and having the exact Gaussian value makes a wrong intermediate bound visible immediately.

[Prop 16 of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] Take $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}$ and fix an open set $D$. Suppose one of the following holds: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\rm(1)}] ${\bf X}$ is a diffusion process. 
\item[{\rm(2)}] $u\in L^{\infty}(D;{\m})$.
\item[{\rm(3)}] $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_e$. 
\item[{\rm(4)}] $u\in L^{\infty}_{\loc}(D;{\m})$ and 
for any relatively compact 
open sets $U,V$ with $U\Subset V\Subset D$,
there exists $\phi_V\in\mathscr{C}_D$ such that $0\leq\phi_V\leq1$ on $D$, $\phi_V=1$ on $V$ and 
$\1_U\mathbb{E}_{\cdot}[(1-\phi_V)|\tilde{u}|(X_{\tau_U})]\in D(\mathscr{E}_U)_e$. 
\item[{\rm (5)}] $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{\loc}$, there exists an intrinsic metric ${\sf d}$ in the sense of 
\cite[Definition~4.1]{FLW} such that all open balls with respect to ${\sf d}$ are relatively compact, and 
for any relatively compact open sets $U,V$ with $U\Subset V\Subset D$,
there exists ${\sf d}$-Lipschitz function $\phi_V$ with 
compact support in $D$ such that  $0\leq\phi_V\leq1$ on $D$, $\phi_V=1$ on $V$ and 
$\mathbb{E}_{\cdot}[(1-\phi_V)|\tilde{u}|(X_{\tau_U})]\in D(\mathscr{E}_U)_e$. 
\end{enumerate}
Then \eqref{eq:2.3} holds for $u$.

body:
[Lemma Lemme Propriétés des particules of arXiv:2504.03627, 'Richardson’s model and the contact process with stirring: long time behavior.'] \begin{enumerate} 
\item At every time $t > 0$, the positions $(P_t^a)_{a \in \mathbb Z^d}$ of the particles at time $t$ form a partition of $\mathbb Z^d$. 
\item The process $(\Tilde{\xi}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ satisfies the strong Markov property.  
\item Once a particle $a \in \mathbb Z^d$ is infected, it remains infected forever: 
\[
\text{if } \Tilde{\xi}_t(a) = (1, P_t^a), \text{ then: } \forall s \geq t,~\Tilde{\xi}_s(a) = (1, P_s^a).  
\] 
\item A site $x \in \mathbb Z^d$ is healthy at time $t$ if and only if a healthy particle is located at $x$ at time $t$: 
$$x \notin \xi_t \iff \exists a \in \mathbb Z^d,~\Tilde{\xi}_t(a) = (0, x).$$ 
 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma Lemme Propriétés des particules of arXiv:2504.03627

[Proposition 6 (Nonzero, time-independent Dirichlet data) of arXiv:2608.29854, '2608.29854'] Assume \eqref{eq:ES}, let $q:I\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and Borel, and
let $f:I\to\mathbb R$ be Borel.  Suppose that
\begin{equation*}
  f-\xi\in L^2(I,\mu),
  \qquad
  q\xi\in L^2(I,\mu).
\end{equation*}
Then there exists a function
$
  u:(0,\infty)\times I\to\mathbb R
$
satisfying
\Cref{thm:main}\ref{item:main-a}--\ref{item:main-c}.
Moreover, for every $t>0$,
$
  u(t,\cdot)-\xi\in L^2(I,\mu)
$,
\begin{align} 
  \lim_{x\downarrow\ell}u(t,x)=\gamma_\ell
  \quad\text{if }s(\ell+)>-\infty,
  \qquad
  \lim_{x\uparrow r}u(t,x)=\gamma_r
  \quad\text{if }s(r-)<\infty,
\end{align}
and
$
  u(t,\cdot)- f \to 0
$
in $L^2(I,\mu)$ as $t\downarrow0$.

[Lemma lem:mtfact of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] Suppose that $\Omega$ is a topological space and that $(\nu_N)_{N \in \mathbb{N}}$ are probability measures on $\Omega$
converging weakly to the probability measure $\nu$.
If $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is a bounded continuous function and $A \subseteq \Omega$ is a Borel set
with $\nu(\partial A) = 0$, then
\begin{equation}
    \mu_N(dx) \propto f(x) \ind*{A}(x) \nu_N(dx)
    \qquad \text{converges weakly to} \qquad
    \mu(dx) \propto f(x) \ind*{A}(x) \nu(dx),
\end{equation}
where $\mu_N$ and $\mu$ are normalized to be probability measures.

$$

for every text $\overline{t}\in B_n$

Own-work restricted-data theorem, proof unaudited (C006 v2); novelty not established. Fix n,m,d>=1, unit u, labels y_i in {-1,1}, gamma<=r_i<=1 with gamma>0, and x_i=y_i*r_i*u. Let phi(z)=max(z,lambda*z), 0<lambda<1, and f_i=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j dot x_i). Train BOTH layers simultaneously on average logistic loss with actual step m*eta, eta>0, choosing a derivative in [lambda,1] at zero. Write b_j=w_j dot u, s_j=a_j+b_j, d_j=a_j-b_j; require every s_j(0)!=0. Then all a_j*b_j become positive after finite time; thereafter loss is strictly decreasing and tends to zero. This holds almost surely for iid N(0,sigma^2) initialization of all weights at any sigma>0. An explicit high-probability time bound is as follows. For delta in (0,1) and epsilon in (0,log(2)), define c0=2*eta*lambda*gamma/[max(1,eta)*(1+eta)], c1=eta*lambda*gamma/(1+eta), Pbar=4*sqrt(2)*(m/delta)^(3/2), Bbar=log(2*Pbar)/c0, Kmin=3*lambda*gamma*sigma^2*delta^2/(64*m^2), Fbar=(2*sigma^2/delta)*exp(2*eta*Bbar), T0bar=ceil(Bbar*(1+exp(Fbar))), and Cbar=max(0,log(log(1/epsilon)/Kmin)/(2*c1)). With probability >=1-delta, L_t<=epsilon for every integer t>=T0bar+ceil(n*Cbar/(1-exp(-epsilon))). The same event works for all epsilon. The proof uses exact per-neuron updates s_j^+=(1+k_j)s_j, d_j^+=(1-k_j)d_j, where eta*lambda*gamma*G<=k_j<=eta*G and G is average logistic weight. The cumulative sum of G cannot be finite, since that would bound parameters and hence keep G positive. Ratios contract into |d_j|<=|s_j|/2, fixing all branches and making all margins grow. The probability estimate uses a Gaussian density bound plus Markov and a union bound, not independence between norm and small-ball events. The times can be extremely large; neither Cai et al.'s sharp eta dependence nor convergence for multidirectional data is established. 13149 passing finite exact rational checks support selected algebra only; the analytic theorem remains unaudited. No formal certificate or numerical Gaussian simulation is claimed.
Collinear signed separable data with gamma<=r_i<=1; arbitrary sample count, labels and width.
Literal leaky activation, both layers trained simultaneously, positive arbitrary step and allowed derivative at zero.
Nonzero expanding coordinates deterministically; the quantified Gaussian bound assumes independent equal-variance N(0,sigma^2) coordinates.
Proof (unaudited), C006 v2; no novelty, full-data theorem, sharp Cai rate or formal certificate claimed.

Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. For 0 <= r <= n let R_r be the average over r-element sets A of E Var(f | X_{A^c}). Then R_r = Var(f) - H_{n - r} = sum_{k=1}^n [1 - binom(n - k, r)/binom(n, r)] W_k (the ratio read as 0 when r > n - k), so R_r is nondecreasing in r. If X^(A) keeps X_{A^c} and replaces X_A by an independent draw from its own law, then E Var(f | X_{A^c}) = (1/2) E[(f(X) - f(X^(A)))^2]. In particular n R_1 = sum_i E Var(f | X_{-i}) = sum_k k W_k.

[Proposition 46 (Mixture supermartingales) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Suppose that for every $\lambda \in \Lambda$ (a measurable parameter space), $E_t(\lambda)$ is a nonnegative supermartingale with $E_0(\lambda) \leq 1$.
Let $\mu$ be a prior probability measure on $\Lambda$ and define $\overline E_t := \int E_t(\lambda)\,\mu(\dd\lambda)$.
Then $(\overline E_t)$ is a nonnegative supermartingale.
Moreover, for every adapted posterior $\rho_t \ll \mu$ (possibly data-dependent) with $\rho_t(\{\lambda : E_t(\lambda) = 0\}) = 0$, the mixture log-wealth is a Donsker--Varadhan identity,
\begin{equation}
  \log \overline E_t
  = \int_\Lambda \log E_t(\lambda)\,\rho_t(\dd\lambda)
       - \KL(\rho_t \| \mu) + \KL(\rho_t \| \rho^*_t)
\end{equation}
with $\dd\rho^*_t/\dd\mu \propto E_t(\cdot)$; dropping the nonnegative residual $\KL(\rho_t\|\rho^*_t)$ gives the PAC-Bayes lower bound $\log \overline E_t \ge \int_\Lambda \log E_t(\lambda)\,\rho_t(\dd\lambda) - \KL(\rho_t\|\mu)$.
In particular, if $E_t(\lambda) = \exp(\lambda Y_t - \overline\Psi_t(\lambda))$,
\begin{equation}
  \PP\!\left(
    \exists\,t :
    \int_\Lambda [\lambda Y_t - \overline\Psi_t(\lambda)]\rho_t(\dd\lambda)
    - \KL(\rho_t\|\mu) \geq x\right)
  \leq e^{-x}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let Lambda be a compact hyperbolic set for a diffeomorphism f. There exist a neighbourhood U of Lambda and constants C > 0 and delta_0 > 0 such that: whenever a point x and an integer n satisfy f^k(x) in U for 0 <= k <= n and d(f^n(x), x) < delta < delta_0, there is a genuine PERIODIC point p with f^n(p) = p and d(f^k(p), f^k(x)) <= C delta for every 0 <= k <= n. In words, an orbit segment that almost closes up lies uniformly close to an exactly periodic orbit of the same period. This is the standard device for producing many periodic orbits in a hyperbolic set and for approximating invariant measures by measures on periodic orbits.
Hyperbolicity on the compact set, and the whole segment staying in the neighbourhood U.
The period of the produced orbit is exactly n, and closeness is uniform along the segment.

\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{n,m}^{\mathrm{Gin}}
\in
\Omega\cup
\partial_{n^{-c_{\mathrm{cmp}}}}\Omega
\right)
+
n^{-c_{\mathrm{cmp}}}.
\end{aligned}

\end{equation}

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d7d24572a68ce4263098c324d399774708859cfdac59493b76d5d2697bef2a55","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d7/d7d24572a68ce4263098c324d399774708859cfdac59493b76d5d2697bef2a55.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:cbac8f169ff863a9595053ddefd9aa680d7116085e24b8a5c3f7297ee2ff2704","bundle_entry_key":"scalar-forced-urn-wright-fisher-generator-limit","bundle_id":"population.w336-p0087-checked-attempt-20261010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"w336/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.reinforcement:scalar-forced-urn-wright-fisher-generator-limit","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0087: stationary synchronization and covariance at f=c*r^2

Status: proof written; w346 KEEP pending. This proves a full stationary-law limit, stationary moments and a scalar generator limit under conditional independence. It does not prove the general network's functional diffusion limit or its initial layer.

Assume a fixed finite irreducible row-stochastic Q, its stationary probability row vector pi, p in [0,1]^d, c>0, r>0, f=c*r^2 and r+f<=1. Update

    Z'=(1-r-f)Z+r X+f p,

with conditionally independent X_i given Z, and P(X_i=1|Z)=(QZ)_i. There is a unique stationary law on [0,1]^d. Its mean is z*=f*((r+f)I-rQ)^(-1)p. Write pbar=pi.p and K=sum pi_i^2. As r decreases to zero, its stationary covariance satisfies

    Cov(Z) -> [K*pbar*(1-pbar)/(2c+K)]*1*1^T.

Proof of existence/uniqueness: the transition is Feller on a compact cube. Couple two states using the same independent uniforms for their Bernoulli coordinates. Because 1-r-f>=0, the weighted L1 distance has expected next value at most (1-f) times its present value; use pi Q=pi. Thus stationary laws are unique and the transition contracts in this Wasserstein distance. Taking expectations yields the displayed mean; the matrix is invertible because its eigenvalues have positive real part.

For synchronization, let D=diag(pi), S=pi.Z, and E_Q(z)=z^T D(I-Q)z=(1/2)sum pi_i Q_ij(z_i-z_j)^2. At stationarity, with Delta=r(X-Z)+f(p-Z),

    2r E[E_Q(Z)] = 2f E[<Z,p-Z>_D] + E[||Delta||_D^2]
                   <= 2f+(r+f)^2 = O(r^2).

Irreducibility makes E_Q(z)>=gamma*||z-1*(pi.z)||_D^2 for some fixed gamma>0: the finite symmetric quadratic form has kernel precisely the constants. Hence E||Z-1*S||_D^2=O(r). Also E[S]=pbar exactly, so z*_i tends to pbar.

The martingale innovation for S has conditional variance r^2 sum pi_i^2 (QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i); conditional independence is used exactly here. Total variance at stationarity gives

    (2f-f^2) Var(S)=r^2 sum pi_i^2 E[(QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i)].

Synchronization shows (QZ)_i-S tends to zero in L2. The variables are bounded, so for any subsequential limit V of Var(S), division by r^2 gives 2c V=K*(pbar*(1-pbar)-V). Its solution is unique. Every subsequence has that limit, and synchronization gives the full covariance limit.

For the scalar case Q=(1), stationarity gives the exact variance

    Var(Z)=r^2*p*(1-p)/(2f-f^2+r^2)
          =p*(1-p)/(1+2c-c^2*r^2).

For h in C^3([0,1]), the one-step scalar generator divided by r^2 converges uniformly to

    Lh(z)=c(p-z)h'(z)+(1/2)z(1-z)h''(z).

Indeed E[Delta]=c*r^2(p-z), E[Delta^2]=r^2*z(1-z)+c^2*r^4(p-z)^2, and |Delta|<=r+cr^2. Taylor's remainder, divided by r^2, is bounded by ||h'''||_infinity*r*(1+cr)^3/6, with the additional second-order drift term O(r^2). This identifies the candidate Wright-Fisher generator; path tightness and martingale-problem uniqueness are further steps.

Theorem (full stationary law). Under the same fixed-network assumptions and 0<pbar<1, the joint stationary law of Z converges weakly to Y*1, where

    Y ~ Beta(2c*pbar/K, 2c*(1-pbar)/K).

Proof: write S'=S+f*(pbar-S)+r*eta, where eta=pi.(X-QZ), E[eta|Z]=0, |eta|<=1 and E[eta^2|Z]=sum pi_i^2 (QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i). For every polynomial h, the stationary Taylor identity divided by r^2 gives

    0=c E[(pbar-S)h'(S)]
      +(1/2)E[sum pi_i^2 (QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i)*h''(S)] + O(r).

The drift-square contribution is O(r^2), and the third-order remainder is uniformly O(r). The proved L2 synchronization implies that the sum inside the second term differs from K*S*(1-S) by a quantity tending to zero in L1. Every subsequence has a further weakly convergent subsequence of S because [0,1] is compact. If its limiting moments are mu_k, use h(s)=s^k, k>=1, to obtain

    [2c+K*(k-1)]*mu_k = [2c*pbar+K*(k-1)]*mu_(k-1), mu_0=1.

These are exactly the moments of the displayed beta law: iterating gives the product of (2c*pbar/K+j)/(2c/K+j) for j=0,...,k-1, which also follows by integrating the beta density. A probability law on [0,1] is determined by its moments, since polynomials approximate continuous functions uniformly. Hence all subsequential limits agree and S converges weakly. Synchronization gives Z-S*1 tending to zero in probability, so the joint law converges to Y*1. If pbar=0 or 1, positivity of pi forces every p_i to be that endpoint and the unique stationary law is the corresponding point mass.

This proof uses all polynomial moments, not an inference from the first two moments. It proves convergence of stationary laws, not a limit for trajectories begun away from synchronization. Without conditional independence, the innovation variance changes. For example, Q=J_d/d, constant p, and one shared Bernoulli coin across all coordinates preserve a synchronized state and give the scalar beta parameters 2cp and 2c(1-p), rather than 2cdp and 2cd(1-p).

For reproducible finite checks, the exact covariance identity is

    V=B V B^T+r^2*diag(s*(1-s)-diag(Q V Q^T)),
    B=(1-r-f)I+rQ, s=Q z*.

Checks: the scalar exact formula; first four scalar stationary moments; exact polynomial generators; finite-network covariance systems; first four moments of the exact consensus Markov chain for Q=J_d/d at d=2,3,5; a common-coin control that changes the beta variance. The conditional-independence hypothesis is essential for K, the covariance formula and the stationary beta law.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:97f3a85196e873990e9567366e0506ef248b0ce7c5366d200c12cde129cf9cd6","revision_digest":"sha256:ab6b4233beab0d6c3f9dc2a0723255bcc94f136350015b7664ed31456e9bcff1","source_id":"owner:campaign:w336:P0087:scalar-forced-urn-wright-fisher-generator-limit","source_revision":"author-proof-2026-10-10; independent audit w346 pending","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Prop boundconditionalmomentsdoubling of arXiv:2602.08739, '\large \bf MOMENTS OF C$\beta$E FIELD PARTITION FUNCTION, $\mathsf{Sine}_{\beta}$ CORRELAT'] For $p \geq 2$, let $(\theta_m)_{1 \leq m \leq p}\in \mathbb{R}^p$ , $(s_m)_{1 \leq m \leq p}\in \mathbb{R}_+^p$. 
Let 
$$\mu \overset{\textnormal{def}}{=} \min_{1 \leq m_1 \neq m_2 \leq p} 
||\theta_{m_1} - \theta_{m_2}||.$$
Then, for all $j\in \mathbb{N}$ so that $j \geq \mu^{-1}$, 
$$\mathbb{E} \left[ \prod_{m=1}^p \left|\Phi^*_{2j} (\mathrm{e}^{\textnormal{i} \theta_m})\right|^{2s_m} \;  \bigg| \mathcal{F}_j \right]
\leq \prod_{m=1}^p \left|\Phi^*_{j} (\mathrm{e}^{\textnormal{i} \theta_m})
\right|^{2s_m} \, \exp \left(
\frac{2 \log 2}{\beta}  
 \sum_{m=1}^{p} s_m^2 
+ K \left( \frac{\log (1 + j \mu)}{j \mu} \right)^{1/3} \right)
$$
where $K > 0$ depends only on $\beta, p$
and on the sequence $(s_m)_{1 \leq m \leq p}$.

body: [Cor coho to compact indep of ambient of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $\Gamma$ be a countable group, $(X, \nu)$ an ergodic $\Gamma$-system, $G$ a locally compact second countable group, and $\alpha: \Gamma \times X \to G$ a cocycle. [Lemma 4 of arXiv:2608.01081, 'The Optimal Rate in the Averaged Random-Marginal Central Limit Theorem for Log-Concave Mea'] Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability measures on $\R$ with finite first
moments, and let
\[
 Q_\mu(s)=\inf\{t:F_\mu(t)\ge s\},
 \qquad 0<s<1,
\]
with the analogous definition for $Q_\nu$. Then
\begin{equation}
 W_1(\mu,\nu)
 =\int_0^1|Q_\mu(s)-Q_\nu(s)|\,\dd s
 =\int_\R|F_\mu(t)-F_\nu(t)|\,\dd t.
\end{equation}
Moreover, if $h:\R\to\R$ is one-Lipschitz, then
\begin{equation}
 \left|\int h\,\dd\mu-\int h\,\dd\nu\right|
 \le W_1(\mu,\nu).
\end{equation}
