[Theorem 5 (Fitted FORE with empirical normalization) of arXiv:2608.24858, 'Bellman Calibration for Marginalized Importance Weighting in Offline Reinforcement Learnin'] Let \(\gamma\in[0,1)\). Assume Conditions~\ref{cond:fore-class}--
\ref{cond:fore-target} and suppose that \(0\in\sH\). Let
\(\widehat h_0,\ldots,\widehat h_K\in\sH\) be the log-ratio representatives
generated by the exact fitted \textnormal{\textsc{FORE}} recursion over \(\sH\),
initialized at \(\widehat h_0=0\).
Write
\[
  \widehat\Lambda_n(h)
  =
  \log\left\{
    \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \exp h(X_i)
  \right\},
  \qquad
  \widehat\omega^{(k)}(x)
  =
  \exp\{\widehat h_k(x)-\widehat\Lambda_n(\widehat h_k)\},
  \qquad 0\le k\le K .
\]
In particular, \(\widehat\omega^{(0)}\equiv1\).
The iterates are constructed from independent transition
draws from \(\nu\) and independent initial draws from \(\mu_{0,\pi}\), and
each empirical subproblem is solved exactly.
Then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\begin{equation}

\begin{aligned}
  D_{\nu}^{\rm KL}(\widehat\omega^{(K)}\|w_\pi)
  \le{}&
  C_{\rm env}
  \left(\frac{1+\gamma}{2}\right)^K
  D_{\nu}^{\rm KL}(\widehat\omega^{(0)}\|w_\pi)\\
  &+\frac{C_{\rm env}}{1-\gamma}\varepsilon_{\sH}\\
  &+\frac{C_{\rm env}}{(1-\gamma)^2}
  \log^2(eN)
  \left\{
    \mathfrak r_{N,\rm fit}^2
    +\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{N}
  \right\},
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where \(N=n\wedge m\). For universal finite exponents \(p,q\),
\begin{equation}

  C_{\rm env}
  \le
  C_0(A,\alpha)(1+K_0+K_+)^q(1+e^{2R})^p.
\end{equation}

[Theorem thm:near-core of arXiv:2609.02845, 'Degeneracy bounds, stability, and a sharp gap for $B$-colorings'] Let $d$, $\Delta$, and $s$ be integers satisfying
$1\le d\le\Delta$ and $0\le s<\Delta$.  Let $G$ be a
$d$-degenerate graph with $\Delta(G)\le\Delta$.  If
$q_B(G)\ge d\Delta-s$, then there is a vertex $v$ with distinct
neighbors $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ such that
\begin{equation}

 d\bigl(\Delta-d_G(u_1)\bigr)
 +\sum_{j=2}^{d}|N_G(u_1)\setminus N_G(u_j)|
 \le s.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
  \left|\bigcap_{j=1}^{d}N_G(u_j)\right|\ge\Delta-s,
\]
and hence $G$ contains a copy of $K_{d,\Delta-s}$.

body:
The spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators (an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors, real eigenvalues tending to 0, ||T|| = max |eigenvalue|, min-max characterisation of eigenvalues) requires self-adjointness or at least normality. Compactness alone gives only the Riesz-Schauder picture: the nonzero spectrum consists of eigenvalues of finite algebraic multiplicity accumulating only at 0, and the set of such eigenvalues may be empty. The standard counterexample is the Volterra operator on L^2([0,1]), (V f)(x) = integral from 0 to x of f(t) dt, which is Hilbert-Schmidt (kernel k(x,t) = 1 for t < x, 0 otherwise) hence compact, but has no eigenvalues at all: V f = lambda f with lambda nonzero forces f to be absolutely continuous with f' = f/lambda and f(0) = 0, so f = 0; and V f = 0 forces f = 0 a.e. Thus sigma(V) = {0}, spectral radius 0, while ||V|| = 2/pi; the singular values of V are 1/((n + 1/2) pi), n >= 0, so V is Hilbert-Schmidt but not trace class, and the moduli of its eigenvalues (all zero) are nowhere near its singular values. Consequences for an auditor: (a) 'compact, so expand in eigenfunctions' is invalid without normality; the right substitute is the Schmidt decomposition in singular values, which always exists; (b) 'compact, so the spectral radius equals the norm' is false; (c) Rayleigh-quotient and min-max formulas for eigenvalues are statements about self-adjoint operators and become statements about singular values otherwise; (d) Mercer-type positivity conclusions require a self-adjoint positive kernel, not just an L^2 kernel.

[Definition def:moment-constraints of arXiv:2606.21391, 'Extreme points and faces in the moment problem'] Let $\mathbf{p}\colon X\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be measurable with respect to $\mathcal{F}$ and let
\begin{align*}
P\!_\mathrm{a.i.}  & \textstyle 
:=\{ \mu\in P\!_\mathrm{fin} : 
\text{$\mu$ is concentrated on a finite subset $\{x_1,\dots,x_k\}\subset X$}\\
& \textstyle \hspace{\widthof{$:=\{$}}
\text{such that $\mathbf{p}(x_1),\dots,\mathbf{p}(x_k)$ are affinely independent}\,\}.
\end{align*}
We refer to the measures in $P\!_\mathrm{a.i.}$ as finitely atomic measures having the 
affine independence property. Let $C\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a  convex subset and let
\begin{align*}
G_\mathrm{fin}(C) & \textstyle
:= \{\mu\in P\!_\mathrm{fin} : \int\mathbf{p}\mathrm{d}\mu\in C\},\\

G_\mathrm{a.i.}(C) & \textstyle
:= \{\mu\in P\!_\mathrm{a.i.} : \int\mathbf{p}\mathrm{d}\mu\in C\}.
\end{align*}
Let $Q\subset P$ be a convex set of probability measures. Denoting the components of 
$\mathbf{p}=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)$ by $p_i\colon X\to\mathbb{R}$, $i=1,\ldots,d$, we define
\begin{align*}
Q^\mathbf{p} & \textstyle 
:= \{\mu\in Q : \text{$p_i$ is $\mu$-integrable $\forall i=1,\dots,d$}\,\},\\

G(C) & \textstyle
:= \{\mu\in Q^\mathbf{p} : \int\mathbf{p}\mathrm{d}\mu\in C\}.
\end{align*}
We abbreviate $G_\mathrm{fin}(\mathbf{q}):=G_\mathrm{fin}(\{\mathbf{q}\})$, etc., for singletons 
$\{\mathbf{q}\}$ with elements $\mathbf{q}\in\mathbb{R}^d$.
title: Moment constraints

[Proposition prop:everyone-settles of arXiv:2609.02820, 'Sharpness and critical scaling of parking'] Let $\eta=(\eta(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ have i.i.d.\ integer-valued coordinates.
	Suppose that $\eta(0)$ is nonconstant, $\mathbb{E}\eta(0)=0$, and
	$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta|\eta(0)|}<\infty$ for some $\theta>0$. Then the following hold
	together on one event of probability one: every particle settles after
	finitely many rounds; every hole is filled after finitely many rounds; and
	infinitely many distinct particles leave every site, so that
	$U_\infty(x)=\infty$ for every $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$.

[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $Z$ be a normal projective variety of dimension $d\geq2$, let $x\in Z$ be a closed point, and let $\mathcal I_x\subset\mathcal O_Z$ be the ideal sheaf of $x$. Let $f\colon Y\to Z$ be the normalized blow-up of $\mathcal I_x$, write $\mathcal I_x\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_Y(-E)$ with $E$ effective, and let $H:=-E$. Then 

\begin{enumerate}
\item $H$ is $f$-ample and $F\cdot H^{d-1}>0$ for every prime component $F$ of $E$.
\item $-H^d=\mult_xZ$.
\item $K_Y\cdot H^{d-1}=(d-1)\mult_xZ-2\ebarone(\m_{Z,x})$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $\sum_F\ord_F(\m_{Z,x})(F\cdot H^{d-1})=\mult_xZ$, where $F$ runs over the prime components of $E$.

[Lemma l:sde-disc of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] {chewi2024log}, [dalalyan2012sparse]}]

Fix a stepsize $h>0$ and let $t^-=h\left\lfloor\frac th\right\rfloor$.
Suppose that $f:\mathbb R^n\to \mathbb R^n$ is $L$-Lipschitz. 
    Consider the two SDE's in $\mathbb R^n$,
    \begin{align*}
        dy_t &= f(y_t) dt + dB_t\\
        d\widetilde{y}_t &= f(\widetilde{y}_{t^-}) dt + dB_t,
    \end{align*}
    where $y_0,\widetilde{y}_0\sim \rho_0$.
    Let $T=Nh$, $N\in \mathbb N$. 
    Then
    \begin{align*}
\operatorname{KL}(\mathcal L((\widetilde{y}_t)_{t\in [0,T]})\| \mathcal L((y_t)_{t\in [0,T]}))

&\leqslant 
\fc{L^2h^3}{6} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\ve{f(\widetilde{y}_{kh})}^2 + \fc{T L^2 n h}{2}\\
&\leqslant 
TL^2\pa{\fc{h^2M^2}{6}+ \fc{n h}{2}}
    \end{align*}
where the last inequality holds if $\left\Vert {f}\right\Vert_{\infty}\leqslant M$. If $h\leqslant \fc{\sqrt{3/2}\varepsilon}{\sqrt T LM}\wedge \fc{\varepsilon^2}{2nTL^2}$, then $\operatorname{TV}(\mathcal L((\widetilde{y}_t)_{t\in [0,T]}), \mathcal L((y_t)_{t\in [0,T]}))\leqslant \varepsilon$. [Proposition prop:sec5-continuum-probe of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] Fix finitely many pairs
\((x_i,y_i)\in D^2\), \(1\leq i\leq r\), with \(x_i\ne y_i\);
repetitions of a pair are allowed.  For every
\(0\leq\lambda\leq1\) there is a random compact set \(C\Subset D\), with
at most \(r\) nondegenerate components, such that for every compact
\(E\subset\overline{D}\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E}_C\!\left[
 \mathbf 1_{\{C\cap E=\varnothing\}}e^{-\lambda m_D(C,E)}\right]
 =\prod_{i=1}^r
   \frac{G_{D\setminus E}(x_i,y_i)}{G_D(x_i,y_i)}.
\end{equation}
Here a numerator is zero if an endpoint belongs to \(E\) or the endpoints
 lie in different components of \(D\setminus E\).
If all pairs share one endpoint, \(C\) can be chosen connected.

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Assuming that $a\in A$ is normal, $aa^*=a^*a$, its law corresponds to a probability measure on its spectrum $\sigma(a)\subset\mathbb C$, according to the following formula:
$$tr(P(a))=\int_{\sigma(a)}P(x)d\mu(x)$$
When the trace is faithful we have $supp(\mu)=\sigma(a)$. Also, in the particular case where the variable is self-adjoint, $a=a^*$, this law is a real probability measure.

Own-work draft; T419-C010 v1, proof (unaudited), no novelty claimed; known-theorem application. Let X be any full-row-rank p-by-n real design, Delta a fixed m-by-p matrix, and Z=Delta X+E, where the entries of E are independent N(0,sigma^2), sigma>0. Fix 1<=r<min(m,p), and minimize (1/(2n))||BA X-Z||F^2 over B m-by-r,A r-by-p. Almost surely over E, every second-order stationary point is a global rank-r empirical regression optimum, and every nonglobal critical point has a negative Hessian direction, for every positive definite covariance C=XX^T/n without a condition-number restriction. Writing H=C^(1/2), M=(ZX^T/n)H^(-1), its product is the unique reduced-rank regression estimate M_r H^(-1), with M_r the rank-r singular-value truncation. For iid Gaussian input vectors, full row rank holds almost surely when n>=p. This does not prove that ordinary factor GD from B0=0 and Gaussian A0 reaches an SOSP or has the estimator's statistical risk; those trajectory, stopping and integrability conditions remain to be established.

Independent positive-variance isotropic Gaussian label noise

body: [Definition of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] We say $\blacksquare\subset \Sigma$ is an admissible flow rectangle if $\partial \blacksquare$ is the union of two (possibly empty) flow lines and two transverse curves $\gamma, \tilde \gamma  $ of same type (either $\operatorname{I}$ or $\operatorname{II}$) with $\tilde{\gamma}\preccurlyeq\gamma$  (with $\mathscr{A}_\gamma(t)$ increasing) and if $\blacksquare\subset \Sigma$ does not contain any critical points.

body:
[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] Let $\Sigma$ be a connected compact strongly stable minimal capillary surface with
\[
 \langle\nu_\Sigma,\nu_S\rangle=-\tanh t,
 \qquad t\geq0,
\]
and suppose $H_S\geq0$ along $\partial\Sigma$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \frac12\int_\Sigma|h_\Sigma|^2\,dA
 +\cosh t\int_{\partial\Sigma}H_S\,ds
 \leq2\pi\chi(\Sigma).
 
\end{equation}
In particular, $\Sigma$ is a disk.

[Thm Weak.Win of arXiv:2609.02588, 'Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games'] Let a hypergraph $(X,\mathcal{F})$ and a bias $b\in\mathbb{N}$ be given. If
$$
\sum_{F\in \mathcal{F}} (1+b)^{-|F|} > \frac{b^2}{(1+b)^3} \Delta_2(\mathcal{F}) |X|
$$
holds, Maker (as first player) has a winning strategy for the $(1:b)$ Maker-Breaker game on 
$(X,\mathcal{F})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Weak Win Criterion,~Theorem 2 in~\cite{beck1982remarks}

body:
[Lemma lem:lapl of arXiv:2607.26169, 'Scaling and partial universality of the height zero probability in the 2D Abelian sandpile'] Let $g : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ have continuous and bounded partial derivatives of order up to $3$.
Then for any $u \in \mathcal{V}$ we have that
\eqnst{
  \Delta g(u)
  = \sum_{u' \sim u} (g(u) - g(u'))
  = - \frac{1}{4} \Delta^{(c)} g (u) \sum_{u' \sim u} |u - u'|^2
    + O( \| D^3 g \|_\infty \max_{u'\sim u} |u'-u|^3 ), }
where $\Delta^{(c)} g = (\partial_{11} + \partial_{22}) g$ is the (continuous) Laplacian.
title: Lemma lem:lapl of arXiv:2607.26169

body:
[Thm 4 of arXiv:2607.17576, 'How much randomness is needed to symmetrize a random variable?'] Let $\lambda>0$. Let $X\sim \text{Exp}(\lambda)$ be an exponential random variable with the probability density function $f_X(x)=\lambda e^{-\lambda x}\mathbbm{1}_{\mathbb{R}_+}(x)$. Let $Y$ be an absolutely continuous independent symmetrizer of $X$.  Then we have
$$
\Var (Y)\ge \Var(X).
$$
Equality holds if and only if $Y$ is an independent copy of $-X$.

body:
[Prop subseq of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] Assume that $t_n\in\mathbb R$ and $\lambda_n>0$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$ such that $\lambda_n\to 0$. Then, the following two statements are equivalent:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\item  The shifted Poisson point process $\iota_{t_n}(X^{(\lambda_n)})$ converges weakly as $\lambda\downarrow 0$ to a point process on $\mathrm{Lip}_1$ with respect to the topology of $\mathcal M$,  and its limit is nonempty with positive probability.
			\item  The sequence of measures $\lambda_n \iota_{t_n}^*\mu$‌ converges in $\mathcal M$ and its limit is nonzero.
		\end{enumerate}
		If these conditions hold, then:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\setcounter{enumi}{2}
			\item  $t_n\to\infty$ and the measure $\nu\coloneqq\lim_n \lambda_n \iota_{t_n}^*\mu$ is supported on $\widehat{\partial E}$.
			\item  The weak limit of $\iota_{t_n} X^{(\lambda_n)}$ is a (marked) Poisson point process on $\widehat{\partial E}$ with intensity measure $\nu$, namely $\Phi\coloneqq(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i \geq 1}$.
			\item  \textsc{[Convergence of Ordered Points]} Assuming that either $E$ is a graph (with the graph-distance metric) or that the delays $(\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ are distinct a.s., if the points $(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ are ordered with the same rule as in (def:PPP of the paper), then the joint distribution of the ordered sequence of points $\left(\iota_{t_n}X^{(\lambda_n)}_i\right)_{i\geq 1}$ converges to that of $(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ as $n\to\infty$.
		\end{enumerate}
title: \textsc{Converging Subsequences}

[Thm thm 5.1 of arXiv:2411.01847, 'Well-Posedness of Stochastic Chemotaxis System'] Let $(u, v, \tau_m)$ be a local mild solution of system ((main2 of the paper)), with $\tau_m$ defined by
    \begin{align*}
        \tau_m = \inf \{ t > 0 \mid \|u\|_{\Upsilon^u_t} \geq m \}.
    \end{align*}
    Then, for $p\geq 2$, the following It\^{o} formula for $\|u(t)\|_{p}^{p}$ holds $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. for all $t \in [0, \tau_m]$,
    \begin{align}
        &\|u(t)\|_{p}^{p} - \|u_0\|_{p}^{p} +p(p - 1)  \int_0^{t}\|\nabla u^{\frac{p}{2}}(s)\|_2^2 \, ds \nonumber \\
        &= p(p - 1) \chi \int_0^{t} \int_\mathcal{O} u^{p - 1}(s) \nabla u(s) \cdot \nabla G * u(s) \, dx \, ds \nonumber \\
        &\quad + p \int_0^{t} \int_\mathcal{O} u^{p - 1}(s) g(u(s)) \, dx \, ds \nonumber \\
        &\quad + p \sum_{i=1}^\infty \int_0^{t} \int_\mathcal{O} b_i\|u(s)\|_q^{r}|u(s)|^{p} \, dx \, dW^i_s \nonumber \\
        &\quad + \frac{p(p - 1)}{2} \int_0^{t} \|u(s)\|_q^{2r}\int_\mathcal{O} \sum_{i=1}^\infty b_i^2 |u(s)|^{p} \, dx \, ds.
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm thm 5.1 of arXiv:2411.01847

[Theorem thm:variance_asymptotics of arXiv:2609.02491, 'Generalised Random Parking for Trapeziums on a Strip'] There exist finite constants $\lambda_2(a,b)>0$ and $C_{a,b}>0$ such that, 
\begin{equation}
    \max_{s \in \{\mathcal{P},\mathcal{T}\}}\mleft| \mathrm{Var}(X_s(x))-\lambda_2(a,b)\mleft(x+\frac{a+b}{2} \mright)\mright| \le C_{a,b} \mathcal R_2(x),
\end{equation} for all $x>(3a-b)/2$, where

\begin{equation*}
    \mathcal R_2(x)
\coloneqq
\begin{dcases}
    \mleft(\dfrac{4e}{x/a}\mright)^{x/a-4},
    &\text{if }a=b,\\
    \mleft(\dfrac{4e}{x/a}\mright)^{x/a-(5+(a+b)/(2a))},
    &\text{if }a>b.
\end{dcases}
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:variance_asymptotics of arXiv:2609.02491

[Lemma lem:affine-stability of arXiv:2607.00149, '\bf Uniform-in-time Propagation-of-Chaos for\\ Stein Variational Gradient Descent'] Fix $R<\infty$ and $c_0>0$, and define
\[
        \mathcal{D}_{R,c_0}
        :=
        \Bigl\{
        (m,S):\ \|m\|+\|S\|_F\le R,\quad
        S-mm^\top\ge c_0 I_d
        \Bigr\}.
\]
Then there exist constants
\[
        \eta=\eta(R,c_0,d)>0,
        \qquad
        L=L(R,c_0,d)<\infty,
\]
such that, for every $(m_0,S_0)\in\mathcal D_{R,c_0}$ and every
$(m,S)$ in
$
       U\coloneqq \{ (m,S): D_2\bigl((m,S),(m_0,S_0)\bigr)\le \eta\},
$
the flow $\Phi_t$ of (equation eq:affine-moment-ode of the paper) satisfies
\[
        \sup_{t\ge0}
        D_2\bigl(\Phi_t(m,S),\Phi_t(m_0,S_0)\bigr)
        \le
        L\,D_2\bigl((m,S),(m_0,S_0)\bigr).
\]

body:
[Proposition 38 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Suppose $U=\sum_{j=0}^\infty u^j$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{asmp:main for refreshing} for some $\beta>0$. Additionally, suppose that for some $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $p>1$, we have a constant $K\geq 1$ such that for $n\in\{0,1,2\}$ and all $j\in\N$,
\begin{equation}
\|\nabla^n u^j\|_{L^p_\omega C^0_{t,x}}\leq K 2^{(n-\alpha)j}.
\end{equation}
    Then for all $\eps>\frac{\beta}{p}$ and $A\geq 1$, there exist vector fields $\{u^{j,A}\}_{j \geq 0}$ (on possibly a larger probability space, though coupled to the original $u^j$) also satisfying Assumption~\ref{asmp:main for refreshing} such that for all $j\geq 0$, $n\in\{0,1,2\}$,
\[\|\nabla^n u^{j,A}\|_{C^0_{t,x}} \leq A K 2^{(n-\alpha+\eps)j},
\]
and, letting $U^A:=\sum_{j=0}^\infty u^{j,A}$, there exists $C(\beta,p,\eps)>0$ such that
\[\P(U^A\neq U)\leq C A^{1-p}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 38 of arXiv:2608.05931

[Lemma ldepsum of arXiv:2412.04396, 'Superdiffusive Scaling Limits for the Symmetric\\ Exclusion Process with Slow Bonds'] Let $\mu$ be a measure on a finite set $\Omega$ and let $f$ be a density with respect to $\mu$.  Let $\{X_i: i\in{\mathbb T}_k\}$ be $\ell$-dependent with respect to $\mu$ with $\ell<n/2$. Then for any $\gamma>0$,
	$$\int \sum_{i\in{\mathbb T}_k} X_i f d\mu\;\leq\; \frac{2}{\gamma}\Big\{H(f|\mu)\,+\,\frac{1}{\ell}\sum_{i\in{\mathbb T}_k}\log \int e^{\gamma \ell X_i} d\mu\Big\}\,,$$
	where $H(f |\mu)$ is the relative entropy of $d\nu =f d\mu$ with respect to $d\mu$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma F.4 in \cite{jm}
Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.02104

body: Green-Tao theorem: The sequence of prime numbers contains arbitrarily long finite arithmetic progressions; that is, for every natural number k >= 1 there exist positive integers a and d such that the k numbers a, a + d, a + 2d, ..., a + (k-1)d are all prime. (The progressions are finite: no infinite arithmetic progression can consist only of primes.) The theorem was proved by Ben Green and Terence Tao in 2004; the proof extends Szemeredi's theorem, via a transference principle, from sets of positive density in the integers to subsets of positive relative density inside a pseudorandom set of almost primes.
title: Green–Tao theorem

[Proposition 18 (Structural properties of the Einstein--Navier--Stokes models) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Consider the system of equations in \autoref{def-prod-areal-flow} under the pressure assumptions~\eqref{hyperbolic-eos-zero}.
Then the following properties hold for sufficiently regular solutions~$(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$.
\bei

\item \emph{Hyperbolicity.} \emph{Under the non-vacuum condition $- \Jbb \cdot \Jbb>0$,} the evolution system consisting of~\eqref{eqchi-evol} and either~\eqref{prod-energy-conservation} or~\eqref{energy-dissip-Sigma} is a first-order hyperbolic system of $12+\dim\mathscr E$ nonlinear balance laws with characteristic cones in the causal cone.

\item \emph{Constraint propagation.}  Given a solution of this hyperbolic system, if the constraints~\eqref{eqchi-constr} on $\log\Omega, K_2, K_3$ are satisfied at initial time they propagate to all future times.

\item \emph{Equivalence property.}
Given such a solution $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$, together with the value of the modular parameter~$\tau$ at one spacetime point and the spatial averages of $G,H$ at initial time, one recovers a unique solution $(g,\beta,\zeta)$ of the Einstein--Navier--Stokes equations, specifically a particle-production relaxation flow (\autoref{def-prod-pot}) or dissipated-energy relaxation flow (\autoref{def-diss-en}).
In particular, the wave equation for the lapse~\eqref{eq:waveconffac-NS} below holds.

\item \emph{Particle-number current.}
The convex current derived from the potential~$\chi$ satisfies
\bel{eq:pot-areal-production}
\aligned
\divuntrois\vNumb_\chi
& = \mathfrak d_{\mathscr B}
\quad && \text{(particle-production areal flow),}
\\
\divuntrois\vNumb_\chi & = 0
\quad && \text{(dissipated-energy areal flow),}
\endaligned
\ee
where $\mathfrak d_{\mathscr B} = \zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta) \geq 0$.
\eei (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Structural properties of the Einstein--Navier--Stokes models

[Lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $T$ and ${\mathcal{C}}$ be as in the proposition. Then $\lambda$ is a Bousfield localization such that the unit is pointwise given by cocartesian edges.
    \begin{proof}
        The first statement is clear as $\lambda$ is left adjoint to the fully faithful inclusion ${\mathcal{C}}(1)\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{C}}$. For the identification of the units, let $x\in{\mathcal{C}}(A)$ and let $\tilde a\colon x\to x'$ be a cocartesian lift of the unique map $a\colon A\to 1$. Then
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                {\textup{Hom}}_{\textup{Un}^\textup{ct}}(x',y)\arrow[d]\arrow[r, "-\circ\tilde a"] & {\textup{Hom}}_{\textup{Un}^\textup{ct}}(x,y)\arrow[d]\\
                {\textup{Hom}}_T(1,1)\arrow[r, "-\circ a"']&{\textup{Hom}}_T(A,1)
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        is a pullback by definition of cocartesian edges. As both spaces in the bottom row are contractible, we see that ${\textup{Hom}}(\tilde a,y)$ is an equivalence. Letting $y$ vary, this is precisely the defining property of a unit for our Bousfield localization.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'

continuous representative, which we identify with $T_t^qf$.
Furthermore, the following statements hold with $u(t,x)=T_t^qf(x)
$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},ref=\textup{(\roman*)}]

For every $k\in\N_0$, $\partial_t^ku$ and

continuous there.

For every $t>0$, $\partial_xu(t,\cdot)\in\AC_{\loc}(I)$, and for almost every $x\in I$,

  \partial_tu(t,x)

  +b(x)\partial_xu(t,x)-q(x)u(t,x).
\end{equation}
For every $k\in\N_0$, the same assertions hold with $u$ replaced by
$\partial_t^ku$.

If $a$, $b$, and $q$ are continuous on $I$, then

and \eqref{eq:a.e.-PDE} holds pointwise on $(0,\infty)\times I$.  Moreover,
$\partial_t^ku\in C^{1,2}((0,\infty)\times I)$ for every $k\in\N_0$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.02169, '2609.02169'] Let $R$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$.  Let
$\pi:\mathscr X\to\Spec R$ be a smooth projective family of geometrically
integral surfaces, let $\mathscr M$ be a line bundle, and suppose that
$\mathscr E=\pi_*\mathscr M$ is finite free and commutes with base change.
Let $\mathscr V\subset\mathscr E$ be a saturated free submodule of rank
three.  Put $V_K=\mathscr V\otimes_RK$ and
$V_0=\mathscr V\otimes_Rk$, and assume that their evaluation maps define
dominant rational maps $f_K:\mathscr X_K\dashrightarrow\PP(V_K^\vee)$
and $f_0:\mathscr X_0\dashrightarrow\PP(V_0^\vee)$.  Then
$\deg(f_0)\leq\deg(f_K)$.

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2606.00945, 'Ising model and percolation: from hexagonal lattice to 3-12 lattice'] Fix a bounded $3$-polygon $(\Omega; A, B, C)$. Suppose $\PO$ is the unique conformal map from $\Omega$ onto the equilateral triangle $\rhd$ with three vertices $(1, \tau, \tau^2)$ such that $\PO(A)=1, \PO(B)=\tau, \PO(C)=\tau^2$. 
Suppose $(\Omega_{\312}^{\delta}; A^{\delta}, B^{\delta}, C^{\delta})$ is a family of discrete polygons such that $(\Omega_{\312}^{\delta}; A^{\delta}, B^{\delta}, C^{\delta})$ converges to $(\Omega; A, B, C)$ in the Carathéodory sense as $\delta\to 0$. 
Consider site percolation with $p=1/2$ in $\Omega_{\312}^{\delta, *}$. 
Then the observable $\PO_{\312}^{\delta}$ defined in~\eqref{eqn::perco_observable} converges to $\PO$ uniformly as $\delta\to 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

	$\varepsilon>0$, the stroke layer recovers every concept's stroke set exactly from its
	clean cue in the sense that, with probability $1-o(1)$,
	\[
	x_\mu(\eta^{(\alpha)})=\mathbf 1\{\mu\in S_\alpha\}
	\qquad\text{for all }\alpha\le P\text{ and all }\mu\in\mathcal U.
	\]
	Moreover, for each fixed $\alpha$, the same conclusion holds without the union over
	$\alpha$ (i.e.\ only for the fixed cue $\eta^{(\alpha)}$).

	whenever

	PL \le N_f^{a-\varepsilon}.

[Proposition prop:music-chordal-residual of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Let \(Z=\{{\bm z}_1,\ldots,{\bm z}_s\}\) be a configuration for which
$
    G_Z:=\Phi_Z^*\Phi_Z
$
is invertible, and set
\[
    Q_Z:=\Phi_ZG_Z^{-1/2}.
\]
Then \(Q_Z^*Q_Z=I_s\) and
\[
    \sum_{j=1}^s\widetilde q({\bm z}_j)
    =
    \|(I-P_{\widetilde{\mathcal U}})\Phi_Z\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2.
\]
If
\[
    (1-\mu)I_s
    \preceq
    G_Z
    \preceq
    (1+\mu)I_s,\qquad 0<\mu<1,
\]
then
\begin{eqnarray}
    (1-\mu)
    d_{\mathrm{ch}}^2(
        \mathcal U_Z,\widetilde{\mathcal U}
    )
    \leq
    \sum_{j=1}^s\widetilde q({\bm z}_j)
    \leq
    (1+\mu)
    d_{\mathrm{ch}}^2(
        \mathcal U_Z,\widetilde{\mathcal U}
    ),
\end{eqnarray}
where
\[
    d_{\mathrm{ch}}^2(
        \mathcal U_Z,\widetilde{\mathcal U}
    )
    :=
    \|(I-P_{\widetilde{\mathcal U}})Q_Z\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
    =
    \frac12
    \|P_{\mathcal U_Z}
       -P_{\widetilde{\mathcal U}}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2.
\]

[Theorem 27 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Suppose $U = \sum_{j=0}^\infty u^j$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{asmp:main for refreshing} for some $\beta >0$ and let $\alpha \in (0,1)$ such that $\alpha + \beta/2 > 1$. Let
    \[p >\frac{ \beta}{\alpha + \beta/2-1} \lor \frac{\beta}{\alpha}\]
    and suppose for some $K \geq 1$, 
     we have that for all $j \in \N,$ and  $n \in \{0,1,2\},$
     \begin{equation*}
         \|\nabla^n u^j\|_{L^p_\omega \continuous^0_{t,x}} \leq K 2^{(n-\alpha)j}.
     \end{equation*}
     Then there exist $\delta(\alpha,\beta,p)>0, \gamma(\alpha,\beta,p)>0$, and a random field $M : \T^d \to [1,\infty)$ such that $\gamma \to \infty$ as $p \to \infty$ and
        \begin{enumerate}
         \item almost surely $\sup_{y \in \T^d} |M(y)| < \infty$; in fact $\E \big[\big(\log \log\big(\sup_{y \in \T^d} |M(y)| + e\big)\big)^{\gamma}\big]<\infty$,
         \item $\E \big[\big(\log\big(\|M\|_{L^p_y} + 1\big)\big)^{\gamma}\big]<\infty$,
         \item and for any $y,z \in \T^d$, any $w \in C^{1/2 + \delta}([0,1])$ with $w_0=0$, if we have any solution $X$ to~\eqref{eq:main refreshing ODE 0}, and any solution $\tilde X$ to 
          \begin{equation*}
         \tilde X_t=z+\int_0^t U(s,\tilde X_s)\,ds+w_t,\qquad t\in[0,1],
         \end{equation*}
         then we have the stability estimate on the time interval $[0,1]$,
         \[\|X - \tilde X\|_{C^{1/2 +\delta}_t} \leq M(y)\big(|y-z| + \|w\|_{C^{1/2+\delta}_t}\big),\]
        and, in the case that $w=0$, the expansion/compression estimate for all $t \in [0,1],$
        \[\frac{1}{M(y)} |y-z| \leq |X_t - \tilde X_t| \leq M(y) |y-z|.\]
     \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem \cite{ferrari1991microscopic}, Lemma 3.3 of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] Let $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \dots, \lambda_n \geq 0$ be given such that

[Proposition prop:adaptive of arXiv:2608.23638, 'Replicable Conformal Prediction'] Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $\rho\in(0,1]$, and a score law with density $f$ continuous and positive at $q=F^{-1}(1-\alpha)$; let $\hat f_n$ be any shared pilot with $\hat f_n\to_pf(q)$, $\hat f_n\ge f_0>0$, independent of both calibration samples, and run \textsc{ReCal}{} with $\beta_n=2B_n/(\hat f_n\rho)$, $\hat\kappa{=}1$. Then, with $Z$ standard normal,
(i) $\mathbb{P}[\tau\neq\tau']\to\mathbb{E}[\min(\rho|Z|/2,1)]\le\rho\sqrt{2/\pi}/2<2\rho/5$;
(ii) $\mathbb{E} F(\tau)-\tfrac{k}{n+1}=(1+o(1))\,B_n/\rho$; and
(iii) $\mathbb{P}[F(\tau)\le\tfrac{k}{n+1}+e_n(\delta)+(2+o(1))B_n/\rho]\ge1-\delta-o(1)$.
The width, hence the premium, carries no $\kappa$: the factor $\kappa^{2}$ in Corollary~(cor:protocol of the paper) is a finite-sample certificate, not an asymptotic necessity, and (ii)--(iii) meet Corollary~(cor:sizelb of the paper) within an absolute factor; a $\sqrt{2/\pi}$ width makes (i) exactly $\rho$. (Proof: Appendix~(app:upper of the paper); empirical check: Appendix~(app:exp of the paper).) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 12 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] There exists $r > 0$ such that the following holds. Take $\epsilon \in (0,1)$. There exist $C = C_{\epsilon} > 0$ and $N = N_{\epsilon} \ge 1$ depending on $\epsilon$ such that for $n \ge N$ and for $l$ and $j$ satisfying either
 $$ \epsilon M  \le l \le M \ \ \text{ and } \ \  \epsilon l \le j \le (1- \epsilon ) l $$
 or 
 $$ (1 + \epsilon ) M \le l \le 2M \ \ \text{ and } \ \  l-M \le j \le M,$$
 we have 
 $$ P \Big( W (1) \cap W (2) \cap \cdots \cap W (9) \Big) \ge P \big( W (1) \big) \Big\{ 1 - C (\log n)^{-\frac{1}{2}} (\log \log n)^{r} \Big\}.$$
title: Lem 12 of arXiv:2604.01748

body: In mathematics, low-rank approximation refers to the process of approximating a given matrix by a matrix of lower rank. More precisely, it is a minimization problem, in which the cost function measures the fit between a given matrix and an approximating matrix, subject to a constraint that the approximating matrix has reduced rank. The problem is used for mathematical modeling and data compression. The rank constraint is related to a constraint on the complexity of a model that fits the data. In applications, often there are other constraints on the approximating matrix apart from the rank constraint, e.g., non-negativity and Hankel structure.
title: Low-rank approximation

[Lemma 190 (Covariant divergence identity for the elliptic-hyperbolic current) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let 
	$\SigmatTan$ be a $\Sigma_t$-tagnent vectorfield,
	let $\ellipticCoerciveQuadratic[\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]$
	be the quadratic form defined by \eqref{E:NULLHYPERSURFACEADAPTEDCOERCIVEQUADRATICFORM},
	and let $\widetilde \weight$ be an arbitrary ``weight function,'' not necessarily the weight $\weight$ from \eqref{E:BLOWUPWEIGHT}. 
	Then the following identity holds relative to the Cartesian coordinates, 
	where $\Dfour$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $\gfour$:
	\begin{align}	
		\begin{split} 
			\widetilde \weight \ellipticCoerciveQuadratic[\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			& = \Dfour_{\alpha} (\widetilde \weight \ehcurrent^{\alpha}[\SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan])
			+
			\widetilde \weight
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\textnormal{Antisymmetric)}}[\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			+
			\widetilde \weight
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\textnormal{Div})}[\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			\\
			& \ \
			+
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\pmb{\partial} \widetilde \weight)}[\SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			+
			\widetilde \weight
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\textnormal{Absorb}-1)}[\SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			+
			\widetilde \weight
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\textnormal{Absorb}-2)}[\SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			\\
			& \ \
			+
			\widetilde \weight
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\textnormal{Material})}[\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			+
			\widetilde \weight
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\textnormal{Null Geometry})}[\SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan],
		\end{split}
	\end{align}
	where with 
	$(\mathrm{d} \SigmatTan_{\flat})_{\alpha \beta} 
	\eqdef \partial_{\alpha} \SigmatTan_{\beta} 
	- 
	\partial_{\beta} \SigmatTan_{\alpha}
	$,
	we have:
	\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align} 
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\textnormal{Antisymmetric)}}[\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			& \eqdef
			 \frac{1}{2} \Nullhypersurfaceproject_{\beta}^{\ \alpha} \Nullhypersurfaceproject_{\gamma}^{\ \delta} (\mathrm{d} \SigmatTan_\flat)_{\alpha\gamma} (\mathrm{d} \SigmatTan_\flat)_{\kappa\delta} (\gfour^{-1})^{\beta\kappa}  (\gfour^{-1})^{\gamma\nu}
			\\
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\textnormal{Div})}[\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			& \eqdef
			\left( \frac{6-\sqrt{6}}{6}\right)^2 (\p_a \SigmatTan^a)^2,
			 
			\\
			\mathfrak{J}_{(\pmb{\partial} \widetilde \weight)}[\SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
			& \eqdef
			-
			\ehcurrent^{\alpha}[\SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan] \partial_{\alpha} \widetilde \weight,
			 
			\\
			\begin{split} 		 
				\mathfrak{J}_{(\textnormal{Absorb}-1)}[\SigmatTan,\pmb{\partial} \SigmatTan]
				& \eqdef
				 \Nullhypersurfaceproject_{\beta}^{\ \alpha} \Nullhypersurfaceproject_{\gamma}^{\ \delta}  \SigmatTan^{\nu} \p_\alpha \gfour_{\nu \gamma'} (\mathrm{d} \SigmatTan_\flat)_{\delta\kappa}  (\gfour^{-1})^{\beta\kappa} (\gfour^{-1})^{\gamma \gamma'}
				\\
				& \ \
				- 2 \left\{  \frac{6-\sqrt{6}}{6}\p_a \SigmatTan^a + \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6} \nullangpartial_a \SigmatTan^a + \frac{\ReciprocaluLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction \ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction}{2\MagnitueofinnerproductofnewLandnewuL} \left(\frac{3-\sqrt{6}}{6}\right) \Lunit^\perp_a \uLunit^\perp \SigmatTan^a

body:
[Theorem thm:lyapunov-stuff of arXiv:2511.10223, 'Stochastic Reaction Networks Within Interacting Compartments with Content-Dependent Fragme'] Let $X$ be a continuous-time Markov chain on a countable state space $\mathbb S$ with generator $\mathcal L$. Suppose there exists a finite set $K\subset\mathbb S$ and a positive function $V$ on $\mathbb S$ such that
\[
    \mathcal LV(x)\le-1
\]
for all $x\in\mathbb S\setminus K$. Suppose further that $X$ is not explosive. Then each state in a closed, irreducible component of $\mathbb S$ is positive recurrent. Moreover, if $\tau_{x_0}$ is the time for the process to enter the union of the closed irreducible components given an initial condition $x_0$, then $\mathbb E_{x_0}[\tau_{x_0}]<\infty$.
\begin{proof}
    See Theorem 7.3 in [Anderson_Cappelletti_Kim_Nguyen_2020].
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 46 (Density of the systematic scan) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Assume \eqref{eq:condexists} and define
\[
  \tau : \XX\times\XX \to (0,\infty), \qquad

\]
Then $\tau$ is $\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable, strictly positive at every point of
$\XX\times\XX$, and
\[
  T_{\mathrm{sc}}(A \mid x) = \int_{A} \tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)
  \qquad (A \in \XXA,\ x \in \XX) .
\]

body: In mathematics, power iteration (also known as the power method) is an eigenvalue algorithm: given a diagonalizable matrix $A$, the algorithm will produce a number $\lambda$, which is the greatest (in absolute value) eigenvalue of $A$, and a nonzero vector $v$, which is a corresponding eigenvector of $\lambda$, that is, $Av=\lambda v$. The algorithm is also known as the Von Mises iteration.

Nevertheless h(n)-n=n^beta is not O(n^q log n) for q<beta. This is a counterexample to a generic inference, not an iid lattice FPP law.

G|_{\widehat{\mathcal{E}}^{n}}={\bf g}(n);\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z},

\]

PRIVATE AUTHOR-CHECKED DRAFT, no independent review. Let n be even, Z_1, Z_2 independent standard Gaussians, (g_i) independent N(0, sigma^2) with sigma small, and X_i = Z_1 + g_i for i <= n/2, X_i = Z_2 + g_i for i > n/2. Then (a) with probability tending to one as sigma -> 0 there are two near-maximal indices with correlation R = 0 (multiple peaks in Chatterjee's sense with deficit |Z_1 - Z_2| of order one), (b) Var(max_i X_i) -> Var(max(Z_1, Z_2)) > 0, so the field is not superconcentrated relative to its variance scale, and (c) the argmax half is determined by sign(Z_1 - Z_2) and is unchanged under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise of size t unless t exceeds a level of order |Z_1 - Z_2|, so the field is not chaotic. Hence any multiple-peaks condition that admits two peaks cannot be equivalent to chaos or superconcentration; this refutes the two-peak reading of Chatterjee's open problem 6 in 'Chaos, concentration, and multiple valleys' and leaves the growing-number version open.

body:
[Prop 12 (Terminal-to-earlier differential blocks) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Use the notation of Theorem~\ref{thm:arbitrary-path-kernel} and put
\[
 r=Q-P,
 \qquad
 R_P(x,y)
 =
 \sum_{k=0}^{P-1}
 \frac{k!}{(k+r)!}
 L_k^{(r)}(x)L_k^{(r)}(y).
\]
For $h\geq0$ and an operator $C$, define
\[
 C^{\mathrm{fall}\,0}=I,
 \qquad
 C^{\mathrm{fall}\,h}
 =
 C(C-I)\cdots(C-(h-1)I)
 \quad(h\geq1).
\]
Let $E_y=y\,\frac{\dd}{\dd y}$. Fix $t<T$ and put
\[
 A=P-p_t,
 \qquad
 B=Q-q_t.
\]
If $\epsilon_t=1$, then
\begin{equation}
 K(T,x;t,y)
 =
 \left(\frac{\dd}{\dd y}\right)^A
 (rI+E_y)^{\mathrm{fall}\,B}R_P(x,y).
\end{equation}
If $\epsilon_t=0$, then
\begin{equation}
 K(T,x;t,y)
 =
 \left(\frac{\dd}{\dd y}\right)^B
 (E_y-rI)^{\mathrm{fall}\,A}
 [y^rR_P(x,y)].
\end{equation}
At the terminal level,
\begin{equation}
 K(T,x;T,y)=\ee^{-y}y^rR_P(x,y).
\end{equation}
Apart from the outgoing-step gauge, these blocks depend only on $(p_t,q_t)$ and $(P,Q)$.

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. A nearest-neighbour proxy for the bias shift (P35, the simplex's out-of-fold residuals at the nearest calibration rows standing in for its bias at the scored rows): P35 (a) REFUTED: the full-shift blend reads -0.69 vs the R-blend on EMIT split B and -0.12 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.08 and -0.14 on split C; (c) REFUTED: cross-only vs full on EMIT -0.05 vs -0.62 (split B); falsifier (either variant worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. Scarce calibration, the ratio-metric criterion (P41, 240 calibration rows, split B, three-vertex form, registered and R_1 choices side by side): P41 (a) HELD: at n_cal = 240 the R_1 blend reads +1.17 vs the simplex on EMIT (within 1.0; the registered three-vertex blend reads -1.83); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R_1 blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells (at least 25); (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on EMIT +1.38 (at least +1.0); falsifier (R_1 worse than the simplex by more than 2.0 on EMIT) not triggered. So the P30 caveat is confined to the squared-loss criterion; the criterion in the score's own metric keeps the simplex where it should at scarce calibration.
the members' predictions on the rows to be scored are available (transductive setting); their targets are not
the blend w(t) = (1 - t) w_simplex + t w_leastsquares is linear in t, so the cross-validated and bootstrap predictions of every t come from the two base estimators' predictions; the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows

Lindeberg-Levy form: let X_1, X_2, ... be independent identically distributed random variables with mean mu and finite variance sigma^2 > 0, and let bar X_n = (X_1 + ... + X_n) / n. Then sqrt(n) (bar X_n - mu) / sigma converges in distribution to the standard normal law: P(sqrt(n) (bar X_n - mu) / sigma <= x) -> Phi(x) for every real x. Lindeberg-Feller form: for a triangular array of independent, mean-zero rows with s_n^2 = sum_k Var(X_{n,k}), the normalised sums S_n / s_n converge to N(0, 1) provided the Lindeberg condition holds: for every epsilon > 0, (1 / s_n^2) sum_k E[X_{n,k}^2 ; |X_{n,k}| > epsilon s_n] -> 0.
finite, non-zero variance; with infinite variance the limit, when it exists, is a stable law
independence (identically distributed in the Lindeberg-Levy form, the Lindeberg condition otherwise)

[Lemma lem-LF-SLE of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $W \in (0, \frac{\gamma^2}2)$ and $\alpha = Q - \frac W{2\gamma}$. 
	    Sample $(\psi, \eta^\mathrm{wp})$ from $\frac1{2\pi(Q-\alpha)} \mathrm{LF}_{\mathbb C}^{(\alpha, 0), (\gamma, 1), (2Q-\alpha, \infty)} \times \mathrm{SLE}_\kappa^\mathrm{wp}(W-2)$. For each connected component $B$ of $\mathbb{C} \backslash \eta^\mathrm{wp}$, let $p_B$ and $q_B$ be the first and last points of $\partial B$ hit by $\eta^\mathrm{wp}$. Let $\tilde \mathcal{W}$ be the collection of all quantum surfaces $(B, \psi, p_B, q_B)/{\sim_\gamma}$, and  endow $\tilde \mathcal{W}$ with the ordering where $(B_1, \psi, p_{B_1}, q_{B_1})/{\sim_\gamma}$ precedes $(B_2, \psi, p_{B_2}, q_{B_2})/{\sim_\gamma}$ if $\eta^\mathrm{wp}$ hits $q_{B_1}$ for the last time before it hits $q_{B_2}$ for the last time. 
	
	    
	    Let $B_\bullet$ be the connected component of $\mathbb{C} \backslash \eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$ containing $1$, and let $\mathcal{B}_\bullet = (B_\bullet, \psi, 1, p_{B_\bullet}, q_{B_\bullet})/{\sim_\gamma}$. Let $ \mathcal{D} \subset \tilde \mathcal{W}$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{W} \subset \tilde \mathcal{W}$) be the ordered collection of elements that come before (resp.\ after) $(B_\bullet, \psi, p_{B_\bullet}, q_{B_\bullet})/{\sim_\gamma}$. Then the joint law of $(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{B}_\bullet, \mathcal{W})$ is $(1 - \frac{2W}{\gamma^2})^2 {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2}(W) \times {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{1,2}(\gamma^2 - W) \times \mathcal{M}^\mathrm{wed}(W)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:torsor of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] For every open interval $I$, the subgroup of $\mathcal{G}$ of
		distortions with continuous positive derivative on $(0,1)$ acts
		freely and transitively on the laws of $\mathcal{D}_{+}$ with support
		$\overline{I}$, and the full group $\mathcal{G}$ acts so on the
		enlargement of $\mathcal{D}_{+}$ by all laws whose restricted
		distribution function is an absolutely continuous homeomorphism with
		absolutely continuous inverse: for two such laws $f, g$ the unique
		$A \in \mathcal{G}$ with $\alpha_{A}f = g$ is
		\begin{equation}
			A = F_{g}\circ Q_{f}.
			
		\end{equation}
		Consequently, for a reference law $f_{0} \in \mathcal{D}_{+}^{2}$
		with support $\overline{I}$, the potential map is the coadjoint
		orbit map $A \mapsto \operatorname{Ad}^{*}_{A}U_{f_{0}}$, and its
		fibers are the cosets of the stabilizer, which by
		Theorem~(thm:fibers of the paper) is the conjugated M\"obius group
		\begin{equation}
			\operatorname{Stab}_{\mathcal{G}}(U_{f})

		sense, on the $C^{3}$-regular part of the fiber.

[campaign result 2026-09-14, Author-checked, no independent read.] This is an elementary special case recorded alongside Open Problem 14.12 in David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html). Let K_n be the complete simple graph with n>=2 vertices and start one particle per vertex. Each particle jumps independently at rate one to a uniformly chosen different vertex; particles merge on meeting. If T_coal is the time until one particle remains, then E[T_coal]=sum_{k=2}^n (n-1)/(k(k-1))=(n-1)^2/n. The discrete-time simple-walk matrix has n-1 nonconstant eigenvalues all equal to -1/(n-1), so its spectral mean hitting-time sum K=sum_{j=2}^n 1/(1-lambda_j) is also (n-1)^2/n. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
Complete graph; rate-one simple walks; one initial particle at every vertex.

The masses p_r = (r mu - 2 beta)/r, p_{r+1} = (2 beta - (r-1) mu)/(r+1) and p_0 = 1 - p_r - p_{r+1} are nonnegative, p_{r+1} = 0 when r = m, and the law on {0, r, r+1} with these masses has the same mu and beta as N and P(> 0) equal to the optimized bound D. So the bound is sharp for every feasible pair (mu, beta).
N is integer valued with 0 <= N <= m

[Proposition 40 (Universal factorization of finite-dimensional triangular tests) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $m\in\mathbb N$, let $C\in\mathcal L(H,\mathbb R^m)$, and let
$B\in\mathcal L(\mathfrak I(H),\mathbb R^m)$.  For an accessible type, the
restarted finite-dimensional triangular system
\begin{equation}
 \dd Y_r^{P,s}=C\,\dd X_r+B\bigl(U_r^{P,s}\otimes\dd X_r\bigr),
 \qquad Y_s^{P,s}=0,
\end{equation}
where $U^{P,s}$ solves the first equation in
\eqref{eq:primitive-triangular-system}, has the coordinatewise It\^o solution
\begin{equation}
 Y_{s,t}^{P,s}=C X_{s,t}+B V_{s,t}^{P,s}.
\end{equation}
Consequently its complete restarted response is a stable-causal
readout of $\mathcal J_\tau Z_\tau$.  Thus every coefficient-defined
finite-dimensional triangular It\^o test whose second-order coefficient
extends continuously to $\mathfrak I(H)$ factors through the single
operator-valued step-two signature response.

Let p = Bernoulli(a) and q = Bernoulli(b) with a, b in [0, 1]. Every coupling is determined by t = P(X = 1, Y = 1): its table is P(1,1) = t, P(1,0) = a - t, P(0,1) = b - t, P(0,0) = 1 - a - b + t, and these are nonnegative exactly for t in [max(0, a + b - 1), min(a, b)]. The mismatch probability is a + b - 2t, so it takes every value in [|a - b|, 1 - |a + b - 1|], each for exactly one coupling.

[Theorem 23 (Subcritical shape) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] Suppose $p = o(1/m)$. Then
  $(T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0})/m \stackrel{P}{\to} 0$ as $m \to \infty$.
  It follows that $(T_{m,p} - m \log{m})/m$ converges
  in law to a standard Gumbel distribution.
  \begin{proof}
    The first claim follows by observing that $\PP(T_{m, 0} = T_{m, p}) = (1-p)^m \to 1$.
    Then Proposition~\ref{thm:classical mgf convergence}
    confirms $m^{-t}\,M_{T_{m,0}}(t/m) \to \Gammaop(1-t)$.
    By Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} and Definition~\ref{def:Gumbel},
    $(T_{m,0} - m \log{m})/m$ converges in law to a standard Gumbel.
    By Slutsky's theorem, so does $(T_{m,p} - m \log{m})/m$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Subcritical shape

[Lemma lem:fixed.point.certificate of arXiv:2604.22453, 'Adapted Wasserstein Barycenters of Gaussian Processes'] Let $(\mathbf M_t,\mathbf Y_t)$ satisfy (equation eq:FPE.unrestricted of the paper) and set $\mathbf P_t:=\mathbf M_t\mathbf M_t^\intercal$,
\[
Z_t^k:=\lambda_k(L_{\cdot,t}^k)^\intercal\mathbf Y_t(\mathbf M_t^k)^\intercal,
\qquad k\in[K],
\qquad
\mathbf S_t:=\diag(Z_t^1,\ldots,Z_t^K)-\mathbf C_t.
\]
Then each $Z_t^k$ is symmetric positive semidefinite and $\mathbf S_t\mathbf P_t=0$.  Consequently, if $\mathbf S_t\succeq0$, then $\mathbf P_t$ is a global minimizer of $\Phi_t$ over $\mathscr{P}_+(K,d)$.

$\sup\limits_{\alpha\in A}\|f_\alpha\|_\infty<\infty$ and $\|f_\alpha\|_{L_1({\mathcal M},\tau)}\to0,$
then
$$\|f_\alpha\|_{E({\mathcal M},\tau)}\to0.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 130 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $X^1$ and $X^2$ be solutions to SDEs
    \[
    dX^i(t)
    =
    b^i(t,X^i(t))\,dt
    +
    \sigma^i(t,X^i(t))\,dB_t\,,
    \]
such that $X^1(q_*)$ and $X^2(q_*)$ are equidistributed.
Suppose for some finite constant $\oL$ that the SDE coefficients $b^i$ and $\sigma^i$ are uniformly bounded by $\oL$, and moreover are $\oL$-Lipschitz in the space coordinate. Lastly suppose
	\[
    \sup_{(t,x)\in [q_*
    ,1]\times \mathbb R}
    \bigg\{
    \Big|b^1(t,x) - b^2(t,x)\Big|
    +
 	\Big|\sigma^1(t,x)-\sigma^2(t,x)\Big|
    \bigg\}
    \le \epsilon\,.
    \]
Then the marginal laws of $X^1$ and $X^2$ are close in $L^2$-Wasserstein distance for all time: more precisely, there is a coupling of $X^1$ with $X^2$ under which
	\[
	\sup\bigg\{
	\E\bigg[\Big(X^1(t)-X^2(t)\Big)^2\bigg] 
	: t\in[q_*
        ,1]
	\bigg\} \le 
	C(\oL) \epsilon^2\,,
	\]
where $C(\oL)$ denotes a constant depending only on $\oL$.

\begin{proof}
Couple $X^1$ and $X^2$ with the same Brownian motion $B$, and same initial value (almost surely). For this coupling let $Z(t) = X^1(t)-X^2(t)$, and $E(t) = \E[Z(t)^2]$. By It\=o's formula, for any
$0\le t\le t'\le1$, we have
	\[
	E(t')-E(t)
	=\E \int_t^{t'} \bigg\{
		2 Z(s)
		\Big(b^1(s,X^1(s))-b^2(s,X^2(s))
		\Big)
	+\Big( \sigma^1(s,X^1(s))
		-\sigma^2(s,X^2(s))
		\Big)^2
		\bigg\}\,ds\,.
	\]
For $s\in[q_*,1]$, using that $b^1$ and $b^2$ are $\epsilon$-close to one another, and $\oL$-Lipschitz in the space coordinate, gives
	\[
	\Big|b^1(s,X^1(s))-b^2(s,X^2(s))
	\Big|
	\le \oL\Big| X^1(s)-X^2(s)\Big|
		+ \epsilon
	=\oL |Z(s)|
		+ \epsilon\,.
	\]
A similar bound holds with $\sigma^i$ in place of $b^i$. It follows that 
for $[t,t']\subseteq[q_*,1]$, we have
	\[
	E(t')-E(t)
	\le 3
	\E \int_t^{t'}
	\Big(\oL |Z(s)| + \epsilon\Big)^2\,ds
	\le 6 \bigg\{
	\oL^2 \int_t^{t'} E(s)\,ds
	+ \epsilon^2 (t'-t)
	\bigg\}\,.
	\]
The claimed bound follows from Gr\"onwall's inequality. More precisely, we can use the form stated in \cite[Lem.~6.1]{MR1071170} which says that if for all $t\in[q_*
    ,1]$ we have
	\[
	E(t) \le a(t) +\int_{q_0}^t b(s) E(s)\,ds
	\]
with $a,b$ continuous nonnegative functions, then it holds that
	\[
	E(1)
	\leq 
	E(q_*)
	+
	\int_{q_*
        }^1
	a(s)b(s)
	\exp
	\lt(
	\int_s^1 b(r)\,dr
	\rt)\,ds.
	\]
In our setting $E(q_*)=0$, $b(t)=6\oL^2$, and $a(t)=6\epsilon^2(t-q_*)$. Therefore
$a(1) \le 6\epsilon^2$, and the claimed bound follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 161 (Completeness of the upper-expectation space) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] For every separable Banach space $B$ and $1\le p<\infty$,
$\mathcal L_{\cP}^p(B)$ is a Banach space.  Consequently,
$\mathbb L_{\cP}^p(B)$ is a closed Banach subspace.  If $\cP=\{P\}$, these
spaces reduce to the usual $L^p(P;B)$ space and the $L^p(P)$ closure of
$C_b(\Omega;B)$, respectively.

[Corollary 6 (Stationary Choquet-integral asymptotics) of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] Let \(\bm X\) be a continuous stationary Gaussian process satisfying
Assumptions~\ref{R1}--\ref{R2} on \([0,T]\), and fix \(L>0\).  Let
\((\nu,\psi)\) be \(L\)-admissible Choquet data in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-choquet-data}, and assume that the stationary
limiting model in Theorem~\ref{thm:stationary_case} is non-trivial for
\(\Gamma^{\nu,\psi}\).  Set
\[
  \mathcal H_{\nu,\psi}^{\mathrm{stat}}(L)
  =
  \mathcal H_{\Gamma^{\nu,\psi},L,\alpha,V_{I,I},\Sigma,\bm b}.
\]
Then, as \(u\to\infty\),
\begin{equation}
  
  \pk{
    \Gamma_{[0,T]}^{\nu,\psi}\bigl(\uu(\bm X-u\bm b)\bigr)
    > L u^{-2\lambda_\nu/\alpha}
  }
  \sim
  T\,\mathcal H_{\nu,\psi}^{\mathrm{stat}}(L)\,
  u^{2/\alpha-|I|}\,
  \varphi_\Sigma(u\bb).
\end{equation}
The constant \(\mathcal H_{\nu,\psi}^{\mathrm{stat}}(L)\) is finite and
positive.

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent mathematical, priority and target-scope audit pending. # Neutral truth/false bundles defeat the smaller-count hypothesis

T379-C016 v2, proof (unaudited), exact checks PASS; independent audit pending.
Targets 1/2: auxiliary-route failure, no target score claimed.

For every integer m>=5 and N>=3 set K=3m,r=3(m-1),d=1. In the two
variable contexts L,R suppose the known truth unions have sizes
s=2(m-1),t=r, respectively. There are N-2 fixed known S contexts.
No partition tags are supplied. Both orientations remain compatible:
if L is A its r-support contains C_L of size s; if R is A its support
is exactly C_R of size r. Such unions have positive probability from
actual untagged factual samples with ell=0, e.g. one occurrence of
every known truth, n=s+r. The identities can be permuted within each
context without affecting the construction or source probabilities.

Put lambda=1/(NK). Partition the variable-context atoms as follows:

* B: all K-s=m+2 atoms outside C_L and two atoms outside C_R;
* T: all s known L truths and any s of the known R truths;
* Z: the remaining m-1 known R truths and its one remaining outside atom.

B has m+4 atoms; T has 4(m-1); Z has m. In either orientation and
for EVERY compatible residual L support, their source masses are

 p(B)=lambda*(m+2),
 p(T)=lambda*(4m-2),
 p(Z)=lambda*m.

For B, if L is A its residual true count is r-s=m-1, so
p(B)=(m-1)/(Nr)+2/(NK)=lambda*(m+2). If R is A the same mass comes
from K-s systematic L atoms and no R truths. T's mass is always
s/(Nr)+s/(NK). Z's mass is (m-1)/(Nr)=m/(NK) when R is A and is
also m/(NK) when R is S. This checks invariance directly from p.

Define g as the uniform coarsening of these groups:

 g(B atom)=lambda*(m+2)/(m+4)=q,
 g(T atom)=lambda*(2m-1)/(2(m-1)),
 g(Z atom)=lambda,
 g(fixed S atom)=lambda.

The total is one and all probabilities are nonnegative. Equal lambda
scores merge Z and fixed S; their source masses remain invariant.
Thus g is source Mis_infinity=0 for every compatible world, not just
on average or conditional on a correct orientation prediction.

If L is A all three false atoms lie in B, giving H_L=3q.
If R is A two false atoms lie in B and one in Z, giving H_R=2q+lambda.
Since q<lambda, the worst-world false mass is

 max H=lambda*(3m+8)/(m+4).                              (1)

C016 v1 conjectured that the smaller known count alone gives the exact
value. Here h=s yields that conjectured value

 V_small=3lambda*(m+1)/(m+2).

The actual feasible worst risk (1) is strictly smaller, by

 V_small-max H=lambda*(m-4)/((m+2)(m+4))>0.               (2)

For m=5,N=3 these are 2/35 versus 23/405, gap 1/2835.
This refutes the entire proposed smaller-count formula; it does not
establish the optimal risk in this family. In particular the nine
complete small-alphabet score-partition checks were consistent with
the conjecture but insufficient to prove it. No general lower bound
was promoted from those computations.

The neutral Z group contains truths and possible falsehoods in exactly
the systematic true-density ratio. Its p mass is orientation-invariant
even though the known truth counts are unequal. This mechanism is
invisible to a rule that discards all surplus known truths. A general
unequal-count frontier must account for invariant weighted count
identities, not merely the minimum count or posterior risk ordering.
This is a route obstruction, not a solution of the unrestricted target.
Primary calibration basis: Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3 Definitions 1--2.

Verification: logs/neutral_bin_counterexample_check.json records 33
exact rational parameter cases and 582 compatible-world source-bin
calibration checks. It exhausts residual L supports for m=5,6,7;
larger m use the displayed general cardinality proof plus one
representative support, without claiming exhaustive enumeration there.
N>=3,K>=2,1<=r<K,0<=s,t<=r integers
One arbitrary and one systematic context, remaining contexts known S; source uniform contexts then uniform truths
Known truth identities from actual untagged factual samples and optional verifier; all compatible supports/orientations allowed
Robust source exact-level zero miscalibration; arbitrary generators

[Theorem Th2 of arXiv:2609.04080, 'On radicals in differential invariants: \\ global theory vs moving frames'] Let $\ell$ be the order of stabilization of singularities of the $G$ action on $\mathcal{E}$. Assume that stabilizers of generic points
of $\mathcal{E}^\ell$ belong to the same conjugacy class in $G$. Then there exists a quasi-section that is a $\Gamma$-section 
of the action for a finite subgroup $\Gamma\subset G$. (In particular, this is so if $G$ has one open orbit in $\mathcal{E}^\ell$.)

More generally, provided a $\Gamma$-section on $\mathcal{E}^\ell$ exists, the group $\Gamma$ can be chosen as its stabilizer. 
In this case $\mathcal{A}$ is the fixed point set of the action of $\Gamma$ by automorphisms of $\mathcal{I}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 51 of arXiv:2511.20322, 'Dissertation'] Let $X,Y : \Om \times [0,T]\times \R^d\to \R^d$ be random fields with $X\in \wHoel 0 \delt \cV(\R^d, \Lfininf(\Om)), Y\in \wHoel 0 \ga \cW(\R^d, \Lfininf(\Om))$. Define
		\[(Y\circ X)(\om, t, x) = Y(\om,t(X(\om,t,x))), \quad \om \in \Om, t\in [0,T], x\in \R^d.\]
		Then $Y\circ X$ is a random field with $Y\circ X\in \wHoel 0 {\delt\ga}{\cW\circ \cV}(\R^d, \Lfininf(\Om))$ and
		\[\nrm{Y\circ X}{\wHoel 0 {\delt\ga}{\cW\circ \cV}(\R^d, \Lpinf{p}(\Om))} \leq \nrm{Y}{\wHoel 0 \ga \cW(\R^d, \Lpinf{2p}(\Om))}(1 + \nrm{X}{\wHoel 0 \delt \cV(\R^d, \Lpinf{2p}(\Om))}), \quad p\geq 1.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem LM51 of arXiv:2608.16170, '\bf On hitting time distributions of Markov processes with sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds'] Assume that the Borel right process $X$ satisfies  (AC), (H2a) and (H2b). Let $B\in \mathscr{B}^n(E)$ be such that $\overline{B}$ is compact in $E$. Then for any $\lambda>0$ ($\lambda\geq 0$ if $X$ is transient), there exists a unique positive  measure $\nu^{(\lambda)}_B$ on $E$ such that 
\[
   p_B^{(\lambda)}(x)
   =\int_E u_\lambda(x,y)\nu^{(\lambda)}_B(\mathrm{d} y),\quad \forall x\in E. 
\]
Moreover, $\nu^{(\lambda)}_B$ is finite and concentrated on $\overline{B}$.

body:
[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2606.22611, 'Upper and Lower Bounds on Expected Soft Maxima\\of Gaussian Processes'] Let $X = (X_t)_{t \in T}$ be a centered Gaussian process on a finite index set $T$. Then
\begin{align*}
\sup_{\mu \in \eP(T)}\eF_\beta(P_X;\mu) \asymp \sup_{\mu \in \eP(T)}\eG_\beta(P_X;\mu) 
\asymp \sup_{\mu\in \eP(T)}\int_0^\Delta \Big(\sqrt{R_{\mu}(\epsilon^2)}\wedge \beta \epsilon\Big) 
\dif \epsilon.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2606.22611

				\mathrm{d}y_t &= A\left( y_t, \int_{-r}^{0} y_{\theta+t} \, \pi(\mathrm{d}\theta) \right) \mathrm{d}t + G(y_t, y_{t-r}) \, \mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}_t(\omega), \\
				y_{\theta} &= \xi_{\theta}, \quad \text{for } \theta \in [-r, 0], \quad \xi \in \mathscr{D}_{\mathbf{B}(\omega)}^{\beta, \gamma}([-r,0]),
			\end{aligned}
			\]
			where we assume that the conditions in Theorem (ASXXZA of the paper) regarding \(A\), \(\pi\), and \(G\) are satisfied, and that \(G(0,0) = 0\). Let \( \lambda_1 \) be as defined in (equation TRFVV of the paper). Then, there exists \(l > 0\) such that if \(\Vert D_{(0,0)}G \Vert < l\), the zero path is locally exponentially stable. More specifically, we can find a random variable \(R^{l}: \Omega \to (0, \infty)\) such that
			\[
			\liminf_{p \to \infty} \frac{1}{p} \log R^{l}(\theta_{pr} \omega) \geq 0,
			\]
			and for every \(\xi \in \mathscr{D}_{\mathbf{B}(\omega)}^{\beta, \gamma}([-r,0])\) with
			\[
			\Vert \xi \Vert_{\mathscr{D}_{\mathbf{B}(\omega)}^{\beta, \gamma}([-r,0])} \leq R^{l}(\omega),
			\]
			the following holds:
			\[
			\limsup_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log | y^{\xi}_t(\omega) | \leq \lambda^\epsilon < 0,
			\]
			where $y^{\xi}_{t}(\omega)$ is our solution. In particular, our local stability result holds for every \(\xi \in C^{2\gamma}([-r, 0], \mathbb{R}^n)\), where \(\frac{1}{3} < \gamma < H\) and \(\gamma\) can be chosen arbitrarily close to \(\frac{1}{3}\).

[Lemma 7 (Shifted trace quadratic form) of arXiv:2609.03958, '2609.03958'] Let $n\geq 2$ and $K\geq 0$. Suppose that $\lambda\in \Gamma_2$ satisfies $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\geq -K$ and $\sigma_2(\lambda)=f$ with $f_0\leq f\leq f_1$ for two constants $f_1\geq f_0>0$ and that $$\ell_i:=\sigma_1(\lambda)-\lambda_i,\ \ \ i=1,\ldots,n.$$
Then there exist  some constants $C>0$ and $J_0>0$ depending only on $n$, $K$, $f_0$ and $f_1$ such that  
\begin{equation}
 z_k^2+3\sum_{i\ne k}z_i^2
 -\left[1+\frac{7}{6}\frac{\ell_k}{\sigma_1(\lambda)+J_0}\right]
       \left(\sum_iz_i\right)^2
 \geq-C\left(\sum_i\ell_iz_i\right)^2
\end{equation}
 for  any $1\leq k\leq n$ and $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\in\R^n$.

body:
Let mu be a nonnegative Borel measure on R such that every polynomial is absolutely integrable and integral q(t)^2 dmu(t)>0 for every nonzero real polynomial q. Let p_j be its monic orthogonal polynomial of degree j, with p_0=1. For any integer n>=1 and any real alpha, p_n+alpha p_(n-1) has n distinct real roots r_1<...<r_n. For every integer k with 0<=k<n, the polynomial product_(i=1)^k(t-r_i) has strictly positive coefficients in the basis p_0,...,p_k. The product for k=0 is 1. The ordering from the smallest roots is essential; no restriction alpha>=0 is imposed, and no corresponding assertion is made for k=n. This is Theorem3.1 of Cohn-Kumar math/0607446v2.

[Corollary 3 (A six-vertex tree without a pure equilibrium) of arXiv:2608.24837, 'Strategic geometry of competing first-passage random walks'] The double-star tree \(G_{2,2}\) has six vertices and no pure Nash
equilibrium. Its complete optimal-strategy set is
\[
\mathcal O(G_{2,2})
=\left\{p\delta_{u_1}+(1-p)\delta_{u_2}:
\frac{228}{2153}\leq p\leq\frac{1925}{2153}\right\}.
\]
In particular, every optimal strategy randomizes over both hubs.

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Let U in R^(N by M) and V in R^(P by M) be independent arrays with fixed centered symmetric iid real entry laws, variance one and finite absolute fourteenth moments. Put X=UV^T/sqrt(N), d=NP,b=M/N, and let C_j be the ordered joint cumulant tensor of vec(X). Write T4=sum_(a,b,c,d,e,f) C4(a,b,c,d) C4(a,b,e,f) C4(c,d,e,f). For standard independent Gaussian G and all s>=0, I(X;sqrt(s)X+G)=dbs/2-db^2s^2/4+db^3s^3/6+(-db^4/8-||C4||_F^2/48)s^4+(db^5/10+b||C4||_F^2/12)s^5+(-db^6/12-5b^2||C4||_F^2/24-||C6||_F^2/1440+T4/48)s^6+R(s), with |R(s)|<=3041280 E||vec(X)||^14 s^7. If P/N->alpha>0 and M/N->beta>0 finitely, the coefficients of s^j in I/d tend for j=1,...,6 to beta/2,-beta^2/4,beta^3/6,-(beta^4+alpha beta^2)/8,beta^5/10+alpha beta^3/2, and -beta^6/12-5alpha beta^4/4-alpha^2 beta^2/12+alpha(1+alpha)beta^3/12, respectively. These limits are independent of the symmetric factor laws. The proof includes complete exact enumeration of 2197 fourth-cumulant triangle terms. The remainder is finite-dimensional and grows with dimension: this does not identify Taylor coefficients of the thermodynamic MI or justify exchanging limits.
Independent fixed real symmetric iid factor laws
Centered unit variance and finite absolute fourteenth moments
Positive finite limiting aspect ratios only for the coefficient-limit conclusion
Independent standard Gaussian noise, nats
Finite exact combinatorial enumeration in scripts/check_sixth_order.py is part of this unaudited proof
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:7f62f0f5d229c4d4fab7cc3df9b0697a63db7d47b0312fb44c0aed13c14c9b55","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/7f/7f62f0f5d229c4d4fab7cc3df9b0697a63db7d47b0312fb44c0aed13c14c9b55.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:4b63b4d5e0e27fb5fc35472ff5eb469e6c139a18443923de29d17fa9cb3919ee","bundle_entry_key":"iid-product-mi-sixth-coefficient-limits-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-all-aspect-mi-and-sixth-coefficients-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:iid-product-mi-sixth-coefficient-limits-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Prior independence of the first six finite-size MI coefficient limits

Target 1. Computer-assisted proof draft, unaudited. The finite diagram
enumeration is scripts/check_sixth_order.py; its run artifact must say
PASS before this draft is entered as a proved claim. Novelty is
unestablished. This is a theorem about limits of finite-size Taylor
coefficients. It does not interchange the Taylor expansion and the
large-matrix limit.

## Statement and explicit finite-size remainder

Let U in R^(N by M) and V in R^(P by M) have independent iid entries,
with fixed symmetric real laws, mean zero, variance one and finite
absolute fourteenth moments. The laws of U and V need not coincide.
Let X=UV^T/sqrt(N), d=NP and b=M/N. For independent standard Gaussian
noise G define I_N(s)=I(X;sqrt(s)X+G), in nats. Let C_j be the ordered
joint cumulant tensor of order j of vec(X), and put

 T_4 = sum_(a,b,c,d,e,f) C_4(a,b,c,d) C_4(a,b,e,f) C_4(c,d,e,f).

The vector input is centrally symmetric, Cov(vec X)=b I_d. Its exact
finite-dimensional Taylor polynomial through order six is

 I_N(s) = db s/2 -db^2 s^2/4 +db^3 s^3/6
   +(-db^4/8-||C_4||_F^2/48)s^4
   +(db^5/10+b||C_4||_F^2/12)s^5
   +(-db^6/12-5b^2||C_4||_F^2/24
       -||C_6||_F^2/1440+T_4/48)s^6 + R_N(s),        (1)

with the explicit bound, for all s>=0,

 |R_N(s)| <= 3041280 E||vec X||^14 s^7.              (2)

One completely factorized bound in (2) is

 E||vec X||^14 <= d^7 M^14 N^(-7)
                         E|U_11|^14 E|V_11|^14.    (3)

Let P/N->alpha in (0,infinity), M/N->beta in (0,infinity).
The coefficient of s^j in I_N(s)/d tends, for j=1,...,6, to

 c_1=beta/2,
 c_2=-beta^2/4,
 c_3=beta^3/6,
 c_4=-(beta^4+alpha beta^2)/8,
 c_5=beta^5/10+alpha beta^3/2,
 c_6=-beta^6/12-5alpha beta^4/4-alpha^2 beta^2/12
                         +alpha(1+alpha)beta^3/12. (4)

In particular none of these coefficient limits depends on the fourth
cumulant, or any higher moment, of either symmetric factor law.

## 1. Finite-dimensional Gaussian-channel coefficient extraction

First let the centrally symmetric vector X be bounded and isotropic.
Standardize the output by its covariance (1+bs)I. Relative to standard
Gaussian measure its density is 1+q_s. The Hermite generating identity is

 E exp(t.W_s-||t||^2/2)
   = exp[sum_(j>=3) C_j:t^j (s/(1+bs))^(j/2)/j!],

interpreted for coefficient extraction at zero; odd tensors vanish.
Consequently the Hermite chaos components of degrees four and six are

 q_[4] = (s/(1+bs))^2 (C_4:H_4)/4!,
 q_[6] = (s/(1+bs))^3 (C_6:H_6)/6!.

There is no degree-two component. Higher components begin at s^4.
Hermite orthogonality kills their cross terms with degrees four and six
in integral q_s^2. The entropy expansion is

 D((1+q_s)gamma || gamma)
        = (1/2) integral q_s^2 -(1/6) integral q_s^3 +O(s^7).

These local expansions are justified for bounded X in any fixed
dimension: the Mehler-density bound and Gaussian hypercontractivity
used in bounded_prior_expansion.md bound the chaos tails in L^4 for
s in a sufficiently small interval. In particular ||q_s||_4=O(s^2),
and the entropy Taylor error after the cubic term is O(||q_s||_4^4).
The scalar remainder divided by |q|^4 is bounded on [-1,infinity),
with its continuous value at q=0, so the possible endpoint q=-1
does not invalidate this argument. All constants here are allowed
to depend on the fixed bounded input and dimension.

The quadratic terms are

 ||C_4||^2 s^4/[48(1+bs)^4]
       +||C_6||^2 s^6/[1440(1+bs)^6].

For the cubic degree-four contribution, Wick pairing connects the
three Hermite factors by two edges between each pair of factors.
There are choose(4,2)^3 (2!)^3=1728 such pairings. After division by
(4!)^3 and by the entropy coefficient 6, its contribution to D is

                      -T_4 s^6/48+O(s^7).

Use I_N(s)=d log(1+bs)/2-D, and expand the displayed denominators.
This gives exactly the polynomial (1).

For its explicit remainder use the already derived posterior-replica
streaming identity in finite_moment_expansion.md. For
F(s)=E||E[X|sqrt(s)X+G]||^2, that identity bounds the k-th derivative by

 |F^(k)(s)| <= 2^k (2k)! E||X||^(2k+2).

At k=6, I_N^(7)=-F^(6)/2 gives the Taylor remainder constant
2^6 (12)!/[2(7)!]=3041280. This uses the combinatorial coefficient
bound, not an enumeration of a growing replica polynomial. It holds
on every finite SNR interval for bounded X. Symmetric norm truncation
followed by covariance whitening preserves central symmetry and
converges in L^14 to X. The finite-moment approximation argument in
finite_moment_expansion.md therefore extends (1)-(2) to finite
fourteenth moments: the polynomial tensors and remainder bounds
converge, and Gaussian-smoothed output entropy is continuous.

Finally (3) follows by Jensen first over the d coordinates and then
over the M summands in each product entry. Independence of the U and
V entry in one summand factors the fourteenth absolute moment.

## 2. Sixth-cumulant norm: its only leading terms are simple cycles

Write W_ij=u_i v_j for a single rank-one summand. Additivity and
scaling of cumulants give C_6(X)=(M/N^3) C_6(W).
Expand each U- and V-moment by its set partitions. Since the laws
are symmetric, all blocks have even size at least two. For six
positions the possible block sizes are (2,2,2), (4,2), (6).
Their coefficients are products of factor cumulants.

Each row partition imposes equality of the row indices in its blocks;
each column partition imposes the corresponding column equalities.
Non-Gaussian factor cumulants require a block of size four or six,
so there are at most two free row indices, or at most two free column
indices, in every such term. In the squared norm a second copy can
only merge index classes. Hence any term involving a higher factor
cumulant has at most five free indices and total degree at most five
in N,P. This argument applies after the moment-cumulant subtraction,
which changes coefficients but never releases an index constraint.

Terms with six free indices must have three row pairs and three
column pairs in both copies, identical respectively across copies.
For a row pairing p and column pairing q, the coefficient in C_6(W)
is one precisely when their union is a connected six-cycle. One can
see this without a limiting argument: if p,q have one shared pair,
the (4,2) subtraction cancels the moment; if p=q, the coefficient is
1-3+2=0; if their union is connected, no proper moment partition can
be factored off, so its coefficient is one.

There are 15 row pairings and eight connected column pairings for
each, giving 120. The exact script checks every one of the 225 pairs.
Consequently, with constants depending only on the fixed moments,

 ||C_6(W)||^2 =120 N^3 P^3 +polynomial of total degree <=5,
 ||C_6(X)||^2/(NP) ->120 beta^2 alpha^2.              (5)

## 3. Three fourth cumulants: complete exact index enumeration

Let k_U=E u^4-3 and k_V=E v^4-3. For the three pairings p of four
positions write delta_p(i) for its row equalities, and delta_all(i)
for equality of all four rows. The exact identity is

 C_4(W) = sum_(p!=q) delta_p(i)delta_q(j)
       +k_U delta_all(i) sum_q delta_q(j)
       +k_V delta_all(j) sum_p delta_p(i)
       +k_U k_V delta_all(i)delta_all(j).             (6)

There are 6+3+3+1=13 terms. This is just the fourth moment of u times
the fourth moment of v, minus the three covariance pairings.

In T_4(W) the three tensors use the six entry positions
(0,1,2,3), (0,1,4,5), (2,3,4,5). The script expands all 13^3 choices
in (6). Union-find separately counts the free row and column indices.
Each choice contributes exactly
N^(row classes) P^(column classes) k_U^u k_V^v.
These are integer symbolic monomials; negative numerical values of
k_U or k_V do not affect the identity.

The full polynomial is saved in logs/sixth_order_checks.json. Its
only terms of total degree at least five are

                      4 N^3 P^2+4 N^2 P^3.         (7)

Every term containing k_U or k_V has degree at most four. This is
the only computer-assisted enumeration in the proof; it is complete,
uses exact integers, has no numerical tolerance, and fits in a few
kilobytes. Its script and complete output permit every case to be
checked from (6), with no downloaded code or stochastic step.

As C_4(X)=(M/N^2)C_4(W), equation (7) implies

                T_4(X)/(NP)->4 beta^3 alpha(1+alpha). (8)

## 4. Conclusion and limitation

The fourth-cumulant norm already computed in the dossier's settled
ground, and explicitly in finite_moment_expansion.md, gives
||C_4(X)||^2/(NP)->6 beta^2 alpha. Combine this with (5),(8) and
the exact finite-size polynomial (1) to obtain all coefficients (4).

No step above asserts a size-independent bound on (2) or (3). Their
constants grow with dimension. We have not proved that the limiting
MI is six times differentiable at zero, or that its coefficients are
the limits in (4). The hardest unpaid piece of Target 1 remains a
uniform small-SNR remainder or another argument justifying the
exchange of limits. It is also open here whether all fixed-order
coefficient limits are prior independent. These findings do not

[Theorem 5 ({\cite[Theorem 1) of arXiv:2609.03171, 'Factorization patterns and fields of definition of $\ell$-torsion points on the Jacobians '] {Xing}}]
The possible characteristic polynomials of abelian varieties of dimension three over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ (where $q=p^k$) are all $f(t) \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$ of degree six satisfying one of the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $f(t)=t^{6}+a_{1}t^{5}+a_{2}t^{4}+a_{3}t^{3}+a_{2}qt^{2}+a_{1}q^{2}t+q^{3}$ whose roots are Weil numbers, $v_p(d(0))/k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for any irreducible factor $d(t)$ of $f(t)$ in $\mathbb{Q}_{p}[t]$, and the polynomial $t^{3}+a_{1}t^{2}+(a_{2}-3q)t+a_{3}-2qa_{1}$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$.
    
    \item $f(t)=(t^{2}+\beta t+q)^{3}$, where $\beta$ is equal to either:
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item $\beta=aq^{1/3}$ with $3 \mid k$, $p \nmid a$, and $|a| < 2q^{1/6}$.
        \item $\beta=\pm q^{2/3}$ with $q=8$ or $27$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    \item $f(t)=f_{1}(t)f_{2}(t)$, where $f_{1}(t)$ and $f_{2}(t)$ are the characteristic polynomials of abelian varieties of dimensions one and two, respectively.
\end{enumerate}
The abelian varieties in case (i) and case (ii) are simple, and not simple in case (iii). The abelian varieties in case (ii) are supersingular. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For a finite star with at least one leaf and positive edge lengths, and a nearest-unvisited walk that stops after all vertices are visited, every random start distribution satisfies sd(L)/E L<=1/(2*sqrt(6)). A one-leaf star has constant positive length and coefficient zero. The constant is sharp over arbitrary start distributions; the uniform-start case is included but no optimality claim for that subclass is made. For integer d>=3, in Biskup-Chayes Main Theorem (1.12) with q=3 and its rescaled Potts inner product, n=2 and kappa=2/3. At J0=4 log 2 its supplied approximation allowance is E_d=(2J0/3)I_d, where I_d=int_{[-pi,pi]^d} a(k)^2/(1-a(k)) dk/(2pi)^d and a(k)=d^{-1}sum_j cos k_j. One has I_d>=1/(2d), hence E_d>=4 log 2/(3d). For d<=818 this lower bound is at least the exact q=3 mean-field barrier Delta=log 3-(19/12)log 2, so the unmodified allowance alone cannot establish a strict below-barrier criterion in those dimensions. The actual Gibbs approximation error may be smaller; this says nothing about the true lattice transition.
