body:
[Theorem T:growth of arXiv:2412.09655, 'The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree III: The exchangeable partition representation and'] Given a realization of\/ $\operatorname{CTCS}(n)$ for some $n \ge 1$:
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item Pick a uniform random bud; move up the path from the root toward that
   bud. 
A {\sf stop}{} event occurs at rate = $1$/(size of clade from current position).
 \item If\/ {\sf stop}{} before reaching the target bud, make a side-bud at that
   point, random on left or right. 
 \item Otherwise, extend the target bud into a branch of\/ $\operatorname{Exp}(1)$
   length to make a bud-pair. 
\end{enumerate}
 Then the result is a realization of\/ $\operatorname{CTCS}(n+1)$.
Consequently, 
we obtain a realization of the growth process $\bigpar{\operatorname{CTCS}(n), n=1,2,\dots}$
by starting with $\operatorname{CTCS}(1)$, which has a single bud at the root,
and then repeating this algorithm ad infinitum. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The growth algorithm

body:
[Theorem existence and uniqueness of arXiv:2606.29352, 'Exponential Mixing for 2D Stochastic Damped Euler Equation Driven by Bounded Noise'] Let $\gamma\geq 0$ and assume ((eqn:noise H norm of the paper)) with $a >3$. \\
 i) If $u_0 \in V$ , then on each interval $[0,T]$ there exists at least one weak global solution for equation ((eqn:Euler 0 of the paper)) with the initial condition $u(0)=u_0$, in the sense that $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.
    $$u \in C([0,T];H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$$ 
    and for every $ \phi \in V$, $t \in [0,T]$
    \begin{align*}
        \langle u(t) , \phi\rangle+ \gamma\int_0^t\langle u(s), \phi\rangle\;ds - \int_0^t\langle [u(s)\cdot \nabla] \phi, u(s)\rangle\;ds  = \langle u_0,\phi\rangle+ \int_0^t\langle H(s),\phi\rangle\;ds     \end{align*}
$\mathbb{P}$-a.s.. \\
ii) Let $p \in [2,\infty)$. If $u_0 \in V^{1,p} $, the weak global solution u satisfies $$u \in L^\infty(0,T;V^{1,p}), \;\mathbb{P}-a.s. . $$ \\
iii) If $u_0\in V$ and $w_0=\nabla \wedge u_0\in L^\infty$, then $w=\nabla\wedge u$ satisfies $$w \in L^\infty(0,T;L^\infty), \;\mathbb{P}-a.s.$$ and pathwise uniqueness holds. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem existence and uniqueness of arXiv:2606.29352

body:
[Theorem 12 (Finite-sample population-risk curve recovery) of arXiv:2608.30261, 'Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample'] Let $\tau_n\in[0,1)$ be deterministic, and let
\(
 \overline M_n,\overline L_{3,n},\overline\kappa_n,
 \overline G_{{\rm out},n},\overline C_{PP,n}
\)
be deterministic nonnegative scalars.  Suppose a measurable event
$\mathcal E_n^{\rm reg}$ satisfies
$\Pp(\mathcal E_n^{\rm reg})\geq1-\tau_n$.  On
$\mathcal E_n^{\rm reg}$, suppose \cref{ass:tube} and
\eqref{eq:evaluation-gradient-bound} hold.  On
$\mathcal E_n^{\rm reg}$, suppose also that
\cref{eq:deletion-chord-differentiability,eq:average-first-order-cancellation}
hold and that, for a finite $C_{PP}\geq0$,
\eqref{eq:measure-curvature-bound} holds uniformly over $i\in[n]$ and
$(t,\lambda)\in\cH$.  On $\mathcal E_n^{\rm reg}$, suppose furthermore
that the constants
$M,L_3,\kappa,G_{\rm out},C_{PP}$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 M\leq\overline M_n,\quad
 L_3\leq\overline L_{3,n},\quad
 \kappa\leq\overline\kappa_n,\quad
 G_{\rm out}\leq\overline G_{{\rm out},n},\quad
 C_{PP}\leq\overline C_{PP,n}.
\end{equation}
Assume globally one of the two enumerated sets of concentration hypotheses.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\emph{Absolute.}] For $\mathcal U=\cH$ and $\rho=d_{\cH}$, a
deterministic interval $I_{n-1}$ of finite length
$B_{n-1}^{\rm rng}$ satisfies \eqref{eq:loss-range-length},
$\beta_{n-1}<\infty$ for the quantity in \eqref{eq:uniform-stability}, the
deterministic nondecreasing modulus $\omega_{n-1}$ satisfies
$\lim_{v\downarrow0}\omega_{n-1}(v)=0$ and
\eqref{eq:hyper-modulus}, and \eqref{eq:loo-joint-measurability} holds.
Fix $r>0$ with $\mathcal N(\cH,d_{\cH},r)<\infty$.
\item[\emph{Chained.}] The quantities in
\cref{eq:hyper-lipschitz-constant,eq:mixed-stability} satisfy
$L_{n-1}^{\rm hyp},\beta_{n-1}^{\rm mix}<\infty$, the entropy integral in
\eqref{eq:entropy-integral} satisfies
$\mathfrak E(\cH,d_{\cH})<\infty$, and
\eqref{eq:loo-joint-measurability} holds with $\mathcal U=\cH$ and
$u=(t,\lambda)$.  A deterministic anchor $(t_0,\lambda_0)\in\cH$ satisfies
\eqref{eq:loo-anchor-integrability}.
\end{enumerate}
For the absolute route, set the deterministic $C_S=0$ and the finite
deterministic radius $s_n^\star(\delta)=s_n(r,\delta)$; for the chained
route, set the sample-dependent $C_S=D_S(t_0,\lambda_0)$ and the finite
deterministic radius $s_n^\star(\delta)=s_n^{\rm ch}(\delta)$.
Thus $s_n^\star:(0,1)\to[0,\infty)$.  For $\delta\in(0,1-\tau_n)$, define
the finite deterministic risk-curve recovery radius
$\mathfrak r_n:(0,1-\tau_n)\to[0,\infty)$ by
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak r_n(\delta)
 =\frac{\overline G_{{\rm out},n}\overline L_{3,n}
              \overline M_n^2}{2(n-1)^2}
       \mathcal J_{\overline\kappa_n}(T)
  +s_n^\star(\delta)
  +\frac{2\overline C_{PP,n}}{(n-1)^2}.
\end{equation}
Then there is a measurable event $\mathcal O_{n,\delta}$ with
$\Pp(\mathcal O_{n,\delta})\geq1-\delta-\tau_n$ such that, on
$\mathcal O_{n,\delta}$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{(t,\lambda)\in\cH}
 \big|\widetilde\Score_n(t,\lambda)-\Risk_S(t,\lambda)-C_S\big|
 \leq\mathfrak r_n(\delta).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-sample population-risk curve recovery

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2605.17296, 'Zero correlations and averaged fields of orthonormal Gaussian Functions'] Let
\[
 S_N(z):=\frac1N\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\big| e^{-|z|^2/2}f_n(z,\bar
 z) \big|^2, \qquad z\in\C.
\]
Then, for every compact $K\subset\C$ and every
 $0<\alpha <1$, 
\[
S_N \to 1 \quad \text{a.s. in $C^{0,\alpha}(K)$}. 
\]

By \eqref{eq:1}, we have that $S_N(z_0)\to 1$ a.s. 
On the other hand, Lemma~\ref{lem:holder} implies that for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$\sum_{N=1}^\infty 
\mathbb{P}\!\left([S_N]_{C^{0,\alpha}(K)}>\varepsilon\right) <
\infty$ since $p>2$. 
Hence, by the Borel--Cantelli lemma, we conclude that
$[S_N]_{C^{0,\alpha}(K)} \to 0$ almost surely. 
For every $z\in K$,
\[
|S_N(z)-1|
\le
|S_N(z)-S_N(z_0)| + |S_N(z_0)-1|
\le
[S_N]_{C^{0,\alpha}(K)}\,|z-z_0|^{\alpha} + |S_N(z_0)-1|.
\]
Taking the supremum over $z\in K$, we get
\[
\sup_{z\in K}|S_N(z)-1|
\le
(\operatorname{diam}K)^{\alpha}[S_N]_{C^{0,\alpha}(K)}
+

body:
Let (X_t) and (Y_t) be CENTRED Gaussian processes indexed by a finite set T. SUDAKOV-FERNIQUE: if E[(X_s - X_t)^2] <= E[(Y_s - Y_t)^2] for all s, t in T, then E[ sup_t X_t ] <= E[ sup_t Y_t ]. Note that only the increment variances are compared and the individual variances may differ; the conclusion is about EXPECTED suprema only. SLEPIAN: if in addition E[X_t^2] = E[Y_t^2] for every t - so that the increment comparison is equivalent to E[X_s X_t] >= E[Y_s Y_t] for all s, t - then the stronger distributional conclusion P( sup_t X_t >= u ) <= P( sup_t Y_t >= u ) holds for every u, and indeed the whole joint law is stochastically ordered coordinatewise. Slepian's extra hypothesis of equal variances is not decorative: without it the distributional conclusion is false, while the Sudakov-Fernique conclusion about expectations survives. Both require CENTRED and GAUSSIAN; there is no comparable general statement for non-Gaussian processes. The finite index set is a convenience; both extend to separable processes by approximation. [Slepian (1962), Sudakov (1971), Fernique (1975); see Adler and Taylor, Random Fields and Geometry, Chapter 2, or Boucheron-Lugosi-Massart Section 13.3]
both processes centred and Gaussian
Sudakov-Fernique: increment variances compared; conclusion only for expected suprema
Slepian: additionally equal pointwise variances; conclusion is distributional

Let f be a smooth function of the vector (z_t) approximating the maximum, for instance the soft maximum f_beta(z) = beta^{-1} log sum_t e^{beta z_t}, which converges to the maximum as beta -> infinity and has second derivatives with the sign structure d^2 f / dz_s dz_t <= 0 for s != t. For the soft maximum the diagonal and off-diagonal second derivatives combine so that F'(u) can be written as a sum over pairs s != t of ( E[(X_s - X_t)^2] - E[(Y_s - Y_t)^2] ) times a NONPOSITIVE quantity, using that the row sums of the Hessian of f_beta vanish because f_beta is invariant under adding a constant to all coordinates. For Slepian, run the same interpolation with f a smooth approximation to the indicator of the orthant {z_t < u for all t}, whose mixed second derivatives are nonnegative; the equal-variance hypothesis kills the diagonal terms, which is exactly what the orthant test function needs and what the soft maximum did not.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:65bc8bd338d9119f2b8ee6c53a7945a71c4d874c489921ae4c702fb50c6fd474","revision_digest":"sha256:b4b2e0be77f5756917d65ef45275366760a72b9a8c024ebef3f9c4928a398295","source_id":"rederived:urn:mb-agent:dc73dee333054e1d-M9","source_revision":"re-derived-2026-08-22; the statement and the hypothesis distinction were checked by the author; the interpolation proof is written at sketch level, with the sign bookkeeping in the soft-maximum step asserted rather than expanded","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma lem:active-pair-cumulative-height of arXiv:2609.03532, 'Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion'] Fix a sign-word segment $\mathcal S_j$ contained in the $p^{\mathrm{th}}$ excursion
block, and let $t$ be a reference position in $\mathcal S_j$.
Let $\mathcal O_j(t)$ be any collection of pairs $e$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
  \item the positive occurrence $t_+(e)$ is an ordinary jump belonging to
  $\mathcal S_j$;
  \item
  \[
    t_-(e)<t<t_+(e),
  \]
  where $t_-(e)$ is the negative occurrence of $e$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{equation*}
  \sum_{e\in\mathcal O_j(t)}d_e
  \leq C_m\widehat M(\Gamma),
\end{equation*}
where $C_m$ depends only on $m$.

Let N>=1 and d_0,...,d_N be positive integers, with d_j>=min(d_0,d_N) for 1<=j<N. Let Phi be a real d_N-by-d_0 matrix of full rank min(d_0,d_N). For real matrices W_j of size d_j-by-d_{j-1}, write P=W_N...W_1 and L(W_1,...,W_N)=||P-Phi||_F^2/2. All layers are updated simultaneously by W_j(t+1)=W_j(t)-eta grad_{W_j} L(W_1(t),...,W_N(t)). Assume c>0 and ||P(0)-Phi||_F<=sigma_min(Phi)-c, where sigma_min denotes the min(d_0,d_N)-th singular value. Put delta=c^2/(256 N^3 ||Phi||_F^{2(N-1)/N}). Assume ||W_{j+1}(0)^T W_{j+1}(0)-W_j(0) W_j(0)^T||_F<=delta for all 1<=j<N. Choose 0<eta<=c^{(4N-2)/N}/(6144 N^3 ||Phi||_F^{(6N-4)/N}). Write ell(t)=L(W_1(t),...,W_N(t)) and P(t)=W_N(t)...W_1(t). Then for every integer t>=0, ell(t+1)<=ell(t)-(eta/2) sigma_min(P(t))^{2(N-1)/N} ||P(t)-Phi||_F^2. This is a discrete-iteration result under the stated initialization and step restrictions, not an unconditional gradient-flow statement.
positive integer depth and layer dimensions; no hidden bottleneck
real full-rank target Phi
loss is one half squared Frobenius error of the end-to-end product (equivalently the whitened-data objective after dropping its constant)
positive deficiency margin c at initialization
adjacent-layer Gram imbalance at most delta=c^2/(256 N^3 ||Phi||_F^{2(N-1)/N})
simultaneous gradient descent with the stated positive step-size upper bound

\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\cC[\ell-1]\arrow[dr, phantom, "\pushout", very near end, yshift=0.2cm, xshift=0.1cm]\arrow[r]\arrow[d,hook]\arrow[d]&\Cone\cC[\ell-1]\arrow[d]&\\
\cC[\ell]\arrow[r]&\cA'[\ell]\arrow[d]&\cC[\ell]\arrow[dl, phantom, "\text{\reflectbox{$\pushout$}}", very near end, yshift=0.2cm, xshift=0.1cm]\arrow[l]\arrow[d,hook]\\
&\Cone\cC[\ell]&\cC[\ell+1]\arrow[l]\\
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Moreover, the vertical composite
\[
\Cone\cC[\ell-1]\to\cA'[\ell]\to\Cone\cC[\ell]
\]
is induced by the cotarget map $\cC[\ell-1]\to\cC[\ell]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 28 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01},
the action of $G$ on $B$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B}, 
and the continuous cocycle $\sigma_0: G \times B \to \bb R$ 
satisfies the integrability condition \eqref{moment-assumption-02} and $M_1^{\mu} = M_0^{\mu} \times \bb R$. 
Suppose that, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b) \in \supp \nu$,   
we have $\wt b M \subset \overline{\Gamma_{\mu} \wt b}$. 
Let $h$ be a Schwartz function on $\bb R$ whose Fourier transform has compact support,
and let $\psi$ be a continuous function on $\wt B$. 
Then, uniformly in $\wt b \in \wt B$ and in $w_n \in \bb R$ with $|w_n| = o(\sqrt{n})$,   
\begin{align*}
 \upsilon_{\mu} \sqrt{2 \pi n} \,  
& \bb E \left[ \psi\left( g_n \cdots g_1 \wt b \right) h \left( \sigma_0(g_n \cdots g_1, \eta(\wt b)) - n \lambda_{\mu} - w_n \right) \right]  \notag\\
& \qquad\quad -  \int_{M/M_0^{\mu}}  Q \psi((m_0^{\mu})^n m)  \, \theta_{\wt b}(d m)  \int_{\bb R}  h(u) du 
\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} 0. 
\end{align*}
title: Corollary 28 of arXiv:2607.19873

[Lem 12 of arXiv:2609.00743, '$L_p$ Brunn-Minkowski inequality for the eigenvalue of generalized Monge-Ampère equation'] Let $\Omega_\alpha$ be the interior of the set $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:u_\alpha(x)\le 0\}$. Then
    \[
    \bar\Omega_\alpha=(1-\alpha)\bar\Omega_0+_p \alpha\bar\Omega_1.
    \]
    Equivalently, the support function of $\bar\Omega_\alpha$ is
    \[
    h_\alpha(\xi)=\left[(1-\alpha)h_0(\xi)^p+\alpha h_1(\xi)^p\right]^{\frac1p},
    \]
    where $h_0$ and $h_1$ are support functions of $\bar\Omega_0$ and $\bar\Omega_1$ respectively.

    Furthermore, $u_\alpha=0$ on $\partial \Omega_\alpha$.

\[
\rho_t:=\rho_{\xi_0}+t(\rho_{\xi_1}-\rho_{\xi_0})

Suppose that Assumption~\ref{ass:regular-interior} holds on \(J\Subset(0,a_{\xi_\star})\) for \(\xi_\circ=\xi_\star\) and uniformly along the path \((\xi_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\), i.e.,

Then, if 
\[
G(r):=\int_1^r (\rho_1(u)-\rho_0(u))\,du 
=0 
\quad\forall\, r\in[0,U]\setminus J,
\]
and
\[
\Vert G\Vert_\infty

\end{equation}
where \(C_{J,\kappa,K,V}\) is a uniform constant independent of the particular pair \((\xi_0,\xi_1)\) or \(G\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let G be a connected d-regular graph on n vertices with adjacency eigenvalues d = lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ... >= lambda_n >= -d. G is Ramanujan if every eigenvalue other than +-d satisfies |lambda| <= 2 sqrt(d - 1); the number 2 sqrt(d-1) is the spectral radius of the infinite d-regular tree. Alon-Boppana theorem: for every fixed d >= 3 and every epsilon > 0, every d-regular graph with sufficiently many vertices has lambda_2 >= 2 sqrt(d - 1) - epsilon; more precisely lambda_2 >= 2 sqrt(d-1) (1 - O(1/ log^2 n)) (Friedman; Nilli). So Ramanujan graphs are the best possible spectral expanders. Existence: Lubotzky, Phillips and Sarnak (1988) and independently Margulis constructed explicit infinite families of (p+1)-regular Ramanujan graphs for every prime p congruent to 1 mod 4 (Cayley graphs of PSL(2, Z/qZ) or PGL(2, Z/qZ) according to the Legendre symbol of p modulo q, the eigenvalue bound coming from the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for modular forms proved by Deligne), later extended to all prime powers (Morgenstern 1994); Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava proved by the method of interlacing families, non-constructively, that infinite families of bipartite Ramanujan graphs of every degree d >= 3 exist (Ann. Math. 2015, via 2-lifts) and then that bipartite Ramanujan graphs of every degree exist on every even number of vertices (interlacing families IV, 2018); Friedman (2008) proved Alon's conjecture that a random d-regular graph is nearly Ramanujan, lambda_2 <= 2 sqrt(d-1) + epsilon with high probability, and Bordenave (2020) gave a shorter proof. Ramanujan graphs give the optimal expander mixing lemma constant and near-optimal derandomisation gadgets.
d >= 3, G connected and d-regular (bipartite graphs have lambda_n = -d, which is excluded from the Ramanujan condition together with +d)
the Alon-Boppana bound is asymptotic in n for fixed d
existence results are cited, not proved

Since G is connected and large, it contains two vertices u and v at distance at least 2k + 2 for a k that grows with n (a d-regular graph of diameter D has at most 1 + d [ (d-1)^D - 1 ] / (d-2) vertices, so its diameter is at least log_{d-1} n - O(1)). Let U_i and V_i be the sets of vertices at distance exactly i from u and from v, for i = 0..k; the two families are disjoint and no edge joins a U_i to a V_j. Define a test vector f on the vertices by f = a_i on U_i and f = -c b_i on V_i, with a_i = (d-1)^{-i/2} and b_i likewise, the constant c chosen so that f is orthogonal to the all-ones vector (the top eigenvector), and f = 0 elsewhere. Then lambda_2 >= <f, A f> / <f, f> by the Courant-Fischer variational principle. On each side the Rayleigh quotient of the radial test function on a ball of the d-regular tree computes to at least 2 sqrt(d-1) - O(1/k) (the radial decay (d-1)^{-i/2} is the spectral-radius eigenfunction of the tree truncated at depth k, and the truncation costs O(1/k)), and because |U_i| <= d (d-1)^{i-1} the graph's balls are no larger than the tree's, which only helps the estimate; the two sides do not interact, so the quotient is at least the minimum of the two. [Defn def:downwards-closed of arXiv:2412.09535, 'Local limit theorem for joint subgraph counts'] A finite set of non-$\kone$ connected graphs $\mathcal{H}$ is \emph{downwards closed} if for all $H \in \mathcal{H}$ and $H' \preceq H$ with $H'$ connected and not $\kone$, we have $H' \in \mathcal{H}$. In this case, it is true that if $H' \preceq H \in \mathcal{H}$, all components of $H'$ are in $\mathcal{H} \cup \set{\kone}$; thus (prop:linrel of the paper) implies that
\[\setr[X_H \colon H \in \mathcal{H} \cup \set{\kone}] = \setr[\gamma_H \colon H \in \mathcal{H} \cup \set{\kone}].\]
Call this algebra $\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{H}}$.
title: Defn def:downwards-closed of arXiv:2412.09535

For each $i < j$, let
\[

\[
\log V_n(\widetilde\lambda_n)
\geq
\log V_n(\lambda_n) - O(n).
\]
Consequently,

\mathbb E\log V_n(\widetilde\lambda_n)
\geq
\mathbb E\log V_n(\lambda_n) - O(n).

[Definition def:diffuse_vs_atomic of arXiv:2607.08551, 'Weighted-threshold Coupon Collection'] We say that the weights are \emph{diffuse} if
\[
    w_N^\ast \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{} 0 .
\]

We say that the weights are \emph{atomic} if there exists a sequence \(w^{(\infty)}=(w_i^{(\infty)})_{i\ge1}\) such that
\[
    w_i^{(N)} \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{} w_i^{(\infty)} \qquad\text{for every fixed } i\ge1,
\]
and
\[
     w_i^{(\infty)} >0 \mbox{ for some } i.
\]
title: Definition def:diffuse_vs_atomic of arXiv:2607.08551

Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: A useful sufficient condition is a common local coding from instruction stacks. Suppose the output on a finite window W can be determined by stacks within a random radius R, with the same coding rule for both source geometries after their fronts pass, and P(R>r)<=C*r^(-beta). Coupling the stacks then bounds total variation of the two W-laws by 2*C*r^(-beta) whenever both available bulk neighborhoods have radius r. With r proportional to inverse mesh, this gives a quantitative microscopic universality rate. Check: On the intersection of the two successful coding events the outputs are identical; the union bound supplies the factor two. The argument remains valid without independence of the coding radii. Obstruction: A common finite-radius coding rule is unproved at criticality and may itself be too strong. This is an explicit coupling reduction, not an assertion that ARW has a finite influence radius.

non-negative sums and products of $h_q$ remains valid after replacing $h_q$ by $H_q$.
Identities involving $h_q$ give the corresponding upper inequalities. For example,
\begin{equation*}
  \forall x,y \in V\,,\qquad \Pp(x\leftrightarrow_q y)
  \leq\sum_{z\in V}H_q(x,z)H_q(y,z),
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation*}
    \forall x \in V\,,\qquad  \Ee[\pi(R_x^{\mathrm{raw}})]
  \leq\sum_{z\in V}\pi(z)H_q(x,z).
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop diff-dimensions of arXiv:2606.01627, 'The geometry of the giant component of random geometric graphs'] Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be connected compact Riemannian manifolds of dimension $d_1 > d_2 \geq 2$ and volume $1$.  Let $\Delta_c(d_j)$ denote the critical average degree for having a giant component. 
    There is $\alpha = \alpha(M_1,M_2)$ so that for each $\Delta_0 > \max\{\Delta_c(d_1),\Delta_c(d_2)\}$ there is $c = c(M_1,M_2,\Delta_0)$ so for all $\Delta \in [\Delta_0, \alpha n]$, given the adjacency matrices of the random geometric graphs  $G_{M_1}(n;r_1)$ and $G_{M_2}(n;r_2)$ of expected average degree $\Delta$, there is a $O(n^2 \Delta)$ algorithm which can correctly identify which graph came from $M_1$ and $M_2$ with probability at least $1- \exp(-c \log^2 n)\,.$

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.02019, '2609.02019'] Let Assumption~\ref{Hypo-Q} hold, and let $\delta_{\mathcal Q}$ be defined
		by \eqref{delta-Qi}. For $n\ge1$, set
		\[
		\mathcal Q_n\triangleq J_n\mathcal QJ_n.
		\]
		Then the following properties hold.
		\begin{enumerate}[label={\bf (\arabic*)},leftmargin=0.79cm]
			\setlength\itemsep{0.2em}
			\item For each $n\ge1$,
			$\mathcal Q_n\in\mathrm{OP}\mathcal S^{-\infty}$.
			If the description selected in Assumption~\ref{Hypo-Q} is
			$\mathcal Q\in\mathbb A^\alpha$, then
			$\{\mathcal Q_n\}_{n\ge1}$ is bounded in $\mathbb A^\alpha$.
			If the selected description is
			$\mathcal Q\in\mathbb B^\beta$, then
			$\{\mathcal Q_n\}_{n\ge1}$ is bounded in $\mathbb B^\beta$.
			
			\item For every $r\ge0$,
			\[
			\lim_{n\to\infty}
			\|\mathcal Q_nf-\mathcal Qf\|_{H^r}=0,
			\quad f\in H^{r+\delta_{\mathcal Q}},
			\]
			and
			\[
			\lim_{n\to\infty}
			\|\mathcal Q_n^2f-\mathcal Q^2f\|_{H^r}=0,
			\quad f\in H^{r+2\delta_{\mathcal Q}}.
			\]
			
			\item Let $r,\theta\ge0$ and
			$r>\theta+\delta_{\mathcal Q}$. Then
			\[
			\|\mathcal Q_n-\mathcal Q_m\|_{
				\mathscr L(H^r;H^\theta)}
			\lesssim
			(n\wedge m)^{-(r-\theta-\delta_{\mathcal Q})}.
			\]
			Moreover, for all $f,g\in H^r$,
			\begin{align*}
				\left|
				\left\langle
				\mathcal Q_nf-\mathcal Q_mg,
				f-g
				\right\rangle_{H^\theta}
				\right| \lesssim
				(n\wedge m)^{-2(r-\theta-\delta_{\mathcal Q})}
				\bigl(\|f\|_{H^r}+\|g\|_{H^r}\bigr)^2
				+
				\|f-g\|_{H^\theta}^2.
			\end{align*}
			The implicit constants are independent of $n,m$.
			
			\item Let $r,\theta\ge0$ and
			$r>\theta+2\delta_{\mathcal Q}$. Then
			\[
			\|\mathcal Q_n^2-\mathcal Q_m^2\|_{
				\mathscr L(H^r;H^\theta)}
			\lesssim
			(n\wedge m)^{-(r-\theta-2\delta_{\mathcal Q})}.
			\]
			Moreover, for all $f,g\in H^r$,
			\begin{align*}
				\left|
				\left\langle
				\mathcal Q_n^2f-\mathcal Q_m^2g,
				f-g
				\right\rangle_{H^\theta}
				+
				\|\mathcal Q_nf-\mathcal Q_mg\|_{H^\theta}^2
				\right| \lesssim
				(n\wedge m)^{-(r-\theta-\delta_{\mathcal Q})}
				\bigl(\|f\|_{H^r}+\|g\|_{H^r}\bigr)^2
				+
				\|f-g\|_{H^\theta}^2.
			\end{align*}
			The implicit constants are independent of $n,m$.
			
			\item For every $r\ge0$ and $f\in H^r$,
			\begin{equation}
				\sup_{n\ge1}
				\left|
				\langle\mathcal Q_nf,f\rangle_{H^r}
				\right|
				\lesssim
				\|f\|_{H^r}^2,
				\quad
				\sup_{n\ge1}
				\left|
				\langle\mathcal Q_n^2f,f\rangle_{H^r}
				+
				\|\mathcal Q_nf\|_{H^r}^2
				\right|
				\lesssim
				\|f\|_{H^r}^2.
				
			\end{equation}
			
			\item For every $r\ge0$ and $f\in H^r$,
			\begin{equation}
				\sup_{n\ge1}
				\left|
				\langle J_n\mathcal Qf,J_n f\rangle_{H^r}
				\right|
				\lesssim
				\|f\|_{H^r}^2,
				\quad
				\sup_{n\ge1}
				\left|
				\langle J_n\mathcal Q^2f,J_n f\rangle_{H^r}
				+
				\|J_n\mathcal Qf\|_{H^r}^2
				\right|
				\lesssim
				\|f\|_{H^r}^2.
				
			\end{equation}
		\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2604.16002, 'Normal approximation for iterated inner functions'] The sequence $(Y_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ forms a reverse martingale difference sequence with respect to $(\F_n)_{n=0}^\infty$, that is, $$Y_n \text{ is $\F_n$-measurable}, \,\, \text{and }\,\, \E[Y_n|\F_{n+1}] = 0.$$
		Moreover, we have the following identities:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),font=\normalfont]
			\item  $\E\big[|Y_n|^2 | \F_{n+1}\big]=\E\big[|Y_n|^2\big] = 1-|\lambda|^2.$
			\item  $\E\big[Y_n^2| \F_{n+1}\big]=\mu f^{\circ (n+1)}$.
			\item  For any $\alpha \in \mathbb C$, $$\E\big[({\rm Re}\, \alpha Y_n)^2 |\mathscr F_{n+1}\big]=\frac{1-|\lambda|^2}{2}|\alpha|^2 + \frac{{\rm Re}\,(\alpha^2 \mu f^{\circ (n+1)})}{2}.$$
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 14 of arXiv:2605.31344, 'Subcritical sharpness for real-valued spin models'] We say that $f: (\mathbb{R}^{+})^{\overline{\Lambda}} \times \{0, 1\}^{\overline{E}(\Lambda)} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is an increasing function if for any $\mathsf{a}, \mathsf{a}' \in \mathbb{R}^{\overline{\Lambda}}$ and any $\omega, \omega' \in \{0, 1 \}^{\overline{E}(\Lambda)}$ with $\mathsf{a} \leq \mathsf{a}'$ and $\omega \leq \omega'$ pointwise,
    $f(\mathsf{a}, \omega) \leq f(\mathsf{a}', \omega').$
    We say an event $A$ is an increasing event if $\mathbbm{1}_{A}$ is an increasing function. For measures $\mu, \mu'$ on $(\mathbb{R}^{+})^{\overline{\Lambda}} \times \{0, 1\}^{\overline{E}(\Lambda)}$, we say that $\mu$ is stochastically dominated by $\mu'$ and write $\mu \preceq \mu'$ if $\mu[f] \leq \mu'[f]$ for any bounded increasing function $f$.

Let V = V(f_1, ..., f_m) be an affine algebraic set in A^n_k and let p in V. If I(V) = (f_1, ..., f_m), then the Zariski tangent space T_p(V) is canonically isomorphic to the nullspace (kernel) of the Jacobian matrix J_F(p) in k^n: T_p(V) = {v in k^n : J_F(p) * v = 0}.

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:4d0dd9163c5404d1fe99c89990ea2a179ab857eff446b8793059554d2ce64afd","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/4d/4d0dd9163c5404d1fe99c89990ea2a179ab857eff446b8793059554d2ce64afd.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:55abb58d3893dd65e266367c9d71a1a8b37c9321e1077a89f6666981c945dcea","bundle_entry_key":"transition-kappa-common-hessian","bundle_id":"population.t362-transition-kappa-005","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"optimization; random reshuffling; transition condition number; optimal constant step","draft":"w732/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.randomreshuffling:common-hessian-random-reshuffling-exact-transition-condition-number-optimizer","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Target 1: the exact transition path kappa=4T/log(T)

Status: proof draft (unaudited). This is an exact transition path, not a theorem for every sequence with kappa*log(T)/T->4. No priority claim.

## Statement

Use the normalized common-Hessian model of C001 with fixed n>=2, fixed deterministic x0!=0,y0, fixed zero-sum linear terms of mean squares s1>=0,s2>0, and fresh independent uniform epoch permutations shared across coordinates. For T=nK->infinity set exactly kappa=4T/log T. Put ell=log T, m=log ell and

    D_n = n/(n-1) if n is even,
          (n+1)/n if n is odd.

Then the globally minimized final-epoch expected function error P_T obeys

    min_{eta>=0} P_T(eta) ~ s2*D_n*ell^2/(16*T*m).         (1)

Every sequence of global minimizers has

    kappa*eta_T = 2 - (4+o(1))*m/ell.                    (2)

The exact transition path is essential to the proof; subleading changes in kappa can change the competing transient scale.

## Endpoint residue

In the settled recursion put q=kappa*eta, a=1-q,

    W_n(q)=sum_{0<=i<j<n}(a^i-a^j)^2,
    J_n(q)=q^2*W_n(q)/[2(n-1)(1-a^(2n))],  0<q<2.

The stiff variance is exactly (s2/kappa)*J_n(q)*(1-a^(2T)). At q=2, the n powers (-1)^i have floor(n/2) of one parity and ceil(n/2) of the other. Thus

    W_n(2)=4*floor(n/2)*ceil(n/2)
          = n^2 (n even), or n^2-1 (n odd).

For delta=2-q->0 positively, 1-a^(2n)=1-(1-delta)^(2n)~2n*delta. Hence

    delta*J_n(2-delta) -> W_n(2)/[n(n-1)] = D_n.         (3)

Here n is fixed; n-1>0 and the stationary denominator is positive on (0,2). The finite-horizon variance, including q=2 and q>2, is always

    R_T = [s2*q^2*W_n(q)/(2(n-1)*kappa)]
                *sum_{r=0}^{K-1}(1-q)^(2nr).             (4)

## Upper bound

1. Choose z_c=2m-3log m, delta_c=2z_c/ell and q_c=2-delta_c. For all sufficiently large T, z_c>0, delta_c->0 and delta_c*T->infinity. Thus 0<q_c<2. From (3)-(4),

    R_T(eta_c) ~ s2*D_n/(kappa*delta_c)
              = s2*D_n*ell^2/(8*T*z_c)
              ~ s2*D_n*ell^2/(16*T*m).                 (5)

We used (1-delta_c)^(2T)<=exp(-2delta_c*T)->0.

2. Let A=x0^2/2>0. Since eta_c=q_c/kappa and T/kappa^2->0, the flat deterministic contribution is

    A*(1-eta_c)^(2T)
       = (A/T)*exp(z_c+O(T/kappa^2))
       ~ A*ell^2/(T*m^3),                               (6)

which is o(ell^2/(T*m)). The identity -2q_c*T/kappa=-ell+z_c uses the exact definition kappa=4T/ell, not merely its leading ratio.

The stiff deterministic term is at most (kappa*y0^2/2)*exp(-2delta_c*T), negligible compared with the scale in (5). Indeed delta_c*T is of order T*m/ell, which dominates log T, whereas the logarithms of kappa and the reciprocal target scale are O(log T). The flat variance is O(eta_c^3)=O(ell^3/T^3), also negligible. Thus the minimum is at most (1+o(1)) times (5), and tends to zero.

## Localization of every unrestricted global optimizer

3. A global minimizer exists because the exact error is a continuous coercive polynomial: the last epoch and pair (0,1) in (4) give P_T>=s2*q^4/[2(n-1)*kappa]. Write q_T=kappa*eta_T for any sequence of global minimizers. Eventually q_T<2. In fact if q_T>=2, then W_n(q_T)>=q_T^2 and every term of the geometric sum in (4) is >=1, so

    P_T(eta_T) >= 8*s2*K/[(n-1)*kappa]
                 = [2*s2/(n(n-1))]*ell ->infinity,

contradicting the vanishing upper bound. This excludes all unstable steps, not only those close to the endpoint.

4. For 0<=q_T<2, eta_T->0 and T*eta_T^2=O(ell^2/T)->0. Uniformly in this interval the flat transient equals

    A*exp(-q_T*ell/2+o(1)).

If q_T<=2-epsilon along a subsequence for any fixed epsilon>0, that transient is at least A*T^(-1+epsilon/2)*exp(o(1)), exceeding the candidate bound of order ell^2/(T*m). Therefore q_T->2 from below. Set delta_T=2-q_T->0.

5. Necessarily delta_T*T->infinity. Otherwise take a subsequence on which delta_T*T<=M. For large T on that subsequence delta_T<=1/2 and log(1-delta_T)>=-2delta_T. Every summand in (4) is then at least

    (1-delta_T)^(2n(K-1)) >= exp(-4delta_T*T)>=exp(-4M).

Since q_T->2 and W_n(q_T)>=q_T^2, (4) gives P_T>=const*K/kappa, diverging like ell. This contradicts the upper bound. The constant can depend on M but is strictly positive. Hence (3) applies and the finite-horizon variance multiplier tends to one.

## Optimization on the transition scale

6. Define z_T=delta_T*ell/2>0. By the endpoint residue and step 5,

    R_T(eta_T) = (1+o(1))*s2*D_n*ell^2/(8*T*z_T).        (7)

The flat transient is (A/T)*exp(z_T+o(1)), by the same uniform expansion used in step 4. Comparing this transient with the upper bound gives

    z_T <= 2m-log m+O(1),                               (8)

so limsup z_T/m<=2. Comparing (7) with that upper bound gives liminf z_T/m>=2. Consequently z_T/m->2, which is (2). Substitution into (7), combined with the upper bound, proves (1). All other objective contributions are nonnegative, so no cancellation or exchange of expectation and minimization is required.

## Hypotheses and unpaid step

x0!=0 is used in (8); if initialization is exactly the optimum, eta=0 gives zero error and (1) would fail. s2>0 is used in every noise localization and in (7); with no stiff noise the endpoint pole is absent. Fixed n is used in (3) and the stationary estimates. n>=2 makes n-1 positive. Independent epoch permutations enter the inherited recursion; coordinate-noise independence is not needed because the objective is diagonal. Exact kappa=4T/log T is used in (6) and (8).

This proves a named-target-1 transition path in draft form. General sequences satisfying only kappa*log(T)/T->4 remain unpaid, as do general finite-sum Hessians and the full T362 obstruction. Independent audit should focus on the uniform all-minimizer localization in steps 3-5 and the two comparisons in step 6. Exact finite algebra checks are checks of (3)-(4), not certificates of the asymptotic theorem. [Definition def:surface of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] A \emph{two-sided Lipschitz surface} $F$ is a set of base-height cells $(b,h)\in\mathbb{Z}^{d+1}$ such
that for every $b\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ there are exactly two, possibly equal, integers $F_+(b)\ge0$ and
$F_-(b)\le0$ with $(b,F_+(b)),(b,F_-(b))\in F$, and such that $F_+$ and $F_-$ are Lipschitz
functions. We say that $F$ \emph{exists} if $F_+(b)<\infty$ and $F_-(b)>-\infty$ for every $b$.
For $D\in\mathbb{N}$ we say that $F$ \emph{surrounds} a cell $(b',h')$ at distance $D$ if every path
$(b',h')=(b_0,h_0),(b_1,h_1),\dots,(b_n,h_n)$ with $\|(b_k,h_k)-(b_{k-1},h_{k-1})\|_1=1$ for all
$k$ and $\|(b_n,h_n)-(b_0,h_0)\|_1>D$ intersects $F$. We say that a space-time cell belongs to
$F$ if its base-height index does.
title: Two-sided Lipschitz surface

[Definition Def:urd of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] Let  $p$ be a semi-directed path from the origin to a point $(n,m)$. The number of \emph{right-turns} of $p$ is defined as 
\[
R(p):=\left| k \in \{0,...,n\} : \, f_p(k)=f_p(k+1)\right|.
\] 
similarily, we define the number of \emph{up-turns} by
\[
U(p):=\left| k \in \{0,...,n\} : \, f_p(k)<f_p(k+1)\right|,
\] 
and the number of \emph{down-turns} by
\[
D(p):=\left| k \in \{0,...,n\} : \, f_p(k)>f_p(k+1)\right|.
\]
title: Definition Def:urd of arXiv:2411.13030

[Lemma 86 (Series law) of arXiv:2507.07702, 'Observables of random spanning trees in random environment'] Suppose $v \in V$ is a vertex of degree $2$ with incident edges $e_1 = (u_1, v)$ and $e_2 = (v, u_2)$ that have resistances $r_1 := 1/\weight(e_1)$ and $r_2 := 1/\weight(e_2)$, respectively. Consider the  graph $G'$
   on $V \setminus \{v\}$  where $e_1$ and $e_2$ are replaced by a single edge $e$ between $u_1$ and $u_2$, with resistance $r(e) := r_1 + r_2$. Then, for any disjoint $A,B\subseteq V\setminus\{v\}$, the effective resistance between $A$ and $B$ in $G$ is equal to that in $G'$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Series law

[Cor 19 of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Fix \(n\in\mathbb N\), and let \(r^{(n)}_\varphi\) denote the truncated coding radius. Define
\[
b_m := \mathbb E\!\big[
|B_\infty(0,r^{(n)}_0)\cap B_\infty(m,r^{(n)}_{m})|
\big],
\qquad m\in\mathbb Z^d.
\]
For each \(L\ge 1\), let \(\Lambda_L := [-L,L]^d\cap\mathbb Z^d\), and let \(f^{(L)}\) be a local observable such that
\[
\delta_k f^{(L)} = 1 \quad \text{for all } k\in \Lambda_L,
\qquad
\delta_k f^{(L)} = 0 \quad \text{for } k\notin \Lambda_L.
\]
Then \(\|\delta f^{(L)}\|_2^2 = |\Lambda_L|\), and
\[
\liminf_{L\to\infty}
\frac{\mathbb E\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}\big(c_i^{(n)}(X)\big)^2}
{\|\delta f^{(L)}\|_2^2}
=
\|b\|_1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 19 of arXiv:2602.14618

[Propn weakRepPropn of arXiv:2605.04860, 'Branching Brownian motion with rank-based selection and reaction-diffusion equations'] Let $(\mu_t^N)_{t\geq 0}$ be the measure-valued Markov process corresponding to the $(\psi,r,N)$-BBM process. Let $f(x,t)\in \mathcal{BC}^{2,1}(\mathbb{R}\times [0,\infty),\mathbb{R})$. Then $\mu^N$, and $f$ satisfy the following equation:
    \begin{align}\langle \mu_t^N,f(\cdot,t)\rangle = \langle \mu_0^N, f(\cdot,0)\rangle &+ \int_0^t \langle \mu_s^N, \frac12 f_{xx}(\cdot,s) + f_t(\cdot,s) + r(s)f(\cdot,s)\rangle \\
    \nonumber&-\left\langle \mu_s^N, Nf(\cdot,s)r(s)\int_{(H\star \mu^N_s)(\cdot)-1/N}^{(H\star \mu^N_s)(\cdot)}\psi(u)du\right\rangle ds + M_t^{N,W} + M_t^{N,P},\end{align}
    where $M^{N,W}_t$ is a continuous local martingale with $\mathbb{E}[[M^{N,W}]_t]\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}0$ for fixed $t$, and $M^{N,P}_t$ is a local martingale with $\mathbb{E}[[M^{N,P}]_t]\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}0$ for fixed $t$.

[Theo 4 of arXiv:2609.02261, 'Quantization and process'] i) For all $F\in D_h( \R^{2n})$,  we have, 
  
    
      $$ F(X) =  ( \pi h)^{-n} \int _{\R^{2n}}e^{ - \frac {1 }  {h}   |X-T|^2 }
      H_hF(T) dT, $$
      
         for every $X\in \R^{2n}$ where
      
      $$  H_hF(T) =  ( 4 \pi h)^{-n}   \int _{\R^{2n}} 
       F^{\rm ext} \Big(  T+\frac{Z}{2} , T-\frac{Z}{2}\Big ) 
      e^{ - \frac {1 }  {4h}   |Z|^2 } dZ,$$
      for any $T\in \R^{2n}$.
      
      
    ii) The operator $H_h$ maps $D_h (\R^{2n})$ into 
    $ L^{\infty} (\R^{2n}) $. It is  commuting with translations and its symbol equals to  $u\rightarrow e^{ \frac { h|u|^2}   {4} }$. 
   
    iii)  Let  $F\in D_h( \R^{2n})$. There exists a function $\widetilde F$ on $\C^{2n} \simeq \R^{4n} $ which is holomorphic in the following sense,     
    \be (\partial _1 + i \partial _2 ) \widetilde F = 0,\
    (\partial _3  + i \partial _4 ) \widetilde F = 0
  \ee 
    
   with a restriction to $\R^{2n}$ 
     equals to $F$, that is to say,  $\widetilde F (x , 0, \xi , 0) = F(x , \xi)$. Moreover, for $X,Y\in\R^{2n}$,
      
      \be   | \widetilde F (X+iY) |  \leq 
    ( 4 \pi h)^{-n}   \Vert \psi_F \Vert _{L^1 (\R^{2n})} 
  \  e^{  \frac {1}  {h}   |Y|^2 }, \ee 
  
that is to say, for any $(x_1 , x_2 , x_3 , x_4)\in\R^{4n}$,
  
  $$  | \widetilde F (x_1 , x_2 , x_3 , x_4) | \leq
  ( 4 \pi h)^{-n}   \Vert \psi_F \Vert _{L^1 (\R^{2n})} 
  \  e^{  \frac {1}  {h}  ( |x_2|^2 + |x_4|^2) }.$$ 
      
    iv) Fix $F\in D_h( \R^{2n})$. We have,  with  $X = (x , \xi)\in \R^{2n}$ and $Y = (y , \eta)\in \R^{2n}$, 
   
   \be   F^{\rm ext}(X , Y)=  \widetilde F \left ( 
 \frac {x+y} {2} ,   \frac {\xi - \eta } {2} , 
 \frac {\xi + \eta} {2} ,   \frac {y-x} {2}\right ) .\ee 
 
 If $\widetilde F$ is satisfying  (\ref{Cauchy-Riem}) then $F^{\rm ext}$ 
 is verifying (\ref{CR-et-anti}). 
 
 v)  If a function  $F$ on $\R^{2n}$  has a holomorphic extension 
  $\widetilde F$ in the sense of  (\ref{Cauchy-Riem}) on  $\C^{2n}$ which satisfies,
 
  \be  | \widetilde F (X+iY) |  \leq 
     | \psi_F (Y) | 
  \  e^{  \frac {1}  {h}   |Y|^2 }, \ee 
  
  where $\psi_F \in L^1 (\R^{2n}) \cap L^{\infty} (\R^{2n}) $, 
  then the function  $F\in D_h (\R^{2n})$. 
  
  vi) The  convolution by a bounded measure is an operator in $D_h (\R^{2n})$ having a norm smaller or equal than $1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop P:half-space-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] As $n\to\infty$, the process $R^{(n)}$ has a distributional limit $R^{\mathsf{DL}}=\{R^{\mathsf{DL}}_i\}_{i=1}^k$, under the uniform-on-compact topology. 
    We can describe the process $R^{\mathsf{DL}}$ explicitly as follows.
	
Let $\mathcal{B} = (\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2, \ldots, \mathcal{B}_{2k})$ be $2k$ independent Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ of diffusivity $2$, drift $\lambda_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_i, i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket$ and $-\lambda_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_{2k+1-i}$. Next, let $\{X(-i, j) : i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket, j \in \llbracketi +1, 2k +1 - i \rrbracket\}$ be an array of exponential random variables, independent of each other and $\mathcal B$, satisfying 
\[
X(-i, j) \sim \begin{cases}
\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda_i/2 - \lambda_j/2), \qquad &j \in \llbracketi + 1, k \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda_i/2 + \lambda_{2k + 1 -j}/2), \qquad &j\in\llbracketk + 1, 2k - i \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda_i/2 - \rho), \qquad &j=2k + 1- i.
\end{cases}
\]
We turn this array into a 
sequence of cadlag functions $X = (X_1, \dots, X_{2k})$ on $(-\infty, 0]$ by the rule that $X_j(0) = 0$ for all $j$, and the measure $dX$ has atoms of size $X(-i, j)$ at each coordinate $(-i, j)$ where $X(-i, j)$ is defined (and is supported on these points). Equivalently, the path $X_j$ has a jump of size $X(-i, j)$ at location $-i$.

Let $X \mathcal{B}$ be the concatenation of $X$ and $\mathcal{B}$. (See Figure (fig:hfsh of the paper) for an illustration.) Then:
$$
R^{\mathsf{DL}}_i(x) = \begin{cases}
X\mathcal{B}(-i, i; x, 2k) - X\mathcal{B}(-i, i; 0, 2k), \qquad &x \ge 0, \\
X\mathcal{B}^{\Delta_{2k+1}}(-i, i; |x|, 2k) - X\mathcal{B}(-i, i; 0, 2k), \qquad &x \le 0.
\end{cases}
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop P:half-space-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020

[Theorem t:mppmix_double of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $\tilde\mathcal{P}$ be a marked point process on $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{K}$
  having summable exponential $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations  as in
Definition~(def.A2 of the paper). Consider the functionally constructed mark $V(x) :=\xi(\tilde{x}, \tilde{\mathcal{P}})$, with 
  $\xi:
\mathbb{R}^d \times\mathbb{K}\times\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \longrightarrow \mathbb{K}'$ and set $\dbtilde\mathcal{P} :=  \sum_{x \in \mathcal{P}}
\delta_{(x, V(x))}$, a marked point process on $\mathbb{R}^d\times \mathbb{K}'$. Fix $p,q \in \mathbb{N}$.
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item  If $\xi$ satisfies 
   fast \textnormal{BL}-localization  
   (equation Lp-stab-infinite of the paper) on $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ for $p,q$ and $p+q$, 
   then  $\dbtilde\mathcal{P}$ 
satisfies the fast \textnormal{BL}-mixing correlation condition for $p$ and $q$, that is to say (equation e.mppmixing of the paper) holds  for $f \in \textnormal{BL}((\mathbb{K}')^{p})$, $g \in \textnormal{BL}((\mathbb{K}')^{q}),$ and some fast decreasing function $\omega_{p+q}$. 
\item   Part~(i.BL-iterated-marks of the paper)
 above remains valid if
$\xi$ satisfies fast \textnormal{BL}~cluster-localization---that is,
conditions~(equation Lp-stab-infinite-weak1 of the paper) and~(equation Lp-stab-infinite-weak2 of the paper)---on
$\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ for  $p,q$, and $p+q$.

 \item  If 
  $\xi$ is fast stabilizing on $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ as in (equation stab-infinite of the paper) (via stopping sets) for $p,q$ and $p+q$, 
then  $\dbtilde\mathcal{P}$ has fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations for $p$ and $q$, i.e., (equation e.mppmixing of the paper) holds for $f \in \mathbb{B} ((\mathbb{K}')^{p})$, $g \in \mathbb{B} ((\mathbb{K}')^{q}),$ and some fast decreasing function $\omega_{p+q}$.
\end{enumerate}
In  all cases~(i.BL-iterated-marks of the paper), (i.BLc-iterated-marks of the paper), and~(i.iterated-marks of the paper), the  fast decreasing function $\omega_{p+q}$ associated to $\dbtilde \mathcal{P}$ depends on the functions $\varphi_{p+q}$ and $\phi $ as well as on  the constants $(C_k)_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ and $\kappa_{p+q}$ related to $\xi$ and $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$, respectively. In particular, there exist constants $C<\infty$, $c>0$ which  depend on $p,q$,  such that for all $s > 0$
  
\begin{equation} \omega_{p+q}(s) \leq C \exp(-cs^b) + C\varphi_{p + q}\big( cs^{b(1-a)/2( p + q + d)} \big),
\end{equation}
where $a,b$ are as in~(equation eqn:sum of the paper) and (equation phibd of the paper), respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Fast mixing properties of point processes with functionally constructed iterated marks

[Cor full-graph of arXiv:2607.17048, 'Concentration Inequalities for Incomplete U-statistics over Arbitrary Sampling Graphs'] Suppose (equation main-condition of the paper) is satisfied, and let $\sigma^2=\frac{2}{n(n-1)}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq n}\mathrm{Var}(h_e(X_i, X_j))$. Consider $U^{\text{\text{full}}}= \sum_{1\leq i<j\leq n}h_e(X_i, X_j)$. Then, for all $t>0$,
\[
\mathbb{P}\biggl(\frac{U^{\text{full}}-\mathbb{E}U^{\text{full}}}{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}>t\biggr)\leq \exp\biggl\{ - \frac{(n-1)t^2}{4\sigma^2}\biggr\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

At d=250 on two random a no interior bulk local maximum was found (slab face f-Ef ~1.05, an ascent direction), the component maxima near a_i reach 1.13-1.26, so the bulk/component crossover is between 150 and 250; a_i are saddles below d~108. Kac-Rice (23 Oct): given the projections <a_i,x> the gradient is exactly Gaussian and every proxy covariance matches, so the slab first moment equals the proxy rate 0.0082 d given two standard estimates (log-det concentration, bounded moderate deviation), both sketched 23 Oct, so the expected number of spurious maxima is at least exp(0.0082 d) (checkable argument, not a written proof); second moment (23 Oct): the proxy two-point complexity stays below twice the one-point rate for every overlap 0<q<=0.95 at levels 1.48-1.545 incl. the peak, failing only at the band top; near-diagonal exponent also below (3af); open: the in-plane prefactor at the diagonal, the term-by-term transfer, and high probability.

Let X_1, ..., X_n be INDEPENDENT random variables taking values in arbitrary measurable spaces - they need NOT be identically distributed and need not be real-valued - and let Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) with E[Z^2] < infinity. Let X_i' be an independent copy of X_i, independent of everything else, and put Z^{(i)} = f(X_1, ..., X_{i-1}, X_i', X_{i+1}, ..., X_n). Then Var(Z) <= (1/2) sum_{i=1}^n E[ (Z - Z^{(i)})^2 ] = sum_{i=1}^n E[ ((Z - Z^{(i)})_+)^2 ]. Equivalently, and often more convenient, Var(Z) <= sum_{i=1}^n E[ (Z - Z_i)^2 ] for ANY random variables Z_i that are measurable functions of the n-1 variables other than X_i; taking Z_i = inf over the i-th coordinate of f gives the version used for suprema and for first-passage times. Equality holds if and only if f is a sum of functions of the individual coordinates. Independence is the only structural hypothesis and it is essential; the inequality is FALSE for dependent coordinates. Applied with a bounded-difference function it recovers the variance half of McDiarmid's inequality; applied to first-passage percolation with the geodesic length as the influence bound it produces the linear variance upper bound. [Efron and Stein (1981), Steele (1986); see Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 3.1]
X_1, ..., X_n independent (arbitrary measurable state spaces, not necessarily identically distributed)
E[Z^2] < infinity
X_i' an independent copy of X_i

body: [Lemma one side lemma of arXiv:2411.07125, 'Mixing on the cycle with constant size perturbation'] For any $ 0<\delta_2<1$ as exception probability, there exists $\alpha_2<\infty$ such that with probability at least $1-\delta_2$, for all $Y_m\in \mathcal{Y}_m$, there exists $0 \neq y \in Y_m$ such that $\alpha_1s <d(f(y),0) \leq \alpha_2 s$. In other word, with probability 1, for all possible $Y_m$, there exists a non-zero point $y$ in $Y_m$ such that the distance between $f(y)$ and $0$ is in the order of the standard distance $s$.

[Proposition excerpt-from-CGS-AAP of arXiv:2608.23202, 'Locally finite Fixed points of Branching Brownian Motion'] Let $\theta$ be a point process such that $\theta \in \mathcal{N}_2$ and $\theta$  has a finite top particle almost surely. Suppose 
\[ Y_t := \frac{1}{t^{3/2}}\int_{-\infty}^0(-x)e^{\sqrt{2}x} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2t}} \theta(dx) \]
is tight in $t>0$. Then, given a sequence $\{t_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ and a non-negative random variable $Z$ such that $Y_{t_n} \overset{d}{\to} Z$, it holds that  
\begin{equation}
     \langle f, \theta_{t_n}^{\sqrt{2}} \rangle \overset{d}{\to} \langle f, \widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_\infty(\cdot - S)\rangle,
\end{equation}
for all $f$ of form (equation Form of f of the paper), where $\theta_t^{\sqrt{2}}$ is given by (equation theta_t-def of the paper) for $\lambda =\sqrt{2}$ started from $\theta_0^{\sqrt{2}} = \theta $ and $S= \log Z/\sqrt{2}$. In particular, (equation main-result-CGS-along-subsequence of the paper) holds for all $f\in C_c^+(\mathbb{R})$ as well. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 4 (Characterization of limits of global empirical measures) of arXiv:2510.22533, 'Marginal dynamics of probabilistic cellular automata on trees'] Let any of the following three cases hold for $\{G_n\}_{n \in \N}$:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item Let $\kappa \ge 2$ be an integer. For each $n \ge \kappa+1$ with $n\kappa$ even, there exists at least one $\kappa$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, and we let $G_n$ be chosen uniformly at random.
    \item Let $\lambda > 0$, and let $G_n$ be the \Erdos graph $G(n,\lambda/n)$, on the vertex set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
    \item Let $G_n$ be drawn from the configuration model with vertex set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and with degree distribution converging weakly to $\rho_{\myroot}$.
    Assume $\rho_{\myroot}$ has finite first and second moments, that is, $\sum_{k=0}^\infty k^2 \rho_{\myroot}(k) < \infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Suppose the initial states $\{X^{G_n}_v(0) : v \in G_n, n \in \N\}$ are i.i.d.\ with law $\mu_0$.
Let $\Xbar$ and $G$ be given as follows, for each case above:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item Let $\Xbar$ be as in Construction \ref{constr:regulartree_local}, with $(\Xbar_v(0))_{v=0}^{\kappa}$ i.i.d.\ with law $\mu_0$.
    \item Let $\Xbar$ be as in Construction \ref{constr:UGWlocal}, with $\rho_{\myroot}=\mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$ and with $(\Xbar_v(0))_{v\in\V_1}$ i.i.d.\ with law $\mu_0$.
    \item Let $\Xbar$ be as in Construction \ref{constr:UGWlocal}, with $(\Xbar_v(0))_{v\in\V_1}$ i.i.d.\ with law $\mu_0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the $\PolishX^\infty$-valued random trajectory 
$X^{G_n}_{\myroot_n}$ converges in law  to $\Xbar_{\myroot}$ (or $\Xbar_0$ in case (i)). Moreover, 
the $\P(\PolishX^\infty)$-valued random measure  
$\mu^{G_n}$ converges in law  to $\Lmc(\Xbar_{\myroot})$ (or  $\Lmc(\Xbar_0)$ in case (i)).

[Lemma lem:churn of arXiv:2608.23638, 'Replicable Conformal Prediction'] For any two runs of a shared-grid threshold rule with outputs $\tau,\tau'\in u+\beta\mathbb{Z}$ and any input $x$,
$|\mathcal{C}_\tau(x)\,\triangle\,\mathcal{C}_{\tau'}(x)|=\#\{y:\ \tau\wedge\tau'<s(x,y)\le\tau\vee\tau'\}$, and on $\{\tau\neq\tau'\}$ the interval is a disjoint union of full grid cells, so the churn is at least the label mass of one full cell. Consequently $\mathbb{E}_X\big[|\mathcal{C}_\tau(X)\triangle\mathcal{C}_{\tau'}(X)|\,\big|\,\tau\neq\tau'\big]\ge\min_{C}m_\beta(C)$, the minimum over grid cells $C$ meeting the localization window of Theorem~(thm:upper of the paper)(ii) of $m_\beta(C):=\mathbb{E}_X\#\{y:s(X,y)\in C\}$. (Proof: Appendix~(app:lower of the paper).) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (T, d) be a metric space and alpha > 0. An admissible sequence of partitions of T is an increasing sequence of partitions (A_n)_{n >= 0} such that |A_0| = 1 and |A_n| <= 2^{2^n} for all n >= 1. Let A_n(t) denote the set in A_n containing t. The Talagrand gamma_alpha functional is defined by gamma_alpha(T, d) = inf_{(A_n)} sup_{t in T} sum_{n=0}^infinity 2^{n / alpha} * diam(A_n(t), d).
(T, d) is a metric space
alpha > 0

body:
[Prop max_action of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] For any $\beta\in \mathbb R$, the action $A_{\beta}$ has a unique minimizer $(\pi_1^{(\beta)}, \pi_2^{(\beta)})$ in $\mathcal{D}$. For $\beta \leq 0$, we have $\pi_1^{(\beta)}=\pi_2^{(\beta)}=\frac{1}{2}\Leb_{[0,1]}$. 
    For $\beta>0$, the densities of $\pi_1^{(\beta)}$ and $\pi_2^{(\beta)}$ on $[0,1]$ are given by
	\begin{equation}
	    \rho_1^{(\beta)}(x) := \frac{1}{1+\exp\left(\beta(\frac12-x) \right)}, 
        \quad \rho_2^{(\beta)}(x) := \frac{1}{1+\exp\left(\beta(x-\frac12) \right)}.
	\end{equation}
	In particular, both $\pi_1^{(\beta)}$ and $\pi_2^{(\beta)}$ have total mass $\frac{1}{2}$.

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2608.26001, 'The kernel of the Birman--Craggs--Johnson homomorphism'] Let $g \geq 3$ and let $H = \HH_1(\Sigma_g^1;\bbF_2)$.  The following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] The group $\QK_g^1$ is generated by elements of the form
$[V]_Q$ with $V$ a genus-$1$ symplectic subspace of $H$.
\item[(ii)] Let $V,W < H$ be nonzero orthogonal symplectic subspaces.  
We then have $[V]_Q+[W]_Q = [V \oplus W]_Q$.
\end{itemize}

Then, $\mathcal{D}$ is geodesically $\nabla$-invariant if and only if  
\[
\nabla_X Y + \nabla_Y X \in \mathfrak{X}(\mathcal{D})
\]
for all $X, Y \in \mathfrak{X}(\mathcal{D})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$$

Let $ x\in X $, $T\in\RR$, 
$n>2$, $\delta\in(0,1]$, $r_2\geq 2r_1\geq 256 S$ and constants $\phi,\Phi\geq 1$.
Assume $S_{\phi}(n,r_1,r_2)$ in $ x$.
 For all non-negative $\Delta_\omega$-subsolutions $v\geq 0$ on $[T-r_2^2,T+r_2^2]\times B_{x}(r_2)$, we have
 \[
\left(\frac{1}{m({B_{x}(r_1)})}\fint\limits_{ T-\delta r_1^2}^{T+\delta r_1^2}\sum_{B_{x}(r_1)} mv_t^{2w}\drm t\right)^{\frac{1}{w}}\leq C_{n,C_S}\left(\frac{r_2}{r_1}\right)^{2n^2}

\fint\limits_{T- \delta r_2^2}^{T+\delta r_2^2}\sum_{B_{x}(r_2)} mv_t^{2}\drm t,
\]
where $C_{n,C_S}:=2^{19n^2}C_S^{2n}A'(n)^{2n}$ 
and 
\[
{w=w(r_2)={\left(\frac{r_2}{2^6S}\right)^{\frac{1}{n}}}.}
\]

body:
[Corollary 20 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Let $l_0:=0$. For a strictly increasing sequence $l_1<\cdots<l_s$ of positive integers, the following statements are equivalent.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} There exists a cyclic $C_{p^s}$-extension of $k((t))$ whose lower jumps are $l_1<\cdots<l_s$.

\smallskip
{\bf (2)} The following conditions hold.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (2.a)} We have $p\nmid l_1$.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (2.b)} For each $j\in\llbracket1,s-1\rrbracket$ we have $p^j\mid l_{j+1}-l_j$ and
$$l_{j+1}-l_j\ge (p-1)\sum_{i=0}^{j-1} p^{j-i}(l_{i+1}-l_i).$$

\noindent
{\bf (2.c)} For each $j\in\llbracket1,s-1\rrbracket$ such that $l_{j+1}-l_j> (p-1)\sum_{i=0}^{j-1} p^{j-i}(l_{i+1}-l_i)$, the positive integer $l_1+\sum_{i=1}^{j}\frac{l_{i+1}-l_i}{p^i}$ is not divisible by $p$.

body: [Lemma uniform-lipschitz of arXiv:2608.12056, 'Deviation inequalities for U-processes of growing order, with applications to half-space d'] Let $X_1, X_2 \ldots$ be i.i.d. copies of a random variable $X \in \mathbb R^d$ with $\mathbb E X = 0$ and $\mathrm{cov} (X) = I_d$. Moreover, assume that $X$ has elliptically symmetric distribution with characteristic generator $\psi : \mathbb R_+ \mapsto \mathbb R$. Given $u \in \mathcal{S}^{d-1}$, let $Z_n(u) = \dotp{\frac{\sum_{j=1}^n X_j}{\sqrt{n}}}{u}$. Assume that there exists $\alpha > 0$ and $M > 0$ such that $\psi(t^2) = o\left(\frac{1}{t^\alpha}\right)$ whenever $t > M$. Then for $n_0 \in \mathbb N$ large enough and all $n \geq n_0$, the density of $Z_n(u)$ exists and is Lipschitz continuous with a uniform Lipschitz constant for all $n$ sufficiently large.

body:
[Prop integrable-mtg of arXiv:2411.08725, 'Berry-Esseen bounds for large-time asymptotics of one-dimensional diffusion processes via '] Let $a>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\rm (i)}] 
Let $f$ be a bounded nonnegative Borel function on ${\mathbb R}$ such that 
$\int_0^{\infty}f(x)dx<\infty$, and let $M=\sup_{x\in {\mathbb R}}f(x)$. 
Then for any $c<\frac{\sigma_1^2 a^2}{2M}$,
\[
E\left[\exp\left(c\int_0^{\infty}f(x+M_t^x+a\langle M^x\rangle_t)dt\right)\right]<\infty, 
\quad x\in {\mathbb R}.
\]
Moreover, if $f$ is nonincreasing, then for any $x_0\in {\mathbb R}$,
\[
\sup_{x\in [x_0,\infty)}E\left[\exp\left(c\int_0^{\infty}f(x+M_t^x+a \langle M^x\rangle_t)dt\right)\right]<\infty.
\]
\item[{\rm (ii)}] 
Let $f$ be a bounded Borel function on ${\mathbb R}$ such that $\int_0^{\infty}|f(x)|dx<\infty$. 
Then for any $p\in [0,\infty)$, 
\[
\sup_{t\ge 0}E\left[\left|\int_0^t f(x+M_t^x+a \langle M^x\rangle_t)dt\right|^p\right]<\infty, \quad x\in {\mathbb R}.
\]
Moreover, if $f$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing, then for any $x_0\in {\mathbb R}$,
\[
\sup_{x\in [x_0,\infty)}E\left[\left(\int_0^{\infty} f(x+M_t^x+a \langle M^x\rangle_t)dt\right)^p\right]<\infty.
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Prop integrable-mtg of arXiv:2411.08725

[Lemma 31 ({\cite[Lemma A.1) of arXiv:2607.08696, 'Spectrum of Directed Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] {Coste}}] 
Let $\xx$ and $\yy$ be two vectors of $\R^n$ and $\deterministic =\xx\yy^t$. Let $H_n$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The eigenvalues of the matrix $\deterministic + H_n$ are contained in  
$\mathcal{B}(0, \eps_n) \cup \mathcal{B}(\yy^t\xx, \eps_n)$, where
$$\eps_n = 2\|\xx\|^2\|\yy\|^2(\yy^t\xx)^{-2}\|H_n \|;$$
\item[(ii)] If 
$\mathcal{B}(0, \eps_n) \cap \mathcal{B}(\yy^t\xx, \eps_n) = \emptyset$, then there is exactly one eigenvalue of $\deterministic + H_n$ inside 
$\mathcal{B}(\yy^t\xx, \eps_n)$ and all the other eigenvalues of $\deterministic + H_n$ are contained in $\mathcal{B}(0, \eps_n)$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For nearest-neighbour independent Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d, integer d>=2, Duminil-Copin and Tassion's Theorem 1.1 states that for each fixed p<p_c there exists c(p)>0 such that P_p(0 connects to the boundary of [-n,n]^d)<=exp(-c(p)n) for all n>=1. The quantifiers do not supply a rate bounded away from zero uniformly as p increases to p_c and do not give an upper one-arm bound at p=p_c. A proof requiring critical decay needs another argument.
Independent nearest-neighbour Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d
Integer d>=2
Each p is fixed strictly below its critical parameter
title: Sharpness gives a separate exponential rate for each subcritical parameter

[Lemma lem:corner of arXiv:2608.30491, 'The Daugavet property in symmetric operator spaces'] Let $\mathcal{M}$ be atomless,  let $0\neq p\in\mathcal{M}$ be a projection, let $u\in\mathcal{M}$ be a partial isometry with $p\leq u^*u$, and let $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_n\in\mathcal{M}_*$. $$\|d\omega_i\|<\delta,\qquad \|\omega_i r\|<\delta,\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.$$

body:
[Corollary cor:label-configuration-reversal of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] For fixed $h\geq2$ and $k\geq3$, as $q\to\infty$ a uniformly random
$A\in\binom{[q]}k$ satisfies
\[
 \mathbb P(A\text{ is not }B_h)
 =\frac{k!K_{h,k}}q+O_{h,k}(q^{-2}),
 \qquad K_{h,k}\asymp_k h^{k-2}.
\]
For each $2\leq r\leq h$,
\[
 \mathbb P(|hA|=M_{h,k}-M_{h-r,k})
 =\frac{k!\kappa_{k,r}}q+O_{h,k}(q^{-2}).
\]
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
  \mathbb P\bigl(r_{h,k}(|hA|)\leq1\bigr)
   &=1-O_{h,k}(q^{-2}),\\
  \mathbb P\bigl(r_h(A)=1\mid A\text{ is not }B_h\bigr)
   &=1-O_{h,k}(q^{-1}).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
By contrast, if $k\geq4$ is fixed and $N_{h,k}$ is uniform in the finite set
$\mathcal R(h,k)$, then, as $h\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P\bigl(r_{h,k}(N_{h,k})\leq1\bigr)
 =\frac{h}{|\mathcal R(h,k)|}
 =h^{-(k-2)+o_k(1)}\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Thus principal labels are asymptotically negligible among attainable
cardinalities, although their realizations account for asymptotically almost
every fixed-order configuration in a growing interval.
Here $h$ is fixed before $q\to\infty$;
no joint $(h,q)$ assertion is made.

body:
[Pro Pro_basic_properties of arXiv:2606.22183, 'Expected loss of quasi-arithmetic means of exchangeable random variables'] Let $I\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a nondegenerate interval.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
 \item If $L_i:I\to\mathbb{R}$ is strongly $\alpha_i$-convex for $i=1,2$, where $\alpha_1,\alpha_2:(I-I)\to\mathbb{R}_+$ are even error functions
       and $c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{R}_+$, then $c_1L_1+c_2L_2$ is strongly $(c_1\alpha_1+c_2\alpha_2)$-convex.
 \item If $\alpha_1,\alpha_2:(I-I)\to\mathbb{R}_+$ are even error functions with $\alpha_1\leqslant\alpha_2$ and $L:I\to\mathbb{R}$ is strongly $\alpha_2$-convex, then $L$ is strongly $\alpha_1$-convex as well.
 \item If, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $L_n:I\to\mathbb{R}$ is strongly $\alpha_n$-convex, where $\alpha_n:(I-I)\to\mathbb{R}_+$ is an even error function,
 and the sequences $(L_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and $ (\alpha_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ pointwise converge to $L:I\to\mathbb{R}$ and to $\alpha:(I-I)\to\mathbb{R}_+$ as $n\to\infty$, respectively, then $L$ is strongly $\alpha$-convex.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED.

    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item For any flat $G$ in $L$, we have
    \(
        \rk_M F + \rk_M G = \rk_M (F \vee G) + \rk_M (F \cap G).
    \)
    \item For any flat $G$ of $M$ with $\rk_M F + \rk_M G > \rk M$, we have $\rk_M (F \cap G) > 0$.
    \end{enumerate}
    We say $F$ is \textbf{{modular}} in $M$ if it satisfies these equivalent conditions.

\left(\fint_{t/2-\delta r_1^2}^{t/2+\delta r_1^2}\|{B_z(r_1)}P_\tau^\omega\|_{2,2p}^{2p}\drm \tau\right)^\frac{1}{p}
\leq \phi_z(h(\omega))^2\fint_{t/2-\delta  r_2^2}^{t/2+\delta r_2^2}\| P_\tau^\omega\|_{2,2}^2\drm \tau.

Then, for $t\geq 2r_1^2$,  we have

Let H: R^n → R be convex and superlinear, i.e. H(p)/|p| → +∞ as |p| → ∞. Its Legendre (Fenchel) transform is L(q) := sup_{p ∈ R^n} ( p·q - H(p) ), q ∈ R^n, and L is called the Lagrangian associated with H. Then: (i) the supremum is attained for every q, and L is finite, convex and superlinear; (ii) L* = H, i.e. H(p) = sup_q ( p·q - L(q) ) (duality of H and L); (iii) Fenchel-Young: p·q ≤ H(p) + L(q) for all p,q, with equality iff q ∈ ∂H(p) iff p ∈ ∂L(q); (iv) if in addition H ∈ C^2 with D^2H(p) ≥ θ I for all p and some θ > 0, then DH: R^n → R^n is a bijection, L ∈ C^1, DL = (DH)^{-1}, DL is Lipschitz with constant 1/θ, and consequently L(q+w) + L(q-w) - 2L(q) ≤ |w|^2/θ for all q,w.
H: R^n → R is finite everywhere and convex (hence continuous)
H is superlinear: H(p)/|p| → ∞ as |p| → ∞
for part (iv): H ∈ C^2 and D^2H ≥ θI with θ > 0 (which already implies superlinearity)

[Lemma 8 (Laplace transform of the ordinary uniform collector) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Let $C_n$ be the ordinary uniform coupon collector time measured in standard-coupon draws.  Then, for $0\le x<1$,
\[
        \phi_n(x)=\prod_{j=1}^n\frac{(j/n)x}{1-(1-j/n)x}.
\]
Consequently, with $q_n=1-\rho_n$,
\[
        s_n=\phi_n(q_n)
        =\prod_{j=1}^n\frac{j}{j+n\rho_n/q_n}
        =\frac{\Gamma(n+1)\Gamma(1+n\rho_n/q_n)}
        {\Gamma(n+1+n\rho_n/q_n)}.
\]

[Corollary cor:BMcC of arXiv:2605.10491, 'Zero-couplings of infinite measures with cyclically monotone support and multivariate regu'] Let $\mu,\nu\in\mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be such that at least one of them has infinite mass and suppose $\mu$ vanishes on sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $d-1$.
    Then $\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{cm}}(\mu,\nu)$ is a singleton with single element $\gamma$, say, and there exists a closed convex function $\psi$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\operatorname{spt} \gamma \subset \partial \psi$ such that
    \begin{align*}
        \gamma(A \times B) 
        &= (\operatorname{Id} \times \nabla\psi)_{\#}\mu(A\times B)
        = \mu \rbr{A \cap (\nabla\psi)^{-1}(B)}, &&
        A \in \mathcal{B}(\reals^d_{\smallsetminus 0}), \, B \in \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d), \\
        \gamma(\left\{0\right\} \times B)
        &= \nu(B) - (\nabla\psi)_{\#} \mu(B), &&
        B \in \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d), \, 0 \not\in \operatorname{cl}(B).
    \end{align*}
    Although $\psi$ may not be unique, the map $\nabla\psi$ is defined and uniquely determined $\mu$-almost everywhere. If, in addition, $\gamma$ is proper, then
    \begin{equation}
    
        \nu(B) 
        = (\nabla\psi)_{\#}\mu(B) 
        = \mu \rbr{\reals^d_{\smallsetminus 0} \cap (\nabla\psi)^{-1}(B)},
        \qquad B \in \mathcal{B}(\reals^d_{\smallsetminus 0}).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The chi laws in small dimensions are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\item At $n=1$ the chi law and its moments are as follows:
$$\chi_{1t}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{t\pi}}\,e^{-x^2/2t}dx\quad,\quad 
M_k=\sqrt{\frac{(2t)^k}{\pi}}\,\Gamma\left(\frac{k+1}{2}\right)$$

\item At $n=2$ the chi law and its moments are as follows:
$$\chi_{2t}=\frac{1}{t}\,xe^{-x^2/2t}dx\quad,\quad 
M_k=\sqrt{(2t)^k}\,\Gamma\left(\frac{k}{2}+1\right)$$

\item At $n=3$ the chi law and its moments are as follows:
$$\chi_{3t}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{t^3\pi}}\,x^2e^{-x^2/2t}dx\quad,\quad 
M_k=2\sqrt{\frac{(2t)^k}{\pi}}\,\Gamma\left(\frac{k+3}{2}\right)$$
\end{enumerate}
The law $\chi_{2t}$ is called Rayleigh law, and the law $\chi_{3t}$ is called Maxwell-Boltzmann law.

  $$(u+v)^p\le (1+\delta) u^p+ C_{p,\delta} v^p.$$

body:
[Thma 1 (Model-potential nonuniqueness) of arXiv:2609.03296, 'Nonuniqueness of Model Potentials and Weak Geodesic Rays'] For every \(\rho\in(0,1)\), there exist distinct normalized positive-mass model
potentials
\[
 \phi,\psi\in\PSH(\CP^1,\omega_{\mathrm{FS}})
\]
and a closed Fubini--Study disk \(C\subset\CP^1\) such that
\[
 \left\langle\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}+\ddc\phi\right\rangle
 =
 \left\langle\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}+\ddc\psi\right\rangle
 =
 \one_C\omega_{\mathrm{FS}},
\]
with total mass \(1-\rho>0\). By the contact-set formula
\cite[Corollary~3.4(ii)]{DNT21}, this is equivalent to
\[
 \one_{\{\phi=0\}}
 =
 \one_{\{\psi=0\}}
 =
 \one_C
 \qquad \omega_{\mathrm{FS}}\text{-a.e.}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \nu(\phi,x)=\nu(\psi,x)=0
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in\CP^1,
\]
and
\[
 \cI(c\phi)=\OO_{\CP^1}=\cI(c\psi)
 \qquad\text{for every }c>0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Model-potential nonuniqueness

[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2607.17192, 'Geometric Regime--Switching Diffusions on Stratified Riemannian Spaces with an Application'] Let $\P_x$ be the solution to $(A,\cl D_0)$ constructed in Theorem~\ref{thm:existence} and call $X$ the corresponding process on $E$. Then:
		\begin{itemize}
			\item[(iii)] the jumps of $X$ are governed by the structural kernels and rates:
			whenever $X_{t-}=x\in S_\alpha$, jumps of type $e\in\cl E$ with $\alpha(e)=\alpha$
			occur with conditional intensity $\lambda_e(x)$, and conditional on such a jump of type $e$,
			the post-jump location has law $K_e(x,\cdot)$;
			\item[(iv)] for every $f\in\cl D_0$, the process
			\[
			M_t^f=f(X_t)-f(X_0)-\int_0^t A f(X_s)\,ds
			\]
			is an $(\cl F_t^x)$--martingale. In particular, the law of $X$
			on $D_E$ is a solution of the martingale problem for
			$(A,\cl D_0)$ with initial condition $x$.
		\end{itemize}

[Lemma lemma mean and var bounds of arXiv:2505.15940, 'Degrees of Freedom for Critical Random 2-SAT'] Let $r,s\in[0,R]$ with $s<r$. Then
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
        \item $\mathbb{E}[N_1^{(r)}|N_1^{(1)},\dotsc,N_1^{(s)}]\leq N_1^{(s)},$
        \item $\mathbb{E}[(N_1^{(r)})^2|N_1^{(1)},\dotsc,N_1^{(s)}]\leq RN_1^{(s)}+(N_1^{(s)})^2$,
        \item Assume $N_1^{(s)}\leq C_0 n^q$ for some $C_0>0$. Then there exists $C_1 >0$ (dependent on $C_0$ but independent of $r$ and $s$) such that  
        $\mathbb{E}[N_1^{(r)}|N_1^{(1)},\dotsc,N_1^{(s)}]\geq N_1^{(s)}-C_1 n^{1-2q}\log^4{n}$
        \item Assume $c_0 n^q\leq N_1^{(s)}\leq C_0 n^q$ for some $c_0,C_0>0$. Then there exists $C_2 >0$ (dependent on $c_0$ and $C_0$ but independent of $r$ and $s$) such that $\mathbb{V}\big[N_1^{(r)}\big|N_1^{(1)},\dotsc,N_1^{(s)}\big]\leq C_2 n^{1-q}\log^4{n}.$
    \end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lemma mean and var bounds of arXiv:2505.15940

[Corollary 21 of arXiv:2510.24244, 'Statistical properties of Markov shifts: part II-LLT'] \,

(i) If $\|S_nf\|_{L^2}\not\to \infty$ then $\mathsf{H}=\bbR$.
\vskip0.2cm

(ii) If $(f_j)$ is irreducible then $\mathsf{H}=\{0\}$.
\vskip0.2cm

(iii) If $(f_j)$ is reducible and $\|S_nf\|_{L^2}\to \infty$    then 
$
\mathsf{H}=t_0\bbZ
$
for some $t_0>0$. 

As a consequence, the number $h_0=1/t_0$ is the largest positive number such that $(f_j)$ is reducible to an $h_0\bbZ$-valued sequence.

body: [Theorem thm:twolist of arXiv:2608.23638, 'Replicable Conformal Prediction'] Fix public constants $\Delta>0$, $0<f_{\min}\le f_{\max}<\infty$; let $\mathfrak F$ be the nonempty class of continuous score distributions satisfying Assumption~(ass:margin of the paper) with these constants, $\kappa=f_{\max}/f_{\min}$, $\beta=\varepsilon/(2f_{\max})\le\Delta/2$, and $0<\varepsilon<\min(\alpha,1-\alpha)$. \emph{(a)} For $F\in\mathfrak F$ and $n\ge\lceil32\kappa^{2}\log(2/\delta)/\varepsilon^{2}\rceil$, deterministic-grid \textsc{ReCal}{} ($u=0$) satisfies, with probability $\ge1-\delta$ over the calibration sample, the \emph{joint} event that $\tau$ lies in a sample-independent two-element list $\mathcal{L}_{n,\delta}(F)=\{g,g+\beta\}\subset\beta\mathbb Z$, depending only on $F$ and the public parameters and hence unknown to the analysts, \emph{and} $F(\tau)\in[1-\alpha-\tfrac{\varepsilon}{4\kappa},\,1-\alpha+\tfrac\varepsilon2+\tfrac{\varepsilon}{4\kappa}]\subseteq[1-\alpha\pm\varepsilon]$; any $m$ analysts all land in the common list with probability $\ge1-m\delta$, marginal validity is preserved, and no $\rho^{-2}$ factor appears. \emph{(b)} For $\delta<\tfrac12$, list size two is optimal within $\mathfrak F$: no procedure (any sample size, any seed law) has both a deterministic singleton output $v_F$ and the two-sided band, each with probability $\ge1-\delta$, for every $F\in\mathfrak F$; this is already impossible on $\{\mathrm{Unif}[t,t+f_{\min}^{-1}]\}\subseteq\mathfrak F$, whose membership needs only $f_{\min}\Delta\le\min(\alpha,1-\alpha)$, forced by $\mathfrak F\neq\varnothing$ (Lemma~(lem:translate of the paper)). The optimality claim is about numerical thresholds; it transfers to classifier maps whenever $t\mapsto\mathcal{C}_t$ is injective on the admissible range (Appendix~(app:twolist of the paper)). (Proof: Appendix~(app:twolist of the paper).) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:finite-information of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] Let $A$ take values in a finite set $\mathcal A$, let $B,D$ be
countable-valued, and let $C$ take values in a standard Borel space.  Fix
one regular conditional law $p_{A,B,D\mid c}$ of the joint triple
$(A,B,D)$ given $C=c$.  Every conditional marginal and every further
conditional law below is understood to be derived from this joint kernel.
Then
\begin{align}
 0\leq I(A;B\mid C)
 &=H(A\mid C)-H(A\mid B,C)\notag\\
 &\leq H(A\mid C)\leq H(A)\leq\log|\mathcal A|,
 \\
 I(A;B,D\mid C)
 &=I(A;B\mid C)+I(A;D\mid B,C).
 
\end{align}
In particular, $I(A;B)\leq I(A;B,D)$.  Conditional mutual information is
symmetric in its first two arguments.  Consequently, if $B$ is also finite,
then $I(A;B\mid C)\leq H(B\mid C)$.  If $X$ is countable-valued with
$H(X)<\infty$, then $H(A,X)<\infty$ and
\begin{align}
 H(A,X)&=H(X)+H(A\mid X)\leq H(X)+H(A),
 \\
 I(A;X)&=H(A)+H(X)-H(A,X).
 
\end{align}
In particular, independence gives $H(A,X)=H(A)+H(X)$.  If $Y$ is a
deterministic function of a discrete $X$ with $H(X)<\infty$, then
$H(Y)\leq H(X)$.

body:
[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2511.01456, 'Zero distribution of multiplicative Hermite and Laguerre polynomials'] Let $(b_n)_{n\in \N} \subseteq \C$ and $(c_n)_{n\in \N} \subseteq \N_0$ be sequences such that
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{b_n}{n} = \beta\in\C, \qquad \beta \neq -1,
\qquad
\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{c_n}{n} = \gamma \geq 0.
$$
The dependence on the parameters $b_n$ and $\beta$ will be suppressed in the notation.  Recall that $\sigma_{k;n}(c_n)$ is the $k$-th moment of the zero distribution of $L_n^*(x; b_n, c_n)$. Then, for all $k\in \N_0$,
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} \sigma_{k;n}(c_n) = f_k(\gamma) := \eee^{- \frac{\gamma k}{1+\beta}} g_k(\gamma),
$$
where the functions $g_k(\gamma)$, $k\in \N_0$, are the same as in Proposition~\ref{prop:conv_to_ODE_laguerre}, and the functions $f_k(\gamma)$, $k\in \N_0$, satisfy the following  system of ODE's:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&f_k'(\gamma)
=
-\frac 1 {1+\beta}  \sum_{j=1}^{k} j  f_j(\gamma)
\widehat{B}_{ k-j} \left(f_1(\gamma),\ldots, f_{k-j}(\gamma); - \frac 1 {1+\beta}\right),
\quad k\in \N,\ \gamma\geq 0,
\\
&f_{0}(\gamma) =  1 \quad (\text{for all } \gamma\geq 0), \qquad f_{k}(0) = 1 \quad (\text{for all } k\in  \mathbb N).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2607.22470, 'A Logarithmic Fluctuation Hierarchy for Sequential Interacting Diffusions'] Fix \(n\ge0\) and let \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\R^d)\). Then, as
\(N\to\infty\),
\[
  \mathbb E\sup_{0\le t\le T}
  \left|
  \int_0^t \mathcal R_s^{N,n}(\varphi)\,\dd s
  \right|
  \to0
\]
and hence \(\int_0^\cdot \mathcal R_s^{N,n}(\varphi)\,\dd s\to0\) in probability in
\(C([0,T];\R)\).

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.08242, 'Bang--bang representation of $3\times 3$ embeddable stochastic matrices'] Let $L=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3)$ and
$R=\operatorname{diag}(\rho_1,\rho_2,\rho_3)$ be positive, and put
$\lambda=\det L$ and $\rho=\det R$. Let $A\in \mathcal M_+$ and put $B=LAR$. Then
\[
T_{ij}(B)=\frac{\lambda\rho}{\lambda_i\rho_j}T_{ij}(A),
\qquad
G(B)=\lambda\rho G(A),
\]
\[
V_{ii}(B)=\lambda\rho V_{ii}(A),
\qquad
V_{ij}(B)=\lambda\rho\lambda_j\rho_iV_{ij}(A)
\quad(i\neq j),
\]
\[
C_{ij}(B)=\frac{\rho_j}{\rho_i}C_{ij}(A),
\]
and
\[
q_{ij}^{B}(c)
=\lambda\rho\lambda_i\rho_j\,
 q_{ij}^A\!\left(\frac{\rho_i}{\rho_j}c\right).
\]
Moreover,
$T_{ij}(A^t)=T_{ji}(A)$ and
$V_{ij}(A^t)=V_{ji}(A)$.

[Definition def:optimalweightoperator of arXiv:2608.23765, '\texorpdfstring{Tight Majorizations and Convergence Rates\\ of Nuclear Norm Minimization I'] Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and $\mathbf{X} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ be a matrix with the full singular value decomposition 
$\mathbf{X}= \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag (\boldsymbol{\sigma}) \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top$, 
where $\mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}}  \in \R^{d_1 \times d_1}$ and $\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}} \in \R^{d_2 \times d_2}$ are orthogonal
and $\diag (\boldsymbol{\sigma}) \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ is the rectangular diagonal matrix with the extended vector of singular values $\boldsymbol{\sigma} \in \R^{D}$ of $\mathbf{X}$ on the diagonal.
Then the  \emph{weight operator}  $\W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon}: \R^{d_1 \times d_2} \to \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ 
is defined by
\begin{equation} 
	\W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon}(\mathbf{Z}) = \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \left[\mathbf{H}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma},\varepsilon} \circ (\mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}}^{\top} \mathbf{Z} \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}})\right] \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^{\top}
\end{equation}
for each $\mathbf{Z} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$.
Here $\mathbf{H}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma},\varepsilon}$ is the 
weight operator core matrix of (def:weightcore of the paper).

There are exactly 9270 self-avoiding walks of length 13 that start at (0,0), stay in the strip 0 <= y < 3, and avoid the sites (-4,2), (-3,1), (-2,0).
