[Definition 8 (XY model) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d\in\Z_{\geq 1}$ and $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
    For any domain $\Lambda$ and $\zeta:\Z^d\to\S^1$,
    the \emph{XY model} on $\Lambda$ with boundary condition $\zeta$
    at inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure  on $\sigma\in(\S^1)^\Lambda$ given by
    \[
        \diff\mu_{\XYM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma) = \frac1{Z_{\XYM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta} e^{-\beta H_{\XYM,\Lambda}^\zeta(\sigma)} \diff\sigma,
    \]
    where $Z_{\XYM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta$ is the normalising constant,
    $\diff\sigma$ the Haar measure, and
    \[
        H_{\XYM,\Lambda}^\zeta(\sigma) := \sum_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda\\x\sim y}} |\sigma_x-\sigma_y|^2/2 + \sum_{\substack{x\in\Lambda,\,y\in\Lambda^c\\x\sim y}} |\sigma_x-\zeta_y|^2/2.
    \]
    The \emph{critical inverse temperature} is defined as the largest $\beta_c=\beta_c(d)\in(0,\infty)$
    such that $\mu_{\XY,\Lambda_n,\beta}^{+1}[\sigma_0]$ decays exponentially fast in $n$
    for any fixed $\beta\in[0,\beta_c)$.
    Classical arguments based on correlations inequalities imply the existence of an infinite-volume Gibbs measure with $+1$ boundary conditions at inverse temperature $\beta\geq 0$, that we refer to as $\mu^{+1}_{\XY, \beta}$.
    The label $\XYM$ is omitted from notations when it is clear from the context.
title: XY model

[Lemma lem:arnold of arXiv:2604.28068, 'Mean-square Stability and Bifurcations for Dissipative SDEs'] Let ${\widetilde{Y}}$ be a solution of the SDE (equation eq:sdeLinMult of the paper). Then the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The mean vector $M(t):=\expect{{\widetilde{Y}}(t)}$, $t\geq 0$, is the unique solution of the ODE
        \[
            M'(t)=AM(t)+\Lambda,
        \]
        with initial value $M(0)={\widetilde{Y}}(0)$.
        \item The second moment matrix $P(t):=\expect{{\widetilde{Y}}(t){\widetilde{Y}}(t)^T}$, $t\geq 0$, is the unique nonnegative definite symmetric solution of the equation
        \begin{multline}
            P'(t)=AP(t)+P(t)A^T+\Lambda M(t)^T+M(t)\Lambda^T
            \\+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(B_i P(t)B_i^T+B_i M(t)\Gamma_i^T+\Gamma_i M(t)^T B_i^T+\Gamma_i\Gamma_i^T\right),
        \end{multline}
        with initial value $P(0)={\widetilde{Y}}(0){\widetilde{Y}}(0)^T$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 8.5.5, Arnold~\cite{arnold1974stochastic}

body:
[Prop 39 of arXiv:2609.01932, 'Essential dimension and faithful rank of finite $p$-gerbes'] Choose a $P$-representation $W$ with a nonempty $P$-stable open subset
$U\subset W$ on which $P$ acts freely.  Put
\[
K=k(U/P),
\qquad
E_{\mathrm{gen}}=U_K.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\ed_K\bigl(\operatorname{Lift}_{P'}(E_{\mathrm{gen}});p\bigr)
=\rdim_p(P',N).
\end{equation}
In particular, $E_{\mathrm{gen}}$ realizes the supremum in
Corollary~\ref{cor:embedding-problem}.

Moreover, let $F=k^{(p)}$ be a $p$-closure of $k$, put
\[
K_F=F(U_F/P),
\]
and let $E_{\mathrm{gen},F}$ be the generic fiber of
$U_F\to U_F/P$.  Then
\begin{equation}
\ed_{K_F}\bigl(\operatorname{Lift}_{P'}(E_{\mathrm{gen},F})\bigr)
=
\ed_{K_F}\bigl(\operatorname{Lift}_{P'}(E_{\mathrm{gen},F});p\bigr)
=
\rdim_p(P',N).
\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] There exists a universal constant \(C>0\) such that the following
	holds. Let \(N\geq d\ge C\), \(0<\eps<C^{-1}\), and let
	\(X\subseteq \R^d\) with \(|X|=N\). Then there
	exists an ORA-based random linear map
	\(\Phi:\R^d\to\R^m\), with \(m\le C\eps^{-2}\log N\), such that
	\[
	(1-\eps)\norm{x}_2
	\le
	\norm{\Phi x}_2
	\le
	(1+\eps)\norm{x}_2
	\qquad
	\text{for every }x\in X,
	\]
	with probability at least \(2/3\). Moreover, \(\Phi x\) can be computed in time
	\[
	O\left(
	d\log d+
	\min\left\{
	d\log d\log N,\,
	\eps^{-2}(\log N)^2(\log\log N)^2(\log d)^4
	\right\}
	\right)
	\]
	using \(O(1)\) additional working memory. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 214 (Integral inequalities for the below-top-order vorticity- and entropy gradient-controlling quantities) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $0 \leq N \leq \Ntop$, and recall that the $L^2$-controlling quantities
	$\fluxcontrolVort_{ N}$, 
	$\fluxcontrolGradEnt_{ N}$,
	$\cdots$, are defined in
	Defs.\,\ref{D:MAINCOERCIVE} and\,\ref{D:SUMMEDL2CONTROLLINGQUANTITIES}.
	Then by making the constant $\varsigma_0$ from Lemma\,\ref{L:PRELIMINARYBELOWTOPORDERL2ESTIMATESFOREIKONALFUINCTIONQUANTITIES} (see also Remark\,\ref{R:SMALLNESSCONSTANTFORBELOWTOPORDERACOUSTICVARIABLES}) potentially even smaller, the following integral inequality holds for
	$(\ubar,u) \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot) \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]$:
	\begin{align}   
		\begin{split}
			& \fluxcontrolVort_{N}(\ubar,u)
			+
			\fluxcontrolGradEnt_{N}(\ubar,u) + \blowuprateoftransportWRTnumberofcommutations(N) \left( \bulkcontrolVort_N(\ubar,u) + \bulkcontrolGradEnt_N(\ubar,u) \right)\\
			& \ \   \lesssim
			\initialsmall^2
				+ 
			\int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar} \frac{1}{|\ubar'|^{0.13}} 
			\left\lbrace 
				\fluxcontrolVort_{\leq N}(\ubar,u')
				+
				\fluxcontrolGradEnt_{\leq N}(\ubar,u')
			\right\rbrace
			\, \rmd \ubar' 
			\\	
			& \ \ \ \ +
			\int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u
				\left\lbrace 
					\fluxcontrolVort_{\leq N}(\ubar,u')
					+
					\fluxcontrolGradEnt_{\leq N}(\ubar,u')
				\right\rbrace
			\, \rmd u'
			+
			(1+\varsigma_0^{-1})\fundbootsmall^2 
			\int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar} \frac{1}{|\ubar'|^{0.13}} 
				\totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar',u) 
			\, \rmd \ubar' \\
			& \ \ \ \ + (1 + \varsigma_0^{-1})\fundbootsmall^2 \int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u \totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,N+1]}(\ubar,u') \, \mathrm{d} u' + (1+\varsigma_0^{-1}) \fundbootsmall^2 \strongangularcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar,u) \\
			& \ \ \ \ + \fundbootsmall^2 \weakspacetimetransvelocitycontrol_{[1,N]}(\ubar,u) + \fundbootsmall^2 \weakspacetimeangularvelocitycontrol_{[1,N]}(\ubar,u)
		\end{split}
	\end{align}
	

	
	
	Moreover, the following estimates hold for $0 \leq N \leq \Ntop - 1$:
	\begin{align} 
	\begin{split} 
		\fluxcontrolVortVort_{\leq N}(\ubar,u)
		+
		\fluxcontrolDivGradEnt_{\leq N}(\ubar,u)
		& \lesssim
		\initialsmall^2 +	\int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar}	\left\lbrace 
				\fluxcontrolVortVort_{\leq N}(\ubar,u')
				+
				\fluxcontrolDivGradEnt_{\leq N}(\ubar,u')
			\right\rbrace
			\, \rmd \ubar' 
		+
		\int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u
			\left\lbrace
				\;{\leq N}(\ubar,u')
				+
				\fluxcontrolDivGradEnt_{\leq N}(\ubar,u)
			\right\rbrace
		\, \rmd u'
			\\
	& \ \
		+
		\int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u 
			\left\lbrace
				\fluxcontrolVort_{\leq N+1}(\ubar,u')
				+
				\fluxcontrolGradEnt_{\leq N+1}(\ubar,u')
			\right\rbrace
		\, \rmd u'	
			+
		(1 + \varsigma_0^{-1})\fundbootsmall^2 
		\int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar}	\totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar',u) 
		\, \rmd \ubar' \\
		& \ \ 
		+
		(1 + \varsigma_0^{-1})\fundbootsmall^2 
		\int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u 
			\totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar,u')
		\, \rmd u' 
		+ 
		(1 + \varsigma_0^{-1})\fundbootsmall^2 \strongangularcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar,u).
	\end{split}
	\end{align}

[Theorem 5 (McLeish, 1974) of arXiv:2604.07579, 'Topology of Percolation Clusters: Central Limit Theorems beyond the Lattice'] Let $\{X_{r,j}\}_{r \geq 1, 1 \leq
      j \leq b_r}$ be a martingale difference array with respect to filtrations
      $\{\mathcal{F}_{r,j}\}$, satisfying:
      \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\max_{1 \leq j \leq b_r}|X_{r,j}|$ is uniformly bounded in
          $L_{2}$-norm;

        \item $\max_{1 \leq j \leq b_r}|X_{r,j}|$ converges in probability
          to $0$; and

        \item $\sum_{j=1}^{b_r}X^{2}_{r,j}$ converges in probability to $1$.
      \end{enumerate}
      Then, denoting $S_{r}= \sum_{j=1}^{b_r}X_{r,j}$, $S_{r}$ converges in
      distribution to $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

	\mE \eta_{\tau}^p\leq \bigg(\mE \exp\bigg[\frac{p}{1-p}(\theta^{1/\theta} (A_\tau^1)^\theta+A_\tau^2)\bigg]\bigg)^{1-p}(\mE V_{\tau})^p, ~\mbox{when}~ \theta> 1.

[Theorem 20 (Perfect reduction of the parabolic bar complex) of arXiv:2609.01882, '\textbf{Coxeter Descents and Parabolic Homotopy Colimits}\\[2mm] \large A Hochster-type de'] Let $(W,S)$ be a finite Coxeter system, $r=|S|$, and $N=\ell(w_0)$. The based complex $\BK(W)$ admits a unit acyclic matching whose only critical generators are
\[
  [e;\varnothing]\quad\text{in degree }0,
  \qquad
  \xi_{w_0}\quad\text{in degree }2N+r-1.
\]
Consequently its algebraic Morse complex is
\begin{equation}
  \BK(W)_{\mathrm{Morse}}\cong\Z[0]\oplus\Z[2N+r-1]
\end{equation}
with zero differential.

[Thm 3 (see Theorem \ref{thm:coho-ring-conf} and Corollary \ref{cor:Hdef-group-structure}) of arXiv:2608.28200, '\textbf On the Formality of Configuration Spaces of $\aka$'] For $n'+n\ge2$, the cohomology ring $\Hdef(\maka)$ is generated  by 
$$
\C[z_j^1,\cdots,z_j^n]\oplus \oplus_{i<j} {\C[\partial_{z^1_j},\cdots, \partial_{z^n_j}]\omega_{ij}},
$$
subject to the following relations:  
\begin{itemize}
\item $f(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij}\cdot g(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij}=0$, for $f(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij}, g(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij}\in {\C[\partial_{z^1_j},\cdots, \partial_{z^n_j}]\omega_{ij}}$,
\item $
\zz_{ij}^{\xalpha}\partial_{\zz_j}^{\xbeta}\omega_{ij}=
\begin{cases}
(-1)^{\alpha_1+\cdots +\alpha_n} \prod_{i=1}^n \frac{\beta_i!}{(\beta_i-\alpha_i)!} \, \partial_{\zz_j}^{\xbeta-\xalpha}\omega_{ij} & \alpha_i\le \beta_i \text{ for all } i \\
0 & \alpha_i>\beta_i \text{ for some } i \\
\end{cases},
$
\item the Arnold relation:
$$g(\partial_{\zz_j})(f(\partial_{\zz_i})\omega_{ij}h(\partial_{\zz_k})\omega_{jk})+h(\partial_{\zz_k})(g(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{jk}f(\partial_{\zz_i})\omega_{ki})+f(\partial_{\zz_i})(h(\partial_{\zz_k})\omega_{ki}g(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij})=0.$$
\end{itemize}
Moreover, when identified with subspaces of $\A(\maka)$, $H^\bullet(\maka)$ is the closure of \\ $\Hconk(\maka)$ with respect to the nuclear topology. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Defn uniqueness of arXiv:2512.17736, 'Pathwise uniqueness by noise for singular stochastic PDEs'] Assume (H0 of the paper)--(H4 of the paper) and let $H_0\subseteq H$. 
\begin{itemize}
\item[(Weak)] We say that weak uniqueness 
holds for (equation SDE of the paper) with initial data in $H_0$
if for every $x\in H_0$ and
for every pair $(X_1,W_1)$ and $(X_2,W_2)$ of weak mild solutions to (equation SDE of the paper) defined on the same probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\{\mathcal F_t\}_{t\geq0},\mathbb P)$ with $X_1(0)=X_2(0)=x$, 
it holds that $X_1$ and $X_2$ have the same law on $C^0(\mathbb R_+; H)$, namely that for every measurable bounded $\psi:C^0(\mathbb R_+; H)\to \mathbb R$
\[
\mathbb E\left[\psi(X_1)\right] =\mathbb E\left[\psi(X_2)\right]\,.
\]
\item[(Pathwise)] We say that pathwise $($or strong$)$ uniqueness holds for (equation SDE of the paper) with initial data in $H_0$
if for every $x\in H_0$ and for every pair $(X_1,W)$ and $(X_2,W)$ of weak mild solutions to (equation SDE of the paper)
with the same $H$-cylindrical process $W$ defined on the same probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\{\mathcal F_t\}_{t\geq0},\mathbb P)$ with $X_1(0)=X_2(0)=x$, it holds that
\[
\mathbb{P}\left(X_1(t)=X_2(t), \;\;\forall\,t\geq0 \right)=1\,.
\]
\end{itemize}
title: Defn uniqueness of arXiv:2512.17736

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2606.21591, '\textbf{Equal probabilities maximize the expected deficit\\ in the siblings of the coupon '] Fix $N\ge 2$ and an integer $j\ge 2$. For every $\mathbf{p}\in\mathcal{P}_N$ with $\mathbf{p}\ne\mathbf{u}$,
write $\mathbf{q}(\theta)=\mathbf{u}+\theta(\mathbf{p}-\mathbf{u})$, $\theta\in[0,1]$, for the segment from
$\mathbf{u}$ to $\mathbf{p}$. Then
\[
\frac{d}{d\theta}\,\mathbb{E}[U_j^N]\bigl(\mathbf{q}(\theta)\bigr)<0
\qquad\text{for every }\theta\in(0,1].
\]
In particular $\mathbb{E}[U_j^N]$ is strictly decreasing along this segment, so
\[
\mathbb{E}[U_j^N](\mathbf{p})<\mathbb{E}[U_j^N](\mathbf{u})\qquad\text{for all }\mathbf{p}\in\mathcal{P}_N\setminus\{\mathbf{u}\},
\]
and the uniform vector is the unique maximizer of $\mathbb{E}[U_j^N]$ on $\mathcal{P}_N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 45 (Evaluation bounds on the intersection branch) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] For every $m\ge1$ there are constants $C_m,A_m<\infty$, depending only on
$m$, such that for $1\le p<\infty$ and $2\le r<\infty$,
\begin{align}

 \|\cT_K^{(m)}\|_{L^p(\Omega;\Sch_r)}
 &\le C_m(p+r)^{m/2}\Prof_{m,r}(K),\\

 \|I_m(K)\|_{L^p(\Omega;\Sch_r)}
 &\le A_m(p+r)^{m/2}\|K\|_{\mathfrak W_{m,r}}.
\end{align}
One may take $C_m\le C_0^m$ and $A_m=m^{m/2}C_m$.
The first assertion is Theorem~\ref{thm:m-finite} together with the completed
map of Proposition~\ref{prop:completed-decoupled-chaos-map}; the second is
Proposition~\ref{prop:wick-completion}.  The range $1\le p<2$ follows from
$p=2$ and monotonicity of probability norms.  Since $r\ge2$,
$r+2\le\frac43(r+p)$ in this range, so the displayed $(p+r)^{m/2}$ form is
retained after enlarging the absolute exponential base $C_0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Evaluation bounds on the intersection branch

[Thm lever of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let $(M,J)$ be a compact complex surface of general  type, and let $(X, \check{J})$ be its minimal model. 
 Then any Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ satisfies the   curvature estimate 
 $$
\frac{1}{4\pi^2} \int_M \left( \frac{s^2}{24} + 2 |W_+|^2 \right)d\mu_g \geq  \frac{2}{3} c_1^2(X),
 $$
and  the inequality is strict if $M$ satisfies the Hitchin-Thorpe inequality (equation htineq of the paper).

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] Let X and Y be Polish subspaces of $\R$. Let $f \in \Fc^{|\cdot|}(X)$ and $g \in \Fc^{|\cdot|}(Y )$, $C : X \times \Pc_g(Y ) \to R$ be measurable, continuous and convex in the second argument and such that there exists a constant $K > 0$ which satisfies for all $(x, p) \in X \times \Pc_g (Y )$,
$$
|C(x,p)| \leq K \left( f(x) + \int_{\R} g(y) p(dy)  \right).
$$
then
\be* 
\lim_{k\to\infty} P(\mu^k,\nu^k)=P(\mu,\nu). 
\ee* 
For $k \in \N$, let $\mu_k \in \Pc_f(X)$ and $\nu_k \in \Pc_g(Y)$ such that $\mu_k \leq_{cd} \nu_k$. Suppose $\mu_k$ converge in $\Pc_f(X)$ and strongly to $\mu$,  and $\nu_k$ converge  in $\Pc_g(X)$ as $k \to + \infty$ to $\nu$. Then

\be* 
\lim_{k\to\infty} P(\mu^k,\nu^k)=P(\mu,\nu). 
\ee* (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2603.27940

[Theorem thm:asymptotic-plateau of arXiv:2608.30700, 'Convex hulls and area minimizing currents in asymptotically locally hyperbolic manifolds'] Let $(M^{n+1}, g)$ be $C^3$ conformally compact asymptotically locally hyperbolic, and let $2 \leq p \leq n$. Suppose that $A\in\mathbf{I}_{p-1}(\partial M)$ is a nonzero integral cycle and that $\partial Q=A$ for some $Q\in\mathbf{I}_p(\overline{M})$. Then there exists $\overline{T} \in \mathbf{I}_p(\overline{M})$ such that $\partial \overline{T}=A$ and $\overline{T}$ has no mass on $\partial M$.
    If $T := \overline{T} \mathbin{\vrule height 1.6ex depth 0pt width 0.13ex\vrule height 0.13ex depth 0pt width 1.1ex} M$, then
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
        \item $\partial T = 0$,
        \item $T$ is locally absolutely area minimizing in $(M,g)$,
        \item $\partial_\infty \spt T = \spt A$ and $T \neq 0$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:asymptotic-plateau of arXiv:2608.30700

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); T385-w737-C05 v1; no independent PASS. Let n tend to infinity, let X and W be n by n and a be in R^n. The entries of X are iid N(0,1/n); the entries of W and a are iid N(0,1), jointly independent and independent of X. For the bias-free scalar network f(x)=n^(-1/2) sum_j a_j ReLU(w_j dot x), include both W and a in the empirical NTK. Write H=ReLU(XW), G_ij=1{(XW)_ij>0}, D=(XX^T) elementwise-multiplied by (G diag(a_j^2)G^T/n), and K=HH^T/n+D. Set mu_i=||x_i||/sqrt(2pi), H0=H-mu 1_n^T, v=H0 1_n/n, B=H0 H0^T/n+D, and U=[mu,v]. Let alpha_plus be the positive eigenvalue of U[[1,1],[1,0]]U^T. Define lambda_iso>lambda_max(B) by alpha_plus Tr((lambda_iso I-B)^(-1))/n=1; the positive-eigenvalue and root events hold with probability tending to one, and arbitrary extensions off them do not affect the limit. The recorded unaudited derivation asserts lambda_1(K)-lambda_iso converges in probability to 3/(4pi). This is an asymptotic prediction of order-one underestimation by a trace-resolvent surrogate, not an exact finite-n identity or an assumption of isotropy near the bulk. No bounded-edge outlier theorem is claimed. No general ReLU bulk law or deeper-network result follows. No novelty claim is made, and independent review is pending.

[Lem 9 of arXiv:2605.20115, 'Moment bounds on correctors for the degenerate random conductance model'] Let  $a$ satisfy \eqref{eq.mombd-a} for some $\gamma\ge d+1$.
There exist a vector field $\phi=\{\phi_i\}_{1\le i \le d}$ and a tensor field $\sigma=\{\sigma_{ijk}\}_{1\le i,j,k\le d}$ with the following properties. For each $1\le i,j,k\le d$, $\phi_i$ solves \eqref{eq.corrector} and $\sigma_{ijk}$ solves \eqref{eq.flux}. The gradient fields are stationary (that is, their laws are invariant under translations), have some finite moments, and have zero mean: $\expec{\nabla \phi_i}=\expec{\nabla \sigma_{ijk}}=0$, and 

\[
\sum_{i=1}^d \expecb{a |\nabla \phi_i|^2}^\frac12+\sum_{i=1}^d \expecb{|\nabla \phi_i|^\frac{2\gamma}{\gamma+1}}^\frac{\gamma+1}{2\gamma} + \sum_{i,j,k=1}^d \expecb{|\nabla \sigma_{ijk}|^\frac{2\gamma}{\gamma+1}}^\frac{\gamma+1}{2\gamma} \,\lesssim \, \Gamma.
\]

Moreover, the correctors grow sub-linearly at infinity:
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n\to+\infty} \frac1n \fint_{B_{n}} |(\phi_i,\sigma_{ijk})|=0,
\end{equation} 
where $\fint_{B_{n}}$ denotes the average on the ball $B_n$ of size $n$ (see notation for details). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 9 of arXiv:2605.20115

[Prop eigen of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] For $0\le i\le b_{\max}$,

\[
H^0\bigl(C,\Omega^1(-iS)\bigr)=\bigoplus_{b'\ge i}V_{b'}.
\]

In particular, for $b_{\max}\ge 1$, $V_{b_{\max}}$ and $V_{b_{\max}-1}\oplus V_{b_{\max}}$ are the Riemann--Roch spaces of the divisors $K-b_{\max}S$ and $K-(b_{\max}-1)S$, over any field over which $S$ is rational.

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^n$ be bounded, open and connected, $T>0$, and let $u\in C^2_1(U_T)\cap C(\overline{U_T})$ satisfy $u_t-\Delta u=0$ in $U_T$. If there is a point $(x_0,t_0)\in U_T$ (so $x_0\in U$, $0<t_0\le T$) with $u(x_0,t_0)=\max_{\overline{U_T}}u$, then $u$ is constant on $\overline{U_{t_0}}=\overline U\times[0,t_0]$. Nothing is asserted for $t>t_0$. The same conclusion (constancy on $U\times(0,t_0]$) holds for subsolutions $u_t+Lu\le0$ of a uniformly parabolic nondivergence operator with $c\equiv0$ and continuous bounded coefficients (Nirenberg), and for $c\ge0$ provided the maximum is nonnegative. The minimum version follows by applying the theorem to $-u$.

[Defn def:VSSM of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] The hard-core model on a family $\mathcal{G}$ of bounded degree graphs satisfies
    \emph{very strong spatial mixing (VSSM)} at a parameter $\lambda>0$ if there
    exist constants $\alpha\in[0,1)$ and $C>0$ such that for all $G=(V,E)\in\mathcal{G}$, any induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ and $v\in V(H)$, and for all boundary conditions $\sigma,\tau:S_{T_{\mathrm{SAW}(H,v)}}(v,\ell)\to\{0,1\}$ we have
    \begin{equation}
        \abs{R_{(T_{\mathrm{SAW}(H,v)},\sigma,v}(\lambda)-R_{(T_{\mathrm{SAW}(H,v)},\tau,v}(\lambda)}\le C\cdot \alpha^{\ell}\quad \text{for all }\ell\in \mathbb{N}.
        
    \end{equation}
    
    We refer to $\alpha$ as the \emph{rate of VSSM}.

body: In number theory, Dirichlet's theorem, also called the Dirichlet prime number theorem, states that for any two positive coprime integers a and d, there are infinitely many primes of the form a + nd, where n is also a positive integer. In other words, there are infinitely many primes that are congruent to a modulo d. The numbers of the form a + nd form an arithmetic progression

[Proposition prop-Poisson point process stationary-2 of arXiv:2505.24043, 'Weak solutions of Navier-Stokes Equation with purely discontinuous L\'evy Noise'] Suppose that $(X, \mathscr{B}_X) $ is a non-empty measure space  and
$\bigl( {\Omega}, {\mathscr{F}}, {\mathbb{P}}  \bigr)$ is a probability space. If
$n$ is a non-negative measure  on $(X, \mathscr{B}_X)$ then a  point process $p: \Omega \to \Pi_X$  is a  stationary Poisson point process with the characteristic measure $n$ iff
for all $t>s \geq 0$, every $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$  and all pair-wise disjoint sets $U_1, \ldots,U_\ell \in \mathscr{B}_X$ the following identity holds
\begin{align}

\mathbb{E} \Bigl[ e^{-\sum_{j=1}^\ell \lambda_j \eta_p((s,t] \timesU_j) }\Big\vert \tilde{\mathscr{F}}_s \Bigr]
&=e^{(t-s)\sum_{j=1}^\ell (e^{-\lambda_j t}-1)n(U_j)}
\end{align}
where $\tilde{\mathscr{F}}_s$ is the $\sigma$-field generated by the following family  of random variables
\[
\eta_p((0,r]\timesU): \;\; r\in (0,s], \;\; u \in \mathscr{B}_X.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop-Poisson point process stationary-2 of arXiv:2505.24043

[Thm 6 of arXiv:2511.02763, 'The Cayley-Moser problem with Poissonian arrival of offers'] The cumulative density of the sale price $S_t$ is given by
	\begin{align}G_t(x)&=
		\phi(\mu(t))\left[ \frac{F_0(x)}{\phi(\mu_0)}+\int_{\mu_0}^{\mu(t)} \frac{[F(x)-F(w)]_+}{\phi(w)^2} dw\right]\\
		&=\phi(\mu(t)) \frac{F_0(x)}{\phi(\mu_0)}+\phi(\mu(t))\cdot 
		\begin{cases}
			0 &  x<\mu_0\\
			\frac{1}{\phi(x)}-\frac{1}{\phi(\mu_0)}+\phi'(x)\int_{\mu_0}^{x}\frac{dw}{\phi(w)^2}    & \mu_0\leq x<\mu(t)\\
			\frac{1}{\phi(\mu(t))}-\frac{1}{\phi(\mu_0)}+\phi'(x)\int_{\mu_0}^{\mu(t)}\frac{dw}{\phi(w)^2}	& x\geq \mu(t)
		\end{cases}.\nonumber
	\end{align}
	In case $F$,$F_0$ are absolutely continuous with densities $f,f_0$, the probability density function $g_t(x)$  of $S_t$ is given by
	\begin{equation}g_t(x)
		=\phi(\mu(t)) \frac{f_0(x)}{\phi(\mu_0)}+\phi(\mu(t)) f(x)\cdot \begin{cases}
			0 & x<\mu_0\\
			\int_{\mu_0}^{x}\frac{dw}{\phi(w)^2}  & \mu_0\leq x<\mu(t)\\
			\int_{\mu_0}^{\mu(t)}\frac{dw}{\phi(w)^2}	& x>\mu(t)
		\end{cases}
		.\end{equation}

Let $U$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{R}^M$ with $\dim U \le d$, and let $r(U)$ be the number of open coordinate orthants of $\mathbb{R}^M$ that $U$ meets. Then $r(U) \le 2\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\binom{M-1}{j}$. If $U$ lies inside a coordinate hyperplane then $r(U)=0$. If $\dim U = d$ and the $M$ coordinate functionals restricted to $U$ are in general position, meaning every $d$ or fewer of them are linearly independent, then equality holds. Equivalently, $M$ points in general position in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admit exactly $2\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\binom{M-1}{j}$ homogeneously linearly separable dichotomies.

[Lemma lem:finite-energy-potential of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Let $\nu,\eta\in\mathcal M_{\rm fe}(D)$.  Then $I_D(|\nu|,|\eta|)<\infty$, so the mutual Green
energy $I_D(\nu,\eta)$ is well defined.  For each
$\sigma\in\{\nu,\eta\}$ there is a unique $U_D\sigma\inH$ characterized by
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E(U_D\sigma,v)=\int_D\widetilde v\,d\sigma,
 \qquad v\inH.
 
\end{equation}
Its quasi-continuous representative is
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde{U_D\sigma}(z)
 =\int_DG_D(z,w)\,\sigma(dw)
 \qquad\text{for $\mathcal E$-q.e. }z\in D,
 
\end{equation}
where the signed integral is taken through the Jordan decomposition.  In
addition,
\begin{align}
 I_D(\nu,\eta)
 &=\mathcal E(U_D\nu,U_D\eta),
 \\
 |I_D(\nu,\eta)|
 &\le I_D(\nu)^{1/2}I_D(\eta)^{1/2},
 \\
 \|U_D\nu\|_{H}^2
 &=I_D(\nu),
 \qquad
 \langleU_D\nu,f\rangle_{H}=\int_D\widetilde f\,d\nu,
 \quad f\inH.
 
\end{align}

body:
Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be a probability space, $T: X \to X$ measure-preserving (not necessarily invertible), $A \in \mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$, and $n_A(x) = \min\{n \ge 1 : T^n x \in A\}$ the first return time (finite for a.e. $x \in A$ by Poincare recurrence; set $n_A = \infty$ where no return occurs). Then, in general,
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = \mu\Big(\bigcup_{j \ge 0} T^{-j} A\Big),$$
the measure of the set of points whose forward orbit ever meets $A$. In particular $\int_A n_A\,d\mu \le 1$ always, so $n_A$ is integrable over $A$ for EVERY positive-measure set in a probability-preserving system, ergodic or not. If $T$ is ERGODIC, the union has full measure and
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = 1, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \frac{1}{\mu(A)} \int_A n_A\,d\mu = \frac{1}{\mu(A)}:$$
the mean return time to $A$, with respect to the normalised measure $\mu_A = \mu(\cdot \cap A)/\mu(A)$, is exactly $1/\mu(A)$. Equivalently, the induced (first-return) map $T_A = T^{n_A}$ on $A$ preserves $\mu_A$ and $(X, \mu, T)$ is recovered from $(A, \mu_A, T_A, n_A)$ as a tower of total mass $\int_A n_A\,d\mu / \mu(A)$.

WHERE IT FAILS. (1) Without ergodicity the mean return time can be strictly less than $1/\mu(A)$: if $A$ is itself invariant then $n_A = 1$ on $A$ and $\int_A n_A = \mu(A) < 1$. (2) In an infinite measure space $\int_A n_A\,d\mu$ can be infinite even for a conservative ergodic $T$ (in fact for an ergodic conservative infinite-measure system it is always infinite for sets of finite positive measure), so 'mean return time $= 1/\mu(A)$' is a finite-measure statement. (3) The lemma controls only the MEAN of $n_A$: no bound on its variance or tail follows; $n_A$ need not be in $L^2$.
mu is a probability measure
T is measure-preserving, not necessarily invertible
mu(A) > 0
the value 1/mu(A) for the mean return time requires ergodicity; the general identity does not

Let (X_i,Y_i) be independent paired standard Gaussians of correlation c, fresh conditional on that past. Set Qnew=n^-1 sum_i tanh(sqrt(q)X_i)^2 and Rnew=n^-1 sum_i tanh(sqrt(r)Y_i)^2. Put e=q-r, T=qr(1-c), B=e^2+8T, and a=1-(q+r)/12. Then E[(Qnew-Rnew)^4|past] <= a^4 e^4 + 18 e^2 B/n + 1079 B^2/n^2. In particular when q=r this is at most 69056 q^4(1-c)^2/n^2. This is a one-step positive-moment component, not a closed depth-uniform rate. No Lean certificate is claimed.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:28b4c01225d9f3a0088abfcf3c78cc7985fc07a288be546c3cbb777bf706c180","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/28/28b4c01225d9f3a0088abfcf3c78cc7985fc07a288be546c3cbb777bf706c180.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:5cbd0d9aa0cd90471687623e7786a4fc06a651f1fd9b152e8f2edc2d6b230a1d","bundle_entry_key":"tanh_contrast_fourth_moment","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c013-contrast-fourth-moment","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Quantitative Gaussian-process limits and paired empirical norm fluctuations","draft":"w712/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:critical-tanh-paired-norm-contrast-conditional-fourth-moment","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C013 v1: conditional fourth moment of radial contrast

Kind: moved. Target: 1, positive joint moments for the two-input tanh chain.
Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unverified. This is a one-step component,
not a closed multi-layer rate.

Fix q,r in [0,1], c in [-1,1], and an integer n>=1. Given the completed
network past, let (X_i,Y_i) be independent standard Gaussian pairs of
correlation c. Let Q'=mean tanh(sqrt(q)X_i)^2 and
R'=mean tanh(sqrt(r)Y_i)^2. Set

    e=q-r, T=qr(1-c), B=e^2+8T, a=1-(q+r)/12.

All quantities on the right are fixed by the past. Then

    E[(Q'-R')^4 | past]
      <= a^4 e^4 + (18/n)e^2 B + (1079/n^2)B^2.      (1)

In particular at a state q=r,

    E[(Q'-R')^4 | past] <=69056 q^4(1-c)^2/n^2.       (2)

## Proof

1. Put A=sqrt(q)X, C=sqrt(r)Y and Z=tanh(A)^2-tanh(C)^2.
The function f(t)=tanh(sqrt(t))^2 is 1-Lipschitz on [0,infinity):
f'(t)=[tanh(sqrt(t))/sqrt(t)]sech(sqrt(t))^2 lies in [0,1], with
continuous derivative 1 at zero. Thus |Z|<=|A^2-C^2|.
Gaussian fourth moments give

    E[(A^2-C^2)^2]=3e^2+4qr(1-c^2)<=3e^2+8T<=3B.

For P=A-C and M=A+C, Holder gives

    E[(A^2-C^2)^4]=E[P^4 M^4]
      <=sqrt(E P^8 E M^8)
      =105 (Var(P)Var(M))^2
      =105[e^2+4qr(1-c^2)]^2 <=105B^2.

No independence of P and M is used. E G^8=105 for a standard Gaussian;
successive integration by parts gives E G^(2k)=(2k-1)E G^(2k-2), with
Gaussian polynomial boundary terms zero. A Gaussian of zero variance is
identically zero, so the calculation includes degenerate c=+/-1 and q=0.

2. Let m=E Z=F(q)-F(r), where F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)G)^2.
Audited C002 v2 gives increasing concave F, F(0)=0 and F(t)<=t-t^2/6
on [0,1]. Its derivative exists, by domination with G^2, and satisfies
0<=F'(t)<=F(t)/t<=1-t/6 for t>0, with F'(0)=1. Integrating between
q and r in either order gives |m|<=a|e|. Here 5/6<=a<=1, hence also
|m|<=|e|<=sqrt(B).

For W=Z-m, let sigma2=E W^2 and mu_j=E W^j. From step 1,

    sigma2<=3B,
    mu_4<=8(E Z^4+m^4)<=848B^2,
    |mu_3|<=sqrt(sigma2*mu_4)<=51B^(3/2).

The last coefficient is valid because 3*848=2544<=51^2. The centering
inequality uses |x-y|^4<=8(|x|^4+|y|^4), and m^4<=e^4<=B^2.

3. Let eta=n^(-1)sum_i W_i. Conditional on the past, the W_i are
independent and centered. Expanding the finite sums shows exactly

    E eta=0, E eta^2=sigma2/n, E eta^3=mu_3/n^2,
    E eta^4=mu_4/n^3+3(n-1)sigma2^2/n^3.

In the fourth expansion only index patterns with four equal indices or
two pairs survive: respectively n and 3n(n-1) ordered terms, before
division by n^4. In the third expansion only n all-equal terms survive.
These formulas hold for n=1; the two-pair term is then zero.
Consequently

    E eta^2<=3B/n,
    |E eta^3|<=51B^(3/2)/n^2,
    E eta^4<=848B^2/n^3+27B^2/n^2<=875B^2/n^2.

4. Since Q'-R'=m+eta, expand the fourth power and use E eta=0:

    E[(Q'-R')^4]
      =m^4+6m^2 E eta^2+4m E eta^3+E eta^4
      <=a^4e^4+18e^2B/n+(204+875)B^2/n^2.

For the cubic cross term use |m|<=sqrt(B); its sign is not presumed.
This proves (1). When e=0, B=8q^2(1-c), so 1079*64=69056 proves (2).
No fourth moments at distinct layers are multiplied or declared independent.

## Boundary, hypothesis and scope checks

- At q=r and c=1, B=0, and the two output vectors coincide exactly.
- At q=r and c=-1 they are exact negatives before squaring, so contrast
  is again zero; (2) is a valid, deliberately non-sharp upper bound.
- At q=0 or r=0, T=0. The proof and bounds remain defined without any
  division by variance or angular gap. n=1 is covered by the exact formulas.
- Fresh independent rows are load-bearing for the n^-2 source. If all rows
  were duplicates, the sample mean would be a single row at every n and the
  asserted n^-2 decay at q=r, -1<c<1 would fail. That single-row contrast has
  positive fourth moment because the nondegenerate Gaussian pair gives
  unequal squared tanh values with positive probability.
- Gaussianity is used for the exact fourth/eighth moments; within-row
  independence is not assumed. q,r<=1 is used for the scalar secant bound.
- Self-check: CLEAN for the displayed finite expansions and analytic bounds;
  this author check is not independent review. No Lean certificate is claimed.

For any fixed initial deterministic gap Dbar_0>0, divide (1) by Dbar_0^2
and take expectations. The remaining mixed quantities include
E[e_l^2 Q_l R_l(1-c_l)] and E[Q_l^2 R_l^2(1-c_l)^2]. C012 allows that
fixed denominator to replace the deterministic gap at depth l. This lemma
supplies a correctly scaled fourth-moment source but does not bound those
mixed quantities, close the moment hierarchy, or solve Target 1.

needed as a premise. [Lemma lem.balanced_approx_optimal of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] For each $\delta \in (0,1)$ and each positive integer $K$ 
    there is a constant $V_{\delta, K}$ such that the following holds.

    
    Let $1 \ge \alpha_1 \ge \dots \ge \alpha_m \ge \frac 1 K > \alpha_{m+1} \ge \dots \ge \alpha_n > 0$.
    
    Assume that 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_m)$ is strongly balanced;
        \item if $\frac 1 K \le \alpha_i \le \frac 1 2$ then $\alpha_i = \frac {j_i} {K^2}$, where $j_i$ is an integer;
        \item if $\alpha_i < \frac 1 K$ (i.e., $i \ge m+1$) then $\alpha_i^{-1}$ is an odd integer, so $(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n)$ is balanced.
    \end{itemize}
    
    
    For $\alpha \in (0,1]$, denote by $Y_\alpha$ a random variable distributed according to $\nu_\alpha$. If
    \[
        V:=\sum_i {\mathrm{Var}}\, Y_{\alpha_i} > V_{\delta, K}
    \]
    then
    \[
        t(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n) \le (1+\delta) {t_{SE}^{bal}}(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n).
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem.balanced_approx_optimal of arXiv:2603.11043

body: [Definition 2.1 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] Given $0< t \le T$, we say that the process $X^\varepsilon$ does not jump from $0$ to $1$ during the time interval $(0,t)$ if and only if for any $r \in (0,t)$, we have $0 \le X_r^\varepsilon \le y_*^\varepsilon$, i.e. $e_1^\varepsilon \ge t$. This is equivalent to saying that for all $i\ge 1$ such that $\tau_i^\varepsilon \in (0,t)$, the condition $0<\tau^{\varepsilon}_{i+1} -\tau_i^\varepsilon<T_*^\varepsilon$ holds.

body:
[Defn anc of arXiv:2601.09537, 'Gene genealogies in haploid populations evolving according to sweepstakes reproduction'] A (genomic) ancestral process $\pi_{\ensuremath{\mathds h} } \equiv \{\pi_{\ensuremath{\mathds h} }(t); t \ge 0\}$ for some fixed ${\ensuremath{\mathds h} } \in \mathds N$ is a
continuous-time Markov chain with values in the set of partitions of
$\mathds N^{\ensuremath{\mathds h} }$, and where homologous leaves $i$ and $j$ are in the same block
at time $t \ge 0$ if and only if they share a common ancestor at time
$t \ge 0$ measured from the present (time of sampling). The only
possible transitions are mergers of homologous blocks in the current
partition.  Denote by $\pi_{{\ensuremath{\mathds h} },n} \equiv \{\pi_n(t); t \ge 0\}$ the
restriction of $\pi$ to $[n]^{\ensuremath{\mathds h} }$.
title: Defn anc of arXiv:2601.09537

body: For a memoryless information source that emits symbols independently from a fixed probability distribution of Shannon entropy H bits per symbol, Shannon's source coding theorem states that blocks of n such symbols can be losslessly compressed by a uniquely decodable code into approximately n*H bits, with probability of decoding error vanishing as n grows, and that no code can compress the source below n*H bits per n symbols on average without an error rate bounded away from zero. Entropy H is thus the fundamental limit of lossless data compression. Proved by Claude Shannon in his 1948 paper founding information theory.
title: Shannon's source coding theorem

[Lemma lem:mon of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Take any $X, H, G, R, L, H', G', R', L' \in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$, with $X+H+G$ and $X+H'+G'$ even, and $H\le H'$, $G\le G'$, $R\le R'$, $L\le L'$.
Sample $\mathfrak{f}:\llbracket 0, X\rrbracket \to \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ uniformly from $\overline\mathscr F(X;H,G)$, conditional on $R\le \min \mathfrak{f}\le \max \mathfrak{f}\le L$; and $\mathfrak{f}':\llbracket 0, X\rrbracket \to \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ uniformly from $\overline\mathscr F(X;H',G;)$, conditional on $R'\le\min \mathfrak{f}'\le \max \mathfrak{f}'\le L'$.
Then we can couple $\mathfrak{f}$ and $\mathfrak{f}'$ in such a way that $\mathfrak{f}(t)\le \mathfrak{f}'(t)$ for all $t\in\llbracket 0, X\rrbracket$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:mon of arXiv:2411.10829

[Lemma l.transformed_coefficients of arXiv:2608.31071, 'Global smooth solutions to the inhomogeneous Landau--Fermi--Dirac equation'] Consider any coefficients $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal B$, and $\mathcal C$ on $[0,T] \times \Omega \times \mathbb R^3$ satisfying~(equation defn:coercivity_assumption of the paper)-(equation defn:bounded_coefficient_assumption of the paper), and fix any $z_0 = (t_0,x_0,v_0) \in (0,T]\times B_1\times \mathbb R^3$. Then, $\overline \mathcal A$, $\overline \mathcal B$, and $\overline \mathcal C$, defined by~(equation eq:new_coefficients of the paper), satisfy~(equation eq:uniform_ellipticity of the paper) in $Q_2$ and, for any $m\geq 0$ and $z\in Q_2$,
    \begin{equation}
        |g_{z_0}(z)|
        \lesssim \left\langle v_0 \right\rangle^{-m} \|g\|_{L^\infty_m}.
    \end{equation}.
title: Lemma l.transformed_coefficients of arXiv:2608.31071

	and $g : I\times \R^d \to \R\in G^l(\R^d)$. Define
	\[v^{i,s}_t(x) := \E g^i(X^{i,s}_t(x)).\]
	Then $v\in G^l(\R^d)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Cor CPRE-2 of arXiv:2507.00329, 'Oriented bond-site percolation in random environment and contact processes with periodic r'] Let $\varDelta>0$ be a random variable, with $\mathbb{E}[\varDelta^{1+\varepsilon}]<\infty$ for some $\varepsilon>0$. Let $(\varDelta_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$ be an i.i.d.\ family of random variables distributed according to $\mathcal{L}(\varDelta)$. Consider the generalised contact process on $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$ with $\mathbb{X}\sim\mathrm{PPP}(\lambda)$ and independent recovery times  $(\mathbb{Y}_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$, where $\mathbb{Y}_x\sim\mathrm{PPP}(\varDelta_x)$. Then, the generalised contact process has a positive probability of survival for every sufficiently large $\lambda$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Contact process in (spatial) random environment II

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a sequence of Wigner random matrices
$$Z_N\in M_N(L^\infty(X))$$
having independent $G_t$ variables as entries, with $t>0$, up to $Z_N=Z_N^*$, we have
$$M_k\left(\frac{Z_N}{\sqrt{N}}\right)\simeq t^{k/2}|NC_2(k)|$$
for any integer $k\in\mathbb N$, in the $N\to\infty$ limit.

[Theorem thm-homeomorphism of arXiv:2512.17727, 'Stochastic transport equation with L\'evy noise'] Under  the assumptions of Theorem (d32 of the paper),  there exists an $\mathbb{P}$-full event $\bar{\Omega}^\prime$ such that,
for each $\omega \in \bar{\Omega}^\prime$,  $s,  t\ge 0$,
the mapping: \[\mathbb R^d \ni  x \mapsto \phi_{s,t}(x)(\omega) \in \mathbb R^d\] is a
surjective homeomorphism.

Moreover, on  $\bar{\Omega}^\prime$,  for every $y \in \mathbb R^d$,  we have
\begin{equation} 
\phi_{s,t}^{-1}(y) =  y - \int_s^t b(\phi_{r,t}^{-1}(y)) dr - (L_t - L_s), \;\;  0\le s \le t,
\end{equation}
and
$$
\phi_{s,t}^{-1}(y) =  y, \;\;  0\le t \le s.
$$
Finally, for every $x \in \mathbb R^d,$ $t \in [0,\infty)$, the mapping: $s  \mapsto \phi_{s,t}^{-1}(x)$  is c\`adl\`ag on $[0,\infty)$ and,
 for every $s \in [0,\infty)$, the mapping: $t   \mapsto \phi_{s,t}^{-1}(x)$  is c\`adl\`ag on $[0,\infty)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm-homeomorphism of arXiv:2512.17727

body: [Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.24611, 'Beyond Fixed Points: Superpolynomial Capacity of Asymmetric Hopfield Networks'] Let $m\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}$ be sufficiently large. Fix a sufficiently large constant $K$, set $d=\lceil K(\log m)^{2}\rceil$. Let $n$ denote the number of neurons in $\mathrm{BCA}\left(d,m\right)$. Then there exist constants $c_{1},c_{2}>0$ such that, with probability $1-o(1)$, $\mathrm{BCA}\left(d,m\right)$ contains a family $\mathcal{A}$ of limit-cycle attractors satisfying the following: 1. (Number of limit cycles) Writing $N_{\mathrm{cycles}}:=|\mathcal{A}|$, we have $N_{\mathrm{cycles}}\geq\exp\!\Big(c_{1}\frac{n}{(\log n)^{2}}\Big).$ (2) 2. (Periods of the constructed attractors) Every attractor $\mathcal{C}\in\mathcal{A}$ has period at least $\exp\!\Big(c_{2}\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\log n}\Big).$ (3) 3. (Noise robustness) For $n$ large enough, fix any $\mathcal{C}\in\mathcal{A}$ and any state $x\in\mathcal{C}$. If each neuron of $x$ is independently flipped with probability $p_{n}$ at time $t=0$, where $p_{n}\leq\frac{1}{2}-\sqrt{\nicefrac{{\log n}}{{d}}}$, then with probability $1-o(1)$ the perturbed trajectory returns to $\mathcal{C}$.

body: [Lemma lem:df-dirspace of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $(X,d,\mu,\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ be an MMD space. Let $\mathcal{F}_2=\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{E}_2: \mathcal{F}_2 \to [0,\infty)$ be defined by $\mathcal{E}_2(f):= \mathcal{E}(f,f)$ for all $f \in \mathcal{F}_2$. Let $\Gamma_2: \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{M}(X)$ denote the energy measure $\Gamma_2(f):=\Gamma(f,f)$ as given in Definition (d:EnergyMeas of the paper). Then  $(X,d,\mu,\mathcal{E}_2, \mathcal{F}_2, \Gamma_2)$ is a regular, local $2$-Dirichlet space in the sense of Definition (d:dir-space of the paper).
title: Lemma lem:df-dirspace of arXiv:2510.13659

[Definition 11 of arXiv:2604.09933, 'Explicit cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles'] For \(0\le u\le n\), define
\[
A_u:=\supp(\widetilde Q_{n-u,p})=\supp(B_{n-u})\subseteq G_{n,p}.
\]
Equivalently, for \(1\le u\le n\) and \(x=(s,\sigma)\in G_{n,p}\),
\begin{equation}
x\in A_u
\iff
\sigma^{-1}(n-u+1)<\cdots<\sigma^{-1}(n)
\ \text{and}\
s_{\sigma^{-1}(n-u+1)}=\cdots=s_{\sigma^{-1}(n)}=0.
\end{equation}
Also,
\[
A_0=\supp(B_n)=G_{n,p},
\qquad
A_{u+1}\subseteq A_u,
\qquad
|A_u|=|B_{n-u}|=\binom{n}{u}p^{\,n-u}(n-u)!.
\]
title: Definition 11 of arXiv:2604.09933

body:
[Defn 5 of arXiv:2512.02538, 'On the spectral geometry of Liouville quantum gravity'] For a Borel nonnegative function $f:\Sigma\to \R$ we define 
$$
\mathbf{G} f(x) = \mathbf{E}_x [ \int_0^{\mathbf{T}_\Sigma} f(Z_t)\dd t ] = \int_\Sigma f(y) g_\Sigma(x,y) \mu_\ph (\dd y).
$$
In other words it is the operator associated to the integral kernel $g_\Sigma(x,y)$, but with respect to $\mu_\ph$ rather than the Lebesgue measure $\dd y$.
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2512.02538

body:
[Lemma lem:KPZ_preserve_lim of arXiv:2505.09604, 'Exceptional force, uncountably many solutions in the KPZ fixed point'] [Busa-Sepp-Sore-22a] 
The following holds simultaneously for all initial data and all $t > s$ on the event of probability one from Lemma~(lem:Landscape_global_bound of the paper). Let $\mathfrak h \in \operatorname{UC}$ (the space of upper semi-continuous functions $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$) be initial data for the KPZ fixed point, sampled at time $s$. 
For $t > s$, let 
\[
h_t(y;\mathfrak h) = \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}}\{\mathfrak h(x) + \mathcal{L}(x,s;y,t)\}.
\]
Then, simultaneously for all $t > s$,
\begin{equation} 
\liminf_{x \to +\infty} \frac{h_t(x;\mathfrak h)}{x} \ge \liminf_{x \to + \infty} \frac{\mathfrak h(x)}{x},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \limsup_{x \to - \infty} \frac{h_t(x;\mathfrak h)}{x} \le \limsup_{x \to -\infty} \frac{\mathfrak h(x)}{x}.
\end{equation}

Furthermore, assuming that $\mathfrak h:\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is \textbf{continuous} and satisfies
\begin{equation} 
\liminf_{x \to \pm \infty} \frac{\mathfrak h(x)}{x} > -\infty \qquad\text{and}\qquad \limsup_{x \to \pm \infty} \frac{\mathfrak h(x)}{x} < +\infty,
\end{equation}
then also
\begin{equation} 
\limsup_{x \to + \infty} \frac{h_t(x;\mathfrak h)}{x} \le \limsup_{x \to +\infty} \frac{\mathfrak h(x)}{x},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \liminf_{x \to -\infty} \frac{h_t(x;\mathfrak h)}{x} \ge \liminf_{x \to - \infty} \frac{\mathfrak h(x)}{x}.
\end{equation}

In particular, for \textbf{continuous} initial data $\mathfrak h$ satisfying~(equation liminfsupfinite of the paper), if either \rm{(}or both\rm{)} of the limits
$
\lim_{x \to \pm \infty} \frac{\mathfrak h(x)}{x}
$
exist \rm{(}potentially with different limits on each side\rm{)}, then for $t > s$,
\[
\lim_{x \to \pm \infty} \frac{h_t(x;\mathfrak h)}{x} = \lim_{x \to \pm \infty} \frac{\mathfrak h(x)}{x}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theo thm:weakconvergence of arXiv:2411.19543, 'Feller property and convergence for semigroups of time-changed processes'] For each $n\in\mathbb{N}_\infty$, let $\mathbb{P}^n$ be the probability law on 
the path space $D_{F_{\partial}}[0,\infty)$ of right continuous paths having left-hand limit in $F_{\partial}$ 
with respect to the process $\check{\mathbb{X}}^n$ with initial distribution $\mu_n$. Let $F_n,\,F$ be the fine support of $\mu_n,\,\mu_{\infty}$, respectively.  
Assume that $F_n,\,F$ are closed, $F_n\subset F$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Then $\check{\mathbb{X}}^n$ converges weakly $\check{\mathbb{X}}^\infty$.

[Corollary cor: solution is locally Lipschitz in inputs of arXiv:2609.03589, 'Correlated initialization of deep residual networks'] Assume that Assumption (assmpt: sufficiently nice function of the paper),
    including the optional condition (it: extra assumption of the paper), holds.
    For \(\beta\in (\frac12, 1]\) and \(\alpha \in (\frac12, \beta)\) let
    \[
        \Psi_\alpha \colon 
        \begin{cases}
            C^\beta([0,T], \banachSpace[V]) \times C^\alpha([0,T], \banachSpace[W]) \times \banachSpace[X]
            &\to C^\alpha([0,T], \banachSpace[X])
            \\
            (g,w,a) &\mapsto  \Psi_\alpha(g, w, a)
        \end{cases}
    \]
    be the map that maps the driving signal \(g\), the parameters \(w\) and the initial condition \(a\) to the unique solution \(\Psi_\alpha(g, w, a)\) of the differential equation (equation e:sdeb of the paper).
    Then \(\Psi_\alpha\) is locally Lipschitz continuous, where
    the space \(C^\beta([0,T], \banachSpace[V]) \times C^\alpha([0,T], \banachSpace[W]) \times \banachSpace[X]\)
    is equipped with the norm
    \[
        \norm{(g,w,a)} = \norm{g}_\beta + \norm{w}_\alpha + \abs{a}.
    \]
    Without the optional assumption (it: extra assumption of the paper) local Lipschitz continuity in \(g\) and \(a\) remains. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem.local0 of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] Under the condition of $Q_1 = 0$, the local limit theorem for $\mathbb{P}\left(Q_{n+1} = \lfloor y \sqrt{n} \rfloor\right)$ holds. We have
    \begin{equation}
        \lim_{n \to \infty} \sqrt{n}\mathbb{P}\left(Q_{n+1} = \lfloor y \sqrt{n} \rfloor | Q_1 = 0\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{c\pi}} e^{-\frac{y^2}{4c}}.
    \end{equation}
    Thus, 
    \[
    \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{Q_{n+1}}{\sqrt{n}}|_{Q_1 = 0} \overset{\left(d\right)}{=} |\mathcal{N}\left(0,2c\right)|.
    \]

body: Publication record. A probability measure mu on the real line is freely strongly unimodal if mu ⊞ nu is unimodal for every unimodal probability measure nu. Y. [Definition 16 (Tripartite orientation class) of arXiv:2608.26516, '2608.26516'] For every integer $m\ge2$, set $N_m:=2^{m-1}$ and let $G_m=K_{N_m,N_m,N_m}$ be the complete tripartite graph whose three vertex parts each have cardinality $N_m$. Write $E_m$ for its edge set, so $|E_m|=3N_m^2$ and every vertex has degree $2N_m$.

Let $X_m:=\{0,1\}^{E_m}$ denote the set of all orientations of $G_m$, where the bit indexed by an edge determines which endpoint is its head. For $z\in X_m$ and $e=\{u,v\}\in E_m$, write $\operatorname{head}_z(e)\in\{u,v\}$ for the head of $e$ in the orientation $z$. The vertex sets of the graphs $G_m$ are pairwise disjoint and serve as labels, and the full domain is $\CX^{\mathrm{or}}:=\bigsqcup_{m\ge2}X_m$.

For every edge $e=\{u,v\}\in E_m$, fix one distinguished endpoint $\ell(e)\in\{u,v\}$ and define
\[
    h_e(x)
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \operatorname{head}_x(e),
            & x\in X_m,\\
        \ell(e),
            & x\notin X_m.
    \end{cases}
\]
The \edefn{tripartite orientation class} is $\Hor:=\{h_e:e\in E_m,\ m\ge2\}$.
title: Tripartite orientation class

[Definition 3 (\cite{voiculescu2000lectures,voiculescu_analogues_1999,gao2008}) of arXiv:2606.31528, 'Well-posedness and stationary distribution of free stochastic differential equations'] Let $\{U_t\}_{t\ge0}$ be a family of self-adjoint operators in $\widetilde{\mathscr A}$.
For each $t\ge0$, define von Neumann subalgebras
\begin{equation*}
\mathscr B_{\le t}:=W^*(U_s:0\le s\le t),\qquad
\mathscr B_{\ge t}:=W^*(U_s:s\ge t),\qquad
\mathscr B_{=t}:=W^*(U_t).
\end{equation*}
We say that $\{U_t\}_{t\ge0}$ is a \emph{free Markov process} if, for every $t\ge0$, $\mathscr B_{\le t}$ and $\mathscr B_{\ge t}$ are $\mathscr B_{=t}$-free.

Let B1 and B2 be closed Euclidean balls in R^d centered at zero, with radii 0<R2<R1<infinity, and let Gamma1,Gamma2 be their metric projections. Let beta_t be deterministic, positive and nonincreasing, with sum_t beta_t=infinity and sum_t beta_t^2<infinity. Start theta_0 in B1 and update theta_(t+1)=Gamma1(theta_t+beta_t[Gamma2(w_t)-theta_t]). Suppose there is a deterministic map F:R^d->R^d and a constant kappa<1 with 0<=kappa, ||F(x)-F(y)||<=kappa||x-y|| for all x,y, sup_x ||F(x)||<R2, and ||w_t-F(theta_t)||->0 almost surely. Then w_t and theta_t both converge almost surely to the unique fixed point theta_star of F. This is a conditional target-network theorem: the required tracking property and contraction must be proved for the concrete main-network update; it does not assert them for an arbitrary neural network.
Two concentric closed Euclidean projection balls with strict radius separation
Positive deterministic nonincreasing beta_t, nonsummable and square-summable
theta_0 in the outer ball
Global strict contraction F with image uniformly strictly inside the inner ball
Almost-sure main-network tracking of F(theta_t)

    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 1$, and suppose that $J : V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel satisfying $J(x,y) = \Omega(d_G(x,y)^{-d \alpha})$ with $\alpha \in (0,2)$. 
    
    Let $\beta > \beta_c$.
    
    Then there exist $\nu = \nu(G, J) > 0$ and $A = A(G,J) > 0$ such that for all $r \in \mathbf{N}$
    
    \begin{equation}
    
        \mathbf{P}_{\beta}
        \left(
            \# K_{r}^{\scriptscriptstyle (1)}
            \leq 
            \nu
            \# B(r)
        \right) 
        \leq 
        \exp(
            -
           \beta 
           (\# B(r))^{\min(2 - \alpha,1)}
           /
           A
        ).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Conditional Gaussian surrogate from Cui, Pesce, Dandi, Krzakala, Lu, Zdeborova and Loureiro: take x~N(0,I_d) independent of the weights and spike, a spike vector v with ||v||_2=sqrt(d), bulk variance c>0, and F=W+r*1_p*v^T/sqrt(d), where the rows of W are independent uniform vectors on the sphere of radius sqrt(c). The sRF map is phi(x)=sigma(Fx). Put kappa=v^T*x/sqrt(d). For Z~N(0,c), define mu_0(kappa)=E sigma(Z+r*kappa), mu_1(kappa)=E[Z*sigma(Z+r*kappa)]/c, and mu_2(kappa)=sqrt(E sigma(Z+r*kappa)^2-mu_0(kappa)^2-c*mu_1(kappa)^2). Assuming these second moments exist, define phi_g(x)=mu_0(kappa)*1_p+mu_1(kappa)*W*x+mu_2(kappa)*xi, with xi~N(0,I_p) independent of x,W and fresh for each example. This is Gaussian conditional on kappa and W; its coefficients depend nonlinearly on kappa, so the construction does not replace the spike coordinate by a fully unconditional Gaussian feature vector. Source Result3.2 reports asymptotically equal ridge test errors for these two maps in the proportional-dimensional setting. AppendixB explicitly labels its derivation heuristic; this card records the surrogate construction and source scope, not an independently established equivalence theorem. The trained-network-to-sRF substitution also models a correlated bulk correction by independent spherical rows (source discussion after Result3.1), and the final fixed-point test-error equations of Result3.3 are derived using the non-rigorous replica method. These are distinct steps with distinct qualifications.
Gaussian input; fixed spike norm sqrt(d); positive c and independent spherical bulk rows.
Spike left vector is exactly the all-ones vector; finite Gaussian second moments for the coefficient definitions.
Fresh independent Gaussian surrogate noise per example; conditioning retains the spike coordinate.
The paper uses odd activation in its network setting; no rigorous equivalence theorem is asserted by this concept card.

[Lemma fix_path-new of arXiv:2506.06559, 'Bi-infinite incipient cluster in high dimensions'] Let $G$ be a finite connected simple graph, $S \subset V(G)$, $|S| = 3$. 
 Assume that $G$ is 3-connected to $S$, all $v \in V(G) \setminus S$ have degree $3$, and all elements of 
 $S$ have degree at most $2$.
 \begin{itemize}
 \item[(i)] If $x, y \in V(G) \setminus S$, $\{x,y\} \in E(G)$, then $G$ is H-reducible by $\{x,y\}$, and its
 H-reduction by $\{x,y\}$ is a finite connected graph in which all vertices not in $S$ have degree $3$.
 \item[(ii)] If $\{x,y\}$ is strongly H-reducible, then the H-reduction of $G$ by $\{x,y\}$ is also a 
 simple graph (and 3-connected to $S$).
 \item[(iii)] If $x, y \in V(G) \setminus S$, $x \not= y$, and $\mathcal{P}$ is a simple path in $G$ which 
 does not use $\{x,y\}$ which starts and ends in $V(G)\setminus \{x,y\}$ then there is a simple path 
 $\mathcal{P}'$ in the H-reduction of $G$ by $\{x,y\}$, that has the same start and end points as $\mathcal{P}$
 and coincides with $\mathcal{P}$ on edges that belong to both graphs. 
 \end{itemize}

Let P be a convex polytope with n vertices. The realization space of P, denoted R(P), is the space of all vertex coordinate matrices V in R^{d x n} such that the convex hull conv(V) has face lattice isomorphic to L(P). It is a semialgebraic set defined by polynomial equalities (coplanarities and affine dependencies) and strict polynomial inequalities (orientation / face-separating hyperplanes).
P is a convex polytope
title: Realization Space of a Polytope

body:
[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2607.12666, 'Sample-path Large deviations for \\Scheduled Arrival Processes with Unpunctuality'] The sequence $\{\bar A^{(n)}\}_{n\ge1}$ satisfies a large deviations principle on $D([0,T])$, equipped with the Skorokhod $J_1$ topology, with speed $n$ and good rate function
\[
I_T(\phi)
=
\sup_{m\ge1}\sup_{0<t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T}
I_{t_1,\dots,t_m}\bigl(\phi(t_1),\dots,\phi(t_m)\bigr),
\]
where, for each $0<t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T$,
\[
I_{t_1,\dots,t_m}(x)
=
\sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb R^m}
\left\{
\sum_{\ell=1}^m \alpha_\ell x_\ell-\Lambda_{t_1,\dots,t_m}(\alpha)
\right\}.
\]
Moreover, the rate function admits the variational representation
\begin{equation}
    I_T(\phi) = \sup_{\theta\in C([0,T]),\gamma\in\R} \left\{ \int_0^T \theta(t) \phi(t)\, dt + \gamma\phi(T) - \Lambda_T(\theta,\gamma)\right\},
\end{equation}
with $\Lambda_T(\theta,\gamma)$ given by
\begin{equation}
    \Lambda_T(\theta,\gamma):=\log \E \exp \left(\int_0^T \theta(t)A(t)\, dt + \gamma A(T)\right).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def_elementaty_curve of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow\Sigma$ be a $\mathcal{C}^1$ curve. We say that $\gamma$ is of elementary type if $\gamma([0,1])$ is transverse\footnote{It precisely means that, for every $t\in[0,1]$, $\text{Span}\{\gamma'(t),V(\gamma(t))\}=T_{\gamma(t)}\Sigma$.} to the flow lines of $\varphi_f^t$, $\gamma((0,1))\subset W^u(a_1)$ and if
$$
N(\gamma):=\sharp \gamma(\{0,1\})\cap (\Sigma\setminus W^u(a_1))\leq 1.
$$
Equivalently, $\gamma$ cuts at most once the union $\cup_{ \mathrm{ind} (a)=1}W^u(a)$ of unstable curves and only at endpoints.

An elementary curve is said to be \textbf{positively (resp. negatively) $V$-oriented} if, for every $t\in[0,1]$, $\gamma'(t)\wedge V(\gamma(t))$ has the same (resp. opposite) orientation compared to $\Sigma$. A $V$-oriented elementary curve is said to be \textbf{primitive} if the map
$$
(s,t)\in(0,1)\times\mathbb{R}_+\mapsto\varphi_f^{-t}(\gamma(s))
$$
is injective.
title: Elementary curves

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The axioms for probability theory are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\item A probability space is a measured space $(X,M,\nu)$ of mass one, $\nu(X)=1$.

\item A random variable on $X$ is a real measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb R$.

\item The expectation of $f:X\to\mathbb R$ is its integral, $E(f)=\int_Xf(x)d\nu(x)$.

\item The law of $f$ is the real probability measure $\mu=f_*\nu$, push-forward of $\nu$ by $f$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

\[
C_0

\]
and, for $L\in\mathbb N$, define
\[
h_L(x)
:=
\sum_{i=1}^{L}\ell_i x^i.
\]

Then, for every $x\in\mathcal X_h$, every admissible $(n,s)$, and every
$L\in\mathbb N$,
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\phi_k(x^k)
\mathbb E_{\varepsilon_k}^{n,s}
\left[
h_L\bigl(\Delta_k^{X,\varepsilon_k}(x)\bigr)-h_L(x)
\right]
\leq
C_*\bigl(C_0+h(x)\bigr).
\]
Moreover, on every sublevel set $\{h<m\}$,
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\phi_k(x^k)
\mathbb E_{\varepsilon_k}^{n,s}
\left|
h\bigl(\Delta_k^{X,\varepsilon_k}(x)\bigr)-h(x)
\right|
<\infty,

\end{align}
uniformly in the admissible reinforcement state $(n,s)$.

The same bound holds uniformly with $h$ replaced by $h_L$,
$L\in\mathbb N$.

Also, using normalized random-walk rho, pc<1/rho is not the adjacency-Neumann criterion, and its proposed obstruction pc>=1/rho is impossible when rho<1. On T4 at p=3/4 the squared root-column norm is 1+4p^2 sum_{n>=0}(3p^2)^n and diverges since 3p^2=27/16>1, although tau_p=p^distance decays exponentially. The adjacency norm is 2sqrt(3), normalized rho=sqrt(3)/2 and pc=1/3. This refutes the insufficient operator inference, not the parent conjecture.
Bernoulli bond percolation on T_4
p=3/4 for the exponential-decay counterexample
rho=||A||/4=sqrt(3)/2
pc=1/3
title: Draft refutation of two insufficient spectral routes

[Lem ABregularvarying of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] \
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item If $\hat{\Sigma}$ is regularly varying at $\infty$ with index $1+\beta, \beta\in [0,1]$, that is $\hat\Sigma(x)=x^{1+\beta}\hat{L}(x)$, $x\in [0,\infty)$, then
\[A(z)=\frac{\Phi(z)\hat{W}(z)}{z} \underset{z\rightarrow 0}{\sim}  \frac{1}{\Gamma(1+\beta)} \frac{\Phi(z)}{z^{1-\beta}\hat{L}(1/z)}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(1+\beta)} \frac{\Phi(z)}{z^{2}\Sigma(1/z)}\]
and 
	$$\overline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi,\hat{\Sigma}}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(1+\beta)}\underset{z\rightarrow 0}{\limsup} \frac{\Phi(z)}{z^2\hat\Sigma(1/z)} \text{ and }\underline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi,\hat{\Sigma}}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(1+\beta)}\underset{z\rightarrow 0}{\liminf}\frac{\Phi(z)}{z^2\hat\Sigma(1/z)}.$$
\item If $\hat\Phi$ is regularly varying at $0$ with index $\alpha\in (0,1]$, $\hat\Phi(x)=x^{\alpha}\hat{\ell}(x)$, and its potential measure $\hat{U}$ admits a density $\hat{u}$ that is monotone on some neighbourhood of $\infty$, then
\[B(z)=\frac{\Sigma(z)\hat{u}(z)}{z} \underset{z\rightarrow \infty}{\sim} \frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)}\frac{\Sigma(z)}{z^{2-\alpha}\hat{\ell}(1/z)}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)}\frac{\Sigma(z)}{z^{2}\hat\Phi(1/z)}\]
and
\[\overline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma,\hat\Phi}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)}\underset{z\rightarrow \infty}{\limsup} \frac{\Sigma(z)}{z^2\hat\Phi(1/z)} \text{ and }\underline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma,\hat\Phi}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)}\underset{z\rightarrow \infty}{\liminf}\frac{\Sigma(z)}{z^2\hat\Phi(1/z)}.\]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a non-compact connected semisimple real Lie group and $X$ be its symmetric space endowed with the canonical $G$-invariant metric $d_X$, $G$-invariant measure $\vol$ and the base point $o\in X$.
    Then 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[{\rm(1)}] $G$ is non-amenable and unimodular. The canonical action of $G$ on $X$ is continuous, proper, transitive and by measure-preserving isometries. Moreover, the measure ${\rm vol}$ is invariant under all isometries of $X$, 
        \item[{\rm(2)}] $(X,d_X)$ is a proper geodesic metric space,
        \item[{\rm(3)}] $\vol(C)<\infty$ for every compact or $d_X$-bounded set $C\subseteq X$ and $\vol(X)=\infty$,
        \item[{\rm(4)}] $\vol(\{x\in X:d_X(o,x)=r\})=0$ for every $r\in [0,\infty)$,
        \item[{\rm(5)}] the map $t\mapsto \vol(\mathcal{B}_t(o))$ is a continuous bijection from $[0,\infty)$ to $[0,\infty)$,
        \item[{\rm(6)}] there exist $a,b,c>0$ such that 
        \begin{equation*}
            \vol(\mathcal{B}_t(o))=ce^{at}t^{b}(1+o(1)),
        \end{equation*} 
        where the quantity $o(1)$ vanishes as $t\to \infty$.
    \end{enumerate}

[Definition defn:IXHG of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] We denote\[
I(X;H,G)=2^{-X-1}\sum_{F\in \mathscr F(X;H,G)} \prod_{\substack{t\in \llbracket 1, X \rrbracket: \\ F(t)=F(t-1)-1 }}\left(1+\frac{2F(t)}{\beta N}\right).
\]
When $H\le G$, we also denote $I^+(X;H,G)$ to be the same, except for that the summation is over $F\in\mathscr F^+(X;H,G)$.

body:
[Lem 147 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $Z$ be a standard gaussian random variable, and suppose $Y(q_0)\sim\zeta^\Ising$ satisfies assumption~\eqref{i:IAMP-main-init} of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}. Then for any $\eta>0$ there exists an odd function $\prxpsi:\bbR\to\bbR$ with bounded Lipschitz norm $\|\prxpsi\|_{\textup{Lip}}\leq \overline{L}(\eta,\zeta^{\Ising})$ such that $\bbW_2\big(\prxpsi(Z),\zeta^{\Ising}\big)\leq \eta$. Additionally, we have $|\bbE[\prxpsi(Z)^2] - q_0| \le 4\epsilon^{1/2}$.

\begin{proof}
    Using a standard quantile coupling, there exists an odd measurable function $\hat\psi\in L^2(\bbR)$ such that the law of $\hat\psi(Z)$ is precisely $\zeta^{\Ising}$. Since bounded Lipschitz functions are dense in $L^2$, there exists a bounded Lipschitz function $\tilde\psi:\bbR\to\bbR$ with $\bbW_2\big(\tilde\psi(Z),\zeta^{\Ising}\big)\leq \min\{\eta, \epsilon^{1/2}\}$.
The first assertion of the lemma immediately follows by taking $\prxpsi=\tilde\psi$.  For the second assertion, recall that under assumption~\eqref{i:IAMP-main-init} of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}, the random variable $Y(q_0)\sim\zeta^\Ising$ satisfies
	\[\Big|\E[Y(q_0)^2-q_0]
	\Big|\le\epsilon\,.\]
Under the $\bbW_2$-optimal coupling of $\prxpsi(Z)$ with $Y(q_0)$, we have
	\begin{align*}
	&\bigg|\E[\prxpsi(Z)^2]
	-\E[Y(q_0)^2] \bigg|
	=\bigg|\E\Big[
	(\prxpsi(Z)-Y(q_0))
	(\prxpsi(Z)-Y(q_0)
		+2Y(q_0))
	\Big]\bigg|\\
	&\qquad=\bigg| \E\Big[
	(\prxpsi(Z)-Y(q_0))^2
	\Big]
	+ 2\E\Big[
	(\prxpsi(Z)-Y(q_0)) Y(q_0)\Big]
	\bigg|
	\le \epsilon + 2 \epsilon^{1/2}
		\E[Y(q_0)^2]^{1/2} \le 3\epsilon^{1/2}\,.
	\end{align*}
Combining these gives
	\[
	\Big|\E[\prxpsi(Z)^2-q_0]
	\Big|
	\le 4\epsilon^{1/2}\,,
	\]
as claimed.\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.26516, '2608.26516'] For a node $v \in T_d$, identify a vector $c \in \{0, 1\}^d$ as a function on the block
    \[ E_{d, v}:=\{x_{d, v, j}:j \in [d]\} \]
    that maps $x_{d, v, j}$ to $c(j)$, where $c(j)$ denotes the $j$th component of $c$. Then at least one of the following holds:
    \begin{description}
        \item[Condition 1] There exists a node $v \in T_d$ such that
        \[ \forall c \in \{0, 1\}^d\ \exists f_c \in \operatorname{im}(A) \quad \restr{f_c}{E_{d, v}}=c. \]
        \item[Condition 2] There exists an infinite sequence $b_1, b_2, \dotsc$ with $b_i \in \{0, 1\}^d$ such that for every $i \geq 1$
        \[ b_i \notin \restr{\operatorname{im}(A)}{E_{d, (b_1, \dotsc, b_{i-1})}}. \]
    \end{description}

[Thm cohyp of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let $M^4$ be a smooth compact isometric quotient of the complex-hyperbolic plane  
$\mathbb{C}{\cal H}_2=SU(2,1)/U(2)$, 
 and let $g_0$ be its standard complex-hyperbolic metric.
 Then the moduli space $\mathscr{E}(M)$ of Einstein metrics
 on $M$ consists of a single point, represented by $g_0$.  That is, 
every Einstein metric $g$  on $M$   is of the form 
$g=\Psi^*(cg_0)$ for  some self-diffeomorphism  $\Psi$ of $M$ and some positive constant 
   $c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2609.02713, 'On divergence related to Riemann--von Mangoldt's explicit formula of the prime-counting fu'] For every sufficiently large $T$ there exists $T'\in[T,T+1]$, which is not a zero ordinate, such that
$$
\frac{\zeta'(\sigma\pm iT')}{\zeta(\sigma\pm iT')}=O((\log(T'))^2)
$$
uniformly for $-1\le\sigma\le2$.  Moreover, if $T'=T'(T)$ is any such choice made in dependence of $T$, and $1<c\le2$ and $0<a<1$ are arbitrary, but fixed, then
$$
H_{a,c}(T')=o(1)\qquad(T\to\infty).
$$

[Theorem 31 of arXiv:2605.16560, 'Seasonal Statistics of Shannon Rate in a Dynamical Poisson-Voronoi Cellular Network'] The interference power in the non-tropical and tropical cases satisfies the following orderings:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item with or without fading: $I_{\sst \Vcal}\geq_{\textnormal{L}} I_{t} \geq_{\textnormal{L}} I_{\sst S}$ and $I_{\sst \Ical}\geq_{\textnormal{L}}  I_{\sst I}$,
    \item with fading: $\Tcal_{\sst{\Vcal}}\geq_{\textnormal{st}} \Tcal_{t} \geq_{\textnormal{st}} \Tcal_{\sst S}$ and $\Tcal_{\sst \Ical} \geq_{\textnormal{st}}  \Tcal_{\sst I}$,
    \item without fading: $\Tcal_{\sst{\Vcal}}\stackrel{d}{=} \Tcal_{\sst S} \geq_{\textnormal{lrd}} \Tcal_{t}  $ and $\Tcal_{\sst I} \geq_{\textnormal{lrd}}  \Tcal_{\sst \Ical}$,
\end{enumerate}
compared under their respective Palm probability spaces. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 9 of arXiv:2607.26564, 'Stochastic Scalar Conservation Laws on Moving Hypersurfaces'] Let $u_0 \in L^\infty(\Gamma_0)$. We say that a stochastic process $\{u(t)\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a generalized entropy solution to \eqref{eq74} if
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. $u \in L^\infty(Q_T)$.

\item[(ii)] $u$ is a predictable random process with respect to the filtration $ \{ \mathcal{F}_t \} _{t\in[0,T]} $.
\item[(iii)] For any $\varrho \in C^2(Q_T)$, $\phi \in C^2(\mathbb{R})$ with $\phi^{\prime\prime} \geq 0$, and any $\eta \in C^1(Q_T)$ with $\eta \geq 0$ and $\eta(\cdot, T)= 0$, $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.
\begin{eqnarray}
 & &  \langle \phi(u_0), \eta(0) \rangle_{\Gamma_0}
   + \int_0^T \langle \big(\phi(u(s)- \Psi(s))-u(s)\phi^{\prime}(u(s) - \Psi(s))\big)\nabla_{\Gamma_s}\cdot v(s), \eta(s) \rangle_{\Gamma_s} ds \nonumber\\
 & &  + \int_0^T \langle \phi(u(s)- \Psi(s)), \overset{\scalebox{0.4}{$\bullet$}}{\eta}(s) \rangle_{\Gamma_s} ds
   + \int_0^T \langle \phi^{\prime}(u(s)- \Psi(s))(\sigma(s)- \varrho(s)), \eta(s) \rangle_{\Gamma_s} dB_s \nonumber\\
 & & + \frac{1}{2}\int_0^T \langle \phi^{\prime\prime}(u(s)- \Psi(s))(\sigma(s)-\varrho(s))^2, \eta(s) \rangle_{\Gamma_s} ds \nonumber\\
   
 & & + \int_0^T \int_{\Gamma_s} q_{\varrho,\phi}((s,x),u(s,x)-\Psi(s,x))\cdot \nabla_{\Gamma_s}\eta(s,x) \mathrm{dvol}_{\Gamma_s}(dx)ds \nonumber\\
  & & -\int_0^T \langle \phi^{\prime}(u(s)- \Psi(s))f_u((s,\cdot), u(s))\cdot \nabla_{\Gamma_s}\Psi(s), \eta(s) \rangle_{\Gamma_s} ds\nonumber\\
  & &  +\int_0^T  \langle l_{\varrho,\phi}((s,\cdot),u(s) - \Psi(s)), \eta(s) \rangle_{\Gamma_s} ds
  \geq 0,
\end{eqnarray}
where $\Psi(s,x) = \int_0^s \varrho(r, G(r, G^{-1}(s,x)))dB_r$.
\end{itemize}

body: For kernel ridge regression with power-law spectrum $\eta_k = k^{-\alpha}$ ($\alpha>1$, the capacity) and teacher coefficients $\theta_k = k^{-(1+\alpha(2r-1))/2}$ ($r \ge 0$, the source), with label noise of variance $\sigma^2$ and ridge $\lambda = n^{-\ell}$, the excess risk of the ridgeless estimator ($\ell \ge \alpha$, including interpolation) is of order $\max(\sigma^2, n^{-2\alpha\min(r,1)})$, while the optimally regularised excess risk is of order $n^{-2\alpha\min(r,1)}$ for $n$ below a crossover $n_* \asymp \sigma^{-1/(\alpha\min(r,1))}$ and of order $n^{1/(1+2\alpha\min(r,1)) - 1}$ above it (Cui, Loureiro, Krzakala, Zdeborova, NeurIPS 2021). Two consequences that a learning-curve experiment can test directly: (i) with no label noise the interpolant is the optimum of the whole path, so the ratio of the interpolant's risk to the best risk on the path is $1$; (ii) with noise, once $n$ is past the crossover, that ratio grows like $n^{2\alpha\min(r,1)/(1+2\alpha\min(r,1))}$, and a tenfold increase in the noise level moves the crossover by a factor $10^{1/(\alpha\min(r,1))}$ in $n$. Both exponents are read off the Gram spectrum and the labels of the same fit, so the prediction and the measurement come from one object. (For a Burgers-equation emulation corpus at $n=4000$ the estimates are $\hat\alpha = 2.02$, $\hat r = 0.63$, giving a growth exponent $0.72$ and a crossover exponent $0.78$; the noiseless ratio measured $1.00$.)

body:
[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.04153, '\vspace*{-3cm}Smooth autonomous fast dynamo action on the three-torus'] Consider the solution to the equation \eqref{eq:elliptic evolution}, subject to the boundary condition $B(x,y,0)=B_{\mathrm{in}}$, and the growth condition of Lemma \ref{lemma:notion of solution}. Let $\mathcal{K}_{\lambda,\eps}B_{\mathrm{in}}$ denote the trace of the solution at $z=1$. Then, iterates of the map $\mathcal{K}_{\lambda,\eps}$ may be factored as 
$$
\mathcal{K}^m_{\lambda,\eps}=\mathcal{E}_u \circ \left ( D^m_{u,\lambda}\mathcal{U}^{[m]}_{\lambda,\eps} \right ) \circ\mathcal{E}_u^{-1},
$$
where $\mathcal{U}^{[m]}_{\lambda,\eps}v_0$ denotes the trace at $s=m$ of the solution to \eqref{eq:abstract elliptic equation} with boundary conditions $v(x,y,0)=v_0$, and $v(x,y,T)=C_{u,T,\lambda}^{-1}(x,y) B(F_{u,T}(\kappa_u(x,y)),T)$, where $B(x,y,z)$ is the solution to \eqref{eq:elliptic evolution} with $B(x,y,0)=B_{\mathrm{in}}$, satisfying the growth condition of Lemma \ref{lemma:notion of solution}, and $T>m$. Furthermore, the operator $D_{u,\lambda}$ satisfies the following \emph{Lasota--Yorke} inequality: there exists $C>0$ independent of $u,\lambda$, so that if $\Re(\lambda) \geq 0$ it holds
\begin{align*}
\|D^m_{u,\lambda} B\|_{\mathcal X} &\leq C_{LY}(u,\lambda,m)\|B\|_{\mathcal X}
\\
& \quad +\e^{-\Re(\lambda)\inf_{a \in \TT^2}\tau^m_u(a)}(1+\|\lambda  \nabla (\tau^m_u(P_u^{-m}))\|_{L^\infty})C(\|DP^m_u\|_{L^\infty},\|D \tau^m_u\|_{C^1}) \|B\|_{\mathcal Y},
\end{align*}
where 
$$C_{LY}(u,\lambda,m)=C\e^{-\Re(\lambda)\inf_{a \in \TT^2}\tau^m_u(a)}\left (\|DP^m_u\|_{L^\infty}^{1-r}+\|DP_u^{m}\|_{L^\infty}^{r+\delta} \right ).$$
Similarly, there holds 
$$
\|D^m_{u,\lambda} B\|_{\mathcal Y} \leq C_0(\lambda, \tau^m_u(P_u^{-m}))C(\|DP^m_u\|_{L^\infty},\|D \tau^m_u(P_u^{-m})\|_{C^1})\|B\|_{\mathcal Y}.
$$

[Cor 5 of arXiv:2512.03884, '2512.03884'] Assume $X_1$ is nondegenerate, and $\alpha$ is badly approximable. Then
\[ \mathbb{E} \left( W_{\mathbb{T},2}^2 (\mu_N, \lambda) \right) \ll \frac{\log N}{N} \quad \textrm{and} \quad \mathrm{Var} \left( W_{\mathbb{T},2}^2 (\mu_N, \lambda) \right) \ll \frac{\log N}{N^2} . \]
If in addition $\mathbb{E} (X_1) =0$ and $0<\mathbb{E} (X_1^2) < \infty$, then
\[ \mathbb{E} \left( W_{\mathbb{T},2}^2 (\mu_N, \lambda) \right) \asymp \frac{\log N}{N} \quad \textrm{and} \quad \mathrm{Var} \left( W_{\mathbb{T},2}^2 (\mu_N, \lambda) \right) \asymp \frac{\log N}{N^2} . \]
All implied constants depend only on $\alpha$ and the distribution of $X_1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In computational complexity theory, the time hierarchy theorems are important statements about time-bounded computation on Turing machines. Informally, these theorems say that given more time, a Turing machine can solve more problems. For example, there are problems that can be solved with n2 time but not n time, where n is the input length.

The zero mode contribution $-1/\Gamma(s+1)$ is kept separate and evaluated below. The remainder part is
		\[
		\frac1{\Gamma(s)}\left(
		\int_0^1t^{s-1}
		\bigl[p_t(e)-C_{G,L}t^{-Q/2}e^{\beta_{G,L}t}\bigr] \,\mathrm dt
		+\int_1^\infty t^{s-1}[p_t(e)-1] \,\mathrm dt
		\right).

[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Consider the following maps:
    
    \begin{enumerate}[font=\normalfont,label=(\roman*)]
    
        \item $T_{\sigma,\nu}:\cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell,m}$ for $\sigma,\nu$ permutations, such that 
        $$ T_{\sigma,\nu}(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l\otimes a_1\otimes \cdots \otimes a_m) = h_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\sigma(l)}\otimes a_{\nu(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{\nu(m)}, $$
        
        \item $\langle f|:\cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell-1,m}$ such that 
        $$\langle f|(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l\otimes a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_m) = \langle f| h_1\rangle h_2\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l \otimes a_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{m}, $$
        
        \item given $\cU$ a subset of $\cB$ and $p_{\cU}$ the orthogonal projection on $\spn(\cU)$, $\eta_{\cU}: \cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell-2,m}$ such that 
        $$\eta_{\cU}(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l\otimes a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_m) = \langle p_{\cU}(h_1)| p_{\cU}(h_2)\rangle h_3\otimes\cdots\otimes h_l\otimes a_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{m},$$

        \item $m:\cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell,m-1}$ such that 
        $$ m(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell}\otimes a_1\otimes \cdots \otimes a_m) = h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell}\otimes a_1a_2\otimes a_3\otimes\cdots\otimes a_m, $$

        \item $\tr:\cA^{\ell,m}\mapsto\cA^{\ell,m-1}$ such that 
        $$ \tr(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell}\otimes a_1\otimes \cdots \otimes a_m) = \tau(a_1) h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell}\otimes a_2\otimes\cdots\otimes a_m. $$

    \end{enumerate}

    \noindent If $\mathbf{f} \in \cC^k(\cB)$, and $\cJ \colon \cA^{j,j+1} \mapsto \cA$ is a linear map built out of the maps above, then given $j_0,\dots,j_n$ such that $j_0+\dots+j_n = j$, we have that $\cJ\circ \widetilde{\partial}^{(j_n)}\circ\cdots\circ \widetilde{\partial}^{(j_1)}\circ \partial^{(j_0)} \mathbf{f} \in \cC^{k-j}(\cB)$. Besides there exists a constant $C_{\cJ}$ such that for any $R>0$,
    \begin{equation}
    
        \norm{\cJ\circ \widetilde{\partial}^{(j_n)}\circ\cdots\circ \widetilde{\partial}^{(j_1)}\circ \partial^{(j_0)} \mathbf{f} }_{\cC^{k-j}(\cB),R} \leq C_{\cJ} \norm{\mathbf{f}}_{\cC^k(\cB),R}.
    \end{equation}

body:
[Definition 23 (Coalescent process) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] Fix a height $0 \le h^* \le h(q_n)$ and an integer $1\le k\le q_n(h^*)$. For $0 \le j \le h^*$, set
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  \cX^{(k)}_j = \cX^{(k)}_j(n,h^*)&=\big\{\text{Anc}(u^{h^*}_i,j):1\le i\le k\big\} \\
  &=\big\{v \in V(\mathscr{T}^n) : |v| = j,\ \operatorname{Desc}(v) \cap \{u^{h^*}_i:1\le i\le k\} \neq \emptyset \big\}.  
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The coalescent process (based at height $h^*$) is then defined as
\[
X^{(k)}_j = X^{(k)}_j(n,h^*) := \#\cX^{(k)}_j,\qquad 0 \le j \le h^*.
\]
In the special case $k=q_n(h^*)$, we write $\cX_j$ and $X_j$ in place of $\cX^{(k)}_j$ and $X^{(k)}_j$, respectively.

In other words, $X^{(k)}_j$ represents the number of distinct ancestral lineages at height $j$ traced from $k$ uniformly sampled vertices at height $h^*$.  
At $j=h^*$, we have $X^{(k)}_0 = k$, since all sampled vertices are distinct.  
As $j$ decreases, the lineages are traced backward through the tree and may coalesce whenever two or more sampled vertices share a common ancestor.  
Thus, the process $\big(X^{(k)}_j : 0 \le j \le h^*\big)$ is non-increasing as $j$ decreases, and each downward jump corresponds to a coalescence event between ancestral lineages.

For normalized self-inclusive spherical attention with Q^T K=V=V^T, finite n and beta>0, let V have eigenvalues lambda_k and unit eigenvector e_p. The consensus equilibrium x_i=e_p for all i is linearly asymptotically stable if lambda_p>0 and lambda_k<lambda_p for every k!=p. Its opposite orientation is stable too. It is unstable if lambda_p<0 or any lambda_k>lambda_p. In particular signature (2,1) with a simple largest positive eigenvalue has open positive-volume basins of positive-axis consensus for every fixed beta>0; generic negative-axis bipolar convergence cannot be asserted throughout this class. This is a literature result, not a new campaign proof.

[Defi Equ:weighted-Boun-DW of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] A \emph{descending type weighted simplicial complex}
 is a pair $(L, \overline{w})$ where $L$ is a simplicial complex and $\overline{w}$ is a function assigning a positive integer to each simplex of $L$, which satisfy: for any simplices $\sigma, \sigma'$ in $L$,
  \[ \sigma'\ \text{is a face of}\ \sigma \Rightarrow \overline{w}(\sigma)\, |\, \overline{w}(\sigma').  \]
  
  We call $\overline{w}$ a \emph{descending weight} on $L$. Similarly to~(equation Equ:weighted-Boun-AW of the paper),
  we define a weighted boundary operator $\partial^{\overline{w}}: C_n(L)\rightarrow C_{n-1}(L)$ for every $n\geqslant 0$ by:
  \begin{equation} 
   \partial^{\overline{w}}: \sigma \longmapsto \sum^n_{j=0} (-1)^j \frac{\overline{w}(\partial_j(\sigma))}{\overline{w}(\sigma)}  \partial_j \sigma. 
   \end{equation}
  It is easy to show that $\partial^{\overline{w}}\circ\partial^{\overline{w}}=0$.  We call $(C_*(L), \partial^{\overline{w}})$ the
  \emph{weighted simplicial chain complex} of $(L,\overline{w})$, whose homology group is called the \emph{weighted simplicial homology group} of $(L,\overline{w})$, denoted by 
  $H_*(L,\partial^{\overline{w}})$.
title: Defi Equ:weighted-Boun-DW of arXiv:2608.29013

\[
I \in \mathcal{I}_n:= \mathcal{P}([n]) \setminus \{\{1\},...,\{n\},\{1,2\}, \{2,3\}, ...,\{n-1,n\}\},

where $\mathcal{P}$ denotes the power set.

    \begin{equation*}
        \Psi_\beta[I] = |\gamma_1|   \mathcal{O}\big(\myexp{(-4(4(m-1))\beta)}\big),
    \end{equation*}

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2607.22441, 'The martingale representation theorem for cylindrical martingale valued measures'] Let $\Phi, \Psi\in\Lambda(M,X,Y)$ and $\lambda \in \R$, we have
$$
\int (\lambda \Phi + \Psi)\; dM = \lambda \int \Phi\;dM + \int \Psi\; dM. 
$$
More precisely, for any given   $A\in\mathcal{A}$, the identity
$$
\int_0^t\int_A (\lambda \Phi(s,u) + \Psi(s,u))\; M(ds,du) = \lambda \int_0^t\int_A \Phi(s,u)\;M(ds,du) + \int_0^t\int_A \Psi(s,u)\; M(ds,du)
$$
holds $\Prob$-a.e. simultaneously for all $t\in [0,T]$.
