[Lemma Lemme_sur_le_couplage of arXiv:2504.03627, 'Richardson’s model and the contact process with stirring: long time behavior.'] Let $\lambda,\nu>0$. 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There exist processes $(\eta_t^{\mathrm{RMS}})_{t\ge 0}$, $(\xi_t^{\mathrm{RMS}})_{t\ge 0}$, $(\zeta_t^{\mathrm{RMS}})_{t\ge 0}$, all defined on the measurable space $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$, such that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item the process $(\eta_t^{\mathrm{RMS}})_{t\ge 0}$ is a $\mathrm{CP}(\lambda,2d)$.
        \item the process $(\xi_t^{\mathrm{RMS}})_{t\ge 0}$ is a $\mathrm{RMS}(\lambda,1)$.
        \item the process $(\zeta_t^{\mathrm{RMS}})_{t\ge 0}$ is a $\mathrm{RM}(\lambda+1)$.
        \item if $A\subset B\subset C\subset \mathbb Z^d$ and $\eta_0=A$, $\xi_0=B$ and $\zeta_0=C$, then we have, for all $t\ge0$:
        $$\eta_t^{\mathrm{RMS}} \subset \xi_t^{\mathrm{RMS}} \subset \zeta_t^{\mathrm{RMS}}.$$
    \end{itemize}
        \item There exist processes $(\eta_t^{\mathrm{CPS}})_{t\ge 0}$, $(\xi_t^{\mathrm{CPS}})_{t\ge 0}$ and $(\zeta_t^{\mathrm{CPS}})_{t\ge 0}$, all defined on the measurable space $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$, such that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item the process $(\eta_t^{\mathrm{CPS}})_{t\ge 0}$ is a $\mathrm{CP}(\lambda,2d\nu+1)$.
        \item the process $(\xi_t^{\mathrm{CPS}})_{t\ge 0}$ is a $\mathrm{CPS}(\lambda,1,\nu)$.
        \item the process $(\zeta_t^{\mathrm{CPS}})_{t\ge 0}$ is a $\mathrm{RM}(\lambda+\nu)$.
        \item if $A\subset B\subset C\subset \mathbb Z^d$ and $\eta_0=A$, $\xi_0=B$ and $\zeta_0=C$, then we have, for all $t\ge0$:
        $$\eta_t^{\mathrm{CPS}} \subset \xi_t^{\mathrm{CPS}} \subset \zeta_t^{\mathrm{CPS}}.$$
    \end{itemize}
    Moreover, we have 
    $$0<\lambda_c^{\mathrm{CPS}}(d,\nu)\le (2d\nu+1)\lambda_c^{\mathrm{CP}}(d)<+\infty.$$
    \end{enumerate}

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2609.03386, 'Twisted Gradient Flow Approach to Vegetation-Rainfall-Bushfire Interactions Model'] For each $z_0 \in H^1(\Omega)$ and $\tilde{v} \in \mathcal{V}(v_0)$ the initial-boundary value problem $\text{(AP2)}{}_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}}$ has a unique 
strong solution $z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}} (z_0,\tilde{v})$ on $[0,T]$ satisfying 

\begin{gather}

\hspace*{-0.8cm}z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}} (z_0,\tilde{v}) \in W^{1,2}(0,T\,;L^2(\Omega)) \cap L^\infty (0,T\,;H^1(\Omega)) \cap L^2(0,T\,;H^2(\Omega)),\\

(z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}}(z_0,\tilde{v}))'(t)-\varepsilon \Delta_N z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}}(z_0,\tilde{v}\,;t)=\tilde{v}'(t) \quad 
\text{in} \quad L^2(\Omega), \quad \text{a.e.}~t \in (0,T),\\

z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}}(z_0,\tilde{v}\,;0)=z_0 \quad \text{in} \quad L^2(\Omega).
\end{gather}

\indent
Moreover, there exists a constant $C_6>0$, which depends on the following values:

\begin{equation*}
T,\quad \|z_0\|_{H^1(\Omega)},\quad \int_0^T \|\tilde{v}'(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2dt,
\end{equation*}

such that the following estimate holds for all $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$:

\begin{align*}
&\left(\max_{0 \le t \le T} \|z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}} (z_0,\tilde{v}\,;t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\right)^2
+\int_0^T \|z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}}'(z_0,\tilde{v}\,;t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2dt\\
&\hspace*{1cm}+\varepsilon \left(\sup_{0 \le t \le T} \|\nabla z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}} (z_0,\tilde{v}\,;t)\|_{\bm{L}^2(\Omega)} \right)^2
+\varepsilon^2 \int_0^T \|z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}} (z_0,\tilde{v}\,;t)\|_{H^2(\Omega)}^2dt \le C_6.
\end{align*}

Especially, as a result of this estimate we have the boundedness of the strong solutions $z_{\text{{\tiny $\varepsilon$}}} (z_0,\tilde{v})$ in 
$C([0,T]\,;L^2(\Omega)) \cap W^{1,2}(0,T\,;L^2(\Omega))$ uniformly with respect to $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$.

body:
On the uniform cube {-1, 1}^n let f be real, f^(S) = E[f chi_S] its Walsh coefficients and W_k = sum over |S| = k of f^(S)^2. For rho in [-1, 1], T_rho is the noise operator: T_rho f(x) = E[f(Y)] where the Y_i are independent with P(Y_i = x_i) = (1 + rho)/2, so T_rho chi_S = rho^|S| chi_S. Let H(t) = Stab_{e^{-t}}[f] for t >= 0. For every m >= 0, (-1)^m H^(m)(t) = sum_k k^m W_k e^{-kt} >= 0, so H is completely monotone; H(t) > 0 if f is not 0, H(t) -> W_0 = (E f)^2 as t -> infinity, and for m >= 1 the derivative is strictly signed iff f is not constant. With the tilted degree law nu_t(k) = W_k e^{-kt}/H(t), (log H)'(t) = -E_{nu_t}[K] and (log H)''(t) = Var_{nu_t}(K) >= 0, so H is log-convex, strictly at every t unless all the nonzero mass sits at a single level.

[Corollary 12 of arXiv:2608.18834, 'The Parabolic Anderson Model's Total Mass at Small Times: Geometry, Fluctuations, and Reno'] Suppose that Assumption \ref{Assumption} holds,
and let $\ka>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\rho>H_0-1$, then
\[\mbf E\big[\msf Q_\ka(t)\big]=o(t^{H_0})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mbf E[\msf Q_\ka(t)^2]^{1/2}\sim\ka\mf c\,t^{H_0}.\]
\item If $\rho=H_0-1$ and $H_0\neq1$, then
\[\mbf E\big[\msf Q_\ka(t)\big]\sim\frac{\ka^2|D|(2H_0-1)}{(H_0-1)2^{H}}\prod_{j=1}^d\frac{\Ga(2H_j+1)}{\Ga(H_j)}\,t^{H_0}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\sqrt{\mbf{Var}[\msf Q_\ka(t)]}\sim\ka\mf c\,t^{H_0}.\]
\item Otherwise:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\rho=H_0-1$ and $H_0=1$, then
\[\lim_{t\to0}\frac{\msf Q_\ka(t)}{t\log(1/t)}=-\frac{\ka^2|D|}{2^{d-1}}\prod_{j=1}^d\frac{\Ga(2H_j+1)}{\Ga(H_j)}\qquad\text{in probability.}\] 
\item If $\rho<H_0-1$, then
\[\lim_{t\to0}\frac{\msf Q_\ka(t)}{t^{1+\rho}}
=\frac{\ka^2|D|H_0(2H_0-1)}{2^H(1+\rho)\rho}\prod_{j=1}^d\frac{\Ga(2H_j+1)}{\Ga(H_j)}\qquad\text{in probability.}\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

windows of length at most \(2T\).  Then there exist constants

\[
\left|

\right|
\le
  C_{F,G}
  \exp\{-c_{F,G}(d_S(u,v)-4T)_+\},
\]
where
\[
  d_S(u,v)=\min\{|u-v|,S-|u-v|\}
\]
is the cyclic distance on the time circle of length \(S\).
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 85 (One universal Hall test path) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] The finite concatenations converge in $p$-variation to one weakly geometric
$p$-rough path $\mathbf X_*$ on $H_*$.  It is independent of tensor degree,
Schur sector, and dual probe.  For every finite stable coefficient sector
$M_{\lambda,n}$ and every nonzero $q\in M_{\lambda,n}^*$, a bounded block
projection of $\mathbf X_*$ followed by one signed native corner gives
\begin{equation}
 Q_+\operatorname{Mat}_S\!\left(
 q(\pi_n\log_\otimes(P_{k\#}\mathbf X_*)_{0,1})\right)Q_-
 =c_qUD_\infty^{\otimes a_F(q)}V,
 \qquad c_q\ne0.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently one fixed geometric path, together with labelled bounded
readers, tests every finite primitive layer and reconstructs every finite
ancestry flag.

[Defi gs of arXiv:2507.20324, 'Non-existence of several random fractals in Brownian motion and Brownian loop soup'] Fix $\delta>0$. Let $N(\delta)$ be the smallest integer $n$ such that $2^{-n}<\delta/16$. For $n\geq N(\delta)$, let $\mathfrak{S}_{n}=\mathfrak{S}_{n}(\delta)$ stand for the collection of $\delta$-good boxes, i.e.\ the set of all $S\in\mathcal{S}_{n}$ with the following properties:
\par
(1) $S$ is visited three times by $W_{t}$ and the trajectories between successive visits reach distance at least $(\delta-2^{-n-1/2})$ to the centre of $S$. Using the notation in Section~(subsec:notation of the paper), that is,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{T}(S):=\tau(S,\partial\mathcal{B}(S,\delta-2^{-n-1/2}),S,\partial\mathcal{B}(S,\delta-2^{-n-1/2}),S)<\tau_{\mathbb{D}}.
\end{equation}
We use $V_{\delta}^{\mathrm{PTP}}(S)$ to denote this event.
\par
(2) $\mathcal{D}_{-n}(S)$ is not disconnected from infinity by the path $\{W_{s}:0\leq s\leq\mathcal{T}(S)\}$.

[Theorem 30 of arXiv:2511.10814, '\Large \bf \boldmath\ \\ Convergence of the extended Kalman filter with small and state-de'] Let $A, B \in \mathcal{M}_{n}(\mathbb{R})$ be symmetric. Let $\lambda_1(A) \leq \ldots \leq \lambda_n(A)$ and $\lambda_1(B) \leq \ldots \leq \lambda_n(B)$ be the ordered eigenvalues of A and B, respectively.
										
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A \gm  0$ and $B \gm 0$, then $A \geqm B$ if and only if $ B^{-1} \geqm A^{-1}$.
\item If $A \gm  0$, $B \geqm 0$, and $A \geqm  B$ , then $A^{1/2} \geqm  B^{1/2}$.
	\item If $A \geqm B$, then $ \lambda_i(A)\geq \lambda_i(B)$ for each $i = 1, \ldots , n$.
	\item If $A \geqm  B$, then $\trace A \geq  \trace B$ with equality if and only if $A = B$.
	\item If $A \geqm B \geqm 0$, then $\det A \geq  \det B \geq 0$.
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:hard_lim of arXiv:2412.04579, 'Solvable Families of Random Block Tridiagonal Matrices'] Given a block bidiagonal matrix $\mathbf{L}_n$ with independent diagonal and upper diagonal $r \times r$ blocks $\mathbf{D}_k=\mathbf{D}_{n,k}$ and $\mathbf{O}_k=\mathbf{O}_{n,k}$, embed $ \mathbf{ L}_n^{-1}$ into $L^2([0,1], \mathbb{F}^r)$
in the manner of~(equation embed of the paper) with now $m_n = n$. In particular,
define the piecewise step kernel
\begin{equation*}

 \ell_{n}(x,y) = \sqrt{ \frac{ {n} \gamma}{r}}
 {\mathbf{D}}_{\lfloor nx \rfloor}^{-1}
 {\mathbf{X}}_n(x)^{-1} \mathbf{X}_n(y) \mathbf{1}_{0 \le x < y \le 1},
 \qquad
 {\mathbf{X}}_n(x) = \prod_{k= 1}^{ \lfloor nx \rfloor}
 {\mathbf{O}}_k {\mathbf{D}}_{k+1}^{-1}.
\end{equation*}
Assume that
\begin{itemize}\itemsep=0pt
\item[$(i)$] As $n \rightarrow \infty$, in the uniform-on-compacts topology
\[
 \left( \sqrt{\frac{{n} \gamma}{r}} \mathbf{D}_{\lfloor nx \rfloor}^{-1}, \mathbf{X}_n(x) \right) \Rightarrow
 \left( \frac{1}{r \sqrt{ 1-x}} \mathbf{I}_r, \mathbf{X}_x \right) \qquad
\text{for} \ x\in [0,1),
\]
where $\mathbf{X}_x$ satisfies the matrix stochastic differential equation
\[
 \mathbf{X}_x^{-1} {\rm d}\mathbf{X}_x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{r \gamma (1-x)}} {\rm d} B_x - \frac{a -\frac{1}{ \beta}}{2 r\gamma (1- x)} {I}_r{\rm d}x, \qquad \mathbf{X}_0=0.
\]

\item[$(ii)$] There is the bound
\[
 \int_0^1 \int_0^y | \ell_n(x,y) |^2 {\rm d}x {\rm d}y \le \kappa_n
\]
with $\kappa_n$ a sequence of tight random constants.
\end{itemize}
Then $\operatorname{spec}\bigl( \frac{rn}{ \gamma} \mathbf{L}_n \mathbf{L}_n^\dagger\bigr) \rightarrow \operatorname{spec}(\mathcal{G}_{\beta, \gamma})$ in the manner described in Proposition {\rm(Model_SoftEdgeConv of the paper)}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let n >= 2k >= 2 and let F be a family of k-element subsets of an n-element set such that every two members of F intersect. Then |F| <= binom(n-1, k-1). When n > 2k, equality holds exactly when F consists of all k-subsets containing one fixed element; when n = 2k every intersecting family of size binom(2k-1, k-1) is obtained by choosing one set from each complementary pair, so the extremal families are not unique.
n >= 2k (for n < 2k any two k-subsets intersect and the bound is different)

body:
Let (X, B, mu, T) be a measure-preserving system on a Lebesgue space and let P be a countable measurable partition of finite entropy. If P is a GENERATOR - that is, the smallest T-invariant sigma-algebra containing P is B modulo null sets (for invertible T one uses the two-sided join over all integers, for non-invertible T the one-sided join over nonnegative integers) - then the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of the system equals the entropy of that one partition: h(T) = h(T, P). There is also an increasing-partitions form: if P_1 is contained in P_2 is contained in ... is an increasing sequence of finite-entropy partitions whose union generates B modulo null sets, then h(T, P_n) increases to h(T).
Finite entropy of the generating partition, and generation modulo null sets.
For an invertible T it suffices that P generate under the two-sided join; h(T, P) itself is always defined with the one-sided joins P v T^{-1}P v ... v T^{-(n-1)}P.
One-sided generation is a stronger hypothesis for an invertible T and forces h(T) = 0: the join of T^{-n}P over n >= 1 is then T^{-1}B = B, so h(T, P) = H(P | that join) = 0.
The Lebesgue-space assumption is the usual standing hypothesis.

[Lemma lem.block-compatibility of arXiv:2605.26082, 'Quantitative Einstein relation for reversible diffusions in a random environment'] For every $k\ge1$, the following hold.
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[\rm(i)] If $1\le i\le k-2$, then $M_i$ is $\mathcal G_k$-measurable.
			\item[\rm(ii)] There is a measurable map $\Psi$ on the common state space of the shifted future data such that
			\[
				(M_k,M_{k+1},\ldots)=\Psi(\mathcal Y_k)
			\]
			$\widehat{\mathbb P}_0^\lambda$-almost surely.
		\end{enumerate}

[Lem reduce of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] Let $\tilde h$ be as in (eq:htilde of the paper) and put

\[
r(t)=\prod_{j=1}^{r}(t-a_j)^{-\lfloor e_j/n\rfloor},\qquad u=t,\qquad v=s\,r(t).
\]

Then $v^n=h(u)$ with

\begin{equation}
h(u)=c\prod_{j=1}^{r}(u-a_j)^{\bar e_j},\qquad \bar e_j\equiv e_j\pmod n,\quad 0\le\bar e_j<n,
\end{equation}

so $h\in k[u]$, and $k(u,v)=k(C)$.

body: Sylvester's law of inertia is a theorem in matrix algebra about certain properties of the coefficient matrix of a real quadratic form that remain invariant under a change of basis. Namely, if $S$ is a symmetric matrix, then for any invertible matrix $P$, the numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of $S'=PSP^{\mathsf {T}}$ are constant (i.e., the inertia of $S'$ is constant). This result is particularly useful when $S'$ is diagonal, as the inertia of a diagonal matrix can easily be obtained by looking at the signs of its diagonal elements.

[Thm zetaM_fourier_An of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Suppose $0\le M\le n/3$. Then, we have
\[
\widehat{\xi_M}(\lambda)
=
\frac{K_{\lambda,\mu}}{d_\lambda}\,\Id_{d_\lambda},
\]
where
\[
\mu=\mu_M:=(n-M,1,1,\dots,1)\vdash n,
\]
and $K_{\alpha,\mu}$ denotes the Kostka number.

Moreover, if $\lambda_1<n-M$, then $\widehat{\xi_M}(\lambda)=0$. If $\lambda_1\ge n-M$, we have
$$\widehat{\xi_M}(\lambda)=\binom{M}{\,n-\lambda_1\,}\frac{
d_{\lambda^*}}{d_\lambda}\Id_{d_\lambda}.$$

body:
[Proposition 20 (No universal bound below the first moment) of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Let \(K>0\), and let \(\Psi\) be a nondecreasing functional on the class of nonnegative integer-valued random variables. Assume that for every finitary coding \(\varphi\), every i.i.d.\ input \(X\), every local observable \(f\), and every \(n\in\mathbb N\),
\[
\E\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}\big(c_i^{(n)}(X)\big)^2
\le
K\,\|\delta f\|_2^2\,\Psi\big(r_\varphi^{(n)}(X)\big).
\]
Then necessarily
\[
\E\,|B_\infty(0,r_\varphi^{(n)}(X))|
\le
K\,\Psi\big(r_\varphi^{(n)}(X)\big).
\]
In particular, any universal squared-influence bound depending only on the coding radius must control at least the first moment of the coding volume.

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2608.31164, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality'] Consider a Borel set $\Gamma \subset \bG(N,m)$.
For every $\kappa_* > 0$ and $B_* < \infty$, there is a constant $C(N,\phi,\kappa_*, B_*)$ so that for every anisotropy with
\begin{equation}
\textstyle \kappa(\Psi,\Gamma,\phi,\rho) > \kappa_* > 0, \qquad \sup_{T \in \Gamma} \|B_{\Psi}(T) \| < B_*< \infty,
\end{equation}
every rectifiable $m$-varifold $V = v(M,\theta)$ with $T_x M \in \Gamma$ for $\cH^m$-a.e.~$x$ satisfies
\[
\| V\| (\bR^N) \leq C \, \cH^m(M)^{\frac{1}{m}} |\delta_{\Psi}V |(\bR^N).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\sup_{0\le{} t\le{} T}\mathbb{E}|\delta Y_t|^2 + \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T|\delta Z_s|^2\dif s\right] \le{} C\left(\mathbb{E}|\delta\xi|^2 + \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T|\delta f(s,Y_s^2,Z_s^2,\nu_s^2)|^2\dif s\right]\right),
\]
where the difference processes and terms are denoted by $\delta Y_t :={} Y_t^1-Y_t^2$, $\delta Z_t :={} Z_t^1-Z_t^2$, $\delta K_t :={} K_t^1-K_t^2$, $\delta\xi :={} \xi^1-\xi^2$, and the difference between the generators is $\delta f(t,y,z,\nu) :={} f^1(t,y,z,\nu)-f^2(t,y,z,\nu)$.

For every integer $i\ge 2$,
\[
  A_i \le 4\,i!.
\]

body:
Let Omega be a bounded open subset of R^n with boundary of class C^1 and outward unit normal nu. RELLICH IDENTITY: for every u in C^2(closure of Omega) one has integral_Omega (x . grad u) Laplacian(u) dx = ((n-2)/2) integral_Omega |grad u|^2 dx - (1/2) integral_{boundary} (x . nu) |grad u|^2 dS + integral_{boundary} (x . grad u)(du/dnu) dS. POHOZAEV IDENTITY: if in addition u = 0 on the boundary of Omega and -Laplacian(u) = f(u) in Omega with f continuous and F(t) = integral_0^t f(s) ds, then, since on the boundary grad u = (du/dnu) nu, the two boundary terms collapse and one gets ((n-2)/2) integral_Omega |grad u|^2 dx + (1/2) integral_{boundary} (x . nu) |du/dnu|^2 dS = n integral_Omega F(u) dx. CONSEQUENCE (nonexistence): let n >= 3, let Omega be star-shaped with respect to the origin (x . nu >= 0 on the boundary) with C^1 boundary, and let f(u) = |u|^(p-1) u with p >= (n+2)/(n-2). Multiplying the equation by u gives integral |grad u|^2 = integral |u|^(p+1), while Pohozaev gives ((n-2)/2) integral |u|^(p+1) + (1/2) integral_{boundary}(x . nu)|du/dnu|^2 = (n/(p+1)) integral |u|^(p+1). Since p >= (n+2)/(n-2) is exactly n/(p+1) <= (n-2)/2, the boundary term is <= 0 while star-shapedness makes it >= 0; hence it vanishes and integral |u|^(p+1) = 0 for p > (n+2)/(n-2). In the critical case p = (n+2)/(n-2) the two bulk terms cancel identically and one concludes only that (x . nu)|du/dnu|^2 = 0 on the boundary; if Omega is strictly star-shaped (x . nu > 0) this forces du/dnu = 0 on the whole boundary and then u = 0 by the Hopf lemma or unique continuation. WHERE IT FAILS: star-shapedness is essential, not technical - on an annulus {a < |x| < b} in R^n there exist positive radial solutions of -Laplacian(u) = u^p vanishing on both boundary spheres for EVERY p > 1, including supercritical p (Kazdan-Warner). Regularity is also essential: the identity is proved for u in C^2 up to the boundary (it is valid for H^1_0 weak solutions only after elliptic regularity has upgraded them, which requires growth conditions on f), and the boundary must be regular enough for the divergence theorem. The origin matters: star-shapedness is with respect to the point used in the multiplier x . grad u.
Omega is bounded and open in R^n with C^1 (or piecewise C^1) boundary, so the divergence theorem applies
u is in C^2 up to the closure of Omega
for the Pohozaev form: u = 0 on the boundary, f is continuous, F(t) = integral_0^t f and F(0) = 0
for the nonexistence corollary: n >= 3, Omega star-shaped about the origin, f(u) = |u|^(p-1)u with p >= (n+2)/(n-2), and strict star-shapedness plus Hopf or unique continuation in the critical case

[Prop 33 of arXiv:2609.03653, 'The derived set of multiple star polylogarithms'] The map
\[
(b,z)\mapsto H_{{\bf k}(b)}(z)
\]
is jointly continuous on $(0,1]\times\mathcal{D}$, locally uniformly in $z$ on compact subsets of $\mathcal{D}$.
It extends continuously to the natural unit-circle parameter domain
\[
\Omega=\big((0,1]\times(S^1\setminus\{1\})\big)
\cup\big((0,\tfrac12)\times\{1\}\big).
\]
In particular, for $0<b_0<1/2$, the finite boundary value at $(b_0,1)$ is continuous under all approaches through $\Omega$.

[Thm 15 of arXiv:2609.03054, 'The classes of bivariate Schur and Herglotz matrix-valued rational functions: realizations'] Let $F(z) \in \mathbb{R}^{k\times l}(z)$ be a real rational matrix function that takes on contractive values for $z\in {\mathbb D}=\{ z \in{\mathbb C} : |z|<1\}$. Then $F(z)$ has a real contractive finite dimensional realization; that is, there exists a real contractive block matrix ${\scriptscriptstyle \begin{bmatrix} A & B \\ C & D \end{bmatrix}}\in{\mathbb R}^{(d{+}k)\times(d{+}l)}$ so that 
\begin{equation} F(z) = D +zC (I -zA)^{-1} B   ,\quad z\in {\mathbb D}. \end{equation} This realization can be chosen to be minimal, i.e., $$
\bigcap_{j=0}^\infty \ker CA^{d-1} = \{0\}, \quad \bigvee_{j=0}^{d-1} \operatorname{ Ran} A^jB = {\mathbb R}^d. $$
title: Thm 15 of arXiv:2609.03054

[Theorem 41 ($\mathscr{S}_L$ properties) of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Let $f \in \mathcal{B}_L^n$. Let $\emptyset \neq G = G^1 \times \cdots \times G^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, with all $G^k$ closed. Then 
   \begin{align*}
      \mathscr{S}_L(f,G) = &(\mathscr{S}_L(f_1,G^1),...,\mathscr{S}_L(f_n,G^n)) \\
      = &\Big(\inf \big(G^1 \cup [\sup G^1, \infty)\big)_{\geq \inf f_1^{-1}[s,1]},\\ &...,\inf \big(G^n \cup [\sup G^n, \infty)\big)_{\geq \inf f_n^{-1}[s,1]}\Big)
      \end{align*}
   has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
   \item $\mathscr{S}_L(f,G) \in \mathcal{T}_L(f)$
   \item $\forall k$, $P(\mathscr{S}_L(f_k,G^k) \leq t) = f_k \big( \sup \big(G^k \cup [\sup G^k, \infty)\big)_{\leq t} \big), \ \forall t \in \mathbb{R}$ (employing the convention $f_k(-\infty) = 0$)
   \item $\mathscr{S}_L(f_k,G^k)$ are left continuous
   \item $\mathscr{S}_L(f,G) :(0,1)^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n$ is the unique function which satisfies (i)-(iii)
   \item $\forall s_k \in (0,1)^n, \ \mathscr{S}_L(f_k,G^k)(s_k) \in G^k \cup [\sup G^k, +\infty)$
   \item $\forall s_k\in(0,1), \ \mathscr{S}_L(f_k,G^k)(s_k) \geq \inf f_k^{-1}[s_k,1], \ k=1,...,n$
   \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 3 (Action of $L^X$ on monomials) of arXiv:2606.00781, '2606.00781'] The generator $L^X$ acts on the $n$-th monomial $f_n(x):=x^n$ via
   \begin{equation} 
      L^Xf_n(x)\ =\ \sum_{k=1}^n \varphi(k,n)x^{n-k}-2\varphi(n)x^n,
      \qquad n\in\nz_0,
   \end{equation}
   where $\varphi(k,n)$ is defined via (\ref{lambda_rep}) and
   the total rate $\varphi(n)$ is defined via
   \begin{equation} 
      \varphi(n)
      \ :=\ \sum_{k=1} ^n\varphi(k,n)
      \ =\ dn+\kappa+\int_{(0,1)}\frac{1-(1-t)^n}{t}\,\Lambda({\rm d}t),
      \qquad n\in\nz_0,
   \end{equation}
   with drift $d:=\Lambda(\{0\})$ and killing rate $\kappa:=\Lambda(\{1\})$. In particular, $L^X$ acts on the identity $f_1$ via $L^Xf_1(x)=(1-2x)\Lambda([0,1])$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Action of $L^X$ on monomials

[Lemma 12 (Quantitative Khasminskii's lemma) of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Let $0\leq S\leq T$ and let $\xi(t)$ be a nonnegative measurable $(\sF_t)$-adapted process. Assume that for all $S\leq s\leq t\leq T$, 
   	\be 
   	\mE_s\bigg[\int_s^t\xi(r)dr\bigg]\leq \beta(s,t),
   	\ee
   	where $(s,t)\mapsto \beta(s,t)$ is a deterministic function on $\Delta([S,T])$ satisfying:
   	$\beta(t_1,t_2)\leq \beta(t_3,t_4)$ if $(t_1,t_2)\subset (t_3,t_4)$ and there exists $\delta_0>0$ such that
   	\be
   	 \sup_{S\leq s<t\leq T,|t-s|\leq \delta_0}\beta(s,t)\leq \lambda,~\lambda\geq 0. 
   	 \ee
   	 Then for any real number $\kappa<\lambda^{-1}$ if $\lambda\neq 0$, $\lambda^{-1}=\infty$ otherwise and any integer $m\geq 1$, 
   	\ce 
   	\|\int_S^T\xi(r)dr\|_{L_m(\Omega|\sF_S)}^m\leq m!\beta(S,T)^m,
   	\de
   	and there exists positive constant $N$ only depending on $\delta_0$ such that
   	\ce 
   	 \mE_S\bigg[\exp\bigg(\kappa\int_S^T\xi(r)dr\bigg)\bigg]\leq \bigg(\frac{1}{1-\lambda\kappa}\bigg)^N.
   	 \de 
   	 We furthermore suppose that there exists $\gamma>0$ and a continuous control $\sW$ on $\Delta([S,T])$ such that $\beta(s,t)\leq \sW(s,t)^\gamma$ for $(s,t)\in \Delta([S,T])$. Then for every $\lambda>0$,
   	 \be
   	 \mE_S\bigg[\exp\bigg(\kappa\int_S^T\xi(r)dr\bigg)\bigg] \leq 2^{1+(2\kappa)^{1/\gamma}\sW(S,T)}.
   	 \ee

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: in ‖e^{itΔ}f‖_{L^q_t L^r_x(R×R^n)} ≤ C‖f‖_{L²} the exponents must satisfy 2/q + n/r = n/2 exactly, and q ≥ 2 (and r ≥ 2). None of these can be relaxed, so an argument that 'interpolates' to a pair off the scaling line, or that uses a short-time-looking pair with q < 2, is wrong. Scaling: for f_λ(x) = f(λx) one has (e^{itΔ}f_λ)(x) = (e^{iλ²tΔ}f)(λx), hence ‖e^{itΔ}f_λ‖_{L^q_t L^r_x} = λ^{−2/q − n/r}‖e^{itΔ}f‖_{L^q_t L^r_x} while ‖f_λ‖_{L²} = λ^{−n/2}‖f‖_{L²}. If 2/q + n/r ≠ n/2 the ratio of the two sides is λ^{n/2 − 2/q − n/r}, which is unbounded as λ → 0 or λ → ∞ for any fixed f ≠ 0. So an estimate off the scaling line fails for every nonzero f. Necessity of q ≥ 2 (the case r > 2; on the scaling line r = 2 forces q = ∞, so there is nothing to prove there): take φ ∈ S(R^n) and f_N = Σ_{k=1}^N e^{−i t_k Δ}φ with t_1 ≪ t_2 ≪ ... ≪ t_N separated enough that Σ_{j≠k}|t_k − t_j|^{−n(1/2−1/r)} is small for every k. Since |⟨e^{isΔ}φ, φ⟩| ≤ (4π|s|)^{−n/2}‖φ‖_{L¹}² → 0, the summands are almost orthogonal in L² and ‖f_N‖_{L²}² ≈ N‖φ‖²_{L²}; and for t within O(1) of t_k the dispersive estimate makes every term but the k-th small in L^r_x, so ‖e^{itΔ}f_N‖_{L^q_t L^r_x} ≳ N^{1/q}‖e^{itΔ}φ‖_{L^q_t([−1,1]) L^r_x}. The ratio is ≳ N^{1/q − 1/2}, unbounded when q < 2. Known excluded endpoints, where the pair is on the scaling line and q = 2 but the estimate is still false: (q,r) = (2,∞) for Schrödinger in n = 2 (Montgomery-Smith), and (q,r) = (2,∞) for the wave equation in n = 3 (Klainerman–Machedon). Also for the wave equation the Lebesgue-space estimate is stated with r < ∞; at r = ∞ one must pass to Besov spaces.
title: Pitfall: A Strichartz Estimate Needs the Scaling Relation and q ≥ 2

body: [Lem lem-geo-slice of arXiv:2510.26123, 'Directed distances in bipolar-oriented triangulations:\\ exact exponents and scaling limit'] Let $G_k$ be the (directed) submap of $M_{0,\infty}$ consisting of the vertices, edges, and faces of $M_{0,\infty}$ which lie between $P_{x_{k-1}}([1,\theta_k^-])$ and $P_{x_k}([1,\theta_k])$, including the vertices and edges which lie on these ${\operatorname{XDP}}$ geodesic segments. We call $G_k$ an \textbf{${\operatorname{XDP}}$ geodesic slice} (see Figure~(fig-geo-slice of the paper)). The maps $\{G_k\}_{k\in\mathbbm Z}$ are independent. Furthermore, the maps $\{G_k\}_{k \geq 1}$ all have the same law, and the maps $\{G_k\}_{k \leq 0}$ all have the same law.

[Prop gamma of arXiv:2608.12954, 'Rainbow percolation'] Fix $\gamma>0$, $\lambda>0$ and $\beta>0$, and consider the
weight-dependent random connection model with kernel $(t\vee s)^{\gamma}$
and profile function $\rho=\1_{[0,1]}$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If $\gamma<1$, then almost surely every connected component is
finite; hence $\beta_c=\infty$ at every intensity.
\item If $\gamma>1$, then almost surely an infinite connected component
exists; hence $\beta_c=0$ at every intensity.
\end{enumerate}

[Cor 5 of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] Let $L(x,{\d} y)$ be a kernel on $E\times\mathscr{B}(E)$.
Suppose that the jumping measure $J$ satisfies $J({\d} x{\d} y)\leq D_2L(x,{\d} y){\m}({\d} x)$ for some $D_2>0$. 
Let ${\sf d}$ be a distance function consistent with the given topology. Assume 
that there exists $\beta\in]0,+\infty[$ such that 
\begin{align}
M_{\beta}:={\m}\text{\rm-ess-sup}_{x\in E}\int_E(1\land {\sf d}(x,y)^{\beta})L(x,{\d} y)<\infty.
\end{align} 
Then, for $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{\loc}\cap L^p(E;{\m})$ with $p\in[1,+\infty]$ and $v\in D(\mathscr{E})_c\cap L^{\infty}(E;{\m})$, 
the quantity $\mathscr{E}_{\alpha}(u,v)$ for $\alpha\geq0$ is well-defined. Moreover, 
for $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}\cap L^p(E;{\m})$ with $p\in[1,+\infty]$ and $v\in D(\mathscr{E})_c\cap L^{\infty}(E;{\m})$, 
the quantity $\mathscr{E}(u,v)$ is well-defined.

[Lemma 9 (Borel closure of probabilistic limits) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let \(S,Y\) be Polish spaces, let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on
\(S\), and let \(\Gamma_m:S\to Y\) be Borel maps converging in
\(\mu\)-probability to a unique \(Y\)-valued limit.  Then a deterministic
subsequence converges pointwise on a Borel set of full \(\mu\)-measure;
extending that limit arbitrarily off the set gives a Borel version
\(\Gamma:S\to Y\).

[Lemma 38 (Pigato stopping time for the remainder covariance) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Let
\[
    Q=\int_0^1G(u)G(u)^\top\,du,
    \qquad q_0=\lambda_{\min}(Q)>0.
\]
For $0<\xi\le1$ define the block matrix process
\[
    \rho_s^{\delta,t,\xi}
    =
    \left(
        \xi^{-(\ell+j-1)}
        \int_0^s
        \widetilde R_{t,u}^{\delta,\ell}
        \left(\widetilde R_{t,u}^{\delta,j}\right)^\top du
    \right)_{1\le \ell,j\le3}
\]
and the stopping time
\[
    S_\xi
    =
    \inf\left\{0\le s\le t:\
        \left\|\rho_s^{\delta,t,\xi}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
        \ge q_0/4\right\}\wedge t ,
\]
with the convention $\inf\varnothing=\infty$.
For every $N\ge1$, after decreasing $t_0$ if necessary,
\[
    \sup_{0\le\delta\le1,\ z\in K_0,\ 0<t\le t_0}
    \mathbb P_z(S_\xi<t\xi)
    \le C_N\xi^N,
    \qquad 0<\xi\le1 .
\]
title: Pigato stopping time for the remainder covariance

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2511.14379, 'Stability of storage processes with general release rates'] Assume $\textbf{(C1)-(C3)}$ (or $\textbf{(\={C}1)-(\={C}2)}$ and  $\textbf{(C3)}$ in the case when $\bar\upnu(0)<\infty$), that $\process{X}$ is  $\uppsi$-irreducible and aperiodic, and that every compact set is petite for $\process{X}$. 
	Further, assume  $\int_1^\infty \frac{\D u}{r(u)}<\infty$ and $\limsup_{u\to\infty}\int_0^\infty \frac{\bar\upnu(v)}{r(u+v)}\D v<1$.
	Then the process $\process{X}$ is uniformly ergodic.
	The tail behavior of the invariant measure is as follows.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[(i)] (Sub-geometric upper bounds) If it holds that $\bar\upnu(u)>0$ for all $u>0$, the mapping $u\mapsto  r(u)/u^{1+\epsilon}\bar\upnu(u)$ is non-decreasing for all sufficiently large $u$,
		and 
		$$
		\limsup_{u\to\infty}\frac{u^{1+\epsilon}\bar\upnu(u)}{r(u)}\int_0^\infty\frac{\bar\upnu(v)}{(u+v)^{1+\epsilon}\bar\upnu(u+v)}\D v<1
		$$ for some $\epsilon>0$,
		then 
		$$\limsup_{u\to\infty}\frac{r(u)}{u^{1+\epsilon}\bar\upnu(u)}\bar\uppi(u)<\infty.$$
		\item[(ii)] (Exponential upper bounds) If $\lim_{u\to\infty}r(u)=\infty$  and $\limsup_{u\to\infty}\E^{cu}\bar\upnu(u)<\infty$, then for every $\epsilon\in(0,c)$ it holds that $$\limsup_{u\to\infty}r(u)\E^{(c-\epsilon)u}\bar\uppi(u)<\infty.$$
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For every integer m >= 1 there are two different probability laws on {0, ..., m} with the same binomial moments F_r = E[binom(N, r)] for r = 0, ..., m - 1 and different F_m. For instance p_k = binom(m, k) 2^(-m) and q_k = binom(m, k) (2^(-m) + epsilon (-1)^k) with 0 < epsilon < 2^(-m); then F_m(q) - F_m(p) = epsilon (-1)^m. So the law of a count on {0, ..., m} is determined by F_0, ..., F_m but not by F_0, ..., F_(m-1).
m >= 1

body:
[Theorem 256 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Assume $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ is realized by a bipartite gluing graph $\mathsf{G}$, with bipartition $\epsilon : [m] \rightarrow \{\pm 1\}$. Then the vector $\boldsymbol{v} = \epsilon_1\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_1}$ has $\mathfrak{G}$-orbit $\{\epsilon_i\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i}\,\,|\,\,i\in [m]\}$, this orbit is good (\textit{cf.} Definition~\ref{def:goodor}) and has minimal size $m = \textnormal{rank}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}) + 1$. For any $i \in [m]$ and $h \in [H]$ we have
\[
T^{(h)}(\epsilon_i \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i}) = \left\{\begin{array}{ccc}  \epsilon_i \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i} && \textnormal{if}\,\,h \notin \mathcal{H}_i, \\[0.6ex] \epsilon_{i'_h}\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_{i'_h}} && \textnormal{if}\,\,h \in \mathcal{H}_i. \end{array}\right.
\]
The genus of the spectral curve $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ is $\mathsf{g}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = \textnormal{corank}(\boldsymbol{\Theta})$ and the group $\hat{\mathfrak{G}}$ is the Weyl group of type $A_{m - 1}$ (\textit{i.e.} the symmetric group in $m$ elements).

The bidifferential $\mathcal{B}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}}$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:Bcont} is defined on $\Sigma^{[2],\circ}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} \times \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ and can simply be denoted $\mathcal{B}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$. Its matrix of biresidues is \textbf{\foreignlanguage{russian}{B}} = $\textnormal{\textbf{Id}} - \boldsymbol{1}$, and the bidifferential itself is equal to
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{B}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = \mathcal{B}^{\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\mathcal{L}} - \frac{\dd z_1\dd z_2}{(z_1 - z_2)^2},
\end{equation}
where $(z_1,z_2) = Z_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}}$, the Lagrangian $\mathcal{L} \subset H_1(\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\amsmathbb{Z})$ is spanned by cycles around the components of the gluing locus (\textit{cf.} Definition~\ref{def:spcurv1}), and $\mathcal{B}^{\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\mathcal{L}}$ is the fundamental bidifferential of Section~\ref{sec:fund02}.

From the analytic continuation of first-kind functions in Proposition~\ref{Lem:Holo1form}, we get a linear isomorphism
\[
\begin{array}{ccc} \textnormal{Ker}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}) & \longrightarrow & H^1(\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\amsmathbb{C}) \\
\boldsymbol{v}' & \longmapsto & \mathfrak{u}_{\boldsymbol{v};\boldsymbol{v}'} \end{array}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 256 of arXiv:2601.16377

body:
[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.31168, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality for surfaces in every codimension'] Let $m \geq 2$ and consider a vector field $S \in C_c^{\infty}(\bR^m;\bR^m)$.
For every sufficiently small $\tau> 0$, there exists a finite set $F_{\tau} \subset \bR^m$ and
\[
S_{\tau} \in C_c^{\infty}(\bR^m; \bR^m), \qquad \eta_{\tau} \in C_c^{\infty} (\bR^m), \qquad U_{\tau} \in C^{\infty}(\bR^m \setminus F_{\tau} ; \bS^{m-1})
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item We have $S_{\tau} = \eta_{\tau} U_{\tau}$ for $\eta_{\tau} \geq 0$, $U_{\tau}$ is a unit vector field, and, as $\tau \downarrow 0$,
    \[
    S_{\tau} \to S, \qquad \textup{div} \, S_{\tau} \to \textup{div} \, S \quad \text{in } \; L^1(\bR^m).
    \]
    \item We have $U_{\tau} = e$ outside a compact set, where $e \in \bS^{m-1}$ is any prescribed vector.
    Also, for every $p \in F_{\tau}$, there exist $r_p > 0$ and $Q_p \in O(m)$ such that
    \[
    U_{\tau}(x) = Q_p \frac{x-p}{|x-p|} \quad \text{for } \; 0 < |x-p| < r_p.
    \]
    The sign $\det Q_p = \pm 1$ is the local degree of the singularity.
    \item For $m=2$, depending on the index $\pm 1$ of the point $p$, we can moreover arrange
    \[
    U_{\tau}(z) = i \frac{z-p}{|z-p|} \quad \text{if $p$ has index $1$}, \qquad U_{\tau}(z) = i \frac{\overline{z-p}}{|z-p|} \quad \text{if $p$ has index $-1$}.
    \]
    Moreover, all but finitely many maximal integral curves of $U_{\tau}$ are defined for all time and are disjoint from $F_{\tau}$.
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 4 of arXiv:2608.00813, 'Convex order, log-convexity and Moments of Averages of Random Variables'] Let $a,b\in\z_{>0}^n$ be partitions of the same integer such that $a\maj b$.
Then for $p \in (-\infty,0]\cup [1,\infty)$ we have
\[
\prod_{j=1}^n\beta_{a_j}(p)
\leq
\prod_{j=1}^n\beta_{b_j}(p).
\]
For $p\in (0,1)$ the inequality is reversed. In particular, the sequence $(\be_k(p))_{k\geq 1}$ is log-convex for $p \in (-\infty,0]\cup[1,\infty)$ and log-concave for $p\in (0,1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 4 of arXiv:2608.00813

[Definition D:Noise of arXiv:2412.03521, 'On ergodic properties of stochastic PDEs'] In equation~(equation E:NS-vort of the paper), the finite dimensional noise $QW_t$ is defined
  as follows: we start from a $\mathbb{R}^m$-valued Wiener process $W$ defined
  on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$. Recall that $f_k$
  is given in~(equation D:f_k of the paper) and denote by $\{e_n; n=1,\ldots,m\}$ the standard
  basis of $\mathbb{R}^m$.  Define $Q:\mathbb{R}^m\to{H}$ by $Qe_n = q_n
  f_{k_n}$, where the $q_n$ are some strictly positive numbers, and the wave
  numbers $k_n$ are given by the set $\mathcal{Z}_0$. Then for $t \ge 0$ and $x
  \in \mathbb{T}^2$ we have
  \begin{align}
    QW_t(x)=\sum_{n=1}^m q_nW^n_tf_{k_n}(x).
  \end{align}
  Notice that $QW_t$ is an element of $H=L^2_0(\mathbb{T}^2)$.

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.24549, 'Persistent Cross Entropy'] Let $D_X, D_Y$ be nonempty finite persistence diagrams.
There exists $C_X>0$ so that the induced probability satisfies the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\textit{\roman*}),leftmargin=2em,itemsep=0.4em]
\item The unexplained mass vanishes as $D_Y$ approaches $D_X$:
$$
p_X^Y(\partial)\leq
C_X W_1(D_X,D_Y)^2.
$$

\item For fixed $D_X$, the induced probability is stable under changes in
$D_Y$; for any nonempty finite persistence diagram $D_{Y'}$,
$$
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p_X^Y,p_X^{Y'})
\leq
C_X W_1(D_Y,D_{Y'}).
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.24549

[Definition H-reduced graph of arXiv:2506.06559, 'Bi-infinite incipient cluster in high dimensions'] Let $G$ be a multigraph, we say that an edge $\{x,y\}$ is \emph{H-reducible} if $x$ and $y$ both have an edge degree at least 3 in $G$ and $x$, $y$ are only connected by one edge. 

We define a multigraph $\tilde{G}$, called \emph{H-reduction of $G$ by $\{x,y\}$}, in the following manner:
\begin{itemize}
\item if $x$ and $y$ have degree 3, then $V(\tilde{G})=V(G)\setminus \{x,y\}$ and $E(\tilde{G})=E(G) \setminus (\{\{x,z\}; x\sim_G z\} \cup \{\{y,z\}; y\sim_G z\}) \cup \{e_{x\setminus y}, e_{y \setminus x}\}$ with $e_{x\setminus y}=\{z_1, z_2\}$ where $z_1,z_2$ are the neighbours of $x$ which are not $y$ (and a symmetrical definition of $e_{y\setminus x}$)
\item if $x$ has degree 3, $y$ has degree at least 4, then then $V(\tilde{G})=V(G)\setminus \{x\}$ and $E(\tilde{G})=E(G) \setminus (\{\{x,z\}; z\sim_G z\} ) \cup \{e_{x\setminus y}\}$.
\item if $x$ and $y$ both have degree at least 4, then  $V(\tilde{G})=V(G)$ and $E(\tilde{G})=E(G)\setminus \{x,y\}$.
\end{itemize}
title: H-reduced graph

[Corollary cor:SA-JSQ of arXiv:2607.13748, 'Load Balancing with Individually Heterogeneous Servers'] For the JFSQ system, $\eta^{\mathrm{JFSQ},n}\stackrel{f}{\rightarrow} \eta^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}$ as given in Proposition~(prop:priority_idleness of the paper) and $\hat{\alpha}_1^{\mathrm{JFSQ},n}(n^{1/2}\cdot)\Rightarrow \iota(\cdot)\times \delta_{\mu_{\max}}$. Moreover, if $\xi_i(0) = \delta_{\mu_{\max}}X_i(0)$ for all $i \geq 2$, then $\mathbf{X}^{\mathrm{JFSQ}, n} \Rightarrow \mathbf{X}^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}$, where $\mathbf{X}^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}$ is the unique solution of
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber X_1^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(t) & = X_1(0) - (\varsigma + \nu)t + \sqrt{2} W(t)\\
        &\qquad\qquad\qquad- \mu_{\min} \int_0^t X_1^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(s) \, ds + \mu_{\max} \int_0^t X_2^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(s) \, ds - U_1^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(t), \\
        X_2^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(t) & = X_2(0) + U_1^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(t) - \mu_{\max} \int_0^t X_2^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(s) \, ds + \mu_{\max} \int_0^t X_3^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(s) \, ds, \\
        X_i^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(t) & = X_i(0) - \mu_{\max} \int_0^t X_i^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(s) \, ds + \mu_{\max} \int_0^t X_{i+1}^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(s) \, ds, \quad \text{for all } i \geq 3,
    \end{align}
    where $U_1^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}\in \mathbb{D}_{\mathbb{R}_+}[0,\infty)$ is a non-decreasing function with $U_1^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(0)=0$ and satisfies 
    \begin{align*}
        \int_0^\infty \mathbb{I}(X_1^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(s)<0)\,dU_1^{\mathrm{JFSQ}}(s) = 0.
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Put sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)) and E_good={||Z_0||_F<=4, sigma_min(E^T Z_0)>=sigma_0}. This right-orthogonally invariant event has probability at least 2/5, using the settled Gaussian singular-value estimate of C07. For 0<rho<=1/100 and S=10 log(100/(sigma_0 rho)), on E_good the flow is global, ||Z(s)||_F<=4 and min_{O in O(2)}||Z(S)-E Lambda^(1/2)O||_F<rho/2. Conditional on E_good and either determinant branch, the angle of the orthogonal polar factor of Lambda^(-1/2)E^T Z(S) is uniform. This is not an entry guarantee or failure probability for exact DDPM GD: finite-step comparison, free centroid and subsequent unrestricted angular tracking remain open.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:92b7f4c445312ae0f1543ef32880eb76688589f6d22f03c71cf972636381a685","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/92/92b7f4c445312ae0f1543ef32880eb76688589f6d22f03c71cf972636381a685.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ba6f0e3af1f9cf70660d7ca1b6bbc70a1aa812bf95b8a3cbaf03087d57123297","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c16","bundle_id":"population.t309-anisotropic-covariance-gaussian-entry-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and covariance gradient flows","draft":"w721/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:anisotropic-covariance-factor-flow-gaussian-random-entry-uniform-phase","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own work draft; T309-w721-C16 v1; proof (unaudited); Target 2 route 12 entry substep.

# Quantitative Gaussian entry for the anisotropic covariance-factor surrogate

This supplies the covariance-surrogate random-entry estimate missing from C12. It uses C07's Gaussian singular-value event as settled input, without re-proving its probability. It does not compare unrestricted exact DDPM GD with this surrogate, release the centroid, or prove a full-GD failure probability. No target resolution or novelty finding is asserted.

## Statement

Let d>=2, E^T E=I_2, Lambda=diag(1,9), D=E Lambda E^T. Let Z(s) solve

    Z_dot=(D-ZZ^T)Z,

from a d-by-2 matrix Z_0 with iid N(0,1/d) entries. Put sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)). Define the event

    E_good={||Z_0||_F<=4, sigma_min(E^T Z_0)>=sigma_0}.

It has probability at least 2/5. For every 0<rho<=1/100, set

    L=100/(sigma_0 rho), S=10 log L.

On E_good the flow exists globally, ||Z(s)||_F<=4, and

    min_{O in O(2)} ||Z(S)-E Lambda^(1/2) O||_F <rho/2.    (1)

Conditional on E_good and either determinant branch, the angle of the orthogonal polar factor of Lambda^(-1/2)E^T Z(S) is uniform. The time S=O(log d+log(1/rho)); all constants here are independent of d. This is an exact deterministic-flow and Gaussian-initialization statement, not a training experiment or a claim that the DDPM trajectory equals this flow.

## 1. Global bounded flow

Set Q=ZZ^T, R=tr Q=||Z||_F^2. Then

    R_dot=2 tr(DQ)-2||Q||_F^2
         <=2||Q||_F(sqrt(82)-||Q||_F).

The rank of Q is at most two, hence ||Q||_F>=R/sqrt(2). At R>=16 this is larger than sqrt(82), since 16^2/2=128>82. Thus the derivative points inward at the norm-4 boundary and beyond it. On ||Z_0||<=4 the solution cannot exit this ball. The polynomial ODE is locally Lipschitz and bounded solutions extend globally. This bound does not use an incorrect isotropic replacement for the largest eigenvalue 9.

## 2. Exact covariance formula

Write A=E^T Z_0, B=(I-EE^T)Z_0. On E_good, A is invertible, ||A||_F,||B||_F<=4 and sigma_min(A)>=sigma_0. Define

    W(s)=E exp(Lambda s) A+B,
    H(s)=I+A^T diag(e^(2s)-1,(e^(18s)-1)/9) A+2s B^T B.

Then H=I+2 integral_0^s W(u)^T W(u) du is positive definite and

    Q(s)=W(s) H(s)^(-1) W(s)^T.                        (2)

Differentiating gives Q_dot=DQ+QD-2Q^2 and Q(0)=Z_0 Z_0^T. The actual covariance has this same Riccati equation, so uniqueness gives (2). No identity Z=W H^(-1/2) for the actual factor trajectory is assumed.

Let Q_pp=E^T Q E. Inverting its planar factor in (2) gives

    Q_pp^(-1)=Lambda^(-1)+T(s),
    T(s)=exp(-Lambda s) A^(-T)
       [I+2s B^T B-A^T Lambda^(-1) A]
          A^(-1) exp(-Lambda s).

Consequently

    ||T(s)||_op<=e^(-2s) sigma_0^(-2)(17+32s).         (3)

All inverses are legitimate: A is invertible on E_good and H is positive definite for every nonnegative time.

## 3. Planar and perpendicular entry errors

At S, (3) and sigma_0^(-2)=L^2 rho^2/10000 give

    ||T(S)||<=rho^2(17+320 log L)/(10000 L^18)
              <=337 rho^2/(10000 L^17)<rho^2/25,       (4)

using L>=1 and log L<=L. Our actual parameters give S>=1. In particular ||T||<1/18. Matrix inversion then yields

    ||Q_pp-Lambda||_op
       <=81||T||/(1-9||T||)<=162||T||.                (5)

Let C=Lambda^(-1/2)E^T Z(S), and O its orthogonal polar factor. Its singular values are positive. The inequality |sqrt(x)-1|<=|x-1| for x>=0 gives

    ||C-O||_F<=||CC^T-I||_F
                  <=||Q_pp-Lambda||_F.

Multiplying by Lambda^(1/2), and using (5), bounds the planar factor error by

    ||E^T Z(S)-Lambda^(1/2)O||_F
          <=486 sqrt(2)||T||<700||T||<=28rho^2.         (6)

For the perpendicular part, (e^(18s)-1)/9 >= e^(2s)-1 for s>=0; this follows by comparing the corresponding integrals of 2e^(18u) and 2e^(2u). Therefore

    H(s)>=(e^(2s)-1) A^T A.

For s>=1 this gives

    ||(I-EE^T)Z(s)||_F^2
       =tr(B H(s)^(-1) B^T)
       <=32 sigma_0^(-2)e^(-2s).

At S the last expression is at most 32rho^2/(10000 L^18)<rho^2/100. Combining with (6) and rho<=1/100 bounds the total factor error by

    28rho^2+rho/10 <=(19/50)rho<rho/2.

This proves (1). Orthogonality of planar and perpendicular errors could give a slightly tighter bound, but is not needed.

## 4. Probability and the correct phase symmetry

C07's settled Gaussian good event has probability at least 2/5 and implies both ||Z_0||<=4 and sigma_min(E^T Z_0)>=sigma_0. It is therefore a subset of E_good, proving the stated probability. We do not condition on C07's particular column-based construction of that event, since that construction need not be invariant under right rotations.

E_good itself IS invariant under Z_0 -> Z_0 O for every O in O(2), because Frobenius norm and singular values are unchanged. The Gaussian law has the same right invariance. The ODE is right equivariant: (ZO)(ZO)^T=ZZ^T, and uniqueness implies Z(s;Z_0 O)=Z(s;Z_0)O. Thus C at time S right-rotates in the same manner. Its left polar decomposition C=S_C O_C is unique because C is invertible; right rotation preserves S_C and rotates O_C. Rotations preserve either determinant branch and act transitively on its circle. The conditional angular law on each nonnull branch is therefore uniform. Reflection interchanges the two branches, and both have positive probability on this invariant event.

This is right-factor symmetry of the covariance surrogate. It is not a physical-plane rotational symmetry of the anisotropic teacher, and it is not a symmetry of the component-identifying DDPM correction. Keeping those distinct is necessary for the eventual probability-transfer argument.

## Remaining transfer

This result supplies a norm-bounded logarithmic-time surrogate entry estimate and the invariant event needed for its uniform phase. To connect it to C15 one must still compare actual finite-step DDPM GD over this entry interval, release centering and planarity, and control their accumulated angular effects. The free-centroid and extra-direction estimates for the equilateral case do not automatically establish those anisotropic statements. No product of independent success probabilities, full-GD basin mass, or annealing obstruction is claimed here.

Let $\Sigma$ be a spacelike hypersurface with timelike unit normal $e_0$ in a spacetime $(\bar{M}, \bar{g})$. For any normal variation with variation vector field $V = \phi e_0$ compactly supported on $\Sigma$, the second variation of the volume functional $\operatorname{Vol}(\Sigma_t)$ at $t=0$ is given by $\left. \frac{d^2}{dt^2} \operatorname{Vol}(\Sigma_t) \right|_{t=0} = - \int_\Sigma \left( |\nabla \phi|^2 - (|h|^2 + \operatorname{Ric}(e_0, e_0)) \phi^2 \right) d\mu_g$. In particular, when $\operatorname{Ric}(e_0, e_0) \ge 0$, any maximal hypersurface ($H=0$) strictly maximizes volume among nearby compact perturbations.

[Lemma 1 ({\cite[Lemma 2.1) of arXiv:2608.06232, 'The mean absolute deviation of the classical discrete distributions:\\ collapse identities'] {elezovic_mad}}]
	Let $\lambda_j,\mu_k>0$ and $u_j,v_k\in\R$, where $1\le j\le\rho$ and
	$1\le k\le\sigma$.  Put
	\[
		F(x)=\frac{\prod_j\Gamma(\lambda_jx+u_j)}
			{\prod_k\Gamma(\mu_kx+v_k)} .
	\]
	If $\Lambda:=\sum_j\lambda_j-\sum_k\mu_k=0$, then, as $x\to\infty$,
	\begin{equation}
		\log F(x)\sim \Theta\,x+U\log x+K
		+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n(n+1)}\,S_{n+1}\,\frac{1}{x^{n}},
	\end{equation}
	where
	\[
		\Theta=\sum_j\lambda_j\log\lambda_j-\sum_k\mu_k\log\mu_k,\qquad
		U=\sum_j\Bigl(u_j-\tfrac12\Bigr)-\sum_k\Bigl(v_k-\tfrac12\Bigr),
	\]
	\[
		K=\sum_j\Bigl(u_j-\tfrac12\Bigr)\log\lambda_j
		 -\sum_k\Bigl(v_k-\tfrac12\Bigr)\log\mu_k+\frac{\rho-\sigma}{2}\log2\pi,
	\]
	\begin{equation}
		S_{n+1}=\sum_{j}\lambda_j^{-n}B_{n+1}(u_j)-\sum_{k}\mu_k^{-n}B_{n+1}(v_k),
	\end{equation}
	and, for every $M$, the remainder after $M$ series terms is $O(x^{-M-1})$, uniformly for the
	shifts in compact sets and the scalings in compact subsets of $(0,\infty)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 16 (The PF continuity equation is not well posed) of arXiv:2607.25685, 'Mimicking diffusion processes with differential equations'] Let $v$ be given by \eqref{eq:cev} and $T>0$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] $v\notin L^1_\loc\big([0,T]\times\R\big)$. The weak
formulation of Definition~\ref{def:class} is not meaningful for general
$u\in L^\infty((0,T);L^1\cap L^\infty)$, and assumptions \textup{(R1)}, \textup{(R3)} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:DL} fail.
\item[\textup{(ii)}] For every $x_0$ with $|x_0|\ge1$ there is \emph{no} absolutely
continuous $Z:[0,T]\to\R$ with $Z(0)=x_0$ and $Z(t)=x_0+\int_0^tv(Z(s),s)\,\dd s$.
Consequently no regular Lagrangian flow exists: condition \textup{(i)} of
Definition~\ref{def:rlf} fails on the set $\{|x|>1\}$.
\item[\textup{(iii)}] For every $x\in(-1,1)$ there is exactly one such solution, namely
\eqref{eq:cequantile}, and\\ $Z(t,\cdot):(-1,1)\to\R$ is a smooth increasing bijection.
\item[\textup{(iv)}] The Cauchy problem fails to be solvable
for any initial condition $u_0\in L^1\cap L^\infty$  with
$u_0=0$ a.e.\ on $[-1,1]$: there is no
narrowly continuous family of probability measures $(\mu_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ with
$\mu_0=u_0\Leb$ solving \eqref{eq:cont} and satisfying the integrability
hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:super}.  
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The PF continuity equation is not well posed

[Proposition 47 of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] There exists a constant $C=C(\delta,\varepsilon,M_0)>0$ such that for any $1\le m\le M_0$, conditionally on $X_{h^*-\lfloor \frac12 \delta n \rfloor}=m$,
    \[
    h^*- \lfloor \tfrac12 \delta n \rfloor-T \;\ge_{\rm sto}\; {\rm Geometric}\bigg(\frac Cn\bigg)\wedge \frac14 \delta n.
    \]
    Consequently, for any $\eta>0$, there exists $c_0=c_0(C,\delta,\eta)\in(0,\delta/2)$ such that for all $1\le m\le M_0$,  
    \begin{align}
        \p_n\!\Big(T \le  h^* - \left\lfloor \tfrac12 \delta n \right\rfloor - \lfloor c_0 n \rfloor \,\Big|\, X_{h^*-\lfloor \frac12 \delta n \rfloor}=m\Big) 
        \ge 1-\tfrac\eta4, 
        \quad \forall\, n\ge 1.

[Definition 12 ($\AS$) of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] Define the random independent set $\hat{I}$ in $\Qp$ via the following procedure.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Let $\cH$ be $\cE$ or $\cO$, with probabilities proportional to $e^{\Psi^\cE}$ and $e^{\Psi^\cO}$ respectively.
		\item Let $\tilde{S}$ denote a subset of $\cH$ which includes each $v \in \cH$ independently with probability
		$\fr{2^{-\N(v)}}{1 + 2^{-\N(v)}}$.
		\item If $\tilde{S}$ contains any triple of vertices which is \emph{2-linked},
        terminate the algorithm with a result of failure.
		Otherwise, remove all dimers from $\tilde{S}$ and let $S_1$ denote the resulting set of well-separated singletons (which share no neighbors).
		\item Let $S_2$ denote a collection of dimers constructed by including each $\{u,v\} \in \Dim^\cH$ independently with probability
		$\fr{2^{-\N(\{u,v\})}}{1 + 2^{-\N(\{u,v\})}}$.
		\item If any neighbor of a dimer in $S_2$ also neighbors a vertex in $S_1$, {or if any pair of dimers in $S_2$ overlap or share a neighbor,}
        terminate the algorithm with a result of failure.
		Otherwise, let $\hat{S} = S_1 \cup S_2$.
		\item Let $\hat{I}$ denote the independent set with $\hat{I} \cap \cH = \hat{S}$ and with every vertex in $\Q \setminus \cH$
		which does not neighbor $\hat{S}$ included independently with probability $\fr{1}{2}$ each.
	\end{enumerate}

[Definition def-thin-disk of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $W\in(0, \frac{\gamma^2}{2})$. 
	    Sample $(\mathcal{W}, T) \sim \mathcal{M}^\mathrm{wed}(W) \times (1-\frac{2}{\gamma^2}W)^{-2}\textup{Leb}_{\mathbb{R}_+}$, and write $\mathcal{W} = \{(u, \mathcal{D}_u)\}$. The \emph{weight $W$ quantum disk} is the concatenation of the quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u \: : \: u \leq T\}$ according to the ordering induced by $u$. Its left (resp.\ right) boundary length is the sum of the left (resp.\ right) boundary lengths of its constituent $\mathcal{D}_u$.
	    We define the infinite measure ${\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2}(W)$ to be the law of the weight $W$ quantum disk.
	    For $x\in [0,T]$, the \emph{quantum cut point measure} assigns  mass
	    $x$ to the collection of cut points between the quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u:u\leq x\}$.
title: Definition def-thin-disk of arXiv:2411.19810

Write L_tr = sum_i s_i (y_i - yhat_i)^2 for the weighted training loss and L_te = sum_i s_i (y_i* - yhat_i)^2 for the same loss on an independent copy y* of y at the same design. Then E[L_te] - E[L_tr] = 2 sum_i s_i^2 sigma_i^2 x_i'(X'SX)^(-1) x_i = 2 tr( (X'SX)^(-1) X' S^2 Sigma X ), where Sigma = diag(sigma_i^2). No distributional assumption beyond independence and finite second moments is used.

[Lemma of arXiv:2412.06615, 'A family of log-correlated Gaussian processes'] ~
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item
For each $\epsilon>0$, the process $\{\wt G_t\topp\epsilon\}_{t\ge0}$ is a centered Gaussian process with
\[
{\rm{Cov}}\pp{\wt G\topp\epsilon_s,\wt G\topp\epsilon_t} = \int_0^{\epsilon^{-1}}\frac{e^{-2r|t-s|} - e^{-2r(t+s)}}r{\rm d} r. 
\]
\item For each $\epsilon>0$, we have
\[
{\rm{Cov}}\pp{G\topp\epsilon(f),G\topp\epsilon(g)} = \int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty f(s)g(t)\int_0^{\epsilon^{-1}}\frac{e^{-2r|t-s|}-e^{-2r(t+s)}}r{\rm d} r{\rm d} s{\rm d} t, f,g\in{\mathcal F}_0.
\]
In particular, $ \int_0^\infty \wt G_t\topp\epsilon f(t){\rm d} t\Rightarrow G(f)$ 
as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ for all $f\in{\mathcal F}_0$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2412.06615, 'A family of log-correlated Gaussian processes'

\[
 \partial_tv+\Div_x(v\otimes v-B\otimes B)+\nabla p_{\mathrm R}=0
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal D'((0,T)\times\Rn).
\]

[Theorem 36 (Negligible resets give the ordinary Gumbel law) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Assume equal standard probabilities and
\[
        \rho_n n\log n\to0.
\]
Let $T_n$ be the reset-button completion time.  Then, for every $y\in\Rbb$,
\[
        \Pbb\left(T_n\le n\log n+ny\right)
        \longrightarrow
        \exp(-e^{-y}).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
        \frac{T_n-n\log n}{n}\Rightarrow G,
\]
where $G$ is the standard coupon-collector Gumbel variable with distribution function
\[
        \Pbb(G\le y)=\exp(-e^{-y}).
\]

body:
[Thm sharp of arXiv:2411.14236, 'Size of chaos for Gibbs measures\\of mean field interacting diffusions'] Suppose that the following three conditions hold true.
\begin{itemize}
\item
(Log-Sobolev inequalities)
There exists $\rho > 0$ such that the non-linear and linear
log-Sobolev inequalities hold:
\[
\forall m \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X),
\qquad
2\rho H(m|m_*)
\leqslant
\begin{cases}
I(m|\Pi[m]),~\text{and} \\
I(m|m_*).
\end{cases}
\]
\item
(Transport inequalities)
There exists $\gamma \geqslant 0$ such that
for both $\mu = m^{N,k|[k-1]}_{*,\bm{x}^{[k-1]}}$ and $\mu = m_*$,
the probability measure $\mu$ satisfies the transport inequality
\[
\forall \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X),\qquad
\lvert \langle \nabla_1 W(x^k, \cdot),
\nu - \mu \rangle\rvert^2
\leqslant \gamma
H(\nu | \mu )
\]
uniformly in $k \in [N]$, $\bm{x}^{[k]} \in \mathcal X^{k}$.
\item
(Square integrability)
There exists $M \geqslant 0$ such that
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathcal X^2} \lvert \nabla_1 W(x,y)
- \langle \nabla_1 W(x,\cdot), m_*\rangle\rvert^2
m^{N,2}_*(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} x\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} y) &\leqslant M, \\
\int_{\mathcal X} \lvert \nabla_1 W(x,x)
- \langle \nabla_1 W(x,\cdot), m_*\rangle\rvert^2
m^{N,1}_*(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} x) &\leqslant M.
\end{align*}
\end{itemize}
Then for all $k \in [N]$,
\[
\int_{\mathcal X^{k-1}} H(m^{N,k|[k-1]}_{*,\bm{x}^{[k-1]}} | m_*)
m^{N,k-1}_*(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\bm{x}^{[k-1]})
\leqslant
\frac{36\bigl(1+\frac\gamma\rho\bigr)^3M}{\rho N^2}
\biggl( k + \frac{3\gamma}{\rho}\biggr),
\]
and consequently,
\[
H(m^{N,k}_* | m_*^{\otimes k}) \leqslant
\frac{18\bigl(1+\frac\gamma\rho\bigr)^3M}{\rho N^2}
\biggl( k^2+ \Bigl(1+\frac{6\gamma}{\rho}\Bigr)k\biggr).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm sharp of arXiv:2411.14236

[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2606.15178, 'The distribution of the de Moivre experiment'] Let $ X\sim \mathcal{B}^{(s)}(n,p) $ be a bi$^{s}$nomial random variable with parameters $ n $ and $ p $, with $p\neq q$, and set
	$$ \mu_s=E(X)=np\frac{(s+1)p^{s}-1}{(p-q)},\qquad \sigma^2_s=V(X)=npq\frac{ 1-(s+1)^2(pq)^s}{(p-q)^2}. $$
	Then the standardized variable $ Z=\frac{X-\mu_s}{\sigma_s} $ converges in distribution, as $n\rightarrow\infty$, to the standard normal distribution $N(0,1)$; in other words, $X$ has, for large $n$, an approximate normal distribution with mean $\mu_s$ and variance $\sigma_s^2$.

Then for every t > 0, P(X_n - X_0 >= t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2 sum_{k=1}^n c_k^2)) and P(X_n - X_0 <= -t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2 sum c_k^2)); hence P(|X_n - X_0| >= t) <= 2 exp(-t^2 / (2 sum c_k^2)). body: A discrete-time Markov chain on a countable state space S with transition matrix P is irreducible if for every pair of states x, y in S there exists n >= 0 with P^n(x,y) > 0 (y is reachable from x). The period of a state x is the greatest common divisor of {n >= 1 : P^n(x,x) > 0}; an irreducible chain has a single common period shared by all states, and the chain is aperiodic if this common period equals 1, equivalently if for some x and all sufficiently large n, P^n(x,x) > 0. [standard, e.g. Levin and Peres, Markov Chains and Mixing Times]
title: Irreducible and Aperiodic Discrete-Time Markov Chain
Theorem 11 of arXiv:2604.15226
Corollary 25 of arXiv:2609.02785

[Lemma lem_NN20 of arXiv:2607.11469, 'Breuer-Major-Donsker invariance principle'] Let $(Y_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of random elements 
in $\mathbf{D}([0,1])$. 
Suppose that there is some $p > 2$ and $C \in(0, \infty)$
such that 

\noindent
\begin{align}
\| Y_n(t) - Y_n(s) \|_{p} \leq C \Big(  \frac{  \lfloor nt \rfloor - \lfloor ns \rfloor}{n} \Big)^{\frac12}
\end{align}
for any $0 \leq s \leq t \leq 1$
and for any $n\geq 1$.
Then,  $\{Y_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ is tight
in $\mathbf{D}([0,1])$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(q\in Y^{\rm rv}\), and suppose that a Zariski-open neighbourhood
\(U_{\rm prod}\ni q\) admits a biregular product trivialization
\[
 \pi^{-1}(U_{\rm prod})\cong U_{\rm prod}\times F
\]
over \(U_{\rm prod}\).  Then there is a principal Zariski-open product
neighbourhood \(U\ni q\), \(U\subset U_{\rm prod}\), such that for every
\(V\Subset U\) there are constants \(0<c_V\le C_V<\infty\), independent
of \(t<T\), for which
\begin{equation}
 c_V\eta\le S_t\le C_V\eta
 \qquad\text{on }\pi^{-1}(V).
\end{equation}
Moreover, uniformly in \(f\in F\),
\begin{equation}
 \omega(t)|_{V\times\{f\}}
 \le C_V\pi^*\eta|_{V\times\{f\}},
 \qquad 0\le t<T.
\end{equation}
Consequently, if \(K\Subset Y^{\rm rv}\) has the
Zariski-open-product property, then
\[
 c_K\eta\le S_t\le C_K\eta
 \qquad\text{on }\pi^{-1}(K)
\]
for constants independent of \(t<T\).

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.18073, 'Pick-up Sticks and the General Fibonacci Numbers'] If \(n\) real numbers are chosen uniformly from the unit interval \([0, 1]\), for \(k\geq 3\),
the probability that no \(k+1\) of the numbers can form a \(k+1\)-gons  is
\[P_n^{(k)}=\prod_{l=1}^{n-k+2}\frac{1}{F^l_k} \prod_{i=1}^{k-2}\frac{1}{F^{n-i+1}_k-\sum_{j=1}^{k-i-1}(k-i-j)F_k^{n-k+j}},\]
where \(F_k^l\) is the \(l\)-th term in  \(k\)-step Fibonacci-type recurrence. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.18073

[Proposition PROP:gglimit of arXiv:2411.07840, 'Central limit theorem for the focusing $Φ^4$-measure in the infinite volume limit'] Let $g$ be a real-valued, smooth, compactly supported function with $\textup{dist}(\supp g, x_0)>0$, where $x_0\in \mathbb{T}_L$. Then, we have
\begin{align}
&\frac{ \mathbb{E}_{\nu^\perp_{Q, x_0}}  \Big[  e^{i\langle \Re h^\perp, g_L \rangle+it^{+}\langle \gamma_L,g \rangle  }  e^{\bar {\mathcal{E}}(h^\perp, t^{+}) } e^{c_0(t^+)^2+b(h^\perp)t^+}  , \,D_L, \, B_K  \Big]}{ \mathbb{E}_{\nu^\perp_{Q, x_0}}  \Big[ e^{\bar {\mathcal{E}}(h^\perp, t^{+}) } e^{c_0(t^+)^2+b(h^\perp)t^+}  , \,D_L, \, B_K  \Big] }=e^{-\frac{1}{2}\|g\|^2_{L^2}}(1+o_L(1)) \\

body:
[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\) and \(r_a(\xi)=e^{-2\xi}-e^{-2a\xi}\), \(\xi>0\). Then
\(0<r_a(\xi)<1\) for every \(\xi>0\), and
\[
        \rho_a:=\sup_{\xi>0}r_a(\xi)
        =
        (a-1)a^{-a/(a-1)}<1.
\]
Moreover, \(r_a\in L^1(0,\infty)\),
\begin{equation}

        \int_0^\infty r_a(\xi)\,\mathrm d\xi
        =
        \frac12\left(1-\frac1a\right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

        \int_0^\infty r_a(\xi)(1-r_a(\xi))\,\mathrm d\xi
        =
        \frac{(a-1)(a+3)}{4a(a+1)}.
\end{equation}
Finally, \(r_a(\xi)=2(a-1)\xi+O(\xi^2)\) as \(\xi\downarrow0\), and \(r_a\)
decays exponentially as \(\xi\to\infty\).

body:
[Proposition 43 (Type II blow-up limits split along $\mathcal{V}' \oplus \mathcal{H}'$) of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] Suppose the singularity at $T$ is of Type II. 
	
	{(i) The limit splits along} $\mathcal{V}' \oplus \mathcal{H}'$\emph{.} The distributions subconverge to complementary orthogonal distributions $\mathcal{V}'_\infty$ (rank $2 m + 2$) and $\mathcal{H}'_\infty$ (rank $2 n'$, where $n' := \sum_{k \geq 2} n_k$) whose O'Neill tensors vanish: both are parallel, and by the de Rham decomposition theorem the universal cover splits isometrically and holomorphically, for each $t$,
	
	\begin{equation}
		\widetilde{M}_\infty \;=\; \Phi \times Y \,, \qquad \widetilde{g}_\infty (t) \;=\; g^\Phi (t) \,\oplus\, g^Y (t) \,, \qquad \dim_{\mathbb{R}} \Phi \;=\; 2 m + 2 \,,
	\end{equation}
	
	with each factor a complete eternal Kähler--Ricci flow.\\
	
	{(ii) The} $\mathcal{H}'$\emph{-factor is flat.} $( Y, g^Y (t) )$ is flat and static, hence $Y = \mathbb{C}^{n'}$, being simply connected; all curvature is carried by the fiber factor, $| \mathrm{Rm}_{g^\Phi} | \leq 1$ with equality at $( x_\infty, 0 )$, so $\Phi$ is nonflat.\\
	
	{(iv) The fiber factor is a limit of Calabi fibers.} Under \eqref{eq:typeII-splitting}, $\Phi$ is the leaf of $\mathcal{V}'_\infty$ through $x_\infty$: the pointed limit of the rescaled totally geodesic fibers $\big( ( \widehat{\pi}' )^{-1} \big( \widehat{\pi}' ( x_j ) \big), \, g_j (t) \big)$ --- each a Calabi-symmetric Kähler metric on $\mathbb{CP}^{m+1}$.
title: Type II blow-up limits split along $\mathcal{V}' \oplus \mathcal{H}'$

As N -> infinity the overlaps Q_ij = w_i . w_j and R_in = w_i . v_n follow a deterministic ODE in time t = steps/N (the Saad-Solla equations, including the eta^2 term). Take K = M = 2 and restrict to the symmetric slice Q_11 = Q_22 = q, Q_12 = c, all R_in = r, which the ODE preserves. For every eta in [2499/5000, 2501/5000], the solution from (q, c, r) = (1, 0, 0) exists for all t >= 0 and converges exponentially to an equilibrium x*(eta). That equilibrium is the unique zero of the slice drift in a certified box where it is physical (q - c > 0, q + c - 4 r^2 > 0) and Hurwitz in the slice. Its antisymmetric block has exactly the plateau's unstable direction (lambda > 0). Hence the spherical start reaches the symmetric saddle along its stable manifold.

[Proposition thm|S3DSwitchConfiguration of arXiv:2504.08938, 'Fourier Levels and Almost Sure Bounds on Higher-Order Derivatives in First-Passage Percola'] Assume that $S=\{k,l,m\}$ and that $k$ is a direction switching edge with respect to $(l,m)$. 
Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be the endpoints of $k$. Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be two fixed paths. Assume that $\lambda$ is a geodesic on $\sigma_l^a\sigma_m^b(\omega)$ and that $K_1$ appears before $K_2$ on $\lambda$. Assume that $\mu$ is a geodesic on $\sigma_l^b\sigma_m^a(\omega)$ and that $K_2$ appears before $K_1$ on $\mu$. Denote by $\lambda^-$ the section of $\lambda$ between the source and $K_1$ and by $\lambda^+$ the section of $\lambda$ between $K_2$ and the sink. Similarly, let $\mu^-$ and $\mu^+$ be the sections of $\mu$ before and after the edge $k$.  
Then, one of the following two mathematical propositions $P(\lambda^-,\mu^+)$ and $P(\lambda^+,\mu^-)$ is satisfied
\begin{eqnarray}
P(\lambda^-,\mu^+)&\equiv&\left\{ (l\in \lambda^-) \quad\mbox{and}\quad (m\in\mu^+)\right\},\\
P(\lambda^+,\mu^-)&\equiv&\left\{ (l\in \lambda^+) \quad\mbox{and}\quad (m\in\mu^-)\right\}.
\end{eqnarray}

body: Localized regime of the bounded-density conjecture for quadratic forms (Proposition 4). Let X_1..X_n be independent with densities <=1 and Q(x)=x^T A x with A symmetric. (a) If some 2x2 PRINCIPAL submatrix B of A (two original coordinates i, j) is definite, then ||p_Q||_inf <= pi/sqrt(det B). Proof: condition on the other n-2 ORIGINAL coordinates (independent, so Fubini is genuine); given them Q is a quadratic-plus-linear form in (X_i, X_j); complete the square (B invertible), which shifts (X_i, X_j) and keeps their joint density <=1; for definite B each set {s <= y^T B y <= s+h} is an elliptic annulus of area at most pi h/sqrt(det B), so the conditional density is at most pi/sqrt(det B); average. (b) Hence if A has a 3x3 PRINCIPAL submatrix A_[S] all of whose eigenvalues have modulus >= c>0, and A_[S] is definite or diagonal, then ||p_Q||_inf <= pi/c: for definite A_[S], Cauchy interlacing puts both eigenvalues of every 2x2 principal block of A_[S] at modulus >= c with one sign, so det >= c^2; for diagonal A_[S], two of the three diagonal entries share a sign and form a definite diagonal block with det >= c^2. This contains the separable case. (c) For other well-conditioned blocks the bound K/c is not proved. A block may have no definite 2x2 principal block at all, e.g. [[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,0]] (eigenvalues 2, -1, -1), and the rank-3 coarea bound ||p_S||_inf <= K||rho||_inf^{2/3} is false for general bounded densities on R^3: a density rho <= B placed on a thin shell around {S = s} gives p_S of order B s^{1/2}/sqrt(l1 l2 l3) for a definite form, unbounded in s. So the localized regime is settled for forms with a definite 2x2 principal block of determinant >= c^2, in particular when a well-conditioned 3x3 principal block is definite or diagonal; the other localized forms stay open, together with the DELOCALIZED forms (every 3x3 principal block near-singular), which is the CLT regime.

[Corollary corollary_repl_lemma_ave of arXiv:2411.17653, 'Exclusion processes with non-reversible boundary: hydrodynamics and large deviations'] For any function $H \in C^{1,2}( {\Omega_T})$and for every $\delta > 0$, it holds that
\begin{equation} 
\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}\lim_{N\to+\infty}\mathbb{P}_{\nu_N} \left( \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \Big | \int_0^t \eta_{sN^2}(\epsilon_N)\nabla^+_N H_s(0) - \pi^N_s \ast \iota_\epsilon(\epsilon_N)\partial_u H_s(0) ds\Big| > \delta \right) =0,
\end{equation} and
\begin{equation} 
\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}\lim_{N\to+\infty}\mathbb{P}_{\nu_N} \left( \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \Big | \int_0^t \eta_{sN^2}(\tau_N)\nabla^+_N H_s(\tau_N) - \pi^N_s \ast \iota_\epsilon(\tau_N)\partial_u H_s(1) ds\Big| > \delta \right) =0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary corollary_repl_lemma_ave of arXiv:2411.17653

[Theorem thm: DPP2 of arXiv:2411.12474, 'Multi-type branching processes with immigration generated by point processes'] Assume that immigration 
	is spanned by a
	stationary $(\Lambda,K)$-DPP
	with $\Lambda(\mathrm{d} x) = \lambda(x) \mathrm{d} x$,
	and that $\lambda(x)\stackrel{\infty}{\sim}\lambda_\infty e^{\delta x}$ for some $\lambda_\infty > 0$ and $\delta \in \mathbb{R}$.

	\begin{enumerate}
		\item  Under (equation eq:strong of the paper), 
		if $\delta> \max\{\rho,0\}$, 
		then 
		\[
		\frac{{Z_i}(t)}{e^{\delta t}}\xrightarrow[t \to \infty]{L^2} A_i:=
 K_\ast \lambda_\infty\int_0^\infty e^{-\delta x}\Ebb{Z_{\times,i}(x)}\mathrm{d} x,
		\]
        where $K_\ast:=K(0,0)$.
		\item  Under (equation eq:strong of the paper), 
		if the process is \textbf{supercritical}, that is, 
		$
		\rho>0$, and  $\delta = \rho$, then
		\[\frac{{Z_i}(t)}{te^{\delta t}}
		\xrightarrow[t\to\infty]{L^2} A_i':=K_\ast \lambda_\infty 
        \langle \boldsymbol{u},
	\Ebb{\boldsymbol{I}}\rangle v_i.\]
		
		
		\item  
		 
		If the process is \textbf{critical}, that is		$
		\rho=0$, $\Ebb{||\boldsymbol{\nu}||^2}$ is finite, $\lambda$ is bounded, $\delta = \rho$, and the covariance function $K(x, 0)$ of the DPP tends to $0$ as $x\to \infty$. Then
		\[\frac{\boldsymbol{Z}(t) }{t}\xrightarrow[t\to\infty]{d} 
		Y
		\boldsymbol{v}  ,\]  where $Y\sim \Gamma(K(0,0)\lambda_\infty \beta,1/Q)$ with
\[
Q := \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i, j, k = 1}^d \left. \frac{\partial^2 G_{\nu_i}}{\partial x_j \partial x_k} \right|_{\boldsymbol{x} = \boldsymbol{1}} \mu_i^{-1}v_i u_j u_k,
    \qquad
	\beta :=
	\frac{\langle\boldsymbol{u}, \Ebb{\boldsymbol{I}}\rangle}{Q},
	
	
\]
    and $\Gamma(\alpha, \beta)$ is
		the Gamma law with shape $\alpha$
		and rate $\beta$, that is,
		its density is, for $x >0$,
		\[
		f_{\alpha,\beta}(x) = 
		\frac{\beta^\alpha}{\Gamma(\alpha)}x^{\alpha-1}e^{-\beta x}.
		\]
		\item 
		If the process is \textbf{subcritical}, that is, 
		$
		\rho<0$, and $\delta = 0$, then
		\[
		\boldsymbol{Z}(t) \xrightarrow[t\to\infty]{d} \boldsymbol{X},
		\]where $\boldsymbol{X}$ is a random variable whose Laplace transform is available in
		(equation eq:Laplace limit of the paper).
		
		
		
		
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 18 (A sufficient condition for proxy-faithfulness) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Let transforms $A,B$ act on the same operand under a common grouping and produce group-RMS profiles with $\sum_g\sigma_g^2=S_A\ge S_B$ and per-group crest factors $M_g=\mathrm{CF}_g\,\sigma_g$ all lying in a band
$\mathrm{CF}_g\in[\underline c,\bar c]$ (necessarily $1\le\underline c\le\bar c\le\sqrt G$
for a group of size $G$). If that band is tight relative to the proxy gap,
$\bar c^2/\underline c^2 < S_A/S_B$, then the $L^2$ proxy $\sum_g\sigma_g^2$ and the
AbsMax step-size surrogate $\sum_g M_g^2$ rank $A$ and $B$ the \emph{same} way. When
the crest-factor profiles differ enough to break this condition, which a
concentrating transform induces, the ranking can \emph{invert}. Note that the aggregate $\sum_g\sigma_g^2$ is the operand's Frobenius energy divided by $G$, hence unchanged by any orthogonal map: between two rotations $S_A=S_B$ and the sufficient condition is unavailable, so this proposition bites only where the transforms change that energy. What a concentrating rotation still changes is the crest-factor band, and that is the route by which the two surrogates come apart.

[Lemma lem_2a of arXiv:2607.11469, 'Breuer-Major-Donsker invariance principle'] Let $\mathbf G$ have an absolutely continuous spectral measure with density
$\mathfrak m\in L^1(\mathbb T)$. For $q\ge2$, the $q$-decimated sequence
has spectral density
\begin{align}
\mathfrak m_q(\theta)
=
\frac1q\sum_{\ell=0}^{q-1}
\mathfrak m\left(\left[\frac{\theta+2\pi\ell}{q}\right]_{\mathbb T}\right)
\end{align}
for a.e. $\theta\in\mathbb T$.
If, in addition, $\rho_G\in\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$, then the equality holds
pointwise for the continuous versions.
title: Lemma lem_2a of arXiv:2607.11469

This appendix removes the need to treat (A) and (B) as unverified black boxes. Their source is still credited to Ye-Du. It keeps the negative second-order term in the residual case explicitly.

Let X be real symmetric with ||X||op<=2 and let mu I<=Lambda<=I. For either sign define H_+=I+eta(Lambda-X), H_-=I-eta(Lambda-X). Direct expansion, requiring no commutation between Lambda and X, gives
 H_+ X H_+ = [X/2-2eta X^2+eta^2 X^3] + C_+ X C_+ - eta^2 R,
 H_- X H_- = [X/2+2eta X^2+eta^2 X^3] + C_- X C_- - eta^2 R,
where
 C_+=I/sqrt(2)+sqrt(2)eta Lambda,
 C_-=I/sqrt(2)-sqrt(2)eta Lambda,
 R=Lambda X Lambda+Lambda X^2+X^2 Lambda.
Here ||R||op<=2+4+4=10.
Both identities are independently verified as universal free noncommutative polynomial identities in scripts/check_spectral_splits.py.

For (A), X is positive definite. On [0,2], the scalar polynomial
 h_+(x)=x/2-2eta x^2+eta^2 x^3
is nondecreasing because h_+'(x)>=1/2-8eta>=0 for eta<=1/16. If w=lambda_min(X)>0, spectral calculus therefore gives
 lambda_min(h_+(X))=h_+(w).
Since C_+ is positive definite and lambda_min(C_+)>=1/sqrt(2)+sqrt(2)eta mu,
 lambda_min(C_+ X C_+)>=w(1/2+2eta mu+2eta^2 mu^2).
Adding these bounds and subtracting the remainder gives
 lambda_min(H_+ X H_+)
 >=(1+eta(mu-w))^2 w
     +eta^2(mu^2 w+2mu w^2)-10eta^2
 >=(1+eta(mu-w))^2 w-22eta^2.
This proves (A).

For (B), if p=lambda_min(X)>=0, congruence preserves positive semidefiniteness.
If p<0, the polynomial h_-(x)=x/2+2eta x^2+eta^2 x^3 is nondecreasing on [-2,2], since h_-'(x)>=1/2-8eta>=0. Thus lambda_min(h_-(X))=h_-(p).
The matrix C_- is positive definite for eta<=1/16 and
 ||C_-||op<=1/sqrt(2)-sqrt(2)eta mu.
From X>=pI and p<0,
 C_- X C_->=p C_-^2>=p||C_-||op^2 I.
Consequently,
 lambda_min(H_- X H_-)
 >=(1-eta mu)^2 p
    +2eta p^2+eta^2 p^3+eta^2 mu^2 p-10eta^2.
The first two correction terms combine as eta p^2(2+eta p)>=0, since p>=-2 and eta<=1/16. Also mu^2 p>=-2. The whole correction is therefore >=-12eta^2, which is stronger than the required -22eta^2. This proves (B), including every sign condition in the congruence comparison.

This appendix uses only the real symmetric spectral theorem, scalar polynomial monotonicity, norm submultiplicativity and the elementary Loewner-order congruence rule. Let V = V(F) and p in V. If v in ker(J_F(p)) is tangent to an analytic curve gamma(t) = p + t*v + (t^2 / 2)*w + O(t^3) in V, then the quadratic form Q_F(p)(v) must lie in the image of J_F(p): specifically, J_F(p)*w + Q_F(p)(v) = 0. Therefore, the quadratic obstruction q_p(v) must vanish: q_p(v) = 0 in k^m / im(J_F(p)).

body:
[Thm mainhaar of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Let $\boldsymbol{U}^N=(U_1^N,\ldots,U_r^N)$ be i.i.d.\ Haar-distributed
random matrices in $\mathrm{U}(N)/\mathrm{O}(N)/\mathrm{Sp}(N)$,
and let $\boldsymbol{u}=(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ be free Haar unitaries.
Let $\varepsilon\in [\frac{1}{c\sqrt{N}},1]$ and $q_0\in\mathbb{N}$. 
For every noncommutative polynomial $P\in\mathrm{M}_D(\mathbb{C})\otimes 
\mathbb{C}\langle\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{u}^*\rangle$ of degree $q_0$ 
with matrix coefficients of dimension $D\le e^{cN\varepsilon^2/
\log^2(N\varepsilon^2)}$, we have
$$
	\mathbf{P}\big[
	\|P(
	\boldsymbol{U}^N,
	\boldsymbol{U}^{N*})\|\ge (1+\varepsilon)
	\|P(\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{u}^*)\|
	\big] \le
	\frac{N}{c\varepsilon}
	\,e^{-cN\varepsilon^2/\log^2(N\varepsilon^2)}.
$$
Here $c$ is a constant that depends only on $q_0$ and $r$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be measures on the same measurable space $(X, \Sigma)$, with $
u$ possibly signed or complex. $
u$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$, written $
u \ll \mu$, if $
u(A) = 0$ for every $A \in \Sigma$ with $\mu(A) = 0$ (for signed $
u$, equivalently $|
u|(A) = 0$, where $|
u|$ is the total variation). If $
u$ is FINITE (or finite signed/complex), this is equivalent to the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $\delta > 0$ with $|
u(A)| < \varepsilon$ whenever $\mu(A) < \delta$; for infinite $
u$ the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition is strictly stronger (e.g. $
u(A) = \int_A |x|^{-1}dx$ on $(0,1)$ has $
u \ll$ Lebesgue but fails $\varepsilon$-$\delta$). Any measure of the form $
u(A) = \int_A f\,d\mu$ with $f \geq 0$ measurable (or $f \in L^1(\mu)$ for signed $
u$) satisfies $
u \ll \mu$; the Radon-Nikodym theorem is the converse under $\sigma$-finiteness. $\mu$ and $
u$ are mutually singular, $\mu \perp 
u$, if there is $A \in \Sigma$ with $\mu(A) = 0$ and $
u(X\setminus A) = 0$. Lebesgue decomposition: for $\sigma$-finite $\mu, 
u$ there is a unique splitting $
u = 
u_{ac} + 
u_s$ with $
u_{ac} \ll \mu$ and $
u_s \perp \mu$. Related but different: a FUNCTION $F: [a,b]	o\mathbb{R}$ is absolutely continuous iff its Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure is absolutely continuous w.r.t. Lebesgue measure iff $F(x) = F(a) + \int_a^x F'$ with $F' \in L^1$; the Cantor function is continuous, increasing, but not absolutely continuous (its measure is singular). Sharp edge: $
u \ll \mu$ is not symmetric, and $
u \ll \mu$ with $\mu \ll 
u$ (equivalence) does not make the density bounded or bounded below.
mu and nu are measures on a common measurable space (X, Sigma); nu may be signed or complex
the epsilon-delta characterisation requires nu finite

[Dfn 232 (truncated Lipschitz algorithm) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Consider an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$ with input $(\bG, \bg^\aux)$. Denote its output $\bx\equiv\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)$. For $a\in [M]$, define the random variable
	\[\fm_a\equiv
		\fm_a(\bG,\bg^\aux;\cA_N)
		\equiv
		\frac{(\bg^a,\bx)}{N^{1/2}}\,,
	\]
where we recall that $\bg^a$ is the $a$-th row of $\bG$.
	For $K > 0$, define
	\[
		S_K(\cA_N) = \bigg\{
			a \in [M] : 
			\Big|\E\fm_a(\bG,\bg^\aux;\cA_N)\Big|
			\ge K
		\bigg\}\,.
	\]
Let $\hbG \in \R^{M\times N}$ be a matrix of i.i.d. gaussians independent of $(\bG, \bg^\aux)$.
	Then define the \textbf{truncated algorithm} $\cA_{N[K]}$ as the function
	\[\cA_{N[K]}\Big(\bG, 
	\bg^{\aux+}
	\equiv(\bg^\aux, \hbG)\Big)
	\equiv
	\cA_N\Big(\tbG(\bG,\hbG;S_K(\cA_N)), \bg^\aux\Big)\,,
	\]
where $\tbG$ is the row-splicing operation from Definition~\ref{d:row.splice}. In words, if $|\E\fm_a| \ge K$, then $\cA_{N[K]}$ ignores the $a$-th row $\bg^a$ of $\bG$ and replaces this input with the independent gaussian vector $\hat\bg$. 	Clearly $\cA_{N[K]}$ is also an $L$-Lipschitz function, with output
	\[\tilde{\bx} \equiv 
		\cA_{N[K]}(\bG, (\bg^\aux, \hbG)) \stackrel{\textit{d}}{=}
		\bx
		= \cA_N(\bG, \bg^\aux)\,.
	\]
It follows that $\cA_{N[K]}$ is also an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}.
title: truncated Lipschitz algorithm
